CategoryTheory.Functor.category.comment:
`Functor.category C D` gives the category structure on functors and natural transformations
between categories `C` and `D`.

Notice that if `C` and `D` are both small categories at the same universe level,
this is another small category at that level.
However if `C` and `D` are both large categories at the same universe level,
this is a small category at the next higher level.
CategoryTheory.Functor.category.fullDefinition: instance Functor.category : Category.{max u₁ v₂} (C ⥤ D) where   Hom F G := NatTrans F G   id F := NatTrans.id F   comp α β := vcomp α β
CategoryTheory.Functor.category.description: This assigns a category structure to functors and natural transformations between two categories while noting the implications of their sizes on the category's classification.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Faithful.div.fullDefinition: protected def Faithful.div (F : C ⥤ E) (G : D ⥤ E) [G.Faithful] (obj : C → D)     (h_obj : ∀ X, G.obj (obj X) = F.obj X) (map : ∀ {X Y}, (X ⟶ Y) → (obj X ⟶ obj Y))     (h_map : ∀ {X Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}, HEq (G.map (map f)) (F.map f)) : C ⥤ D :=   { obj, map := @map,     map_id := by       intros X       apply G.map_injective       apply eq_of_heq       trans F.map (𝟙 X)       · exact h_map       · rw [F.map_id, G.map_id, h_obj X]     map_comp := by       intros X Y Z f g       refine G.map_injective <| eq_of_heq <| h_map.trans ?_       simp only [Functor.map_comp]       convert HEq.refl (F.map f ≫ F.map g)       all_goals { first | apply h_obj | apply h_map } }

CategoryTheory.Functor.comp.fullDefinition: def comp (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) : C ⥤ E where   obj X := G.obj (F.obj X)   map f := G.map (F.map f)   map_comp := by intros; dsimp; rw [F.map_comp, G.map_comp]
CategoryTheory.Functor.comp.description: This statement defines the composition of two functors, where the first functor is applied to an object followed by the second functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.comp_obj.description: This theorem states that the application of a composed functor to an object yields the same result as applying the first functor to the object and then the second functor to the result.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_dite.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]

CategoryTheory.Functorial.map'.code:
CategoryTheory.Functorial.map'.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {F : C → D} [self : Functorial F] {X Y : C} : (X ⟶ Y) → (F X ⟶ F Y)
CategoryTheory.Functorial.map'.comment: A functorial map extends to an action on morphisms.
CategoryTheory.Functorial.map'.fullDefinition: map' : ∀ {X Y : C}, (X ⟶ Y) → (F X ⟶ F Y)   /-- A functorial map preserves identities. -/   map_id' : ∀ X : C, map' (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (F X) := by aesop_cat   /-- A functorial map preserves composition of morphisms. -/   map_comp' : ∀ {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), map' (f ≫ g) = map' f ≫ map' g := by     aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Functorial.map'.description: This definition describes a functorial map that allows for the application of a functor to morphisms between objects in a category, transforming them accordingly in a target category.

CategoryTheory.map.code:
CategoryTheory.map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C → D)
  [Functorial F] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : F X ⟶ F Y
CategoryTheory.map.comment:
If `F : C → D` (just a function) has `[Functorial F]`,
we can write `map F f : F X ⟶ F Y` for the action of `F` on a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`.
CategoryTheory.map.fullDefinition: def map (F : C → D) [Functorial.{v₁, v₂} F] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : F X ⟶ F Y :=   Functorial.map'.{v₁, v₂} f
CategoryTheory.map.description: This definition introduces a method to apply a function that behaves like a functor to a morphism between objects in a category, allowing for the transformation of that morphism into a corresponding morphism in another category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.of.fullDefinition: def of (F : C → D) [I : Functorial.{v₁, v₂} F] : C ⥤ D :=   { I with obj := F            map := map F }

CategoryTheory.functorial_comp.fullDefinition: def functorial_comp (F : C → D) [Functorial.{v₁, v₂} F] (G : D → E) [Functorial.{v₂, v₃} G] :     Functorial.{v₁, v₃} (G ∘ F) :=   { Functor.of F ⋙ Functor.of G with map' := fun f => map G (map F f) }
CategoryTheory.functorial_comp.description: This definition establishes that the composition of two functorial functions results in a function that is also functorial.

CategoryTheory.Functor.const.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (J : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] :
  C ⥤ J ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.comment: The functor sending `X : C` to the constant functor `J ⥤ C` sending everything to `X`.
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.fullDefinition: def const : C ⥤ J ⥤ C where   obj X :=     { obj := fun _ => X       map := fun _ => 𝟙 X }   map f := { app := fun _ => f }
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.description: This definition describes a functor that maps objects from one category to a constant functor which sends every object to the same fixed object in another category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjOp.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjOp.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {C : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] (X : C) : (const Jᵒᵖ).obj (op X) ≅ ((const J).obj X).op
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjOp.comment:
The constant functor `Jᵒᵖ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ` sending everything to `op X`
is (naturally isomorphic to) the opposite of the constant functor `J ⥤ C` sending everything to `X`.
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjOp.fullDefinition: def opObjOp (X : C) : (const Jᵒᵖ).obj (op X) ≅ ((const J).obj X).op where   hom := { app := fun j => 𝟙 _ }   inv := { app := fun j => 𝟙 _ }
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjOp.description: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism between a constant functor that maps everything to the opposite of a given object in one category and the opposite of a constant functor that maps everything to that object in another category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {C : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] (X : Cᵒᵖ) : (const Jᵒᵖ).obj (unop X) ≅ ((const J).obj X).leftOp
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop.comment:
The constant functor `Jᵒᵖ ⥤ C` sending everything to `unop X`
is (naturally isomorphic to) the opposite of
the constant functor `J ⥤ Cᵒᵖ` sending everything to `X`.
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop.fullDefinition: def opObjUnop (X : Cᵒᵖ) : (const Jᵒᵖ).obj (unop X) ≅ ((const J).obj X).leftOp where   hom := { app := fun j => 𝟙 _ }   inv := { app := fun j => 𝟙 _ }
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop.description: This definition asserts a natural isomorphism between a constant functor that maps everything to the underlying object of a given object in one category and the opposite of a constant functor that maps everything to that object in another category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop_h.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop_hom_app.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {C : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] (X : Cᵒᵖ) (j : Jᵒᵖ) : (opObjUnop X).hom.app j = 𝟙 (((const Jᵒᵖ).obj (unop X)).obj j)
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop_h.description: This theorem states that the application of the morphism in the natural isomorphism between specific functors yields the identity morphism on the object mapped by a constant functor for a given object.

CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop_i.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop_inv_app.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {C : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] (X : Cᵒᵖ) (j : Jᵒᵖ) : (opObjUnop X).inv.app j = 𝟙 (((const J).obj X).leftOp.obj j)
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.opObjUnop_i.description: This theorem demonstrates that the component of the inverse of the natural isomorphism from one functor to another, evaluated at a specific object, is equivalent to the identity morphism of the image of that object under the left operation of the second functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.const.unop_functo.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.unop_functor_op_obj_map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {C : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] (X : Cᵒᵖ) {j₁ j₂ : J} (f : j₁ ⟶ j₂) : (unop ((const J).op.obj X)).map f = 𝟙 (unop X)
CategoryTheory.Functor.const.unop_functo.description: This theorem shows that the mapping of a morphism in the opposite category under a specific functor results in the identity morphism of the underlying object in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.constComp.comment:
These are actually equal, of course, but not definitionally equal
(the equality requires F.map (𝟙 _) = 𝟙 _). A natural isomorphism is
more convenient than an equality between functors (compare id_to_iso).
CategoryTheory.Functor.constComp.fullDefinition: def constComp (X : C) (F : C ⥤ D) : (const J).obj X ⋙ F ≅ (const J).obj (F.obj X) where   hom := { app := fun _ => 𝟙 _ }   inv := { app := fun _ => 𝟙 _ }
CategoryTheory.Functor.constComp.description: This definition asserts a natural isomorphism between the composition of a constant functor with a given functor and the constant functor applied to the image of an object under that given functor.

CategoryTheory.uncurry.code:
CategoryTheory.uncurry.{v₂, v₃, v₄, u₂, u₃, u₄} {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] {D : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} D]
  {E : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄, u₄} E] : (C ⥤ D ⥤ E) ⥤ C × D ⥤ E
CategoryTheory.uncurry.comment: The uncurrying functor, taking a functor `C ⥤ (D ⥤ E)` and producing a functor `(C × D) ⥤ E`.

explanatories.Prod.fst: The first element of a pair.
explanatories.Prod.snd: The second element of a pair.

CategoryTheory.uncurry.fullDefinition: def uncurry : (C ⥤ D ⥤ E) ⥤ C × D ⥤ E where   obj F :=     { obj := fun X => (F.obj X.1).obj X.2       map := fun {X} {Y} f => (F.map f.1).app X.2 ≫ (F.obj Y.1).map f.2       map_comp := fun f g => by         simp only [prod_comp_fst, prod_comp_snd, Functor.map_comp, NatTrans.comp_app,           Category.assoc]         slice_lhs 2 3 => rw [← NatTrans.naturality]         rw [Category.assoc] }   map T :=     { app := fun X => (T.app X.1).app X.2       naturality := fun X Y f => by         simp only [prod_comp_fst, prod_comp_snd, Category.comp_id, Category.assoc, Functor.map_id,           Functor.map_comp, NatTrans.id_app, NatTrans.comp_app]         slice_lhs 2 3 => rw [NatTrans.naturality]         slice_lhs 1 2 => rw [← NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.naturality, NatTrans.comp_app]         rw [Category.assoc] }
CategoryTheory.uncurry.description: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor from the category of C to the functor category from D to E into a functor from the product category of C and D to E.

CategoryTheory.curryObj.code:
CategoryTheory.curryObj.{v₂, v₃, v₄, u₂, u₃, u₄} {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] {D : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} D]
  {E : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄, u₄} E] (F : C × D ⥤ E) : C ⥤ D ⥤ E
CategoryTheory.curryObj.comment: The object level part of the currying functor. (See `curry` for the functorial version.)
CategoryTheory.curryObj.fullDefinition: def curryObj (F : C × D ⥤ E) : C ⥤ D ⥤ E where   obj X :=     { obj := fun Y => F.obj (X, Y)       map := fun g => F.map (𝟙 X, g)       map_id := fun Y => by simp only [F.map_id]; rw [← prod_id]; exact F.map_id ⟨X,Y⟩       map_comp := fun f g => by simp [← F.map_comp]}   map f :=     { app := fun Y => F.map (f, 𝟙 Y)       naturality := fun {Y} {Y'} g => by simp [← F.map_comp] }   map_id := fun X => by ext Y; exact F.map_id _   map_comp := fun f g => by ext Y; dsimp; simp [← F.map_comp]
CategoryTheory.curryObj.description: This definition outlines the object-level aspect of a functor that converts a functor from the product category of C and D to E into a functor from C to the functor category from D to E.

CategoryTheory.curry.code:
CategoryTheory.curry.{v₂, v₃, v₄, u₂, u₃, u₄} {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] {D : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} D]

CategoryTheory.curry.comment: The currying functor, taking a functor `(C × D) ⥤ E` and producing a functor `C ⥤ (D ⥤ E)`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.curryObj: This definition outlines the object-level aspect of a functor that converts a functor from the product category of C and D to E into a functor from C to the functor category from D to E.

CategoryTheory.curry.fullDefinition: def curry : (C × D ⥤ E) ⥤ C ⥤ D ⥤ E where   obj F := curryObj F   map T :=     { app := fun X =>         { app := fun Y => T.app (X, Y)           naturality := fun Y Y' g => by             dsimp [curryObj]             rw [NatTrans.naturality] }       naturality := fun X X' f => by         ext; dsimp [curryObj]         rw [NatTrans.naturality] }
CategoryTheory.curry.description: This definition introduces a functor that transforms a functor from the product category of C and D into a functor from C to the functor category from D to E.

CategoryTheory.currying.code:
CategoryTheory.currying.{v₂, v₃, v₄, u₂, u₃, u₄} {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] {D : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} D]
  {E : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄, u₄} E] : C ⥤ D ⥤ E ≌ C × D ⥤ E
CategoryTheory.currying.comment: The equivalence of functor categories given by currying/uncurrying.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.uncurry: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor from the category of C to the functor category from D to E into a functor from the product category of C and D to E.
explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.

CategoryTheory.currying.fullDefinition: def currying : C ⥤ D ⥤ E ≌ C × D ⥤ E :=   Equivalence.mk uncurry curry     (NatIso.ofComponents fun F =>         NatIso.ofComponents fun X => NatIso.ofComponents fun Y => Iso.refl _)     (NatIso.ofComponents fun F => NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => eqToIso (by simp))       (by intros X Y f; cases X; cases Y; cases f; dsimp at *; rw [← F.map_comp]; simp))
CategoryTheory.currying.description: This definition states that there is an equivalence between the functor category from C to the functor category from D to E and the functor category from the product of C and D to E, established through the processes of currying and uncurrying.

CategoryTheory.flipIsoCurrySwapUncurry.comment: `F.flip` is isomorphic to uncurrying `F`, swapping the variables, and currying.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.curry: This definition introduces a functor that transforms a functor from the product category of C and D into a functor from C to the functor category from D to E.

CategoryTheory.flipIsoCurrySwapUncurry.fullDefinition: def flipIsoCurrySwapUncurry (F : C ⥤ D ⥤ E) : F.flip ≅ curry.obj (Prod.swap _ _ ⋙ uncurry.obj F) :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun d => NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.flipIsoCurrySwapUncurry.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a flipped version of a functor and the result of a process that swaps the variables, uncurries the functor, and then curries it back.

CategoryTheory.uncurryObjFlip.comment:
The uncurrying of `F.flip` is isomorphic to
swapping the factors followed by the uncurrying of `F`.
CategoryTheory.uncurryObjFlip.fullDefinition: def uncurryObjFlip (F : C ⥤ D ⥤ E) : uncurry.obj F.flip ≅ Prod.swap _ _ ⋙ uncurry.obj F :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun p => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.uncurryObjFlip.description: This definition states that the result of uncurrying a flipped functor is isomorphic to first swapping the categories and then uncurrying the original functor.

CategoryTheory.whiskeringRight₂.comment:

explanatories.CategoryTheory.uncurry: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor from the category of C to the functor category from D to E into a functor from the product category of C and D to E.

CategoryTheory.whiskeringRight₂.fullDefinition: def whiskeringRight₂ : (C ⥤ D ⥤ E) ⥤ (B ⥤ C) ⥤ (B ⥤ D) ⥤ B ⥤ E :=   uncurry ⋙     whiskeringRight _ _ _ ⋙ (whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj (prodFunctorToFunctorProd _ _ _) ⋙ curry

CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence.map.comment:

CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence.map.fullDefinition: def map : ∀ {X : ℕ → C} (_ : ∀ n, X n ⟶ X (n + 1)) (i j : ℕ), i ≤ j → (X i ⟶ X j)   | _, _, 0, 0 => fun _ ↦ 𝟙 _   | _, f, 0, 1 => fun _ ↦ f 0   | _, f, 0, l + 1 => fun _ ↦ f 0 ≫ map (fun n ↦ f (n + 1)) 0 l (by omega)   | _, _, k + 1, 0 => nofun   | _, f, k + 1, l + 1 => fun _ ↦ map (fun n ↦ f (n + 1)) k l (by omega)
CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence.map.description: This statement defines a method to obtain a morphism between two objects in a sequence by composing the morphisms that connect consecutive elements when the first index is less than or equal to the second index.

CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence.map_id.description: This theorem states that composing a morphism that maps an object to itself in a sequence results in the identity morphism for that object.

CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence.map_co.description: This theorem establishes that the morphism between the first and last objects in a sequence is equal to the sequential composition of the morphisms between intermediate objects when the indices are appropriately ordered.

The functor `ℕ ⥤ C` constructed from a sequence of
morphisms `f : X n ⟶ X (n + 1)` for all `n : ℕ`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence.map: This statement defines a method to obtain a morphism between two objects in a sequence by composing the morphisms that connect consecutive elements when the first index is less than or equal to the second index.

CategoryTheory.Functor.LeftExtension.IsP.fullDefinition: def IsPointwiseLeftKanExtension.homFrom (G : LeftExtension L F) : E ⟶ G :=   StructuredArrow.homMk     { app := fun Y => (h Y).desc (LeftExtension.coconeAt G Y)       naturality := fun Y₁ Y₂ φ => (h Y₁).hom_ext (fun X => by         rw [(h Y₁).fac_assoc (coconeAt G Y₁) X]         simpa using (h Y₂).fac (coconeAt G Y₂) ((CostructuredArrow.map φ).obj X)) }     (by       ext X       simpa using (h (L.obj X)).fac (LeftExtension.coconeAt G _) (CostructuredArrow.mk (𝟙 _)))

CategoryTheory.Functor.RightExtension.Is.fullDefinition: def IsPointwiseRightKanExtension.homTo (G : RightExtension L F) : G ⟶ E :=   CostructuredArrow.homMk     { app := fun Y ↦ (h Y).lift (RightExtension.coneAt G Y)       naturality := fun Y₁ Y₂ φ ↦ (h Y₂).hom_ext (fun X ↦ by         rw [assoc, (h Y₂).fac (coneAt G Y₂) X]         simpa using ((h Y₁).fac (coneAt G Y₁) ((StructuredArrow.map φ).obj X)).symm) }     (by       ext X       simpa using (h (L.obj X)).fac (RightExtension.coneAt G _) (StructuredArrow.mk (𝟙 _)) )

CategoryTheory.Functor.pointwiseLeftKanE.fullDefinition: noncomputable def pointwiseLeftKanExtension : D ⥤ H where   obj Y := colimit (CostructuredArrow.proj L Y ⋙ F)   map {Y₁ Y₂} f :=     colimit.desc (CostructuredArrow.proj L Y₁ ⋙ F)       (Cocone.mk (colimit (CostructuredArrow.proj L Y₂ ⋙ F))         { app := fun g => colimit.ι (CostructuredArrow.proj L Y₂ ⋙ F)             ((CostructuredArrow.map f).obj g)           naturality := fun g₁ g₂ φ => by             simpa using colimit.w (CostructuredArrow.proj L Y₂ ⋙ F)               ((CostructuredArrow.map f).map φ) })   map_id Y := colimit.hom_ext (fun j => by     dsimp     simp only [colimit.ι_desc, comp_id]     congr     apply CostructuredArrow.map_id)   map_comp {Y₁ Y₂ Y₃} f f' := colimit.hom_ext (fun j => by     dsimp     simp only [colimit.ι_desc, colimit.ι_desc_assoc, comp_obj, CostructuredArrow.proj_obj]     congr 1     apply CostructuredArrow.map_comp)

CategoryTheory.Functor.pointwiseLeftKanE.fullDefinition: noncomputable def pointwiseLeftKanExtensionUnit : F ⟶ L ⋙ pointwiseLeftKanExtension L F where   app X := colimit.ι (CostructuredArrow.proj L (L.obj X) ⋙ F)     (CostructuredArrow.mk (𝟙 (L.obj X)))   naturality {X₁ X₂} f := by     simp only [comp_obj, pointwiseLeftKanExtension_obj, comp_map,       pointwiseLeftKanExtension_map, colimit.ι_desc, CostructuredArrow.map_mk]     rw [id_comp]     let φ : CostructuredArrow.mk (L.map f) ⟶ CostructuredArrow.mk (𝟙 (L.obj X₂)) :=       CostructuredArrow.homMk f     exact colimit.w (CostructuredArrow.proj L (L.obj X₂) ⋙ F) φ

CategoryTheory.Functor.pointwiseRightKan.fullDefinition: noncomputable def pointwiseRightKanExtension : D ⥤ H where   obj Y := limit (StructuredArrow.proj Y L ⋙ F)   map {Y₁ Y₂} f := limit.lift (StructuredArrow.proj Y₂ L ⋙ F)       (Cone.mk (limit (StructuredArrow.proj Y₁ L ⋙ F))         { app := fun g ↦ limit.π (StructuredArrow.proj Y₁ L ⋙ F)             ((StructuredArrow.map f).obj g)           naturality := fun g₁ g₂ φ ↦ by             simpa using (limit.w (StructuredArrow.proj Y₁ L ⋙ F)               ((StructuredArrow.map f).map φ)).symm })   map_id Y := limit.hom_ext (fun j => by     dsimp     simp only [limit.lift_π, id_comp]     congr     apply StructuredArrow.map_id)   map_comp {Y₁ Y₂ Y₃} f f' := limit.hom_ext (fun j => by     dsimp     simp only [limit.lift_π, assoc]     congr 1     apply StructuredArrow.map_comp)

CategoryTheory.Functor.pointwiseRightKanExtension_map.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2}

  [L.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] {Y₁ Y₂ : D} (f : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂) :

    limit.lift (StructuredArrow.proj Y₂ L ⋙ F)
      { pt := limit (StructuredArrow.proj Y₁ L ⋙ F),

CategoryTheory.lanEvaluationIsoColim.fullDefinition: noncomputable def lanEvaluationIsoColim (F : C ⥤ D) (X : D)     [∀ X : D, HasColimitsOfShape (CostructuredArrow F X) E] :     F.lan ⋙ (evaluation D E).obj X ≅       (whiskeringLeft _ _ E).obj (CostructuredArrow.proj F X) ⋙ colim :=   NatIso.ofComponents (fun G =>     IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (Functor.isPointwiseLeftKanExtensionLanUnit F G X)     (colimit.isColimit _)) (fun {G₁ G₂} φ => by       apply (Functor.isPointwiseLeftKanExtensionLanUnit F G₁ X).hom_ext       intro T       have h₁ := fun (G : C ⥤ E) => IsColimit.comp_coconePointUniqueUpToIso_hom         (Functor.isPointwiseLeftKanExtensionLanUnit F G X) (colimit.isColimit _) T       have h₂ := congr_app (F.lanUnit.naturality φ) T.left       dsimp at h₁ h₂ ⊢       simp only [Category.assoc] at h₁ ⊢       rw [reassoc_of% h₁, NatTrans.naturality_assoc, ← reassoc_of% h₂, h₁,         ι_colimMap, whiskerLeft_app]       rfl)
CategoryTheory.lanEvaluationIsoColim.description: The left adjoint of a functor applied to a specific object is isomorphic to the composite of the functor and the colimit over the costructured arrows associated with that object.

whiskering:   whiskerLeft_id : ∀ {a b c} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c), whiskerLeft f (𝟙 g) = 𝟙 (f ≫ g) := by     aesop_cat   whiskerLeft_comp :     ∀ {a b c} (f : a ⟶ b) {g h i : b ⟶ c} (η : g ⟶ h) (θ : h whiskerLeft f (whiskerLeft g η) ≫ (associator f g h').inv := by     aesop_cat   -- axioms for right whiskering:   id_whiskerRight : ∀ {a b c} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c), whiskerRight (𝟙 f) g = 𝟙 (f ≫ g) := by     aesop_cat   comp_whiskerRight :     ∀ {a b c} {f g h : a ⟶ b} (η : f ⟶ g) (θ : g ⟶ h) (i : b ⟶ c),       whiskerRight (η ≫ θ) i = whiskerRight η i ≫ whiskerRight θ i := by     aesop_cat   whiskerRight_id :     ∀ {a b} {f g : a ⟶ b} (η : f ⟶ g),       whiskerRight η (𝟙 b) = (rightUnitor f).hom ≫ η ≫ (rightUnitor g).inv := by     aesop_cat   whiskerRight_comp :     ∀ {a b c d} {f f' : a ⟶ b} (η : f ⟶ f') (g : b ⟶ c) (h : c ⟶ d),       whiskerRight η (g ≫ h) =         (associator f g h).inv ≫ whiskerRight (whiskerRight η g) h ≫ (associator f' g h).hom := by     aesop_cat   -- associativity of whiskerings:   whisker_assoc :     ∀ {a b c d} (f : a ⟶ b) {g g' : b ⟶ c} (η : g ⟶ g') (h : c ⟶ d),       whiskerRight (whiskerLeft f η) h =         (associator f g h).hom ≫ whiskerLeft f (whiskerRight η h) ≫ (associator f g' h).inv := by     aesop_cat   -- exchange law of left and right whiskerings:   whisker_exchange :     ∀ {a b c} {f g : a ⟶ b} {h i : b ⟶ c} (η : f ⟶ g) (θ : h ⟶ i),       whiskerLeft f θ ≫ whiskerRight η i = whiskerRight η h ≫ whiskerLeft g θ := by     aesop_cat   -- pentagon identity:   pentagon :     ∀ {a b c d e} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) (h : c ⟶ d) (i : d ⟶ e),       whiskerRight (associator f g h).hom i ≫           (associator f (g ≫ h) i).hom ≫ whiskerLeft f (associator g h i).hom =         (associator (f ≫ g) h i).hom ≫ (associator f g (h ≫ i)).hom := by     aesop_cat   -- triangle identity:   triangle :     ∀ {a b c} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c),       (associator f (𝟙 b) g).hom ≫ whiskerLeft f (leftUnitor g).hom       = whiskerRight (rightUnitor f).hom g := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.OplaxFunctor.mapId.fullDefinition: mapId (a : B) : map (𝟙 a) ⟶ 𝟙 (obj a)   mapComp {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) : map (f ≫ g) ⟶ map f ≫ map g   mapComp_naturality_left :     ∀ {a b c : B} {f f' : a ⟶ b} (η : f ⟶ f') (g : b ⟶ c),       map₂ (η ▷ g) ≫ mapComp f' g = mapComp f g ≫ map₂ η ▷ map g := by     aesop_cat   mapComp_naturality_right :     ∀ {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) {g g' : b ⟶ c} (η : g ⟶ g'),       map₂ (f ◁ η) ≫ mapComp f g' = mapComp f g ≫ map f ◁ map₂ η := by     aesop_cat   -- Porting note: `map₂_associator_aux` was used here in lean 3, but this was a hack   -- to avoid a timeout; we revert this hack here (because it was causing other problems   -- and was not necessary in lean 4)   map₂_associator :     ∀ {a b c d : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) (h : c ⟶ d),       map₂ (α_ f g h).hom ≫ mapComp f (g ≫ h) ≫ map f ◁ mapComp g h =     mapComp (f ≫ g) h ≫ mapComp f g ▷ map h ≫ (α_ (map f) (map g) (map h)).hom := by     aesop_cat   map₂_leftUnitor :     ∀ {a b : B} (f : a ⟶ b),       map₂ (λ_ f).hom = mapComp (𝟙 a) f ≫ mapId a ▷ map f ≫ (λ_ (map f)).hom := by     aesop_cat   map₂_rightUnitor :     ∀ {a b : B} (f : a ⟶ b),       map₂ (ρ_ f).hom = mapComp f (𝟙 b) ≫ map f ◁ mapId b ≫ (ρ_ (map f)).hom := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.OplaxFunctor.comp.fullDefinition: def comp (F : OplaxFunctor B C) (G : OplaxFunctor C D) : OplaxFunctor B D where   toPrelaxFunctor := F.toPrelaxFunctor.comp G.toPrelaxFunctor   mapId := fun a => (G.mapFunctor _ _).map (F.mapId a) ≫ G.mapId (F.obj a)   mapComp := fun f g => (G.mapFunctor _ _).map (F.mapComp f g) ≫ G.mapComp (F.map f) (F.map g)   mapComp_naturality_left := fun η g => by     dsimp     rw [← G.map₂_comp_assoc, mapComp_naturality_left, G.map₂_comp_assoc, mapComp_naturality_left,       assoc]   mapComp_naturality_right := fun η => by     dsimp     intros     rw [← G.map₂_comp_assoc, mapComp_naturality_right, G.map₂_comp_assoc,       mapComp_naturality_right, assoc]   map₂_associator := fun f g h => by     dsimp     -- Porting note: if you use the `map₂_associator_aux` hack in the definition of     -- `map₂_associator` then the `simp only` call below does not seem to apply `map₂_associator`     simp only [map₂_associator, ← PrelaxFunctor.map₂_comp_assoc, ← mapComp_naturality_right_assoc,       whiskerLeft_comp, assoc]     simp only [map₂_associator, PrelaxFunctor.map₂_comp, mapComp_naturality_left_assoc,       comp_whiskerRight, assoc]   map₂_leftUnitor := fun f => by     dsimp     simp only [map₂_leftUnitor, PrelaxFunctor.map₂_comp, mapComp_naturality_left_assoc,       comp_whiskerRight, assoc]   map₂_rightUnitor := fun f => by     dsimp     simp only [map₂_rightUnitor, PrelaxFunctor.map₂_comp, mapComp_naturality_right_assoc,       whiskerLeft_comp, assoc]

CategoryTheory.LaxFunctor.mapComp.fullDefinition: mapComp {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) : map f ≫ map g ⟶ map (f ≫ g)   /-- Naturality of the lax functoriality constraight, on the left. -/   mapComp_naturality_left :     ∀ {a b c : B} {f f' : a ⟶ b} (η : f ⟶ f') (g : b ⟶ c),       mapComp f g ≫ map₂ (η ▷ g) = map₂ η ▷ map g ≫ mapComp f' g:= by aesop_cat   /-- Naturality of the lax functoriality constraight, on the right. -/   mapComp_naturality_right :     ∀ {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) {g g' : b ⟶ c} (η : g ⟶ g'),      mapComp f g ≫ map₂ (f ◁ η) = map f ◁ map₂ η ≫ mapComp f g' := by aesop_cat   /-- Lax associativity -/   map₂_associator :     ∀ {a b c d : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) (h : c ⟶ d),       mapComp f g ▷ map h ≫ mapComp (f ≫ g) h ≫ map₂ (α_ f g h).hom =       (α_ (map f) (map g) (map h)).hom ≫ map f ◁ mapComp g h ≫ mapComp f (g ≫ h) := by aesop_cat   /-- Lax left unity -/   map₂_leftUnitor :     ∀ {a b : B} (f : a ⟶ b),       map₂ (λ_ f).inv = (λ_ (map f)).inv ≫ mapId a ▷ map f ≫ mapComp (𝟙 a) f := by aesop_cat   /-- Lax right unity -/   map₂_rightUnitor :     ∀ {a b : B} (f : a ⟶ b),       map₂ (ρ_ f).inv = (ρ_ (map f)).inv ≫ map f ◁ mapId b ≫ mapComp f (𝟙 b) := by aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.mapId.fullDefinition: mapId (a : B) : map (𝟙 a) ≅ 𝟙 (obj a)   mapComp {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) : map (f ≫ g) ≅ map f ≫ map g   map₂_whisker_left :     ∀ {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) {g h : b ⟶ c} (η : g ⟶ h),       map₂ (f ◁ η) = (mapComp f g).hom ≫ map f ◁ map₂ η ≫ (mapComp f h).inv := by     aesop_cat   map₂_whisker_right :     ∀ {a b c : B} {f g : a ⟶ b} (η : f ⟶ g) (h : b ⟶ c),       map₂ (η ▷ h) = (mapComp f h).hom ≫ map₂ η ▷ map h ≫ (mapComp g h).inv := by     aesop_cat   map₂_associator :     ∀ {a b c d : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c) (h : c ⟶ d),       map₂ (α_ f g h).hom = (mapComp (f ≫ g) h).hom ≫ (mapComp f g).hom ▷ map h ≫       (α_ (map f) (map g) (map h)).hom ≫ map f ◁ (mapComp g h).inv ≫       (mapComp f (g ≫ h)).inv := by     aesop_cat   map₂_left_unitor :     ∀ {a b : B} (f : a ⟶ b),       map₂ (λ_ f).hom = (mapComp (𝟙 a) f).hom ≫ (mapId a).hom ▷ map f ≫ (λ_ (map f)).hom := by     aesop_cat   map₂_right_unitor :     ∀ {a b : B} (f : a ⟶ b),       map₂ (ρ_ f).hom = (mapComp f (𝟙 b)).hom ≫ map f ◁ (mapId b).hom ≫ (ρ_ (map f)).hom := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.Pseudofunctor.comp.fullDefinition: def comp (F : Pseudofunctor B C) (G : Pseudofunctor C D) : Pseudofunctor B D where   toPrelaxFunctor := F.toPrelaxFunctor.comp G.toPrelaxFunctor   mapId := fun a => G.map₂Iso (F.mapId a) ≪≫ G.mapId (F.obj a)   mapComp := fun f g => (G.map₂Iso (F.mapComp f g)) ≪≫ G.mapComp (F.map f) (F.map g)   -- Note: whilst these are all provable by `aesop_cat`, the proof is very slow   map₂_whisker_left f η := by dsimp; simp   map₂_whisker_right η h := by dsimp; simp   map₂_associator f g h := by dsimp; simp   map₂_left_unitor f := by dsimp; simp   map₂_right_unitor f := by dsimp; simp

CategoryTheory.OplaxNatTrans.app.fullDefinition: app (a : B) : F.obj a ⟶ G.obj a   naturality {a b : B} (f : a ⟶ b) : F.map f ≫ app b ⟶ app a ≫ G.map f   naturality_naturality :     ∀ {a b : B} {f g : a ⟶ b} (η : f ⟶ g),       F.map₂ η ▷ app b ≫ naturality g = naturality f ≫ app a ◁ G.map₂ η := by     aesop_cat   naturality_id :     ∀ a : B,       naturality (𝟙 a) ≫ app a ◁ G.mapId a =         F.mapId a ▷ app a ≫ (λ_ (app a)).hom ≫ (ρ_ (app a)).inv := by     aesop_cat   naturality_comp :     ∀ {a b c : B} (f : a ⟶ b) (g : b ⟶ c),       naturality (f ≫ g) ≫ app a ◁ G.mapComp f g =         F.mapComp f g ▷ app c ≫           (α_ _ _ _).hom ≫             F.map f ◁ naturality g ≫ (α_ _ _ _).inv ≫ naturality f ▷ G.map g ≫ (α_ _ _ _).hom := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.bicategory.fullDefinition: instance bicategory : Bicategory (FreeBicategory B) where   homCategory := @fun (a b : B) => FreeBicategory.homCategory a b   whiskerLeft := @fun a b c f g h η => Quot.map (Hom₂.whisker_left f) (Rel.whisker_left f g h) η   whiskerLeft_id := @fun a b c f g => Quot.sound (Rel.whisker_left_id f g)   associator := @fun a b c d f g h =>     { hom := Quot.mk Rel (Hom₂.associator f g h)       inv := Quot.mk Rel (Hom₂.associator_inv f g h)       hom_inv_id := Quot.sound (Rel.associator_hom_inv f g h)       inv_hom_id := Quot.sound (Rel.associator_inv_hom f g h) }   leftUnitor := @fun a b f =>     { hom := Quot.mk Rel (Hom₂.left_unitor f)       inv := Quot.mk Rel (Hom₂.left_unitor_inv f)       hom_inv_id := Quot.sound (Rel.left_unitor_hom_inv f)       inv_hom_id := Quot.sound (Rel.left_unitor_inv_hom f) }   rightUnitor := @fun a b f =>     { hom := Quot.mk Rel (Hom₂.right_unitor f)       inv := Quot.mk Rel (Hom₂.right_unitor_inv f)       hom_inv_id := Quot.sound (Rel.right_unitor_hom_inv f)       inv_hom_id := Quot.sound (Rel.right_unitor_inv_hom f) }   whiskerLeft_comp := by     rintro a b c f g h i ⟨η⟩ ⟨θ⟩     exact Quot.sound (Rel.whisker_left_comp f η θ)   id_whiskerLeft := by     rintro a b f g ⟨η⟩     exact Quot.sound (Rel.id_whisker_left η)   comp_whiskerLeft := by     rintro a b c d f g h h' ⟨η⟩     exact Quot.sound (Rel.comp_whisker_left f g η)   whiskerRight := @fun a b c f g η h => Quot.map (Hom₂.whisker_right h) (Rel.whisker_right f g h) η   id_whiskerRight := @fun a b c f g => Quot.sound (Rel.id_whisker_right f g)   comp_whiskerRight := by     rintro a b c f g h ⟨η⟩ ⟨θ⟩ i     exact Quot.sound (Rel.comp_whisker_right i η θ)   whiskerRight_id := by     rintro a b f g ⟨η⟩     exact Quot.sound (Rel.whisker_right_id η)   whiskerRight_comp := by     rintro a b c d f f' ⟨η⟩ g h     exact Quot.sound (Rel.whisker_right_comp g h η)   whisker_assoc := by     rintro a b c d f g g' ⟨η⟩ h     exact Quot.sound (Rel.whisker_assoc f η h)   whisker_exchange := by     rintro a b c f g h i ⟨η⟩ ⟨θ⟩     exact Quot.sound (Rel.whisker_exchange η θ)   pentagon := @fun a b c d e f g h i => Quot.sound (Rel.pentagon f g h i)   triangle := @fun a b c f g => Quot.sound (Rel.triangle f g)

CategoryTheory.locallyDiscreteBicategory.code: CategoryTheory.locallyDiscreteBicategory.{v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : Bicategory (LocallyDiscrete C)
CategoryTheory.locallyDiscreteBicategory.comment:
The locally discrete bicategory on a category is a bicategory in which the objects and the
1-morphisms are the same as those in the underlying category, and the 2-morphisms are the
equalities between 1-morphisms.

explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.LocallyDiscrete.eq_of_hom: This theorem states that in a locally discrete 2-category, any two morphisms between objects are equal if they are equal as 2-morphisms.

CategoryTheory.locallyDiscreteBicategory.fullDefinition: instance locallyDiscreteBicategory : Bicategory (LocallyDiscrete C) where   whiskerLeft f g h η := eqToHom (congr_arg₂ (· ≫ ·) rfl (LocallyDiscrete.eq_of_hom η))   whiskerRight η h := eqToHom (congr_arg₂ (· ≫ ·) (LocallyDiscrete.eq_of_hom η) rfl)   associator f g h := eqToIso <| by apply Discrete.ext; simp   leftUnitor f := eqToIso <| by apply Discrete.ext; simp   rightUnitor f := eqToIso <| by apply Discrete.ext; simp
CategoryTheory.locallyDiscreteBicategory.description: This definition establishes a bicategory that retains the objects and 1-morphisms of a given category, while its 2-morphisms are restricted to the equalities between those 1-morphisms.

CategoryTheory.locallyDiscreteBicategory.fullDefinition: instance locallyDiscreteBicategory.strict : Strict (LocallyDiscrete C) where   id_comp f := Discrete.ext _ _ (Category.id_comp _)   comp_id f := Discrete.ext _ _ (Category.comp_id _)   assoc f g h := Discrete.ext _ _ (Category.assoc _ _ _)
CategoryTheory.locallyDiscreteBicategory.description: This definition establishes that a locally discrete bicategory is characterized as being strict.

CategoryTheory.Functor.toOplaxFunctor.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.toOplaxFunctor.{w₂, v₂, v₁, u₂, u₁} {I : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} I] {B : Type u₂}

CategoryTheory.Functor.toOplaxFunctor.comment:
If `B` is a strict bicategory and `I` is a (1-)category, any functor (of 1-categories) `I ⥤ B` can

CategoryTheory.Functor.toOplaxFunctor.fullDefinition: def Functor.toOplaxFunctor (F : I ⥤ B) : OplaxFunctor (LocallyDiscrete I) B where   obj i := F.obj i.as   map f := F.map f.as   map₂ η := eqToHom (congr_arg _ (LocallyDiscrete.eq_of_hom η))   mapId i := eqToHom (F.map_id i.as)   mapComp f g := eqToHom (F.map_comp f.as g.as)
CategoryTheory.Functor.toOplaxFunctor.description: This definition describes how any functor from a one-category to a strict bicategory can be transformed into an oplax functor from a locally discrete category to that bicategory.

CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.inclusionP.fullDefinition: def inclusionPathAux {a : B} : ∀ {b : B}, Path a b → Hom a b   | _, nil => Hom.id a   | _, cons p f => (inclusionPathAux p).comp (Hom.of f)
CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.inclusionP.description: This definition describes a function that converts a path in a directed structure into a corresponding morphism between two elements of that structure.

CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.inclusionP.code: CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.inclusionPath.{v, u} {B : Type u} [Quiver B] (a b : B) : Discrete (Path a b) ⥤ Hom a b

The discrete category on the paths includes into the category of 1-morphisms in the free
bicategory.
CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.inclusionP.fullDefinition: def inclusionPath (a b : B) : Discrete (Path.{v + 1} a b) ⥤ Hom a b :=   Discrete.functor inclusionPathAux
CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.inclusionP.description: This definition specifies a functor that maps paths in a directed structure, considered in a discrete category, to morphisms between two corresponding elements of that structure in a free bicategory.

CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.preinclusi.code:
CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.preinclusion.{v, u} (B : Type u) [Quiver B] :
  PrelaxFunctor (LocallyDiscrete (Paths B)) (FreeBicategory B)
CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.preinclusi.comment:
The inclusion from the locally discrete bicategory on the path category into the free bicategory
as a prelax functor. This will be promoted to a pseudofunctor after proving the coherence theorem.
See `inclusion`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.inclusionP: This definition specifies a functor that maps paths in a directed structure, considered in a discrete category, to morphisms between two corresponding elements of that structure in a free bicategory.

CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.preinclusi.fullDefinition: def preinclusion (B : Type u) [Quiver.{v + 1} B] :     PrelaxFunctor (LocallyDiscrete (Paths B)) (FreeBicategory B) where   obj a := a.as   map := @fun a b f => (@inclusionPath B _ a.as b.as).obj f   map₂ η := (inclusionPath _ _).map η
CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.preinclusi.description: This definition establishes a prelax functor that inclusively associates the locally discrete bicategory of paths in a directed structure with the free bicategory formed from that structure.

CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.normalizeA.code: CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.normalizeAux.{v, u} {B : Type u} [Quiver B] {a b c : B} : Path a b → Hom b c → Path a c
CategoryTheory.FreeBicategory.normalizeA.comment:
The normalization of the composition of `p : Path a b` and `f : Hom b c`.
`p` will eventually be taken to be `nil` and we then get the normalization
of `f` alone, but the auxiliary `p` is necessary for Lean to accept the definition of
`normalizeIso` and the `whisker_left` case of `normalizeAux_congr` and `normalize_naturality`.

CategoryTheory.Bicategory.leftZigzag.{w, v, u} {B : Type u} [Bicategory B] {a b : B} {f : a ⟶ b} {g : b ⟶ a}

CategoryTheory.Bicategory.leftZigzag.comment:
The 2-morphism defined by the following pasting diagram:
```
a －－－－－－ ▸ a
  ＼    η      ◥   ＼
  f ＼   g  ／       ＼ f
       ◢  ／     ε      ◢
        b －－－－－－ ▸ b
```
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.leftZigzag.fullDefinition: def leftZigzag (η : 𝟙 a ⟶ f ≫ g) (ε : g ≫ f ⟶ 𝟙 b) :=   η ▷ f ⊗≫ f ◁ ε

CategoryTheory.Bicategory.rightZigzag.comment:
The 2-morphism defined by the following pasting diagram:
```
        a －－－－－－ ▸ a
       ◥  ＼     η      ◥
  g ／      ＼ f     ／ g
  ／    ε      ◢   ／
b －－－－－－ ▸ b
```
CategoryTheory.Bicategory.rightZigzag.fullDefinition: def rightZigzag (η : 𝟙 a ⟶ f ≫ g) (ε : g ≫ f ⟶ 𝟙 b) :=   g ◁ η ⊗≫ ε ▷ g

CategoryTheory.Bicategory.LeftExtension..fullDefinition: def LeftExtension.IsKan.adjunction {f : a ⟶ b} {t : LeftExtension f (𝟙 a)}     (H : IsKan t) (H' : IsKan (t.whisker f)) :       f ⊣ t.extension :=   let ε : t.extension ≫ f ⟶ 𝟙 b := H'.desc <| .mk _ <| (λ_ f).hom ≫ (ρ_ f).inv   have Hε : leftZigzag t.unit ε = (λ_ f).hom ≫ (ρ_ f).inv := by     simpa [leftZigzag, bicategoricalComp] using H'.fac <| .mk _ <| (λ_ f).hom ≫ (ρ_ f).inv   { unit := t.unit     counit := ε     left_triangle := Hε     right_triangle := by       apply (cancel_epi (ρ_ _).inv).mp       apply H.hom_ext       calc _         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ t.unit ⊗≫ f ◁ rightZigzag t.unit ε ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (t.unit ▷ _ ≫ _ ◁ t.unit) ⊗≫ f ◁ ε ▷ t.extension ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           rw [rightZigzag]; simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ t.unit ⊗≫ (t.unit ▷ f ⊗≫ f ◁ ε) ▷ t.extension ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           rw [← whisker_exchange]; simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = _ := by           rw [← leftZigzag, Hε]; simp [bicategoricalComp] }

CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Adjunction.isA.fullDefinition: def Adjunction.isAbsoluteLeftKan {f : a ⟶ b} {u : b ⟶ a} (adj : f ⊣ u) :     IsAbsKan (.mk u adj.unit) := fun {x} h ↦   .mk (fun s  ↦ LeftExtension.homMk     (𝟙 _ ⊗≫ u ◁ s.unit ⊗≫ adj.counit ▷ s.extension ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ : u ≫ h ⟶ s.extension) <|       calc _         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (adj.unit ▷ _ ≫ _ ◁ s.unit) ⊗≫ f ◁ adj.counit ▷ s.extension ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ s.unit ⊗≫ leftZigzag adj.unit adj.counit ▷ s.extension ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           rw [← whisker_exchange, leftZigzag]; simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = s.unit := by           rw [adj.left_triangle]; simp [bicategoricalComp]) <| by     intro s τ₀     ext     /- We need to specify the type of `τ` to use the notation `⊗≫`. -/     let τ : u ≫ h ⟶ s.extension := τ₀.right     have hτ : adj.unit ▷ h ⊗≫ f ◁ τ = s.unit := by       simpa [bicategoricalComp] using LeftExtension.w τ₀     calc τ       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ rightZigzag adj.unit adj.counit ▷ h ⊗≫ τ ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [adj.right_triangle]; simp [bicategoricalComp]       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ u ◁ adj.unit ▷ h ⊗≫ (adj.counit ▷ _ ≫ _ ◁ τ) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [rightZigzag]; simp [bicategoricalComp]       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ u ◁ (adj.unit ▷ h ⊗≫ f ◁ τ) ⊗≫ adj.counit ▷ s.extension ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [← whisker_exchange]; simp [bicategoricalComp]       _ = _ := by         rw [hτ]; simp [bicategoricalComp]

CategoryTheory.Bicategory.Adjunction.isA.fullDefinition: def Adjunction.isAbsoluteLeftKanLift {f : a ⟶ b} {u : b ⟶ a} (adj : f ⊣ u) :     IsAbsKan (.mk f adj.unit) := fun {x} h ↦   .mk (fun s ↦ LeftLift.homMk     (𝟙 _ ⊗≫ s.unit ▷ f ⊗≫ s.lift ◁ adj.counit ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ : h ≫ f ⟶ s.lift) <|       calc _       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (_ ◁ adj.unit ≫ s.unit ▷ _) ⊗≫ s.lift ◁ adj.counit ▷ u ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         simp [bicategoricalComp]       _ = s.unit ⊗≫ s.lift ◁ (rightZigzag adj.unit adj.counit) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [whisker_exchange, rightZigzag]; simp [bicategoricalComp]       _ = s.unit := by         rw [adj.right_triangle]; simp [bicategoricalComp]) <| by       intro s τ₀       ext       /- We need to specify the type of `τ` to use the notation `⊗≫`. -/       let τ : h ≫ f ⟶ s.lift := τ₀.right       have hτ : h ◁ adj.unit ⊗≫ τ ▷ u = s.unit := by simpa [bicategoricalComp] using LeftLift.w τ₀       calc τ         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ h ◁ leftZigzag adj.unit adj.counit ⊗≫ τ ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           rw [adj.left_triangle]; simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ h ◁ adj.unit ▷ f ⊗≫ (_ ◁ adj.counit ≫ τ ▷ _) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           rw [leftZigzag]; simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (h ◁ adj.unit ⊗≫ τ ▷ u) ▷ f ⊗≫ s.lift ◁ adj.counit ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           rw [whisker_exchange]; simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = _ := by           rw [hτ]; simp [bicategoricalComp]

CategoryTheory.Bicategory.LeftExtension..fullDefinition: def isKanOfWhiskerLeftAdjoint     {f : a ⟶ b} {g : a ⟶ c} {t : LeftExtension f g} (H : LeftExtension.IsKan t)       {x : B} {h : c ⟶ x} {u : x ⟶ c} (adj : h ⊣ u) :         LeftExtension.IsKan (t.whisker h) :=   let η' := adj.unit   let H' : LeftLift.IsAbsKan (.mk _ η') := adj.isAbsoluteLeftKanLift   .mk (fun s ↦     let k := s.extension     let θ := s.unit     let τ : t.extension ⟶ k ≫ u := H.desc (.mk _ <| 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ g ◁ η' ⊗≫ θ ▷ u ⊗≫ 𝟙 _)     let σ : t.extension ≫ h ⟶ k := H'.desc <| (.mk _ <| (ρ_ _).hom ≫ τ)     LeftExtension.homMk σ <| (H' g).hom_ext <| by       have Hσ : t.extension ◁ η' ⊗≫ σ ▷ u  = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ τ := by         simpa [bicategoricalComp] using (H' _).fac (.mk _ <| (ρ_ _).hom ≫ τ)       calc _         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (g ◁ η' ≫ t.unit ▷ (h ≫ u)) ⊗≫ f ◁ σ ▷ u ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ t.unit ▷ (𝟙 c) ⊗≫ f ◁ (t.extension ◁ η' ⊗≫ σ ▷ u) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by           rw [whisker_exchange]; simp [bicategoricalComp]         _ = _ := by           rw [Hσ]; simp [τ, bicategoricalComp]) <| by     intro s' τ₀'     let τ' : t.extension ≫ h ⟶ s'.extension := τ₀'.right     have Hτ' : t.unit ▷ h ⊗≫ f ◁ τ' = s'.unit := by simpa [bicategoricalComp] using τ₀'.w.symm     ext     apply (H' _).hom_ext     dsimp only [StructuredArrow.homMk_right]     rw [(H' _).fac]     apply (cancel_epi (ρ_ _).inv).mp     apply H.hom_ext     calc _       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (t.unit ▷ (𝟙 c) ≫ (f ≫ t.extension) ◁ η') ⊗≫ f ◁ τ' ▷ u := by         simp [bicategoricalComp]       _ = 𝟙 g ⊗≫ g ◁ η' ⊗≫ (t.unit ▷ h ⊗≫ f ◁ τ') ▷ u ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [← whisker_exchange]; simp [bicategoricalComp]       _ = _ := by         rw [Hτ']; simp [bicategoricalComp]

CategoryTheory.whiskerLeft.comment:

CategoryTheory.whiskeringLeft.comment:

CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.comment:
The essential image of a functor `F` consists of those objects in the target category which are
isomorphic to an object in the image of the function `F.obj`. In other words, this is the closure
under isomorphism of the function `F.obj`.
This is the "non-evil" way of describing the image of a functor.
CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.fullDefinition: def essImage (F : C ⥤ D) : Set D := fun Y => ∃ X : C, Nonempty (F.obj X ≅ Y)
CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.description: There is no mathematical or logical content to summarize since no definition or theorem is provided.

CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.ofIso.comment: Being in the essential image is a "hygienic" property: it is preserved under isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.ofNatIso.comment:

`F ≅ F'`.
CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.ofNatIso.description: If an object is in the essential image of one functor, it remains in the essential image of another functor that is isomorphic to the first.

CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage_eq_of_na.comment: Isomorphic functors have equal essential images.

CategoryTheory.Sigma.desc.comment:
Given a collection of functors `F i : C i ⥤ D`, we can produce a functor `(Σ i, C i) ⥤ D`.

The produced functor `desc F` satisfies: `incl i ⋙ desc F ≅ F i`, i.e. restricted to just the
subcategory `C i`, `desc F` agrees with `F i`, and it is unique (up to natural isomorphism) with
this property.

This witnesses that the sigma-type is the coproduct in Cat.

CategoryTheory.AsSmall.comment:
`AsSmall C` is a small category equivalent to `C`.
More specifically, if `C : Type u` is endowed with `Category.{v} C`, then
`AsSmall.{w} C : Type (max w v u)` is endowed with an instance of a small category.

The objects and morphisms of `AsSmall C` are defined by applying `ULift` to the
objects and morphisms of `C`.

Note: We require a category instance for this definition in order to have direct
access to the universe level `v`.
CategoryTheory.AsSmall.fullDefinition: def AsSmall.{w, v, u} (D : Type u) [Category.{v} D] := ULift.{max w v} D

Preorder.smallCategory.comment:
The category structure coming from a preorder. There is a morphism `X ⟶ Y` if and only if `X ≤ Y`.

Because we don't allow morphisms to live in `Prop`,
we have to define `X ⟶ Y` as `ULift (PLift (X ≤ Y))`.
See `CategoryTheory.homOfLE` and `CategoryTheory.leOfHom`.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00D3>.

partialFunEquivPointed.fullDefinition: noncomputable def partialFunEquivPointed : PartialFun.{u} ≌ Pointed :=   CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk partialFunToPointed pointedToPartialFun     (NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => PartialFun.Iso.mk       { toFun := fun a => ⟨some a, some_ne_none a⟩         invFun := fun a => Option.get _ (Option.ne_none_iff_isSome.1 a.2)         left_inv := fun a => Option.get_some _ _         right_inv := fun a => by simp only [some_get, Subtype.coe_eta] })       fun f =>         PFun.ext fun a b => by           dsimp [PartialFun.Iso.mk, CategoryStruct.comp, pointedToPartialFun]           rw [Part.bind_some]           -- Porting note: the proof below has changed a lot because           -- `Part.mem_bind_iff` means that `b ∈ Part.bind f g` is equivalent           -- to `∃ (a : α), a ∈ f ∧ b ∈ g a`, while in mathlib3 it was equivalent           -- to `∃ (a : α) (H : a ∈ f), b ∈ g a`           refine (Part.mem_bind_iff.trans ?_).trans PFun.mem_toSubtype_iff.symm           obtain ⟨b | b, hb⟩ := b           · exact (hb rfl).elim           · dsimp [Part.toOption]             simp_rw [Part.mem_some_iff, Subtype.mk_eq_mk]             constructor             · rintro ⟨_, ⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h₃⟩               rw [h₃, ← h₂, dif_pos h₁]             · intro h               split_ifs at h with ha               rw [some_inj] at h               exact ⟨b, ⟨ha, h.symm⟩, rfl⟩) $     NatIso.ofComponents       (fun X ↦ Pointed.Iso.mk (by classical exact Equiv.optionSubtypeNe X.point) (by rfl))       fun {X Y} f ↦ Pointed.Hom.ext _ _ <| funext fun a ↦ by         obtain _ | ⟨a, ha⟩ := a         · exact f.map_point.symm         simp_all [Option.casesOn'_eq_elim, Part.elim_toOption]

CategoryTheory.Grpd.objects.comment:
Functor that gets the set of objects of a groupoid. It is not
called `forget`, because it is not a faithful functor.
CategoryTheory.Grpd.objects.fullDefinition: def objects : Grpd.{v, u} ⥤ Type u where   obj := Bundled.α   map F := F.obj set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.objects.description: This definition describes a functor that extracts the set of objects from a groupoid, distinguishing it from a faithful functor by not fully retaining the morphism structure.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Grpd.of: This definition constructs a bundled groupoid from a given type and an associated groupoid structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.id: The identity functor on a category maps each object and morphism to itself, preserving their structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Cat: This definition establishes a type that represents the category of all categories, providing a framework to study their relationships and structures.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Cat.of: This definition creates a bundled category from a given type and its associated category structure.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.forgetToCat.fullDefinition: def forgetToCat : Grpd.{v, u} ⥤ Cat.{v, u} where   obj C := Cat.of C   map := id set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.forgetToCat.description: This definition describes a functor that maps groupoidal structures to their corresponding categorical structures by forgetting the groupoidal properties.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.forgetToCat_full.fullDefinition: instance forgetToCat_full : forgetToCat.Full where map_surjective f := ⟨f, rfl⟩ set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.forgetToCat_full.description: This definition indicates a full functorial relationship that allows for a complete transformation from groupoids to categories, emphasizing the preservation of structural properties.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.forgetToCat_faithful.fullDefinition: instance forgetToCat_faithful : forgetToCat.Faithful where set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.forgetToCat_faithful.description: This definition asserts that the functor which forgets the structure of a groupoid and treats it merely as a category is faithful, meaning that it distinguishes between different morphisms in the groupoid.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.hom_to_functor.code: CategoryTheory.Grpd.hom_to_functor.{v, u} {C D E : Grpd} (f : C ⟶ D) (g : D ⟶ E) : f ≫ g = f ⋙ g
CategoryTheory.Grpd.hom_to_functor.comment:
Convert arrows in the category of groupoids to functors,
which sometimes helps in applying simp lemmas
CategoryTheory.Grpd.hom_to_functor.description: This theorem shows that the composition of morphisms in the category of groupoids corresponds to the composition of functors.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.id_to_functor.comment: Converts identity in the category of groupoids to the functor identity
CategoryTheory.Grpd.id_to_functor.description: This theorem states that the identity morphism in the category of groupoids corresponds to the identity functor associated with a given groupoid.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fan.mk: This definition constructs a fan by specifying an object and a collection of morphisms from that object to each of the images under a given function in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eval: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.piLimitFan.fullDefinition: def piLimitFan ⦃J : Type u⦄ (F : J → Grpd.{u, u}) : Limits.Fan F :=   Limits.Fan.mk (@of (∀ j : J, F j) _) fun j => CategoryTheory.Pi.eval _ j set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.piLimitFan.description: This definition constructs a fan that represents the product of an indexed family of groupoids.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.piLimitFanIsLimit.code: CategoryTheory.Grpd.piLimitFanIsLimit.{u} ⦃J : Type u⦄ (F : J → Grpd) : Limits.IsLimit (piLimitFan F)
CategoryTheory.Grpd.piLimitFanIsLimit.comment: The product fan over an indexed family of groupoids, is a limit cone.

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Grpd.hom_to_functor: This theorem shows that the composition of morphisms in the category of groupoids corresponds to the composition of functors.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.mkFanLimit: This definition constructs a limit fan by specifying a lifting morphism, a factorization condition, and a uniqueness property for morphisms, thus streamlining the process of defining a limit for a given fan.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.pi': This definition describes a functor that maps between a single category and an indexed family of categories using functors from that single category to each category in the family.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fan.proj: This definition retrieves the morphism from the specified object in a fan to the image associated with a particular index in the family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.pi_ext: This theorem states that two functors from a single category to a product category are equal if they produce the same result when composed with functors that evaluate at every index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.functor: This definition asserts that any function mapping from a discrete type to a category yields a functor between the discrete category and that category.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.piLimitFanIsLimit.fullDefinition: def piLimitFanIsLimit ⦃J : Type u⦄ (F : J → Grpd.{u, u}) : Limits.IsLimit (piLimitFan F) :=   Limits.mkFanLimit (piLimitFan F) (fun s => Functor.pi' fun j => s.proj j)     (by       intros       dsimp only [piLimitFan]       simp [hom_to_functor])     (by       intro s m w       apply Functor.pi_ext       intro j; specialize w j       simpa) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.piLimitFanIsLimit.description: This definition asserts that the product fan formed from an indexed collection of groupoids serves as a limit cone in the context of category theory.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.hasProducts_of_lim: This theorem states that if a category has a limit for each functor indexed by a type, then it possesses products for all objects in that category.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.has_pi.fullDefinition: instance has_pi : Limits.HasProducts.{u} Grpd.{u, u} :=   Limits.hasProducts_of_limit_fans (by apply piLimitFan) (by apply piLimitFanIsLimit) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.has_pi.description: This definition asserts that the category of groupoids possesses products, indicating that it can handle Cartesian products of objects within that category.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.piIsoPi.fullDefinition: noncomputable def piIsoPi (J : Type u) (f : J → Grpd.{u, u}) : @of (∀ j, f j) _ ≅ ∏ᶜ f :=   Limits.IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso (piLimitFanIsLimit f)     (Limits.limit.isLimit (Discrete.functor f)) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Grpd.piIsoPi.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the product of a family of groupoids and the product object in the category of groupoids.

CategoryTheory.Grpd.piIsoPi_hom_π.code:
CategoryTheory.Grpd.piIsoPi_hom_π.{u} (J : Type u) (f : J → Grpd) (j : J) :

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (self : Equivalence C D) : 𝟭 C ≅ self.functor ⋙ self.inverse
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso.comment: The composition `functor ⋙ inverse` is isomorphic to the identity
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso.fullDefinition: unitIso : 𝟭 C ≅ functor ⋙ inverse   /-- The composition `inverse ⋙ functor` is also isomorphic to the identity -/   counitIso : inverse ⋙ functor ≅ 𝟭 D   /-- The natural isomorphisms compose to the identity. -/   functor_unitIso_comp :     ∀ X : C, functor.map (unitIso.hom.app X) ≫ counitIso.hom.app (functor.obj X) =       𝟙 (functor.obj X) := by aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso.description: This definition states that a specific functor composition related to an equivalence between categories is isomorphic to the identity functor of the first category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitIso.comment: The composition `inverse ⋙ functor` is also isomorphic to the identity

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso: This definition states that a specific functor composition related to an equivalence between categories is isomorphic to the identity functor of the first category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitIso.fullDefinition: counitIso : inverse ⋙ functor ≅ 𝟭 D   /-- The natural isomorphisms compose to the identity. -/   functor_unitIso_comp :     ∀ X : C, functor.map (unitIso.hom.app X) ≫ counitIso.hom.app (functor.obj X) =       𝟙 (functor.obj X) := by aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitIso.description: This definition describes that the composition of a functor and its inverse related to an equivalence between categories is isomorphic to the identity functor of the second category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor_unitI.code:

  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (self : Equivalence C D) (X : C) :

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor_unitI.comment: The natural isomorphisms compose to the identity.
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor_unitI.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of specific natural isomorphisms, associated with an equivalence of categories, results in the identity morphism of the functor's image.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unit: This definition describes the unit morphism of an equivalence between two categories, relating the identity functor of the first category to the composition of the equivalence's functor and its inverse.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counit: This definition describes the counit morphism of an equivalence between two categories, relating the composition of the equivalence's inverse and functor to the identity functor of the second category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.Equivalence_m.description: This theorem asserts that the counit morphism of an equivalence between two categories is equal to a specific natural isomorphism linking the composition of the functor and its inverse with the identity functor of the second category, under certain conditions.

        functor_unitIso_comp := f }.unitInv =
    unit_iso.inv

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.Equivalence_m.description: This theorem shows that under certain conditions related to a functor and its inverse, the counit of the equivalence is equal to the inverse of the counit isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor_unit_.description: This theorem establishes that applying the functor of an equivalence to the unit morphism and then applying the counit yields the identity morphism on the image of that functor in the target category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitInv_fun.description: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of a specific natural transformation and the application of a functor related to an equivalence of categories yields the identity morphism for the functor's image.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitInv_app.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitInv_app_functor.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) (X : C) : e.counitInv.app (e.functor.obj X) = e.functor.map (e.unit.app X)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitInv_app.description: This theorem demonstrates that the application of the counit of an equivalence between two categories gives a morphism that matches the mapping of an object through the functor applied to the unit of the equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counit_app_fu.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counit_app_functor.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) (X : C) : e.counit.app (e.functor.obj X) = e.functor.map (e.unitInv.app X)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counit_app_fu.description: This theorem shows that the counit of an equivalence applied to the image of an object under a functor equals the result of applying the functor to the unit's inverse applied to that object.

The other triangle equality. The proof follows the following proof in Globular:
http://globular.science/1905.001
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unit_inverse_.description: This theorem establishes a triangle equality involving the unit and counit of an equivalence between two categories, ensuring that the composition yields the identity morphism on the object mapped by the inverse functor.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.inverse_couni.description: This theorem demonstrates that applying the inverse functor to a counit morphism and then composing it with the corresponding unit morphism yields the identity morphism on the object mapped by the inverse functor in the equivalence of categories.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unit_app_inve.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unit_app_inverse.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) (Y : D) : e.unit.app (e.inverse.obj Y) = e.inverse.map (e.counitInv.app Y)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unit_app_inve.description: This theorem asserts that for an equivalence between two categories, the application of the unit morphism to an object transformed by the inverse functor equals the transformation of the counit's inverse applied to that object.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitInv_app_i.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitInv_app_inverse.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) (Y : D) : e.unitInv.app (e.inverse.obj Y) = e.inverse.map (e.counit.app Y)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitInv_app_i.description: This theorem states that applying the unit's inverse to the image of an object under the inverse functor is equivalent to applying the inverse functor to the counit applied to that object in the equivalence of categories.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fun_inv_map.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between the mapping of a morphism through the functor of an equivalence and the composition of the counit and its inverse, illustrating how these transformations interact within the structure of the categories involved.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.inv_fun_map.description: This theorem expresses that the mapping of a morphism through the functor related to an equivalence of categories can be decomposed into a composition involving the unit and counit of that equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.adjointifyη.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.adjointifyη.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (η : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G) (ε : G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟭 D) : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.adjointifyη.comment:
If `η : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G` is part of a (not necessarily half-adjoint) equivalence, we can upgrade it
to a refined natural isomorphism `adjointifyη η : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G` which exhibits the properties
required for a half-adjoint equivalence. See `Equivalence.mk`.

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.adjointifyη.fullDefinition: def adjointifyη : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G := by   calc     𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G := η     _ ≅ F ⋙ 𝟭 D ⋙ G := isoWhiskerLeft F (leftUnitor G).symm     _ ≅ F ⋙ (G ⋙ F) ⋙ G := isoWhiskerLeft F (isoWhiskerRight ε.symm G)     _ ≅ F ⋙ G ⋙ F ⋙ G := isoWhiskerLeft F (associator G F G)     _ ≅ (F ⋙ G) ⋙ F ⋙ G := (associator F G (F ⋙ G)).symm     _ ≅ 𝟭 C ⋙ F ⋙ G := isoWhiskerRight η.symm (F ⋙ G)     _ ≅ F ⋙ G := leftUnitor (F ⋙ G)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.adjointifyη.description: This definition enhances a natural isomorphism between the identity functor and the composition of two functors into a refined natural isomorphism that satisfies the properties necessary for a half-adjoint equivalence.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.adjointifyη: This definition enhances a natural isomorphism between the identity functor and the composition of two functors into a refined natural isomorphism that satisfies the properties necessary for a half-adjoint equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.adjointify_η_.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of a morphism derived from the adjunction and the counit morphism equals the identity morphism on the image of an object under a functor in the first category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ C) (η : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G) (ε : G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟭 D) : C ≌ D
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk.comment:
Every equivalence of categories consisting of functors `F` and `G` such that `F ⋙ G` and
`G ⋙ F` are naturally isomorphic to identity functors can be transformed into a half-adjoint
equivalence without changing `F` or `G`.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk.fullDefinition: protected def mk (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ C) (η : 𝟭 C ≅ F ⋙ G) (ε : G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟭 D) : C ≌ D :=   ⟨F, G, adjointifyη η ε, ε, adjointify_η_ε η ε⟩
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mk.description: This definition establishes that an equivalence between two categories can be constructed from two functors and natural isomorphisms that relate their compositions to the identity functors of each category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.refl.description: This definition asserts that any category is equivalente to itself, demonstrating the reflexivity of category equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.trans.fullDefinition: def trans (e : C ≌ D) (f : D ≌ E) : C ≌ E where   functor := e.functor ⋙ f.functor   inverse := f.inverse ⋙ e.inverse   unitIso := by     refine Iso.trans e.unitIso ?_     exact isoWhiskerLeft e.functor (isoWhiskerRight f.unitIso e.inverse)   counitIso := by     refine Iso.trans ?_ f.counitIso     exact isoWhiskerLeft f.inverse (isoWhiskerRight e.counitIso f.functor)   -- We wouldn't have needed to give this proof if we'd used `Equivalence.mk`,   -- but we choose to avoid using that here, for the sake of good structure projection `simp`   -- lemmas.   functor_unitIso_comp X := by     dsimp     rw [← f.functor.map_comp_assoc, e.functor.map_comp, ← counitInv_app_functor, fun_inv_map,       Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc, assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id_app, counit_app_functor, ← Functor.map_comp]     erw [comp_id, Iso.hom_inv_id_app, Functor.map_id]
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.trans.description: This definition asserts that the equivalence between categories is transitive, meaning if one category is equivalent to a second, and that second category is equivalent to a third, then the first category is also equivalent to the third.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.funInvIdAssoc.fullDefinition: def funInvIdAssoc (e : C ≌ D) (F : C ⥤ E) : e.functor ⋙ e.inverse ⋙ F ≅ F :=   (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight e.unitIso.symm F ≪≫ F.leftUnitor
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.funInvIdAssoc.description: This definition states that the composition of a functor with both the functor and its inverse from an equivalence of categories results in a functor that is naturally isomorphic to the original functor.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.congrLeft.fullDefinition: def congrLeft (e : C ≌ D) : C ⥤ E ≌ D ⥤ E :=   Equivalence.mk ((whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj e.inverse) ((whiskeringLeft _ _ _).obj e.functor)     (NatIso.ofComponents fun F => (e.funInvIdAssoc F).symm)     (NatIso.ofComponents fun F => e.invFunIdAssoc F)
