CategoryTheory.Equivalence.congrRight.fullDefinition: def congrRight (e : C ≌ D) : E ⥤ C ≌ E ⥤ D :=   Equivalence.mk ((whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj e.functor) ((whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj e.inverse)     (NatIso.ofComponents       fun F => F.rightUnitor.symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerLeft F e.unitIso ≪≫ Functor.associator _ _ _)     (NatIso.ofComponents       fun F => Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫ isoWhiskerLeft F e.counitIso ≪≫ F.rightUnitor)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.congrRight.description: This definition states that if two categories are equivalent, then the categories of functors from a third category to each of those two categories are also equivalent.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_unit_r.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_unit_right.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) {X Y : C} (f f' : X ⟶ Y) : f ≫ e.unit.app Y = f' ≫ e.unit.app Y ↔ f = f'
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_unit_r.description: This theorem states that if two morphisms in one category, when composed with a unit morphism of an equivalence, yield equal results in a second category, then those two morphisms must be equal.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_unitIn.description: This theorem states that if two morphisms in the first category compose with the unit of an equivalence from the second category to the first, then they are equal if and only if the two morphisms themselves are equal.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counit.description: This theorem states that for an equivalence between categories, two morphisms in the target category that give the same result when composed with the counit of the equivalence are equal if they are related through the image of a morphism in the source category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counit.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counitInv_right.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) {X Y : D} (f f' : X ⟶ Y) : f ≫ e.counitInv.app Y = f' ≫ e.counitInv.app Y ↔ f = f'
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counit.description: This theorem states that two morphisms in the second category are equal if their compositions with the counit morphism of an equivalence are equal.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_unit_r.description: This theorem states that the application of the unit morphism from an equivalence of categories on a common target allows for the cancellation of equal composite morphisms, reflecting a correspondence between them when composing other morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counit.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counitInv_right_assoc.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) {W X X' Y : D} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (f' : W ⟶ X') (g' : X' ⟶ Y) :
  f ≫ g ≫ e.counitInv.app Y = f' ≫ g' ≫ e.counitInv.app Y ↔ f ≫ g = f' ≫ g'
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counit.description: This theorem establishes that two compositions of morphisms in one category are equal if and only if their respective transformations through the counit inverse of an equivalence produce the same result after being mapped to another category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_unit_r.description: This theorem establishes a condition under which two sequences of morphisms in one category are equal if their images under a unit transformation related to an equivalence with another category are equal.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counit.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counitInv_right_assoc'.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) {W X X' Y Y' Z : D} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) (f' : W ⟶ X')
  (g' : X' ⟶ Y') (h' : Y' ⟶ Z) :
  f ≫ g ≫ h ≫ e.counitInv.app Z = f' ≫ g' ≫ h' ≫ e.counitInv.app Z ↔ f ≫ g ≫ h = f' ≫ g' ≫ h'
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.cancel_counit.description: This theorem shows that the equality of compositions of morphisms in a category is preserved when involving the counit inverse of an equivalence between two categories, indicating a structural relationship between these morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.powNat.code: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.powNat.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (e : C ≌ C) : ℕ → (C ≌ C)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.powNat.comment: Natural number powers of an auto-equivalence.  Use `(^)` instead.

explanatories.Trans.trans: This definition allows for the combination of two relations through transitivity to derive a new relation connecting the initial and final elements.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.refl: This definition asserts that any category is equivalente to itself, demonstrating the reflexivity of category equivalence.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.trans: This definition asserts that the equivalence between categories is transitive, meaning if one category is equivalent to a second, and that second category is equivalent to a third, then the first category is also equivalent to the third.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.powNat.fullDefinition: def powNat (e : C ≌ C) : ℕ → (C ≌ C)   | 0 => Equivalence.refl   | 1 => e   | n + 2 => e.trans (powNat e (n + 1))
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.powNat.description: This definition introduces a method for constructing the natural number powers of an auto-equivalence within a given category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow.code: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (e : C ≌ C) : ℤ → (C ≌ C)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow.comment: Powers of an auto-equivalence.  Use `(^)` instead.

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.powNat: This definition introduces a method for constructing the natural number powers of an auto-equivalence within a given category.
explanatories.Int.ofNat: Every natural number can be represented as an integer.
explanatories.Int.negSucc: The negation of the successor of any natural number is an integer.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow.fullDefinition: def pow (e : C ≌ C) : ℤ → (C ≌ C)   | Int.ofNat n => e.powNat n   | Int.negSucc n => e.symm.powNat (n + 1)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow.description: This definition introduces a mechanism for obtaining the n-th power of an auto-equivalence within a category, although it is suggested to use an alternative notation for this purpose.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_zero.code: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_zero.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (e : C ≌ C) : e ^ 0 = refl
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_zero.description: This theorem states that raising an equivalence of a category to the zero power yields the identity equivalence on that category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_one.code: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_one.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (e : C ≌ C) : e ^ 1 = e
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_one.description: This theorem asserts that raising an equivalence of a category to the first power yields the equivalence itself.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_neg_one.code: CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_neg_one.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (e : C ≌ C) : e ^ (-1) = e.symm

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pow_neg_one.description: This theorem establishes that raising an equivalence in a category to the power of negative one is equivalent to its inverse equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.essSurj_funct.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.essSurj_functor.{v₁, v₃, u₁, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {E : Type u₃}
  [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (e : C ≌ E) : e.functor.EssSurj
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.essSurj_funct.comment:
The functor of an equivalence of categories is essentially surjective.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02C3>.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor: This definition introduces a functor that represents one direction of an equivalence between two categories.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.essSurj_funct.fullDefinition: instance essSurj_functor (e : C ≌ E) : e.functor.EssSurj :=   ⟨fun Y => ⟨e.inverse.obj Y, ⟨e.counitIso.app Y⟩⟩⟩
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.essSurj_funct.description: This definition asserts that the functor associated with an equivalence between two categories is essentially surjective, meaning every object in the target category is the image of at least one object in the source category.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithfulFunctor.{v₁, v₃, u₁, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {E : Type u₃}
  [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (e : C ≌ E) : e.functor.FullyFaithful
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.comment: The functor of an equivalence of categories is fully faithful.
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.fullDefinition: def fullyFaithfulFunctor (e : C ≌ E) : e.functor.FullyFaithful where   preimage {X Y} f := e.unitIso.hom.app X ≫ e.inverse.map f ≫ e.unitIso.inv.app Y
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.description: This definition confirms that the functor associated with an equivalence between two categories is fully faithful, meaning it perfectly preserves morphisms between objects.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithfulInverse.{v₁, v₃, u₁, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {E : Type u₃}
  [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (e : C ≌ E) : e.inverse.FullyFaithful
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.comment: The inverse of an equivalence of categories is fully faithful.
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.fullDefinition: def fullyFaithfulInverse (e : C ≌ E) : e.inverse.FullyFaithful where   preimage {X Y} f := e.counitIso.inv.app X ≫ e.functor.map f ≫ e.counitIso.hom.app Y
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fullyFaithful.description: This definition states that the inverse functor of an equivalence between two categories is fully faithful.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.changeFunctor.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.changeFunctor.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (e : C ≌ D) {G : C ⥤ D} (iso : e.functor ≅ G) : C ≌ D
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.changeFunctor.comment:
If `e : C ≌ D` is an equivalence of categories, and `iso : e.functor ≅ G` is
an isomorphism, then there is an equivalence of categories whose functor is `G`.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.changeFunctor.fullDefinition: def changeFunctor (e : C ≌ D) {G : C ⥤ D} (iso : e.functor ≅ G) : C ≌ D where   functor := G   inverse := e.inverse   unitIso := e.unitIso ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight iso _   counitIso := isoWhiskerLeft _ iso.symm ≪≫ e.counitIso
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.changeFunctor.description: This definition states that if there is an equivalence between two categories and an isomorphism exists between the functor of that equivalence and another functor, then there is a corresponding equivalence whose functor is the latter.

CategoryTheory.Functor.inv.comment:
A quasi-inverse `D ⥤ C` to a functor that `F : C ⥤ D` that is an equivalence,
i.e. faithful, full, and essentially surjective.
CategoryTheory.Functor.inv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def inv (F : C ⥤ D) [F.IsEquivalence] : D ⥤ C where   obj X := F.objPreimage X   map {X Y} f := F.preimage ((F.objObjPreimageIso X).hom ≫ f ≫ (F.objObjPreimageIso Y).inv)   map_id X := by apply F.map_injective; aesop_cat   map_comp {X Y Z} f g := by apply F.map_injective; simp
CategoryTheory.Functor.inv.description: This definition introduces a functor that acts as a quasi-inverse to a given equivalence functor, establishing a connection from the target category back to the source category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.asEquivalence.fullDefinition: noncomputable def asEquivalence (F : C ⥤ D) [F.IsEquivalence] : C ≌ D where   functor := F   inverse := F.inv   unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents     (fun X => (F.preimageIso <| F.objObjPreimageIso <| F.obj X).symm)       (fun f => F.map_injective (by simp [inv]))   counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents F.objObjPreimageIso (by simp [inv])

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.CoreHomEquiv.h.fullDefinition: homEquiv : ∀ X Y, (F.obj X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X ⟶ G.obj Y)   /-- The property that describes how `homEquiv.symm` transforms compositions `X' ⟶ X ⟶ G Y` -/   homEquiv_naturality_left_symm :     ∀ {X' X Y} (f : X' ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ G.obj Y),       (homEquiv X' Y).symm (f ≫ g) = F.map f ≫ (homEquiv X Y).symm g := by     aesop_cat   /-- The property that describes how `homEquiv` transforms compositions `F X ⟶ Y ⟶ Y'` -/   homEquiv_naturality_right :     ∀ {X Y Y'} (f : F.obj X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Y'),       (homEquiv X Y') (f ≫ g) = (homEquiv X Y) f ≫ G.map g := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv.fullDefinition: def mkOfHomEquiv (adj : CoreHomEquiv F G) : F ⊣ G :=   -- See note [dsimp, simp].   { adj with     unit :=       { app := fun X => (adj.homEquiv X (F.obj X)) (𝟙 (F.obj X))         naturality := by           intros           erw [← adj.homEquiv_naturality_left, ← adj.homEquiv_naturality_right]           dsimp; simp }     counit :=       { app := fun Y => (adj.homEquiv _ _).invFun (𝟙 (G.obj Y))         naturality := by           intros           erw [← adj.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm, ← adj.homEquiv_naturality_right_symm]           dsimp; simp }     homEquiv_unit := @fun X Y f => by erw [← adj.homEquiv_naturality_right]; simp     homEquiv_counit := @fun X Y f => by erw [← adj.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm]; simp   }

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.CoreUnitCounit.fullDefinition: unit : 𝟭 C ⟶ F.comp G   /-- The counit of an adjunction between `F` and `G`s -/   counit : G.comp F ⟶ 𝟭 D   /-- Equality of the composition of the unit, associator, and counit with the identity   `F ⟶ (F G) F ⟶ F (G F) ⟶ F = NatTrans.id F` -/   left_triangle :     whiskerRight unit F ≫ (Functor.associator F G F).hom ≫ whiskerLeft F counit =       NatTrans.id (𝟭 C ⋙ F) := by     aesop_cat   /-- Equality of the composition of the unit, associator, and counit with the identity   `G ⟶ G (F G) ⟶ (F G) F ⟶ G = NatTrans.id G` -/   right_triangle :     whiskerLeft G unit ≫ (Functor.associator G F G).inv ≫ whiskerRight counit G =       NatTrans.id (G ⋙ 𝟭 C) := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mkOfUnitCounit.fullDefinition: def mkOfUnitCounit (adj : CoreUnitCounit F G) : F ⊣ G :=   { adj with     homEquiv := fun X Y =>       { toFun := fun f => adj.unit.app X ≫ G.map f         invFun := fun g => F.map g ≫ adj.counit.app Y         left_inv := fun f => by           change F.map (_ ≫ _) ≫ _ = _           rw [F.map_comp, assoc, ← Functor.comp_map, adj.counit.naturality, ← assoc]           convert id_comp f           have t := congrArg (fun (s : NatTrans (𝟭 C ⋙ F) (F ⋙ 𝟭 D)) => s.app X) adj.left_triangle           dsimp at t           simp only [id_comp] at t           exact t         right_inv := fun g => by           change _ ≫ G.map (_ ≫ _) = _           rw [G.map_comp, ← assoc, ← Functor.comp_map, ← adj.unit.naturality, assoc]           convert comp_id g           have t := congrArg (fun t : NatTrans (G ⋙ 𝟭 C) (𝟭 D ⋙ G) => t.app Y) adj.right_triangle           dsimp at t           simp only [id_comp] at t           exact t } }

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.equivHomsetLef.fullDefinition: def equivHomsetLeftOfNatIso {F F' : C ⥤ D} (iso : F ≅ F') {X : C} {Y : D} :     (F.obj X ⟶ Y) ≃ (F'.obj X ⟶ Y) where   toFun f := iso.inv.app _ ≫ f   invFun g := iso.hom.app _ ≫ g   left_inv f := by simp   right_inv g := by simp
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.equivHomsetLef.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the morphisms from the image of one functor to an object in a category and the morphisms from the image of another naturally isomorphic functor to the same object.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.equivHomsetRig.comment: If G and H are naturally isomorphic functors, establish an equivalence of hom-sets.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.equivHomsetRig.description: This definition states that if two functors are naturally isomorphic, then there is an equivalence between the sets of morphisms from an object to their images in the target category.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv.code:
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_3, u_1} C]
  [Category.{u_4, u_2} D] {F F' : C ⥤ D} {G G' : D ⥤ C} (adj1 : F ⊣ G) (adj2 : F' ⊣ G') : (G ⟶ G') ≃ (F' ⟶ F)
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv.comment:
If `F ⊣ G` and `F' ⊣ G'` are adjunctions, then giving a natural transformation `G ⟶ G'` is the
same as giving a natural transformation `F' ⟶ F`.
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv.fullDefinition: def natTransEquiv {F F' : C ⥤ D} {G G' : D ⥤ C} (adj1 : F ⊣ G) (adj2 : F' ⊣ G') :     (G ⟶ G') ≃ (F' ⟶ F) where   toFun f := {     app := fun X ↦ F'.map ((adj1.unit ≫ whiskerLeft F f).app X) ≫ adj2.counit.app _     naturality := by       intro X Y g       simp only [← Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp]       erw [(adj1.unit ≫ (whiskerLeft F f)).naturality]       simp   }   invFun f := {     app := fun X ↦ adj2.unit.app (G.obj X) ≫ G'.map (f.app (G.obj X) ≫ adj1.counit.app X)     naturality := by       intro X Y g       erw [← adj2.unit_naturality_assoc]       simp only [← Functor.map_comp]       simp   }   left_inv f := by     ext X     simp only [Functor.comp_obj, NatTrans.comp_app, Functor.id_obj, whiskerLeft_app,       Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc, unit_naturality_assoc, right_triangle_components_assoc]     erw [← f.naturality (adj1.counit.app X), ← Category.assoc]     simp   right_inv f := by     ext     simp
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between natural transformations between two pairs of adjoint functors, indicating that a natural transformation from one right adjoint to another corresponds uniquely to a natural transformation from the associated left adjoints.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv_.code:
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv_symm_apply_app.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2}
  [Category.{u_3, u_1} C] [Category.{u_4, u_2} D] {F F' : C ⥤ D} {G G' : D ⥤ C} (adj1 : F ⊣ G) (adj2 : F' ⊣ G')
  (f : F' ⟶ F) (X : D) :
  ((adj1.natTransEquiv adj2).symm f).app X = adj2.unit.app (G.obj X) ≫ G'.map (f.app (G.obj X) ≫ adj1.counit.app X)
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv_.description: This theorem shows how the application of the inverse of the equivalence between natural transformations of two pairs of adjoint functors can be expressed in terms of the natural transformation from the left adjoint to the right adjoint and the unit and counit of the adjunctions evaluated at a specific object.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv_.code:
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv_apply_app.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2}
  [Category.{u_3, u_1} C] [Category.{u_4, u_2} D] {F F' : C ⥤ D} {G G' : D ⥤ C} (adj1 : F ⊣ G) (adj2 : F' ⊣ G')
  (f : G ⟶ G') (X : C) :
  ((adj1.natTransEquiv adj2) f).app X = F'.map ((adj1.unit ≫ whiskerLeft F f).app X) ≫ adj2.counit.app (F.obj X)
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv_.description: This theorem describes how the application of the equivalence between natural transformations of two pairs of adjoint functors at a specific object can be expressed in terms of the unit and counit of the adjunctions and the natural transformation between the right adjoints.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natIsoEquiv.code:
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natIsoEquiv.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_3, u_1} C]
  [Category.{u_4, u_2} D] {F F' : C ⥤ D} {G G' : D ⥤ C} (adj1 : F ⊣ G) (adj2 : F' ⊣ G') : (G ≅ G') ≃ (F' ≅ F)
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natIsoEquiv.comment:
If `F ⊣ G` and `F' ⊣ G'` are adjunctions, then giving a natural isomorphism `G ≅ G'` is the

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natTransEquiv: This definition establishes an equivalence between natural transformations between two pairs of adjoint functors, indicating that a natural transformation from one right adjoint to another corresponds uniquely to a natural transformation from the associated left adjoints.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natIsoEquiv.fullDefinition: def natIsoEquiv {F F' : C ⥤ D} {G G' : D ⥤ C} (adj1 : F ⊣ G) (adj2 : F' ⊣ G') :     (G ≅ G') ≃ (F' ≅ F) where   toFun i := {     hom := natTransEquiv adj1 adj2 i.hom     inv := natTransEquiv adj2 adj1 i.inv   }   invFun i := {     hom := (natTransEquiv adj1 adj2).symm i.hom     inv := (natTransEquiv adj2 adj1).symm i.inv }   left_inv i := by simp   right_inv i := by simp
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.natIsoEquiv.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between natural isomorphisms of two pairs of adjoint functors, indicating that a natural isomorphism from one right adjoint to another is equivalent to a natural isomorphism from the associated left adjoints.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq_trans_app.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2}
  [Category.{u_3, u_1} C] [Category.{u_4, u_2} D] {F F' F'' : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj1 : F ⊣ G) (adj2 : F' ⊣ G)

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.whiskerRight.comment:
Given an adjunction `F ⊣ G`, this provides the natural adjunction
`(whiskeringRight C _ _).obj F ⊣ (whiskeringRight C _ _).obj G`.
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.whiskerRight.fullDefinition: protected def whiskerRight (adj : F ⊣ G) :     (whiskeringRight C D E).obj F ⊣ (whiskeringRight C E D).obj G :=   mkOfUnitCounit     { unit :=         { app := fun X =>             (Functor.rightUnitor _).inv ≫ whiskerLeft X adj.unit ≫ (Functor.associator _ _ _).inv           naturality := by intros; ext; dsimp; simp }       counit :=         { app := fun X =>             (Functor.associator _ _ _).hom ≫ whiskerLeft X adj.counit ≫ (Functor.rightUnitor _).hom           naturality := by intros; ext; dsimp; simp }       left_triangle  := by ext; dsimp; simp       right_triangle := by ext; dsimp; simp     }
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.whiskerRight.description: This definition establishes that for a pair of functors related by an adjunction, the whiskering operation on the functors yields another adjunction between the transformed functors.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.whiskerLeft.comment:
Given an adjunction `F ⊣ G`, this provides the natural adjunction

CategoryTheory.mateEquiv.comment:
Suppose we have a square of functors (where the top and bottom are adjunctions `L₁ ⊣ R₁`
and `L₂ ⊣ R₂` respectively).

      C ↔ D
    G ↓   ↓ H
      E ↔ F

Then we have a bijection between natural transformations `G ⋙ L₂ ⟶ L₁ ⋙ H` and
`R₁ ⋙ G ⟶ H ⋙ R₂`. This can be seen as a bijection of the 2-cells:

         L₁                  R₁
      C --→ D             C ←-- D
    G ↓  ↗  ↓ H         G ↓  ↘  ↓ H
      E --→ F             E ←-- F
         L₂                  R₂

Note that if one of the transformations is an iso, it does not imply the other is an iso.

CategoryTheory.conjugateEquiv.comment:
Given two adjunctions `L₁ ⊣ R₁` and `L₂ ⊣ R₂` both between categories `C`, `D`, there is a
bijection between natural transformations `L₂ ⟶ L₁` and natural transformations `R₁ ⟶ R₂`. This is
defined as a special case of `mateEquiv`, where the two "vertical" functors are identity, modulo
composition with the unitors. Corresponding natural transformations are called `conjugateEquiv`.
TODO: Generalise to when the two vertical functors are equivalences rather than being exactly `𝟭`.

Furthermore, this bijection preserves (and reflects) isomorphisms, i.e. a transformation is an iso
iff its image under the bijection is an iso, see eg `CategoryTheory.conjugateIsoEquiv`.
This is in contrast to the general case `mateEquiv` which does not in general have this property.

CategoryTheory.iterated_mateEquiv_conjug.comment:
When all four functors in a sequare are left adjoints, the mates operation can be iterated:

         L₁                  R₁                  R₁
      C --→ D             C ←-- D             C ←-- D
   F₁ ↓  ↗  ↓  F₂      F₁ ↓  ↘  ↓ F₂       U₁ ↑  ↙  ↑ U₂
      E --→ F             E ←-- F             E ←-- F
         L₂                  R₂                  R₂

In this case the iterated mate equals the conjugate of the original transformation and is thus an
isomorphism if and only if the original transformation is. This explains why some Beck-Chevalley
natural transformations are natural isomorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.restrictFullyF.comment:
If `C` is a full subcategory of `C'` and `D` is a full subcategory of `D'`, then we can restrict
an adjunction `L' ⊣ R'` where `L' : C' ⥤ D'` and `R' : D' ⥤ C'` to `C` and `D`.
The construction here is slightly more general, in that `C` is required only to have a full and
faithful "inclusion" functor `iC : C ⥤ C'` (and similarly `iD : D ⥤ D'`) which commute (up to
natural isomorphism) with the proposed restrictions.

CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.unit_isI.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.unit_isIso.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {i : D ⥤ C} [Reflective i] {A : C} (h : A ∈ i.essImage) :
  IsIso ((reflectorAdjunction i).unit.app A)
CategoryTheory.Functor.essImage.unit_isI.comment:
If `A` is essentially in the image of a reflective functor `i`, then `η_A` is an isomorphism.
This gives that the "witness" for `A` being in the essential image can instead be given as the
reflection of `A`, with the isomorphism as `η_A`.

(For any `B` in the reflective subcategory, we automatically have that `ε_B` is an iso.)

CategoryTheory.unitCompPartialBijective.code:

  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {i : D ⥤ C} [Reflective i] (A : C) {B : C} (hB : B ∈ i.essImage) :
  (A ⟶ B) ≃ (i.obj ((reflector i).obj A) ⟶ B)
CategoryTheory.unitCompPartialBijective.comment:
If `i` has a reflector `L`, then the function `(i.obj (L.obj A) ⟶ B) → (A ⟶ B)` given by
precomposing with `η.app A` is a bijection provided `B` is in the essential image of `i`.
That is, the function `fun (f : i.obj (L.obj A) ⟶ B) ↦ η.app A ≫ f` is bijective,
as long as `B` is in the essential image of `i`.
This definition gives an equivalence: the key property that the inverse can be described
nicely is shown in `unitCompPartialBijective_symm_apply`.

This establishes there is a natural bijection `(A ⟶ B) ≃ (i.obj (L.obj A) ⟶ B)`. In other words,
from the point of view of objects in `D`, `A` and `i.obj (L.obj A)` look the same: specifically
that `η.app A` is an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.leftAdjointOfStructuredAr.fullDefinition: def leftAdjointOfStructuredArrowInitialsAux (A : C) (B : D) :     ((⊥_ StructuredArrow A G).right ⟶ B) ≃ (A ⟶ G.obj B) where   toFun g := (⊥_ StructuredArrow A G).hom ≫ G.map g   invFun f := CommaMorphism.right (initial.to (StructuredArrow.mk f))   left_inv g := by     let B' : StructuredArrow A G := StructuredArrow.mk ((⊥_ StructuredArrow A G).hom ≫ G.map g)     let g' : ⊥_ StructuredArrow A G ⟶ B' := StructuredArrow.homMk g rfl     have : initial.to _ = g' := by aesop_cat     change CommaMorphism.right (initial.to B') = _     rw [this]     rfl   right_inv f := by     let B' : StructuredArrow A G := StructuredArrow.mk f     apply (CommaMorphism.w (initial.to B')).symm.trans (Category.id_comp _)
CategoryTheory.leftAdjointOfStructuredAr.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between morphisms from the right initial object in the structured arrow category to another object and morphisms from the original category to the object under the functor defined by an arrow.

CategoryTheory.rightAdjointOfCostructure.fullDefinition: def rightAdjointOfCostructuredArrowTerminalsAux (B : D) (A : C) :     (G.obj B ⟶ A) ≃ (B ⟶ (⊤_ CostructuredArrow G A).left) where   toFun g := CommaMorphism.left (terminal.from (CostructuredArrow.mk g))   invFun g := G.map g ≫ (⊤_ CostructuredArrow G A).hom   left_inv := by aesop_cat   right_inv g := by     let B' : CostructuredArrow G A :=       CostructuredArrow.mk (G.map g ≫ (⊤_ CostructuredArrow G A).hom)     let g' : B' ⟶ ⊤_ CostructuredArrow G A := CostructuredArrow.homMk g rfl     have : terminal.from _ = g' := by aesop_cat     change CommaMorphism.left (terminal.from B') = _     rw [this]     rfl

CategoryTheory.Over.baseChange.fullDefinition: def baseChange [HasPullbacks C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Over Y ⥤ Over X where   obj g := Over.mk (pullback.snd g.hom f)   map i := Over.homMk (pullback.map _ _ _ _ i.left (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simp) (by simp))   map_id Z := by     apply Over.OverMorphism.ext; apply pullback.hom_ext     · dsimp; simp     · dsimp; simp   map_comp f g := by     apply Over.OverMorphism.ext; apply pullback.hom_ext     · dsimp; simp     · dsimp; simp
CategoryTheory.Over.baseChange.description: This definition describes a functor that transforms morphisms over one object into morphisms over another object by utilizing pullback operations associated with a given morphism.

CategoryTheory.Over.star.fullDefinition: def star [HasBinaryProducts C] : C ⥤ Over X :=   cofree _ ⋙ coalgebraToOver X
CategoryTheory.Over.star.description: This definition describes a functor that maps objects from a category to the over category associated with a fixed object by sending each object to a specific projection morphism.

CategoryTheory.Over.forgetAdjStar.code:

  forget X ⊣ star X
CategoryTheory.Over.forgetAdjStar.comment:
The functor `Over.forget X : Over X ⥤ C` has a right adjoint given by `star X`.

Note that the binary products assumption is necessary: the existence of a right adjoint to
`Over.forget X` is equivalent to the existence of each binary product `X ⨯ -`.

CategoryTheory.LiftAdjoint.otherMap.comment:
(Implementation)
To construct the left adjoint, we use the coequalizer of `F' U ε_Y` with the composite

`F' U F U X ⟶ F' U F U R F U' X ⟶ F' U R F' U X ⟶ F' U X`

where the first morphism is `F' U F ι_UX`, the second is `F' U ε_RF'UX`, and the third is `δ_F'UX`.
We will show that this coequalizer exists and that it forms the object map for a left adjoint to
`R`.

category_theory.lift_adjoint.construct_l.fullDefinition: noncomputable def constructLeftAdjointEquiv [∀ X : B, RegularEpi (adj₁.counit.app X)] (Y : A)     (X : B) : (constructLeftAdjointObj _ _ adj₁ adj₂ X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X ⟶ R.obj Y) :=   calc     (constructLeftAdjointObj _ _ adj₁ adj₂ X ⟶ Y) ≃         { f : F'.obj (U.obj X) ⟶ Y //           F'.map (U.map (adj₁.counit.app X)) ≫ f = otherMap _ _ adj₁ adj₂ _ ≫ f } :=       Cofork.IsColimit.homIso (colimit.isColimit _) _     _ ≃ { g : U.obj X ⟶ U.obj (R.obj Y) //           U.map (F.map g ≫ adj₁.counit.app _) = U.map (adj₁.counit.app _) ≫ g } := by       apply (adj₂.homEquiv _ _).subtypeEquiv _       intro f       rw [← (adj₂.homEquiv _ _).injective.eq_iff, eq_comm, adj₂.homEquiv_naturality_left,         otherMap, assoc, adj₂.homEquiv_naturality_left, ← adj₂.counit_naturality,         adj₂.homEquiv_naturality_left, adj₂.homEquiv_unit, adj₂.right_triangle_components,         comp_id, Functor.comp_map, ← U.map_comp, assoc, ← adj₁.counit_naturality,         adj₂.homEquiv_unit, adj₂.homEquiv_unit, F.map_comp, assoc]       rfl     _ ≃ { z : F.obj (U.obj X) ⟶ R.obj Y // _ } := by       apply (adj₁.homEquiv _ _).symm.subtypeEquiv       intro g       rw [← (adj₁.homEquiv _ _).symm.injective.eq_iff, adj₁.homEquiv_counit,         adj₁.homEquiv_counit, adj₁.homEquiv_counit, F.map_comp, assoc, U.map_comp, F.map_comp,         assoc, adj₁.counit_naturality, adj₁.counit_naturality_assoc]       apply eq_comm     _ ≃ (X ⟶ R.obj Y) := (Cofork.IsColimit.homIso (counitCoequalises adj₁ X) _).symm

CategoryTheory.LiftAdjoint.constructLeft.code:
CategoryTheory.LiftAdjoint.constructLeftAdjointEquiv_apply.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂}
  {C : Type u₃} [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] {U : B ⥤ C} {F : C ⥤ B} (R : A ⥤ B)
  (F' : C ⥤ A) (adj₁ : F ⊣ U) (adj₂ : F' ⊣ R ⋙ U) [HasReflexiveCoequalizers A]
  [(X : B) → RegularEpi (adj₁.counit.app X)] (Y : A) (X : B) :
  ∀ (a : constructLeftAdjointObj R F' adj₁ adj₂ X ⟶ Y),
    (constructLeftAdjointEquiv R F' adj₁ adj₂ Y X) a =
      (Cofork.IsColimit.homIso (counitCoequalises adj₁ X) (R.obj Y)).symm
        ⟨F.map
              ((adj₂.homEquiv (U.obj X) Y)
                ↑((Cofork.IsColimit.homIso
                      (colimit.isColimit
                        (parallelPair (F'.map (U.map (adj₁.counit.app X))) (otherMap R F' adj₁ adj₂ X)))
                      Y)
                    a)) ≫
            adj₁.counit.app (R.obj Y),
          ⋯⟩

CategoryTheory.adjointTriangleLift.comment:
The adjoint triangle theorem: Suppose `U : B ⥤ C` has a left adjoint `F` such that each counit
`ε_X : FUX ⟶ X` is a regular epimorphism. Then if a category `A` has coequalizers of reflexive
pairs, then a functor `R : A ⥤ B` has a left adjoint if the composite `R ⋙ U` does.

Note the converse is true (with weaker assumptions), by `Adjunction.comp`.
See https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+triangle+theorem
CategoryTheory.adjointTriangleLift.description: This theorem asserts that if a functor has a left adjoint such that its counits are regular epimorphisms, then another functor can also be shown to have a left adjoint under certain categorical conditions involving coequalizers.

CategoryTheory.monadicAdjointTriangleLif.comment:
If `R ⋙ U` has a left adjoint, the domain of `R` has reflexive coequalizers and `U` is a monadic
functor, then `R` has a left adjoint.
This is a special case of `adjointTriangleLift` which is often more useful in practice.
CategoryTheory.monadicAdjointTriangleLif.description: This theorem states that if a functor composed with a monadic functor has a left adjoint, the source category possesses reflexive coequalizers, and the composite functor is a right adjoint, then the original functor has a left adjoint as well.

  [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] {D : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄, u₄} D] (Q : A ⥤ B)
  (V : B ⥤ D) (U : A ⥤ C) (R : C ⥤ D) (comm : U ⋙ R ≅ Q ⋙ V) [U.IsRightAdjoint] [V.IsRightAdjoint] [R.IsRightAdjoint]
  [(X : B) → RegularEpi ((Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint V).counit.app X)] [HasReflexiveCoequalizers A] : Q.IsRightAdjoint
CategoryTheory.adjointSquareLift.comment:
Suppose we have a commutative square of functors

      Q
    A → B
  U ↓   ↓ V
    C → D
      R

where `U` has a left adjoint, `A` has reflexive coequalizers and `V` has a left adjoint such that
each component of the counit is a regular epi.
Then `Q` has a left adjoint if `R` has a left adjoint.

See https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/adjoint+lifting+theorem

CategoryTheory.SolutionSetCondition.code:
CategoryTheory.SolutionSetCondition.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u} [Category.{v, u} D]
  (G : D ⥤ C) : Prop
CategoryTheory.SolutionSetCondition.comment:
The functor `G : D ⥤ C` satisfies the *solution set condition* if for every `A : C`, there is a
family of morphisms `{f_i : A ⟶ G (B_i) // i ∈ ι}` such that given any morphism `h : A ⟶ G X`,
there is some `i ∈ ι` such that `h` factors through `f_i`.

The key part of this definition is that the indexing set `ι` lives in `Type v`, where `v` is the
universe of morphisms of the category: this is the "smallness" condition which allows the general
adjoint functor theorem to go through.
CategoryTheory.SolutionSetCondition.fullDefinition: def SolutionSetCondition {D : Type u} [Category.{v} D] (G : D ⥤ C) : Prop :=   ∀ A : C,     ∃ (ι : Type v) (B : ι → D) (f : ∀ i : ι, A ⟶ G.obj (B i)),       ∀ (X) (h : A ⟶ G.obj X), ∃ (i : ι) (g : B i ⟶ X), f i ≫ G.map g = h
CategoryTheory.SolutionSetCondition.description: This definition characterizes a functor as satisfying the solution set condition if, for every object in the target category, there exists a collection of morphisms from that object to the images of specific morphisms such that any other morphism to the functor's output can be factored through one of these morphisms.

Quiver.Hom.unop_inj.code: Quiver.Hom.unop_inj.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Quiver C] {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} : Function.Injective Quiver.Hom.unop
Quiver.Hom.unop_inj.description: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.

Quiver.Hom.unop_op.code: Quiver.Hom.unop_op.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Quiver C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : f.op.unop = f
Quiver.Hom.unop_op.description: The theorem establishes that applying the operation to reverse the direction of a morphism and then applying the operation to revert it returns the original morphism.

Quiver.Hom.op_unop.code: Quiver.Hom.op_unop.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Quiver C] {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) : f.unop.op = f
Quiver.Hom.op_unop.description: The theorem shows that applying the operation to revert the direction of a morphism and then applying the operation to reverse it returns the original morphism.

CategoryTheory.Category.opposite.code: CategoryTheory.Category.opposite.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] : Category.{v₁, u₁} Cᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.Category.opposite.fullDefinition: instance Category.opposite : Category.{v₁} Cᵒᵖ where   comp f g := (g.unop ≫ f.unop).op   id X := (𝟙 (unop X)).op
CategoryTheory.Category.opposite.description: The definition establishes the concept of the opposite category, which reverses the morphisms of a given category.

CategoryTheory.op_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.op_comp.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} :
  (f ≫ g).op = g.op ≫ f.op
CategoryTheory.op_comp.description: The theorem establishes that the operation for reversing the direction of the composition of two morphisms equals the composition of their individual reversals in the opposite order.

CategoryTheory.op_id.code: CategoryTheory.op_id.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} : (𝟙 X).op = 𝟙 (op X)
CategoryTheory.op_id.description: The theorem shows that the operation for reversing the direction of the identity morphism in a category equals the identity morphism of the corresponding opposite object.

CategoryTheory.unop_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.unop_comp.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : Cᵒᵖ} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} :
  (f ≫ g).unop = g.unop ≫ f.unop
CategoryTheory.unop_comp.description: The theorem asserts that the operation for reversing the direction of the composition of two morphisms in an opposite category results in the composition of their individual reversals in the original order.

CategoryTheory.unop_id.code: CategoryTheory.unop_id.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : Cᵒᵖ} : (𝟙 X).unop = 𝟙 (unop X)
CategoryTheory.unop_id.description: The theorem indicates that the operation for reversing the direction of the identity morphism in an opposite category yields the identity morphism of the original object.

CategoryTheory.unop_id_op.code: CategoryTheory.unop_id_op.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} : (𝟙 (op X)).unop = 𝟙 X
CategoryTheory.unop_id_op.description: The theorem demonstrates that the operation for reverting the direction of the identity morphism of the opposite object equals the identity morphism of the original object.

CategoryTheory.op_id_unop.code: CategoryTheory.op_id_unop.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : Cᵒᵖ} : (𝟙 (unop X)).op = 𝟙 X
CategoryTheory.op_id_unop.description: The theorem asserts that the operation for reversing the direction of the identity morphism of the original object corresponds to the identity morphism of the opposite object.

CategoryTheory.unopUnop.code: CategoryTheory.unopUnop.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] : Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.unopUnop.comment: The functor from the double-opposite of a category to the underlying category.
CategoryTheory.unopUnop.fullDefinition: def unopUnop : Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ ⥤ C where   obj X := unop (unop X)   map f := f.unop.unop
CategoryTheory.unopUnop.description: This definition describes a functor that maps from the double opposite of a category back to the original category itself.

CategoryTheory.opOp.code: CategoryTheory.opOp.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.opOp.comment: The functor from a category to its double-opposite.
CategoryTheory.opOp.fullDefinition: def opOp : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ where   obj X := op (op X)   map f := f.op.op
CategoryTheory.opOp.description: This definition describes a functor that maps a category to its double opposite.

CategoryTheory.opOpEquivalence.code: CategoryTheory.opOpEquivalence.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] : Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ ≌ C
CategoryTheory.opOpEquivalence.comment: The double opposite category is equivalent to the original.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.unopUnop: This definition describes a functor that maps from the double opposite of a category back to the original category itself.

CategoryTheory.opOpEquivalence.fullDefinition: def opOpEquivalence : Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ ≌ C where   functor := unopUnop C   inverse := opOp C   unitIso := Iso.refl (𝟭 Cᵒᵖᵒᵖ)   counitIso := Iso.refl (opOp C ⋙ unopUnop C)
CategoryTheory.opOpEquivalence.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between a category and its double opposite category.

CategoryTheory.isIso_op.code: CategoryTheory.isIso_op.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : IsIso f.op
CategoryTheory.isIso_op.comment: If `f` is an isomorphism, so is `f.op`

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.

CategoryTheory.isIso_op.fullDefinition: instance isIso_op {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : IsIso f.op :=   ⟨⟨(inv f).op, ⟨Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (by aesop_cat), Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (by aesop_cat)⟩⟩⟩
CategoryTheory.isIso_op.description: This definition states that if a morphism is an isomorphism in a category, then the morphism obtained by reversing its direction is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.isIso_of_op.code: CategoryTheory.isIso_of_op.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f.op] : IsIso f
CategoryTheory.isIso_of_op.comment:
If `f.op` is an isomorphism `f` must be too.
(This cannot be an instance as it would immediately loop!)
CategoryTheory.isIso_of_op.description: The theorem establishes that if a morphism in the opposite category is an isomorphism, then the corresponding morphism in the original category is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.isIso_op_iff.code: CategoryTheory.isIso_op_iff.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : IsIso f.op ↔ IsIso f
CategoryTheory.isIso_op_iff.description: The theorem establishes a condition for a morphism to be an isomorphism in a category based on whether its reversed counterpart is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.isIso_unop_iff.code:
CategoryTheory.isIso_unop_iff.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  IsIso f.unop ↔ IsIso f
CategoryTheory.isIso_unop_iff.description: The theorem states that a morphism in the opposite category is an isomorphism if and only if its reversal is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.isIso_unop.code: CategoryTheory.isIso_unop.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : IsIso f.unop

explanatories.CategoryTheory.isIso_unop_iff: The theorem states that a morphism in the opposite category is an isomorphism if and only if its reversal is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.isIso_unop.fullDefinition: instance isIso_unop {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : IsIso f.unop :=   (isIso_unop_iff _).2 inferInstance
CategoryTheory.isIso_unop.description: The definition indicates that if a morphism in the opposite category is an isomorphism, then its corresponding morphism in the original category is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.op_inv.code:
CategoryTheory.op_inv.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] :
  (inv f).op = inv f.op
CategoryTheory.op_inv.description: The theorem states that the inverse of an isomorphism, when the direction of the morphism is reversed, is equal to the reversal of the inverse of that isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.unop_inv.code:
CategoryTheory.unop_inv.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] :
  (inv f).unop = inv f.unop
CategoryTheory.unop_inv.description: The theorem states that reversing the direction of the inverse of an isomorphism in an opposite category is equivalent to taking the inverse of the reversal of that isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.op.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.op.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.Functor.op.comment:
The opposite of a functor, i.e. considering a functor `F : C ⥤ D` as a functor `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ`.
In informal mathematics no distinction is made between these.
CategoryTheory.Functor.op.fullDefinition: protected def op (F : C ⥤ D) : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ where   obj X := op (F.obj (unop X))   map f := (F.map f.unop).op
CategoryTheory.Functor.op.description: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.

CategoryTheory.Functor.unop.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.unop.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : C ⥤ D
CategoryTheory.Functor.unop.comment:
Given a functor `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ` we can take the "unopposite" functor `F : C ⥤ D`.
In informal mathematics no distinction is made between these.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.

CategoryTheory.Functor.unop.fullDefinition: protected def unop (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : C ⥤ D where   obj X := unop (F.obj (op X))   map f := (F.map f.op).unop
CategoryTheory.Functor.unop.description: This definition outlines the process of converting a functor from the opposite category back to a functor in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.opUnopIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.opUnopIso.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) : F.op.unop ≅ F

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.unop: This definition outlines the process of converting a functor from the opposite category back to a functor in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.opUnopIso.fullDefinition: def opUnopIso (F : C ⥤ D) : F.op.unop ≅ F :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.opUnopIso.description: The definition establishes an isomorphism between a functor and its corresponding functor obtained by reversing and then re-reversing the direction of its morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Functor.unopOpIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.unopOpIso.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : F.unop.op ≅ F

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.

CategoryTheory.Functor.unopOpIso.fullDefinition: def unopOpIso (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : F.unop.op ≅ F :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.unopOpIso.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a functor from the opposite category and its corresponding functor obtained by first reversing its direction and then applying the operation for the original category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.opHom.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.opHom.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  (C ⥤ D)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.Functor.opHom.comment: Taking the opposite of a functor is functorial.

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.unop: This definition outlines the process of converting a functor from the opposite category back to a functor in the original category.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.Functor.opHom.fullDefinition: def opHom : (C ⥤ D)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ where   obj F := (unop F).op   map α :=     { app := fun X => (α.unop.app (unop X)).op       naturality := fun X Y f => Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (α.unop.naturality f.unop).symm }
CategoryTheory.Functor.opHom.description: This definition states that the process of taking the opposite functor is itself a functor that maps between categories and their opposites.

CategoryTheory.Functor.opInv.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.opInv.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) ⥤ (C ⥤ D)ᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.Functor.opInv.comment: Take the "unopposite" of a functor is functorial.

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.op_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in a quiver is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.unop: This definition outlines the process of converting a functor from the opposite category back to a functor in the original category.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.Functor.opInv.fullDefinition: def opInv : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) ⥤ (C ⥤ D)ᵒᵖ where   obj F := op F.unop   map α :=     Quiver.Hom.op       { app := fun X => (α.app (op X)).unop         naturality := fun X Y f => Quiver.Hom.op_inj <| (α.naturality f.op).symm }
CategoryTheory.Functor.opInv.description: The definition describes a functorial construction that transforms a functor from the opposite category to a functor in the original category's opposite.

CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp.comment:
Another variant of the opposite of functor, turning a functor `C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ` into a functor `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D`.
In informal mathematics no distinction is made.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.unop: This definition outlines the process of converting a functor from the opposite category back to a functor in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp.fullDefinition: protected def leftOp (F : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D where   obj X := unop (F.obj (unop X))   map f := (F.map f.unop).unop
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp.description: This definition specifies a method for transforming a functor from a category to the opposite of another category into a functor from the opposite of the first category to the second category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp.comment:
Another variant of the opposite of functor, turning a functor `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D` into a functor `C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ`.
In informal mathematics no distinction is made.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp.fullDefinition: protected def rightOp (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ where   obj X := op (F.obj (op X))   map f := (F.map f.op).op
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp.description: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor from the opposite category to another into a functor from the original category to the opposite of the second category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_faithful.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_faithful.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D} [F.Faithful] : F.rightOp.Faithful
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_faithful.comment: If F is faithful then the right_op of F is also faithful.

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.op_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in a quiver is injective.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_faithful.fullDefinition: instance rightOp_faithful {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D} [Faithful F] : Faithful F.rightOp where   map_injective h := Quiver.Hom.op_inj (map_injective F (Quiver.Hom.op_inj h))
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_faithful.description: The definition states that if a functor from the opposite category is faithful, then its right adjoint functor is also faithful.

CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp_faithful.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp_faithful.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ} [F.Faithful] : F.leftOp.Faithful
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp_faithful.comment: If F is faithful then the left_op of F is also faithful.

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.

CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp_faithful.fullDefinition: instance leftOp_faithful {F : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ} [Faithful F] : Faithful F.leftOp where   map_injective h := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (map_injective F (Quiver.Hom.unop_inj h))
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp_faithful.description: This definition establishes that if a functor from one category to the opposite of another category is faithful, then its corresponding transformation into a functor from the opposite of the first category to the second category is also faithful.

CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOpRightOpIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOpRightOpIso.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : F.leftOp.rightOp ≅ F

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor from the opposite category to another into a functor from the original category to the opposite of the second category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOpRightOpIso.fullDefinition: def leftOpRightOpIso (F : C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ) : F.leftOp.rightOp ≅ F :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOpRightOpIso.description: This definition asserts that there exists an isomorphism between a functor obtained by applying left and then right operation to a functor from one category to the opposite of another category, and the original functor itself.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOpLeftOpIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOpLeftOpIso.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) : F.rightOp.leftOp ≅ F

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp: This definition specifies a method for transforming a functor from a category to the opposite of another category into a functor from the opposite of the first category to the second category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOpLeftOpIso.fullDefinition: def rightOpLeftOpIso (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) : F.rightOp.leftOp ≅ F :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOpLeftOpIso.description: This definition describes an isomorphism between a functor's right operation followed by its left operation and the original functor itself.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_leftOp_eq.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_leftOp_eq.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) : F.rightOp.leftOp = F
CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_leftOp_eq.comment:
Whenever possible, it is advisable to use the isomorphism `rightOpLeftOpIso`
instead of this equality of functors.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp: This definition specifies a method for transforming a functor from a category to the opposite of another category into a functor from the opposite of the first category to the second category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.rightOp_leftOp_eq.description: The theorem states that applying the right operation followed by the left operation to a functor from the opposite of one category to another yields the original functor itself.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {F G : C ⥤ D} (α : F ⟶ G) : G.op ⟶ F.op
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op.comment: The opposite of a natural transformation.

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.unop: This definition outlines the process of converting a functor from the opposite category back to a functor in the original category.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op.fullDefinition: protected def op (α : F ⟶ G) : G.op ⟶ F.op where   app X := (α.app (unop X)).op   naturality X Y f := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (by simp)
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op.description: This definition describes how to construct a natural transformation between the opposite of one functor and the opposite of another functor from a given natural transformation between those functors.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op_id.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op_id.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) : NatTrans.op (𝟙 F) = 𝟙 F.op

explanatories.CategoryTheory.op_id: The theorem shows that the operation for reversing the direction of the identity morphism in a category equals the identity morphism of the corresponding opposite object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op_id.description: The theorem states that the operation of reversing the direction of the identity natural transformation of a functor yields the identity transformation of the functor in its opposite category.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.unop.code:

CategoryTheory.opEquiv.comment:
The equivalence between arrows of the form `A ⟶ B` and `B.unop ⟶ A.unop`. Useful for building
adjunctions.
Note that this (definitionally) gives variants
```
def opEquiv' (A : C) (B : Cᵒᵖ) : (Opposite.op A ⟶ B) ≃ (B.unop ⟶ A) :=
  opEquiv _ _

def opEquiv'' (A : Cᵒᵖ) (B : C) : (A ⟶ Opposite.op B) ≃ (B ⟶ A.unop) :=
  opEquiv _ _

def opEquiv''' (A B : C) : (Opposite.op A ⟶ Opposite.op B) ≃ (B ⟶ A) :=
  opEquiv _ _
```
