explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.op: This definition describes how to construct a natural transformation between the opposite of one functor and the opposite of another functor from a given natural transformation between those functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.unop: This definition explains how to construct a natural transformation between the original functors from the opposite of one functor to the opposite of another functor based on a given natural transformation between those functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.leftOp: This definition describes a method to construct a natural transformation between the left-opposite functors of two functors from a category to the opposite of another category, using a given natural transformation between the original functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.rightOp: This definition describes how to create a natural transformation between the right opposites of two functors from the right opposite of a given natural transformation between those functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.op: This definition introduces the concept of the opposite isomorphism, which associates an isomorphism between two objects in a category with an isomorphism between their opposites.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.unop: This definition describes a method for retrieving an isomorphism in the original category from an isomorphism that exists in the opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.op: This definition describes a natural isomorphism between the opposite functors of two functors that are naturally isomorphic to each other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.unop: This definition describes the natural isomorphism between the unopposed functors derived from a natural isomorphism between the original functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.op: This definition indicates that an equivalence between two categories implies an equivalence between their respective opposite categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unop: The definition specifies that an equivalence between two opposite categories implies an equivalence between the original categories.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: A value of a type indicates that the type is nonempty.

CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOpRightOpEqui.fullDefinition: def leftOpRightOpEquiv : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D)ᵒᵖ ≌ C ⥤ Dᵒᵖ where   functor :=     { obj := fun F => F.unop.rightOp       map := fun η => NatTrans.rightOp η.unop }   inverse :=     { obj := fun F => op F.leftOp       map := fun η => η.leftOp.op }   unitIso :=     NatIso.ofComponents (fun F => F.unop.rightOpLeftOpIso.op)       (by         intro F G η         dsimp         rw [show η = η.unop.op by simp, ← op_comp, ← op_comp]         congr 1         aesop_cat)   counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun F => F.leftOpRightOpIso
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOpRightOpEqui.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the category of functors from the opposite of one category to another category and the category of functors from the first category to the opposite of the second category.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom.code: CategoryTheory.eqToHom.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) : X ⟶ Y
CategoryTheory.eqToHom.comment:
An equality `X = Y` gives us a morphism `X ⟶ Y`.

It is typically better to use this, rather than rewriting by the equality then using `𝟙 _`
which usually leads to dependent type theory hell.
CategoryTheory.eqToHom.fullDefinition: def eqToHom {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) : X ⟶ Y := by rw [p]; exact 𝟙 _
CategoryTheory.eqToHom.description: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom_refl.code: CategoryTheory.eqToHom_refl.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (X : C) (p : X = X) : eqToHom p = 𝟙 X
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_refl.description: The morphism induced by the reflexive equality of an object in a category is equal to the identity morphism of that object.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom_trans.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_trans.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C} (p : X = Y) (q : Y = Z) :
  eqToHom p ≫ eqToHom q = eqToHom ⋯
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_trans.description: The composition of morphisms induced by two equalities in a category is equal to the morphism induced by the transitive equality relating the first and the last objects.

CategoryTheory.comp_eqToHom_iff.code:
CategoryTheory.comp_eqToHom_iff.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Y' : C} (p : Y = Y') (f : X ⟶ Y)
  (g : X ⟶ Y') : f ≫ eqToHom p = g ↔ f = g ≫ eqToHom ⋯

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.comp_eqToHom_iff.description: The composition of a morphism with an equality-induced morphism is equivalent to the equality of two morphisms when one of them is composed with the same equality-induced morphism on the opposite side.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom_comp_iff.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_comp_iff.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X X' Y : C} (p : X = X') (f : X ⟶ Y)
  (g : X' ⟶ Y) : eqToHom p ≫ g = f ↔ g = eqToHom ⋯ ≫ f
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_comp_iff.description: The equality-induced morphism composed with another morphism is equal to a given morphism if and only if the other morphism can be expressed as the composition of the equality-induced morphism with the given morphism.

CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_left.code:
CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_left.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C} (p : X = Y) (q : Y ⟶ Z) :
  ⋯.mpr q = eqToHom p ≫ q
CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_left.comment:
If we (perhaps unintentionally) perform equational rewriting on
the source object of a morphism,
we can replace the resulting `_.mpr f` term by a composition with an `eqToHom`.

It may be advisable to introduce any necessary `eqToHom` morphisms manually,
rather than relying on this lemma firing.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.Eq.mpr: This defines a cast operation that allows an element from one type to be converted to another type when there is a proof of their equality.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: This theorem states that if two propositions are equivalent and one is true, then the other must also be true.

CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_left.description: The morphism obtained by applying equational rewriting to the source object of another morphism can be expressed as the composition of an equality-induced morphism and that original morphism.

CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_right.code:
CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_right.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C} (p : X ⟶ Y) (q : Z = Y) :
  ⋯.mpr p = p ≫ eqToHom ⋯
CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_right.comment:
If we (perhaps unintentionally) perform equational rewriting on
the target object of a morphism,
we can replace the resulting `_.mpr f` term by a composition with an `eqToHom`.

It may be advisable to introduce any necessary `eqToHom` morphisms manually,
rather than relying on this lemma firing.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.Eq.mpr: This defines a cast operation that allows an element from one type to be converted to another type when there is a proof of their equality.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: This theorem states that if two propositions are equivalent and one is true, then the other must also be true.

CategoryTheory.congrArg_mpr_hom_right.description: The morphism obtained by applying equational rewriting to the target object of another morphism can be expressed as the composition of that original morphism and an equality-induced morphism.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso.code: CategoryTheory.eqToIso.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) : X ≅ Y
CategoryTheory.eqToIso.comment:
An equality `X = Y` gives us an isomorphism `X ≅ Y`.

It is typically better to use this, rather than rewriting by the equality then using `Iso.refl _`
which usually leads to dependent type theory hell.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso.fullDefinition: def eqToIso {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) : X ≅ Y :=   ⟨eqToHom p, eqToHom p.symm, by simp, by simp⟩
CategoryTheory.eqToIso.description: An equality between two objects in a category corresponds to an isomorphism between those objects.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso.hom.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToIso.hom.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) :
  (eqToIso p).hom = eqToHom p

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso.hom.description: The morphism of an isomorphism induced by an equality between two objects in a category is equal to the morphism derived from that equality.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso.inv.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToIso.inv.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) :
  (eqToIso p).inv = eqToHom ⋯

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso.inv.description: The inverse of the isomorphism induced by an equality between two objects in a category is equal to the morphism induced by the equality.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso_refl.code: CategoryTheory.eqToIso_refl.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} (p : X = X) : eqToIso p = Iso.refl X
CategoryTheory.eqToIso_refl.description: The isomorphism induced by an equality of an object with itself is equal to the identity isomorphism of that object.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso_trans.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToIso_trans.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C} (p : X = Y) (q : Y = Z) :
  eqToIso p ≪≫ eqToIso q = eqToIso ⋯
CategoryTheory.eqToIso_trans.description: The composition of isomorphisms induced by two successive equalities between objects is equivalent to the isomorphism induced by the combined equality.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom_op.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_op.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (h : X = Y) :
  (eqToHom h).op = eqToHom ⋯
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_op.description: The morphism induced by an equality between two objects in a category, when taken in the opposite direction, is equal to the morphism induced by that equality.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom_unop.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_unop.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (h : X = Y) :
  (eqToHom h).unop = eqToHom ⋯
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_unop.description: The morphism induced by an equality between two opposite objects in a category corresponds to the morphism induced by that equality but in the original category.

CategoryTheory.inv_eqToHom.code:
CategoryTheory.inv_eqToHom.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (h : X = Y) :
  inv (eqToHom h) = eqToHom ⋯

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToIso.inv: The inverse of the isomorphism induced by an equality between two objects in a category is equal to the morphism induced by the equality.

CategoryTheory.inv_eqToHom.description: The inverse of the morphism induced by an equality between two objects in a category is equal to the morphism induced by the equality in the opposite direction.

_auto._@..lake.packages.mathlib.Mathlib..description: There is a syntax representation in Lean4 called _auto✝ that is used within the context of the language.

CategoryTheory.Functor.ext.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.ext.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {F G : C ⥤ D} (h_obj : ∀ (X : C), F.obj X = G.obj X)
  (h_map : ∀ (X Y : C) (f : X ⟶ Y), F.map f = eqToHom ⋯ ≫ G.map f ≫ eqToHom ⋯ := by aesop_cat) : F = G
CategoryTheory.Functor.ext.comment:
Proving equality between functors. This isn't an extensionality lemma,
because usually you don't really want to do this.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.Functor.ext.description: Two functors from one category to another are equal if they produce the same results on objects and on morphisms for all cases.

CategoryTheory.Functor.conj_eqToHom_iff_.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.conj_eqToHom_iff_heq.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {W X Y Z : C} (f : W ⟶ X)
  (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : W = Y) (h' : X = Z) : f = eqToHom h ≫ g ≫ eqToHom ⋯ ↔ HEq f g
CategoryTheory.Functor.conj_eqToHom_iff_.comment: Two morphisms are conjugate via eqToHom if and only if they are heterogeneously equal.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.Functor.conj_eqToHom_iff_.description: Two morphisms are considered conjugate through an equality-induced morphism if and only if they are heterogeneous equal.

CategoryTheory.Functor.hext.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.hext.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {F G : C ⥤ D} (h_obj : ∀ (X : C), F.obj X = G.obj X) (h_map : ∀ (X Y : C) (f : X ⟶ Y), HEq (F.map f) (G.map f)) :
  F = G
CategoryTheory.Functor.hext.comment: Proving equality between functors using heterogeneous equality.
CategoryTheory.Functor.hext.description: Two functors between categories are equal if they produce the same objects and the same results for morphisms, as verified using heterogeneous equality.

CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_obj.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_obj.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F G : C ⥤ D} (h : F = G) (X : C) : F.obj X = G.obj X
CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_obj.description: If two functors between categories are equal, then they yield equal results when applied to any object from the source category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_hom.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_hom.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F G : C ⥤ D} (h : F = G) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : F.map f = eqToHom ⋯ ≫ G.map f ≫ eqToHom ⋯

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_hom.description: If two functors between categories are equal, then the image of a morphism under one functor can be expressed in terms of the image under the other functor using a specific morphism derived from their equality.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToIso.hom: The morphism of an isomorphism induced by an equality between two objects in a category is equal to the morphism derived from that equality.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToIso.inv: The inverse of the isomorphism induced by an equality between two objects in a category is equal to the morphism induced by the equality.

CategoryTheory.Functor.congr_inv_of_cong.description: The inverse of a natural isomorphism between two objects in a category behaves in a way that is consistent with the equality conditions of the functors acting on those objects.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp_heq.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp_heq.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F G : C ⥤ D} {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} (hx : F.obj X = G.obj X)
  (hy : F.obj Y = G.obj Y) (hz : F.obj Z = G.obj Z) (hf : HEq (F.map f) (G.map f)) (hg : HEq (F.map g) (G.map g)) :
  HEq (F.map (f ≫ g)) (G.map (f ≫ g))
CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp_heq.description: The equality of the functor outputs allows the composition of morphisms to be preserved when the functors are equal up to coherence.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp_heq'.description: If two functors agree on the results for all objects in a category and maintain the equality of their mapped morphisms, then their composition also yields equal results.

CategoryTheory.Functor.precomp_map_heq.description: If two functors produce equal morphisms for all morphisms in a category when composed with another functor, then their compositions with that functor also yield equal morphisms for all morphisms in the resulting category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.postcomp_map_heq.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.postcomp_map_heq.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] {F G : C ⥤ D} {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} (H : D ⥤ E)
  (hx : F.obj X = G.obj X) (hy : F.obj Y = G.obj Y) (hmap : HEq (F.map f) (G.map f)) :
  HEq ((F ⋙ H).map f) ((G ⋙ H).map f)
CategoryTheory.Functor.postcomp_map_heq.description: If two functors produce the same results for specific objects and map corresponding morphisms equally, then their compositions with a subsequent functor also map those morphisms equally.

CategoryTheory.Functor.postcomp_map_heq'.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.postcomp_map_heq'.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] {F G : C ⥤ D} {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} (H : D ⥤ E)
  (hobj : ∀ (X : C), F.obj X = G.obj X) (hmap : ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), HEq (F.map f) (G.map f)) :
  HEq ((F ⋙ H).map f) ((G ⋙ H).map f)
CategoryTheory.Functor.postcomp_map_heq'.description: The equality of the functor outputs and the preservation of morphisms allows the mapping of composed morphisms through a functor to be coherent when both functors are equal.

CategoryTheory.Functor.hcongr_hom.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.hcongr_hom.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F G : C ⥤ D} (h : F = G) {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : HEq (F.map f) (G.map f)
CategoryTheory.Functor.hcongr_hom.description: The equality of two functors implies that they act identically on the morphisms in the source category.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom_map.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) : F.map (eqToHom p) = eqToHom ⋯
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_map.comment:
This is not always a good idea as a `@[simp]` lemma,
as we lose the ability to use results that interact with `F`,
e.g. the naturality of a natural transformation.

In some files it may be appropriate to use `attribute [local simp] eqToHom_map`, however.
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_map.description: Applying a functor to an equality-induced morphism produces a morphism that is equivalent to the equality-induced morphism applied to the functor's source.

CategoryTheory.eqToIso_map.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToIso_map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (p : X = Y) : F.mapIso (eqToIso p) = eqToIso ⋯
CategoryTheory.eqToIso_map.comment: See the note on `eqToHom_map` regarding using this as a `simp` lemma.
CategoryTheory.eqToIso_map.description: The action of a functor on an isomorphism induced by an equality between objects results in an isomorphism that corresponds to the same equality in the target category.

CategoryTheory.eqToHom_app.code:
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_app.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {F G : C ⥤ D} (h : F = G) (X : C) : (eqToHom h).app X = eqToHom ⋯
CategoryTheory.eqToHom_app.description: The morphism induced by the equality of two functors applied to an object in a category is equal to the morphism induced by the same equality when considering that object.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.congr.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.congr.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {F G : C ⥤ D} (α : F ⟶ G) {X Y : C} (h : X = Y) : α.app X = F.map (eqToHom h) ≫ α.app Y ≫ G.map (eqToHom ⋯)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.congr.description: The application of a natural transformation between two functors at equal objects can be expressed in terms of the mappings induced by the equality and the natural transformation itself.

CategoryTheory.eq_conj_eqToHom.code:
CategoryTheory.eq_conj_eqToHom.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  f = eqToHom ⋯ ≫ f ≫ eqToHom ⋯

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.eq_conj_eqToHom.description: A morphism between two objects in a category is equal to the composition of an equality-induced morphism on one side and itself on the other side.

CategoryTheory.dcongr_arg.code:
CategoryTheory.dcongr_arg.{v₁, u₁, u_2} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {ι : Type u_2} {F G : ι → C}
  (α : (i : ι) → F i ⟶ G i) {i j : ι} (h : i = j) : α i = eqToHom ⋯ ≫ α j ≫ eqToHom ⋯

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.

CategoryTheory.dcongr_arg.description: The equality of two morphisms in a category that originate from the same indexed family is preserved when applying a morphism induced by an equality between their indices.

CategoryTheory.prod.code:
CategoryTheory.prod.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  Category.{max v₁ v₂, max u₂ u₁} (C × D)
CategoryTheory.prod.comment:
`prod C D` gives the cartesian product of two categories.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001K>.
CategoryTheory.prod.fullDefinition: instance prod : Category.{max v₁ v₂} (C × D) where   Hom X Y := (X.1 ⟶ Y.1) × (X.2 ⟶ Y.2)   id X := ⟨𝟙 X.1, 𝟙 X.2⟩   comp f g := (f.1 ≫ g.1, f.2 ≫ g.2)
CategoryTheory.prod.description: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.

CategoryTheory.prod_id.code:
CategoryTheory.prod_id.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (X : C)
  (Y : D) : 𝟙 (X, Y) = (𝟙 X, 𝟙 Y)
CategoryTheory.prod_id.comment: Two rfl lemmas that cannot be generated by `@[simps]`.
CategoryTheory.prod_id.description: The theorem states that the identity morphism of the product of two objects is equal to the pair of identity morphisms of the individual objects.

CategoryTheory.prod_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.prod_comp.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {P Q R : C} {S T U : D} (f : (P, S) ⟶ (Q, T)) (g : (Q, T) ⟶ (R, U)) : f ≫ g = (f.1 ≫ g.1, f.2 ≫ g.2)
CategoryTheory.prod_comp.description: The theorem establishes that the composition of two morphisms in the product of two categories corresponds to the composition of their respective components.

CategoryTheory.prod_Hom.code:
CategoryTheory.prod_Hom.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (X Y : C × D) : (X ⟶ Y) = ((X.1 ⟶ Y.1) × (X.2 ⟶ Y.2))
CategoryTheory.prod_Hom.description: The theorem states that the morphisms between two objects in the product of two categories correspond to the pairs of morphisms between their respective components.

CategoryTheory.isIso_prod_iff.code:
CategoryTheory.isIso_prod_iff.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {P Q : C} {S T : D} {f : (P, S) ⟶ (Q, T)} : IsIso f ↔ IsIso f.1 ∧ IsIso f.2
CategoryTheory.isIso_prod_iff.description: The theorem asserts that a morphism in the product of two categories is an isomorphism if and only if both component morphisms are isomorphisms.

CategoryTheory.prod.etaIso.code:
CategoryTheory.prod.etaIso.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (X : C × D) : (X.1, X.2) ≅ X
CategoryTheory.prod.etaIso.fullDefinition: def prod.etaIso (X : C × D) : (X.1, X.2) ≅ X where   hom := (𝟙 _, 𝟙 _)   inv := (𝟙 _, 𝟙 _)
CategoryTheory.prod.etaIso.description: This definition describes the isomorphism between the pair of objects from two categories and their product object in the category formed by their Cartesian product.

CategoryTheory.Iso.prod.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.prod.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  {P Q : C} {S T : D} (f : P ≅ Q) (g : S ≅ T) : (P, S) ≅ (Q, T)
CategoryTheory.Iso.prod.comment: Construct an isomorphism in `C × D` out of two isomorphisms in `C` and `D`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.

CategoryTheory.Iso.prod.fullDefinition: def Iso.prod {P Q : C} {S T : D} (f : P ≅ Q) (g : S ≅ T) : (P, S) ≅ (Q, T) where   hom := (f.hom, g.hom)   inv := (f.inv, g.inv)
CategoryTheory.Iso.prod.description: This definition creates an isomorphism in the product of two categories using two given isomorphisms from each individual category.

CategoryTheory.uniformProd.code:
CategoryTheory.uniformProd.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] :
  Category.{v₁, u₁} (C × D)
CategoryTheory.uniformProd.comment:
`Category.uniformProd C D` is an additional instance specialised so both factors have the same
universe levels. This helps typeclass resolution.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.prod: This definition creates an isomorphism in the product of two categories using two given isomorphisms from each individual category.

CategoryTheory.uniformProd.fullDefinition: instance uniformProd : Category (C × D) :=   CategoryTheory.prod C D
CategoryTheory.uniformProd.description: This definition introduces a category structure on the product of two categories when both categories are in the same universe level.

CategoryTheory.Prod.sectl.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectl.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]
  (Z : D) : C ⥤ C × D
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectl.comment: `sectl C Z` is the functor `C ⥤ C × D` given by `X ↦ (X, Z)`.
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectl.fullDefinition: def sectl (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (Z : D) : C ⥤ C × D where   obj X := (X, Z)   map f := (f, 𝟙 Z)
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectl.description: This definition describes a functor that maps an object from one category to a corresponding object in the product of that category and another category, holding one component constant.

CategoryTheory.Prod.sectr.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectr.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (Z : C) (D : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] : D ⥤ C × D
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectr.comment: `sectr Z D` is the functor `D ⥤ C × D` given by `Y ↦ (Z, Y)` .
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectr.fullDefinition: def sectr {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] (Z : C) (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂} D] : D ⥤ C × D where   obj X := (Z, X)   map f := (𝟙 Z, f)
CategoryTheory.Prod.sectr.description: This definition specifies a functor that maps elements from one category to pairs consisting of a fixed element from another category and the original element.

CategoryTheory.Prod.fst.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.fst.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  C × D ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.Prod.fst.fullDefinition: def fst : C × D ⥤ C where   obj X := X.1   map f := f.1
CategoryTheory.Prod.fst.description: This definition describes a functor that maps an object from the product of two categories to its first component.

CategoryTheory.Prod.snd.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.snd.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  C × D ⥤ D
CategoryTheory.Prod.snd.fullDefinition: def snd : C × D ⥤ D where   obj X := X.2   map f := f.2
CategoryTheory.Prod.snd.description: This definition describes a functor that extracts the second component from pairs in the product of two categories.

CategoryTheory.Prod.swap.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.swap.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  C × D ⥤ D × C
CategoryTheory.Prod.swap.comment: The functor swapping the factors of a cartesian product of categories, `C × D ⥤ D × C`.
CategoryTheory.Prod.swap.fullDefinition: def swap : C × D ⥤ D × C where   obj X := (X.2, X.1)   map f := (f.2, f.1)
CategoryTheory.Prod.swap.description: This definition describes a functor that interchanges the positions of the components in the Cartesian product of two categories.

CategoryTheory.Prod.symmetry.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.symmetry.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  swap C D ⋙ swap D C ≅ 𝟭 (C × D)
CategoryTheory.Prod.symmetry.comment:
Swapping the factors of a cartesian product of categories twice is naturally isomorphic
to the identity functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.swap: This definition describes a functor that interchanges the positions of the components in the Cartesian product of two categories.

CategoryTheory.Prod.symmetry.fullDefinition: def symmetry : swap C D ⋙ swap D C ≅ 𝟭 (C × D) where   hom := { app := fun X => 𝟙 X }   inv := { app := fun X => 𝟙 X }
CategoryTheory.Prod.symmetry.description: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism between the double swapping of factors in the Cartesian product of two categories and the identity functor on that product.

CategoryTheory.Prod.braiding.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.braiding.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  C × D ≌ D × C
CategoryTheory.Prod.braiding.comment: The equivalence, given by swapping factors, between `C × D` and `D × C`.

explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.swap: This definition describes a functor that interchanges the positions of the components in the Cartesian product of two categories.

CategoryTheory.Prod.braiding.fullDefinition: def braiding : C × D ≌ D × C :=   Equivalence.mk (swap C D) (swap D C)     (NatIso.ofComponents fun X => eqToIso (by simp))     (NatIso.ofComponents fun X => eqToIso (by simp))
CategoryTheory.Prod.braiding.description: This definition identifies a categorical equivalence between the product of two categories and the product with swapped factors.

CategoryTheory.Prod.swapIsEquivalence.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.swapIsEquivalence.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] : (swap C D).IsEquivalence

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.braiding: This definition identifies a categorical equivalence between the product of two categories and the product with swapped factors.

CategoryTheory.Prod.swapIsEquivalence.fullDefinition: instance swapIsEquivalence : (swap C D).IsEquivalence :=   (by infer_instance : (braiding C D).functor.IsEquivalence)
CategoryTheory.Prod.swapIsEquivalence.description: This definition asserts that the functor that swaps the components of a Cartesian product of two categories is an equivalence of categories.

CategoryTheory.evaluation.code:
CategoryTheory.evaluation.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  C ⥤ (C ⥤ D) ⥤ D
CategoryTheory.evaluation.comment:
The "evaluation at `X`" functor, such that
`(evaluation.obj X).obj F = F.obj X`,
which is functorial in both `X` and `F`.

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.evaluation.fullDefinition: def evaluation : C ⥤ (C ⥤ D) ⥤ D where   obj X :=     { obj := fun F => F.obj X       map := fun α => α.app X }   map {X} {Y} f :=     { app := fun F => F.map f       naturality := fun {F} {G} α => Eq.symm (α.naturality f) }
CategoryTheory.evaluation.description: This definition describes a functor that evaluates a morphism in a category at a specific object, yielding a functor from the category of functors to another category.

CategoryTheory.evaluationUncurried.code:
CategoryTheory.evaluationUncurried.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] : C × (C ⥤ D) ⥤ D
CategoryTheory.evaluationUncurried.comment:
The "evaluation of `F` at `X`" functor,
as a functor `C × (C ⥤ D) ⥤ D`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod_comp: The theorem establishes that the composition of two morphisms in the product of two categories corresponds to the composition of their respective components.

CategoryTheory.evaluationUncurried.fullDefinition: def evaluationUncurried : C × (C ⥤ D) ⥤ D where   obj p := p.2.obj p.1   map := fun {x} {y} f => x.2.map f.1 ≫ f.2.app y.1   map_comp := fun {X} {Y} {Z} f g => by     cases g; cases f; cases Z; cases Y; cases X     simp only [prod_comp, NatTrans.comp_app, Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]     rw [← NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.naturality, NatTrans.comp_app, Category.assoc,       NatTrans.naturality]
CategoryTheory.evaluationUncurried.description: This definition describes a functor that takes a pair consisting of an object from one category and a morphism from that category to another, mapping it to the object in the second category determined by the morphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.constCompEvaluati.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.constCompEvaluationObj.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (X : C) : Functor.const C ⋙ (evaluation C D).obj X ≅ 𝟭 D
CategoryTheory.Functor.constCompEvaluati.comment: The constant functor followed by the evaluation functor is just the identity.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.evaluation: This definition describes a functor that evaluates a morphism in a category at a specific object, yielding a functor from the category of functors to another category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.constCompEvaluati.fullDefinition: def Functor.constCompEvaluationObj (X : C) : Functor.const C ⋙ (evaluation C D).obj X ≅ 𝟭 D :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun Y => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.constCompEvaluati.description: This definition states that the composition of a constant functor with the evaluation functor at an object is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor on the target category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod.comment: The cartesian product of two functors.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.prod: This definition creates an isomorphism in the product of two categories using two given isomorphisms from each individual category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod.fullDefinition: def prod (F : A ⥤ B) (G : C ⥤ D) : A × C ⥤ B × D where   obj X := (F.obj X.1, G.obj X.2)   map f := (F.map f.1, G.map f.2)
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod.description: This definition establishes a functor that maps the Cartesian product of two categories to the Cartesian product of the images of two functors.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] {B : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] {C : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] (F : A ⥤ B) (G : A ⥤ C) : A ⥤ B × C
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'.comment: Similar to `prod`, but both functors start from the same category `A`
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'.fullDefinition: def prod' (F : A ⥤ B) (G : A ⥤ C) : A ⥤ B × C where   obj a := (F.obj a, G.obj a)   map f := (F.map f, G.map f)
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'.description: This definition describes a functor that creates a new functor from two functors mapping from the same category to a product of two different categories.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompFst.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompFst.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] {B : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] {C : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] (F : A ⥤ B) (G : A ⥤ C) : F.prod' G ⋙ Prod.fst B C ≅ F
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompFst.comment: The product `F.prod' G` followed by projection on the first component is isomorphic to `F`

explanatories.Prod.fst: The first element of a pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.fst: This definition describes a functor that maps an object from the product of two categories to its first component.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompFst.fullDefinition: def prod'CompFst (F : A ⥤ B) (G : A ⥤ C) : F.prod' G ⋙ CategoryTheory.Prod.fst B C ≅ F :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompFst.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a functor that represents the product of two functors followed by the projection onto the first component and the original functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompSnd.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompSnd.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] {B : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] {C : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] (F : A ⥤ B) (G : A ⥤ C) : F.prod' G ⋙ Prod.snd B C ≅ G
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompSnd.comment: The product `F.prod' G` followed by projection on the second component is isomorphic to `G`

explanatories.Prod.snd: The second element of a pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.snd: This definition describes a functor that extracts the second component from pairs in the product of two categories.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompSnd.fullDefinition: def prod'CompSnd (F : A ⥤ B) (G : A ⥤ C) : F.prod' G ⋙ CategoryTheory.Prod.snd B C ≅ G :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompSnd.description: This definition asserts that the composition of the functor formed from two functors followed by the projection onto the second component is isomorphic to the second functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.diag.code: CategoryTheory.Functor.diag.{v₃, u₃} (C : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] : C ⥤ C × C

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod': This definition describes a functor that creates a new functor from two functors mapping from the same category to a product of two different categories.

CategoryTheory.Functor.diag.fullDefinition: def diag : C ⥤ C × C :=   (𝟭 C).prod' (𝟭 C)
CategoryTheory.Functor.diag.description: This definition specifies a functor that maps each object in a category to the corresponding pair of identical objects in the Cartesian product of that category with itself.

CategoryTheory.Functor.diag_obj.code: CategoryTheory.Functor.diag_obj.{v₃, u₃} (C : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] (X : C) : (diag C).obj X = (X, X)
CategoryTheory.Functor.diag_obj.description: The theorem asserts that the object obtained from the diagonal functor at a specified object in a category is a pair consisting of two copies of that object.

CategoryTheory.Functor.diag_map.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.diag_map.{v₃, u₃} (C : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  (diag C).map f = (f, f)
CategoryTheory.Functor.diag_map.description: This theorem states that the diagonal functor applied to a morphism in a category results in a pair consisting of the morphism itself mapped to both components of the product category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.prod: This definition creates an isomorphism in the product of two categories using two given isomorphisms from each individual category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.prod_map.description: This theorem shows that the mapping of morphisms in the Cartesian product of two categories can be expressed as the pair of the individual mappings from each functor.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.prod.comment: The cartesian product of two natural transformations.

explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod_comp: The theorem establishes that the composition of two morphisms in the product of two categories corresponds to the composition of their respective components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.prod: This definition creates an isomorphism in the product of two categories using two given isomorphisms from each individual category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod: This definition establishes a functor that maps the Cartesian product of two categories to the Cartesian product of the images of two functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod_map: This theorem shows that the mapping of morphisms in the Cartesian product of two categories can be expressed as the pair of the individual mappings from each functor.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.prod.fullDefinition: def prod {F G : A ⥤ B} {H I : C ⥤ D} (α : F ⟶ G) (β : H ⟶ I) : F.prod H ⟶ G.prod I where   app X := (α.app X.1, β.app X.2)   naturality {X} {Y} f := by     cases X; cases Y     simp only [Functor.prod_map, prod_comp]     rw [Prod.mk.inj_iff]     constructor     repeat {rw [naturality]}
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.prod.description: This definition constructs a natural transformation between the Cartesian products of two functors by pairing individual transformations from each functor.

CategoryTheory.NatIso.prod.comment: The cartesian product of two natural isomorphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.prod: This definition creates an isomorphism in the product of two categories using two given isomorphisms from each individual category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod: This definition establishes a functor that maps the Cartesian product of two categories to the Cartesian product of the images of two functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.prod: This definition constructs a natural transformation between the Cartesian products of two functors by pairing individual transformations from each functor.

CategoryTheory.NatIso.prod.fullDefinition: def prod {F F' : A ⥤ B} {G G' : C ⥤ D} (e₁ : F ≅ F') (e₂ : G ≅ G') :     F.prod G ≅ F'.prod G' where   hom := NatTrans.prod e₁.hom e₂.hom   inv := NatTrans.prod e₁.inv e₂.inv
CategoryTheory.NatIso.prod.description: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism between the Cartesian products of two functors based on the natural isomorphisms of each functor pair.

CategoryTheory.flipCompEvaluation.comment: `F.flip` composed with evaluation is the same as evaluating `F`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.evaluation: This definition describes a functor that evaluates a morphism in a category at a specific object, yielding a functor from the category of functors to another category.

CategoryTheory.flipCompEvaluation.fullDefinition: def flipCompEvaluation (F : A ⥤ B ⥤ C) (a) : F.flip ⋙ (evaluation _ _).obj a ≅ F.obj a :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun b => eqToIso rfl
CategoryTheory.flipCompEvaluation.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the composition of a flipped functor and an evaluation functor, showing they yield the same result when applied to a specific object from the first category.

CategoryTheory.prodFunctorToFunctorProd.code:
CategoryTheory.prodFunctorToFunctorProd.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (A : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] (B : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] (C : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] : (A ⥤ B) × (A ⥤ C) ⥤ A ⥤ B × C

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod': This definition describes a functor that creates a new functor from two functors mapping from the same category to a product of two different categories.

CategoryTheory.prodFunctorToFunctorProd.fullDefinition: def prodFunctorToFunctorProd : (A ⥤ B) × (A ⥤ C) ⥤ A ⥤ B × C where   obj F := F.1.prod' F.2   map f := { app := fun X => (f.1.app X, f.2.app X) }
CategoryTheory.prodFunctorToFunctorProd.description: This definition describes a functor that maps the Cartesian product of two functors over the same category to a functor that represents the product of their respective outputs.

CategoryTheory.Prod.fst_map.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.fst_map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  ∀ {X Y : C × D} (f : X ⟶ Y), (Prod.fst C D).map f = f.1
CategoryTheory.Prod.fst_map.description: This theorem states that the image of a morphism between pairs in the product of two categories under the projection functor to the first component is equal to the first component of the morphism itself.

CategoryTheory.prod_comp_fst.code:
CategoryTheory.prod_comp_fst.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  ∀ {X Y Z : C × D} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), (f ≫ g).1 = f.1 ≫ g.1
CategoryTheory.prod_comp_fst.description: This theorem establishes that for morphisms in the product of two categories, the composition of morphisms preserves the projection of their first components.

CategoryTheory.Prod.snd_map.code:
CategoryTheory.Prod.snd_map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  ∀ {X Y : C × D} (f : X ⟶ Y), (Prod.snd C D).map f = f.2
CategoryTheory.Prod.snd_map.description: This theorem establishes that the projection functor onto the second component of a product category applied to a morphism yields the second element of the pair corresponding to that morphism.

CategoryTheory.prod_comp_snd.code:
CategoryTheory.prod_comp_snd.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] :
  ∀ {X Y Z : C × D} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z), (f ≫ g).2 = f.2 ≫ g.2
CategoryTheory.prod_comp_snd.description: The theorem asserts that in the composition of morphisms in the product of two categories, the second component of the resulting morphism is equal to the composition of the second components of the individual morphisms.

CategoryTheory.functorProdToProdFunctor.code:
CategoryTheory.functorProdToProdFunctor.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (A : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] (B : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] (C : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] : (A ⥤ B × C) ⥤ (A ⥤ B) × (A ⥤ C)

explanatories.Prod.fst: The first element of a pair.
explanatories.Prod.snd: The second element of a pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.fst: This definition describes a functor that maps an object from the product of two categories to its first component.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.snd: This definition describes a functor that extracts the second component from pairs in the product of two categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.fst_map: This theorem states that the image of a morphism between pairs in the product of two categories under the projection functor to the first component is equal to the first component of the morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod_comp_fst: This theorem establishes that for morphisms in the product of two categories, the composition of morphisms preserves the projection of their first components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.snd_map: This theorem establishes that the projection functor onto the second component of a product category applied to a morphism yields the second element of the pair corresponding to that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod_comp_snd: The theorem asserts that in the composition of morphisms in the product of two categories, the second component of the resulting morphism is equal to the composition of the second components of the individual morphisms.

CategoryTheory.functorProdToProdFunctor.fullDefinition: def functorProdToProdFunctor : (A ⥤ B × C) ⥤ (A ⥤ B) × (A ⥤ C) where   obj F := ⟨F ⋙ CategoryTheory.Prod.fst B C, F ⋙ CategoryTheory.Prod.snd B C⟩   map α :=     ⟨{  app := fun X => (α.app X).1         naturality := fun X Y f => by           simp only [Functor.comp_map, Prod.fst_map, ← prod_comp_fst, α.naturality] },       { app := fun X => (α.app X).2         naturality := fun X Y f => by           simp only [Functor.comp_map, Prod.snd_map, ← prod_comp_snd, α.naturality] }⟩
CategoryTheory.functorProdToProdFunctor.description: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor mapping from one category to the product of two categories into a pair of functors, each mapping to one of those categories.

CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivUn.code:
CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivUnitIso.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (A : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] (B : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] (C : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] :
  𝟭 ((A ⥤ B) × (A ⥤ C)) ≅ prodFunctorToFunctorProd A B C ⋙ functorProdToProdFunctor A B C

explanatories.Prod.fst: The first element of a pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod: This definition constructs the category formed by the Cartesian product of two given categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod.etaIso: This definition describes the isomorphism between the pair of objects from two categories and their product object in the category formed by their Cartesian product.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.prod: This definition creates an isomorphism in the product of two categories using two given isomorphisms from each individual category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Prod.fst: This definition describes a functor that maps an object from the product of two categories to its first component.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod: This definition establishes a functor that maps the Cartesian product of two categories to the Cartesian product of the images of two functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompFst: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a functor that represents the product of two functors followed by the projection onto the first component and the original functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.prod'CompSnd: This definition asserts that the composition of the functor formed from two functors followed by the projection onto the second component is isomorphic to the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.prod: This definition constructs a natural transformation between the Cartesian products of two functors by pairing individual transformations from each functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.prod: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism between the Cartesian products of two functors based on the natural isomorphisms of each functor pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prodFunctorToFunctorProd: This definition describes a functor that maps the Cartesian product of two functors over the same category to a functor that represents the product of their respective outputs.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.functorProdToProdFunctor: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor mapping from one category to the product of two categories into a pair of functors, each mapping to one of those categories.

CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivUn.fullDefinition: def functorProdFunctorEquivUnitIso :     𝟭 _ ≅ prodFunctorToFunctorProd A B C ⋙ functorProdToProdFunctor A B C :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun F =>     (((Functor.prod'CompFst F.fst F.snd).prod (Functor.prod'CompSnd F.fst F.snd)).trans       (prod.etaIso F)).symm
CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivUn.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the identity functor of the product of two functors and the composition of a functor that represents the product of their outputs with another functor that combines them.

CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivCo.code:
CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivCounitIso.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (A : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} A]
  (B : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} B] (C : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] :
  functorProdToProdFunctor A B C ⋙ prodFunctorToFunctorProd A B C ≅ 𝟭 (A ⥤ B × C)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod.etaIso: This definition describes the isomorphism between the pair of objects from two categories and their product object in the category formed by their Cartesian product.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prodFunctorToFunctorProd: This definition describes a functor that maps the Cartesian product of two functors over the same category to a functor that represents the product of their respective outputs.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.functorProdToProdFunctor: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor mapping from one category to the product of two categories into a pair of functors, each mapping to one of those categories.

CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivCo.fullDefinition: def functorProdFunctorEquivCounitIso :     functorProdToProdFunctor A B C ⋙ prodFunctorToFunctorProd A B C ≅ 𝟭 _ :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun F => NatIso.ofComponents fun X => prod.etaIso (F.obj X)
CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivCo.description: This definition states that the composition of a specific functor and its inverse functor results in an isomorphism to the identity functor on the category of functors from one category to the product of two others.

CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquiv.code:
CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquiv.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (A : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} A] (B : Type u₂)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.functorProdToProdFunctor: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor mapping from one category to the product of two categories into a pair of functors, each mapping to one of those categories.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquivCo: This definition states that the composition of a specific functor and its inverse functor results in an isomorphism to the identity functor on the category of functors from one category to the product of two others.

CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquiv.fullDefinition: def functorProdFunctorEquiv : (A ⥤ B) × (A ⥤ C) ≌ A ⥤ B × C :=   { functor := prodFunctorToFunctorProd A B C,     inverse := functorProdToProdFunctor A B C,     unitIso := functorProdFunctorEquivUnitIso A B C,     counitIso := functorProdFunctorEquivCounitIso A B C, }
CategoryTheory.functorProdFunctorEquiv.description: This definition establishes an equivalence of categories between the product of functors from one category to two separate categories and a functor from that category to the Cartesian product of the two categories.

CategoryTheory.prod.associator.code:
CategoryTheory.prod.associator.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (E : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] : (C × D) × E ⥤ C × D × E
CategoryTheory.prod.associator.comment: The associator functor `(C × D) × E ⥤ C × (D × E)`.
CategoryTheory.prod.associator.fullDefinition: def associator : (C × D) × E ⥤ C × D × E where   obj X := (X.1.1, (X.1.2, X.2))   map := @fun _ _ f => (f.1.1, (f.1.2, f.2))
CategoryTheory.prod.associator.description: This definition specifies a functor that transforms the product of two categories and a third category into a rearranged product of the same categories.

CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociator.code:
CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociator.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (E : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] : C × D × E ⥤ (C × D) × E
CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociator.comment: The inverse associator functor `C × (D × E) ⥤ (C × D) × E `.
CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociator.fullDefinition: def inverseAssociator : C × D × E ⥤ (C × D) × E where   obj X := ((X.1, X.2.1), X.2.2)   map := @fun _ _ f => ((f.1, f.2.1), f.2.2)
CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociator.description: This definition specifies a functor that rearranges the product of three categories into a product of two categories and a third one.

CategoryTheory.prod.associativity.code:
CategoryTheory.prod.associativity.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂)
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (E : Type u₃) [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] : (C × D) × E ≌ C × D × E
CategoryTheory.prod.associativity.comment: The equivalence of categories expressing associativity of products of categories.

explanatories.Prod.mk: This theorem provides a way to create a pair consisting of two elements from potentially different types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod.associator: This definition specifies a functor that transforms the product of two categories and a third category into a rearranged product of the same categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociator: This definition specifies a functor that rearranges the product of three categories into a product of two categories and a third one.

CategoryTheory.prod.associativity.fullDefinition: def associativity : (C × D) × E ≌ C × D × E :=   Equivalence.mk (associator C D E) (inverseAssociator C D E)     (NatIso.ofComponents fun X => eqToIso (by simp))     (NatIso.ofComponents fun X => eqToIso (by simp))
CategoryTheory.prod.associativity.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the category formed by the product of two categories and a third category, and the category formed by rearranging the same categories.

CategoryTheory.prod.associatorIsEquivale.code:
CategoryTheory.prod.associatorIsEquivalence.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₂)

CategoryTheory.prod.associatorIsEquivale.description: This definition asserts that the functor which rearranges the product of two categories and a third category into a specific format is an equivalence of categories.

CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociatorIsE.code:
CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociatorIsEquivalence.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]

CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociatorIsE.fullDefinition: instance inverseAssociatorIsEquivalence : (inverseAssociator C D E).IsEquivalence :=   (by infer_instance : (associativity C D E).inverse.IsEquivalence)
CategoryTheory.prod.inverseAssociatorIsE.description: This definition asserts that the functor which rearranges the product of three categories into a product of two categories and a third one is an equivalence of categories.

CategoryTheory.Bifunctor.map_id.code:
CategoryTheory.Bifunctor.map_id.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (F : C × D ⥤ E) (X : C) (Y : D) : F.map (𝟙 X, 𝟙 Y) = 𝟙 (F.obj (X, Y))
CategoryTheory.Bifunctor.map_id.description: This theorem states that applying a bifunctor to the identity morphisms of two objects results in the identity morphism of the image of their pair under the bifunctor.

CategoryTheory.Bifunctor.map_id_comp.description: This theorem establishes that the application of a bifunctor to the composition of two morphisms, along with an identity morphism from a third object, results in the same output as performing the bifunctor on each morphism separately and then composing the results.

CategoryTheory.Bifunctor.map_comp_id.description: This theorem asserts that the application of a bifunctor to the composition of two morphisms from one category alongside an identity morphism from another category yields the same result as applying the bifunctor to each morphism individually with the identity morphism and then composing the resulting transformations.

CategoryTheory.Bifunctor.diagonal.description: This theorem demonstrates that applying a bifunctor to the pair formed by an identity morphism from one object and another morphism, followed by the composition of the bifunctor's outputs, is equivalent to applying the bifunctor directly to the pair of morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Bifunctor.diagonal'.description: This theorem establishes that using a bifunctor on a pair of morphisms, where one is paired with an identity morphism from the second category and the other is paired with an identity morphism from the first category, yields the same result as applying the bifunctor directly to the pair of morphisms from both categories.

CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitor.code: CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitor.{w, v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : Discrete PUnit.{w + 1} × C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitor.comment: The left unitor functor `1 × C ⥤ C`
CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitor.fullDefinition: def leftUnitor : Discrete (PUnit : Type w) × C ⥤ C where   obj X := X.2   map f := f.2
CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitor.description: This definition introduces a functor that maps ordered pairs consisting of a singleton type and an object from a category to that same category, serving as the left unitor in the context of categorical operations.

CategoryTheory.prod.leftInverseUnitor.code: CategoryTheory.prod.leftInverseUnitor.{w, v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : C ⥤ Discrete PUnit.{w + 1} × C

CategoryTheory.prod.leftInverseUnitor.fullDefinition: def leftInverseUnitor : C ⥤ Discrete (PUnit : Type w) × C where   obj X := ⟨⟨PUnit.unit⟩, X⟩   map f := ⟨𝟙 _, f⟩
CategoryTheory.prod.leftInverseUnitor.description: This definition establishes a functor that maps objects from a category to ordered pairs consisting of a singleton type and that same object, acting as the left inverse unitor in categorical operations.

CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitor.code: CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitor.{w, v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : C × Discrete PUnit.{w + 1} ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitor.fullDefinition: def rightUnitor : C × Discrete (PUnit : Type w) ⥤ C where   obj X := X.1   map f := f.1
CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitor.description: This definition introduces a functor that maps ordered pairs consisting of an object from a category and a singleton type back to that same category, serving as the right unitor in categorical operations.

CategoryTheory.prod.rightInverseUnitor.code: CategoryTheory.prod.rightInverseUnitor.{w, v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : C ⥤ C × Discrete PUnit.{w + 1}

explanatories.PUnit.unit: This theorem states that there exists a distinguished element of the unit type.

CategoryTheory.prod.rightInverseUnitor.fullDefinition: def rightInverseUnitor : C ⥤ C × Discrete (PUnit : Type w) where   obj X := ⟨X, ⟨PUnit.unit⟩⟩   map f := ⟨f, 𝟙 _⟩
CategoryTheory.prod.rightInverseUnitor.description: This definition defines a functor that maps objects from a category to ordered pairs consisting of that same object and a singleton type, functioning as the right inverse unitor in categorical contexts.

CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitorEquivalenc.code: CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitorEquivalence.{w, v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : Discrete PUnit.{w + 1} × C ≌ C
CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitorEquivalenc.comment: The equivalence of categories expressing left unity of products of categories.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.prod.leftInverseUnitor: This definition establishes a functor that maps objects from a category to ordered pairs consisting of a singleton type and that same object, acting as the left inverse unitor in categorical operations.

CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitorEquivalenc.fullDefinition: def leftUnitorEquivalence : Discrete (PUnit : Type w) × C ≌ C where   functor := leftUnitor C   inverse := leftInverseUnitor C   unitIso := Iso.refl _   counitIso := Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.prod.leftUnitorEquivalenc.description: This definition asserts that there is an equivalence of categories between the product of a singleton type and a category and the category itself, reflecting the concept of left unity in categorical products.

CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitorEquivalen.code: CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitorEquivalence.{w, v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : C × Discrete PUnit.{w + 1} ≌ C
CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitorEquivalen.comment: The equivalence of categories expressing right unity of products of categories.

CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitorEquivalen.fullDefinition: def rightUnitorEquivalence : C × Discrete (PUnit : Type w) ≌ C where   functor := rightUnitor C   inverse := rightInverseUnitor C   unitIso := Iso.refl _   counitIso := Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.prod.rightUnitorEquivalen.description: This definition asserts the equivalence of categories between ordered pairs of objects from a category and a singleton type and the original category itself, demonstrating the concept of right unity in categorical products.

CategoryTheory.Comma.isoMk.fullDefinition: def isoMk {X Y : Comma L₁ R₁} (l : X.left ≅ Y.left) (r : X.right ≅ Y.right)     (h : L₁.map l.hom ≫ Y.hom = X.hom ≫ R₁.map r.hom := by aesop_cat) : X ≅ Y where   hom :=     { left := l.hom       right := r.hom       w := h }   inv :=     { left := l.inv       right := r.inv       w := by         rw [← L₁.mapIso_inv l, Iso.inv_comp_eq, L₁.mapIso_hom, ← Category.assoc, h,           Category.assoc, ← R₁.map_comp]         simp }

CategoryTheory.Comma.map.fullDefinition: def map : Comma L R ⥤ Comma L' R' where   obj X :=     { left := F₁.obj X.left       right := F₂.obj X.right       hom := α.app X.left ≫ F.map X.hom ≫ β.app X.right }   map {X Y} φ :=     { left := F₁.map φ.left       right := F₂.map φ.right       w := by         dsimp         rw [assoc, assoc]         erw [α.naturality_assoc, ← β.naturality]         dsimp         rw [← F.map_comp_assoc, ← F.map_comp_assoc, φ.w] }
