CategoryTheory.Comma.post.fullDefinition: def post (L : A ⥤ T) (R : B ⥤ T) (F : T ⥤ C) : Comma L R ⥤ Comma (L ⋙ F) (R ⋙ F) where   obj X :=     { left := X.left       right := X.right       hom := F.map X.hom }   map f :=     { left := f.left       right := f.right       w := by simp only [Functor.comp_map, ← F.map_comp, f.w] }
CategoryTheory.Comma.post.description: This definition establishes a functor that transforms objects in a comma category defined by two functors into a comma category defined by the composition of those functors with a third functor.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.{v, u} (T : Type u) [Category.{v, u} T] : Type (max u v)
CategoryTheory.Arrow.comment:
The arrow category of `T` has as objects all morphisms in `T` and as morphisms commutative
squares in `T`.
CategoryTheory.Arrow.fullDefinition: def Arrow :=   Comma.{v, v, v} (𝟭 T) (𝟭 T)
CategoryTheory.Arrow.description: This definition characterizes the arrow category of a given category by including its morphisms as objects and defining its morphisms as commutative squares among these morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.inhabited.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.inhabited.{v, u} (T : Type u) [Category.{v, u} T] [Inhabited T] : Inhabited (Arrow T)

explanatories.Inhabited.default: A default function provides a standard element from any inhabited type, which typically represents a general or neutral value.
explanatories.Lean.Meta.TransparencyMode.default: This theorem defines a mode for evaluating expressions that allows all constants to be unfolded except those marked as irreducible.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.inhabited.fullDefinition: instance Arrow.inhabited [Inhabited T] : Inhabited (Arrow T) where   default := show Comma (𝟭 T) (𝟭 T) from default
CategoryTheory.Arrow.inhabited.description: This definition states that if a category has inhabitants, then its arrow category also possesses inhabitants.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_left.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_left.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] (f : Arrow T) : (𝟙 f).left = 𝟙 f.left
CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_left.description: This theorem demonstrates that the left component of the identity morphism in the arrow category corresponds to the identity morphism of the left object in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_right.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] (f : Arrow T) : (𝟙 f).right = 𝟙 f.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_right.description: This theorem establishes that the right component of the identity morphism in the arrow category is equal to the identity morphism of the right object in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {X Y : T} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Arrow T
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk.comment: An object in the arrow category is simply a morphism in `T`.
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk.fullDefinition: def mk {X Y : T} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Arrow T where   left := X   right := Y   hom := f
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk.description: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_eq.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_eq.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] (f : Arrow T) : mk f.hom = f
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_eq.description: This theorem asserts that the construction of an arrow category object from a morphism is equivalent to the original arrow object itself.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_injective.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_injective.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] (A B : T) : Function.Injective mk
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_injective.description: This theorem establishes that the operation of constructing arrow objects in a category is injective, meaning different inputs lead to different outputs.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_inj.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_inj.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] (A B : T) {f g : A ⟶ B} : mk f = mk g ↔ f = g
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_inj.description: This theorem asserts that two arrow objects constructed from morphisms are equal if and only if the morphisms themselves are equal.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} {u : f.left ⟶ g.left}
  {v : f.right ⟶ g.right} (w : u ≫ g.hom = f.hom ≫ v) : f ⟶ g
CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk.comment:
A morphism in the arrow category is a commutative square connecting two objects of the arrow
category.
CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk.fullDefinition: def homMk {f g : Arrow T} {u : f.left ⟶ g.left} {v : f.right ⟶ g.right}     (w : u ≫ g.hom = f.hom ≫ v) : f ⟶ g where   left := u   right := v   w := w
CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk.description: This definition describes a morphism in the arrow category as a commutative square that connects two specified objects within that category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk'.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk'.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {X Y : T} {f : X ⟶ Y} {P Q : T} {g : P ⟶ Q}
  {u : X ⟶ P} {v : Y ⟶ Q} (w : u ≫ g = f ≫ v) : mk f ⟶ mk g
CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk'.comment: We can also build a morphism in the arrow category out of any commutative square in `T`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk'.fullDefinition: def homMk' {X Y : T} {f : X ⟶ Y} {P Q : T} {g : P ⟶ Q} {u : X ⟶ P} {v : Y ⟶ Q} (w : u ≫ g = f ≫ v) :     Arrow.mk f ⟶ Arrow.mk g where   left := u   right := v   w := w
CategoryTheory.Arrow.homMk'.description: This definition allows the construction of a morphism in the arrow category from any commutative square formed by specified objects and morphisms in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.w.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.w.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) :
  sq.left ≫ g.hom = f.hom ≫ sq.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.w.description: This theorem demonstrates a relationship between the components of a morphism between two objects in the arrow category and the homs associated with those objects.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.w_mk_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.w_mk_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f : Arrow T} {X Y : T} {g : X ⟶ Y}
  (sq : f ⟶ mk g) : sq.left ≫ g = f.hom ≫ sq.right

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.w_mk_right.description: This theorem demonstrates a relationship between two morphisms in the context of a square involving an arrow object and a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_of_isIso_left.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_of_isIso_left_of_isIso_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T}
  (ff : f ⟶ g) [IsIso ff.left] [IsIso ff.right] : IsIso ff
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_of_isIso_left.description: This theorem states that if a morphism between two arrow objects is isomorphic on both its left and right components, then the morphism itself is also isomorphic.

_auto._@..lake.packages.mathlib.Mathlib..description: This definition specifies a syntax element for use in Lean's parsing process.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (l : f.left ≅ g.left)
  (r : f.right ≅ g.right) (h : l.hom ≫ g.hom = f.hom ≫ r.hom := by aesop_cat) : f ≅ g
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk.comment:
Create an isomorphism between arrows,
by providing isomorphisms between the domains and codomains,
and a proof that the square commutes.
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk.fullDefinition: def isoMk {f g : Arrow T} (l : f.left ≅ g.left) (r : f.right ≅ g.right)     (h : l.hom ≫ g.hom = f.hom ≫ r.hom := by aesop_cat) : f ≅ g :=   Comma.isoMk l r h
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk.description: This definition establishes a method to construct an isomorphism between two arrows by requiring isomorphisms between their respective domains and codomains, along with a verification that the relevant square commutes.

_auto._@..lake.packages.mathlib.Mathlib..description: This definition specifies a particular syntax structure used in the Lean programming language.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk'.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk'.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {W X Y Z : T} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (e₁ : W ≅ Y)
  (e₂ : X ≅ Z) (h : e₁.hom ≫ g = f ≫ e₂.hom := by aesop_cat) : mk f ≅ mk g
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk'.comment:
A variant of `Arrow.isoMk` that creates an iso between two `Arrow.mk`s with a better type
signature.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk'.fullDefinition: abbrev isoMk' {W X Y Z : T} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (e₁ : W ≅ Y) (e₂ : X ≅ Z)     (h : e₁.hom ≫ g = f ≫ e₂.hom := by aesop_cat) : Arrow.mk f ≅ Arrow.mk g :=   Arrow.isoMk e₁ e₂ h
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isoMk'.description: This definition establishes a way to create an isomorphism between two arrow objects in the arrow category based on given morphisms and specified isomorphisms between their respective source and target objects.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.hom.congr_left.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.hom.congr_left.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} {φ₁ φ₂ : f ⟶ g}
  (h : φ₁ = φ₂) : φ₁.left = φ₂.left
CategoryTheory.Arrow.hom.congr_left.description: This theorem asserts that if two morphisms between arrows are equal, then their corresponding components in the domain must also be equal.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.hom.congr_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.hom.congr_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} {φ₁ φ₂ : f ⟶ g}
  (h : φ₁ = φ₂) : φ₁.right = φ₂.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.hom.congr_right.description: This theorem asserts that if two morphisms between arrow objects are equal, then their corresponding right components are also equal.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {X Y Z : Arrow T} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
  (f ≫ g).right = f.right ≫ g.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_right.description: This theorem demonstrates that the right component of the composition of two morphisms in the arrow category can be expressed as the composition of their respective right components.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.w_assoc.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.w_assoc.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) {Z : T}
  (h : g.right ⟶ Z) : sq.left ≫ g.hom ≫ h = f.hom ≫ sq.right ≫ h
CategoryTheory.Arrow.w_assoc.description: This theorem posits that for a morphism between two arrow objects and a morphism from the right component of the second arrow object to a third object, a specific equality involving the left and right components of the morphism can be established.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.iso_w.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.iso_w.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (e : f ≅ g) :
  g.hom = e.inv.left ≫ f.hom ≫ e.hom.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.iso_w.description: This theorem states that for two isomorphic arrow objects, the morphism of one can be expressed in terms of the morphism of the other and the components of the isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.iso_w'.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.iso_w'.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {W X Y Z : T} {f : W ⟶ X} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
  (e : mk f ≅ mk g) : g = e.inv.left ≫ f ≫ e.hom.right

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.iso_w'.description: This theorem states that an equality involving a morphism between two objects in the arrow category can be expressed in terms of an isomorphism between their corresponding arrow objects and the components of the morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_left.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_left.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) [IsIso sq] :
  IsIso sq.left

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_left: This theorem demonstrates that the left component of the identity morphism in the arrow category corresponds to the identity morphism of the left object in the original category.
explanatories.Exists.intro: This theorem states that if an element exists in a type and satisfies a given property, then there is a proof of the existence of that element with the property.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: This theorem states that any element is equal to itself if and only if the statement is true.
explanatories.and_self_iff: This theorem states that a conjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the original proposition.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_left.fullDefinition: instance isIso_left [IsIso sq] : IsIso sq.left where   out := by     apply Exists.intro (inv sq).left     simp only [← Comma.comp_left, IsIso.hom_inv_id, IsIso.inv_hom_id, Arrow.id_left,       eq_self_iff_true, and_self_iff]     simp
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_left.description: This definition asserts that if a morphism between two arrow objects is an isomorphism, then the left component of that morphism is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) [IsIso sq] :
  IsIso sq.right

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.id_right: This theorem establishes that the right component of the identity morphism in the arrow category is equal to the identity morphism of the right object in the original category.
explanatories.Exists.intro: This theorem states that if an element exists in a type and satisfies a given property, then there is a proof of the existence of that element with the property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_right: This theorem demonstrates that the right component of the composition of two morphisms in the arrow category can be expressed as the composition of their respective right components.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: This theorem states that any element is equal to itself if and only if the statement is true.
explanatories.and_self_iff: This theorem states that a conjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the original proposition.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_right.fullDefinition: instance isIso_right [IsIso sq] : IsIso sq.right where   out := by     apply Exists.intro (inv sq).right     simp only [← Comma.comp_right, IsIso.hom_inv_id, IsIso.inv_hom_id, Arrow.id_right,       eq_self_iff_true, and_self_iff]     simp
CategoryTheory.Arrow.isIso_right.description: This definition shows that if a morphism between arrow objects is an isomorphism, then its corresponding right component is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_left.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_left.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) [IsIso sq] :
  (inv sq).left = inv sq.left
CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_left.description: This theorem establishes that for an isomorphism in the arrow category, the left component of its inverse is equal to the inverse of its left component.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) [IsIso sq] :
  (inv sq).right = inv sq.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_right.description: This theorem asserts that for an isomorphism between two arrows, the right component of the inverse morphism is equal to the inverse of the right component of the original isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.left_hom_inv_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.left_hom_inv_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g)
  [IsIso sq] : sq.left ≫ g.hom ≫ inv sq.right = f.hom
CategoryTheory.Arrow.left_hom_inv_right.description: This theorem states that for an isomorphism in the arrow category, the composition of the left component of a morphism with the right component of its inverse, along with a right morphism from the second arrow object, yields the left morphism of the first arrow object.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_left_hom_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_left_hom_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g)
  [IsIso sq] : inv sq.left ≫ f.hom ≫ sq.right = g.hom
CategoryTheory.Arrow.inv_left_hom_right.description: This theorem asserts that for an isomorphic morphism between two arrow objects, the left inverse of the morphism composed with the left component and the right component of the first arrow yields the right component of the second arrow.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.mono_left.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mono_left.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) [Mono sq] :
  Mono sq.left

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.w: This theorem demonstrates a relationship between the components of a morphism between two objects in the arrow category and the homs associated with those objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_right: This theorem demonstrates that the right component of the composition of two morphisms in the arrow category can be expressed as the composition of their respective right components.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.mono_left.fullDefinition: instance mono_left [Mono sq] : Mono sq.left where   right_cancellation {Z} φ ψ h := by     let aux : (Z ⟶ f.left) → (Arrow.mk (𝟙 Z) ⟶ f) := fun φ =>       { left := φ         right := φ ≫ f.hom }     have : ∀ g, (aux g).right = g ≫ f.hom := fun g => by dsimp     show (aux φ).left = (aux ψ).left     congr 1     rw [← cancel_mono sq]     apply CommaMorphism.ext     · exact h     · rw [Comma.comp_right, Comma.comp_right, this, this, Category.assoc, Category.assoc]       rw [← Arrow.w]       simp only [← Category.assoc, h]
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mono_left.description: This definition states that if a morphism between two arrows is monomorphic, then the left component of that morphism is also monomorphic.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.epi_right.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.epi_right.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {f g : Arrow T} (sq : f ⟶ g) [Epi sq] :
  Epi sq.right

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.w_assoc: This theorem posits that for a morphism between two arrow objects and a morphism from the right component of the second arrow object to a third object, a specific equality involving the left and right components of the morphism can be established.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.epi_right.fullDefinition: instance epi_right [Epi sq] : Epi sq.right where   left_cancellation {Z} φ ψ h := by     let aux : (g.right ⟶ Z) → (g ⟶ Arrow.mk (𝟙 Z)) := fun φ =>       { right := φ         left := g.hom ≫ φ }     show (aux φ).right = (aux ψ).right     congr 1     rw [← cancel_epi sq]     apply CommaMorphism.ext     · rw [Comma.comp_left, Comma.comp_left, Arrow.w_assoc, Arrow.w_assoc, h]     · exact h
CategoryTheory.Arrow.epi_right.description: This definition states that if a morphism in the arrow category is epimorphic, then its right component is also epimorphic.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_left.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_left.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {X Y Z : Arrow T} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
  (f ≫ g).left = f.left ≫ g.left
CategoryTheory.Arrow.comp_left.description: This theorem shows that the left component of the composition of two morphisms in the arrow category equals the composition of their respective left components.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_to_iso_inver.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_to_iso_invert.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] (i : Arrow T) {X Y : T} (p : X ≅ Y)
  (sq : i ⟶ mk p.hom) : i.hom ≫ sq.right ≫ p.inv = sq.left
CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_to_iso_inver.comment:
Given a square from an arrow `i` to an isomorphism `p`, express the source part of `sq`
in terms of the inverse of `p`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_to_iso_inver.description: This theorem provides a way to relate the source component of a square involving an arrow to the right component and the inverse of an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_hom.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_hom.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {X Y : T} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (mk f).hom = f
CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk_hom.description: This theorem states that the morphism of an arrow object constructed from a given morphism is equal to the original morphism itself.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_from_iso_inv.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_from_iso_invert.{v, u} {T : Type u} [Category.{v, u} T] {X Y : T} (i : X ≅ Y) (p : Arrow T)
  (sq : mk i.hom ⟶ p) : i.inv ≫ sq.left ≫ p.hom = sq.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_from_iso_inv.comment:
Given a square from an isomorphism `i` to an arrow `p`, express the target part of `sq`
in terms of the inverse of `i`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.square_from_iso_inv.description: This theorem demonstrates how to relate components of a square involving an isomorphism to the elements of an arrow object by expressing the target part in terms of the isomorphism's inverse.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.squareToSnd.code:
CategoryTheory.Arrow.squareToSnd.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y Z : C} {i : Arrow C} {f : X ⟶ Y}
  {g : Y ⟶ Z} (sq : i ⟶ mk (f ≫ g)) : i ⟶ mk g
CategoryTheory.Arrow.squareToSnd.comment:
A helper construction: given a square between `i` and `f ≫ g`, produce a square between
`i` and `g`, whose top leg uses `f`:
A  → X
     ↓f
↓i   Y             --> A → Y
     ↓g                ↓i  ↓g
B  → Z                 B → Z

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.squareToSnd.fullDefinition: def squareToSnd {X Y Z : C} {i : Arrow C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z} (sq : i ⟶ Arrow.mk (f ≫ g)) :     i ⟶ Arrow.mk g where   left := sq.left ≫ f   right := sq.right
CategoryTheory.Arrow.squareToSnd.description: This definition provides a method to derive a square in the arrow category involving a morphism to `g` from a given square related to the composition of two morphisms, where one of the morphisms is used as the upper leg of the square.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftFunc.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftFunc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] : Arrow C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftFunc.comment: The functor sending an arrow to its source.
CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftFunc.fullDefinition: def leftFunc : Arrow C ⥤ C :=   Comma.fst _ _
CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftFunc.description: This definition outlines a functor that maps an arrow in a category to its source object.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.rightFunc.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.rightFunc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] : Arrow C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.Arrow.rightFunc.comment: The functor sending an arrow to its target.
CategoryTheory.Arrow.rightFunc.fullDefinition: def rightFunc : Arrow C ⥤ C :=   Comma.snd _ _
CategoryTheory.Arrow.rightFunc.description: This definition introduces a functor that maps each arrow in a category to its corresponding target object.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftToRight.code: CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftToRight.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] : leftFunc ⟶ rightFunc
CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftToRight.comment: The natural transformation from `leftFunc` to `rightFunc`, given by the arrow itself.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftFunc: This definition outlines a functor that maps an arrow in a category to its source object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.rightFunc: This definition introduces a functor that maps each arrow in a category to its corresponding target object.

CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftToRight.fullDefinition: def leftToRight : (leftFunc : Arrow C ⥤ C) ⟶ rightFunc where app f := f.hom
CategoryTheory.Arrow.leftToRight.description: This definition describes a natural transformation that connects the functor mapping arrows to their sources with the functor mapping arrows to their targets.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapArrow.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapArrow.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D]

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapArrow.fullDefinition: def mapArrow (F : C ⥤ D) : Arrow C ⥤ Arrow D where   obj a :=     { left := F.obj a.left       right := F.obj a.right       hom := F.map a.hom }   map f :=     { left := F.map f.left       right := F.map f.right       w := by         let w := f.w         simp only [id_map] at w         dsimp         simp only [← F.map_comp, w] }
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapArrow.description: This definition establishes that a functor between two categories induces a corresponding functor between their respective arrow categories.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapArrowFunctor.fullDefinition: def mapArrowFunctor : (C ⥤ D) ⥤ (Arrow C ⥤ Arrow D) where   obj F := F.mapArrow   map τ :=     { app := fun f =>         { left := τ.app _           right := τ.app _ } }

CategoryTheory.Functor.toStructuredArrow.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.toStructuredArrow.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (G : E ⥤ C) (X : D) (F : C ⥤ D)
  (f : (Y : E) → X ⟶ F.obj (G.obj Y)) (h : ∀ {Y Z : E} (g : Y ⟶ Z), f Y ≫ F.map (G.map g) = f Z) :
  E ⥤ StructuredArrow X F
CategoryTheory.Functor.toStructuredArrow.comment:
Given `X : D` and `F : C ⥤ D`, to upgrade a functor `G : E ⥤ C` to a functor
`E ⥤ StructuredArrow X F`, it suffices to provide maps `X ⟶ F.obj (G.obj Y)` for all `Y` making
the obvious triangles involving all `F.map (G.map g)` commute.

This is of course the same as providing a cone over `F ⋙ G` with cone point `X`, see
`Functor.toStructuredArrowIsoToStructuredArrow`.

CategoryTheory.Functor.toStructuredArrow.fullDefinition: def toStructuredArrow (G : E ⥤ C) (X : D) (F : C ⥤ D) (f : (Y : E) → X ⟶ F.obj (G.obj Y))     (h : ∀ {Y Z : E} (g : Y ⟶ Z), f Y ≫ F.map (G.map g) = f Z) : E ⥤ StructuredArrow X F where   obj Y := StructuredArrow.mk (f Y)   map g := StructuredArrow.homMk (G.map g) (h g)

CategoryTheory.Functor.toCostructuredArrow.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}

  (f : (Y : E) → F.obj (G.obj Y) ⟶ X) (h : ∀ {Y Z : E} (g : Y ⟶ Z), F.map (G.map g) ≫ f Z = f Y) :
  E ⥤ CostructuredArrow F X
CategoryTheory.Functor.toCostructuredArr.comment:
Given `F : C ⥤ D` and `X : D`, to upgrade a functor `G : E ⥤ C` to a functor
`E ⥤ CostructuredArrow F X`, it suffices to provide maps `F.obj (G.obj Y) ⟶ X` for all `Y`
making the obvious triangles involving all `F.map (G.map g)` commute.

This is of course the same as providing a cocone over `F ⋙ G` with cocone point `X`, see

CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.toUnder.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {T : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} T] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (X : T) (F : D ⥤ T) : StructuredArrow X F ⥤ Under X
CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.toUnder.comment:
Reinterpreting an `F`-structured arrow `X ⟶ F.obj d` as an arrow under `X` induces a functor
`StructuredArrow X F ⥤ Under X`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.pre: This definition describes a functor that maps costructured arrows formed by the composition of two functors to a costructured arrow formed by the second functor while maintaining a fixed object in the target category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Under: This definition introduces the under category consisting of arrows with a specified object as their domain, where morphisms are represented by commutative diagrams involving these arrows.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.pre: This definition describes a functor that relates structured arrows with a fixed object in one category and two functors, transitioning from the composition of the functors to the latter functor alone while maintaining the same structured arrow object.

CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.toUnder.fullDefinition: def toUnder (X : T) (F : D ⥤ T) : StructuredArrow X F ⥤ Under X :=   StructuredArrow.pre X F (𝟭 T)
CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.toUnder.description: This definition establishes a functor that maps structured arrows formed by an object in one category and a functor to another category into arrows under that object in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.toOver.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.toOver.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {T : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} T] {S : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} S]
  (F : S ⥤ T) (X : T) (f : (Y : S) → F.obj Y ⟶ X) (h : ∀ {Y Z : S} (g : Y ⟶ Z), F.map g ≫ f Z = f Y) : S ⥤ Over X
CategoryTheory.Functor.toOver.comment:
Given `X : T`, to upgrade a functor `F : S ⥤ T` to a functor `S ⥤ Over X`, it suffices to
provide maps `F.obj Y ⟶ X` for all `Y` making the obvious triangles involving all `F.map g`
commute.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow: This definition describes a structure where the objects are morphisms from the image of a functor to a target, along with morphisms that maintain a commutative triangle relationship.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Over: This definition describes a category where the objects are arrows with a specified codomain, and the morphisms are structures that maintain the commutativity of triangles formed by these arrows.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Over.map: A given morphism between two objects induces a functor that maps the over category of the first object to the over category of the second object in a straightforward manner.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.toOver: This definition describes a functor that translates costructured arrows into over arrows over a given object, providing a way to relate these two categorical structures.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Under.map: This definition describes a functor that maps the under category of one object to the under category of another object based on the morphism connecting them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.toCostructuredArr: This definition describes how to upgrade a functor from one category to a functor into the category of costructured arrows by providing mappings that ensure the necessary commutativity conditions involving the functor compositions are satisfied.

CategoryTheory.Functor.toOver.fullDefinition: def toOver (F : S ⥤ T) (X : T) (f : (Y : S) → F.obj Y ⟶ X)     (h : ∀ {Y Z : S} (g : Y ⟶ Z), F.map g ≫ f Z = f Y) : S ⥤ Over X :=   F.toCostructuredArrow (𝟭 _) X f h
CategoryTheory.Functor.toOver.description: The definition establishes a method for transforming a functor into one that operates in the over category by providing appropriate mappings and ensuring the necessary commutativity conditions are satisfied.

CategoryTheory.Functor.toUnder.code:

  (F : S ⥤ T) (X : T) (f : (Y : S) → X ⟶ F.obj Y) (h : ∀ {Y Z : S} (g : Y ⟶ Z), f Y ≫ F.map g = f Z) : S ⥤ Under X
CategoryTheory.Functor.toUnder.comment:
Given `X : T`, to upgrade a functor `F : S ⥤ T` to a functor `S ⥤ Under X`, it suffices to

CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.OverArrows.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {A F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (η : F ⟶ A)
  {X : C} (s : yoneda.obj X ⟶ A) : Type v
CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.OverArrow.comment:
This is equivalent to the type `Over.mk s ⟶ Over.mk η`, but that lives in the wrong universe.
However, if `F = yoneda.obj Y` for some `Y`, then (using that the Yoneda embedding is fully
faithful) we get a good statement, see `OverArrow.costructuredArrowIso`.
CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.OverArrow.fullDefinition: def OverArrows {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (η : F ⟶ A) {X : C} (s : yoneda.obj X ⟶ A) : Type v :=   Subtype (MakesOverArrow η s)
CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.OverArrow.description: This definition introduces a type representing relationships between a presheaf morphism and a structure in the context of the Yoneda embedding within a given category.

CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.OverArrow.code:

  {X : C} {s : yoneda.obj X ⟶ A} : OverArrows η s → F.obj (op X)
CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.OverArrow.comment:
Since `OverArrows η s` can be thought of to contain certain morphisms `yoneda.obj X ⟶ F`, the
Yoneda lemma yields elements `F.obj (op X)`.

CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.YonedaCol.comment:
To give an object of `Over A`, we will in particular need a presheaf `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v`. This is the
definition of that presheaf on objects.

We would prefer to think of this sigma type to be indexed by natural transformations
`yoneda.obj X ⟶ A` instead of `A.obj (op X)`. These are equivalent by the Yoneda lemma, but

CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.counitAux.fullDefinition: def counitAuxAux (F : (CostructuredArrow yoneda A)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (s : CostructuredArrow yoneda A) :     F.obj (op s) ≅ OverArrows (yonedaCollectionPresheafToA F) s.hom where   hom := counitForward F s   inv := counitBackward F s   hom_inv_id := counitBackward_counitForward F s   inv_hom_id := counitForward_counitBackward F s

CategoryTheory.overEquivPresheafCostruct.code:
CategoryTheory.overEquivPresheafCostructuredArrow.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (A : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) :
  Over A ≌ (CostructuredArrow yoneda A)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v
CategoryTheory.overEquivPresheafCostruct.comment:
If `A : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` is a presheaf, then we have an equivalence between presheaves lying over
`A` and the category of presheaves on `CostructuredArrow yoneda A`. There is a quasicommutative
triangle involving this equivalence, see
`CostructuredArrow.toOverCompOverEquivPresheafCostructuredArrow`.

This is Lemma 1.4.12 in [Kashiwara2006].

CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.toOverYon.code:
CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.toOverYonedaCompRestrictedYoneda.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (A : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) : toOver yoneda A ⋙ restrictedYoneda A ≅ yoneda
CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.toOverYon.comment:
Further restricting the functor
`restrictedYoneda : Over A ⥤ (CostructuredArrow yoneda A)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` along the forgetful
functor in the first argument recovers the Yoneda embedding
`CostructuredArrow yoneda A ⥤ (CostructuredArrow yoneda A)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v`. This basically follows
from the fact that the Yoneda embedding on `C` is fully faithful.

CategoryTheory.OverPresheafAux.toOverYon.fullDefinition: def toOverYonedaCompRestrictedYoneda (A : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) :     CostructuredArrow.toOver yoneda A ⋙ restrictedYoneda A ≅ yoneda :=   NatIso.ofComponents     (fun s => NatIso.ofComponents (fun t => OverArrows.costructuredArrowIso _ _) (by aesop_cat))     (by aesop_cat)

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.comment: The induced functor on the quotient category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.as: This definition identifies an object in a category associated with a specific equivalence relation on the morphisms of that category.
explanatories.Quot.liftOn: This defines an operation that rearranges the arguments of a lifting function to prioritize the quotient as the first input.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a quotient category, ensuring that the composition is well-defined under a specified relation on the morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.fullDefinition: def lift : Quotient r ⥤ D where   obj a := F.obj a.as   map := @fun a b hf ↦     Quot.liftOn hf (fun f ↦ F.map f)       (by         rintro _ _ ⟨_, _, _, _, h⟩         simp [H _ _ _ _ h])   map_id a := F.map_id a.as   map_comp := by     rintro a b c ⟨f⟩ ⟨g⟩     exact F.map_comp f g
CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.description: This definition describes a functor that is induced from a functor between categories and a relation on morphisms, allowing for the mapping of the quotient category formed by that relation to another category.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift_spec.code:
CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift_spec.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] (r : HomRel C)
  {D : Type u_3} [Category.{u_4, u_3} D] (F : C ⥤ D) (H : ∀ (x y : C) (f₁ f₂ : x ⟶ y), r f₁ f₂ → F.map f₁ = F.map f₂) :

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor: This definition describes a functor that maps a category to its quotient category formed by an equivalence relation on the morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift_spec.description: This theorem demonstrates that a functor that respects a specified relation on morphisms can be equivalently represented as the composition of lifting this relation through the functor and the functor itself.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift_unique.code:
CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift_unique.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_3} [Category.{u_1, u_3} C] (r : HomRel C)
  {D : Type u_4} [Category.{u_2, u_4} D] (F : C ⥤ D) (H : ∀ (x y : C) (f₁ f₂ : x ⟶ y), r f₁ f₂ → F.map f₁ = F.map f₂)
  (Φ : Quotient r ⥤ D) (hΦ : functor r ⋙ Φ = F) : Φ = lift r F H

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift_unique.description: This theorem establishes that if a functor from one category to another respects a given morphism relation in terms of equality after mapping, then the functor from the quotient category to the target category is uniquely defined up to isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift.comment: The original functor factors through the induced functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor: This definition describes a functor that maps a category to its quotient category formed by an equivalence relation on the morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift.fullDefinition: def lift.isLift : functor r ⋙ lift r F H ≅ F :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X ↦ Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift.description: This definition indicates that a functor from one category can be equivalently expressed as a composition with a lifted functor that respects a given relation on morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift_hom.code:
CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift_hom.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_4} [Category.{u_3, u_4} C] (r : HomRel C)
  {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_1, u_2} D] (F : C ⥤ D) (H : ∀ (x y : C) (f₁ f₂ : x ⟶ y), r f₁ f₂ → F.map f₁ = F.map f₂)

explanatories.HomRel: This definition specifies a relation on the set of morphisms for a given quiver, capturing the structure of hom-sets within that quiver.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift_hom.description: This theorem establishes that a specific natural transformation associated with a functor from one category to another, under a given relationship on morphisms, maps each object to its identity in the target category.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift_inv.code:

CategoryTheory.Quotient.lift.isLift_inv.description: This theorem demonstrates that the inverse of a lift induced by a functor on a category respects equivalence relations by mapping an object to the identity morphism of its image under the functor.

  {D : Type u_4} [Category.{u_3, u_4} D] (F : C ⥤ D) (H : ∀ (x y : C) (f₁ f₂ : x ⟶ y), r f₁ f₂ → F.map f₁ = F.map f₂)

CategoryTheory.Quotient.natTransLift.comment:
In order to define a natural transformation `F ⟶ G` with `F G : Quotient r ⥤ D`, it suffices
to do so after precomposing with `Quotient.functor r`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor: This definition describes a functor that maps a category to its quotient category formed by an equivalence relation on the morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.natTransLift.fullDefinition: def natTransLift {F G : Quotient r ⥤ D} (τ : Quotient.functor r ⋙ F ⟶ Quotient.functor r ⋙ G) :     F ⟶ G where   app := fun ⟨X⟩ => τ.app X   naturality := fun ⟨X⟩ ⟨Y⟩ => by     rintro ⟨f⟩     exact τ.naturality f
CategoryTheory.Quotient.natTransLift.description: This definition describes a method to obtain a natural transformation between two functors from a quotient category by first applying a functor that respects the underlying morphism relation.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.comp_natTransLif.code:
CategoryTheory.Quotient.comp_natTransLift.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_3} [Category.{u_1, u_3} C] (r : HomRel C)
  {D : Type u_4} [Category.{u_2, u_4} D] {F G H : Quotient r ⥤ D} (τ : functor r ⋙ F ⟶ functor r ⋙ G)
  (τ' : functor r ⋙ G ⟶ functor r ⋙ H) : natTransLift r τ ≫ natTransLift r τ' = natTransLift r (τ ≫ τ')

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.natTransLift: This definition describes a method to obtain a natural transformation between two functors from a quotient category by first applying a functor that respects the underlying morphism relation.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.comp_natTransLif.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of two natural transformations, obtained by lifting through a functor related by a specified relation, results in the natural transformation obtained by composing the original transformations before lifting.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.natTransLift_id.code:

CategoryTheory.Quotient.natTransLift_id.description: This theorem shows that the natural transformation lifting from the identity functor of a quotient category to a functor respects the identity by being equal to the identity natural transformation of the target functor.

CategoryTheory.sum.code:
CategoryTheory.sum.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] :
  Category.{v₁, u₁} (C ⊕ D)
CategoryTheory.sum.comment: `sum C D` gives the direct sum of two categories.

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.sum.fullDefinition: instance sum : Category.{v₁} (Sum C D) where   Hom X Y :=     match X, Y with     | inl X, inl Y => X ⟶ Y     | inl _, inr _ => PEmpty     | inr _, inl _ => PEmpty     | inr X, inr Y => X ⟶ Y   id X :=     match X with     | inl X => 𝟙 X     | inr X => 𝟙 X   comp {X Y Z} f g :=     match X, Y, Z, f, g with     | inl X, inl Y, inl Z, f, g => f ≫ g     | inr X, inr Y, inr Z, f, g => f ≫ g   assoc {W X Y Z} f g h :=     match X, Y, Z, W with     | inl X, inl Y, inl Z, inl W => Category.assoc f g h     | inr X, inr Y, inr Z, inr W => Category.assoc f g h
CategoryTheory.sum.description: This definition describes a category that represents the direct sum of two given categories.

CategoryTheory.hom_inl_inr_false.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  {X : C} {Y : D} (f : inl X ⟶ inr Y) : False

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.hom_inl_inr_false.description: This theorem states that there are no morphisms from an object of the first category to an object of the second category within a direct sum type.

CategoryTheory.hom_inr_inl_false.code:
CategoryTheory.hom_inr_inl_false.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  {X : C} {Y : D} (f : inr X ⟶ inl Y) : False

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.hom_inr_inl_false.description: This theorem asserts that there can be no morphisms from an object of the second category to an object of the first category within a direct sum type.

CategoryTheory.sum_comp_inl.code:
CategoryTheory.sum_comp_inl.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] {P Q R : C}
  (f : inl P ⟶ inl Q) (g : inl Q ⟶ inl R) : f ≫ g = f ≫ g

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.sum_comp_inl.description: This theorem confirms that the composition of two morphisms from one object to another within the first category remains consistent when expressed in terms of their compositions.

CategoryTheory.sum_comp_inr.code:
CategoryTheory.sum_comp_inr.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] {P Q R : D}
  (f : inr P ⟶ inr Q) (g : inr Q ⟶ inr R) : f ≫ g = f ≫ g

explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.sum_comp_inr.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of two morphisms from one object to another within the second category remains consistent when expressed in terms of their compositions.

CategoryTheory.Sum.inl_.code: CategoryTheory.Sum.inl_.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] : C ⥤ C ⊕ D
CategoryTheory.Sum.inl_.fullDefinition: def inl_ : C ⥤ Sum C D where   obj X := inl X   map {X Y} f := f
CategoryTheory.Sum.inl_.description: This definition describes a functor that maps objects from the first category to a sum type by embedding them as elements of the left part of the union.

CategoryTheory.Sum.inr_.code: CategoryTheory.Sum.inr_.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] : D ⥤ C ⊕ D
CategoryTheory.Sum.inr_.fullDefinition: def inr_ : D ⥤ Sum C D where   obj X := inr X   map {X Y} f := f
CategoryTheory.Sum.inr_.description: This definition describes a functor that maps objects from the second category to a sum type by embedding them as elements of the right part of the union.

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap.code: CategoryTheory.Sum.swap.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] : C ⊕ D ⥤ D ⊕ C
CategoryTheory.Sum.swap.comment: The functor exchanging two direct summand categories.

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.
explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap.fullDefinition: def swap : Sum C D ⥤ Sum D C where   obj X :=     match X with     | inl X => inr X     | inr X => inl X   map := @fun X Y f =>     match X, Y, f with     | inl _, inl _, f => f     | inr _, inr _, f => f   map_comp := fun {X} {Y} {Z} _ _ =>     match X, Y, Z with     | inl X, inl Y, inl Z => by rfl     | inr X, inr Y, inr Z => by rfl
CategoryTheory.Sum.swap.description: This definition introduces a functor that swaps the two components of a direct sum type, mapping objects from the first category to the second and vice versa.

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_obj_inl.code:
CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_obj_inl.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  (X : C) : (swap C D).obj (inl X) = inr X

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_obj_inl.description: This theorem states that applying the functor that swaps two direct summand categories to an object from the first category results in an object from the second category.

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_obj_inr.code:
CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_obj_inr.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  (X : D) : (swap C D).obj (inr X) = inl X

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_obj_inr.description: This theorem states that applying a certain operation to an object embedded in the second category yields an object embedded in the first category.

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_map_inl.code:
CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_map_inl.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]

CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_map_inr.code:
CategoryTheory.Sum.swap_map_inr.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  {X Y : D} {f : inr X ⟶ inr Y} : (swap C D).map f = f

CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.equivalence.code:
CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.equivalence.{v₁, u₁} (C : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (D : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} D] :
  C ⊕ D ≌ D ⊕ C
CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.equivalence.comment: `swap` gives an equivalence between `C ⊕ D` and `D ⊕ C`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sum.swap: This definition introduces a functor that swaps the two components of a direct sum type, mapping objects from the first category to the second and vice versa.

CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.equivalence.fullDefinition: def equivalence : Sum C D ≌ Sum D C :=   Equivalence.mk (swap C D) (swap D C)     (NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => eqToIso (by cases X <;> rfl)))     (NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => eqToIso (by cases X <;> rfl)))
CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.equivalence.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the direct sum of two categories and the direct sum of those categories in reverse order.

CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.isEquivalence.fullDefinition: instance isEquivalence : (swap C D).IsEquivalence :=   (by infer_instance : (equivalence C D).functor.IsEquivalence)

CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.symmetry.fullDefinition: def symmetry : swap C D ⋙ swap D C ≅ 𝟭 (Sum C D) :=   (equivalence C D).unitIso.symm
CategoryTheory.Sum.Swap.symmetry.description: This definition shows that applying the swap operation between two categories in both directions results in a structure that is naturally isomorphic to the original sum type.

CategoryTheory.Functor.sum.fullDefinition: def sum (F : A ⥤ B) (G : C ⥤ D) : Sum A C ⥤ Sum B D where   obj X :=     match X with     | inl X => inl (F.obj X)     | inr X => inr (G.obj X)   map {X Y} f :=     match X, Y, f with     | inl X, inl Y, f => F.map f     | inr X, inr Y, f => G.map f   map_id {X} := by cases X <;> (erw [Functor.map_id]; rfl)   map_comp {X Y Z} f g :=     match X, Y, Z, f, g with     | inl X, inl Y, inl Z, f, g => by erw [F.map_comp]; rfl     | inr X, inr Y, inr Z, f, g => by erw [G.map_comp]; rfl
CategoryTheory.Functor.sum.description: This definition describes a functor that combines two functors, mapping objects from their respective categories into a direct sum of these categories.

CategoryTheory.Functor.sum'.fullDefinition: def sum' (F : A ⥤ C) (G : B ⥤ C) : Sum A B ⥤ C where   obj X :=     match X with     | inl X => F.obj X     | inr X => G.obj X   map {X Y} f :=     match X, Y, f with     | inl _, inl _, f => F.map f     | inr _, inr _, f => G.map f   map_id {X} := by cases X <;> erw [Functor.map_id]   map_comp {X Y Z} f g :=     match X, Y, Z, f, g with     | inl _, inl _, inl _, f, g => by erw [F.map_comp]     | inr _, inr _, inr _, f, g => by erw [G.map_comp]

CategoryTheory.sum.associator.fullDefinition: def associator : Sum (Sum C D) E ⥤ Sum C (Sum D E) where   obj X :=     match X with     | inl (inl X) => inl X     | inl (inr X) => inr (inl X)     | inr X => inr (inr X)   map {X Y} f :=     match X, Y, f with     | inl (inl _), inl (inl _), f => f     | inl (inr _), inl (inr _), f => f     | inr _, inr _, f => f   map_id := by rintro ((_|_)|_) <;> rfl   map_comp := by     rintro ((_|_)|_) ((_|_)|_) ((_|_)|_) f g <;> first | cases f | cases g | aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.sum.inverseAssociator.fullDefinition: def inverseAssociator : Sum C (Sum D E) ⥤ Sum (Sum C D) E where   obj X :=     match X with     | inl X => inl (inl X)     | inr (inl X) => inl (inr X)     | inr (inr X) => inr X   map {X Y} f :=     match X, Y, f with     | inl _, inl _, f => f     | inr (inl _), inr (inl _), f => f     | inr (inr _), inr (inr _), f => f   map_id := by rintro (_|(_|_)) <;> rfl   map_comp := by     rintro (_|(_|_)) (_|(_|_)) (_|(_|_)) f g <;> first | cases f | cases g | aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.sum.associativity.fullDefinition: def associativity : Sum (Sum C D) E ≌ Sum C (Sum D E) :=   Equivalence.mk (associator C D E) (inverseAssociator C D E)     (NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => eqToIso       (by rcases X with ((_|_)|_) <;> rfl)) -- Porting note: aesop_cat fails       (by rintro ((_|_)|_) ((_|_)|_) f <;> first | cases f | aesop_cat))     (NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => eqToIso       (by rcases X with (_|(_|_)) <;> rfl)) -- Porting note: aesop_cat fails       (by rintro (_|(_|_)) (_|(_|_)) f <;> first | cases f | aesop_cat))
CategoryTheory.sum.associativity.description: This definition establishes an equivalence of categories that reflects the associative property of nested sums of three categories.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [self : MonoidalCategory C]

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon.description: This theorem expresses the pentagon identity that relates different ways to associate tensor products in a monoidal category, ensuring coherence in the structure of these products.

  {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : f ▷ 𝟙_ C = (ρ_ X).hom ≫ f ≫ (ρ_ Y).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerR.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between the whiskering operation and the identity morphism in a monoidal category, showing how the structure is preserved through this operation.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_id.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [self : MonoidalCategory C]
  (X₁ X₂ : C) : 𝟙 X₁ ⊗ 𝟙 X₂ = 𝟙 (X₁ ⊗ X₂)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.comment: Tensor product of identity maps is the identity: `(𝟙 X₁ ⊗ 𝟙 X₂) = 𝟙 (X₁ ⊗ X₂)`
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.description: The theorem establishes that the tensor product of identity morphisms for two objects in a monoidal category is equal to the identity morphism for their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whisker_.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whisker_exchange.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y Z : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : W ◁ g ≫ f ▷ Z = f ▷ Y ≫ X ◁ g
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whisker_.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between the composition of left whiskering and right whiskering of morphisms in a monoidal category, showing that these operations can be interchanged under certain conditions.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (W : C) {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : W ◁ (f ≫ g) = W ◁ f ≫ W ◁ g
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.description: This theorem establishes that left whiskering a composition of morphisms in a monoidal category is equivalent to the composition of the left whiskerings of each individual morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_whi.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_whiskerRight.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (Z : C) : (f ≫ g) ▷ Z = f ▷ Z ≫ g ▷ Z
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_whi.description: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two morphisms followed by a right whiskering operation with a fixed object is equal to the sequential application of the right whiskering operation to each morphism followed by their composition.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeftIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] (X : C)
  {Y Z : C} (f : Y ≅ Z) : X ⊗ Y ≅ X ⊗ Z
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.comment: The left whiskering of an isomorphism is an isomorphism.
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.fullDefinition: def whiskerLeftIso (X : C) {Y Z : C} (f : Y ≅ Z) : X ⊗ Y ≅ X ⊗ Z where   hom := X ◁ f.hom   inv := X ◁ f.inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.description: This definition states that applying the left whiskering operation to an isomorphism between two objects in a monoidal category results in an isomorphism between their tensor products with a third object.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerR.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerRightIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X Y : C} (f : X ≅ Y) (Z : C) : X ⊗ Z ≅ Y ⊗ Z
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerR.comment: The right whiskering of an isomorphism is an isomorphism.
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerR.fullDefinition: def whiskerRightIso {X Y : C} (f : X ≅ Y) (Z : C) : X ⊗ Z ≅ Y ⊗ Z where   hom := f.hom ▷ Z   inv := f.inv ▷ Z
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerR.description: This definition states that whiskering an isomorphism on the right with another object in a monoidal category yields a new isomorphism between the tensor products of the two objects.

CategoryTheory.tensorIso.code:
CategoryTheory.tensorIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} {X Y X' Y' : C} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] (f : X ≅ Y)
  (g : X' ≅ Y') : X ⊗ X' ≅ Y ⊗ Y'
CategoryTheory.tensorIso.comment: The tensor product of two isomorphisms is an isomorphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_c: This theorem establishes that the composition of tensor products of morphisms equals the tensor product of their respective compositions in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i: The theorem establishes that the tensor product of identity morphisms for two objects in a monoidal category is equal to the identity morphism for their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.tensorIso.fullDefinition: def tensorIso {C : Type u} {X Y X' Y' : C} [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory.{v} C] (f : X ≅ Y)     (g : X' ≅ Y') : X ⊗ X' ≅ Y ⊗ Y' where   hom := f.hom ⊗ g.hom   inv := f.inv ⊗ g.inv   hom_inv_id := by rw [← tensor_comp, Iso.hom_inv_id, Iso.hom_inv_id, ← tensor_id]   inv_hom_id := by rw [← tensor_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id, Iso.inv_hom_id, ← tensor_id]
CategoryTheory.tensorIso.description: This definition states that the tensor product of two isomorphic objects in a monoidal category is also an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.«term_⊗_».comment: Notation for `tensorIso`, the tensor product of isomorphisms
CategoryTheory.«term_⊗_».fullDefinition: /- Copyright (c) 2018 Michael Jendrusch. All rights reserved. Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE. Authors: Michael Jendrusch, Scott Morrison, Bhavik Mehta, Jakob von Raumer -/ import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Trifunctor import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Products.Basic
CategoryTheory.«term_⊗_».description: This definition introduces notation for the tensor product operation specifically for isomorphisms in category theory.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_isIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {W X Y Z : C}
  (f : W ⟶ X) [IsIso f] (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsIso g] : IsIso (f ⊗ g)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.fullDefinition: instance tensor_isIso {W X Y Z : C} (f : W ⟶ X) [IsIso f] (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsIso g] : IsIso (f ⊗ g) :=   (asIso f ⊗ asIso g).isIso_hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.description: This definition specifies that the tensor product of two isomorphisms in a monoidal category is itself an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_tens.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_tensor.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {W X Y Z : C}
  (f : W ⟶ X) [IsIso f] (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsIso g] : inv (f ⊗ g) = inv f ⊗ inv g
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_tens.description: This theorem states that the inverse of the tensor product of two isomorphisms in a monoidal category is equal to the tensor product of their respective inverses.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_d.description: This theorem states that the tensor product of a morphism with a decision-dependent morphism can be expressed equivalently using conditional branching based on the truth of a property.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.dite_ten.description: This theorem shows that the tensor product with a morphism in a monoidal category behaves consistently under a dependent choice based on a proposition that is decidable.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnit.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnitor_inv_naturality.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : f ≫ (λ_ Y).inv = (λ_ X).inv ≫ 𝟙_ C ◁ f
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnit.description: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the left unitor morphism behaves naturally with respect to the composition of morphisms in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUnitor_inv_naturality.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X X' : C} (f : X ⟶ X') : f ≫ (ρ_ X').inv = (ρ_ X).inv ≫ f ▷ 𝟙_ C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.description: This theorem establishes the naturality of the inverse of the right unitor in a monoidal category by relating the composition of morphisms with the inverses of the right unitors for different objects.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon_inv.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y Z : C} :
  W ◁ (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ (α_ W (X ⊗ Y) Z).inv ≫ (α_ W X Y).inv ▷ Z = (α_ W X (Y ⊗ Z)).inv ≫ (α_ (W ⊗ X) Y Z).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon.description: This theorem expresses a specific relationship between the inverse isomorphisms involved in the associativity of objects within a monoidal category, demonstrating a certain symmetry in their composition.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle_assoc_comp_right.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (X Y : C) : (α_ X (𝟙_ C) Y).inv ≫ (ρ_ X).hom ▷ Y = X ◁ (λ_ Y).hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of specific isomorphisms involving the tensor products and unit object in a monoidal category satisfies an associativity condition.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle_assoc_comp_right_inv.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y : C) : (ρ_ X).inv ▷ Y ≫ (α_ X (𝟙_ C) Y).hom = X ◁ (λ_ Y).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle.description: This theorem demonstrates a relationship in a monoidal category involving the composition of certain morphisms and associators, indicating how the inverse of the right unitor whiskered with an object together with the associator yields a specific reconfiguration of objects and morphisms.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle_assoc_comp_left_inv.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y : C) : X ◁ (λ_ Y).inv ≫ (α_ X (𝟙_ C) Y).inv = (ρ_ X).inv ▷ Y
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle.description: This theorem describes a relationship involving the composition of morphisms and the associator and left unitor inverses in a monoidal category, illustrating an equation that connects them through objects.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_iff.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y : C}
  (f g : X ⟶ Y) : 𝟙_ C ◁ f = 𝟙_ C ◁ g ↔ f = g
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.description: This theorem establishes that if the left whiskering of two morphisms by the identity morphism is equal, then the two morphisms must be identical.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [self : MonoidalCategory C]
  (W X Y Z : C) :
  ∀ {Z_1 : C} (h : W ⊗ X ⊗ Y ⊗ Z ⟶ Z_1),
    (α_ W X Y).hom ▷ Z ≫ (α_ W (X ⊗ Y) Z).hom ≫ W ◁ (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ h = (α_ (W ⊗ X) Y Z).hom ≫ (α_ W X (Y ⊗ Z)).hom ≫ h
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon.description: This theorem expresses a relationship among the associators in a monoidal category, illustrating a specific equation involving the composition of morphisms across four objects that reflects the pentagon associativity property.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associator_naturality_middle.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X : C) {Y Y' : C} (f : Y ⟶ Y') (Z : C) :
  (X ◁ f) ▷ Z ≫ (α_ X Y' Z).hom = (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ X ◁ f ▷ Z
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This theorem establishes the naturality of the associator in a monoidal category, indicating a specific relationship between the morphisms and the associator when composing with a morphism between two objects.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_whi.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_whiskerRight_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (Z : C) : ∀ {Z_1 : C} (h : Y ⊗ Z ⟶ Z_1), (f ≫ g) ▷ Z ≫ h = f ▷ Z ≫ g ▷ Z ≫ h
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_whi.description: This theorem establishes an associative property of right whiskering in a monoidal category, allowing for the sequential application of morphisms while preserving the structure when combined with another object.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associator_naturality_left.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X X' : C} (f : X ⟶ X') (Y Z : C) : f ▷ Y ▷ Z ≫ (α_ X' Y Z).hom = (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ f ▷ (Y ⊗ Z)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This theorem asserts that the composition of a morphism with the left naturality condition of the associator in a monoidal category is preserved under certain morphisms between objects.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerR.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerRight_iff.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y : C}
  (f g : X ⟶ Y) : f ▷ 𝟙_ C = g ▷ 𝟙_ C ↔ f = g
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerR.description: This theorem states that two morphisms between objects in a monoidal category are equal if and only if their right whiskering with the identity morphism of the category results in the same morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon_inv_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y Z : C} :
  ∀ {Z_1 : C} (h : ((W ⊗ X) ⊗ Y) ⊗ Z ⟶ Z_1),
    W ◁ (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ (α_ W (X ⊗ Y) Z).inv ≫ (α_ W X Y).inv ▷ Z ≫ h = (α_ W X (Y ⊗ Z)).inv ≫ (α_ (W ⊗ X) Y Z).inv ≫ h
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon.description: This theorem expresses a certain equation involving the inverses of associators in a monoidal category, which relates morphisms coming from different configurations of tensor products.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associator_inv_naturality_middle.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X : C) {Y Y' : C} (f : Y ⟶ Y') (Z : C) :
  X ◁ f ▷ Z ≫ (α_ X Y' Z).inv = (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ (X ◁ f) ▷ Z
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This theorem shows that the inverse of the associator morphism in a monoidal category is compatible with the naturality condition when one of the objects changes through a morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (W : C) {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : ∀ {Z_1 : C} (h : W ⊗ Z ⟶ Z_1), W ◁ (f ≫ g) ≫ h = W ◁ f ≫ W ◁ g ≫ h
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL.description: This theorem demonstrates the associativity of the left whiskering operation in a monoidal category when applied to the composition of morphisms.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associator_inv_naturality_right.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y : C) {Z Z' : C} (f : Z ⟶ Z') : X ◁ Y ◁ f ≫ (α_ X Y Z').inv = (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ (X ⊗ Y) ◁ f
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This theorem describes the naturality of the inverse of the associator in a monoidal category, relating the left whiskering of a morphism and the corresponding morphism adjusted by the associator's inverse.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUnitor_tensor.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (X Y : C) : (ρ_ (X ⊗ Y)).hom = (α_ X Y (𝟙_ C)).hom ≫ X ◁ (ρ_ Y).hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.description: This theorem establishes an equality involving morphisms in a monoidal category, relating the right unitor of a tensor product to an associator and a morphism from the first object.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUnitor_tensor_inv.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (X Y : C) : (ρ_ (X ⊗ Y)).inv = X ◁ (ρ_ Y).inv ≫ (α_ X Y (𝟙_ C)).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.description: This theorem shows the equivalence of the inverse of the right unitor for the tensor product of two objects in a monoidal category with a specific composition of the left action of one object and the inverse of the right unitor of the other object along with the associator.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associator_inv_naturality.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X Y Z X' Y' Z' : C} (f : X ⟶ X') (g : Y ⟶ Y') (h : Z ⟶ Z') :
  (f ⊗ g ⊗ h) ≫ (α_ X' Y' Z').inv = (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ ((f ⊗ g) ⊗ h)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This theorem demonstrates the naturality of the inverse of the associator in a monoidal category, showing how it relates morphisms through the tensor product structure.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associator_conjugation.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X X' Y Y' Z Z' : C} (f : X ⟶ X') (g : Y ⟶ Y') (h : Z ⟶ Z') :
  (f ⊗ g) ⊗ h = (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ (f ⊗ g ⊗ h) ≫ (α_ X' Y' Z').inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between the tensor product of three morphisms in a monoidal category and their rearrangement via the associator isomorphisms, showing that the compositions yield the same result.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associator_inv_conjugation.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X X' Y Y' Z Z' : C} (f : X ⟶ X') (g : Y ⟶ Y') (h : Z ⟶ Z') :
  f ⊗ g ⊗ h = (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ ((f ⊗ g) ⊗ h) ≫ (α_ X' Y' Z').hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This theorem establishes an equation involving the associator morphism in a monoidal category, demonstrating a relationship between the tensor product of three morphisms and the action of the associator's inverse and its corresponding morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tensor_associator_naturality.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y Z Z' : C} (h : Z ⟶ Z') :
  (𝟙 (X ⊗ Y) ⊗ h) ≫ (α_ X Y Z').hom = (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ (𝟙 X ⊗ 𝟙 Y ⊗ h)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.description: This theorem establishes how the naturality of the associator in monoidal categories relates the identity morphism on a tensor product with a morphism into another object through appropriate compositions.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tensor_associator_inv_naturality.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y Z X' : C} (f : X ⟶ X') :
  (f ⊗ 𝟙 (Y ⊗ Z)) ≫ (α_ X' Y Z).inv = (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ ((f ⊗ 𝟙 Y) ⊗ 𝟙 Z)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.description: This theorem establishes a compatibility condition for the inverse of the associator morphism in a monoidal category when applying a morphism to an object while keeping others fixed through tensor operations.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.hom_inv_.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.hom_inv_id_tensor.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {V W X Y Z : C} (f : V ≅ W) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (f.hom ⊗ g) ≫ (f.inv ⊗ h) = (𝟙 V ⊗ g) ≫ (𝟙 V ⊗ h)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.hom_inv_.description: This theorem states that the composition of a morphism obtained from isomorphisms and other morphisms in a monoidal category will yield the same result as the composition of identity morphisms with those morphisms.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_hom_.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_hom_id_tensor.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {V W X Y Z : C} (f : V ≅ W) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (f.inv ⊗ g) ≫ (f.hom ⊗ h) = (𝟙 W ⊗ g) ≫ (𝟙 W ⊗ h)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_hom_.description: This theorem establishes a relationship involving the inverse and homomorphism of an isomorphism combined with morphisms in a monoidal category, equating two specific compositions of these morphisms.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_h.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_hom_inv_id.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {V W X Y Z : C} (f : V ≅ W) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (g ⊗ f.hom) ≫ (h ⊗ f.inv) = (g ⊗ 𝟙 V) ≫ (h ⊗ 𝟙 V)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_h.description: This theorem asserts that the composition of a morphism with the homomorphism and the inverse of an isomorphism in a monoidal category is equal to the composition of the morphism with the identity morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_inv_hom_id.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {V W X Y Z : C} (f : V ≅ W) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (g ⊗ f.inv) ≫ (h ⊗ f.hom) = (g ⊗ 𝟙 W) ≫ (h ⊗ 𝟙 W)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.description: This theorem demonstrates a specific condition that relates the composition of tensor products involving an isomorphism and morphisms in a monoidal category, indicating a particular equivalence under certain operations.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.hom_inv_.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.hom_inv_id_tensor'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {V W X Y Z : C} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f] (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (f ⊗ g) ≫ (inv f ⊗ h) = (𝟙 V ⊗ g) ≫ (𝟙 V ⊗ h)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.hom_inv_.description: This theorem establishes a relationship involving the tensor product of morphisms in a monoidal category, asserting that a specific composition of these morphisms is equivalent to another composition that includes the identity morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_hom_.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_hom_id_tensor'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {V W X Y Z : C} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f] (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (inv f ⊗ g) ≫ (f ⊗ h) = (𝟙 W ⊗ g) ≫ (𝟙 W ⊗ h)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.inv_hom_.description: This theorem asserts an equivalence involving the tensor product and morphisms in a monoidal category, demonstrating that the composition of an inverse morphism with another morphism equals the composition of identity morphisms with the latter morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_h.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_hom_inv_id'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {V W X Y Z : C} (f : V ⟶ W) [IsIso f] (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z) : (g ⊗ f) ≫ (h ⊗ inv f) = (g ⊗ 𝟙 V) ≫ (h ⊗ 𝟙 V)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_h.description: This theorem asserts that for a morphism that is an isomorphism, the composition of certain tensor products of morphisms involving the isomorphism and its inverse is equivalent to a specific simplified tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_inv_hom_id'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
