CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_ten.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_tensor_id.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y Z : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) : f ≫ g ⊗ 𝟙 Z = (f ⊗ 𝟙 Z) ≫ (g ⊗ 𝟙 Z)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_ten.description: This theorem shows that when composing morphisms in a monoidal category, the tensor product with the identity morphism behaves consistently with the composition of the individual operations.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tensor_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y Z : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) : 𝟙 Z ⊗ f ≫ g = (𝟙 Z ⊗ f) ≫ (𝟙 Z ⊗ g)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.description: This theorem states that in a monoidal category, the composition of morphisms respects the structure of the tensor product, specifically showing that tensoring with the identity morphism distributes over morphism composition.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tensor_comp_tensor_id.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y Z : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : (𝟙 Y ⊗ f) ≫ (g ⊗ 𝟙 X) = g ⊗ f
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso.description: The theorem states that the composition of a tensor product with an identity morphism on one side is equivalent to the tensor product of two morphisms in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_id_comp_id_tensor.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {W X Y Z : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : (g ⊗ 𝟙 W) ≫ (𝟙 Z ⊗ f) = g ⊗ f
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_i.description: This theorem shows that the composition of a tensor product with the identity morphisms behaves like the tensor product of the two morphisms in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_l.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_left_iff.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y : C}
  (f g : X ⟶ Y) : 𝟙 (𝟙_ C) ⊗ f = 𝟙 (𝟙_ C) ⊗ g ↔ f = g
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_l.description: This theorem establishes that in a monoidal category, the equality of two morphisms can be inferred from their identical behavior when tensored with the identity morphism.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_r.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_right_iff.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] {X Y : C}
  (f g : X ⟶ Y) : f ⊗ 𝟙 (𝟙_ C) = g ⊗ 𝟙 (𝟙_ C) ↔ f = g
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor_r.description: This theorem states that two morphisms in a monoidal category are equal if and only if their tensor products with the identity morphism are equal.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor.code: CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] : C × C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor.comment: The tensor product expressed as a functor.
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor.fullDefinition: def tensor : C × C ⥤ C where   obj X := X.1 ⊗ X.2   map {X Y : C × C} (f : X ⟶ Y) := f.1 ⊗ f.2
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensor.description: This definition describes the tensor product in a monoidal category as a functor that maps pairs of objects to a single object in the category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAssocTensor.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :
  C × C × C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.comment: The left-associated triple tensor product as a functor.
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.fullDefinition: def leftAssocTensor : C × C × C ⥤ C where   obj X := (X.1 ⊗ X.2.1) ⊗ X.2.2   map {X Y : C × C × C} (f : X ⟶ Y) := (f.1 ⊗ f.2.1) ⊗ f.2.2
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.description: This definition describes a functor that represents the left-associated triple tensor product of objects in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAssocTensor_obj.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (X : C × C × C) : (leftAssocTensor C).obj X = (X.1 ⊗ X.2.1) ⊗ X.2.2
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.description: This theorem states that the left associator in a monoidal category allows for the re-grouping of tensor products involving three objects.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAssocTensor_map.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X Y : C × C × C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (leftAssocTensor C).map f = (f.1 ⊗ f.2.1) ⊗ f.2.2
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso.description: The theorem establishes that mapping a morphism between two products of three objects in a monoidal category corresponds to a specific way of combining the components of that morphism using the tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAssocTensor.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :
  C × C × C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.comment: The right-associated triple tensor product as a functor.
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.fullDefinition: def rightAssocTensor : C × C × C ⥤ C where   obj X := X.1 ⊗ X.2.1 ⊗ X.2.2   map {X Y : C × C × C} (f : X ⟶ Y) := f.1 ⊗ f.2.1 ⊗ f.2.2
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.description: This definition describes a functor that represents the right-associated tensor product of three objects in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAssocTensor_obj.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (X : C × C × C) : (rightAssocTensor C).obj X = X.1 ⊗ X.2.1 ⊗ X.2.2
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.description: This theorem demonstrates that the right associative tensor operation on a triple of objects in a monoidal category can be expressed as the tensor product of the first object with the components of the second object.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAssocTensor_map.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {X Y : C × C × C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (rightAssocTensor C).map f = f.1 ⊗ f.2.1 ⊗ f.2.2
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss.description: This theorem states that the mapping of a morphism between objects in a product of three categories in a monoidal context corresponds to the tensor product of their individual components.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :
  C ⥤ C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT.comment: The tensor product bifunctor `C ⥤ C ⥤ C` of a monoidal category.
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT.fullDefinition: def curriedTensor : C ⥤ C ⥤ C where   obj X :=     { obj := fun Y => X ⊗ Y       map := fun g => X ◁ g }   map f :=     { app := fun Y => f ▷ Y }
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT.description: This definition establishes the tensor product bifunctor of a monoidal category, which is a functor mapping pairs of objects to their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLeft.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] (X : C) :
  C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.comment: Tensoring on the left with a fixed object, as a functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT: This definition establishes the tensor product bifunctor of a monoidal category, which is a functor mapping pairs of objects to their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.fullDefinition: def tensorLeft (X : C) : C ⥤ C := (curriedTensor C).obj X
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.description: This definition describes a functor that represents the operation of tensoring an object on the left within a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRight.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] (X : C) :
  C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.comment: Tensoring on the right with a fixed object, as a functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT: This definition establishes the tensor product bifunctor of a monoidal category, which is a functor mapping pairs of objects to their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.fullDefinition: def tensorRight (X : C) : C ⥤ C := (curriedTensor C).flip.obj X
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.description: This definition describes a functor that represents the operation of tensoring objects in a monoidal category on the right with a fixed object.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn.code: CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUnitLeft.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] : C ⥤ C

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe: This definition describes a functor that represents the operation of tensoring an object on the left within a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn.fullDefinition: abbrev tensorUnitLeft : C ⥤ C := tensorLeft (𝟙_ C)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn.description: This definition describes a functor that applies the tensor product of a fixed unit object with any object in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn.code: CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUnitRight.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] : C ⥤ C

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi: This definition describes a functor that represents the operation of tensoring objects in a monoidal category on the right with a fixed object.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn.fullDefinition: abbrev tensorUnitRight : C ⥤ C := tensorRight (𝟙_ C)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn.description: This definition specifies a functor that takes an object from a monoidal category and returns its tensor product with the unit object of that category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associatorNatIso.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :
  leftAssocTensor C ≅ rightAssocTensor C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.comment: The associator as a natural isomorphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.as: This definition describes an isomorphism that relates the tensor product of three objects in a monoidal category, establishing the equivalence between two ways of grouping the tensor products.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftAsso: This definition describes a functor that represents the left-associated triple tensor product of objects in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightAss: This definition describes a functor that represents the right-associated tensor product of three objects in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.fullDefinition: def associatorNatIso : leftAssocTensor C ≅ rightAssocTensor C :=   NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ => MonoidalCategory.associator _ _ _)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.associat.description: This definition identifies the associator in a monoidal category as a natural isomorphism between the left and right associativity of the tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnit.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnitorNatIso.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :
  tensorUnitLeft C ≅ 𝟭 C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnit.comment: The left unitor as a natural isomorphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn: This definition describes a functor that applies the tensor product of a fixed unit object with any object in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnit.fullDefinition: def leftUnitorNatIso : tensorUnitLeft C ≅ 𝟭 C :=   NatIso.ofComponents MonoidalCategory.leftUnitor
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.leftUnit.description: This definition states that the left unitor of a monoidal category is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor on that category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUnitorNatIso.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :
  tensorUnitRight C ≅ 𝟭 C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.comment: The right unitor as a natural isomorphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorUn: This definition specifies a functor that takes an object from a monoidal category and returns its tensor product with the unit object of that category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.fullDefinition: def rightUnitorNatIso : tensorUnitRight C ≅ 𝟭 C :=   NatIso.ofComponents MonoidalCategory.rightUnitor
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.rightUni.description: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism between the tensor product with the right unit object and the identity functor in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLeftTensor.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (X Y : C) : tensorLeft (X ⊗ Y) ≅ tensorLeft Y ⋙ tensorLeft X
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.comment:
Tensoring on the left with `X ⊗ Y` is naturally isomorphic to
tensoring on the left with `Y`, and then again with `X`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.as: This definition describes an isomorphism that relates the tensor product of three objects in a monoidal category, establishing the equivalence between two ways of grouping the tensor products.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.fullDefinition: def tensorLeftTensor (X Y : C) : tensorLeft (X ⊗ Y) ≅ tensorLeft Y ⋙ tensorLeft X :=   NatIso.ofComponents (associator _ _) fun {Z} {Z'} f => by simp
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.description: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism between the operation of tensoring on the left with the composite object formed by two given objects and the sequential operation of tensoring on the left with each object individually.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLeftTensor_hom_app.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y Z : C) : (tensorLeftTensor X Y).hom.app Z = (α_ X Y Z).hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.description: This theorem states that the morphism resulting from the left tensor product applied to three objects in a monoidal category is equal to the morphism given by the associator for those objects.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLeftTensor_inv_app.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y Z : C) : (tensorLeftTensor X Y).inv.app Z = (α_ X Y Z).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorLe.description: This theorem states that the application of the inverse of the tensor product on three objects in a monoidal category is equal to the inverse of the associativity natural isomorphism for those objects.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensoringLeft.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT: This definition establishes the tensor product bifunctor of a monoidal category, which is a functor mapping pairs of objects to their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorin.fullDefinition: abbrev tensoringLeft : C ⥤ C ⥤ C := curriedTensor C
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorin.description: This definition describes a functor that represents the operation of tensoring on the left within a monoidal category, mapping objects from the category into a category of endofunctors.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorin.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensoringRight.{v, u} (C : Type u) [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :
  C ⥤ C ⥤ C

Tensoring on the right, as a functor from `C` into endofunctors of `C`.

We later show this is a monoidal functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.curriedT: This definition establishes the tensor product bifunctor of a monoidal category, which is a functor mapping pairs of objects to their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorin.fullDefinition: abbrev tensoringRight : C ⥤ C ⥤ C := (curriedTensor C).flip
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorin.description: This definition establishes a functor that maps objects in a monoidal category to their tensor products when combined on the right with other objects in the same category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRightTensor.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (X Y : C) : tensorRight (X ⊗ Y) ≅ tensorRight X ⋙ tensorRight Y
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.comment:
Tensoring on the right with `X ⊗ Y` is naturally isomorphic to
tensoring on the right with `X`, and then again with `Y`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.as: This definition describes an isomorphism that relates the tensor product of three objects in a monoidal category, establishing the equivalence between two ways of grouping the tensor products.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.fullDefinition: def tensorRightTensor (X Y : C) : tensorRight (X ⊗ Y) ≅ tensorRight X ⋙ tensorRight Y :=   NatIso.ofComponents (fun Z => (associator Z X Y).symm) fun {Z} {Z'} f => by simp
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.description: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism between the functor that tensors on the right with the tensor product of two objects and the composition of the functors that tensor on the right with each object separately.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRightTensor_hom_app.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y Z : C) : (tensorRightTensor X Y).hom.app Z = (α_ Z X Y).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between the application of a tensor product morphism and the inverse of the associator in a monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRightTensor_inv_app.{v, u} {C : Type u} [𝒞 : Category.{v, u} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y Z : C) : (tensorRightTensor X Y).inv.app Z = (α_ Z X Y).hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorRi.description: This theorem shows that the application of the inverse of a specific tensor product operation in a monoidal category is equivalent to the action of the associator morphism on the third object and the first two objects involved in the tensor product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMonoidal.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C₁ : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C₁]
  [MonoidalCategory C₁] (C₂ : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} C₂] [MonoidalCategory C₂] : MonoidalCategory (C₁ × C₂)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.te: This definition introduces the curried tensor product operation for objects within a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.wh: This definition specifies the operation of left whiskering for morphisms in a monoidal category, allowing the application of a fixed object to morphisms between two other objects.
This definition describes the operation of right whiskering for morphisms in a monoidal category, which allows the application of a morphism between two objects to a fixed object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.te: This definition specifies the operation for constructing a morphism between the tensor products of two pairs of objects in a monoidal category, based on the morphisms between each pair.
This definition identifies the tensor unit, which serves as the identity element in the tensor product structure of a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.as: This definition describes an isomorphism that relates the tensor product of three objects in a monoidal category, establishing the equivalence between two ways of grouping the tensor products.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.le: This definition establishes an isomorphism that demonstrates the equivalence between the tensor product of the tensor unit and any object in a monoidal category, effectively showing that the tensor unit acts as a left identity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategoryStruct.ri: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the tensor product of an object and the tensor unit with the original object in a monoidal category, demonstrating the right unitor property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorHo: This theorem establishes the relationship between the tensor product of morphisms in a monoidal category and the associated actions on the objects involved.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.fullDefinition: instance prodMonoidal : MonoidalCategory (C₁ × C₂) where   tensorObj X Y := (X.1 ⊗ Y.1, X.2 ⊗ Y.2)   tensorHom f g := (f.1 ⊗ g.1, f.2 ⊗ g.2)   whiskerLeft X _ _ f := (whiskerLeft X.1 f.1, whiskerLeft X.2 f.2)   whiskerRight f X := (whiskerRight f.1 X.1, whiskerRight f.2 X.2)   tensorHom_def := by simp [tensorHom_def]   tensorUnit := (𝟙_ C₁, 𝟙_ C₂)   associator X Y Z := (α_ X.1 Y.1 Z.1).prod (α_ X.2 Y.2 Z.2)   leftUnitor := fun ⟨X₁, X₂⟩ => (λ_ X₁).prod (λ_ X₂)   rightUnitor := fun ⟨X₁, X₂⟩ => (ρ_ X₁).prod (ρ_ X₂)
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.description: This definition introduces a construction that forms a monoidal category from the product of two existing monoidal categories.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMonoidal_leftUnitor_hom_fst.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C₁ : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C₁]
  [MonoidalCategory C₁] (C₂ : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} C₂] [MonoidalCategory C₂] (X : C₁ × C₂) :
  (λ_ X).hom.1 = (λ_ X.1).hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.description: This theorem states that the first component of the homomorphism associated with the left unitor for a product object in a monoidal category is equal to the homomorphism corresponding to the first component of that product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMonoidal_leftUnitor_hom_snd.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C₁ : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C₁]
  [MonoidalCategory C₁] (C₂ : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} C₂] [MonoidalCategory C₂] (X : C₁ × C₂) :
  (λ_ X).hom.2 = (λ_ X.2).hom
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.description: This theorem establishes that the second component of the morphism from the left unitor of the product of two monoidal categories equals the morphism from the left unitor of the second component of that product.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMonoidal_leftUnitor_inv_fst.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C₁ : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C₁]
  [MonoidalCategory C₁] (C₂ : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} C₂] [MonoidalCategory C₂] (X : C₁ × C₂) :
  (λ_ X).inv.1 = (λ_ X.1).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.description: This theorem establishes that in the context of a product of two monoidal categories, the first component of the inverse of the left unitor morphism corresponds to the inverse of the left unitor morphism applied to the first factor.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMonoidal_leftUnitor_inv_snd.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} (C₁ : Type u₁) [Category.{v₁, u₁} C₁]
  [MonoidalCategory C₁] (C₂ : Type u₂) [Category.{v₂, u₂} C₂] [MonoidalCategory C₂] (X : C₁ × C₂) :
  (λ_ X).inv.2 = (λ_ X.2).inv
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.prodMono.description: This theorem shows that the second component of the inverse left unitor for a product of objects in two monoidal categories is equal to the inverse left unitor of the second component alone.

CategoryTheory.OplaxMonoidalFunctor.δ.fullDefinition: δ : ∀ X Y : C, obj (X ⊗ Y) ⟶ obj X ⊗ obj Y   δ_natural_left :     ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (X' : C),       δ X X' ≫ map f ▷ obj X' = map (f ▷ X') ≫ δ Y X' := by     aesop_cat   δ_natural_right :     ∀ {X Y : C} (X' : C) (f : X ⟶ Y) ,       δ X' X ≫ obj X' ◁ map f = map (X' ◁ f) ≫ δ X' Y := by     aesop_cat   /-- associativity of the tensorator -/   associativity :     ∀ X Y Z : C,       δ (X ⊗ Y) Z ≫ δ X Y ▷ obj Z ≫ (α_ (obj X) (obj Y) (obj Z)).hom =         map (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ δ X (Y ⊗ Z) ≫ obj X ◁ δ Y Z := by     aesop_cat   -- unitality   left_unitality : ∀ X : C, (λ_ (obj X)).inv = map (λ_ X).inv ≫ δ (𝟙_ C) X ≫ η ▷ obj X := by     aesop_cat   right_unitality : ∀ X : C, (ρ_ (obj X)).inv = map (ρ_ X).inv ≫ δ X (𝟙_ C) ≫ obj X ◁ η := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.OplaxMonoidalFunctor.η.fullDefinition: η : obj (𝟙_ C) ⟶ 𝟙_ D   /-- cotensorator -/   δ : ∀ X Y : C, obj (X ⊗ Y) ⟶ obj X ⊗ obj Y   δ_natural_left :     ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (X' : C),       δ X X' ≫ map f ▷ obj X' = map (f ▷ X') ≫ δ Y X' := by     aesop_cat   δ_natural_right :     ∀ {X Y : C} (X' : C) (f : X ⟶ Y) ,       δ X' X ≫ obj X' ◁ map f = map (X' ◁ f) ≫ δ X' Y := by     aesop_cat   /-- associativity of the tensorator -/   associativity :     ∀ X Y Z : C,       δ (X ⊗ Y) Z ≫ δ X Y ▷ obj Z ≫ (α_ (obj X) (obj Y) (obj Z)).hom =         map (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ δ X (Y ⊗ Z) ≫ obj X ◁ δ Y Z := by     aesop_cat   -- unitality   left_unitality : ∀ X : C, (λ_ (obj X)).inv = map (λ_ X).inv ≫ δ (𝟙_ C) X ≫ η ▷ obj X := by     aesop_cat   right_unitality : ∀ X : C, (ρ_ (obj X)).inv = map (ρ_ X).inv ≫ δ X (𝟙_ C) ≫ obj X ◁ η := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.monoidalCounit.fullDefinition: def monoidalCounit :     (monoidalAdjoint F h) ⊗⋙ F.toLaxMonoidalFunctor ⟶ LaxMonoidalFunctor.id D where   toNatTrans := h.counit   tensor X Y := by     have eq := h.counit_naturality (F.μ (G.obj X) (G.obj Y)) =≫ inv (F.μ _ _)     simp only [assoc, IsIso.hom_inv_id, comp_id] at eq     dsimp     simp only [Adjunction.homEquiv_unit, comp_id, assoc,       map_comp, map_inv, h.counit_naturality, ← eq,       h.left_triangle_components_assoc,       IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc, IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc]   unit := by     have eq := h.counit.naturality F.ε     dsimp at eq ⊢     rw [Adjunction.homEquiv_unit, map_inv, map_comp, assoc, assoc, map_inv,       ← cancel_mono F.ε, assoc, assoc, assoc, ← eq, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc,       Adjunction.left_triangle_components, comp_id, id_comp]

equal if we apply the relations that are true in a monoidal category. Note that we will prove
that there is only one equivalence class -- this is the monoidal coherence theorem.

CategoryTheory.FreeMonoidalCategory.cate.fullDefinition: instance categoryFreeMonoidalCategory : Category.{u} (F C) where   Hom X Y := Quotient (FreeMonoidalCategory.setoidHom X Y)   id X := ⟦Hom.id X⟧   comp := Quotient.map₂ Hom.comp (fun _ _ hf _ _ hg ↦ HomEquiv.comp hf hg)   id_comp := by     rintro X Y ⟨f⟩     exact Quotient.sound (id_comp f)   comp_id := by     rintro X Y ⟨f⟩     exact Quotient.sound (comp_id f)   assoc := by     rintro W X Y Z ⟨f⟩ ⟨g⟩ ⟨h⟩     exact Quotient.sound (assoc f g h)

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.InducingFunctorData.tensorHom_eq.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategoryStruct D] {F : D ⥤ C}
  (self : InducingFunctorData F) {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂ : D} (f : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (g : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) :

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.InducingFunctorD.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.InducingFunctorData.associator_eq.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategoryStruct D] {F : D ⥤ C}
  (self : InducingFunctorData F) (X Y Z : D) :
  F.map (α_ X Y Z).hom =
    (((self.μIso (X ⊗ Y) Z).symm ≪≫ ((self.μIso X Y).symm ⊗ Iso.refl (F.obj Z))) ≪≫
        α_ (F.obj X) (F.obj Y) (F.obj Z) ≪≫ (Iso.refl (F.obj X) ⊗ self.μIso Y Z) ≪≫ self.μIso X (Y ⊗ Z)).hom

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.InducingFunctorData.leftUnitor_eq.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.InducingFunctorData.rightUnitor_eq.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [MonoidalCategory C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategoryStruct D] {F : D ⥤ C}

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.induced.fullDefinition: abbrev induced [MonoidalCategoryStruct D] (F : D ⥤ C) [F.Faithful]     (fData : InducingFunctorData F) :     MonoidalCategory.{v₂} D where   tensorHom_def {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂} f g := F.map_injective <| by     rw [fData.tensorHom_eq, Functor.map_comp, fData.whiskerRight_eq, fData.whiskerLeft_eq]     simp only [tensorHom_def, assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]   tensor_id X₁ X₂ := F.map_injective <| by cases fData; aesop_cat   tensor_comp {X₁ Y₁ Z₁ X₂ Y₂ Z₂} f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ := F.map_injective <| by cases fData; aesop_cat   whiskerLeft_id X Y := F.map_injective <| by simp [fData.whiskerLeft_eq]   id_whiskerRight X Y := F.map_injective <| by simp [fData.whiskerRight_eq]   triangle X Y := F.map_injective <| by cases fData; aesop_cat   pentagon W X Y Z := F.map_injective <| by     simp only [Functor.map_comp, fData.whiskerRight_eq, fData.associator_eq, Iso.trans_assoc,       Iso.trans_hom, Iso.symm_hom, tensorIso_hom, Iso.refl_hom, tensorHom_id, id_tensorHom,       comp_whiskerRight, whisker_assoc, assoc, fData.whiskerLeft_eq,       MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc, whiskerLeft_hom_inv_assoc,       hom_inv_whiskerRight_assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc, Iso.cancel_iso_inv_left]     slice_lhs 5 6 =>       rw [← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp, hom_inv_whiskerRight]     rw [whisker_exchange_assoc]     simp   leftUnitor_naturality {X Y : D} f := F.map_injective <| by     simp [fData.leftUnitor_eq, fData.whiskerLeft_eq, whisker_exchange_assoc]   rightUnitor_naturality {X Y : D} f := F.map_injective <| by     simp [fData.rightUnitor_eq, fData.whiskerRight_eq, ← whisker_exchange_assoc]   associator_naturality {X₁ X₂ X₃ Y₁ Y₂ Y₃} f₁ f₂ f₃ := F.map_injective <| by     simp [fData.tensorHom_eq, fData.associator_eq, tensorHom_def, whisker_exchange_assoc]

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.InducingFunctorD.fullDefinition: μIso : ∀ X Y,     F.obj X ⊗ F.obj Y ≅ F.obj (X ⊗ Y)   whiskerLeft_eq : ∀ (X : D) {Y₁ Y₂ : D} (f : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂),     F.map (X ◁ f) = (μIso _ _).inv ≫ (F.obj X ◁ F.map f) ≫ (μIso _ _).hom := by     aesop_cat   whiskerRight_eq : ∀ {X₁ X₂ : D} (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) (Y : D),     F.map (f ▷ Y) = (μIso _ _).inv ≫ (F.map f ▷ F.obj Y) ≫ (μIso _ _).hom := by     aesop_cat   tensorHom_eq : ∀ {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂ : D} (f : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (g : X₂ ⟶ Y₂),     F.map (f ⊗ g) = (μIso _ _).inv ≫ (F.map f ⊗ F.map g) ≫ (μIso _ _).hom := by     aesop_cat   /-- Analogous to `CategoryTheory.LaxMonoidalFunctor.εIso` -/   εIso : 𝟙_ _ ≅ F.obj (𝟙_ _)   associator_eq : ∀ X Y Z : D,     F.map (α_ X Y Z).hom =       (((μIso _ _).symm ≪≫ ((μIso _ _).symm ⊗ .refl _))         ≪≫ α_ (F.obj X) (F.obj Y) (F.obj Z)         ≪≫ ((.refl _ ⊗ μIso _ _) ≪≫ μIso _ _)).hom := by     aesop_cat   leftUnitor_eq : ∀ X : D,     F.map (λ_ X).hom =       (((μIso _ _).symm ≪≫ (εIso.symm ⊗ .refl _)) ≪≫ λ_ (F.obj X)).hom := by     aesop_cat   rightUnitor_eq : ∀ X : D,     F.map (ρ_ X).hom =       (((μIso _ _).symm ≪≫ (.refl _ ⊗ εIso.symm)) ≪≫ ρ_ (F.obj X)).hom := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.transportStruct.fullDefinition: def transportStruct (e : C ≌ D) : MonoidalCategoryStruct.{v₂} D where   tensorObj X Y := e.functor.obj (e.inverse.obj X ⊗ e.inverse.obj Y)   whiskerLeft X _ _ f := e.functor.map (e.inverse.obj X ◁ e.inverse.map f)   whiskerRight f X := e.functor.map (e.inverse.map f ▷ e.inverse.obj X)   tensorHom f g := e.functor.map (e.inverse.map f ⊗ e.inverse.map g)   tensorUnit := e.functor.obj (𝟙_ C)   associator X Y Z :=     e.functor.mapIso       (((e.unitIso.app _).symm ⊗ Iso.refl _) ≪≫         α_ (e.inverse.obj X) (e.inverse.obj Y) (e.inverse.obj Z) ≪≫         (Iso.refl _ ⊗ e.unitIso.app _))   leftUnitor X :=     e.functor.mapIso (((e.unitIso.app _).symm ⊗ Iso.refl _) ≪≫ λ_ (e.inverse.obj X)) ≪≫       e.counitIso.app _   rightUnitor X :=     e.functor.mapIso ((Iso.refl _ ⊗ (e.unitIso.app _).symm) ≪≫ ρ_ (e.inverse.obj X)) ≪≫       e.counitIso.app _

CategoryTheory.tensorLeftHomEquiv.code:
CategoryTheory.tensorLeftHomEquiv.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y Y' Z : C)
  [ExactPairing Y Y'] : (Y' ⊗ X ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Y ⊗ Z)
CategoryTheory.tensorLeftHomEquiv.comment:
Given an exact pairing on `Y Y'`,
we get a bijection on hom-sets `(Y' ⊗ X ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Y ⊗ Z)`
by "pulling the string on the left" up or down.

This gives the adjunction `tensorLeftAdjunction Y Y' : tensorLeft Y' ⊣ tensorLeft Y`.

This adjunction is often referred to as "Frobenius reciprocity" in the
fusion categories / planar algebras / subfactors literature.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whisker_: This theorem establishes a relationship between the composition of left whiskering and right whiskering of morphisms in a monoidal category, showing that these operations can be interchanged under certain conditions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.evaluation_c: This theorem demonstrates a specific equality involving the coevaluation and evaluation morphisms associated with an exact pairing in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.coevaluation: This theorem asserts that a specific morphism involving the coevaluation and evaluation morphisms associated with an exact pairing in a monoidal category is equal to a unit morphism.

CategoryTheory.tensorLeftHomEquiv.fullDefinition: def tensorLeftHomEquiv (X Y Y' Z : C) [ExactPairing Y Y'] : (Y' ⊗ X ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Y ⊗ Z) where   toFun f := (λ_ _).inv ≫ η_ _ _ ▷ _ ≫ (α_ _ _ _).hom ≫ _ ◁ f   invFun f := Y' ◁ f ≫ (α_ _ _ _).inv ≫ ε_ _ _ ▷ _ ≫ (λ_ _).hom   left_inv f := by     calc       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ Y' ◁ η_ Y Y' ▷ X ⊗≫ ((Y' ⊗ Y) ◁ f ≫ ε_ Y Y' ▷ Z) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (Y' ◁ η_ Y Y' ⊗≫ ε_ Y Y' ▷ Y') ▷ X ⊗≫ f := by         rw [whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = f := by         rw [coevaluation_evaluation'']; coherence   right_inv f := by     calc       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (η_ Y Y' ▷ X ≫ (Y ⊗ Y') ◁ f) ⊗≫ Y ◁ ε_ Y Y' ▷ Z ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         coherence       _ = f ⊗≫ (η_ Y Y' ▷ Y ⊗≫ Y ◁ ε_ Y Y') ▷ Z ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [← whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = f := by         rw [evaluation_coevaluation'']; coherence
CategoryTheory.tensorLeftHomEquiv.description: This definition establishes a bijection between two hom-sets in a monoidal category, utilizing an exact pairing to relate them.

CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv.code:
CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [MonoidalCategory C] (X Y Y' Z : C)
  [ExactPairing Y Y'] : (X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Z ⊗ Y')
CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv.comment:
Given an exact pairing on `Y Y'`,
we get a bijection on hom-sets `(X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Z ⊗ Y')`
by "pulling the string on the right" up or down.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whisker_: This theorem establishes a relationship between the composition of left whiskering and right whiskering of morphisms in a monoidal category, showing that these operations can be interchanged under certain conditions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.evaluation_c: This theorem demonstrates a specific equality involving the coevaluation and evaluation morphisms associated with an exact pairing in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.coevaluation: This theorem asserts that a specific morphism involving the coevaluation and evaluation morphisms associated with an exact pairing in a monoidal category is equal to a unit morphism.

CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv.fullDefinition: def tensorRightHomEquiv (X Y Y' Z : C) [ExactPairing Y Y'] : (X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) ≃ (X ⟶ Z ⊗ Y') where   toFun f := (ρ_ _).inv ≫ _ ◁ η_ _ _ ≫ (α_ _ _ _).inv ≫ f ▷ _   invFun f := f ▷ _ ≫ (α_ _ _ _).hom ≫ _ ◁ ε_ _ _ ≫ (ρ_ _).hom   left_inv f := by     calc       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ X ◁ η_ Y Y' ▷ Y ⊗≫ (f ▷ (Y' ⊗ Y) ≫ Z ◁ ε_ Y Y') ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ X ◁ (η_ Y Y' ▷ Y ⊗≫ Y ◁ ε_ Y Y') ⊗≫ f := by         rw [← whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = f := by         rw [evaluation_coevaluation'']; coherence   right_inv f := by     calc       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (X ◁ η_ Y Y' ≫ f ▷ (Y ⊗ Y')) ⊗≫ Z ◁ ε_ Y Y' ▷ Y' ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         coherence       _ = f ⊗≫ Z ◁ (Y' ◁ η_ Y Y' ⊗≫ ε_ Y Y' ▷ Y') ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = f := by         rw [coevaluation_evaluation'']; coherence
CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv.description: This definition establishes a bijection between morphisms from the tensor product of an object with one in a monoidal category to another object and morphisms from the first object to the tensor product of another object, given an exact pairing between the two latter objects.

CategoryTheory.tensorLeftAdjunction.code:

  [ExactPairing Y Y'] : tensorLeft Y' ⊣ tensorLeft Y
CategoryTheory.tensorLeftAdjunction.comment:
If `Y Y'` have an exact pairing,
then the functor `tensorLeft Y'` is left adjoint to `tensorLeft Y`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.tensorLeftHomEquiv_natura: This theorem establishes the naturality property of a tensor hom-equivalence in a monoidal category with respect to two specific morphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv: This definition describes how to create an adjunction between two functors using a natural bijection that relates morphisms from one category to those in another.

CategoryTheory.tensorLeftAdjunction.fullDefinition: def tensorLeftAdjunction (Y Y' : C) [ExactPairing Y Y'] : tensorLeft Y' ⊣ tensorLeft Y :=   Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv     { homEquiv := fun X Z => tensorLeftHomEquiv X Y Y' Z       homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := fun f g => tensorLeftHomEquiv_symm_naturality f g       homEquiv_naturality_right := fun f g => tensorLeftHomEquiv_naturality f g }
CategoryTheory.tensorLeftAdjunction.description: This definition states that in a monoidal category, if two objects have an exact pairing, the functor that takes tensor products with one object is the left adjoint of the functor that takes tensor products with the other object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv: This definition establishes a bijection between morphisms from the tensor product of an object with one in a monoidal category to another object and morphisms from the first object to the tensor product of another object, given an exact pairing between the two latter objects.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv_natur: This theorem demonstrates the naturality of the equivalence between morphisms related to tensor products in a monoidal category when composed with other morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.tensorRightHomEquiv_symm_: This theorem demonstrates a naturality property of the inverse of a tensor hom equivalence in a monoidal category, relating the composition of morphisms through different objects in a structured way.

CategoryTheory.tensorRightAdjunction.fullDefinition: def tensorRightAdjunction (Y Y' : C) [ExactPairing Y Y'] : tensorRight Y ⊣ tensorRight Y' :=   Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv     { homEquiv := fun X Z => tensorRightHomEquiv X Y Y' Z       homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := fun f g => tensorRightHomEquiv_symm_naturality f g       homEquiv_naturality_right := fun f g => tensorRightHomEquiv_naturality f g }
CategoryTheory.tensorRightAdjunction.description: This definition asserts that if two objects in a monoidal category have an exact pairing, the functor that tensors on the right with the first object is left adjoint to the functor that tensors on the right with the second object.

CategoryTheory.closedOfHasLeftDual.code:
CategoryTheory.closedOfHasLeftDual.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [MonoidalCategory C] (Y : C)
  [HasLeftDual Y] : Closed Y
CategoryTheory.closedOfHasLeftDual.comment:
If `Y` has a left dual `ᘁY`, then it is a closed object, with the internal hom functor `Y ⟶[C] -`
given by left tensoring by `ᘁY`.
This has to be a definition rather than an instance to avoid diamonds, for example between
`category_theory.monoidal_closed.functor_closed` and
`CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorHasLeftDual`. Moreover, in concrete applications there is often
a more useful definition of the internal hom object than `ᘁY ⊗ X`, in which case the closed
structure shouldn't come from `has_left_dual` (e.g. in the category `FinVect k`, it is more
convenient to define the internal hom as `Y →ₗ[k] X` rather than `ᘁY ⊗ X` even though these are
naturally isomorphic).

explanatories.CategoryTheory.tensorLeftAdjunction: This definition states that in a monoidal category, if two objects have an exact pairing, the functor that takes tensor products with one object is the left adjoint of the functor that takes tensor products with the other object.

CategoryTheory.closedOfHasLeftDual.fullDefinition: def closedOfHasLeftDual (Y : C) [HasLeftDual Y] : Closed Y where   adj := tensorLeftAdjunction (ᘁY) Y

CategoryTheory.exactPairingCongrLeft.fullDefinition: def exactPairingCongrLeft {X X' Y : C} [ExactPairing X' Y] (i : X ≅ X') : ExactPairing X Y where   evaluation' := Y ◁ i.hom ≫ ε_ _ _   coevaluation' := η_ _ _ ≫ i.inv ▷ Y   evaluation_coevaluation' :=     calc       _ = η_ X' Y ▷ X ⊗≫ (i.inv ▷ (Y ⊗ X) ≫ X ◁ (Y ◁ i.hom)) ⊗≫ X ◁ ε_ X' Y := by         coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (η_ X' Y ▷ X ≫ (X' ⊗ Y) ◁ i.hom) ⊗≫           (i.inv ▷ (Y ⊗ X') ≫ X ◁ ε_ X' Y) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [← whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ i.hom ⊗≫ (η_ X' Y ▷ X' ⊗≫ X' ◁ ε_ X' Y) ⊗≫ i.inv ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [← whisker_exchange, ← whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (i.hom ≫ i.inv) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [evaluation_coevaluation'']; coherence       _ = (λ_ X).hom ≫ (ρ_ X).inv := by         rw [Iso.hom_inv_id]         -- coherence failed         simp [monoidalComp]   coevaluation_evaluation' := by     calc       _ = Y ◁ η_ X' Y ≫ Y ◁ (i.inv ≫ i.hom) ▷ Y ⊗≫ ε_ X' Y ▷ Y := by         coherence       _ = Y ◁ η_ X' Y ⊗≫ ε_ X' Y ▷ Y := by         rw [Iso.inv_hom_id]; coherence       _ = _ := by         rw [coevaluation_evaluation'']         -- coherence failed         simp [monoidalComp]

CategoryTheory.exactPairingCongrRight.fullDefinition: def exactPairingCongrRight {X Y Y' : C} [ExactPairing X Y'] (i : Y ≅ Y') : ExactPairing X Y where   evaluation' := i.hom ▷ X ≫ ε_ _ _   coevaluation' := η_ _ _ ≫ X ◁ i.inv   evaluation_coevaluation' := by     calc       _ = η_ X Y' ▷ X ⊗≫ X ◁ (i.inv ≫ i.hom) ▷ X ≫ X ◁ ε_ X Y' := by         coherence       _ = η_ X Y' ▷ X ⊗≫ X ◁ ε_ X Y' := by         rw [Iso.inv_hom_id]; coherence       _ = _ := by         rw [evaluation_coevaluation'']         -- coherence failed         simp [monoidalComp]   coevaluation_evaluation' :=     calc       _ = Y ◁ η_ X Y' ⊗≫ (Y ◁ (X ◁ i.inv) ≫ i.hom ▷ (X ⊗ Y)) ⊗≫ ε_ X Y' ▷ Y := by         coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (Y ◁ η_ X Y' ≫ i.hom ▷ (X ⊗ Y')) ⊗≫           ((Y' ⊗ X) ◁ i.inv ≫ ε_ X Y' ▷ Y) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ i.hom ⊗≫ (Y' ◁ η_ X Y' ⊗≫ ε_ X Y' ▷ Y') ⊗≫ i.inv ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [whisker_exchange, whisker_exchange]; coherence       _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫ (i.hom ≫ i.inv) ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by         rw [coevaluation_evaluation'']; coherence       _ = (ρ_ Y).hom ≫ (λ_ Y).inv := by         rw [Iso.hom_inv_id]         -- coherence failed         simp [monoidalComp]

CategoryTheory.monoidalClosedOfLeftRigid.code:
CategoryTheory.monoidalClosedOfLeftRigidCategory.{v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  [LeftRigidCategory C] : MonoidalClosed C
CategoryTheory.monoidalClosedOfLeftRigid.comment:
Any left rigid category is monoidal closed, with the internal hom `X ⟶[C] Y = ᘁX ⊗ Y`.
This has to be a definition rather than an instance to avoid diamonds, for example between
`category_theory.monoidal_closed.functor_category` and
`CategoryTheory.Monoidal.leftRigidFunctorCategory`. Moreover, in concrete applications there is
often a more useful definition of the internal hom object than `ᘁY ⊗ X`, in which case the monoidal
closed structure shouldn't come the rigid structure (e.g. in the category `FinVect k`, it is more
convenient to define the internal hom as `Y →ₗ[k] X` rather than `ᘁY ⊗ X` even though these are
naturally isomorphic).

explanatories.CategoryTheory.closedOfHasLeftDual: This definition states that if an object in a monoidal category has a left dual, then it qualifies as a closed object with an associated internal hom functor derived from left tensoring by its dual.

CategoryTheory.monoidalClosedOfLeftRigid.description: This definition establishes that any left rigid category possesses a monoidal closed structure, where the internal hom is defined through tensoring with certain objects in the category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_injective: This statement does not provide any specific theorem or definition; therefore, it does not present any mathematical or logical assertion.

CategoryTheory.exactPairingOfFaithful.fullDefinition: def exactPairingOfFaithful [F.Faithful] {X Y : C} (eval : Y ⊗ X ⟶ 𝟙_ C)     (coeval : 𝟙_ C ⟶ X ⊗ Y) [ExactPairing (F.obj X) (F.obj Y)]     (map_eval : F.map eval = inv (F.μ _ _) ≫ ε_ _ _ ≫ F.ε)     (map_coeval : F.map coeval = inv F.ε ≫ η_ _ _ ≫ F.μ _ _) : ExactPairing X Y where   evaluation' := eval   coevaluation' := coeval   evaluation_coevaluation' :=     F.toFunctor.map_injective <| by       simp [map_eval, map_coeval,         MonoidalFunctor.map_whiskerLeft, MonoidalFunctor.map_whiskerRight]   coevaluation_evaluation' :=     F.toFunctor.map_injective <| by       simp [map_eval, map_coeval,         MonoidalFunctor.map_whiskerLeft, MonoidalFunctor.map_whiskerRight]
CategoryTheory.exactPairingOfFaithful.description: This definition characterizes an exact pairing in a category by relating specific evaluation and coevaluation morphisms through a faithful monoidal functor that preserves these structures.

CategoryTheory.exactPairingOfFullyFaithf.fullDefinition: def exactPairingOfFullyFaithful [F.Full] [F.Faithful] (X Y : C)     [ExactPairing (F.obj X) (F.obj Y)] : ExactPairing X Y :=   exactPairingOfFaithful F (F.toFunctor.preimage (inv (F.μ _ _) ≫ ε_ _ _ ≫ F.ε))     (F.toFunctor.preimage (inv F.ε ≫ η_ _ _ ≫ F.μ _ _)) (by simp) (by simp)
CategoryTheory.exactPairingOfFullyFaithf.description: This definition establishes that if two objects in a category are linked by a fully faithful functor to another pair with an exact pairing, then those two objects themselves also form an exact pairing.

CategoryTheory.hasLeftDualOfEquivalence.fullDefinition: def hasLeftDualOfEquivalence (X : C) [HasLeftDual (F.obj X)] :     HasLeftDual X where   leftDual := G.obj (ᘁ(F.obj X))   exact := by     -- Porting note: in Lean3, `apply exactPairingOfFullyFaithful F _ _` automatically     -- created the goals for `ExactPairing` type class     refine @exactPairingOfFullyFaithful _ _ _ _ _ _ F _ _ _ _ ?_     refine @exactPairingCongrLeft _ _ _ _ _ _ ?_ (adj.toEquivalence.counitIso.app _)     dsimp     infer_instance

explanatories.CategoryTheory.rightAdjointMate: This definition describes the right adjoint mate of a morphism between two objects in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.comp_rightAdjointMate: This theorem states that the right adjoint mate of the composition of two morphisms is equal to the composition of their respective right adjoint mates in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_tenso: The theorem states that the composition of a tensor product with an identity morphism on one side is equivalent to the tensor product of two morphisms in a monoidal category.
This theorem states that the tensor product of the identity morphism on one object with a morphism between two objects is equivalent to the left whiskering of that morphism with the tensor product.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorHo: This theorem states that for a morphism between two objects in a monoidal category, tensoring it with the identity morphism on another object is equivalent to the right whiskering of that morphism with the object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.coevaluation_comp_rightAd: This theorem establishes a relationship between the coevaluation morphism and the action of the right dual on morphisms in a monoidal category involving dual objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.comp_whi: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two morphisms followed by a right whiskering operation with a fixed object is equal to the sequential application of the right whiskering operation to each morphism followed by their composition.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.id_whisk: This theorem states that the right whiskering of the identity morphism on one object with respect to a tensor product in a monoidal category results in the identity morphism on the resulting tensor product of the two objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ExactPairing.evaluation: This definition describes the evaluation morphism associated with an exact pairing in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.rightAdjointMate_comp_eva: This theorem establishes a relation between the composition of specific morphisms and the evaluation morphisms related to right duals in a monoidal category, illustrating how they interact under the action of duality.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.whiskerL: This theorem demonstrates the associativity of the left whiskering operation in a monoidal category when applied to the composition of morphisms.

This theorem asserts that the left whiskering of the identity morphism on one object with respect to a tensor product in a monoidal category yields the identity morphism on the resulting tensor product of the two objects.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorHasRightD.fullDefinition: instance functorHasRightDual [RightRigidCategory D] (F : C ⥤ D) : HasRightDual F where   rightDual :=     { obj := fun X => (F.obj X)ᘁ       map := fun f => (F.map (inv f))ᘁ       map_comp := fun f g => by simp [comp_rightAdjointMate] }   exact :=     { evaluation' :=         { app := fun X => ε_ _ _           naturality := fun X Y f => by             dsimp             rw [Category.comp_id, Functor.map_inv, ← id_tensor_comp_tensor_id, Category.assoc,               id_tensorHom, tensorHom_id,               rightAdjointMate_comp_evaluation, ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp_assoc,               IsIso.hom_inv_id, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Category.id_comp] }       coevaluation' :=         { app := fun X => η_ _ _           naturality := fun X Y f => by             dsimp             rw [Functor.map_inv, Category.id_comp, ← id_tensor_comp_tensor_id,               id_tensorHom, tensorHom_id, ← Category.assoc,               coevaluation_comp_rightAdjointMate, Category.assoc, ← comp_whiskerRight,               IsIso.inv_hom_id, id_whiskerRight, Category.comp_id] } }

CategoryTheory.monoidalCategoryOp.fullDefinition: instance monoidalCategoryOp : MonoidalCategory Cᵒᵖ where   tensorObj X Y := op (unop X ⊗ unop Y)   whiskerLeft X _ _ f := (X.unop ◁ f.unop).op   whiskerRight f X := (f.unop ▷ X.unop).op   tensorHom f g := (f.unop ⊗ g.unop).op   tensorHom_def f g := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (tensorHom_def' _ _)   tensorUnit := op (𝟙_ C)   associator X Y Z := (α_ (unop X) (unop Y) (unop Z)).symm.op   leftUnitor X := (λ_ (unop X)).symm.op   rightUnitor X := (ρ_ (unop X)).symm.op   associator_naturality f g h := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj <| by simp   leftUnitor_naturality f := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj <| by simp   rightUnitor_naturality f := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj <| by simp   triangle X Y := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj <| by dsimp; coherence   pentagon W X Y Z := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj <| by dsimp; coherence

CategoryTheory.monoidalCategoryMop.fullDefinition: instance monoidalCategoryMop : MonoidalCategory Cᴹᵒᵖ where   tensorObj X Y := mop (unmop Y ⊗ unmop X)   whiskerLeft X _ _ f := (f.unmop ▷ X.unmop).mop   whiskerRight f X := (X.unmop ◁ f.unmop).mop   tensorHom f g := (g.unmop ⊗ f.unmop).mop   tensorHom_def f g := Quiver.Hom.unmop_inj (tensorHom_def' _ _)   tensorUnit := mop (𝟙_ C)   associator X Y Z := (α_ (unmop Z) (unmop Y) (unmop X)).symm.mop   leftUnitor X := (ρ_ (unmop X)).mop   rightUnitor X := (λ_ (unmop X)).mop   associator_naturality f g h := Quiver.Hom.unmop_inj <| by simp   leftUnitor_naturality f := Quiver.Hom.unmop_inj <| by simp   rightUnitor_naturality f := Quiver.Hom.unmop_inj <| by simp   -- Porting note: Changed `by coherence` to `by simp` below   triangle X Y := Quiver.Hom.unmop_inj <| by simp   pentagon W X Y Z := Quiver.Hom.unmop_inj <| by dsimp; coherence

CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory.braiding.fullDefinition: braiding : ∀ X Y : C, X ⊗ Y ≅ Y ⊗ X   braiding_naturality_right :     ∀ (X : C) {Y Z : C} (f : Y ⟶ Z),       X ◁ f ≫ (braiding X Z).hom = (braiding X Y).hom ≫ f ▷ X := by     aesop_cat   braiding_naturality_left :     ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (Z : C),       f ▷ Z ≫ (braiding Y Z).hom = (braiding X Z).hom ≫ Z ◁ f := by     aesop_cat   /-- The first hexagon identity. -/   hexagon_forward :     ∀ X Y Z : C,       (α_ X Y Z).hom ≫ (braiding X (Y ⊗ Z)).hom ≫ (α_ Y Z X).hom =         ((braiding X Y).hom ▷ Z) ≫ (α_ Y X Z).hom ≫ (Y ◁ (braiding X Z).hom) := by     aesop_cat   /-- The second hexagon identity. -/   hexagon_reverse :     ∀ X Y Z : C,       (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫ (braiding (X ⊗ Y) Z).hom ≫ (α_ Z X Y).inv =         (X ◁ (braiding Y Z).hom) ≫ (α_ X Z Y).inv ≫ ((braiding X Z).hom ▷ Y) := by     aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory.yang_baxt.code:

  [BraidedCategory C] (X Y Z : C) :

  [BraidedCategory C] (X : C) :

CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory.yang_baxter_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  [BraidedCategory C] (X Y Z : C) :
  ∀ {Z_1 : C} (h : Z ⊗ Y ⊗ X ⟶ Z_1),
    (α_ X Y Z).inv ≫
        (β_ X Y).hom ▷ Z ≫ (α_ Y X Z).hom ≫ Y ◁ (β_ X Z).hom ≫ (α_ Y Z X).inv ≫ (β_ Y Z).hom ▷ X ≫ (α_ Z Y X).hom ≫ h =
      X ◁ (β_ Y Z).hom ≫ (α_ X Z Y).inv ≫ (β_ X Z).hom ▷ Y ≫ (α_ Z X Y).hom ≫ Z ◁ (β_ X Y).hom ≫ h

CategoryTheory.reverseBraiding.comment:
The braided monoidal category obtained from `C` by replacing its braiding
`β_ X Y : X ⊗ Y ≅ Y ⊗ X` with the inverse `(β_ Y X)⁻¹ : X ⊗ Y ≅ Y ⊗ X`.
This corresponds to the automorphism of the braid group swapping
over-crossings and under-crossings.

  [BraidedCategory C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] [BraidedCategory D]
  (toMonoidalFunctor : MonoidalFunctor C D)

CategoryTheory.LaxMonoidalFunctor.mapMon.fullDefinition: def mapMon (F : LaxMonoidalFunctor C D) : Mon_ C ⥤ Mon_ D where   obj A :=     { X := F.obj A.X       one := F.ε ≫ F.map A.one       mul := F.μ _ _ ≫ F.map A.mul       one_mul := by         simp_rw [comp_whiskerRight, Category.assoc, μ_natural_left_assoc, left_unitality]         slice_lhs 3 4 => rw [← F.toFunctor.map_comp, A.one_mul]       mul_one := by         simp_rw [MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp, Category.assoc, μ_natural_right_assoc,           right_unitality]         slice_lhs 3 4 => rw [← F.toFunctor.map_comp, A.mul_one]       mul_assoc := by         simp_rw [comp_whiskerRight, Category.assoc, μ_natural_left_assoc,           MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp, Category.assoc, μ_natural_right_assoc]         slice_lhs 3 4 => rw [← F.toFunctor.map_comp, A.mul_assoc]         simp }   map f :=     { hom := F.map f.hom       one_hom := by dsimp; rw [Category.assoc, ← F.toFunctor.map_comp, f.one_hom]       mul_hom := by         dsimp         rw [Category.assoc, F.μ_natural_assoc, ← F.toFunctor.map_comp, ← F.toFunctor.map_comp,           f.mul_hom] }

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.FunctorCategory..fullDefinition: def whiskerLeft (F) (β : F' ⟶ G') : tensorObj F F' ⟶ tensorObj F G' where   app X := F.obj X ◁ β.app X   naturality X Y f := by     simp only [← id_tensorHom]     apply (tensorHom (𝟙 F) β).naturality

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorUnit_obj.code:

  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] {X : C} : (𝟙_ (C ⥤ D)).obj X = 𝟙_ D
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorUnit_obj.description: This theorem states that the identity morphism of functors from one category to a monoidal category evaluated at an object equals the identity morphism of the target monoidal category.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorUnit_map.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorUnit_map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} : (𝟙_ (C ⥤ D)).map f = 𝟙 (𝟙_ D)
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorUnit_map.description: This theorem asserts that the image of a morphism under the identity functor from one category to a monoidal category is the identity morphism on the target category's identity object.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorObj_obj.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorObj_obj.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] {F G : C ⥤ D} {X : C} : (F ⊗ G).obj X = F.obj X ⊗ G.obj X
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorObj_obj.description: This theorem states that the tensor product of functors evaluated at an object is equal to the tensor product of their individual evaluations at that object.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorObj_map.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorObj_map.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorObj_map.description: This theorem establishes that the morphism corresponding to the tensor product of two functors applied to a morphism from one object to another is equal to the tensor product of the respective morphisms of each functor.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.tensorHom_app.description: This theorem asserts that the application of the tensor product of two natural transformations at an object equals the tensor product of their individual applications at that object.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.leftUnitor_hom_a.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.leftUnitor_hom_app.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] {F : C ⥤ D} {X : C} : (λ_ F).hom.app X = (λ_ (F.obj X)).hom
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.leftUnitor_hom_a.description: This theorem states that the application of the left unitor morphism for a functor at an object is equal to the morphism from the left unitor of the image of that object under the functor.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.leftUnitor_inv_a.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.leftUnitor_inv_app.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] {F : C ⥤ D} {X : C} : (λ_ F).inv.app X = (λ_ (F.obj X)).inv
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.leftUnitor_inv_a.description: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the left unitor transformation applied to a functor at an object corresponds to the inverse of the left unitor transformation applied to the image of that object under the functor.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.rightUnitor_hom_.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.rightUnitor_hom_app.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.rightUnitor_hom_.description: This theorem states that the application of the homomorphism corresponding to the right unitor at an object is equal to the homomorphism corresponding to the right unitor applied to the image of that object under a functor.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.rightUnitor_inv_.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.rightUnitor_inv_app.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] {F : C ⥤ D} {X : C} : (ρ_ F).inv.app X = (ρ_ (F.obj X)).inv
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.rightUnitor_inv_.description: This theorem establishes that the inverse of the right unitor transformation for a functor at an object equals the inverse of the right unitor transformation for the image of that object under the functor.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.associator_hom_a.description: This theorem states that the application of the associator natural transformation to functors is equal to the natural transformation evaluated at the tensor products of their images.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.associator_inv_a.description: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the associator for three functors applied at an object is equal to the inverse of the associator for their respective images under the functors.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryM.code:
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryMonoidal.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] : MonoidalCategory (C ⥤ D)
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryM.comment:
When `C` is any category, and `D` is a monoidal category,
the functor category `C ⥤ D` has a natural pointwise monoidal structure,
where `(F ⊗ G).obj X = F.obj X ⊗ G.obj X`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorHo: This theorem establishes the relationship between the tensor product of morphisms in a monoidal category and the associated actions on the objects involved.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.pentagon: This theorem expresses the pentagon identity that relates different ways to associate tensor products in a monoidal category, ensuring coherence in the structure of these products.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryM.fullDefinition: instance functorCategoryMonoidal : MonoidalCategory (C ⥤ D) where   tensorHom_def := by intros; ext; simp [tensorHom_def]   pentagon F G H K := by ext X; dsimp; rw [pentagon]
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryM.description: This definition states that the category of functors from any category to a monoidal category naturally acquires a pointwise monoidal structure.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryB.code:

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryB.comment:

explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.ofComponents: This definition outlines the process of creating a natural isomorphism between functors by providing isomorphisms at the object level and verifying naturality in one direction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory.braiding: This definition describes a natural isomorphism that establishes a specific symmetry between the tensor products of two objects in a braided category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory.hexagon_f: This theorem expresses the first hexagon identity in a braided category, establishing a specific relationship between the braidings and associators of three objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.BraidedCategory.hexagon_r: This theorem establishes the second hexagon identity in a braided category, detailing a specific relationship among the inverse associators and braidings of three objects.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryB.fullDefinition: instance functorCategoryBraided : BraidedCategory (C ⥤ D) where   braiding F G := NatIso.ofComponents fun X => β_ _ _   hexagon_forward F G H := by ext X; apply hexagon_forward   hexagon_reverse F G H := by ext X; apply hexagon_reverse
CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryB.description: This definition states that the functor category formed by functors from any category to a braided monoidal category inherits a braided monoidal structure.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryS.code:

explanatories.CategoryTheory.SymmetricCategory.symmetr: This theorem asserts that in a symmetric category, the composition of braidings between two objects is equal to the identity morphism on their tensor product.

CategoryTheory.Monoidal.functorCategoryS.fullDefinition: instance functorCategorySymmetric : SymmetricCategory (C ⥤ D) where   symmetry F G := by ext X; apply symmetry

CategoryTheory.monoidOfSkeletalMonoidal.fullDefinition: abbrev monoidOfSkeletalMonoidal (hC : Skeletal C) : Monoid C where   mul X Y := (X ⊗ Y : C)   one := (𝟙_ C : C)   one_mul X := hC ⟨λ_ X⟩   mul_one X := hC ⟨ρ_ X⟩   mul_assoc X Y Z := hC ⟨α_ X Y Z⟩

explanatories.CategoryTheory.monoidOfSkeletalMonoidal: This definition states that if a category is both monoidal and skeletal, then it can be classified as a monoid.

CategoryTheory.commMonoidOfSkeletalBraid.fullDefinition: def commMonoidOfSkeletalBraided [BraidedCategory C] (hC : Skeletal C) : CommMonoid C :=   { monoidOfSkeletalMonoidal hC with mul_comm := fun X Y => hC ⟨β_ X Y⟩ }

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.map: This definition establishes a morphism that maps a product of two categories to another product, induced by pairs of morphisms between each respective component of the products.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.associator: This definition establishes an isomorphism that relates the product of three objects to the product of the first two objects with a third object, demonstrating the associativity of binary products in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.leftUnitor: This definition describes an isomorphism that identifies the binary product of a terminal object with another object in a category as being equivalent to that object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.pentagon: This theorem establishes a commutative diagram for the associators of products, demonstrating how morphisms between various combinations of objects can be rearranged without affecting their composition.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.triangle: This theorem asserts a specific relationship between the morphism of a product associator and the mappings involving unitors in a category with binary products and a terminal object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.map: This definition states that if coproducts of two pairs of objects exist, then a pair of morphisms from the first pair induces a morphism from the coproduct of the first pair to the coproduct of the second pair.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.triangle: This theorem demonstrates a specific relationship involving morphisms in a category with binary coproducts and an initial object, linking the associator and unitor morphisms through a commutative diagram.

CategoryTheory.monoidalOfHasFiniteProduc.fullDefinition: def monoidalOfHasFiniteProducts [HasTerminal C] [HasBinaryProducts C] : MonoidalCategory C :=   letI : MonoidalCategoryStruct C := {     tensorObj := fun X Y ↦ X ⨯ Y     whiskerLeft := fun X _ _ g ↦ Limits.prod.map (𝟙 _) g     whiskerRight := fun {_ _} f Y ↦ Limits.prod.map f (𝟙 _)     tensorHom := fun f g ↦ Limits.prod.map f g     tensorUnit := ⊤_ C     associator := prod.associator     leftUnitor := fun P ↦ prod.leftUnitor P     rightUnitor := fun P ↦ prod.rightUnitor P   }   .ofTensorHom     (pentagon := prod.pentagon)     (triangle := prod.triangle)     (associator_naturality := @prod.associator_naturality _ _ _)

CategoryTheory.Functor.toMonoidalFunctor.fullDefinition: def Functor.toMonoidalFunctorOfHasFiniteProducts : MonoidalFunctor C D where   toFunctor := F   ε := (asIso (terminalComparison F)).inv   μ X Y := (asIso (prodComparison F X Y)).inv   μ_natural_left {X Y} f X' := by simpa using (prodComparison_inv_natural F f (𝟙 X')).symm   μ_natural_right {X Y} X' g := by simpa using (prodComparison_inv_natural F (𝟙 X') g).symm   associativity X Y Z := by     dsimp only [monoidalOfHasFiniteProducts.associator_hom]     rw [← cancel_epi (prod.map (prodComparison F X Y) (𝟙 (F.obj Z)))]     dsimp     simp only [prod.map_map_assoc, IsIso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id, prod.map_id_id,       Category.id_comp, prod.lift_map_assoc, IsIso.inv_comp_eq]     rw [← cancel_mono (prodComparison F X (Y ⨯ Z))]     simp only [Category.assoc, IsIso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id, prod.comp_lift,       prod.map_fst_assoc, prodComparison_fst, prodComparison_fst_assoc]     ext     · simp [-Functor.map_comp, ← F.map_comp]     · rw [← cancel_mono (prodComparison F Y Z)]       ext       all_goals simp [-Functor.map_comp, ← F.map_comp]   left_unitality Y := by     rw [← cancel_epi (prod.map (terminalComparison F) (𝟙 (F.obj Y)))]     dsimp     simp only [prod.map_map_assoc, IsIso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id, prod.map_id_id,       Category.id_comp, IsIso.eq_inv_comp]     erw [prod.map_snd, Category.comp_id, prodComparison_snd]   right_unitality X := by     rw [← cancel_epi (prod.map (𝟙 (F.obj X)) (terminalComparison F))]     dsimp     simp only [prod.map_map_assoc, Category.comp_id, IsIso.hom_inv_id, prod.map_id_id,       Category.id_comp, IsIso.eq_inv_comp]     erw [prod.map_fst, Category.comp_id, prodComparison_fst]
CategoryTheory.Functor.toMonoidalFunctor.description: A functor that preserves finite products between categories with terminal objects and binary products can be promoted to a monoidal functor compatible with their monoidal structures.

CategoryTheory.Center.tensorObj.fullDefinition: def tensorObj (X Y : Center C) : Center C :=   ⟨X.1 ⊗ Y.1,     { β := fun U =>         α_ _ _ _ ≪≫           (whiskerLeftIso X.1 (Y.2.β U)) ≪≫ (α_ _ _ _).symm ≪≫             (whiskerRightIso (X.2.β U) Y.1) ≪≫ α_ _ _ _       monoidal := fun U U' => by         dsimp only [Iso.trans_hom, whiskerLeftIso_hom, Iso.symm_hom, whiskerRightIso_hom]         simp only [HalfBraiding.monoidal]         -- We'd like to commute `X.1 ◁ U ◁ (HalfBraiding.β Y.2 U').hom`         -- and `((HalfBraiding.β X.2 U).hom ▷ U' ▷ Y.1)` past each other.         -- We do this with the help of the monoidal composition `⊗≫` and the `coherence` tactic.         calc           _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫             X.1 ◁ (HalfBraiding.β Y.2 U).hom ▷ U' ⊗≫               (_ ◁ (HalfBraiding.β Y.2 U').hom ≫                 (HalfBraiding.β X.2 U).hom ▷ _) ⊗≫                   U ◁ (HalfBraiding.β X.2 U').hom ▷ Y.1 ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by coherence           _ = _ := by rw [whisker_exchange]; coherence       naturality := fun {U U'} f => by         dsimp only [Iso.trans_hom, whiskerLeftIso_hom, Iso.symm_hom, whiskerRightIso_hom]         calc           _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫             (X.1 ◁ (Y.1 ◁ f ≫ (HalfBraiding.β Y.2 U').hom)) ⊗≫               (HalfBraiding.β X.2 U').hom ▷ Y.1 ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by coherence           _ = 𝟙 _ ⊗≫             X.1 ◁ (HalfBraiding.β Y.2 U).hom ⊗≫               (X.1 ◁ f ≫ (HalfBraiding.β X.2 U').hom) ▷ Y.1 ⊗≫ 𝟙 _ := by             rw [HalfBraiding.naturality]; coherence           _ = _ := by rw [HalfBraiding.naturality]; coherence }⟩

Mon_.limit.{v, u} {J : Type v} [SmallCategory J] {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasLimits C] [MonoidalCategory C]

Mon_.limit.comment:
We construct the (candidate) limit of a functor `F : J ⥤ Mon_ C`
by interpreting it as a functor `Mon_ (J ⥤ C)`,
and noting that taking limits is a lax monoidal functor,
and hence sends monoid objects to monoid objects.

Mon_.limit_mul.code:
Mon_.limit_mul.{v, u} {J : Type v} [SmallCategory J] {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasLimits C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  (F : J ⥤ Mon_ C) :
  (limit F).mul =
    limit.lift (F ⋙ forget C)
      ((Cones.postcompose (MonFunctorCategoryEquivalence.Inverse.obj F).mul).obj
        { pt := MonoidalCategory.tensorObj (Limits.limit (F ⋙ forget C)) (Limits.limit (F ⋙ forget C)),
          π :=
            { app := fun j => MonoidalCategory.tensorHom (limit.π (F ⋙ forget C) j) (limit.π (F ⋙ forget C) j),
              naturality := ⋯ } })

explanatories.Algebra.commutes: This theorem asserts that in an algebra over a commutative semiring, the multiplication of a scalar from the semiring and an element from the algebra is commutative.
explanatories.AlgebraCat.id_apply: This theorem asserts that applying the identity morphism of a module to any element of that module yields the element itself.

explanatories.ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.hom_apply: This theorem states that the action of the tensor product of two morphisms on the tensor product of their respective modules is preserved under the application of those morphisms.
explanatories.AlgebraCat.coe_comp: This theorem confirms that the composition of two module morphisms corresponds to the composition of their respective underlying functions.
explanatories.ModuleCat.MonoidalCategory.associator_ho: This theorem verifies the effect of the associator on the tensor product of three modules over a commutative ring, showing that the associator preserves the structure of the tensor product.
explanatories.LinearMap.id_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the identity function applied to an element of a module returns that element unchanged.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.

ModuleCat.monModuleEquivalenceAlgebra.fullDefinition: def monModuleEquivalenceAlgebra : Mon_ (ModuleCat.{u} R) ≌ AlgebraCat R where   functor := functor   inverse := inverse   unitIso :=     NatIso.ofComponents       (fun A =>         { hom :=             { hom :=                 { toFun := _root_.id                   map_add' := fun x y => rfl                   map_smul' := fun r a => rfl }               mul_hom := by                 -- Porting note: `ext` did not pick up `TensorProduct.ext`                 refine TensorProduct.ext ?_                 dsimp at *                 rfl }           inv :=             { hom :=                 { toFun := _root_.id                   map_add' := fun x y => rfl                   map_smul' := fun r a => rfl }               mul_hom := by                 -- Porting note: `ext` did not pick up `TensorProduct.ext`                 refine TensorProduct.ext ?_                 dsimp at *                 rfl } })   counitIso :=     NatIso.ofComponents       (fun A =>         { hom :=             { toFun := _root_.id               map_zero' := rfl               map_add' := fun x y => rfl               map_one' := (algebraMap R A).map_one               map_mul' := fun x y => @LinearMap.mul'_apply R _ _ _ _ _ _ x y               commutes' := fun r => rfl }           inv :=             { toFun := _root_.id               map_zero' := rfl               map_add' := fun x y => rfl               map_one' := (algebraMap R A).map_one.symm               map_mul' := fun x y => (@LinearMap.mul'_apply R _ _ _ _ _ _ x y).symm               commutes' := fun r => rfl } })

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.tensorHo: This theorem states that for a morphism between two objects in a monoidal category, tensoring it with the identity morphism on another object is equivalent to the right whiskering of that morphism with the object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.triangle: This theorem demonstrates a relationship in a monoidal category involving the composition of certain morphisms and associators, indicating how the inverse of the right unitor whiskered with an object together with the associator yields a specific reconfiguration of objects and morphisms.

CategoryTheory.coyonedaTensorUnit.fullDefinition: def coyonedaTensorUnit (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [MonoidalCategory C] :     LaxMonoidalFunctor C (Type v) := .ofTensorHom     (F := coyoneda.obj (op (𝟙_ C)))     (ε := fun _p => 𝟙 _)     (μ := fun X Y p => (λ_ (𝟙_ C)).inv ≫ (p.1 ⊗ p.2))     (μ_natural := by aesop_cat)     (associativity := fun X Y Z => by       ext ⟨⟨f, g⟩, h⟩; dsimp at f g h       dsimp; simp only [Iso.cancel_iso_inv_left, Category.assoc]       conv_lhs =>         rw [← Category.id_comp h, tensor_comp, Category.assoc, associator_naturality, ←           Category.assoc, unitors_inv_equal, tensorHom_id, triangle_assoc_comp_right_inv]       conv_rhs => rw [← Category.id_comp f, tensor_comp]       simp)     (left_unitality := by       intros       ext ⟨⟨⟩, f⟩; dsimp at f       dsimp       simp)     (right_unitality := fun X => by       ext ⟨f, ⟨⟩⟩; dsimp at f       dsimp       simp [unitors_inv_equal])

explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.lift: There is no mathematical or logical content to summarize since no definition or theorem is provided.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.ClosedPr: This theorem asserts that if a property holds for two objects in a monoidal closed category, then it also holds for the morphism between those objects represented by the corresponding internal hom.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mkOfUnitCounit: This definition constructs an adjunction between two functors by providing the required unit and counit that satisfy the triangle identities.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ihom.coev: This definition describes a natural transformation that relates the identity functor to the composition of the functor that tensors objects on the left with a closed object and the functor representing morphisms from that closed object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ihom.coev_naturality: This theorem establishes the naturality of the coevaluation transformation in relation to morphisms between objects in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ihom.ev: This definition describes a natural transformation that represents evaluation from the internal hom associated with a closed object to the identity functor in a monoidal category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ihom.ev_naturality: This theorem establishes a naturality condition for the evaluation natural transformation associated with a closed object in a monoidal category, relating the action of a morphism to evaluations at different points.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.fullMono.fullDefinition: instance fullMonoidalClosedSubcategory : MonoidalClosed (FullSubcategory P) where   closed X :=     { rightAdj := FullSubcategory.lift P (fullSubcategoryInclusion P ⋙ ihom X.1)         fun Y => prop_ihom X.2 Y.2       adj :=         Adjunction.mkOfUnitCounit         { unit :=           { app := fun Y => (ihom.coev X.1).app Y.1             naturality := fun Y Z f => ihom.coev_naturality X.1 f }           counit :=           { app := fun Y => (ihom.ev X.1).app Y.1             naturality := fun Y Z f => ihom.ev_naturality X.1 f }           left_triangle := by ext Y; simp [FullSubcategory.comp_def, FullSubcategory.id_def]           right_triangle := by ext Y; simp [FullSubcategory.comp_def, FullSubcategory.id_def] } }
CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.fullMono.description: This definition asserts that a full subcategory defined by a property that meets certain conditions inherits the structure of a monoidal closed category from the overarching monoidal closed category it belongs to.
