CategoryTheory.Tor.{u_1, u_2} (C : Type u_1) [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [MonoidalCategory C] [Abelian C]
  [MonoidalPreadditive C] [HasProjectiveResolutions C] (n : ℕ) : C ⥤ C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.Tor.comment: We define `Tor C n : C ⥤ C ⥤ C` by left-deriving in the second factor of `(X, Y) ↦ X ⊗ Y`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.leftDerived: The left derived functors of an additive functor provide a functor from one abelian category to another that captures higher homological information through the application of projective resolutions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.leftDerived: A natural transformation between two additive functors induces a corresponding natural transformation between their left derived functors at a specified degree.

CategoryTheory.Tor.fullDefinition: def Tor (n : ℕ) : C ⥤ C ⥤ C where   obj X := Functor.leftDerived ((tensoringLeft C).obj X) n   map f := NatTrans.leftDerived ((tensoringLeft C).map f) n set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Tor.description: This definition introduces a functor that computes the Tor functor in a category, deriving it with respect to the tensor product operation in the context of a monoidal and abelian structure.

CategoryTheory.pi.code:
CategoryTheory.pi.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)] :
  Category.{max w₀ v₁, max u₁ w₀} ((i : I) → C i)
CategoryTheory.pi.comment: `pi C` gives the cartesian product of an indexed family of categories.

explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.

CategoryTheory.pi.fullDefinition: instance pi : Category.{max w₀ v₁} (∀ i, C i) where   Hom X Y := ∀ i, X i ⟶ Y i   id X i := 𝟙 (X i)   comp f g i := f i ≫ g i
CategoryTheory.pi.description: This definition describes the category of functors that can be formed from an indexed family of categories.

CategoryTheory.pi'.code:
CategoryTheory.pi'.{v₁, u₁} {I : Type v₁} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)] :
  Category.{v₁, max u₁ v₁} ((i : I) → C i)
CategoryTheory.pi'.comment:
This provides some assistance to typeclass search in a common situation,
which otherwise fails. (Without this `CategoryTheory.Pi.has_limit_of_has_limit_comp_eval` fails.)
CategoryTheory.pi'.fullDefinition: abbrev pi' {I : Type v₁} (C : I → Type u₁) [∀ i, Category.{v₁} (C i)] : Category.{v₁} (∀ i, C i) :=   CategoryTheory.pi C
CategoryTheory.pi'.description: This definition establishes a category structure for an indexed family of categories, facilitating typeclass search in scenarios where it might otherwise fail.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comp_apply.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.comp_apply.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {X Y Z : (i : I) → C i} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (i : I) : (f ≫ g) i = f i ≫ g i
CategoryTheory.Pi.comp_apply.description: This theorem asserts that the composition of morphisms in an indexed family of objects corresponds to the composition of their respective components at a specific index.

CategoryTheory.Pi.eval.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.eval.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)] (i : I) :
  ((i : I) → C i) ⥤ C i
CategoryTheory.Pi.eval.comment: The evaluation functor at `i : I`, sending an `I`-indexed family of objects to the object over `i`.
CategoryTheory.Pi.eval.fullDefinition: def eval (i : I) : (∀ i, C i) ⥤ C i where   obj f := f i   map α := α i
CategoryTheory.Pi.eval.description: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comap.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.comap.{w₀, w₁, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {J : Type w₁} (h : J → I) : ((i : I) → C i) ⥤ ((j : J) → C (h j))
CategoryTheory.Pi.comap.comment: Pull back an `I`-indexed family of objects to a `J`-indexed family, along a function `J → I`.
CategoryTheory.Pi.comap.fullDefinition: def comap (h : J → I) : (∀ i, C i) ⥤ (∀ j, C (h j)) where   obj f i := f (h i)   map α i := α (h i)
CategoryTheory.Pi.comap.description: This definition describes a functor that pulls back an indexed family of objects from one index type to another through a specified function.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comapId.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapId.{w₀, v₁, u₁} (I : Type w₀) (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)] :
  comap C id ≅ 𝟭 ((i : I) → C i)
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapId.comment:
The natural isomorphism between
pulling back a grading along the identity function,
and the identity functor.

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comapId.fullDefinition: def comapId : comap C (id : I → I) ≅ 𝟭 (∀ i, C i) where   hom := { app := fun X => 𝟙 X }   inv := { app := fun X => 𝟙 X }
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapId.description: This definition establishes a natural isomorphism showing that pulling back an indexed family of categories along the identity function is equivalent to the identity functor on that family.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comapComp.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapComp.{w₀, w₁, w₂, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {J : Type w₁} {K : Type w₂} (f : K → J) (g : J → I) : comap C g ⋙ comap (C ∘ g) f ≅ comap C (g ∘ f)
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapComp.comment:
The natural isomorphism comparing between
pulling back along two successive functions, and
pulling back along their composition

explanatories.funext: This theorem expresses that if two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comapComp.fullDefinition: def comapComp (f : K → J) (g : J → I) : comap C g ⋙ comap (C ∘ g) f ≅ comap C (g ∘ f) where   hom :=   { app := fun X b => 𝟙 (X (g (f b)))     naturality := fun X Y f' => by simp only [comap, Function.comp]; funext; simp }   inv :=   { app := fun X b => 𝟙 (X (g (f b)))     naturality := fun X Y f' => by simp only [comap, Function.comp]; funext; simp }
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapComp.description: This definition describes a natural isomorphism that relates the process of pulling back an indexed family of categories along two successive mappings to pulling back along the composition of those mappings.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comapEvalIsoEval.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapEvalIsoEval.{w₀, w₁, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {J : Type w₁} (h : J → I) (j : J) : comap C h ⋙ eval (C ∘ h) j ≅ eval C (h j)
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapEvalIsoEval.comment: The natural isomorphism between pulling back then evaluating, and just evaluating.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eval: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.

CategoryTheory.Pi.comapEvalIsoEval.fullDefinition: def comapEvalIsoEval (h : J → I) (j : J) : comap C h ⋙ eval (C ∘ h) j ≅ eval C (h j) :=   NatIso.ofComponents (fun f => Iso.refl _) (by simp only [Iso.refl]; aesop_cat)
CategoryTheory.Pi.comapEvalIsoEval.description: This definition describes a natural isomorphism that equates the operation of pulling back an indexed family of categories followed by evaluation at a specific point to a direct evaluation at that point.

CategoryTheory.Pi.sumElimCategory.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.sumElimCategory.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {J : Type w₀} {D : J → Type u₁} [(j : J) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (D j)] (s : I ⊕ J) : Category.{v₁, u₁} (Sum.elim C D s)

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.Pi.sumElimCategory.fullDefinition: instance sumElimCategory : ∀ s : Sum I J, Category.{v₁} (Sum.elim C D s)   | Sum.inl i => by     dsimp     infer_instance   | Sum.inr j => by     dsimp     infer_instance
CategoryTheory.Pi.sumElimCategory.description: This definition describes a category constructed from a coproduct of two indexed families of categories.

CategoryTheory.Pi.sum.comment:
The bifunctor combining an `I`-indexed family of objects with a `J`-indexed family of objects
to obtain an `I ⊕ J`-indexed family of objects.

explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the first type into a union of two types.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection function creates a sum type by embedding an element from the second type into a union of two types.

CategoryTheory.Pi.sum.fullDefinition: def sum : (∀ i, C i) ⥤ (∀ j, D j) ⥤ ∀ s : Sum I J, Sum.elim C D s where   obj X :=     { obj := fun Y s =>         match s with         | .inl i => X i         | .inr j => Y j       map := fun {Y} {Y'} f s =>         match s with         | .inl i => 𝟙 (X i)         | .inr j => f j }   map {X} {X'} f :=     { app := fun Y s =>         match s with         | .inl i => f i         | .inr j => 𝟙 (Y j) }
CategoryTheory.Pi.sum.description: This definition defines a bifunctor that combines an indexed family of objects from one category with an indexed family of objects from another category to create an indexed family of objects in the sum category formed by combining the original categories.

CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {X Y : (i : I) → C i} (f : X ≅ Y) (i : I) : X i ≅ Y i
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp.comment:
An isomorphism between `I`-indexed objects gives an isomorphism between each
pair of corresponding components.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity morphism of an indexed family of objects is equal to the identity morphism of any specific object within that family.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.comp_apply: This theorem asserts that the composition of morphisms in an indexed family of objects corresponds to the composition of their respective components at a specific index.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.

CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp.fullDefinition: def isoApp {X Y : ∀ i, C i} (f : X ≅ Y) (i : I) : X i ≅ Y i :=   ⟨f.hom i, f.inv i,     by rw [← comp_apply, Iso.hom_inv_id, id_apply], by rw [← comp_apply, Iso.inv_hom_id, id_apply]⟩
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp.description: This definition states that an isomorphism between indexed objects implies an isomorphism between their corresponding components at each index.

CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_refl.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_refl.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  (X : (i : I) → C i) (i : I) : isoApp (Iso.refl X) i = Iso.refl (X i)
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_refl.description: This theorem demonstrates that applying the identity isomorphism to an indexed object at a specific index yields the identity isomorphism of that object's corresponding component.

CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_symm.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_symm.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {X Y : (i : I) → C i} (f : X ≅ Y) (i : I) : isoApp f.symm i = (isoApp f i).symm
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_symm.description: This theorem states that the application of the inverse isomorphism at a specific index is equivalent to the inverse of the isomorphism applied at that same index.

CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_trans.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_trans.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {X Y Z : (i : I) → C i} (f : X ≅ Y) (g : Y ≅ Z) (i : I) : isoApp (f ≪≫ g) i = isoApp f i ≪≫ isoApp g i
CategoryTheory.Pi.isoApp_trans.description: This theorem states that the application of the composition of two isomorphisms to an indexed object at a specific index is equivalent to the composition of the isomorphisms applied independently at that index.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi.{w₀, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {D : I → Type u₂} [(i : I) → Category.{v₂, u₂} (D i)] (F : (i : I) → C i ⥤ D i) : ((i : I) → C i) ⥤ ((i : I) → D i)
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi.comment: Assemble an `I`-indexed family of functors into a functor between the pi types.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi: This definition describes the category of functors that can be formed from an indexed family of categories.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (F : ∀ i, C i ⥤ D i) : (∀ i, C i) ⥤ ∀ i, D i where   obj f i := (F i).obj (f i)   map α i := (F i).map (α i)
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi.description: This definition constructs a functor that combines an indexed family of functors into a single functor between two indexed families of objects.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'.{w₀, v₁, v₃, u₁, u₃} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {A : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} A] (f : (i : I) → A ⥤ C i) : A ⥤ ((i : I) → C i)
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'.comment: Similar to `pi`, but all functors come from the same category `A`

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi': This definition establishes a category structure for an indexed family of categories, facilitating typeclass search in scenarios where it might otherwise fail.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'.fullDefinition: def pi' (f : ∀ i, A ⥤ C i) : A ⥤ ∀ i, C i where   obj a i := (f i).obj a   map h i := (f i).map h
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'.description: This definition describes a functor that maps between a single category and an indexed family of categories using functors from that single category to each category in the family.

CategoryTheory.Functor.eqToHom_proj.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.eqToHom_proj.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {x x' : (i : I) → C i} (h : x = x') (i : I) : eqToHom h i = eqToHom ⋯
CategoryTheory.Functor.eqToHom_proj.description: This theorem asserts that if two indexed objects are equal, then the morphisms corresponding to their equality can be expressed uniformly at any index in the family.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'_eval.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'_eval.{w₀, v₁, v₃, u₁, u₃} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {A : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} A] (f : (i : I) → A ⥤ C i) (i : I) : pi' f ⋙ Pi.eval C i = f i

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi': This definition establishes a category structure for an indexed family of categories, facilitating typeclass search in scenarios where it might otherwise fail.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eval: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'_eval.description: This theorem asserts that the natural transformation resulting from applying a functorial evaluation to an indexed family of functors equals the specific functor corresponding to a given index.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi_ext.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi_ext.{w₀, v₁, v₃, u₁, u₃} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {A : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} A] (f f' : A ⥤ ((i : I) → C i)) (h : ∀ (i : I), f ⋙ Pi.eval C i = f' ⋙ Pi.eval C i) :
  f = f'
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi_ext.comment: Two functors to a product category are equal iff they agree on every coordinate.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eval: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi_ext.description: This theorem states that two functors from a single category to a product category are equal if they produce the same result when composed with functors that evaluate at every index.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi.{w₀, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {D : I → Type u₂} [(i : I) → Category.{v₂, u₂} (D i)] {F G : (i : I) → C i ⥤ D i} (α : (i : I) → F i ⟶ G i) :
  Functor.pi F ⟶ Functor.pi G
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi.comment: Assemble an `I`-indexed family of natural transformations into a single natural transformation.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi: This definition describes the category of functors that can be formed from an indexed family of categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.pi: This definition constructs a functor that combines an indexed family of functors into a single functor between two indexed families of objects.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (α : ∀ i, F i ⟶ G i) : Functor.pi F ⟶ Functor.pi G where   app f i := (α i).app (f i)
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi.description: This definition constructs a natural transformation from the functor associated with an indexed family of morphisms to the functor associated with another indexed family of morphisms by assembling these morphisms into a single natural transformation.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi'.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi'.{w₀, v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {E : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} E] {F G : E ⥤ ((i : I) → C i)} (τ : (i : I) → F ⋙ Pi.eval C i ⟶ G ⋙ Pi.eval C i) :
  F ⟶ G
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi'.comment: Assemble an `I`-indexed family of natural transformations into a single natural transformation.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi': This definition establishes a category structure for an indexed family of categories, facilitating typeclass search in scenarios where it might otherwise fail.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eval: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.pi': This definition describes a functor that maps between a single category and an indexed family of categories using functors from that single category to each category in the family.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi'.fullDefinition: def pi' {E : Type*} [Category E] {F G : E ⥤ ∀ i, C i}     (τ : ∀ i, F ⋙ Pi.eval C i ⟶ G ⋙ Pi.eval C i) : F ⟶ G where   app := fun X i => (τ i).app X   naturality _ _ f := by     ext i     exact (τ i).naturality f
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi'.description: This definition constructs a single natural transformation from an indexed family of natural transformations between two functors, effectively aggregating them into one coherent transformation.

CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalence.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalence.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁) [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {i j : I} (h : i = j) : C i ≌ C j
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalence.comment:
For a family of categories `C i` indexed by `I`, an equality `i = j` in `I` induces
an equivalence `C i ≌ C j`.
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalence.fullDefinition: def Pi.eqToEquivalence {i j : I} (h : i = j) : C i ≌ C j := by subst h; rfl
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalence.description: This definition states that if two indices in an indexed family of categories are equal, then the categories at those indices are equivalent.

CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi'.code:
CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi'.{w₀, v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {E : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} E] {F G : E ⥤ ((i : I) → C i)} (e : (i : I) → F ⋙ eval C i ≅ G ⋙ eval C i) : F ≅ G
CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi'.comment: Assemble an `I`-indexed family of natural isomorphisms into a single natural isomorphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi': This definition establishes a category structure for an indexed family of categories, facilitating typeclass search in scenarios where it might otherwise fail.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eval: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.pi': This definition describes a functor that maps between a single category and an indexed family of categories using functors from that single category to each category in the family.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi': This definition constructs a single natural transformation from an indexed family of natural transformations between two functors, effectively aggregating them into one coherent transformation.

CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi'.fullDefinition: def pi' {E : Type*} [Category E] {F G : E ⥤ ∀ i, C i}     (e : ∀ i, F ⋙ Pi.eval C i ≅ G ⋙ Pi.eval C i) : F ≅ G where   hom := NatTrans.pi' (fun i => (e i).hom)   inv := NatTrans.pi' (fun i => (e i).inv)
CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi'.description: This definition constructs a natural isomorphism between two functors by combining an indexed family of natural isomorphisms associated with these functors evaluated at each index.

CategoryTheory.Pi.evalCompEqToEquivalenc.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.evalCompEqToEquivalenceFunctor.{w₀, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} (C : I → Type u₁)
  [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)] {i j : I} (h : i = j) : eval C i ⋙ (eqToEquivalence C h).functor ≅ eval C j
CategoryTheory.Pi.evalCompEqToEquivalenc.comment:
When `i = j`, projections `Pi.eval C i` and `Pi.eval C j` are related by the equivalence
`Pi.eqToEquivalence C h : C i ≌ C j`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalence: This definition states that if two indices in an indexed family of categories are equal, then the categories at those indices are equivalent.

CategoryTheory.Pi.evalCompEqToEquivalenc.fullDefinition: def Pi.evalCompEqToEquivalenceFunctor {i j : I} (h : i = j) :     Pi.eval C i ⋙ (Pi.eqToEquivalence C h).functor ≅       Pi.eval C j :=   eqToIso (by subst h; rfl)
CategoryTheory.Pi.evalCompEqToEquivalenc.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects at one index and the functor that evaluates it at another index, provided the indices are equal, using the equivalence induced by their equality.

CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalenceFunctor.code:
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalenceFunctorIso.{w₀, w₁, v₁, u₁} {I : Type w₀} {J : Type w₁} (C : I → Type u₁)
  [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)] (f : J → I) {i' j' : J} (h : i' = j') :
  (eqToEquivalence C ⋯).functor ≅ (eqToEquivalence (fun i' => C (f i')) h).functor
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalenceFunctor.comment: The equivalences given by `Pi.eqToEquivalence` are compatible with reindexing.
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalenceFunctor.fullDefinition: def Pi.eqToEquivalenceFunctorIso (f : J → I) {i' j' : J} (h : i' = j') :     (Pi.eqToEquivalence C (congr_arg f h)).functor ≅       (Pi.eqToEquivalence (fun i' => C (f i')) h).functor :=   eqToIso (by subst h; rfl)
CategoryTheory.Pi.eqToEquivalenceFunctor.description: This definition asserts that the equivalences derived from a product category are preserved when the indices are changed through a reindexing function.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'CompEval.comment: The projections of `Functor.pi' F` are isomorphic to the functors of the family `F`

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi': This definition establishes a category structure for an indexed family of categories, facilitating typeclass search in scenarios where it might otherwise fail.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Pi.eval: This definition introduces a functor that evaluates an indexed family of objects, mapping it to the specific object corresponding to a given index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi': This definition constructs a single natural transformation from an indexed family of natural transformations between two functors, effectively aggregating them into one coherent transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi': This definition constructs a natural isomorphism between two functors by combining an indexed family of natural isomorphisms associated with these functors evaluated at each index.

CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'CompEval.fullDefinition: def pi'CompEval {A : Type*} [Category A] (F : ∀ i, A ⥤ C i) (i : I) :     pi' F ⋙ Pi.eval C i ≅ F i :=   Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Functor.pi'CompEval.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the functor obtained by applying a family of functors to an index and the corresponding functor from that family evaluated at that index.

CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi.code:
CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi.{w₀, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {D : I → Type u₂} [(i : I) → Category.{v₂, u₂} (D i)] {F G : (i : I) → C i ⥤ D i} (e : (i : I) → F i ≅ G i) :
  Functor.pi F ≅ Functor.pi G
CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi.comment: Assemble an `I`-indexed family of natural isomorphisms into a single natural isomorphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi: This definition describes the category of functors that can be formed from an indexed family of categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.pi: This definition constructs a functor that combines an indexed family of functors into a single functor between two indexed families of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi: This definition constructs a natural transformation from the functor associated with an indexed family of morphisms to the functor associated with another indexed family of morphisms by assembling these morphisms into a single natural transformation.

CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (e : ∀ i, F i ≅ G i) : Functor.pi F ≅ Functor.pi G where   hom := NatTrans.pi (fun i => (e i).hom)   inv := NatTrans.pi (fun i => (e i).inv)
CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi.description: This definition states that a collection of natural isomorphisms between an indexed family of functors can be combined into a single natural isomorphism between the functors formed by taking the product of those families.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pi.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pi.{w₀, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {I : Type w₀} {C : I → Type u₁} [(i : I) → Category.{v₁, u₁} (C i)]
  {D : I → Type u₂} [(i : I) → Category.{v₂, u₂} (D i)] (E : (i : I) → C i ≌ D i) : ((i : I) → C i) ≌ (i : I) → D i
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pi.comment:
Assemble an `I`-indexed family of equivalences of categories
into a single equivalence.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.pi: This definition describes the category of functors that can be formed from an indexed family of categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.pi: This definition constructs a functor that combines an indexed family of functors into a single functor between two indexed families of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatTrans.pi: This definition constructs a natural transformation from the functor associated with an indexed family of morphisms to the functor associated with another indexed family of morphisms by assembling these morphisms into a single natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.pi: This definition states that a collection of natural isomorphisms between an indexed family of functors can be combined into a single natural isomorphism between the functors formed by taking the product of those families.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pi.fullDefinition: def pi (E : ∀ i, C i ≌ D i) : (∀ i, C i) ≌ (∀ i, D i) where   functor := Functor.pi (fun i => (E i).functor)   inverse := Functor.pi (fun i => (E i).inverse)   unitIso := NatIso.pi (fun i => (E i).unitIso)   counitIso := NatIso.pi (fun i => (E i).counitIso)
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.pi.description: This definition combines an indexed family of category equivalences into a single overall equivalence between the functors representing those categories.

CategoryTheory.Paths.comment: A type synonym for the category of paths in a quiver.
CategoryTheory.Paths.fullDefinition: def Paths (V : Type u₁) : Type u₁ := V
CategoryTheory.Paths.description: This defines a type that represents the category of paths within a quiver.

CategoryTheory.Paths.categoryPaths.code: CategoryTheory.Paths.categoryPaths.{v₁, u₁} (V : Type u₁) [Quiver V] : Category.{max u₁ v₁, u₁} (Paths V)

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.

CategoryTheory.Paths.categoryPaths.fullDefinition: instance categoryPaths : Category.{max u₁ v₁} (Paths V) where   Hom := fun X Y : V => Quiver.Path X Y   id X := Quiver.Path.nil   comp f g := Quiver.Path.comp f g
CategoryTheory.Paths.categoryPaths.description: This defines a category structure for the paths in a quiver, using a specified type as the underlying set.

CategoryTheory.Paths.of.code: CategoryTheory.Paths.of.{v₁, u₁} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] : V ⥤q Paths V
CategoryTheory.Paths.of.comment: The inclusion of a quiver `V` into its path category, as a prefunctor.
CategoryTheory.Paths.of.fullDefinition: def of : V ⥤q Paths V where   obj X := X   map f := f.toPath
CategoryTheory.Paths.of.description: This defines a prefunctor that includes a quiver into its corresponding path category.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift.code:
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  (φ : V ⥤q C) : Paths V ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift.comment: Any prefunctor from `V` lifts to a functor from `paths V`

explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift.fullDefinition: def lift {C} [Category C] (φ : V ⥤q C) : Paths V ⥤ C where   obj := φ.obj   map {X} {Y} f :=     @Quiver.Path.rec V _ X (fun Y _ => φ.obj X ⟶ φ.obj Y) (𝟙 <| φ.obj X)       (fun _ f ihp => ihp ≫ φ.map f) Y f   map_id X := rfl   map_comp f g := by     induction' g with _ _ g' p ih _ _ _     · rw [Category.comp_id]       rfl     · have : f ≫ Quiver.Path.cons g' p = (f ≫ g').cons p := by apply Quiver.Path.comp_cons       rw [this]       simp only at ih ⊢       rw [ih, Category.assoc]
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift.description: This defines a way to lift any prefunctor from a quiver to a functor from its path category.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_nil.code:
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_nil.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  (φ : V ⥤q C) (X : V) : (lift φ).map Quiver.Path.nil = 𝟙 (φ.obj X)
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_nil.description: This theorem asserts that the image of the empty path in a quiver under a specific functor is the identity morphism at the image of the corresponding vertex.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_cons.code:
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_cons.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  (φ : V ⥤q C) {X Y Z : V} (p : Quiver.Path X Y) (f : Y ⟶ Z) : (lift φ).map (p.cons f) = (lift φ).map p ≫ φ.map f
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_cons.description: This theorem states that the image of a path extended by a morphism under a specific functor equals the composition of the functor applied to the original path and the morphism itself.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_toPath.code:
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_toPath.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  (φ : V ⥤q C) {X Y : V} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (lift φ).map f.toPath = φ.map f
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_toPath.description: This theorem asserts that the image of a morphism represented as a path under a functor corresponds to the application of that functor directly to the morphism.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_spec.code:
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_spec.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  (φ : V ⥤q C) : of ⋙q (lift φ).toPrefunctor = φ

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Paths.of: This defines a prefunctor that includes a quiver into its corresponding path category.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_spec.description: This theorem states that the composition of the inclusion functor of paths into a category with the lifting functor results in the original functor from the quiver to the category.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_unique.code:
CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_unique.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  (φ : V ⥤q C) (Φ : Paths V ⥤ C) (hΦ : of ⋙q Φ.toPrefunctor = φ) : Φ = lift φ

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Paths.of: This defines a prefunctor that includes a quiver into its corresponding path category.

CategoryTheory.Paths.lift_unique.description: This theorem establishes that any functor from the path category, which agrees with a specific lifting functor when composed with the inclusion functor, must be identical to that lifting functor.

CategoryTheory.Paths.ext_functor.code:
CategoryTheory.Paths.ext_functor.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {V : Type u₁} [Quiver V] {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {F G : Paths V ⥤ C} (h_obj : F.obj = G.obj)

CategoryTheory.quotientPathsEquiv.fullDefinition: def quotientPathsEquiv : Quotient (pathsHomRel C) ≌ C where   functor := quotientPathsTo C   inverse := toQuotientPaths C   unitIso :=     NatIso.ofComponents       (fun X => by cases X; rfl)       (Quot.ind fun f => by         apply Quot.sound         apply Quotient.CompClosure.of         simp [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp, pathsHomRel])   counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => Iso.refl _) (fun f => by simp [Quot.liftOn_mk])   functor_unitIso_comp X := by     cases X     simp only [pathsHomRel, pathComposition_obj, pathComposition_map, Functor.id_obj,                quotientPathsTo_obj, Functor.comp_obj, toQuotientPaths_obj_as,                NatIso.ofComponents_hom_app, Iso.refl_hom, quotientPathsTo_map, Category.comp_id]     rfl

Because we do not allow morphisms in `Prop` (only in `Type`),

CategoryTheory.Discrete.functorComp.fullDefinition: def functorComp {I : Type u₁} {J : Type u₁'} (f : J → C) (g : I → J) :     Discrete.functor (f ∘ g) ≅ Discrete.functor (Discrete.mk ∘ g) ⋙ Discrete.functor f :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun X => Iso.refl _
CategoryTheory.Discrete.functorComp.description: This definition states that the functor resulting from the composition of two functions can be equivalently expressed as the composition of two discrete functors.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.natTrans.code:
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natTrans.{v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] {I : Type u₁} {F G : Discrete I ⥤ C}
  (f : (i : Discrete I) → F.obj i ⟶ G.obj i) : F ⟶ G
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natTrans.comment:
For functors out of a discrete category,
a natural transformation is just a collection of maps,
as the naturality squares are trivial.

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.natTrans.fullDefinition: def natTrans {I : Type u₁} {F G : Discrete I ⥤ C} (f : ∀ i : Discrete I, F.obj i ⟶ G.obj i) :     F ⟶ G where   app := f   naturality := fun {X Y} ⟨⟨g⟩⟩ => by     discrete_cases     rcases g     change F.map (𝟙 _) ≫ _ = _ ≫ G.map (𝟙 _)     simp
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natTrans.description: This definition states that a natural transformation between functors from a discrete category consists of a collection of maps, since the naturality conditions are trivial in this case.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso.{v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] {I : Type u₁} {F G : Discrete I ⥤ C}
  (f : (i : Discrete I) → F.obj i ≅ G.obj i) : F ≅ G
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso.comment:
For functors out of a discrete category,
a natural isomorphism is just a collection of isomorphisms,
as the naturality squares are trivial.

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso.fullDefinition: def natIso {I : Type u₁} {F G : Discrete I ⥤ C} (f : ∀ i : Discrete I, F.obj i ≅ G.obj i) :     F ≅ G :=   NatIso.ofComponents f fun ⟨⟨g⟩⟩ => by     discrete_cases     rcases g     change F.map (𝟙 _) ≫ _ = _ ≫ G.map (𝟙 _)     simp
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso.description: This definition shows that for functors from a discrete category, a natural isomorphism is characterized by a set of isomorphisms since the naturality conditions are trivially satisfied.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso_app.code:
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso_app.{v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} C] {I : Type u₁} {F G : Discrete I ⥤ C}
  (f : (i : Discrete I) → F.obj i ≅ G.obj i) (i : Discrete I) : (natIso f).app i = f i
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso_app.description: This theorem establishes that the natural isomorphism applied to a discrete functor coincides with the morphism defined by that functor at any object in the discrete category.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIsoFunctor.code:

  {F : Discrete I ⥤ C} : F ≅ functor (F.obj ∘ mk)
CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIsoFunctor.comment:
Every functor `F` from a discrete category is naturally isomorphic (actually, equal) to
`Discrete.functor (F.obj)`.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.compNatIsoDiscre.fullDefinition: def compNatIsoDiscrete {I : Type u₁} {D : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} D] (F : I → C) (G : C ⥤ D) :     Discrete.functor F ⋙ G ≅ Discrete.functor (G.obj ∘ F) :=   natIso fun _ => Iso.refl _

CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivalence.fullDefinition: def equivalence {I : Type u₁} {J : Type u₂} (e : I ≃ J) : Discrete I ≌ Discrete J where   functor := Discrete.functor (Discrete.mk ∘ (e : I → J))   inverse := Discrete.functor (Discrete.mk ∘ (e.symm : J → I))   unitIso :=     Discrete.natIso fun i => eqToIso (by aesop_cat)   counitIso :=     Discrete.natIso fun j => eqToIso (by aesop_cat)
CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivalence.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between two discrete categories by promoting a type-level equivalence between their underlying types.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivOfEquivalen.code: CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivOfEquivalence.{u₁, u₂} {α : Type u₁} {β : Type u₂} (h : Discrete α ≌ Discrete β) : α ≃ β

CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivOfEquivalen.fullDefinition: def equivOfEquivalence {α : Type u₁} {β : Type u₂} (h : Discrete α ≌ Discrete β) : α ≃ β where   toFun := Discrete.as ∘ h.functor.obj ∘ Discrete.mk   invFun := Discrete.as ∘ h.inverse.obj ∘ Discrete.mk   left_inv a := by simpa using eq_of_hom (h.unitIso.app (Discrete.mk a)).2   right_inv a := by simpa using eq_of_hom (h.counitIso.app (Discrete.mk a)).1
CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivOfEquivalen.description: This definition provides a method to convert an equivalence of discrete categories into a type-level equivalence between the underlying types.

CategoryTheory.Discrete.opposite.fullDefinition: protected def opposite (α : Type u₁) : (Discrete α)ᵒᵖ ≌ Discrete α :=   let F : Discrete α ⥤ (Discrete α)ᵒᵖ := Discrete.functor fun x => op (Discrete.mk x)   Equivalence.mk F.leftOp F   (NatIso.ofComponents fun ⟨X⟩ => Iso.refl _)   (Discrete.natIso fun ⟨X⟩ => Iso.refl _)
CategoryTheory.Discrete.opposite.description: This definition indicates that a discrete category is equivalent to its opposite category.

The horizontal composition of two commutative squares as below is a commutative square.
```
  W ---f---> X ---f'--> X'
  |          |          |
  g          h          h'
  |          |          |
  v          v          v
  Y ---i---> Z ---i'--> Z'

```

CategoryTheory.CommSq.LiftStruct.unopEqu.fullDefinition: def unopEquiv {A B X Y : Cᵒᵖ} {f : A ⟶ X} {i : A ⟶ B} {p : X ⟶ Y} {g : B ⟶ Y}     (sq : CommSq f i p g) : LiftStruct sq ≃ LiftStruct sq.unop where   toFun := unop   invFun := op   left_inv := by aesop_cat   right_inv := by aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.CommSq.LiftStruct.unopEqu.description: This definition provides a bijective correspondence between the lift structures of a commutative square in an opposite category and its corresponding square in the original category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.LiftStruct.fac_lef: This theorem asserts that for a specific lifting structure associated with a commutative square, the composition of a morphism from one object to another equals the morphism from that object to a third object when projected through the lifting structure.

CategoryTheory.CommSq.subsingleton_liftS.fullDefinition: instance subsingleton_liftStruct_of_epi (sq : CommSq f i p g) [Epi i] :     Subsingleton (LiftStruct sq) :=   ⟨fun l₁ l₂ => by     ext     rw [← cancel_epi i]     simp only [LiftStruct.fac_left]⟩
CategoryTheory.CommSq.subsingleton_liftS.description: This definition states that if a commutative square has an epimorphism in its structure, then its lift structure is unique.

CategoryTheory.CommSq.subsingleton_liftS.code:
CategoryTheory.CommSq.subsingleton_liftStruct_of_mono.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C}
  {f : A ⟶ X} {i : A ⟶ B} {p : X ⟶ Y} {g : B ⟶ Y} (sq : CommSq f i p g) [Mono p] : Subsingleton sq.LiftStruct

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.LiftStruct.fac_rig: This theorem asserts that the composition of a certain morphism with another morphism in a commutative square equals a specified morphism, thereby confirming the commutativity of the lower right triangle.

CategoryTheory.CommSq.subsingleton_liftS.fullDefinition: instance subsingleton_liftStruct_of_mono (sq : CommSq f i p g) [Mono p] :     Subsingleton (LiftStruct sq) :=   ⟨fun l₁ l₂ => by     ext     rw [← cancel_mono p]     simp only [LiftStruct.fac_right]⟩
CategoryTheory.CommSq.subsingleton_liftS.description: This definition states that the lift structure associated with a commutative square is uniquely determined when one of the morphisms in the square is a monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.LargeGroupoid.comment:
A `LargeGroupoid` is a groupoid
where the objects live in `Type (u+1)` while the morphisms live in `Type u`.
CategoryTheory.LargeGroupoid.fullDefinition: abbrev LargeGroupoid (C : Type (u + 1)) : Type (u + 1) :=   Groupoid.{u} C
CategoryTheory.LargeGroupoid.description: This definition describes a large groupoid structure where objects belong to a higher universe level and morphisms belong to a lower one.

CategoryTheory.SmallGroupoid.comment:
A `SmallGroupoid` is a groupoid
where the objects and morphisms live in the same universe.
CategoryTheory.SmallGroupoid.fullDefinition: abbrev SmallGroupoid (C : Type u) : Type (u + 1) :=   Groupoid.{u} C
CategoryTheory.SmallGroupoid.description: This definition introduces a small groupoid structure where both the objects and morphisms exist within the same universe level.

CategoryTheory.Groupoid.inv.code: CategoryTheory.Groupoid.inv.{v, u} {obj : Type u} [self : Groupoid obj] {X Y : obj} : (X ⟶ Y) → (Y ⟶ X)
CategoryTheory.Groupoid.inv.fullDefinition: inv : ∀ {X Y : obj}, (X ⟶ Y) → (Y ⟶ X)   /-- `inv f` composed `f` is the identity -/   inv_comp : ∀ {X Y : obj} (f : X ⟶ Y), comp (inv f) f = id Y := by aesop_cat   /-- `f` composed with `inv f` is the identity -/   comp_inv : ∀ {X Y : obj} (f : X ⟶ Y), comp f (inv f) = id X := by aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Groupoid.inv.description: This definition specifies a process for obtaining the inverse of a morphism between objects in a groupoid.

CategoryTheory.Groupoid.invEquiv.description: This definition establishes a correspondence between morphisms in a groupoid and their inverses, indicating that the process of taking an inverse is an equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Groupoid.vertexGroupIsomO.fullDefinition: def vertexGroupIsomOfMap {c d : C} (f : c ⟶ d) : (c ⟶ c) ≃* (d ⟶ d) where   toFun γ := inv f ≫ γ ≫ f   invFun δ := f ≫ δ ≫ inv f   left_inv γ := by     simp_rw [Category.assoc, comp_inv, Category.comp_id, ← Category.assoc, comp_inv,       Category.id_comp]   right_inv δ := by     simp_rw [Category.assoc, inv_comp, ← Category.assoc, inv_comp, Category.id_comp,       Category.comp_id]   map_mul' γ₁ γ₂ := by     simp only [vertexGroup_mul, inv_eq_inv, Category.assoc, IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
CategoryTheory.Groupoid.vertexGroupIsomO.description: This definition states that a morphism in a groupoid induces a group isomorphism between the endomorphism groups of its source and target objects.

CategoryTheory.Groupoid.vertexGroupIsomO.fullDefinition: def vertexGroupIsomOfMap {c d : C} (f : c ⟶ d) : (c ⟶ c) ≃* (d ⟶ d) where   toFun γ := inv f ≫ γ ≫ f   invFun δ := f ≫ δ ≫ inv f   left_inv γ := by     simp_rw [Category.assoc, comp_inv, Category.comp_id, ← Category.assoc, comp_inv,       Category.id_comp]   right_inv δ := by     simp_rw [Category.assoc, inv_comp, ← Category.assoc, inv_comp, Category.id_comp,       Category.comp_id]   map_mul' γ₁ γ₂ := by     simp only [vertexGroup_mul, inv_eq_inv, Category.assoc, IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc]

CategoryTheory.ComposableArrows.homMk.fullDefinition: def homMk {F G : ComposableArrows C n} (app : ∀ i, F.obj i ⟶ G.obj i)     (w : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < n), F.map' i (i + 1) ≫ app _ = app _ ≫ G.map' i (i + 1)) :     F ⟶ G where   app := app   naturality := by     suffices ∀ (k i j : ℕ) (hj : i + k = j) (hj' : j ≤ n),         F.map' i j ≫ app _ = app _ ≫ G.map' i j by       rintro ⟨i, hi⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩ hij       have hij' := leOfHom hij       simp only [Fin.mk_le_mk] at hij'       obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Nat.le.dest hij'       exact this k i j hk (by valid)     intro k     induction' k with k hk     · intro i j hj hj'       simp only [Nat.zero_eq, add_zero] at hj       obtain rfl := hj       rw [F.map'_self i, G.map'_self i, id_comp, comp_id]     · intro i j hj hj'       rw [← add_assoc] at hj       subst hj       rw [F.map'_comp i (i + k) (i + k + 1), G.map'_comp i (i + k) (i + k + 1), assoc,         w (i + k) (by valid), reassoc_of% (hk i (i + k) rfl (by valid))]
CategoryTheory.ComposableArrows.homMk.description: This definition introduces a constructor for morphisms between two types of composable arrows that require a collection of morphisms and a naturality condition for specific mappings.

CategoryTheory.ComposableArrows.isoMk.code:
CategoryTheory.ComposableArrows.isoMk.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {n : ℕ}
  {F G : ComposableArrows C n} (app : (i : Fin (n + 1)) → F.obj i ≅ G.obj i)
  (w :
    ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < n), F.map' i (i + 1) ⋯ hi ≫ (app ⟨i + 1, ⋯⟩).hom = (app ⟨i, ⋯⟩).hom ≫ G.map' i (i + 1) ⋯ hi) :
  F ≅ G
CategoryTheory.ComposableArrows.isoMk.comment:
Constructor for isomorphisms `F ≅ G` in `ComposableArrows C n` which takes as inputs
a family of isomorphisms `F.obj i ≅ G.obj i` and the naturality condition only for the
maps in `Fin (n + 1)` given by inequalities of the form `i ≤ i + 1`.

CategoryTheory.ComposableArrows.isoMk.fullDefinition: def isoMk {F G : ComposableArrows C n} (app : ∀ i, F.obj i ≅ G.obj i)     (w : ∀ (i : ℕ) (hi : i < n),       F.map' i (i + 1) ≫ (app _).hom = (app _).hom ≫ G.map' i (i + 1)) :     F ≅ G where   hom := homMk (fun i => (app i).hom) w   inv := homMk (fun i => (app i).inv) (fun i hi => by     dsimp only     rw [← cancel_epi ((app _).hom), ← reassoc_of% (w i hi), Iso.hom_inv_id, comp_id,       Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc])

  (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) {R S T : 𝒮} {a b c : 𝒳} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : S ⟶ T) (φ : a ⟶ b) (ψ : b ⟶ c) [p.IsHomLift f φ]

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.of_commSq: This theorem demonstrates that a hom-lifting property for a functor can be derived from a commuting square condition involving specific morphisms within categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.commSq: This theorem establishes that if a functor exhibits a hom-lifting property for certain morphisms, then the corresponding square formed by the mapping of these morphisms commutes.

CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.comp.fullDefinition: instance comp {R S T : 𝒮} {a b c : 𝒳} (f : R ⟶ S) (g : S ⟶ T) (φ : a ⟶ b)     (ψ : b ⟶ c) [p.IsHomLift f φ] [p.IsHomLift g ψ] : p.IsHomLift (f ≫ g) (φ ≫ ψ) := by   apply of_commSq   rw [p.map_comp]   apply CommSq.horiz_comp (commSq p f φ) (commSq p g ψ)
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.comp.description: This definition asserts that if a functor allows for the hom-lifting property for two sequential morphisms, then it also holds for their composite morphism.

CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.isoOfIsoLift.code:
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.isoOfIsoLift.{u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂} {𝒮 : Type u₁} {𝒳 : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₂} 𝒳]
  [Category.{v₂, u₁} 𝒮] (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) {R S : 𝒮} {a b : 𝒳} (f : R ⟶ S) (φ : a ≅ b) [p.IsHomLift f φ.hom] : R ≅ S
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.isoOfIsoLift.comment:
Given a morphism `f : R ⟶ S`, and an isomorphism `φ : a ≅ b` lifting `f`, `isoOfIsoLift f φ` is
the isomorphism `Φ : R ≅ S` with `Φ.hom = f` induced from `φ`

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.domain_eq: This theorem states that for a functor with a hom-lifting property, the object assigned to a specific morphism corresponds exactly to the source of that morphism in the category.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.isoOfIsoLift.fullDefinition: def isoOfIsoLift (f : R ⟶ S) (φ : a ≅ b) [p.IsHomLift f φ.hom] :     R ≅ S where   hom := f   inv := eqToHom (codomain_eq p f φ.hom).symm ≫ (p.mapIso φ).inv ≫ eqToHom (domain_eq p f φ.hom)   hom_inv_id := by subst_hom_lift p f φ.hom; simp [← p.map_comp]   inv_hom_id := by subst_hom_lift p f φ.hom; simp [← p.map_comp]
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.isoOfIsoLift.description: This definition establishes that if a functor has a hom-lifting property for a morphism, then it induces an isomorphism between specified objects related to an isomorphism between their respective sources.

CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv_lift_inv.code:
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv_lift_inv.{u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂} {𝒮 : Type u₁} {𝒳 : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₂} 𝒳]
  [Category.{v₂, u₁} 𝒮] (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) {R S : 𝒮} {a b : 𝒳} (f : R ≅ S) (φ : a ≅ b) [p.IsHomLift f.hom φ.hom] :
  p.IsHomLift f.inv φ.inv
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv_lift_inv.comment:
Given `φ : a ≅ b` and `f : R ≅ S`, such that `φ.hom` lifts `f.hom`, then `φ.inv` lifts
`f.inv`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.of_commSq: This theorem demonstrates that a hom-lifting property for a functor can be derived from a commuting square condition involving specific morphisms within categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.commSq: This theorem establishes that if a functor exhibits a hom-lifting property for certain morphisms, then the corresponding square formed by the mapping of these morphisms commutes.

CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv_lift_inv.fullDefinition: instance inv_lift_inv (f : R ≅ S) (φ : a ≅ b) [p.IsHomLift f.hom φ.hom] :     p.IsHomLift f.inv φ.inv := by   apply of_commSq   apply CommSq.horiz_inv (f := p.mapIso φ) (commSq p f.hom φ.hom)
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv_lift_inv.description: This definition states that if the homomorphism of an isomorphism between two objects can be lifted by a functor, then the inverse of that isomorphism can also be lifted.

CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv.code:
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv.{u₁, v₁, u₂, v₂} {𝒮 : Type u₁} {𝒳 : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₂} 𝒳] [Category.{v₂, u₁} 𝒮]
  (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) {R S : 𝒮} {a b : 𝒳} (f : R ⟶ S) (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsIso f] [IsIso φ] [p.IsHomLift f φ] :
  p.IsHomLift (inv f) (inv φ)
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv.comment: If `φ : a ⟶ b` lifts `f : R ⟶ S` and both are isomorphisms, then `φ⁻¹` lifts `f⁻¹`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv_lift_inv: This definition states that if the homomorphism of an isomorphism between two objects can be lifted by a functor, then the inverse of that isomorphism can also be lifted.

CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv.fullDefinition: protected instance inv (f : R ⟶ S) (φ : a ⟶ b) [IsIso f] [IsIso φ] [p.IsHomLift f φ] :     p.IsHomLift (inv f) (inv φ) :=   have : p.IsHomLift (asIso f).hom (asIso φ).hom := by simp_all   IsHomLift.inv_lift_inv p (asIso f) (asIso φ)
CategoryTheory.IsHomLift.inv.description: This definition states that if both a morphism and its respective lift are isomorphisms, then the inverses of these morphisms also maintain the hom-lifting property under the same functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.unive.description: This theorem asserts that for a functor exhibiting a Cartesian property, there exists a unique morphism that lifts the identity morphism of a specific object, satisfying a particular composition condition with another morphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.map.comment:
Given a cartesian arrow `φ : a ⟶ b` lying over `f : R ⟶ S` in `𝒳`, a morphism `φ' : a' ⟶ b`
lifting `𝟙 R`, then `IsCartesian.map f φ φ'` is the morphism `a' ⟶ a` obtained from the universal
property of `φ`.

explanatories.Classical.choose: The operation returns an element that satisfies a given property when it is known that such an element exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.unive: This theorem asserts that for a functor exhibiting a Cartesian property, there exists a unique morphism that lifts the identity morphism of a specific object, satisfying a particular composition condition with another morphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.map.fullDefinition: protected noncomputable def map : a' ⟶ a :=   Classical.choose <| IsCartesian.universal_property (p := p) (f := f) (φ := φ) φ'
CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.map.description: This definition describes a morphism from one object to another derived from a cartesian morphism and its lifting associated with a functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.map_u.comment:
Given a cartesian arrow `φ : a ⟶ b` lying over `f : R ⟶ S` in `𝒳`, a morphism `φ' : a' ⟶ b`
lifting `𝟙 R`, and a morphism `ψ : a' ⟶ a` such that `g ≫ ψ = φ'`. Then `ψ` is the map induced
by the universal property of `φ`.
CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.map_u.description: This theorem establishes that if a morphism satisfies a specific composition condition with a cartesian morphism, then it is equal to the morphism uniquely derived from the universal property associated with that cartesian morphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.eq_of.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.eq_of_fac.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {𝒮 : Type u₁} {𝒳 : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₁} 𝒮]
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} 𝒳] (p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒮) {R S : 𝒮} {a b : 𝒳} (f : R ⟶ S) (φ : a ⟶ b) [p.IsCartesian f φ] {a' : 𝒳}
  (φ' : a' ⟶ b) [p.IsHomLift f φ'] {ψ ψ' : a' ⟶ a} [p.IsHomLift (𝟙 R) ψ] [p.IsHomLift (𝟙 R) ψ'] (hcomp : ψ ≫ φ = φ')
  (hcomp' : ψ' ≫ φ = φ') : ψ = ψ'
CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.eq_of.comment:
Given a cartesian arrow `φ : a ⟶ b` lying over `f : R ⟶ S` in `𝒳`, a morphism `φ' : a' ⟶ b`
lifting `𝟙 R`, and two morphisms `ψ ψ' : a' ⟶ a` such that `g ≫ ψ = φ' = g ≫ ψ'`. Then we must
have `ψ = ψ'`.
CategoryTheory.Functor.IsCartesian.eq_of.description: This theorem states that if two morphisms satisfying certain composition conditions with a cartesian morphism yield the same result, then those two morphisms must be equal.

CategoryTheory.BasedFunctor.preserves_is.fullDefinition: instance preserves_isHomLift [IsHomLift 𝒳.p f φ] : IsHomLift 𝒴.p f (F.map φ) := by   apply of_fac 𝒴.p f (F.map φ) (Eq.trans (F.w_obj a) (domain_eq 𝒳.p f φ))     (Eq.trans (F.w_obj b) (codomain_eq 𝒳.p f φ))   rw [← Functor.comp_map, congr_hom F.w]   simpa using (fac 𝒳.p f φ)
