CategoryTheory.End.of.description: This definition constructs an endomorphism of an object in a category from a given morphism that maps the object to itself.

CategoryTheory.End.asHom.code: CategoryTheory.End.asHom.{v, u} {C : Type u} [CategoryStruct.{v, u} C] {X : C} (f : End X) : X ⟶ X
CategoryTheory.End.asHom.comment:
Assist the typechecker by expressing an endomorphism `f : CategoryTheory.End X` as a term of
`X ⟶ X`.
CategoryTheory.End.asHom.fullDefinition: def asHom (f : End X) : X ⟶ X := f
CategoryTheory.End.asHom.description: This definition provides a means to represent an endomorphism of an object in a category as a morphism that maps the object to itself.

CategoryTheory.End.one_def.code: CategoryTheory.End.one_def.{v, u} {C : Type u} [CategoryStruct.{v, u} C] {X : C} : 1 = 𝟙 X
CategoryTheory.End.one_def.description: This theorem establishes that the multiplicative identity in the context of endomorphisms of an object in a category is equal to the identity morphism of that object.

CategoryTheory.End.mul_def.code: CategoryTheory.End.mul_def.{v, u} {C : Type u} [CategoryStruct.{v, u} C] {X : C} (xs ys : End X) : xs * ys = ys ≫ xs
CategoryTheory.End.mul_def.description: This theorem establishes that the multiplication of two endomorphisms of an object in a category is equivalent to composing the second endomorphism with the first.

CategoryTheory.End.monoid.code: CategoryTheory.End.monoid.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : C} : Monoid (End X)
CategoryTheory.End.monoid.comment: Endomorphisms of an object form a monoid

explanatories.CategoryTheory.End.one: This definition specifies the identity endomorphism of an object in a category, which serves as the multiplicative identity element in the collection of endomorphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.End.mul: This definition establishes a multiplication operation for the endomorphisms of an object in a category, aligning with function composition rather than the composition typically used in category theory.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.End.monoid.fullDefinition: instance monoid {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {X : C} : Monoid (End X) where   mul_one := Category.id_comp   one_mul := Category.comp_id   mul_assoc := fun x y z => (Category.assoc z y x).symm
CategoryTheory.End.monoid.description: This definition establishes that the collection of endomorphisms of an object in a category forms a monoid under composition.

CategoryTheory.End.mulActionRight.code: CategoryTheory.End.mulActionRight.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} : MulAction (End Y) (X ⟶ Y)

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.End.mulActionRight.fullDefinition: instance mulActionRight {X Y : C} : MulAction (End Y) (X ⟶ Y) where   smul r f := f ≫ r   one_smul := Category.comp_id   mul_smul _ _ _ := Eq.symm <| Category.assoc _ _ _
CategoryTheory.End.mulActionRight.description: This definition indicates that the endomorphisms of an object in a category can act as a multiplicative action on the morphisms from another object to that object.

CategoryTheory.End.mulActionLeft.code:
CategoryTheory.End.mulActionLeft.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : Cᵒᵖ} {Y : C} :
  MulAction (End X) (unop X ⟶ Y)
CategoryTheory.End.mulActionLeft.fullDefinition: instance mulActionLeft {X : Cᵒᵖ} {Y : C} : MulAction (End X) (unop X ⟶ Y) where   smul r f := r.unop ≫ f   one_smul := Category.id_comp   mul_smul _ _ _ := Category.assoc _ _ _
CategoryTheory.End.mulActionLeft.description: This definition establishes a multiplicative action of endomorphisms on morphisms from the underlying object to another object in a category, enabling the interaction of endomorphisms with such morphisms.

CategoryTheory.End.smul_right.code: CategoryTheory.End.smul_right.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} {r : End Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} : r • f = f ≫ r
CategoryTheory.End.smul_right.description: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of a morphism by an endomorphism is equivalent to composing the morphism with the endomorphism.

CategoryTheory.End.smul_left.code:
CategoryTheory.End.smul_left.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : Cᵒᵖ} {Y : C} {r : End X} {f : unop X ⟶ Y} :
  r • f = Quiver.Hom.unop r ≫ f
CategoryTheory.End.smul_left.description: This theorem establishes that the action of an endomorphism on a morphism can be expressed as the composition of the unopposed endomorphism with the morphism.

CategoryTheory.End.group.code: CategoryTheory.End.group.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Groupoid C] (X : C) : Group (End X)
CategoryTheory.End.group.comment: In a groupoid, endomorphisms form a group
CategoryTheory.End.group.fullDefinition: instance group {C : Type u} [Groupoid.{v} C] (X : C) : Group (End X) where   mul_left_inv := Groupoid.comp_inv   inv := Groupoid.inv
CategoryTheory.End.group.description: This definition specifies that in a groupoid, the collection of endomorphisms of an object forms a group.

CategoryTheory.isUnit_iff_isIso.code: CategoryTheory.isUnit_iff_isIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : C} (f : End X) : IsUnit f ↔ IsIso f

explanatories.CategoryTheory.End: This definition describes the collection of endomorphisms of an object in a category, where the order of multiplication corresponds to function composition rather than the composition defined in category theory.

CategoryTheory.isUnit_iff_isIso.description: This theorem states that an endomorphism of an object in a category is a unit if and only if it is an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Aut.code: CategoryTheory.Aut.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) : Type v
CategoryTheory.Aut.comment:
Automorphisms of an object in a category.

The order of arguments in multiplication agrees with
`Function.comp`, not with `CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp`.
CategoryTheory.Aut.fullDefinition: def Aut (X : C) := X ≅ X set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Aut.description: This definition introduces the concept of automorphisms for an object in a category, representing the structure of morphisms that map the object to itself.

CategoryTheory.Aut.inhabited.code: CategoryTheory.Aut.inhabited.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) : Inhabited (Aut X)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.End.inhabited: This definition asserts that there exists at least one endomorphism of an object in a category, indicating that the collection of endomorphisms is non-empty.

CategoryTheory.Aut.inhabited.fullDefinition: protected instance inhabited : Inhabited (Aut X) := ⟨Iso.refl X⟩ set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Aut.inhabited.description: This definition states that there exists at least one automorphism of an object in a category, indicating that the collection of automorphisms is non-empty.

CategoryTheory.Aut.Aut_mul_def.code: CategoryTheory.Aut.Aut_mul_def.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) (f g : Aut X) : f * g = g ≪≫ f
CategoryTheory.Aut.Aut_mul_def.description: This theorem states that the product of two automorphisms of an object in a category is equivalent to their composition when applied in reverse order.

CategoryTheory.Aut.Aut_inv_def.code: CategoryTheory.Aut.Aut_inv_def.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) (f : Aut X) : f⁻¹ = Iso.symm f

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.Aut.Aut_inv_def.description: This theorem states that the inverse of an automorphism of an object in a category is equal to the symmetry of the isomorphism that represents that automorphism.

CategoryTheory.Aut.unitsEndEquivAut.code: CategoryTheory.Aut.unitsEndEquivAut.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) : (End X)ˣ ≃* Aut X
CategoryTheory.Aut.unitsEndEquivAut.comment:
Units in the monoid of endomorphisms of an object
are (multiplicatively) equivalent to automorphisms of that object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.End: This definition describes the collection of endomorphisms of an object in a category, where the order of multiplication corresponds to function composition rather than the composition defined in category theory.
explanatories.rfl: The reflexivity of equality asserts that any element is equal to itself.

CategoryTheory.Aut.unitsEndEquivAut.fullDefinition: def unitsEndEquivAut : (End X)ˣ ≃* Aut X where   toFun f := ⟨f.1, f.2, f.4, f.3⟩   invFun f := ⟨f.1, f.2, f.4, f.3⟩   left_inv := fun ⟨f₁, f₂, f₃, f₄⟩ => rfl   right_inv := fun ⟨f₁, f₂, f₃, f₄⟩ => rfl   map_mul' f g := by cases f; cases g; rfl set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Aut.unitsEndEquivAut.description: This definition indicates that the units in the monoid of endomorphisms of an object are multiplicatively equivalent to the automorphisms of that object.

CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso.code: CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (h : X ≅ Y) : Aut X ≃* Aut Y
CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso.comment: Isomorphisms induce isomorphisms of the automorphism group

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Aut.Aut_mul_def: This theorem states that the product of two automorphisms of an object in a category is equivalent to their composition when applied in reverse order.

CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso.fullDefinition: def autMulEquivOfIso {X Y : C} (h : X ≅ Y) : Aut X ≃* Aut Y where   toFun x := ⟨h.inv ≫ x.hom ≫ h.hom, h.inv ≫ x.inv ≫ h.hom, _, _⟩   invFun y := ⟨h.hom ≫ y.hom ≫ h.inv, h.hom ≫ y.inv ≫ h.inv, _, _⟩   left_inv _ := by aesop_cat   right_inv _ := by aesop_cat   map_mul' := by simp [Aut_mul_def] set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Aut.autMulEquivOfIso.description: This definition establishes that an isomorphism between two objects in a category induces a corresponding isomorphism between their automorphism groups.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapEnd.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapEnd.{v, v', u, u'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) {D : Type u'}
  [Category.{v', u'} D] (f : C ⥤ D) : End X →* End (f.obj X)
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapEnd.comment: `f.map` as a monoid hom between endomorphism monoids.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.End: This definition describes the collection of endomorphisms of an object in a category, where the order of multiplication corresponds to function composition rather than the composition defined in category theory.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapEnd.fullDefinition: def mapEnd : End X →* End (f.obj X) where   toFun := f.map   map_mul' x y := f.map_comp y x   map_one' := f.map_id X
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapEnd.description: This definition describes a mapping from the endomorphism monoid of an object in one category to the endomorphism monoid of its image in another category, using a functor as a structure-preserving transformation.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut.{v, v', u, u'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (X : C) {D : Type u'}
  [Category.{v', u'} D] (f : C ⥤ D) : Aut X →* Aut (f.obj X)
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut.comment: `f.mapIso` as a group hom between automorphism groups.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Aut: This definition introduces the concept of automorphisms for an object in a category, representing the structure of morphisms that map the object to itself.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut.fullDefinition: def mapAut : Aut X →* Aut (f.obj X) where   toFun := f.mapIso   map_mul' x y := f.mapIso_trans y x   map_one' := f.mapIso_refl X set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapAut.description: This definition describes a mapping from the group of automorphisms of an object in one category to the group of automorphisms of its image under a functor, treating this mapping as a group homomorphism.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.sq_has.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.sq_hasLift.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C} {i : A ⟶ B}
  {p : X ⟶ Y} [self : HasLiftingProperty i p] {f : A ⟶ X} {g : B ⟶ Y} (sq : CommSq f i p g) : sq.HasLift
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.sq_has.comment: Unique field expressing that any commutative square built from `f` and `g` has a lift
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.sq_has.description: This theorem asserts that any commutative square formed by specified morphisms in a category possesses a lifting property, allowing for a corresponding lift to be constructed.

CategoryTheory.sq_hasLift_of_hasLiftingP.code:
CategoryTheory.sq_hasLift_of_hasLiftingProperty.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C}
  (i : A ⟶ B) (p : X ⟶ Y) {f : A ⟶ X} {g : B ⟶ Y} (sq : CommSq f i p g) [hip : HasLiftingProperty i p] : sq.HasLift

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.sq_has: This theorem asserts that any commutative square formed by specified morphisms in a category possesses a lifting property, allowing for a corresponding lift to be constructed.

CategoryTheory.sq_hasLift_of_hasLiftingP.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) sq_hasLift_of_hasLiftingProperty {f : A ⟶ X} {g : B ⟶ Y}     (sq : CommSq f i p g) [hip : HasLiftingProperty i p] : sq.HasLift := by apply hip.sq_hasLift
CategoryTheory.sq_hasLift_of_hasLiftingP.description: This definition states that if a given commutative square involves specific morphisms and a lifting property exists for them, then the commutative square can be lifted.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C} {i : A ⟶ B}
  {p : X ⟶ Y} (sq_hasLift : ∀ {f : A ⟶ X} {g : B ⟶ Y} (sq : CommSq f i p g), sq.HasLift) : HasLiftingProperty i p

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.sq_has: This theorem asserts that any commutative square formed by specified morphisms in a category possesses a lifting property, allowing for a corresponding lift to be constructed.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk.description: This theorem establishes that if every commutative square formed by certain morphisms has a lifting property, then a lifting property can be defined for the morphisms themselves.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.op.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.op.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C} {i : A ⟶ B}
  {p : X ⟶ Y} (h : HasLiftingProperty i p) : HasLiftingProperty p.op i.op
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.op.description: This theorem states that if a lifting property exists for a pair of morphisms, then it also holds for their respective dual morphisms in the opposite category.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.unop.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.unop.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : Cᵒᵖ} {i : A ⟶ B}
  {p : X ⟶ Y} (h : HasLiftingProperty i p) : HasLiftingProperty p.unop i.unop
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.unop.description: This theorem states that if a lifting property exists for a pair of morphisms in a category, then it also holds for their respective dual morphisms in the opposite category.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_op.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_op.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C} {i : A ⟶ B}
  {p : X ⟶ Y} : HasLiftingProperty i p ↔ HasLiftingProperty p.op i.op

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.op: This theorem states that if a lifting property exists for a pair of morphisms, then it also holds for their respective dual morphisms in the opposite category.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_op.description: This theorem asserts that the existence of a lifting property for a pair of morphisms is equivalent to the existence of a lifting property for their respective dual morphisms in the opposite category.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_un.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_unop.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (i : A ⟶ B)
  (p : X ⟶ Y) : HasLiftingProperty i p ↔ HasLiftingProperty p.unop i.unop

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.unop: This theorem states that if a lifting property exists for a pair of morphisms in a category, then it also holds for their respective dual morphisms in the opposite category.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_un.description: This theorem states that a lifting property for a pair of morphisms in the opposite category is equivalent to the lifting property for their respective dual morphisms.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_lef.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_left_iso.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C}
  (i : A ⟶ B) (p : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso i] : HasLiftingProperty i p
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_lef.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) of_left_iso [IsIso i] : HasLiftingProperty i p :=   ⟨fun {f} {g} sq =>     CommSq.HasLift.mk'       { l := inv i ≫ f         fac_left := by simp only [IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc]         fac_right := by simp only [sq.w, assoc, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc] }⟩
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_lef.description: This definition establishes that when a morphism is an isomorphism, it guarantees the existence of a lifting property for that morphism with respect to another specified morphism.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_rig.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_right_iso.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {A B X Y : C}
  (i : A ⟶ B) (p : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso p] : HasLiftingProperty i p
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_rig.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) of_right_iso [IsIso p] : HasLiftingProperty i p :=   ⟨fun {f} {g} sq =>     CommSq.HasLift.mk'       { l := g ≫ inv p         fac_left := by simp only [← sq.w_assoc, IsIso.hom_inv_id, comp_id]         fac_right := by simp only [assoc, IsIso.inv_hom_id, comp_id] }⟩
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_rig.description: This definition asserts that if a morphism is an isomorphism, it guarantees the existence of a lifting property for that morphism when paired with another specified morphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk: This theorem establishes that if every commutative square formed by certain morphisms has a lifting property, then a lifting property can be defined for the morphisms themselves.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_com.fullDefinition: instance of_comp_left [HasLiftingProperty i p] [HasLiftingProperty i' p] :     HasLiftingProperty (i ≫ i') p :=   ⟨fun {f} {g} sq => by     have fac := sq.w     rw [assoc] at fac     exact       CommSq.HasLift.mk'         { l := (CommSq.mk (CommSq.mk fac).fac_right).lift           fac_left := by simp only [assoc, CommSq.fac_left]           fac_right := by simp only [CommSq.fac_right] }⟩
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_com.description: This definition states that if two morphisms each possess a lifting property with respect to a specific morphism, then the composition of those two morphisms also has a lifting property with respect to that morphism.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk: This theorem establishes that if every commutative square formed by certain morphisms has a lifting property, then a lifting property can be defined for the morphisms themselves.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_com.fullDefinition: instance of_comp_right [HasLiftingProperty i p] [HasLiftingProperty i p'] :     HasLiftingProperty i (p ≫ p') :=   ⟨fun {f} {g} sq => by     have fac := sq.w     rw [← assoc] at fac     let _ := (CommSq.mk (CommSq.mk fac).fac_left.symm).lift     exact       CommSq.HasLift.mk'         { l := (CommSq.mk (CommSq.mk fac).fac_left.symm).lift           fac_left := by simp only [CommSq.fac_left]           fac_right := by simp only [CommSq.fac_right_assoc, CommSq.fac_right] }⟩
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_com.description: This definition establishes that if a lifting property exists for two morphisms in a category, then it also holds for their composition with a third morphism.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_arr.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_arrow_iso_left.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B A' B' X Y : C} {i : A ⟶ B} {i' : A' ⟶ B'} (e : Arrow.mk i ≅ Arrow.mk i') (p : X ⟶ Y)
  [hip : HasLiftingProperty i p] : HasLiftingProperty i' p

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk: This theorem establishes that if every commutative square formed by certain morphisms has a lifting property, then a lifting property can be defined for the morphisms themselves.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_arr.description: This theorem states that if a morphism has a lifting property and there is an isomorphism between arrows corresponding to two morphisms, then the second morphism also possesses a lifting property with respect to the same specified morphism.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_arr.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_arrow_iso_right.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B X Y X' Y' : C} (i : A ⟶ B) {p : X ⟶ Y} {p' : X' ⟶ Y'} (e : Arrow.mk p ≅ Arrow.mk p')
  [hip : HasLiftingProperty i p] : HasLiftingProperty i p'

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk: This theorem establishes that if every commutative square formed by certain morphisms has a lifting property, then a lifting property can be defined for the morphisms themselves.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.of_arr.description: This theorem states that if there is an isomorphism between two arrows corresponding to morphisms in a category, then the lifting property that holds for one morphism also holds for the other.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_of.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_of_arrow_iso_left.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B A' B' X Y : C} {i : A ⟶ B} {i' : A' ⟶ B'} (e : Arrow.mk i ≅ Arrow.mk i') (p : X ⟶ Y) :
  HasLiftingProperty i p ↔ HasLiftingProperty i' p

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk: This theorem establishes that if every commutative square formed by certain morphisms has a lifting property, then a lifting property can be defined for the morphisms themselves.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_of.description: This theorem states that the lifting property for one morphism is equivalent to the lifting property for another morphism if there exists an isomorphism between their corresponding arrows.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_of.code:
CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_of_arrow_iso_right.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C]
  {A B X Y X' Y' : C} (i : A ⟶ B) {p : X ⟶ Y} {p' : X' ⟶ Y'} (e : Arrow.mk p ≅ Arrow.mk p') :
  HasLiftingProperty i p ↔ HasLiftingProperty i p'

explanatories.CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.mk: This theorem establishes that if every commutative square formed by certain morphisms has a lifting property, then a lifting property can be defined for the morphisms themselves.

CategoryTheory.HasLiftingProperty.iff_of.description: This theorem states that if two arrows in a category are isomorphic, then the existence of a lifting property for one arrow with respect to a morphism is equivalent to the existence of a lifting property for the other arrow with respect to the same morphism.

CategoryTheory.CommSq.right_adjoint.code:
CategoryTheory.CommSq.right_adjoint.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_3, u_1} C]
  [Category.{u_4, u_2} D] {G : C ⥤ D} {F : D ⥤ C} {A B : C} {X Y : D} {i : A ⟶ B} {p : X ⟶ Y} {u : G.obj A ⟶ X}
  {v : G.obj B ⟶ Y} (sq : CommSq u (G.map i) p v) (adj : G ⊣ F) :
  CommSq ((adj.homEquiv A X) u) i (F.map p) ((adj.homEquiv B Y) v)
CategoryTheory.CommSq.right_adjoint.comment:
When we have an adjunction `G ⊣ F`, any commutative square where the left
map is of the form `G.map i` and the right map is `p` has an "adjoint" commutative
square whose left map is `i` and whose right map is `F.map p`.
CategoryTheory.CommSq.right_adjoint.description: This theorem establishes that for an adjunction between two functors, any commutative square involving specific morphisms can be transformed into an equivalent commutative square with adjusted mappings.

CategoryTheory.CommSq.rightAdjointLiftSt.comment:
The liftings of a commutative are in bijection with the liftings of its (right)
adjoint square.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.right_adjoint: This theorem establishes that for an adjunction between two functors, any commutative square involving specific morphisms can be transformed into an equivalent commutative square with adjusted mappings.

CategoryTheory.CommSq.rightAdjointLiftSt.fullDefinition: def rightAdjointLiftStructEquiv : sq.LiftStruct ≃ (sq.right_adjoint adj).LiftStruct where   toFun l :=     { l := adj.homEquiv _ _ l.l       fac_left := by rw [← adj.homEquiv_naturality_left, l.fac_left]       fac_right := by rw [← Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right, l.fac_right] }   invFun l :=     { l := (adj.homEquiv _ _).symm l.l       fac_left := by         rw [← Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left_symm, l.fac_left]         apply (adj.homEquiv _ _).left_inv       fac_right := by         rw [← Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_right_symm, l.fac_right]         apply (adj.homEquiv _ _).left_inv }   left_inv := by aesop_cat   right_inv := by aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.CommSq.left_adjoint.code:

  [Category.{u_3, u_2} D] {G : C ⥤ D} {F : D ⥤ C} {A B : C} {X Y : D} {i : A ⟶ B} {p : X ⟶ Y} {u : A ⟶ F.obj X}
  {v : B ⟶ F.obj Y} (sq : CommSq u i (F.map p) v) (adj : G ⊣ F) :
  CommSq ((adj.homEquiv A X).symm u) (G.map i) p ((adj.homEquiv B Y).symm v)

When we have an adjunction `G ⊣ F`, any commutative square where the left
map is of the form `i` and the right map is `F.map p` has an "adjoint" commutative
square whose left map is `G.map i` and whose right map is `p`.

CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y X₁ Y₁ : C} (α : X ≅ X₁) (β : Y ≅ Y₁) :
  (X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X₁ ⟶ Y₁)
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr.comment:
If `X` is isomorphic to `X₁` and `Y` is isomorphic to `Y₁`, then
there is a natural bijection between `X ⟶ Y` and `X₁ ⟶ Y₁`. See also `Equiv.arrowCongr`.
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr.fullDefinition: def homCongr {X Y X₁ Y₁ : C} (α : X ≅ X₁) (β : Y ≅ Y₁) : (X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X₁ ⟶ Y₁) where   toFun f := α.inv ≫ f ≫ β.hom   invFun f := α.hom ≫ f ≫ β.inv   left_inv f :=     show α.hom ≫ (α.inv ≫ f ≫ β.hom) ≫ β.inv = f by       rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, β.hom_inv_id, α.hom_inv_id_assoc, Category.comp_id]   right_inv f :=     show α.inv ≫ (α.hom ≫ f ≫ β.inv) ≫ β.hom = f by       rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, β.inv_hom_id, α.inv_hom_id_assoc, Category.comp_id]
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr.description: This definition introduces a natural bijection between the morphisms from one object to another in a category when both objects are isomorphic to corresponding objects in another category.

CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_apply.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_apply.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y X₁ Y₁ : C} (α : X ≅ X₁) (β : Y ≅ Y₁)
  (f : X ⟶ Y) : (α.homCongr β) f = α.inv ≫ f ≫ β.hom
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_apply.description: This theorem shows that applying the bijection introduced by the isomorphisms between two objects to a morphism between them results in a specific composition of morphisms involving the inverses and original maps of those isomorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y Z X₁ Y₁ Z₁ : C} (α : X ≅ X₁) (β : Y ≅ Y₁)
  (γ : Z ≅ Z₁) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : (α.homCongr γ) (f ≫ g) = (α.homCongr β) f ≫ (β.homCongr γ) g
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_comp.description: This theorem demonstrates that the bijection between morphisms induced by isomorphisms preserves the composition of morphisms in a category.

CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_refl.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_refl.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  ((refl X).homCongr (refl Y)) f = f
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_refl.description: This theorem states that the bijection induced by the identity isomorphisms between two objects in a category preserves any morphism between those objects.

CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_trans.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_trans.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂ X₃ Y₃ : C} (α₁ : X₁ ≅ X₂)
  (β₁ : Y₁ ≅ Y₂) (α₂ : X₂ ≅ X₃) (β₂ : Y₂ ≅ Y₃) (f : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) :
  ((α₁ ≪≫ α₂).homCongr (β₁ ≪≫ β₂)) f = ((α₁.homCongr β₁).trans (α₂.homCongr β₂)) f
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_trans.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of bijections induced by consecutive isomorphisms between objects in a category can be expressed in terms of the individual bijections applied to morphisms between those objects.

CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_symm.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_symm.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂ : C} (α : X₁ ≅ X₂) (β : Y₁ ≅ Y₂) :
  (α.homCongr β).symm = α.symm.homCongr β.symm
CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr_symm.description: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the bijection between morphisms induced by an isomorphism can be expressed as the bijection induced by the inverses of the original isomorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Iso.isoCongr.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.isoCongr.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂ : C} (f : X₁ ≅ X₂) (g : Y₁ ≅ Y₂) :
  (X₁ ≅ Y₁) ≃ (X₂ ≅ Y₂)
CategoryTheory.Iso.isoCongr.comment:
If `X` is isomorphic to `X₁` and `Y` is isomorphic to `Y₁`, then
there is a bijection between `X ≅ Y` and `X₁ ≅ Y₁`.
CategoryTheory.Iso.isoCongr.fullDefinition: def isoCongr {X₁ Y₁ X₂ Y₂ : C} (f : X₁ ≅ X₂) (g : Y₁ ≅ Y₂) : (X₁ ≅ Y₁) ≃ (X₂ ≅ Y₂) where   toFun h := f.symm.trans <| h.trans <| g   invFun h := f.trans <| h.trans <| g.symm   left_inv := by aesop_cat   right_inv := by aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Iso.isoCongr.description: This definition establishes a bijection between the isomorphisms of two pairs of objects in a category, given that each object in the first pair is isomorphic to a corresponding object in the second pair.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conj.code: CategoryTheory.Iso.conj.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) : End X ≃* End Y
CategoryTheory.Iso.conj.comment:
An isomorphism between two objects defines a monoid isomorphism between their
monoid of endomorphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr: This definition introduces a natural bijection between the morphisms from one object to another in a category when both objects are isomorphic to corresponding objects in another category.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conj.fullDefinition: def conj : End X ≃* End Y :=   { homCongr α α with map_mul' := fun f g => homCongr_comp α α α g f }
CategoryTheory.Iso.conj.description: This definition establishes a monoid isomorphism between the endomorphism monoids of two objects in a category when there is an isomorphism between the objects themselves.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_apply.code:

CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_apply.description: This theorem expresses that the action of an isomorphism on an endomorphism of an object can be described as a specific composition involving the inverse and original maps of the isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f g : End X) :

CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_comp.description: This theorem states that the conjugation operation associated with an isomorphism between two objects in a category distributes over the composition of endomorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Iso.trans_conj.code:

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.conj: This definition establishes a monoid isomorphism between the endomorphism monoids of two objects in a category when there is an isomorphism between the objects themselves.

CategoryTheory.Iso.trans_conj.description: This theorem states that conjugating an endomorphism of one object by the composition of two isomorphisms is equivalent to first conjugating it by the first isomorphism and then by the second isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Iso.symm_self_conj.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.symm_self_conj.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : End X) :
  α.symm.conj (α.conj f) = f

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.conj: This definition establishes a monoid isomorphism between the endomorphism monoids of two objects in a category when there is an isomorphism between the objects themselves.

CategoryTheory.Iso.symm_self_conj.description: This theorem asserts that conjugating an endomorphism of one object by an isomorphism and then by its inverse yields the original endomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Iso.self_symm_conj.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.self_symm_conj.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : End Y) :
  α.conj (α.symm.conj f) = f

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.conj: This definition establishes a monoid isomorphism between the endomorphism monoids of two objects in a category when there is an isomorphism between the objects themselves.

CategoryTheory.Iso.self_symm_conj.description: This theorem states that conjugating a morphism by an isomorphism and then by its inverse results in the original morphism.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_pow.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_pow.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : End X) (n : ℕ) :
  α.conj (f ^ n) = α.conj f ^ n
CategoryTheory.Iso.conj_pow.description: This theorem states that under an isomorphism between two objects in a category, the action of raising an endomorphism to a power is compatible with the bijection provided by the isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut.code: CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) : Aut X ≃* Aut Y
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut.comment: `conj` defines a group isomorphisms between groups of automorphisms
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut.fullDefinition: def conjAut : Aut X ≃* Aut Y :=   (Aut.unitsEndEquivAut X).symm.trans <| (Units.mapEquiv α.conj).trans <| Aut.unitsEndEquivAut Y set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut.description: This definition establishes a group isomorphism between the automorphisms of one object and the automorphisms of another object that is isomorphic to the first.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_apply.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_apply.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : Aut X) :
  α.conjAut f = α.symm ≪≫ f ≪≫ α
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_apply.description: This theorem demonstrates that the conjugation of an automorphism of one object by an isomorphism to another object results in a specific composition of the inverse of the isomorphism, the automorphism, and the isomorphism itself.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_hom.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_hom.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : Aut X) :
  (α.conjAut f).hom = α.conj f.hom
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_hom.description: This theorem establishes that the homomorphism of an automorphism conjugated by an isomorphism between two objects in a category is equal to the conjugation of the homomorphism of the automorphism itself.

CategoryTheory.Iso.trans_conjAut.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.trans_conjAut.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) {Z : C} (β : Y ≅ Z)
  (f : Aut X) : (α ≪≫ β).conjAut f = β.conjAut (α.conjAut f)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut: This definition establishes a group isomorphism between the automorphisms of one object and the automorphisms of another object that is isomorphic to the first.

CategoryTheory.Iso.trans_conjAut.description: This theorem shows how the conjugation operation associated with the composition of isomorphisms between objects in a category is related to the conjugation of automorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_mul.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_mul.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f g : Aut X) :
  α.conjAut (f * g) = α.conjAut f * α.conjAut g
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_mul.description: This theorem shows that conjugating the product of two automorphisms by an isomorphism between two objects in a category results in the same product of the conjugated automorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_trans.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_trans.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f g : Aut X) :
  α.conjAut (f ≪≫ g) = α.conjAut f ≪≫ α.conjAut g
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_trans.description: This theorem states that conjugating the composition of two automorphisms by an isomorphism between two objects in a category results in the same composition of the conjugated automorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_pow.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_pow.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : Aut X) (n : ℕ) :
  α.conjAut (f ^ n) = α.conjAut f ^ n
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_pow.description: This theorem states that the conjugation operation associated with an isomorphism preserves the power of an automorphism by conjugating the base automorphism and raising it to the same exponent.

CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_zpow.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_zpow.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : Aut X) (n : ℤ) :
  α.conjAut (f ^ n) = α.conjAut f ^ n
CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut_zpow.description: This theorem establishes that conjugating a power of an automorphism by an isomorphism between two objects in a category is equivalent to conjugating the automorphism and then taking the same power of the result.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_homCongr.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.map_homCongr.{v, u, v₁, u₁} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y X₁ Y₁ : C} (α : X ≅ X₁) (β : Y ≅ Y₁) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  F.map ((α.homCongr β) f) = ((F.mapIso α).homCongr (F.mapIso β)) (F.map f)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.homCongr: This definition introduces a natural bijection between the morphisms from one object to another in a category when both objects are isomorphic to corresponding objects in another category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_homCongr.description: This theorem states that the image of a morphism under a functor, when conjugated by isomorphisms of the source and target objects, is equal to the image under the functor of the morphism conjugated by the isomorphisms of the objects.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_conj.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.map_conj.{v, u, v₁, u₁} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : End X) : F.map (α.conj f) = (F.mapIso α).conj (F.map f)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.conj: This definition establishes a monoid isomorphism between the endomorphism monoids of two objects in a category when there is an isomorphism between the objects themselves.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_conj.description: This theorem asserts that the functorial image of a conjugated endomorphism under a functor can be represented as the conjugation of the functorial image of the endomorphism by the functorial image of the isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_conjAut.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.map_conjAut.{v, u, v₁, u₁} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} D]
  (F : C ⥤ D) {X Y : C} (α : X ≅ Y) (f : Aut X) : F.mapIso (α.conjAut f) = (F.mapIso α).conjAut (F.mapIso f)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.conjAut: This definition establishes a group isomorphism between the automorphisms of one object and the automorphisms of another object that is isomorphic to the first.

CategoryTheory.Functor.map_conjAut.description: This theorem states that applying a functor to the automorphism of an object that is conjugated by an isomorphism results in the automorphism obtained by first applying the functor to the isomorphism and then to the automorphism.

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.

CategoryTheory.types.fullDefinition: instance types : LargeCategory (Type u) where   Hom a b := a → b   id a := id   comp f g := g ∘ f
CategoryTheory.types.description: This definition specifies that the category of types is a large category in the context of category theory.

CategoryTheory.types_hom.code: CategoryTheory.types_hom.{u} {α β : Type u} : (α ⟶ β) = (α → β)
CategoryTheory.types_hom.description: This theorem states that morphisms in the category of types correspond exactly to functions between those types.

CategoryTheory.types_id.description: This theorem asserts that the identity morphism in the category of types is equivalent to the identity function.

CategoryTheory.types_comp.code: CategoryTheory.types_comp.{u} {X Y Z : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : f ≫ g = g ∘ f
CategoryTheory.types_comp.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of morphisms in the category of types corresponds to the composition of the corresponding functions.

CategoryTheory.types_id_apply.code: CategoryTheory.types_id_apply.{u} (X : Type u) (x : X) : 𝟙 X x = x
CategoryTheory.types_id_apply.description: This theorem asserts that applying the identity morphism to an element of a type yields the element itself.

CategoryTheory.types_comp_apply.code: CategoryTheory.types_comp_apply.{u} {X Y Z : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : X) : (f ≫ g) x = g (f x)
CategoryTheory.types_comp_apply.description: This theorem asserts that the composition of two morphisms applied to an element results in the same outcome as applying the second morphism to the result of the first morphism applied to that element.

CategoryTheory.hom_inv_id_apply.code: CategoryTheory.hom_inv_id_apply.{u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ≅ Y) (x : X) : f.inv (f.hom x) = x
CategoryTheory.hom_inv_id_apply.description: This theorem establishes that applying the inverse of an isomorphism to the image of an element under the isomorphism yields the original element.

CategoryTheory.inv_hom_id_apply.code: CategoryTheory.inv_hom_id_apply.{u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ≅ Y) (y : Y) : f.hom (f.inv y) = y
CategoryTheory.inv_hom_id_apply.description: This theorem states that applying the morphism corresponding to an isomorphism to the image of an element under its inverse returns the original element.

CategoryTheory.asHom.code: CategoryTheory.asHom.{u} {α β : Type u} (f : α → β) : α ⟶ β
CategoryTheory.asHom.comment: `asHom f` helps Lean type check a function as a morphism in the category `Type`.
CategoryTheory.asHom.fullDefinition: abbrev asHom {α β : Type u} (f : α → β) : α ⟶ β :=   f
CategoryTheory.asHom.description: This definition allows a function to be treated as a morphism in the category of types for type-checking purposes in Lean.

CategoryTheory.«term↾_».fullDefinition: /- Copyright (c) 2017 Scott Morrison. All rights reserved. Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE. Authors: Stephen Morgan, Scott Morrison, Johannes Hölzl -/ import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.EpiMono import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful import Mathlib.Tactic.PPWithUniv import Mathlib.Data.Set.Defs
CategoryTheory.«term↾_».description: This definition introduces a parser description term for a specific parsing operation in Lean.

CategoryTheory.Functor.sections.code: CategoryTheory.Functor.sections.{v, w, u} {J : Type u} [Category.{v, u} J] (F : J ⥤ Type w) : Set ((j : J) → F.obj j)
CategoryTheory.Functor.sections.comment:
The sections of a functor `F : J ⥤ Type` are
the choices of a point `u j : F.obj j` for each `j`,
such that `F.map f (u j) = u j'` for every morphism `f : j ⟶ j'`.

We later use these to define limits in `Type` and in many concrete categories.

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.Functor.sections.fullDefinition: def sections (F : J ⥤ Type w) : Set (∀ j, F.obj j) :=   { u | ∀ {j j'} (f : j ⟶ j'), F.map f (u j) = u j' }
CategoryTheory.Functor.sections.description: This definition characterizes the sections of a functor as selections of points from the functor's objects that are consistent with the functor's mapping on morphisms.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_comp_a.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_comp_apply.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F : C ⥤ Type w) {X Y Z : C}
  (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (a : F.obj X) : F.map (f ≫ g) a = F.map g (F.map f a)

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_comp_a.description: This theorem establishes that the application of a functor's mapping to the composition of two morphisms is equivalent to the successive application of the functor's mappings to each morphism individually.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_id_app.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_id_apply.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F : C ⥤ Type w) {X : C}
  (a : F.obj X) : F.map (𝟙 X) a = a

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_id_app.description: This theorem demonstrates that the mapping of an object under a functor with the identity morphism of its category results in the object remaining unchanged.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.naturality.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.naturality.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F G : C ⥤ Type w) {X Y : C}
  (σ : F ⟶ G) (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : F.obj X) : σ.app Y (F.map f x) = G.map f (σ.app X x)

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.naturality.description: This theorem demonstrates that the natural transformation between two functors commutes with morphisms, preserving the structure when mapping through each functor.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.comp.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.comp.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F G H : C ⥤ Type w) {X : C} (σ : F ⟶ G)
  (τ : G ⟶ H) (x : F.obj X) : (σ ≫ τ).app X x = τ.app X (σ.app X x)
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.comp.description: This theorem demonstrates the commutativity of the application of two successive functor morphisms in the context of category theory.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.hcomp.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.hcomp.{v, w, u, u'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F G : C ⥤ Type w) (σ : F ⟶ G)
  {D : Type u'} [𝒟 : Category.{u', u'} D] (I J : D ⥤ C) (ρ : I ⟶ J) {W : D} (x : (I ⋙ F).obj W) :
  (ρ ◫ σ).app W x = G.map (ρ.app W) (σ.app (I.obj W) x)

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.hcomp.description: This theorem describes how the application of the composition of a functor morphism with another morphism between categories corresponds to the application of their respective mappings in the context of functors.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_inv_ma.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_inv_map_hom_apply.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F : C ⥤ Type w)
  {X Y : C} (f : X ≅ Y) (x : F.obj X) : F.map f.inv (F.map f.hom x) = x

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_inv_ma.description: This theorem establishes that mapping an object through the functor with the image obtained from the morphism of an isomorphism and then applying the inverse morphism retrieves the original object.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_hom_ma.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_hom_map_inv_apply.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F : C ⥤ Type w)
  {X Y : C} (f : X ≅ Y) (y : F.obj Y) : F.map f.hom (F.map f.inv y) = y

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.map_hom_ma.description: This theorem establishes that mapping an object through the functor with the image obtained from the inverse morphism of an isomorphism and then applying the corresponding morphism retrieves the original object.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.hom_inv_id.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.hom_inv_id_app_apply.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F G : C ⥤ Type w)
  (α : F ≅ G) (X : C) (x : F.obj X) : α.inv.app X (α.hom.app X x) = x
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.hom_inv_id.description: This theorem asserts that applying the inverse of a natural isomorphism between two functors to the image of an object under the isomorphism yields the original object.

CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.inv_hom_id.code:
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.inv_hom_id_app_apply.{v, w, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (F G : C ⥤ Type w)
  (α : F ≅ G) (X : C) (x : G.obj X) : α.hom.app X (α.inv.app X x) = x
CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.inv_hom_id.description: This theorem states that applying the morphism of an isomorphism in the context of functors to the result of applying its inverse to an element yields the original element.

CategoryTheory.uliftTrivial.code: CategoryTheory.uliftTrivial.{u} (V : Type u) : ULift.{u, u} V ≅ V
CategoryTheory.uliftTrivial.comment:
The isomorphism between a `Type` which has been `ULift`ed to the same universe,
and the original type.

explanatories.ULift.up: This theorem describes a method to elevate a value into a specific type structure.

CategoryTheory.uliftTrivial.fullDefinition: def uliftTrivial (V : Type u) : ULift.{u} V ≅ V where   hom a := a.1   inv a := .up a
CategoryTheory.uliftTrivial.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a type that has been lifted to a higher universe and the original type.

CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor.code: CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor.{v, u} : Type u ⥤ Type (max u v)
CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor.comment:
The functor embedding `Type u` into `Type (max u v)`.
Write this as `uliftFunctor.{5, 2}` to get `Type 2 ⥤ Type 5`.

explanatories.ULift.up: This theorem describes a method to elevate a value into a specific type structure.
explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor.fullDefinition: def uliftFunctor : Type u ⥤ Type max u v where   obj X := ULift.{v} X   map {X} {Y} f := fun x : ULift.{v} X => ULift.up (f x.down)
CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor.description: This definition describes a functor that embeds a type into a higher-level type in a category theory context.

CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor_map.code:
CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor_map.{v, u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : ULift.{v, u} X) :
  uliftFunctor.{v, u}.map f x = { down := f x.down }

explanatories.ULift.down: This definition describes a function that retrieves the underlying value from a lifted type.
explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor_map.description: This theorem establishes the behavior of a functor that lifts morphisms between types, showing how it transforms an object lifted from one type to another by applying the corresponding function.

explanatories.ULift.down: This definition describes a function that retrieves the underlying value from a lifted type.
explanatories.ULift.up: This theorem describes a method to elevate a value into a specific type structure.

CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor_full.fullDefinition: instance uliftFunctor_full : Functor.Full.{u} uliftFunctor where   map_surjective f := ⟨fun x => (f (ULift.up x)).down, rfl⟩
CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor_full.description: This definition indicates that the functor associated with lifting types is a full functor.

explanatories.funext: This theorem expresses that if two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.
explanatories.ULift.down: This definition describes a function that retrieves the underlying value from a lifted type.
explanatories.ULift.up: This theorem describes a method to elevate a value into a specific type structure.

CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor_faithful.fullDefinition: instance uliftFunctor_faithful : uliftFunctor.Faithful where   map_injective {_X} {_Y} f g p :=     funext fun x =>       congr_arg ULift.down (congr_fun p (ULift.up x) : ULift.up (f x) = ULift.up (g x))
CategoryTheory.uliftFunctor_faithful.description: This definition asserts that the ulift functor is faithful, meaning it preserves the distinctness of morphisms when mapped between categories.

CategoryTheory.uliftFunctorTrivial.comment: The functor embedding `Type u` into `Type u` via `ULift` is isomorphic to the identity functor.
CategoryTheory.uliftFunctorTrivial.fullDefinition: def uliftFunctorTrivial : uliftFunctor.{u, u} ≅ 𝟭 _ :=   NatIso.ofComponents uliftTrivial
CategoryTheory.uliftFunctorTrivial.description: This definition states that the functor that lifts types into a higher context using ULift is isomorphic to the identity functor on the category of types.

CategoryTheory.homOfElement.code: CategoryTheory.homOfElement.{u} {X : Type u} (x : X) : PUnit.{u + 1} ⟶ X
CategoryTheory.homOfElement.comment: Any term `x` of a type `X` corresponds to a morphism `PUnit ⟶ X`.
CategoryTheory.homOfElement.fullDefinition: def homOfElement {X : Type u} (x : X) : PUnit ⟶ X := fun _ => x
CategoryTheory.homOfElement.description: This definition establishes a correspondence between an element of a type and a morphism from a unit type to that type.

CategoryTheory.homOfElement_eq_iff.code: CategoryTheory.homOfElement_eq_iff.{u} {X : Type u} (x y : X) : homOfElement x = homOfElement y ↔ x = y
CategoryTheory.homOfElement_eq_iff.description: This theorem states that two elements are equal if and only if their corresponding morphisms, derived from them, are equal.

CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective.code: CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective.{u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Mono f ↔ Function.Injective f
CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective.comment:
A morphism in `Type` is a monomorphism if and only if it is injective.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/003C>.
CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective.description: This theorem states that a morphism in the category of types is a monomorphism if and only if it is an injective function.

CategoryTheory.injective_of_mono.code: CategoryTheory.injective_of_mono.{u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) [hf : Mono f] : Function.Injective f
CategoryTheory.injective_of_mono.description: This theorem asserts that if a morphism is monomorphic, then it is injective as a function.

CategoryTheory.epi_iff_surjective.code: CategoryTheory.epi_iff_surjective.{u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Epi f ↔ Function.Surjective f
CategoryTheory.epi_iff_surjective.comment:
A morphism in `Type` is an epimorphism if and only if it is surjective.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/003C>.
CategoryTheory.epi_iff_surjective.description: This theorem asserts that a morphism in the category of types is an epimorphism if and only if it is a surjective function.

CategoryTheory.surjective_of_epi.code: CategoryTheory.surjective_of_epi.{u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) [hf : Epi f] : Function.Surjective f
CategoryTheory.surjective_of_epi.description: This theorem proves that if a morphism is epimorphic, then it is also surjective.

CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor.code: CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor.{v, u} (m : Type u → Type v) [_root_.Functor m] [LawfulFunctor m] : Type u ⥤ Type v
CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor.comment:
`ofTypeFunctor m` converts from Lean's `Type`-based `Category` to `CategoryTheory`. This
allows us to use these functors in category theory.

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function that applies the first function to the result of the second function.
explanatories.funext: This theorem expresses that if two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.
explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.
explanatories.LawfulFunctor.id_map: There is no definition or theorem presented.
explanatories.LawfulFunctor.comp_map: There is no definition or theorem presented.

CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor.fullDefinition: def ofTypeFunctor (m : Type u → Type v) [_root_.Functor m] [LawfulFunctor m] : Type u ⥤ Type v where   obj := m   map f := Functor.map f   map_id := fun α => by funext X; apply id_map  /- Porting note: original proof is via   `fun α => _root_.Functor.map_id` but I cannot get Lean to find this. Reproduced its   original proof -/   map_comp f g := funext fun a => LawfulFunctor.comp_map f g _
CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor.description: This definition specifies a functor that translates a type-based functor into the context of category theory, enabling its use with categorical structures.

CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor_obj.code:
CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor_obj.{v, u} (m : Type u → Type v) [_root_.Functor m] [LawfulFunctor m] :
  (ofTypeFunctor m).obj = m
CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor_obj.description: This theorem establishes that the object of the type functor corresponds directly to the functor itself.

CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor_map.code:
CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor_map.{v, u} (m : Type u → Type v) [_root_.Functor m] [LawfulFunctor m] {α β : Type u}
  (f : α → β) : (ofTypeFunctor m).map f = Functor.map f

explanatories.Functor.map: A functor allows for the transformation of values within its context by applying a function to each element.

CategoryTheory.ofTypeFunctor_map.description: This theorem states that the mapping of a function by a certain type functor is equal to the mapping of that function by a lawful functor.

Equiv.toIso.code: Equiv.toIso.{u} {X Y : Type u} (e : X ≃ Y) : X ≅ Y
Equiv.toIso.comment:
Any equivalence between types in the same universe gives
a categorical isomorphism between those types.

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.
explanatories.funext: This theorem expresses that if two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.

Equiv.toIso.fullDefinition: def toIso (e : X ≃ Y) : X ≅ Y where   hom := e.toFun   inv := e.invFun   hom_inv_id := funext e.left_inv   inv_hom_id := funext e.right_inv
Equiv.toIso.description: This definition associates any equivalence between types within the same universe with a categorical isomorphism between those types.

Equiv.toIso_hom.code: Equiv.toIso_hom.{u} {X Y : Type u} {e : X ≃ Y} : e.toIso.hom = ⇑e
Equiv.toIso_hom.description: This theorem shows that the morphism associated with an equivalence is equal to the function that corresponds to that equivalence when viewed as a bijection.

Equiv.toIso_inv.code: Equiv.toIso_inv.{u} {X Y : Type u} {e : X ≃ Y} : e.toIso.inv = ⇑e.symm

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

Equiv.toIso_inv.description: This theorem shows that the inverse of the categorical isomorphism induced by an equivalence is equal to the function corresponding to the inverse equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv.code: CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv.{u} {X Y : Type u} (i : X ≅ Y) : X ≃ Y
CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv.comment: Any isomorphism between types gives an equivalence.

explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged while serving as a mechanism to assert or clarify the type of that input.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv.fullDefinition: def toEquiv (i : X ≅ Y) : X ≃ Y where   toFun := i.hom   invFun := i.inv   left_inv x := congr_fun i.hom_inv_id x   right_inv y := congr_fun i.inv_hom_id y
CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv.description: This definition states that an isomorphism between two types can be interpreted as an equivalence between those types.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_fun.code: CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_fun.{u} {X Y : Type u} (i : X ≅ Y) : ⇑i.toEquiv = i.hom
CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_fun.description: This theorem demonstrates that the function corresponding to an isomorphism's equivalence is equal to the isomorphism's homomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_symm_fun.code: CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_symm_fun.{u} {X Y : Type u} (i : X ≅ Y) : ⇑i.toEquiv.symm = i.inv

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_symm_fun.description: This theorem asserts that the inverse of an isomorphism can be expressed as the symmetrization of its corresponding equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_id.code: CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_id.{u} (X : Type u) : (refl X).toEquiv = Equiv.refl X
CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_id.description: This theorem establishes that the equivalence induced by the identity isomorphism on a type corresponds to the identity equivalence on that type.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_comp.{u} {X Y Z : Type u} (f : X ≅ Y) (g : Y ≅ Z) :
  (f ≪≫ g).toEquiv = f.toEquiv.trans g.toEquiv

explanatories.Iff.trans: The theorem demonstrates that if two propositions are equivalent to a third proposition, then the first and the third propositions are also equivalent.
explanatories.Eq.trans: This theorem asserts that equality is transitive, meaning if one value equals a second value and that second value equals a third value, then the first value must equal the third value.

CategoryTheory.Iso.toEquiv_comp.description: This theorem asserts that the equivalence of the composition of two isomorphisms is equal to the composition of their respective equivalences.

CategoryTheory.isIso_iff_bijective.code: CategoryTheory.isIso_iff_bijective.{u} {X Y : Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y) : IsIso f ↔ Function.Bijective f
CategoryTheory.isIso_iff_bijective.comment: A morphism in `Type u` is an isomorphism if and only if it is bijective.
CategoryTheory.isIso_iff_bijective.description: This theorem states that a morphism is an isomorphism if and only if it is bijective.

equivIsoIso.code: equivIsoIso.{u} {X Y : Type u} : X ≃ Y ≅ X ≅ Y
equivIsoIso.comment:
Equivalences (between types in the same universe) are the same as (isomorphic to) isomorphisms
of types.

explanatories.Equiv.toIso: This definition associates any equivalence between types within the same universe with a categorical isomorphism between those types.

equivIsoIso.fullDefinition: def equivIsoIso {X Y : Type u} : X ≃ Y ≅ X ≅ Y where   hom e := e.toIso   inv i := i.toEquiv
equivIsoIso.description: This definition asserts that equivalences between types in the same universe are isomorphic to isomorphisms of those types.

equivEquivIso.code: equivEquivIso.{u} {X Y : Type u} : X ≃ Y ≃ (X ≅ Y)
equivEquivIso.comment:
Equivalences (between types in the same universe) are the same as (equivalent to) isomorphisms
of types.
equivEquivIso.fullDefinition: def equivEquivIso {X Y : Type u} : X ≃ Y ≃ (X ≅ Y) :=   equivIsoIso.toEquiv
equivEquivIso.description: This definition establishes that an equivalence between two types is equivalent to an isomorphism between those types.

equivEquivIso_hom.code: equivEquivIso_hom.{u} {X Y : Type u} (e : X ≃ Y) : equivEquivIso e = e.toIso
equivEquivIso_hom.description: This theorem states that the homomorphism associated with an equivalence between two types is equal to its corresponding isomorphism.

equivEquivIso_inv.code: equivEquivIso_inv.{u} {X Y : Type u} (e : X ≅ Y) : equivEquivIso.symm e = e.toEquiv

explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

equivEquivIso_inv.description: This theorem shows that the inverse of an equivalence is equal to the underlying equivalence of the associated isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.iso_consta.code:
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.iso_constant.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [self : IsPreconnected J]
  {α : Type u₁} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) (j : J) : Nonempty (F ≅ (Functor.const J).obj (F.obj j))
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.iso_consta.comment: A possibly empty category for which every functor to a discrete category is constant.
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.iso_consta.description: This theorem asserts that in a preconnected category, any functor to a discrete category is guaranteed to be constant, ensuring that it yields the same output for all inputs.

CategoryTheory.IsConnected.is_nonempty.code: CategoryTheory.IsConnected.is_nonempty.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [self : IsConnected J] : Nonempty J
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.is_nonempty.description: This theorem states that a connected category contains at least one object, ensuring its non-emptiness.

CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.IsoConstantAux.liftToDiscrete.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J]
