explanatories.Iff.intro: This theorem establishes that two propositions are equivalent if each can be inferred from the other.
explanatories.Equivalence.mk: There are no theorems or definitions provided for consideration.
explanatories.Exists.intro: This theorem states that if an element exists in a type and satisfies a given property, then there is a proof of the existence of that element with the property.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def liftToDiscrete {α : Type u₂} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) : J ⥤ Discrete J where   obj j := have := Nonempty.intro j     Discrete.mk (Function.invFun F.obj (F.obj j))   map {j _} f := have := Nonempty.intro j     ⟨⟨congr_arg (Function.invFun F.obj) (Discrete.ext _ _ (Discrete.eq_of_hom (F.map f)))⟩⟩
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor from a category to a discrete category into a functor that maps the original category to itself, preserving discrete structures.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.code:
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.IsoConstantAux.factorThroughDiscrete.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J]
  {α : Type u₂} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) :
  CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.IsoConstantAux.liftToDiscrete F ⋙ Discrete.functor F.obj ≅ F
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.comment: Implementation detail of `isoConstant`.

explanatories._private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli: This definition describes a functor that transforms a functor from a category to a discrete category into a functor that maps the original category to itself, preserving discrete structures.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def factorThroughDiscrete {α : Type u₂} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) :     liftToDiscrete F ⋙ Discrete.functor F.obj ≅ F :=   NatIso.ofComponents (fun j => eqToIso Function.apply_invFun_apply) (by aesop_cat)
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: This definition describes an isomorphism between a composite functor that lifts a functor to a discrete category and maps it back, and the original functor, highlighting a structural relationship in preconnected categories.

CategoryTheory.isoConstant.code:
CategoryTheory.isoConstant.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsPreconnected J] {α : Type u₂}
  (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) (j : J) : F ≅ (Functor.const J).obj (F.obj j)
CategoryTheory.isoConstant.comment:
If `J` is connected, any functor `F : J ⥤ Discrete α` is isomorphic to
the constant functor with value `F.obj j` (for any choice of `j`).

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.iso_consta: This theorem asserts that in a preconnected category, any functor to a discrete category is guaranteed to be constant, ensuring that it yields the same output for all inputs.
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.
explanatories._private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli: This definition describes an isomorphism between a composite functor that lifts a functor to a discrete category and maps it back, and the original functor, highlighting a structural relationship in preconnected categories.
explanatories.Or.symm: This theorem states that the disjunction of two propositions is symmetric, meaning if one proposition is true or the other is true, then the reverse can also be concluded.
explanatories.Equivalence.symm: It is established that if a relation is an equivalence, then it is symmetric, meaning that if one element is related to another, the reverse relationship also holds.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.isoConstant.fullDefinition: def isoConstant [IsPreconnected J] {α : Type u₂} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) (j : J) :     F ≅ (Functor.const J).obj (F.obj j) :=   (IsPreconnected.IsoConstantAux.factorThroughDiscrete F).symm     ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight (IsPreconnected.iso_constant _ j).some _     ≪≫ NatIso.ofComponents (fun j' => eqToIso Function.apply_invFun_apply) (by aesop_cat)
CategoryTheory.isoConstant.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between any functor from a preconnected category to a discrete category and a constant functor that uniformly maps to a specific object determined by a chosen element of the original category.

CategoryTheory.any_functor_const_on_obj.code:
CategoryTheory.any_functor_const_on_obj.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsPreconnected J]
  {α : Type u₂} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) (j j' : J) : F.obj j = F.obj j'
CategoryTheory.any_functor_const_on_obj.comment:
If `J` is connected, any functor to a discrete category is constant on objects.
The converse is given in `IsConnected.of_any_functor_const_on_obj`.
CategoryTheory.any_functor_const_on_obj.description: In a connected category, any functor mapping to a discrete category produces the same object value for all inputs.

CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_any_fun.code:
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_any_functor_const_on_obj.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J]
  (h : ∀ {α : Type u₁} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) (j j' : J), F.obj j = F.obj j') : IsPreconnected J
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_any_fun.comment:
If any functor to a discrete category is constant on objects, J is connected.
The converse of `any_functor_const_on_obj`.
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_any_fun.description: This theorem states that if any functor from a category to a discrete category has constant outputs for all objects, then that category is considered connected.

CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_any_functo.code:
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_any_functor_const_on_obj.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [Nonempty J]
  (h : ∀ {α : Type u₁} (F : J ⥤ Discrete α) (j j' : J), F.obj j = F.obj j') : IsConnected J
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_any_functo.comment:
If any functor to a discrete category is constant on objects, J is connected.
The converse of `any_functor_const_on_obj`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_any_fun: This theorem states that if any functor from a category to a discrete category has constant outputs for all objects, then that category is considered connected.

CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_any_functo.description: This theorem establishes that if any functor from a category to a discrete category yields the same output for all objects, then the category must be connected.

CategoryTheory.constant_of_preserves_mor.code:
CategoryTheory.constant_of_preserves_morphisms.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsPreconnected J]
  {α : Type u₂} (F : J → α) (h : ∀ (j₁ j₂ : J), (j₁ ⟶ j₂) → F j₁ = F j₂) (j j' : J) : F j = F j'
CategoryTheory.constant_of_preserves_mor.comment:
If `J` is connected, then given any function `F` such that the presence of a
morphism `j₁ ⟶ j₂` implies `F j₁ = F j₂`, we have that `F` is constant.
This can be thought of as a local-to-global property.

The converse is shown in `IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms`
CategoryTheory.constant_of_preserves_mor.description: In a connected category, any function that produces the same output for objects connected by morphisms must yield the same value for all objects in that category.

CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_constan.code:
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J]
  (h : ∀ {α : Type u₁} (F : J → α), (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J}, (j₁ ⟶ j₂) → F j₁ = F j₂) → ∀ (j j' : J), F j = F j') :
  IsPreconnected J
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_constan.comment:
`J` is connected if: given any function `F : J → α` which is constant for any
`j₁, j₂` for which there is a morphism `j₁ ⟶ j₂`, then `F` is constant.
This can be thought of as a local-to-global property.

The converse of `constant_of_preserves_morphisms`.
CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_constan.description: This theorem establishes that a category is connected if any function mapping from the category to another set that is constant on morphisms also remains constant for all elements in the category.

CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_constant_o.code:
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_constant_of_preserves_morphisms.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [Nonempty J]
  (h : ∀ {α : Type u₁} (F : J → α), (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J}, (j₁ ⟶ j₂) → F j₁ = F j₂) → ∀ (j j' : J), F j = F j') : IsConnected J
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_constant_o.comment:
`J` is connected if: given any function `F : J → α` which is constant for any
`j₁, j₂` for which there is a morphism `j₁ ⟶ j₂`, then `F` is constant.
This can be thought of as a local-to-global property.

The converse of `constant_of_preserves_morphisms`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.of_constan: This theorem establishes that a category is connected if any function mapping from the category to another set that is constant on morphisms also remains constant for all elements in the category.

CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_constant_o.description: A category is connected if any function from it to another type that is constant whenever its inputs are related by a morphism is constant on the entire category.

CategoryTheory.induct_on_objects.code:
CategoryTheory.induct_on_objects.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsPreconnected J] (p : Set J) {j₀ : J}
  (h0 : j₀ ∈ p) (h1 : ∀ {j₁ j₂ : J}, (j₁ ⟶ j₂) → (j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p)) (j : J) : j ∈ p
CategoryTheory.induct_on_objects.comment:
An inductive-like property for the objects of a connected category.
If the set `p` is nonempty, and `p` is closed under morphisms of `J`,
then `p` contains all of `J`.

The converse is given in `IsConnected.of_induct`.
CategoryTheory.induct_on_objects.description: This theorem asserts that in a preconnected category, if a nonempty set of objects is closed under morphisms, then it must include every object in the category, demonstrating a form of inductive completeness.

CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_induct.code:
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_induct.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {j₀ : J}
  (h : ∀ (p : Set J), j₀ ∈ p → (∀ {j₁ j₂ : J}, (j₁ ⟶ j₂) → (j₁ ∈ p ↔ j₂ ∈ p)) → ∀ (j : J), j ∈ p) : IsConnected J
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_induct.comment:
If any maximal connected component containing some element j₀ of J is all of J, then J is connected.

The converse of `induct_on_objects`.
CategoryTheory.IsConnected.of_induct.description: This theorem concludes that if every maximal connected component containing a specific element in a category encompasses the entire category, then the category itself is connected.

CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_induction.comment:
Another induction principle for `IsPreconnected J`:
given a type family `Z : J → Sort*` and
a rule for transporting in *both* directions along a morphism in `J`,
we can transport an `x : Z j₀` to a point in `Z j` for any `j`.
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_induction.description: This theorem provides an induction principle for preconnected categories, allowing the transfer of a property defined on objects through morphisms in both directions, ensuring the existence of the property at any chosen object starting from any initial object in the category.

CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_of_equival.code:
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_of_equivalent.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {K : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} K] [IsPreconnected J] (e : J ≌ K) : IsPreconnected K
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_of_equival.comment: If `J` and `K` are equivalent, then if `J` is preconnected then `K` is as well.
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_of_equival.description: This theorem states that if two categories are equivalent and one is preconnected, then the other category must also be preconnected.

CategoryTheory.isConnected_of_equivalent.code:
CategoryTheory.isConnected_of_equivalent.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {K : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} K] (e : J ≌ K) [IsConnected J] : IsConnected K
CategoryTheory.isConnected_of_equivalent.comment: If `J` and `K` are equivalent, then if `J` is connected then `K` is as well.
CategoryTheory.isConnected_of_equivalent.description: This theorem states that if two categories are equivalent and one of them is connected, then the other must also be connected.

CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_op.code: CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_op.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsPreconnected J] : IsPreconnected Jᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_op.comment: If `J` is preconnected, then `Jᵒᵖ` is preconnected as well.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsPreconnected.iso_consta: This theorem asserts that in a preconnected category, any functor to a discrete category is guaranteed to be constant, ensuring that it yields the same output for all inputs.
explanatories.Option.some: The statement defines a constructor that produces an option type containing a specified value of a given type.

CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_op.fullDefinition: instance isPreconnected_op [IsPreconnected J] : IsPreconnected Jᵒᵖ where   iso_constant := fun {α} F X =>     ⟨NatIso.ofComponents fun Y =>       eqToIso (Discrete.ext _ _ (Discrete.eq_of_hom ((Nonempty.some         (IsPreconnected.iso_constant (F.rightOp ⋙ (Discrete.opposite α).functor) (unop X))).app           (unop Y)).hom))⟩
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_op.description: If a category is preconnected, its opposite category is also preconnected.

CategoryTheory.isConnected_op.code: CategoryTheory.isConnected_op.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsConnected J] : IsConnected Jᵒᵖ
CategoryTheory.isConnected_op.comment: If `J` is connected, then `Jᵒᵖ` is connected as well.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsConnected.is_nonempty: This theorem states that a connected category contains at least one object, ensuring its non-emptiness.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: A value of a type indicates that the type is nonempty.
explanatories.Iff.intro: This theorem establishes that two propositions are equivalent if each can be inferred from the other.
explanatories.Exists.intro: This theorem states that if an element exists in a type and satisfies a given property, then there is a proof of the existence of that element with the property.

CategoryTheory.isConnected_op.fullDefinition: instance isConnected_op [IsConnected J] : IsConnected Jᵒᵖ where   is_nonempty := Nonempty.intro (op (Classical.arbitrary J))
CategoryTheory.isConnected_op.description: This definition indicates that if a category is connected, then its opposite category is also connected.

CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_of_isPreco.code:
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_of_isPreconnected_op.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsPreconnected Jᵒᵖ] :
  IsPreconnected J
CategoryTheory.isPreconnected_of_isPreco.description: This theorem asserts that if a category is preconnected in its opposite form, then it is also preconnected in its original form.

CategoryTheory.isConnected_of_isConnecte.code:
CategoryTheory.isConnected_of_isConnected_op.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] [IsConnected Jᵒᵖ] :
  IsConnected J
CategoryTheory.isConnected_of_isConnecte.description: This theorem establishes that if a category is connected when considering its opposite, then it is also connected in its original form.

CategoryTheory.Zag.code: CategoryTheory.Zag.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] (j₁ j₂ : J) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Zag.comment: j₁ and j₂ are related by `Zag` if there is a morphism between them.
CategoryTheory.Zag.fullDefinition: def Zag (j₁ j₂ : J) : Prop :=   Nonempty (j₁ ⟶ j₂) ∨ Nonempty (j₂ ⟶ j₁)
CategoryTheory.Zag.description: This definition establishes a relation between two objects in a category, indicating that they are connected if there exists a morphism between them.

CategoryTheory.zag_symmetric.code: CategoryTheory.zag_symmetric.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] : Symmetric Zag
CategoryTheory.zag_symmetric.description: This theorem states that a specific category is symmetric, satisfying the properties defined by the notion of a symmetric zag.

CategoryTheory.Zigzag.code: CategoryTheory.Zigzag.{v₁, u₁} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] : J → J → Prop
CategoryTheory.Zigzag.comment:
`j₁` and `j₂` are related by `Zigzag` if there is a chain of
morphisms from `j₁` to `j₂`, with backward morphisms allowed.
CategoryTheory.Zigzag.fullDefinition: def Zigzag : J → J → Prop :=   Relation.ReflTransGen Zag
CategoryTheory.Zigzag.description: Two objects in a category are connected by a zigzag relation if there exists a chain of morphisms between them that can include both forward and backward arrows.

CategoryTheory.discreteIsConnectedEquivP.fullDefinition: def discreteIsConnectedEquivPUnit {α : Type u₁} [IsConnected (Discrete α)] : α ≃ PUnit :=   Discrete.equivOfEquivalence.{u₁, u₁}     { functor := Functor.star (Discrete α)       inverse := Discrete.functor fun _ => Classical.arbitrary _       unitIso := isoConstant _ (Classical.arbitrary _)       counitIso := Functor.punitExt _ _ }
CategoryTheory.discreteIsConnectedEquivP.description: If a discrete category derived from a type is connected, then the type is equivalent to a single-point type.

CategoryTheory.nat_trans_from_is_connect.comment:
For objects `X Y : C`, any natural transformation `α : const X ⟶ const Y` from a connected
category must be constant.
This is the key property of connected categories which we use to establish properties about limits.
CategoryTheory.nat_trans_from_is_connect.description: Any natural transformation between two objects from a functor to a connected category must map every element of the domain to the same element in the codomain, demonstrating the constancy of transformations in connected categories.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.isColimitOfI.fullDefinition: def Cofan.isColimitOfIsIsoSigmaDesc {f : β → C} [HasCoproduct f] (c : Cofan f)     [hc : IsIso (Sigma.desc c.inj)] : IsColimit c :=   IsColimit.ofIsoColimit (colimit.isColimit (Discrete.functor f))     (Cofan.ext (@asIso _ _ _ _ _ hc) (fun _ => colimit.ι_desc _ _))

CategoryTheory.Limits.mkCofanColimit.{w, v, u} {β : Type w} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {f : β → C} (s : Cofan f)
  (desc : (t : Cofan f) → s.pt ⟶ t.pt) (fac : ∀ (t : Cofan f) (j : β), s.inj j ≫ desc t = t.inj j := by aesop_cat)
  (uniq : ∀ (t : Cofan f) (m : s.pt ⟶ t.pt), (∀ (j : β), s.inj j ≫ m = t.inj j) → m = desc t := by aesop_cat) :
  IsColimit s
CategoryTheory.Limits.mkCofanColimit.comment:
Make a cofan `f` into a colimit cofan by providing `desc`, `fac`, and `uniq` --
just a convenience lemma to avoid having to go through `Discrete`

CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.map.fullDefinition: abbrev Pi.map {f g : β → C} [HasProduct f] [HasProduct g] (p : ∀ b, f b ⟶ g b) : ∏ᶜ f ⟶ ∏ᶜ g :=   limMap (Discrete.natTrans fun X => p X.as)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.map.description: This definition constructs a morphism between two categorical products, based on a family of morphisms connecting their respective components.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.map_mono.fullDefinition: instance Pi.map_mono {f g : β → C} [HasProduct f] [HasProduct g] (p : ∀ b, f b ⟶ g b)     [∀ i, Mono (p i)] : Mono <| Pi.map p :=   @Limits.limMap_mono _ _ _ _ (Discrete.functor f) (Discrete.functor g) _ _     (Discrete.natTrans fun X => p X.as) (by dsimp; infer_instance)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.π: This definition specifies a projection morphism from the limit object of a functor to the object corresponding to a specific element of the indexing category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.π: This definition describes the morphism from a product object to a component object in a category, specifically extracting the projection for an indexed family of objects.
explanatories.Sigma.mk: This theorem constructs a dependent pair consisting of an element from one type and an element from a type that depends on the first element.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.cone.fullDefinition: def Pi.cone : Cone X where   pt := ∏ᶜ (fun j => X.obj (Discrete.mk j))   π := Discrete.natTrans (fun _ => Pi.π _ _)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.cone.description: This definition constructs a limit cone for a functor from a discrete category to another category, corresponding to the product of objects represented by the functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.fac: This theorem shows that a specific lifting of a cone through a limit cone results in a commutative triangle involving the cone's projection morphisms and the natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.fac: This theorem establishes that the morphism from a cocone to its colimit, when composed with the corresponding arrow from the colimit, yields the arrow from the cocone at the same object, ensuring the commutativity of the involved diagram.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.lift: This definition describes the morphism that connects the cone point of any cone associated with a functor to the limit object of that functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.lift_π: This theorem asserts that for a functor with an established limit, the composition of the morphism lifting from a cone to the limit with the limit projection equals the morphism from the cone to the object corresponding to a specific index in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fan.mk_pt: This theorem establishes that the underlying object of a constructed fan from a specific point and a collection of morphisms is equal to that point itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fan.mk_π_app: The theorem demonstrates that the application of the projection morphism from a constructed fan to a specific point in a discrete indexing category is equal to the corresponding morphism defined for that specific index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.mk_pt: This theorem establishes that the apex of a cofan constructed with a morphism from a family of objects to a particular object is equal to that object itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.ext: This definition establishes an isomorphism between two cofans based on an isomorphism of their points and a compatibility condition for their inclusion maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.cone: This definition constructs a limit cone for a functor from a discrete category to another category, corresponding to the product of objects represented by the functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.productIsProduct'.fullDefinition: def productIsProduct' :     IsLimit (Pi.cone X) where   lift s := Pi.lift (fun j => s.π.app ⟨j⟩)   fac s := by simp   uniq s m hm := by     dsimp     ext     simp only [limit.lift_π, Fan.mk_pt, Fan.mk_π_app]     apply hm
CategoryTheory.Limits.productIsProduct'.description: This definition asserts that the cone formed by the image of a functor from a discrete type into a category is a limit cone, provided that the category has the necessary product structure.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.isoLimit.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the product of objects indexed by a discrete category and the limit of a functor defined on that category, assuming the functor has a limit.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map.{w, v, u} {β : Type w} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {f g : β → C} [HasCoproduct f]
  [HasCoproduct g] (p : (b : β) → f b ⟶ g b) : ∐ f ⟶ ∐ g
CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map.comment:
Construct a morphism between categorical coproducts (indexed by the same type)
from a family of morphisms between the factors.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.natTrans: This definition states that a natural transformation between functors from a discrete category consists of a collection of maps, since the naturality conditions are trivial in this case.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoproduct: This definition characterizes the existence of a coproduct in a category as the presence of a colimit for a functor derived from a discrete type mapping to that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limMap: This definition expresses a morphism from the limit of one functor to the limit of another, given a natural transformation between the two functors, ensuring the functoriality of limits.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.map: This definition constructs a morphism between two categorical products, based on a family of morphisms connecting their respective components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimMap: This definition describes a morphism from the colimit of one functor to the colimit of another, which is induced by a natural transformation between those functors, highlighting the functorial nature of colimits.
explanatories.Prefunctor.map: No definition or action is provided in this case.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map.fullDefinition: abbrev Sigma.map {f g : β → C} [HasCoproduct f] [HasCoproduct g] (p : ∀ b, f b ⟶ g b) :     ∐ f ⟶ ∐ g :=   colimMap (Discrete.natTrans fun X => p X.as)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map.description: This definition constructs a morphism between the coproducts of two families of objects in a category based on a specified collection of morphisms between corresponding objects in each family.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map_epi.fullDefinition: instance Sigma.map_epi {f g : β → C} [HasCoproduct f] [HasCoproduct g] (p : ∀ b, f b ⟶ g b)     [∀ i, Epi (p i)] : Epi <| Sigma.map p :=   @Limits.colimMap_epi _ _ _ _ (Discrete.functor f) (Discrete.functor g) _ _     (Discrete.natTrans fun X => p X.as) (by dsimp; infer_instance)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map_epi.description: This definition states that if a family of morphisms between two coproducts is composed of epimorphisms, then the induced morphism between the coproducts is also an epimorphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitChangeEmpty.fullDefinition: def isLimitChangeEmptyCone {c₁ : Cone F₁} (hl : IsLimit c₁) (c₂ : Cone F₂) (hi : c₁.pt ≅ c₂.pt) :     IsLimit c₂ where   lift c := hl.lift ⟨c.pt, by aesop_cat, by aesop_cat⟩ ≫ hi.hom   uniq c f _ := by     dsimp     rw [← hl.uniq _ (f ≫ hi.inv) _]     · simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id]     · aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitChangeEmpty.description: This definition establishes that the notion of being a limit is unaffected by changes in the empty diagram's universe or the cone structure, provided that the points of the cones are isomorphic.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitEmptyConeEq.fullDefinition: def isLimitEmptyConeEquiv (c₁ : Cone F₁) (c₂ : Cone F₂) (h : c₁.pt ≅ c₂.pt) :     IsLimit c₁ ≃ IsLimit c₂ where   toFun hl := isLimitChangeEmptyCone C hl c₂ h   invFun hl := isLimitChangeEmptyCone C hl c₁ h.symm   left_inv := by dsimp [Function.LeftInverse]; intro; simp only [eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton]   right_inv := by     dsimp [Function.LeftInverse,Function.RightInverse]; intro     simp only [eq_iff_true_of_subsingleton]

CategoryTheory.Limits.coconeOfDiagramIni.fullDefinition: def coconeOfDiagramInitial {X : J} (hX : IsInitial X) (F : J ⥤ C)     [∀ (i j : J) (f : i ⟶ j), IsIso (F.map f)] : Cocone F where   pt := F.obj X   ι :=     { app := fun i => inv (F.map (hX.to _))       naturality := by         intro i j f         dsimp         simp only [IsIso.eq_inv_comp, IsIso.comp_inv_eq, Category.comp_id, ← F.map_comp,           hX.hom_ext (hX.to i ≫ f) (hX.to j)] }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk.fullDefinition: def Fork.IsLimit.mk (t : Fork f g) (lift : ∀ s : Fork f g, s.pt ⟶ t.pt)     (fac : ∀ s : Fork f g, lift s ≫ Fork.ι t = Fork.ι s)     (uniq : ∀ (s : Fork f g) (m : s.pt ⟶ t.pt) (_ : m ≫ t.ι = s.ι), m = lift s) : IsLimit t :=   { lift     fac := fun s j =>       WalkingParallelPair.casesOn j (fac s) <| by         erw [← s.w left, ← t.w left, ← Category.assoc, fac]; rfl     uniq := fun s m j => by aesop}
CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk.description: This definition provides a framework for verifying that a fork is a limit cone by specifying a lifting morphism and conditions for its uniqueness and compatibility with the morphisms of the fork.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk'.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} {f g : X ⟶ Y} (t : Fork f g)
  (create :
    (s : Fork f g) →
      { l //
        l ≫ t.ι = s.ι ∧
          ∀
            {m :
              ((Functor.const WalkingParallelPair).obj s.pt).obj zero ⟶
                ((Functor.const WalkingParallelPair).obj t.pt).obj zero},
            m ≫ t.ι = s.ι → m = l }) :
  IsLimit t
CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk'.comment:
This is another convenient method to verify that a fork is a limit cone. It
only asks for a proof of facts that carry any mathematical content, and allows access to the
same `s` for all parts.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.m.fullDefinition: def Cofork.IsColimit.mk (t : Cofork f g) (desc : ∀ s : Cofork f g, t.pt ⟶ s.pt)     (fac : ∀ s : Cofork f g, Cofork.π t ≫ desc s = Cofork.π s)     (uniq : ∀ (s : Cofork f g) (m : t.pt ⟶ s.pt) (_ : t.π ≫ m = s.π), m = desc s) : IsColimit t :=   { desc     fac := fun s j =>       WalkingParallelPair.casesOn j (by erw [← s.w left, ← t.w left, Category.assoc, fac]; rfl)         (fac s)     uniq := by aesop }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.homIs.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.homIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} {f g : X ⟶ Y} {t : Fork f g}
  (ht : IsLimit t) (Z : C) : (Z ⟶ t.pt) ≃ { h // h ≫ f = h ≫ g }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.homIs.comment:
Given a limit cone for the pair `f g : X ⟶ Y`, for any `Z`, morphisms from `Z` to its point are in
bijection with morphisms `h : Z ⟶ X` such that `h ≫ f = h ≫ g`.
Further, this bijection is natural in `Z`: see `Fork.IsLimit.homIso_natural`.
This is a special case of `IsLimit.homIso'`, often useful to construct adjunctions.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.h.fullDefinition: def Cofork.IsColimit.homIso {X Y : C} {f g : X ⟶ Y} {t : Cofork f g} (ht : IsColimit t) (Z : C) :     (t.pt ⟶ Z) ≃ { h : Y ⟶ Z // f ≫ h = g ≫ h } where   toFun k := ⟨t.π ≫ k, by simp only [← Category.assoc, t.condition]⟩   invFun h := (Cofork.IsColimit.desc' ht _ h.prop).1   left_inv k := Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext ht (Cofork.IsColimit.desc' _ _ _).prop   right_inv h := Subtype.ext (Cofork.IsColimit.desc' ht _ _).prop
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.h.description: This definition states that there exists a bijection between morphisms from the colimit cocone point to any object in the category and morphisms from one of the morphisms in a parallel pair to that object, such that they satisfy a specific equation relating the two morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.ofFork.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.ofFork.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {F : WalkingParallelPair ⥤ C}
  (t : Fork (F.map left) (F.map right)) : Cone F
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.ofFork.comment:
This is a helper construction that can be useful when verifying that a category has all
equalizers. Given `F : WalkingParallelPair ⥤ C`, which is really the same as
`parallelPair (F.map left) (F.map right)`, and a fork on `F.map left` and `F.map right`,
we get a cone on `F`.

If you're thinking about using this, have a look at `hasEqualizers_of_hasLimit_parallelPair`,
which you may find to be an easier way of achieving your goal.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isEqualizerCompMon.fullDefinition: def isEqualizerCompMono {c : Fork f g} (i : IsLimit c) {Z : C} (h : Y ⟶ Z) [hm : Mono h] :     have : Fork.ι c ≫ f ≫ h = Fork.ι c ≫ g ≫ h := by       simp only [← Category.assoc]       exact congrArg (· ≫ h) c.condition     IsLimit (Fork.ofι c.ι (by simp [this]) : Fork (f ≫ h) (g ≫ h)) :=   Fork.IsLimit.mk' _ fun s =>     let s' : Fork f g := Fork.ofι s.ι (by apply hm.right_cancellation; simp [s.condition])     let l := Fork.IsLimit.lift' i s'.ι s'.condition     ⟨l.1, l.2, fun hm => by       apply Fork.IsLimit.hom_ext i; rw [Fork.ι_ofι] at hm; rw [hm]; exact l.2.symm⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.isEqualizerCompMon.description: The definition states that postcomposing the equalizer of two morphisms with a monomorphism results in a new fork that is also an equalizer.

CategoryTheory.Limits.splitMonoOfIdempot.fullDefinition: def splitMonoOfIdempotentOfIsLimitFork {X : C} {f : X ⟶ X} (hf : f ≫ f = f) {c : Fork (𝟙 X) f}     (i : IsLimit c) : SplitMono c.ι where   retraction := i.lift (Fork.ofι f (by simp [hf]))   id := by     letI := mono_of_isLimit_fork i     rw [← cancel_mono_id c.ι, Category.assoc, Fork.IsLimit.lift_ι, Fork.ι_ofι, ← c.condition]     exact Category.comp_id c.ι
CategoryTheory.Limits.splitMonoOfIdempot.description: The definition states that if an idempotent morphism forms a limit fork with the identity morphism, then the morphism from the fork can be split as a monomorphism.

Whenever `f` coequalizes `(f ≫ s)` and `(𝟙 X)`, then `s` is a section of `f`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isCoequalizerEpiCo.fullDefinition: def isCoequalizerEpiComp {c : Cofork f g} (i : IsColimit c) {W : C} (h : W ⟶ X) [hm : Epi h] :     have : (h ≫ f) ≫ Cofork.π c = (h ≫ g) ≫ Cofork.π c := by       simp only [Category.assoc]       exact congrArg (h ≫ ·) c.condition     IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ c.π (this) : Cofork (h ≫ f) (h ≫ g)) :=   Cofork.IsColimit.mk' _ fun s =>     let s' : Cofork f g :=       Cofork.ofπ s.π (by apply hm.left_cancellation; simp_rw [← Category.assoc, s.condition])     let l := Cofork.IsColimit.desc' i s'.π s'.condition     ⟨l.1, l.2, fun hm => by       apply Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext i; rw [Cofork.π_ofπ] at hm; rw [hm]; exact l.2.symm⟩

  {F : WidePushoutShape J ⥤ C} {X : C} (f : F.obj none ⟶ X) (ι : (j : J) → F.obj (some j) ⟶ X)
  (w : ∀ (j : J), F.map (WidePushoutShape.Hom.init j) ≫ ι j = f) (j : WidePushoutShape J) :
  (WidePushoutShape.mkCocone f ι w).ι.app j =
    match j with
    | none => f
    | some j => ι j

  (t : Cotrident f) : (parallelFamily f).obj one ⟶ ((Functor.const (WalkingParallelFamily J)).obj t.pt).obj one
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cotrident.π.comment:
A cotrident `t` on the parallel family `f : J → (X ⟶ Y)` consists of two morphisms
`t.ι.app zero : X ⟶ t.X` and `t.ι.app one : Y ⟶ t.X`. Of these, only the second one is
interesting, and we give it the shorter name `Cotrident.π t`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.IsLimit.li.description: This definition establishes that if a trident represents a limit for a family of morphisms and a morphism satisfies a certain commuting condition with those morphisms, then there is a corresponding morphism from a different object that effectively relates to the limit morphism in the trident.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cotrident.IsColimi.comment:

`Cotrident.π s ≫ l = k`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.IsLimit.mk.fullDefinition: def Trident.IsLimit.mk [Nonempty J] (t : Trident f) (lift : ∀ s : Trident f, s.pt ⟶ t.pt)     (fac : ∀ s : Trident f, lift s ≫ t.ι = s.ι)     (uniq :       ∀ (s : Trident f) (m : s.pt ⟶ t.pt)         (_ : ∀ j : WalkingParallelFamily J, m ≫ t.π.app j = s.π.app j), m = lift s) :     IsLimit t :=   { lift     fac := fun s j =>       WalkingParallelFamily.casesOn j (fac s)         (by rw [← t.w (line (Classical.arbitrary J)), reassoc_of% fac, s.w])     uniq := uniq }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.IsLimit.mk.description: This definition provides a structured approach to verify that a trident serves as a limit cone by requiring a method to lift morphisms and ensuring the conditions for universality are satisfied.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.IsLimit.mk.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.IsLimit.mk'.{w, v, u} {J : Type w} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C}
  {f : J → (X ⟶ Y)} [Nonempty J] (t : Trident f)
  (create :
    (s : Trident f) →
      { l //
        l ≫ t.ι = s.ι ∧
          ∀
            {m :
              ((Functor.const (WalkingParallelFamily J)).obj s.pt).obj zero ⟶
                ((Functor.const (WalkingParallelFamily J)).obj t.pt).obj zero},
            m ≫ t.ι = s.ι → m = l }) :
  IsLimit t

CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.IsLimit.ho.comment:
Given a limit cone for the family `f : J → (X ⟶ Y)`, for any `Z`, morphisms from `Z` to its point
are in bijection with morphisms `h : Z ⟶ X` such that `∀ j₁ j₂, h ≫ f j₁ = h ≫ f j₂`.
Further, this bijection is natural in `Z`: see `Trident.Limits.homIso_natural`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.ofTrident.comment:

equalizers. Given `F : WalkingParallelFamily ⥤ C`, which is really the same as
`parallelFamily (fun j ↦ F.map (line j))`, and a trident on `fun j ↦ F.map (line j)`,

achieving your goal.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms into a limit cone yield the same results when composed with the projection morphisms from the cone, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.IsLimit.ho: This theorem establishes that if two morphisms from an object to the apex of a trident yield the same composition with the trident's unique morphism, then those two morphisms must be equal, reflecting the uniqueness property of limits in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that two morphisms from a colimit are equal if they yield the same result when composed with the cocone's morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cotrident.IsColimi: This theorem demonstrates that if two morphisms yield the same result when composed with the projection of a cotrident that is a colimit, then those two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Trident.ext: This definition states that an isomorphism between two structures called tridents can be established by providing an isomorphism between their cone points and verifying that this isomorphism preserves certain morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cotrident.ext: This definition establishes that an isomorphism between two cotridents can be derived from an isomorphism between their cocone points, provided that this isomorphism respects the corresponding projection morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.π: This definition specifies a projection morphism from the limit object of a functor to the object corresponding to a specific element of the indexing category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.wideEqualizer.hom_: This theorem asserts that two morphisms into a wide equalizer are equal if their compositions with the wide equalizer morphism yield the same result.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.wideCoequalizer.ho: This theorem states that two morphisms from a wide coequalizer to another object are equal if they yield the same result when composed with the morphism from the wide coequalizer.

CategoryTheory.IsSplitCoequalizer.map.fullDefinition: def IsSplitCoequalizer.map {Z : C} {π : Y ⟶ Z} (q : IsSplitCoequalizer f g π) (F : C ⥤ D) :     IsSplitCoequalizer (F.map f) (F.map g) (F.map π) where   rightSection := F.map q.rightSection   leftSection := F.map q.leftSection   condition := by rw [← F.map_comp, q.condition, F.map_comp]   rightSection_π := by rw [← F.map_comp, q.rightSection_π, F.map_id]   leftSection_bottom := by rw [← F.map_comp, q.leftSection_bottom, F.map_id]   leftSection_top := by rw [← F.map_comp, q.leftSection_top, F.map_comp]

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.isColi.fullDefinition: def BinaryCofan.isColimitMk {W : C} {inl : X ⟶ W} {inr : Y ⟶ W}     (desc : ∀ s : BinaryCofan X Y, W ⟶ s.pt)     (fac_left : ∀ s : BinaryCofan X Y, inl ≫ desc s = s.inl)     (fac_right : ∀ s : BinaryCofan X Y, inr ≫ desc s = s.inr)     (uniq :       ∀ (s : BinaryCofan X Y) (m : W ⟶ s.pt) (_ : inl ≫ m = s.inl) (_ : inr ≫ m = s.inr),         m = desc s) :     IsColimit (BinaryCofan.mk inl inr) :=   { desc := desc     fac := fun s j => by       rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩       exacts [fac_left s, fac_right s]     uniq := fun s m w => uniq s m (w ⟨WalkingPair.left⟩) (w ⟨WalkingPair.right⟩) }

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.inr: This definition describes a morphism that serves as the inclusion from the second component of a binary coproduct into the coproduct itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.desc: This definition describes a morphism that relates the colimit object of a functor to the point of any chosen cocone over that functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.inl_desc: This theorem verifies that when using the left injection morphism in a binary coproduct, followed by the unique morphism induced by a pair of morphisms to a third object, the result is equivalent to the original morphism from the first object to that third object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.inr_desc: The theorem establishes that when morphisms from two objects are combined through a coproduct structure, the resulting composite morphism leading to a common object corresponds exactly to the morphism from the second object.

CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.desc'.fullDefinition: def coprod.desc' {W X Y : C} [HasBinaryCoproduct X Y] (f : X ⟶ W) (g : Y ⟶ W) :     { l : X ⨿ Y ⟶ W // coprod.inl ≫ l = f ∧ coprod.inr ≫ l = g } :=   ⟨coprod.desc f g, coprod.inl_desc _ _, coprod.inr_desc _ _⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.desc'.description: This definition states that if a binary coproduct of two objects exists, then for any pair of morphisms from those objects to a third object, there exists a morphism from the coproduct to the third object that factors through the given morphisms appropriately.

  [HasBinaryProduct Y Z] (f : W ⟶ Y) (g : X ⟶ Z) : W ⨯ X ⟶ Y ⨯ Z
CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.map.comment:
If the products `W ⨯ X` and `Y ⨯ Z` exist, then every pair of morphisms `f : W ⟶ Y` and
`g : X ⟶ Z` induces a morphism `prod.map f g : W ⨯ X ⟶ Y ⨯ Z`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.map.fullDefinition: def prod.map {W X Y Z : C} [HasBinaryProduct W X] [HasBinaryProduct Y Z] (f : W ⟶ Y) (g : X ⟶ Z) :     W ⨯ X ⟶ Y ⨯ Z :=   limMap (mapPair f g)
CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.map.description: This definition establishes a morphism that maps a product of two categories to another product, induced by pairs of morphisms between each respective component of the products.

CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.associator.fullDefinition: def prod.associator [HasBinaryProducts C] (P Q R : C) : (P ⨯ Q) ⨯ R ≅ P ⨯ Q ⨯ R where   hom := prod.lift (prod.fst ≫ prod.fst) (prod.lift (prod.fst ≫ prod.snd) prod.snd)   inv := prod.lift (prod.lift prod.fst (prod.snd ≫ prod.fst)) (prod.snd ≫ prod.snd)

CategoryTheory.Limits.prodComparisonNatT.description: This definition describes a natural transformation between functors that relates the product of an object with another object in the source category to the product of the image of that object under the functor with the image of the other object in the target category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.inv_prodComparison.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.inv_prodComparison_map_fst_assoc.{v, u, u₂, w} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u₂}

CategoryTheory.Limits.Multifork.ofι.fullDefinition: def ofι (I : MulticospanIndex.{w} C) (P : C) (ι : ∀ a, P ⟶ I.left a)     (w : ∀ b, ι (I.fstTo b) ≫ I.fst b = ι (I.sndTo b) ≫ I.snd b) : Multifork I where   pt := P   π :=     { app := fun x =>         match x with         | WalkingMulticospan.left a => ι _         | WalkingMulticospan.right b => ι (I.fstTo b) ≫ I.fst b       naturality := by         rintro (_ | _) (_ | _) (_ | _ | _) <;>           dsimp <;> simp         apply w }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Multifork.IsLimit..fullDefinition: def IsLimit.mk (lift : ∀ E : Multifork I, E.pt ⟶ K.pt)     (fac : ∀ (E : Multifork I) (i : I.L), lift E ≫ K.ι i = E.ι i)     (uniq : ∀ (E : Multifork I) (m : E.pt ⟶ K.pt), (∀ i : I.L, m ≫ K.ι i = E.ι i) → m = lift E) :     IsLimit K :=   { lift     fac := by       rintro E (a | b)       · apply fac       · rw [← E.w (WalkingMulticospan.Hom.fst b), ← K.w (WalkingMulticospan.Hom.fst b), ←           Category.assoc]         congr 1         apply fac     uniq := by       rintro E m hm       apply uniq       intro i       apply hm }

CategoryTheory.Limits.MulticospanIndex.m.comment:
The category of multiforks is equivalent to the category of forks over `∏ᶜ I.left ⇉ ∏ᶜ I.right`.
It then follows from `CategoryTheory.IsLimit.ofPreservesConeTerminal` (or `reflects`) that it
preserves and reflects limit cones.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Multicofork.IsColi.fullDefinition: def IsColimit.mk (desc : ∀ E : Multicofork I, K.pt ⟶ E.pt)     (fac : ∀ (E : Multicofork I) (i : I.R), K.π i ≫ desc E = E.π i)     (uniq : ∀ (E : Multicofork I) (m : K.pt ⟶ E.pt), (∀ i : I.R, K.π i ≫ m = E.π i) → m = desc E) :     IsColimit K :=   { desc     fac := by       rintro S (a | b)       · rw [← K.w (WalkingMultispan.Hom.fst a), ← S.w (WalkingMultispan.Hom.fst a),           Category.assoc]         congr 1         apply fac       · apply fac     uniq := by       intro S m hm       apply uniq       intro i       apply hm }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Multicofork.ofSigm.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofSigmaCofork (c : Cofork I.fstSigmaMap I.sndSigmaMap) : Multicofork I where   pt := c.pt   ι :=     { app := fun x =>         match x with         | WalkingMultispan.left a => (Sigma.ι I.left a : _) ≫ I.fstSigmaMap ≫ c.π         | WalkingMultispan.right b => (Sigma.ι I.right b : _) ≫ c.π       naturality := by         rintro (_ | _) (_ | _) (_ | _ | _)         · simp         · simp         · simp [c.condition]         · simp }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Multicofork.ofSigm.description: The definition outlines a method for constructing a multicofork from a given cofork defined over the coproducts of two parts of a multispan index.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Multicofork.ofSigmaCofork_ι_app_left.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]

  (a : I.L) : (ofSigmaCofork I c).ι.app (WalkingMultispan.left a) = Sigma.ι I.left a ≫ I.fstSigmaMap ≫ c.π

CategoryTheory.Limits.MultispanIndex.mul.comment:
The category of multicoforks is equivalent to the category of coforks over `∐ I.left ⇉ ∐ I.right`.
It then follows from `CategoryTheory.IsColimit.ofPreservesCoconeInitial` (or `reflects`) that
it preserves and reflects colimit cocones.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.desc: This definition states that a set of morphisms from each component of a coproduct to a common object induces a morphism from the coproduct itself to that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.MultispanIndex.fst: This definition specifies a morphism that connects the coproduct of elements from the left side of a multispan index to the coproduct of elements from the right side of the same index.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms into a limit cone yield the same results when composed with the projection morphisms from the cone, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.hom_ext: This theorem asserts that if two morphisms to the limit of a functor yield the same results when composed with the canonical projections, then those two morphisms are equal.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork: A cofork on two morphisms in a category represents a structure that captures the notion of a cocone over the parallel pair formed by those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms from the colimit of a functor to an object are equal when composed with the canonical morphisms from the colimit, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.MultispanIndex.toS: This definition establishes a functor that maps a multicofork structure, derived from a given multispan index, to a corresponding cofork structure defined by the specified morphisms in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.MultispanIndex.ofS: The defined functor establishes a systematic transformation from a specific type of cocone relating to coproducts into a structured multicofork representation associated with a given multispan index.

  (I : MulticospanIndex C) [HasMultiequalizer I] [HasProduct I.left] [HasProduct I.right] :
  isoEqualizer I =
    limit.isoLimitCone
      { cone := I.multiforkEquivPiFork.inverse.obj (limit.cone (parallelPair I.fstPiMap I.sndPiMap)),
        isLimit :=
          IsLimit.ofPreservesConeTerminal I.multiforkEquivPiFork.inverse
            (limit.isLimit (parallelPair I.fstPiMap I.sndPiMap)) }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Multicoequalizer.isoCoequalizer.eq_1.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (I : MultispanIndex C) [HasMulticoequalizer I] [HasCoproduct I.left] [HasCoproduct I.right] :
  isoCoequalizer I =
    colimit.isoColimitCocone
      { cocone := I.multicoforkEquivSigmaCofork.inverse.obj (colimit.cocone (parallelPair I.fstSigmaMap I.sndSigmaMap)),
        isColimit :=
          IsColimit.ofPreservesCoconeInitial I.multicoforkEquivSigmaCofork.inverse
            (colimit.isColimit (parallelPair I.fstSigmaMap I.sndSigmaMap)) }

CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingCospan.ext.fullDefinition: def WalkingCospan.ext {F : WalkingCospan ⥤ C} {s t : Cone F} (i : s.pt ≅ t.pt)     (w₁ : s.π.app WalkingCospan.left = i.hom ≫ t.π.app WalkingCospan.left)     (w₂ : s.π.app WalkingCospan.right = i.hom ≫ t.π.app WalkingCospan.right) : s ≅ t := by   apply Cones.ext i _   rintro (⟨⟩ | ⟨⟨⟩⟩)   · have h₁ := s.π.naturality WalkingCospan.Hom.inl     dsimp at h₁     simp only [Category.id_comp] at h₁     have h₂ := t.π.naturality WalkingCospan.Hom.inl     dsimp at h₂     simp only [Category.id_comp] at h₂     simp_rw [h₂, ← Category.assoc, ← w₁, ← h₁]   · exact w₁   · exact w₂

CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim.fullDefinition: def isLimitAux (t : PullbackCone f g) (lift : ∀ s : PullbackCone f g, s.pt ⟶ t.pt)     (fac_left : ∀ s : PullbackCone f g, lift s ≫ t.fst = s.fst)     (fac_right : ∀ s : PullbackCone f g, lift s ≫ t.snd = s.snd)     (uniq : ∀ (s : PullbackCone f g) (m : s.pt ⟶ t.pt)       (_ : ∀ j : WalkingCospan, m ≫ t.π.app j = s.π.app j), m = lift s) : IsLimit t :=   { lift     fac := fun s j => Option.casesOn j (by         rw [← s.w inl, ← t.w inl, ← Category.assoc]         congr         exact fac_left s)       fun j' => WalkingPair.casesOn j' (fac_left s) (fac_right s)     uniq := uniq }

  IsLimit t

CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Z}
  {g : Y ⟶ Z} {t : PullbackCone f g} (ht : IsLimit t) {W : C} (h : W ⟶ X) (k : W ⟶ Y) (w : h ≫ f = k ≫ g) : W ⟶ t.pt
CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim.comment:
If `t` is a limit pullback cone over `f` and `g` and `h : W ⟶ X` and `k : W ⟶ Y` are such that
`h ≫ f = k ≫ g`, then we get `l : W ⟶ t.pt`, which satisfies `l ≫ fst t = h`
and `l ≫ snd t = k`, see `IsLimit.lift_fst` and `IsLimit.lift_snd`.

which you may find to be an easier way of achieving your goal.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo.fullDefinition: def isColimitAux (t : PushoutCocone f g) (desc : ∀ s : PushoutCocone f g, t.pt ⟶ s.pt)     (fac_left : ∀ s : PushoutCocone f g, t.inl ≫ desc s = s.inl)     (fac_right : ∀ s : PushoutCocone f g, t.inr ≫ desc s = s.inr)     (uniq : ∀ (s : PushoutCocone f g) (m : t.pt ⟶ s.pt)     (_ : ∀ j : WalkingSpan, t.ι.app j ≫ m = s.ι.app j), m = desc s) : IsColimit t :=   { desc     fac := fun s j =>       Option.casesOn j (by simp [← s.w fst, ← t.w fst, fac_left s]) fun j' =>         WalkingPair.casesOn j' (fac_left s) (fac_right s)     uniq := uniq }
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo.description: This definition provides a streamlined approach to establish that a given pushout cocone is a colimit by requiring only essential proofs related to its structure and mappings.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isColimitAux'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Y}
  {g : X ⟶ Z} (t : PushoutCocone f g)
  (create :
    (s : PushoutCocone f g) →
      { l //
        t.inl ≫ l = s.inl ∧ t.inr ≫ l = s.inr ∧ ∀ {m : t.pt ⟶ s.pt}, t.inl ≫ m = s.inl → t.inr ≫ m = s.inr → m = l }) :
  IsColimit t

  (uniq : ∀ (s : PushoutCocone f g) (m : W ⟶ s.pt), inl ≫ m = s.inl → inr ≫ m = s.inr → m = desc s) :
  IsColimit (mk inl inr eq)
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.IsCo.comment:

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo.fullDefinition: def isColimitOfFlip (ht : IsColimit t.flip) : IsColimit t :=   IsColimit.ofIsoColimit (flipIsColimit ht) t.flipFlipIso
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo.description: If flipping a pushout cocone results in a colimit cocone, then the original pushout cocone is also a colimit cocone.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ofPushoutCo.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ofPushoutCocone.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C}
  (t : PushoutCocone (F.map fst) (F.map snd)) : Cocone F
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ofPushoutCo.comment:
This is a helper construction that can be useful when verifying that a category has all
pushout. Given `F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C`, which is really the same as
`span (F.map fst) (F.map snd)`, and a pushout cocone on `F.map fst` and `F.map snd`,
we get a cocone on `F`.

If you're thinking about using this, have a look at `hasPushouts_of_hasColimit_span`, which
you may find to be an easier way of achieving your goal.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.pt: This definition specifies the specific object in a category that serves as the cone point for a given cone associated with a functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingCospan.one: This definition identifies the central point of the diagram used to describe a pullback in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone: A pushout cocone is defined as a cocone on the diagram formed by two morphisms from a common object to two distinct objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.pt: This definition specifies the specific object in a category that serves as the cocone point for a given cocone associated with a functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ι: This definition describes a natural transformation from a functor to a constant functor at a specified point in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingSpan: This definition specifies a type representing the objects of a diagram that indexes a pushout, which is a specific instance of a wide pushout shape.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.diagramIsoSpan: This definition states that any functor from a walking span to a category can be uniquely identified with a span formed by mapping the functor's arrows.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ofPushoutCo.fullDefinition: def Cocone.ofPushoutCocone {F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C} (t : PushoutCocone (F.map fst) (F.map snd)) :     Cocone F where   pt := t.pt   ι := (diagramIsoSpan F).hom ≫ t.ι
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ofPushoutCo.description: A pushout cocone for two morphisms induces a cocone over the corresponding span formed by these morphisms in the category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ofCo.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ofCocone.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C}
  (t : Cocone F) : PushoutCocone (F.map fst) (F.map snd)
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ofCo.comment:
Given `F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C`, which is really the same as `span (F.map fst) (F.map snd)`,
and a cocone on `F`, we get a pushout cocone on `F.map fst` and `F.map snd`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ofCo.fullDefinition: def PushoutCocone.ofCocone {F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C} (t : Cocone F) :     PushoutCocone (F.map fst) (F.map snd) where   pt := t.pt   ι := (diagramIsoSpan F).inv ≫ t.ι
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ofCo.description: This definition establishes a relationship where a cocone over a span produces a pushout cocone over the images of the objects in that span.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isoM.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isoMk.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C} (t : Cocone F) :
  (Cocones.precompose (diagramIsoSpan F).inv).obj t ≅
    PushoutCocone.mk (t.ι.app WalkingSpan.left) (t.ι.app WalkingSpan.right) ⋯
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isoM.comment:
A diagram `WalkingSpan ⥤ C` is isomorphic to some `PushoutCocone.mk` after composing with
`diagramIsoSpan`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingCospan.one: This definition identifies the central point of the diagram used to describe a pullback in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.mk: A pullback cone for two morphisms is created by two morphisms from a common object that satisfy a specific compatibility condition with respect to the given morphisms.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingPair.left: This theorem identifies one element of the structured pair in a category theory context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingPair.right: This theorem identifies another element of the structured pair in a category theory context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingCospan.ext: This definition establishes that an isomorphism between points of two cones over a walking cospan suffices if it also preserves the relationships with the respective morphisms to the left and right points.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.ext: An isomorphism between two pullback cones can be established by providing an isomorphism between their cone points and verifying that it respects the first and second projections.
explanatories.And.left: From a conjunction of two propositions, it is possible to extract and prove the first proposition.
explanatories.And.right: This theorem allows for the extraction of the second component from a conjunction when given a proof of that conjunction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: A construction is provided to demonstrate that a specific pullback cone is a limit cone by specifying its projections, a lifting function, and properties that ensure it uniquely determines morphisms consistent with the cone structure.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isoMk: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a diagram represented by a cospan and a specific pullback cone constructed from the morphisms in that diagram after an appropriate transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.mk: A pushout cocone for two morphisms is created by specifying morphisms from each of the source objects to a common object that respect a compatibility condition involving the original morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingSpan: This definition specifies a type representing the objects of a diagram that indexes a pushout, which is a specific instance of a wide pushout shape.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingSpan.ext: This definition states that an isomorphism between two cocones over the walking span can be established by providing an isomorphism between their apex points and verifying that it preserves the structure of the morphisms from the left and right points.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ext: An isomorphism between two pushout cocones can be established if there is an isomorphism between their points that preserves the structure of the morphisms corresponding to the pushout.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.IsCo: This definition provides the conditions under which a specific constructed pushout cocone is a colimit cocone, based on morphisms and factors relating to the original morphisms involved.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.precompose: This definition establishes a functor that allows for the transformation of a cocone over one functor into a corresponding cocone over another functor via a natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isoM.fullDefinition: def PushoutCocone.isoMk {F : WalkingSpan ⥤ C} (t : Cocone F) :     (Cocones.precompose (diagramIsoSpan.{v} _).inv).obj t ≅       PushoutCocone.mk (t.ι.app WalkingSpan.left) (t.ι.app WalkingSpan.right)         ((t.ι.naturality fst).trans (t.ι.naturality snd).symm) :=   Cocones.ext (Iso.refl _) <| by     rintro (_ | (_ | _)) <;>       · dsimp         simp
CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isoM.description: This definition states that a cocone for a diagram represented by the walking span can be transformed into an isomorphism with a pushout cocone after applying a specific functorial adjustment.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift'.fullDefinition: def pullback.lift' {W X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Z} {g : Y ⟶ Z} [HasPullback f g] (h : W ⟶ X) (k : W ⟶ Y)     (w : h ≫ f = k ≫ g) :       { l : W ⟶ pullback f g // l ≫ pullback.fst f g = h ∧ l ≫ pullback.snd f g = k } :=   ⟨pullback.lift h k w, pullback.lift_fst _ _ _, pullback.lift_snd _ _ _⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift'.description: This definition establishes that for a pair of morphisms from an object to a common target, if certain conditions are satisfied, there exists a unique morphism from the constructed pullback object to fulfill the specified compositions with the original morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.desc'.comment:

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.desc'.fullDefinition: def pullback.desc' {W X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : X ⟶ Z} [HasPushout f g] (h : Y ⟶ W) (k : Z ⟶ W)     (w : f ≫ h = g ≫ k) :       { l : pushout f g ⟶ W // pushout.inl _ _ ≫ l = h ∧ pushout.inr _ _ ≫ l = k } :=   ⟨pushout.desc h k w, pushout.inl_desc _ _ _, pushout.inr_desc _ _ _⟩

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.map.fullDefinition: abbrev pullback.map {W X Y Z S T : C} (f₁ : W ⟶ S) (f₂ : X ⟶ S) [HasPullback f₁ f₂] (g₁ : Y ⟶ T)     (g₂ : Z ⟶ T) [HasPullback g₁ g₂] (i₁ : W ⟶ Y) (i₂ : X ⟶ Z) (i₃ : S ⟶ T)     (eq₁ : f₁ ≫ i₃ = i₁ ≫ g₁) (eq₂ : f₂ ≫ i₃ = i₂ ≫ g₂) : pullback f₁ f₂ ⟶ pullback g₁ g₂ :=   pullback.lift (pullback.fst f₁ f₂ ≫ i₁) (pullback.snd f₁ f₂ ≫ i₂)     (by simp only [Category.assoc, ← eq₁, ← eq₂, pullback.condition_assoc])

CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.map_isIso.fullDefinition: instance pushout.map_isIso {W X Y Z S T : C} (f₁ : S ⟶ W) (f₂ : S ⟶ X) [HasPushout f₁ f₂]     (g₁ : T ⟶ Y) (g₂ : T ⟶ Z) [HasPushout g₁ g₂] (i₁ : W ⟶ Y) (i₂ : X ⟶ Z) (i₃ : S ⟶ T)     (eq₁ : f₁ ≫ i₁ = i₃ ≫ g₁) (eq₂ : f₂ ≫ i₂ = i₃ ≫ g₂) [IsIso i₁] [IsIso i₂] [IsIso i₃] :     IsIso (pushout.map f₁ f₂ g₁ g₂ i₁ i₂ i₃ eq₁ eq₂) := by   refine ⟨⟨pushout.map _ _ _ _ (inv i₁) (inv i₂) (inv i₃) ?_ ?_, ?_, ?_⟩⟩   · rw [IsIso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, eq₁, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc]   · rw [IsIso.comp_inv_eq, Category.assoc, eq₂, IsIso.inv_hom_id_assoc]   · aesop_cat   · aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.map_isIso.description: This definition establishes that the canonical morphism resulting from the pushout of two pairs of morphisms is an isomorphism under certain conditions involving the morphisms and their compositions.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.mapDesc_c.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.mapDesc_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y S T S' : C} (f : X ⟶ T)
  (g : Y ⟶ T) (i : T ⟶ S) (i' : S ⟶ S') [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback (f ≫ i) (g ≫ i)]
  [HasPullback (f ≫ i ≫ i') (g ≫ i ≫ i')] [HasPullback ((f ≫ i) ≫ i') ((g ≫ i) ≫ i')] :
  pullback.mapDesc f g (i ≫ i') =
    pullback.mapDesc f g i ≫ pullback.mapDesc (f ≫ i) (g ≫ i) i' ≫ (pullback.congrHom ⋯ ⋯).hom

CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.congrHom.fullDefinition: def pushout.congrHom {X Y Z : C} {f₁ f₂ : X ⟶ Y} {g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Z} (h₁ : f₁ = f₂) (h₂ : g₁ = g₂)     [HasPushout f₁ g₁] [HasPushout f₂ g₂] : pushout f₁ g₁ ≅ pushout f₂ g₂ :=   asIso <| pushout.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (by simp [h₁]) (by simp [h₂])

CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.mapLift_co.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.mapLift_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y S T S' : C} (f : T ⟶ X)
  (g : T ⟶ Y) (i : S ⟶ T) (i' : S' ⟶ S) [HasPushout f g] [HasPushout (i ≫ f) (i ≫ g)]
  [HasPushout (i' ≫ i ≫ f) (i' ≫ i ≫ g)] [HasPushout ((i' ≫ i) ≫ f) ((i' ≫ i) ≫ g)] :
  pushout.mapLift f g (i' ≫ i) = (pushout.congrHom ⋯ ⋯).hom ≫ pushout.mapLift (i ≫ f) (i ≫ g) i' ≫ pushout.mapLift f g i

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.snd: The second projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the second object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.condi: The theorem asserts that in a pullback cone, the composition of the first projection with its associated morphism matches the composition of the second projection with the other morphism in the cospan.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.cond: The theorem states that, in the context of a pushout cocone, the composition of the first morphism with the left inclusion is equal to the composition of the second morphism with the right inclusion.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.condition: This theorem states that the composition of the first morphism with the first inclusion of the pushout equals the composition of the second morphism with the second inclusion of the pushout, establishing a crucial condition for the pushout's universality.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.map: This definition establishes a morphism from the pushout of one pair of morphisms to the pushout of another pair, given compatible mappings between the corresponding objects.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackComparison.fullDefinition: def pullbackComparison (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback (G.map f) (G.map g)] :     G.obj (pullback f g) ⟶ pullback (G.map f) (G.map g) :=   pullback.lift (G.map (pullback.fst f g)) (G.map (pullback.snd f g))     (by simp only [← G.map_comp, pullback.condition])
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackComparison.description: This definition establishes a morphism that relates the pullback of two morphisms in one category to the pullback of their images under a functor in another category, with conditions on the existence of pullbacks in both categories.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackComparison.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackComparison_comp_fst.{v₂, v, u, u₂} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y Z : C}

  [HasPullback (G.map f) (G.map g)] :
  pullbackComparison G f g ≫ pullback.fst (G.map f) (G.map g) = G.map (pullback.fst f g)

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackSymmetry.fullDefinition: def pullbackSymmetry [HasPullback f g] : pullback f g ≅ pullback g f :=   IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso     (PullbackCone.flipIsLimit (pullbackIsPullback f g)) (limit.isLimit _)
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackSymmetry.description: This definition states that the pullback of two morphisms is isomorphic to the pullback of those morphisms in reverse order, reflecting a symmetry in the pullback construction.

CategoryTheory.Limits.bigSquareIsPullback.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X₁ X₂ X₃ Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ : C} (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ X₂)
  (f₂ : X₂ ⟶ X₃) (g₁ : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂) (g₂ : Y₂ ⟶ Y₃) (i₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (i₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) (i₃ : X₃ ⟶ Y₃) (h₁ : i₁ ≫ g₁ = f₁ ≫ i₂)
  (h₂ : i₂ ≫ g₂ = f₂ ≫ i₃) (H : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk i₂ f₂ h₂)) (H' : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk i₁ f₁ h₁)) :
  IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk i₁ (f₁ ≫ f₂) ⋯)
CategoryTheory.Limits.bigSquareIsPullbac.comment:
Given

```
X₁ - f₁ -> X₂ - f₂ -> X₃
|          |          |
i₁         i₂         i₃
↓          ↓          ↓
Y₁ - g₁ -> Y₂ - g₂ -> Y₃
```

Then the big square is a pullback if both the small squares are.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim: This definition describes a condition under which a pullback cone is deemed a limit cone by requiring a specific construction relating to morphisms of the cone to another cone.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: The theorem establishes that if two morphisms from a common source to the point of a pullback cone give the same results when composed with the respective projections, then those two morphisms must be identical.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.cond: The theorem states that, in the context of a pushout cocone, the composition of the first morphism with the left inclusion is equal to the composition of the second morphism with the right inclusion.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.IsCo: If two morphisms from the pushout object to another object agree when composed with both inclusion morphisms, then those two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd: This definition specifies the morphism from the pullback object to one of its original objects, representing the second projection of the pullback for a given pair of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.condition: This theorem states that the composition of the first morphism with the first inclusion of the pushout equals the composition of the second morphism with the second inclusion of the pushout, establishing a crucial condition for the pushout's universality.

CategoryTheory.Limits.bigSquareIsPullbac.fullDefinition: def bigSquareIsPullback (H : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk _ _ h₂))     (H' : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk _ _ h₁)) :     IsLimit       (PullbackCone.mk _ _         (show i₁ ≫ g₁ ≫ g₂ = (f₁ ≫ f₂) ≫ i₃ by           rw [← Category.assoc, h₁, Category.assoc, h₂, Category.assoc])) := by   fapply PullbackCone.isLimitAux'   intro s   have : (s.fst ≫ g₁) ≫ g₂ = s.snd ≫ i₃ := by rw [← s.condition, Category.assoc]   rcases PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift' H (s.fst ≫ g₁) s.snd this with ⟨l₁, hl₁, hl₁'⟩   rcases PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift' H' s.fst l₁ hl₁.symm with ⟨l₂, hl₂, hl₂'⟩   use l₂   use hl₂   use     show l₂ ≫ f₁ ≫ f₂ = s.snd by       rw [← hl₁', ← hl₂', Category.assoc]       rfl   intro m hm₁ hm₂   apply PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext H'   · erw [hm₁, hl₂]   · apply PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext H     · erw [Category.assoc, ← h₁, ← Category.assoc, hm₁, ← hl₂, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, h₁]       rfl     · erw [Category.assoc, hm₂, ← hl₁', ← hl₂']

CategoryTheory.Limits.bigSquareIsPushout.fullDefinition: def bigSquareIsPushout (H : IsColimit (PushoutCocone.mk _ _ h₂))     (H' : IsColimit (PushoutCocone.mk _ _ h₁)) :     IsColimit       (PushoutCocone.mk _ _         (show i₁ ≫ g₁ ≫ g₂ = (f₁ ≫ f₂) ≫ i₃ by           rw [← Category.assoc, h₁, Category.assoc, h₂, Category.assoc])) := by   fapply PushoutCocone.isColimitAux'   intro s   have : i₁ ≫ s.inl = f₁ ≫ f₂ ≫ s.inr := by rw [s.condition, Category.assoc]   rcases PushoutCocone.IsColimit.desc' H' s.inl (f₂ ≫ s.inr) this with ⟨l₁, hl₁, hl₁'⟩   rcases PushoutCocone.IsColimit.desc' H l₁ s.inr hl₁' with ⟨l₂, hl₂, hl₂'⟩   use l₂   use     show (g₁ ≫ g₂) ≫ l₂ = s.inl by       rw [← hl₁, ← hl₂, Category.assoc]       rfl   use hl₂'   intro m hm₁ hm₂   apply PushoutCocone.IsColimit.hom_ext H   · apply PushoutCocone.IsColimit.hom_ext H'     · erw [← Category.assoc, hm₁, hl₂, hl₁]     · erw [← Category.assoc, h₂, Category.assoc, hm₂, ← hl₂', ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, ←         h₂]       rfl   · erw [hm₂, hl₂']
CategoryTheory.Limits.bigSquareIsPushout.description: The definition states that a larger square formed by composing two smaller squares is a pushout if both of the smaller squares are pushouts themselves.

CategoryTheory.Limits.leftSquareIsPullba.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.leftSquareIsPullback.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X₁ X₂ X₃ Y₁ Y₂ Y₃ : C}
  (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ X₂) (f₂ : X₂ ⟶ X₃) (g₁ : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂) (g₂ : Y₂ ⟶ Y₃) (i₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (i₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) (i₃ : X₃ ⟶ Y₃)
  (h₁ : i₁ ≫ g₁ = f₁ ≫ i₂) (h₂ : i₂ ≫ g₂ = f₂ ≫ i₃) (H : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk i₂ f₂ h₂))
  (H' : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk i₁ (f₁ ≫ f₂) ⋯)) : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk i₁ f₁ h₁)
CategoryTheory.Limits.leftSquareIsPullba.comment:
Given

```
X₁ - f₁ -> X₂ - f₂ -> X₃
|          |          |
i₁         i₂         i₃
↓          ↓          ↓
Y₁ - g₁ -> Y₂ - g₂ -> Y₃
```

Then the left square is a pullback if the right square and the big square are.

CategoryTheory.Limits.leftSquareIsPullba.fullDefinition: def leftSquareIsPullback (H : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk _ _ h₂))     (H' :       IsLimit         (PullbackCone.mk _ _           (show i₁ ≫ g₁ ≫ g₂ = (f₁ ≫ f₂) ≫ i₃ by             rw [← Category.assoc, h₁, Category.assoc, h₂, Category.assoc]))) :     IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk _ _ h₁) := by   fapply PullbackCone.isLimitAux'   intro s   have : s.fst ≫ g₁ ≫ g₂ = (s.snd ≫ f₂) ≫ i₃ := by     rw [← Category.assoc, s.condition, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, h₂]   rcases PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift' H' s.fst (s.snd ≫ f₂) this with ⟨l₁, hl₁, hl₁'⟩   use l₁   use hl₁   constructor   · apply PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext H     · erw [Category.assoc, ← h₁, ← Category.assoc, hl₁, s.condition]       rfl     · erw [Category.assoc, hl₁']       rfl   · intro m hm₁ hm₂     apply PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext H'     · erw [hm₁, hl₁]     · erw [hl₁', ← hm₂]       exact (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm
