CategoryTheory.Limits.pushoutPushoutLeftIsPushout.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X₁ X₂ X₃ Z₁ Z₂ : C}
  (g₁ : Z₁ ⟶ X₁) (g₂ : Z₁ ⟶ X₂) (g₃ : Z₂ ⟶ X₂) (g₄ : Z₂ ⟶ X₃) [HasPushout g₁ g₂] [HasPushout g₃ g₄]
  [HasPushout (g₃ ≫ pushout.inr g₁ g₂) g₄] :
  IsColimit
    (PushoutCocone.mk (pushout.inl (g₃ ≫ pushout.inr g₁ g₂) g₄)
      (pushout.desc (pushout.inr g₁ g₂ ≫ pushout.inl (g₃ ≫ pushout.inr g₁ g₂) g₄)
        (pushout.inr (g₃ ≫ pushout.inr g₁ g₂) g₄) ⋯)
      ⋯)
CategoryTheory.Limits.pushoutPushoutLeft.comment: `(X₁ ⨿[Z₁] X₂) ⨿[Z₂] X₃` is the pushout `(X₁ ⨿[Z₁] X₂) ×[X₂] (X₂ ⨿[Z₂] X₃)`.

explanatories.Lean.TSyntax.mk: A syntax node is created from a specified kind and raw syntax input, resulting in a type-safe representation of the syntax.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.mk: A pullback cone for two morphisms is created by two morphisms from a common object that satisfy a specific compatibility condition with respect to the given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.mk: This theorem provides a way to construct a limit cone for a functor by using an existing cone that satisfies the properties of being a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.ext: An isomorphism between two pullback cones can be established by providing an isomorphism between their cone points and verifying that it respects the first and second projections.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPushout: This definition specifies the property of a category having a pushout for a given pair of morphisms from a single object to two target objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.desc: This definition describes how a pair of morphisms from the objects in a pushout to a common object can induce a morphism from the pushout object to that common object, given a specific condition relating the two morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.condition: This theorem states that the composition of the first morphism with the first inclusion of the pushout equals the composition of the second morphism with the second inclusion of the pushout, establishing a crucial condition for the pushout's universality.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.mk: A pushout cocone for two morphisms is created by specifying morphisms from each of the source objects to a common object that respect a compatibility condition involving the original morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.inl_desc: This theorem states that for given morphisms and their related components in a pushout construction, composing the first inclusion with a specified morphism equals that morphism when the appropriate condition involving the pushout is satisfied.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo: If flipping a pushout cocone results in a colimit cocone, then the original pushout cocone is also a colimit cocone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.rightSquareIsPusho: The definition states that the right square formed by certain morphisms is a pushout if both the left square and the larger square are pushouts.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushoutIsPushout: This definition asserts that the cocone formed from the coprojections associated with a pair of morphisms is indeed a pushout in the given category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofIsoCol: This definition states that if a cocone is a colimit and there is an isomorphism between two cocones, then the second cocone is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.flip: This definition states that if a pushout cocone is a colimit, then its corresponding flip version is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ext: An isomorphism between two pushout cocones can be established if there is an isomorphism between their points that preserves the structure of the morphisms corresponding to the pushout.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.ColimitCocone.mk: This theorem constructs a colimit cocone from a given cocone and a proof that this cocone is indeed a colimit.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pushoutPushoutLeft.fullDefinition: def pushoutPushoutLeftIsPushout [HasPushout (g₃ ≫ f₂) g₄] :     IsColimit       (PushoutCocone.mk l₁' l₂' (show f₂ ≫ l₁' = f₃ ≫ l₂' from (pushout.inl_desc _ _ _).symm)) := by   apply PushoutCocone.isColimitOfFlip   apply rightSquareIsPushout   · apply PushoutCocone.isColimitOfFlip     exact pushoutIsPushout g₃ g₄   · exact IsColimit.ofIsoColimit (PushoutCocone.flipIsColimit (pushoutIsPushout (g₃ ≫ f₂) g₄))       (PushoutCocone.ext (Iso.refl _) (by simp) (by simp))   · exact pushout.condition.symm
CategoryTheory.Limits.pushoutPushoutLeft.description: This definition asserts that a specific cocone formed from certain morphisms in a category is a colimit for the pushout diagram created from two distinct pushout constructions.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pushoutAssocIsPush.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.pushoutAssocIsPushout.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X₁ X₂ X₃ Z₁ Z₂ : C} (g₁ : Z₁ ⟶ X₁)
  (g₂ : Z₁ ⟶ X₂) (g₃ : Z₂ ⟶ X₂) (g₄ : Z₂ ⟶ X₃) [HasPushout g₁ g₂] [HasPushout g₃ g₄]
  [HasPushout (g₃ ≫ pushout.inr g₁ g₂) g₄] :
  IsColimit

CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim.comment:
Suppose `f` and `g` are two morphisms with a common codomain and `s` is a limit cone over the
diagram formed by `f` and `g`. Suppose `f` and `g` both factor through a monomorphism `h` via
`x` and `y`, respectively.  Then `s` is also a limit cone over the diagram formed by `x` and
`y`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim.fullDefinition: def isLimitOfFactors (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : W ⟶ Z) [Mono h] (x : X ⟶ W) (y : Y ⟶ W)     (hxh : x ≫ h = f) (hyh : y ≫ h = g) (s : PullbackCone f g) (hs : IsLimit s) :     IsLimit       (PullbackCone.mk _ _         (show s.fst ≫ x = s.snd ≫ y from           (cancel_mono h).1 <| by simp only [Category.assoc, hxh, hyh, s.condition])) :=   PullbackCone.isLimitAux' _ fun t =>     have : fst t ≫ x ≫ h = snd t ≫ y ≫ h := by  -- Porting note: reassoc workaround       rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc]       apply congrArg (· ≫ h) t.condition     ⟨hs.lift (PullbackCone.mk t.fst t.snd <| by rw [← hxh, ← hyh, this]),       ⟨hs.fac _ WalkingCospan.left, hs.fac _ WalkingCospan.right, fun hr hr' => by         apply PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext hs <;>               simp only [PullbackCone.mk_fst, PullbackCone.mk_snd] at hr hr' ⊢ <;>             simp only [hr, hr'] <;>           symm         exacts [hs.fac _ WalkingCospan.left, hs.fac _ WalkingCospan.right]⟩⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim.description: If two morphisms factor through a monomorphism and a limit cone exists for these morphisms, then that limit cone also serves as a limit for the morphisms formed from the factors.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim.fullDefinition: def isLimitOfCompMono (f : X ⟶ W) (g : Y ⟶ W) (i : W ⟶ Z) [Mono i] (s : PullbackCone f g)     (H : IsLimit s) :     IsLimit       (PullbackCone.mk _ _         (show s.fst ≫ f ≫ i = s.snd ≫ g ≫ i by           rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, s.condition])) := by   apply PullbackCone.isLimitAux'   intro s   rcases PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift' H s.fst s.snd       ((cancel_mono i).mp (by simpa using s.condition)) with     ⟨l, h₁, h₂⟩   refine ⟨l, h₁, h₂, ?_⟩   intro m hm₁ hm₂   exact (PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext H (hm₁.trans h₁.symm) (hm₂.trans h₂.symm) : _)

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo.comment:
Suppose `f` and `g` are two morphisms with a common domain and `s` is a colimit cocone over the
diagram formed by `f` and `g`. Suppose `f` and `g` both factor through an epimorphism `h` via
`x` and `y`, respectively. Then `s` is also a colimit cocone over the diagram formed by `x` and
`y`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.isCo.fullDefinition: def isColimitOfFactors (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : X ⟶ Z) (h : X ⟶ W) [Epi h] (x : W ⟶ Y) (y : W ⟶ Z)     (hhx : h ≫ x = f) (hhy : h ≫ y = g) (s : PushoutCocone f g) (hs : IsColimit s) :     have reassoc₁ : h ≫ x ≫ inl s = f ≫ inl s := by  -- Porting note: working around reassoc       rw [← Category.assoc]; apply congrArg (· ≫ inl s) hhx     have reassoc₂ : h ≫ y ≫ inr s = g ≫ inr s := by       rw [← Category.assoc]; apply congrArg (· ≫ inr s) hhy     IsColimit (PushoutCocone.mk _ _ (show x ≫ s.inl = y ≫ s.inr from           (cancel_epi h).1 <| by rw [reassoc₁, reassoc₂, s.condition])) :=   PushoutCocone.isColimitAux' _ fun t => ⟨hs.desc (PushoutCocone.mk t.inl t.inr <| by     rw [← hhx, ← hhy, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, t.condition]),       ⟨hs.fac _ WalkingSpan.left, hs.fac _ WalkingSpan.right, fun hr hr' => by         apply PushoutCocone.IsColimit.hom_ext hs         · simp only [PushoutCocone.mk_inl, PushoutCocone.mk_inr] at hr hr' ⊢           simp only [hr, hr']           symm           exact hs.fac _ WalkingSpan.left         · simp only [PushoutCocone.mk_inl, PushoutCocone.mk_inr] at hr hr' ⊢           simp only [hr, hr']           symm           exact hs.fac _ WalkingSpan.right⟩⟩

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.mk: This theorem provides a way to construct a commutative square from a condition that equates the compositions of specific morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.mk: A pullback cone for two morphisms is created by two morphisms from a common object that satisfy a specific compatibility condition with respect to the given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.mk: A pushout cocone for two morphisms is created by specifying morphisms from each of the source objects to a common object that respect a compatibility condition involving the original morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.fst: The first projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the first object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.snd: The second projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the second object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst: This definition describes the first projection map from the pullback object associated with a pair of morphisms to the first object of one of the morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.snd: This definition specifies the morphism from the pullback object to one of its original objects, representing the second projection of the pullback for a given pair of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal: This definition characterizes an object as terminal if it induces a limiting cone for the empty diagram in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryFan.fst: This definition describes the first projection morphism from a binary fan structure to the left element of a structured pair within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryFan.snd: This definition describes the second projection mapping from a binary fan to the right component of a pair in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsTerminal.from: This definition provides a morphism from any object in a category to a terminal object based on the property of that object being terminal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryFan.mk: This definition constructs a binary fan with a specified vertex and two morphisms projecting to its components in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.fst: This definition describes a morphism that projects an element from a product of two objects back to its first component.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.snd: This definition describes the projection morphism that extracts the second component from a product of two objects in a categorical setting.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.terminal.from: This definition specifies a morphism from any object in a category to a terminal object within that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.mk: This theorem provides a way to construct a limit cone for a functor by using an existing cone that satisfies the properties of being a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: A construction is provided to demonstrate that a specific pullback cone is a limit cone by specifying its projections, a lifting function, and properties that ensure it uniquely determines morphisms consistent with the cone structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.mk: This definition constructs a binary cofan with a specified vertex and two inclusions from the respective objects into that vertex.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.ColimitCocone.mk: This theorem constructs a colimit cocone from a given cocone and a proof that this cocone is indeed a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.fst: This definition describes the morphism from the cone point of a binary bicone to one of the two objects it connects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.snd: This definition describes a morphism from the cone point of a binary bicone to one of its objects, capturing the connection between the bicone and its components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.fst: This definition specifies the morphism that projects an element from a binary biproduct onto its first component.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.snd: This definition specifies the morphism that maps an element from a binary biproduct to its second component.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimit.mk: This theorem asserts that if a functor has a limit cone, then it is characterized as having a limit in the corresponding category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.mk: This theorem states that given a cocone for a functor, one can construct a colimit for that functor, thus confirming the existence of colimits in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.IsCo: This definition provides the conditions under which a specific constructed pushout cocone is a colimit cocone, based on morphisms and factors relating to the original morphisms involved.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk: This definition provides a framework for verifying that a fork is a limit cone by specifying a lifting morphism and conditions for its uniqueness and compatibility with the morphisms of the fork.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_left.code:
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_left.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasZeroMorphisms C]
  (X : C) : IsPullback 0 0 (𝟙 X) 0
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_left.comment: The square with `0 : 0 ⟶ 0` on the left and `𝟙 X` on the right is a pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_left.description: The zero object in a category with zero morphisms establishes that the square defined by the zero morphism and the identity morphism is a pullback.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_top.code:

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_top.comment: The square with `0 : 0 ⟶ 0` on the top and `𝟙 X` on the bottom is a pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_top.description: The morphisms from the zero object to itself constitute a pullback square with the identity morphism at any object preserved.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_right.code:

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_right.comment: The square with `0 : 0 ⟶ 0` on the right and `𝟙 X` on the left is a pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_right.description: The theorem states that a square formed by the zero morphism and the identity morphism on any object is a pullback in categories that include a zero object and zero morphisms.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_bot.comment: The square with `0 : 0 ⟶ 0` on the bottom and `𝟙 X` on the top is a pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.zero_bot.description: A square having an identity morphism on one side and zero morphisms on the other sides forms a pullback in the category with a zero object.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_vert.comment: Paste two pullback squares "vertically" to obtain another pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_vert.description: Combining two vertical pullback squares yields another valid pullback square for the composed morphisms involved.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz.comment: Paste two pullback squares "horizontally" to obtain another pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz.description: Connecting two pullback squares horizontally produces another pullback square, maintaining the pullback property with respect to the composed morphisms.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_bot.comment:
Given a pullback square assembled from a commuting square on the top and
a pullback square on the bottom, the top square is a pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_bot.description: A pullback structure is established for the top square when it is constructed from a commuting square above and a pullback square below, under specific conditions relating the morphisms involved.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right.comment:
Given a pullback square assembled from a commuting square on the left and
a pullback square on the right, the left square is a pullback square.
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.of_right.description: If there is a pullback square defined by a commuting square on the left and another pullback square on the right, then the left square also forms a pullback square.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_vert_iff.description: The condition for a morphism to be a pullback can be rephrased in terms of transformed morphisms under certain compositions if a specific diagram satisfies the pullback property.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.paste_horiz_if.description: The characterization of a morphism as a pullback can be rephrased to connect two different partly defined morphisms by a specific composition and preservation of certain properties.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.mk: This theorem provides a way to construct a commutative square from a condition that equates the compositions of specific morphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.mk: A pushout cocone for two morphisms is created by specifying morphisms from each of the source objects to a common object that respect a compatibility condition involving the original morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ext: An isomorphism between two pushout cocones can be established if there is an isomorphism between their points that preserves the structure of the morphisms corresponding to the pushout.

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: A construction is provided to demonstrate that a specific pullback cone is a limit cone by specifying its projections, a lifting function, and properties that ensure it uniquely determines morphisms consistent with the cone structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.cond: The theorem states that, in the context of a pushout cocone, the composition of the first morphism with the left inclusion is equal to the composition of the second morphism with the right inclusion.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.mk: This definition constructs a binary cofan with a specified vertex and two inclusions from the respective objects into that vertex.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.ColimitCocone.mk: This theorem constructs a colimit cocone from a given cocone and a proof that this cocone is indeed a colimit.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.IsCo: This definition provides the conditions under which a specific constructed pushout cocone is a colimit cocone, based on morphisms and factors relating to the original morphisms involved.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ofι: This definition describes how to create a fork, a specific diagram of morphisms, on two given morphisms by providing a morphism that maps into one of the source objects, under the condition that the compositions with both morphisms are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk: This definition provides a framework for verifying that a fork is a limit cone by specifying a lifting morphism and conditions for its uniqueness and compatibility with the morphisms of the fork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.

CategoryTheory.IsPullback.isLimitFork.fullDefinition: noncomputable def IsPullback.isLimitFork (H : IsPullback f f g g') : IsLimit (Fork.ofι f H.w) := by   fapply Fork.IsLimit.mk   · exact fun s => H.isLimit.lift (PullbackCone.mk s.ι s.ι s.condition)   · exact fun s => H.isLimit.fac _ WalkingCospan.left   · intro s m e     apply PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext H.isLimit <;> refine e.trans ?_ <;> symm <;>       exact H.isLimit.fac _ _
CategoryTheory.IsPullback.isLimitFork.description: If two morphisms from a common object form a pullback square, then these morphisms define the relationships in a limit for the equalizer represented by the first morphism.

CategoryTheory.IsPushout.isLimitFork.fullDefinition: noncomputable def IsPushout.isLimitFork (H : IsPushout f f' g g) :     IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ g H.w) := by   fapply Cofork.IsColimit.mk   · exact fun s => H.isColimit.desc (PushoutCocone.mk s.π s.π s.condition)   · exact fun s => H.isColimit.fac _ WalkingSpan.left   · intro s m e     apply PushoutCocone.IsColimit.hom_ext H.isColimit <;> refine e.trans ?_ <;> symm <;>       exact H.isColimit.fac _ _

If the coproduct of `X₁` and `X₂` is disjoint, then given any pullback square

```
Z  ⟶ X₁
↓    ↓
X₂ ⟶ X
```

where `X₁ ⟶ X ← X₂` is a coproduct, then `Z` is initial.

CategoryTheory.equalizerRegular.fullDefinition: instance equalizerRegular (g h : X ⟶ Y) [HasLimit (parallelPair g h)] :     RegularMono (equalizer.ι g h) where   Z := Y   left := g   right := h   w := equalizer.condition g h   isLimit :=     Fork.IsLimit.mk _ (fun s => limit.lift _ s) (by simp) fun s m w => by       apply equalizer.hom_ext       simp [← w]

CategoryTheory.regularOfIsPullbackSndOfR.fullDefinition: def regularOfIsPullbackSndOfRegular {P Q R S : C} {f : P ⟶ Q} {g : P ⟶ R} {h : Q ⟶ S} {k : R ⟶ S}     [hr : RegularMono h] (comm : f ≫ h = g ≫ k) (t : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk _ _ comm)) :     RegularMono g where   Z := hr.Z   left := k ≫ hr.left   right := k ≫ hr.right   w := by     repeat (rw [← Category.assoc, ← eq_whisker comm])     simp only [Category.assoc, hr.w]   isLimit := by     apply Fork.IsLimit.mk' _ _     intro s     have l₁ : (Fork.ι s ≫ k) ≫ RegularMono.left = (Fork.ι s ≫ k) ≫ hr.right := by       rw [Category.assoc, s.condition, Category.assoc]     obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := Fork.IsLimit.lift' hr.isLimit _ l₁     obtain ⟨p, _, hp₂⟩ := PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift' t _ _ hl     refine ⟨p, hp₂, ?_⟩     intro m w     have z : m ≫ g = p ≫ g := w.trans hp₂.symm     apply t.hom_ext     apply (PullbackCone.mk f g comm).equalizer_ext     · erw [← cancel_mono h, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, comm]       simp only [← Category.assoc, eq_whisker z]     · exact z

CategoryTheory.strongMono_of_regularMono.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) strongMono_of_regularMono (f : X ⟶ Y) [RegularMono f] : StrongMono f :=   StrongMono.mk' (by       intro A B z hz u v sq       have : v ≫ (RegularMono.left : Y ⟶ RegularMono.Z f) = v ≫ RegularMono.right := by         apply (cancel_epi z).1         repeat (rw [← Category.assoc, ← eq_whisker sq.w])         simp only [Category.assoc, RegularMono.w]       obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := RegularMono.lift' _ _ this       refine CommSq.HasLift.mk' ⟨t, (cancel_mono f).1 ?_, ht⟩       simp only [Arrow.mk_hom, Arrow.homMk'_left, Category.assoc, ht, sq.w])

CategoryTheory.regularOfIsPushoutSndOfRe.fullDefinition: def regularOfIsPushoutSndOfRegular {P Q R S : C} {f : P ⟶ Q} {g : P ⟶ R} {h : Q ⟶ S} {k : R ⟶ S}     [gr : RegularEpi g] (comm : f ≫ h = g ≫ k) (t : IsColimit (PushoutCocone.mk _ _ comm)) :     RegularEpi h where   W := gr.W   left := gr.left ≫ f   right := gr.right ≫ f   w := by rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, comm]; simp only [← Category.assoc, eq_whisker gr.w]   isColimit := by     apply Cofork.IsColimit.mk' _ _     intro s     have l₁ : gr.left ≫ f ≫ s.π = gr.right ≫ f ≫ s.π := by       rw [← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, s.condition]     obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := Cofork.IsColimit.desc' gr.isColimit (f ≫ Cofork.π s) l₁     obtain ⟨p, hp₁, _⟩ := PushoutCocone.IsColimit.desc' t _ _ hl.symm     refine ⟨p, hp₁, ?_⟩     intro m w     have z := w.trans hp₁.symm     apply t.hom_ext     apply (PushoutCocone.mk _ _ comm).coequalizer_ext     · exact z     · erw [← cancel_epi g, ← Category.assoc, ← eq_whisker comm]       erw [← Category.assoc, ← eq_whisker comm]       dsimp at z; simp only [Category.assoc, z]

CategoryTheory.Limits.hasImageMapOfIsIso.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) hasImageMapOfIsIso {f g : Arrow C} [HasImage f.hom] [HasImage g.hom]     (sq : f ⟶ g) [IsIso sq] : HasImageMap sq :=   HasImageMap.mk     { map := image.lift ((Image.monoFactorisation g.hom).ofArrowIso (inv sq))       map_ι := by         erw [← cancel_mono (inv sq).right, Category.assoc, ← MonoFactorisation.ofArrowIso_m,           image.lift_fac, Category.assoc, ← Comma.comp_right, IsIso.hom_inv_id, Comma.id_right,           Category.comp_id] }

CategoryTheory.Limits.hasStrongEpiImages.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) hasStrongEpiImages_of_hasPullbacks_of_hasEqualizers [HasPullbacks C]     [HasEqualizers C] : HasStrongEpiImages C where   strong_factorThruImage f :=     StrongEpi.mk' fun {A} {B} h h_mono x y sq =>       CommSq.HasLift.mk'         { l :=             image.lift                 { I := pullback h y                   m := pullback.snd h y ≫ image.ι f                   m_mono := mono_comp _ _                   e := pullback.lift _ _ sq.w } ≫               pullback.fst h y           fac_left := by simp only [image.fac_lift_assoc, pullback.lift_fst]           fac_right := by             apply image.ext             simp only [sq.w, Category.assoc, image.fac_lift_assoc, pullback.lift_fst_assoc] }
CategoryTheory.Limits.hasStrongEpiImages.description: A category with images, equalizers, and pullbacks has the property that its images are strong epimorphic images.

CategoryTheory.Limits.image.isoStrongEpi.comment:
If `C` has strong epi mono factorisations, then the image is unique up to isomorphism, in that if
`f` factors as a strong epi followed by a mono, this factorisation is essentially the image
factorisation.

CategoryTheory.Limits.image.isoStrongEpi.fullDefinition: def image.isoStrongEpiMono {I' : C} (e : X ⟶ I') (m : I' ⟶ Y) (comm : e ≫ m = f) [StrongEpi e]     [Mono m] : I' ≅ image f :=   let F : StrongEpiMonoFactorisation f := { I := I', m := m, e := e}   IsImage.isoExt F.toMonoIsImage <| Image.isImage f
CategoryTheory.Limits.image.isoStrongEpi.description: This definition indicates that in a category possessing strong epimorphic and monomorphic factorizations, the image of a morphism is uniquely characterized up to isomorphism by its factorizations.

  HasZeroMorphisms C
CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero.hasZeroMorp.comment:
A category with a zero object has zero morphisms.

It is rarely a good idea to use this. Many categories that have a zero object have zero
morphisms for some other reason, for example from additivity. Library code that uses
`zeroMorphismsOfZeroObject` will then be incompatible with these categories because
the `HasZeroMorphisms` instances will not be definitionally equal. For this reason library
code should generally ask for an instance of `HasZeroMorphisms` separately, even if it already
asks for an instance of `HasZeroObjects`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero.hasZeroMorp.fullDefinition: def IsZero.hasZeroMorphisms {O : C} (hO : IsZero O) : HasZeroMorphisms C where   zero X Y := { zero := hO.from_ X ≫ hO.to_ Y }   zero_comp X {Y Z} f := by     change (hO.from_ X ≫ hO.to_ Y) ≫ f = hO.from_ X ≫ hO.to_ Z     rw [Category.assoc]     congr     apply hO.eq_of_src   comp_zero {X Y} f Z := by     change f ≫ (hO.from_ Y ≫ hO.to_ Z) = hO.from_ X ≫ hO.to_ Z     rw [← Category.assoc]     congr     apply hO.eq_of_tgt

explanatories.funext: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.
explanatories.Prod.ext: If two pairs of elements have equal first components and equal second components, then the pairs themselves are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.functor: This definition introduces a functor that assigns to each pair of objects in a category their binary product, yielding a mapping from the category to itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.isLimit: This definition provides evidence that the cone derived from a functor has the properties of a limit cone in the context of a category that possesses a limit for that functor.
explanatories.IsCompl.symm: The complementary relationship between two elements in a bounded partially ordered set is symmetric.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.functor: This definition asserts that any function mapping from a discrete type to a category yields a functor between the discrete category and that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.natTrans: This definition states that a natural transformation between functors from a discrete category consists of a collection of maps, since the naturality conditions are trivial in this case.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.π: This definition describes a natural transformation from a constant functor at a specific point to another functor, capturing the relationship between a cone and the functor it pertains to.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.productLimit: The definition states that the product limit cone in the category of types corresponds to the type which is the dependent product of a family of types indexed by a given type.
explanatories.Shrink: A shrink refers to a specific representation in a certain type category for a type that is classified as small.
explanatories.equivShrink: There is a noncomputable equivalence between a type deemed small and its corresponding model in a specified type category.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.π: This definition describes a specific morphism associated with a cofork of two parallel morphisms, mapping from a particular object in a diagram to the point of the cofork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer.π: This definition provides a way to obtain the projection morphism from an object to its coequalizer when a coequalizer of two given morphisms exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.cone: This definition describes an arbitrary limit cone as a specific construction associated with a functor in a category that has a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.isLimit: This definition establishes the condition that a limit cone in a category is considered a limit if its cone satisfies the appropriate limit properties.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.ConeMorphism.w: This theorem states that the composition of two natural transformations and a morphism between cones yields a commutative triangle involving the relevant cone projections at each object in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.pt: This definition specifies the specific object in a category that serves as the cone point for a given cone associated with a functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.CoconeMorphism.w: This theorem states that for any cocone morphism between two cocones over the same functor, the corresponding structure maps produce a commutative diagram.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Small.produc.fullDefinition: noncomputable def productLimitCone :     Limits.LimitCone (Discrete.functor F) where   cone :=     { pt := Shrink (∀ j, F j)       π := Discrete.natTrans (fun ⟨j⟩ f => (equivShrink (∀ j, F j)).symm f j) }   isLimit :=     have : Small.{u} (∀ j, F j) := inferInstance     { lift := fun s x => (equivShrink _) (fun j => s.π.app ⟨j⟩ x)       uniq := fun s m w => funext fun x => Shrink.ext <| funext fun j => by         simpa using (congr_fun (w ⟨j⟩) x : _) }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Small.produc.description: The definition introduces a limit cone for a functor that is constrained to small categories, serving as a specialized version of the product limit cone.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.typeEqualize.fullDefinition: noncomputable def typeEqualizerOfUnique (t : ∀ y : Y, g y = h y → ∃! x : X, f x = y) :     IsLimit (Fork.ofι _ w) :=   Fork.IsLimit.mk' _ fun s => by     refine ⟨fun i => ?_, ?_, ?_⟩     · apply Classical.choose (t (s.ι i) _)       apply congr_fun s.condition i     · funext i       exact (Classical.choose_spec (t (s.ι i) (congr_fun s.condition i))).1     · intro m hm       funext i       exact (Classical.choose_spec (t (s.ι i) (congr_fun s.condition i))).2 _ (congr_fun hm i)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.typeEqualize.description: The definition states that under certain conditions, the specified fork in the category of types acts as an equalizer, indicating that every element that satisfies the equalizing condition originates from the first type.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.equalizerLim.fullDefinition: def equalizerLimit : Limits.LimitCone (parallelPair g h) where   cone := Fork.ofι (Subtype.val : { x : Y // g x = h x } → Y) (funext Subtype.prop)   isLimit :=     Fork.IsLimit.mk' _ fun s =>       ⟨fun i => ⟨s.ι i, by apply congr_fun s.condition i⟩, rfl, fun hm =>         funext fun x => Subtype.ext (congr_fun hm x)⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.equalizerLim.description: The definition indicates that the subtype consisting of elements for which two morphisms agree serves as the equalizer for the respective pair of morphisms in the category of types.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.equalizerIso.code: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.equalizerIso.{u} {Y Z : Type u} (g h : Y ⟶ Z) : equalizer g h ≅ { x // g x = h x }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.equalizerIso.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equalizerIso : equalizer g h ≅ { x : Y // g x = h x } :=   limit.isoLimitCone equalizerLimit

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.coequalizerC.fullDefinition: def coequalizerColimit : Limits.ColimitCocone (parallelPair f g) where   cocone :=     Cofork.ofπ (Quot.mk (CoequalizerRel f g)) (funext fun x => Quot.sound (CoequalizerRel.Rel x))   isColimit :=     Cofork.IsColimit.mk _       (fun s => Quot.lift s.π         (fun a b (h : CoequalizerRel f g a b) => by           cases h           apply congr_fun s.condition))       (fun s => rfl)       (fun s m hm => funext (fun x => Quot.inductionOn x (congr_fun hm)))

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.coequalizer_preimage_image_eq_of_preimage_eq.{u} {X Y Z : Type u} (f g : X ⟶ Y) (π : Y ⟶ Z)
  (e : f ≫ π = g ≫ π) (h : IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ π e)) (U : Set Y) (H : f ⁻¹' U = g ⁻¹' U) : π ⁻¹' (π '' U) = U
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.coequalizer_.comment:
If `π : Y ⟶ Z` is an equalizer for `(f, g)`, and `U ⊆ Y` such that `f ⁻¹' U = g ⁻¹' U`,
then `π ⁻¹' (π '' U) = U`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.MulticospanIndex.s.fullDefinition: def MulticospanIndex.sectionsEquiv :     I.sections ≃ I.multicospan.sections where   toFun s :=     { val := fun i ↦ match i with         | .left i => s.val i         | .right j => I.fst j (s.val _)       property := by         rintro _ _ (_|_|r)         · rfl         · rfl         · exact (s.property r).symm }   invFun s :=     { val := fun i ↦ s.val (.left i)       property := fun r ↦ (s.property (.fst r)).trans (s.property (.snd r)).symm }   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv s := by     ext (_|r)     · rfl     · exact s.property (.fst r)

CategoryTheory.Limits.isKernelOfComp.fullDefinition: def isKernelOfComp {W : C} (g : Y ⟶ W) (h : X ⟶ W) {c : KernelFork h} (i : IsLimit c)     (hf : c.ι ≫ f = 0) (hfg : f ≫ g = h) : IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι c.ι hf) :=   Fork.IsLimit.mk _ (fun s => i.lift (KernelFork.ofι s.ι (by simp [← hfg])))     (fun s => by simp only [KernelFork.ι_ofι, Fork.IsLimit.lift_ι]) fun s m h => by     apply Fork.IsLimit.hom_ext i; simpa using h

CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift_mono.fullDefinition: instance kernel.lift_mono {W : C} (k : W ⟶ X) (h : k ≫ f = 0) [Mono k] : Mono (kernel.lift f k h) :=   ⟨fun {Z} g g' w => by     replace w := w =≫ kernel.ι f     simp only [Category.assoc, kernel.lift_ι] at w     exact (cancel_mono k).1 w⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift_mono.description: The lifting from the kernel of a morphism in a category is monomorphic if the lifting morphism itself is monomorphic and maps to the zero morphism under composition.

CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift_map.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift_map.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] {X Y Z X' Y' Z' : C}
  (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [HasKernel g] (w : f ≫ g = 0) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : Y' ⟶ Z') [HasKernel g'] (w' : f' ≫ g' = 0)
  (p : X ⟶ X') (q : Y ⟶ Y') (r : Z ⟶ Z') (h₁ : f ≫ q = p ≫ f') (h₂ : g ≫ r = q ≫ g') :
  kernel.lift g f w ≫ kernel.map g g' q r h₂ = p ≫ kernel.lift g' f' w'
CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift_map.comment:
Given a commutative diagram
    X --f--> Y --g--> Z
    |        |        |
    |        |        |
    v        v        v
    X' -f'-> Y' -g'-> Z'
with horizontal arrows composing to zero,
then we obtain a commutative square
   X ---> kernel g
   |         |
   |         | kernel.map
   |         |
   v         v
   X' --> kernel g'

CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitAux.fullDefinition: def isColimitAux (t : CokernelCofork f) (desc : ∀ s : CokernelCofork f, t.pt ⟶ s.pt)     (fac : ∀ s : CokernelCofork f, t.π ≫ desc s = s.π)     (uniq : ∀ (s : CokernelCofork f) (m : t.pt ⟶ s.pt) (_ : t.π ≫ m = s.π), m = desc s) :     IsColimit t :=   { desc     fac := fun s j => by       cases j       · simp       · exact fac s     uniq := fun s m w => uniq s m (w Limits.WalkingParallelPair.one) }

CategoryTheory.Limits.isCokernelEpiComp.fullDefinition: def isCokernelEpiComp {c : CokernelCofork f} (i : IsColimit c) {W} (g : W ⟶ X) [hg : Epi g]     {h : W ⟶ Y} (hh : h = g ≫ f) :     IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ c.π (by rw [hh]; simp) : CokernelCofork h) :=   Cofork.IsColimit.mk' _ fun s =>     let s' : CokernelCofork f :=       Cofork.ofπ s.π         (by           apply hg.left_cancellation           rw [← Category.assoc, ← hh, s.condition]           simp)     let l := CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' i s'.π s'.condition     ⟨l.1, l.2, fun hm => by       apply Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext i; rw [Cofork.π_ofπ] at hm; rw [hm]; exact l.2.symm⟩

CategoryTheory.Limits.isCokernelOfComp.fullDefinition: def isCokernelOfComp {W : C} (g : W ⟶ X) (h : W ⟶ Y) {c : CokernelCofork h} (i : IsColimit c)     (hf : f ≫ c.π = 0) (hfg : g ≫ f = h) : IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ c.π hf) :=   Cofork.IsColimit.mk _ (fun s => i.desc (CokernelCofork.ofπ s.π (by simp [← hfg])))     (fun s => by simp only [CokernelCofork.π_ofπ, Cofork.IsColimit.π_desc]) fun s m h => by       apply Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext i       simpa using h

CategoryTheory.Limits.zeroCokernelOfZero.fullDefinition: def zeroCokernelOfZeroCancel {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y)     (hf : ∀ (Z : C) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (_ : f ≫ g = 0), g = 0) :     IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ (0 : Y ⟶ 0) (show f ≫ 0 = 0 by simp)) :=   Cofork.IsColimit.mk _ (fun s => 0)     (fun s => by rw [hf _ _ (CokernelCofork.condition s), comp_zero]) fun s m _ => by       apply HasZeroObject.from_zero_ext
CategoryTheory.Limits.zeroCokernelOfZero.description: If a morphism implies that any morphism composed with it leads to zero only if that second morphism is itself zero, then the zero morphism is the cokernel of the initial morphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsCokernel.ofIsoCo.fullDefinition: def IsCokernel.ofIsoComp {Z : C} (l : Z ⟶ Y) (i : X ≅ Z) (h : i.hom ≫ l = f) {s : CokernelCofork f}     (hs : IsColimit s) :     IsColimit       (CokernelCofork.ofπ (Cofork.π s) <| show l ≫ Cofork.π s = 0 by simp [i.eq_inv_comp.2 h]) :=   Cofork.IsColimit.mk _ (fun s => hs.desc <| CokernelCofork.ofπ (Cofork.π s) <| by simp [← h])     (fun s => by simp) fun s m h => by       apply Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext hs       simpa using h
CategoryTheory.Limits.IsCokernel.ofIsoCo.description: An isomorphism relating two morphisms ensures that if one morphism has a cokernel, then the other morphism also possesses a corresponding cokernel that is a colimit cocone.

CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelComparison.fullDefinition: def kernelComparison [HasKernel f] [HasKernel (G.map f)] : G.obj (kernel f) ⟶ kernel (G.map f) :=   kernel.lift _ (G.map (kernel.ι f))     (by simp only [← G.map_comp, kernel.condition, Functor.map_zero])
CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelComparison.description: A morphism from the kernel of one object to the kernel of the image of that object under a functor is established, given that both the original and the functor preserve kernels.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.condition: The theorem states that for a given fork formed by two morphisms, the morphism from the fork satisfies the condition that it composed with both morphisms results in the same outcome.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.KernelFork.conditi: In a category, if a kernel fork exists for a morphism, then the composition of the first morphism in the fork with the original morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.π: This definition describes a natural transformation from a constant functor at a specific point to another functor, capturing the relationship between a cone and the functor it pertains to.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp: This statement defines the composition of two functors, where the first functor is applied to an object followed by the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel: The kernel of a morphism is defined as the equalizer of that morphism and the zero morphism in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.condition: The inclusion morphism from the kernel of a morphism into its source maps to zero when composed with the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.map: A morphism between kernels is induced in a category when there is a commuting square that relates two morphisms from the original objects to another set of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.π: This definition describes a specific morphism associated with a cofork of two parallel morphisms, mapping from a particular object in a diagram to the point of the cofork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.condition: This theorem states that for a cofork, the composition of its projection with both morphisms yields the same result, ensuring a specific relationship between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.CokernelCofork.con: The projection morphism from a cokernel cofork, when composed with the original morphism, results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.desc: This definition describes a morphism from the point of a colimit cocone to the point of another cocone, ensuring a connection between their respective structures.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer.π: This definition provides a way to obtain the projection morphism from an object to its coequalizer when a coequalizer of two given morphisms exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.π: The morphism from the target of a given morphism in a category to its cokernel is defined, provided the cokernel exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.condition: The composition of a morphism with its cokernel projection always results in zero when the morphism has a cokernel.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.desc: Any morphism that annihilates another morphism can be factored through the cokernel of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.map: A commuting square between two morphisms leads to a corresponding morphism between their cokernels.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_zero: This theorem establishes that a functor, which preserves zero morphisms, will map the zero morphism from one category to the zero morphism in another category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelComparison: A morphism from the kernel of one object to the kernel of the image of that object under a functor is established, given that both the original and the functor preserve kernels.

CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernelComparison.fullDefinition: def cokernelComparison [HasCokernel f] [HasCokernel (G.map f)] :     cokernel (G.map f) ⟶ G.obj (cokernel f) :=   cokernel.desc _ (G.map (coequalizer.π _ _))     (by simp only [← G.map_comp, cokernel.condition, Functor.map_zero])
CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernelComparison.description: The cokernel comparison morphism provides a way to relate the cokernel of a morphism in one category to the image of that cokernel in another category under a given functor that preserves zero morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.π_comp_cokernelCom.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.π_comp_cokernelComparison.{v, v₂, u, u₂} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C]
  {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (G : C ⥤ D) [G.PreservesZeroMorphisms]
  [HasCokernel f] [HasCokernel (G.map f)] : cokernel.π (G.map f) ≫ cokernelComparison f G = G.map (cokernel.π f)

CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel_map_comp_cokernelComparison.{v, v₂, u, u₂} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [HasZeroMorphisms C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (G : C ⥤ D)
  [G.PreservesZeroMorphisms] {X' Y' : C} [HasCokernel f] [HasCokernel (G.map f)] (g : X' ⟶ Y') [HasCokernel g]
  [HasCokernel (G.map g)] (p : X ⟶ X') (q : Y ⟶ Y') (hpq : f ≫ q = p ≫ g) :
  cokernel.map (G.map f) (G.map g) (G.map p) (G.map q) ⋯ ≫ cokernelComparison g G =
    cokernelComparison f G ≫ G.map (cokernel.map f g p q hpq)

explanatories.Nat.zero: This theorem identifies the smallest natural number as zero, which serves as a constructor for natural numbers.
explanatories.exists_surjective_nat: A non-empty countable type has an associated surjective function to the natural numbers.
explanatories.Exists.choose: An existential statement guarantees the existence of an element satisfying a property, allowing for the extraction of such an element from the statement.
explanatories.Nat.succ: This states the successor function for natural numbers, which yields the next integer by adding one to a given natural number.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsCofilteredOrEmpty.cone_: This theorem states that in a cofiltered or empty category, for any two objects, there exists another object that connects to both in a specified manner.

CategoryTheory.Limits.sequentialFunctor_.fullDefinition: noncomputable def sequentialFunctor_obj : ℕ → J := fun   | .zero => (exists_surjective_nat _).choose 0   | .succ n => (IsCofilteredOrEmpty.cone_objs ((exists_surjective_nat _).choose n)       (sequentialFunctor_obj n)).choose
CategoryTheory.Limits.sequentialFunctor_.description: This defines a functor from the reversed natural numbers to a countably filtered preorder system.

explanatories.Antitone: A function is considered antitone if it reverses the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.sequentialFunctor_: This defines a functor from the reversed natural numbers to a countably filtered preorder system.

CategoryTheory.Limits.sequentialFunctor_.description: The functor defined on the countably ordered category is shown to be antitone, meaning it reverses the order of elements.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.leOfHom: This theorem states that given a morphism in a preorder category, one can derive the corresponding inequality between its source and target elements.
explanatories.Opposite.unop: This definition describes the canonical mapping from the opposite category of a type back to the original type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.homOfLE: This definition converts an inequality between two elements in a preorder into a morphism in the associated category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.sequentialFunctor_: The functor defined on the countably ordered category is shown to be antitone, meaning it reverses the order of elements.

CategoryTheory.Limits.sequentialFunctor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def sequentialFunctor : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ J where   obj n := sequentialFunctor_obj J (unop n)   map h := homOfLE (sequentialFunctor_map J (leOfHom h.unop))
CategoryTheory.Limits.sequentialFunctor.description: The sequential functor from the reversed natural numbers to a countable preorder facilitates the transformation of cofiltered limits into sequential limits.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.ι_π.comment:
A `c : Bicone F` is:
* an object `c.pt` and
* morphisms `π j : pt ⟶ F j` and `ι j : F j ⟶ pt` for each `j`,
* such that `ι j ≫ π j'` is the identity when `j = j'` and zero otherwise.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicones.ext.fullDefinition: def ext {c c' : Bicone F} (φ : c.pt ≅ c'.pt)     (wι : ∀ j, c.ι j ≫ φ.hom = c'.ι j := by aesop_cat)     (wπ : ∀ j, φ.hom ≫ c'.π j = c.π j := by aesop_cat) : c ≅ c' where   hom := { hom := φ.hom }   inv :=     { hom := φ.inv       wι := fun j => φ.comp_inv_eq.mpr (wι j).symm       wπ := fun j => φ.inv_comp_eq.mpr (wπ j).symm  }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicones.functorial.fullDefinition: def functoriality (G : C ⥤ D) [Functor.PreservesZeroMorphisms G] :     Bicone F ⥤ Bicone (G.obj ∘ F) where   obj A :=     { pt := G.obj A.pt       π := fun j => G.map (A.π j)       ι := fun j => G.map (A.ι j)       ι_π := fun i j => (Functor.map_comp _ _ _).symm.trans <| by         rw [A.ι_π]         aesop_cat }   map f :=     { hom := G.map f.hom       wπ := fun j => by simp [-BiconeMorphism.wπ, ← f.wπ j]       wι := fun j => by simp [-BiconeMorphism.wι, ← f.wι j] }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicones.functorial.description: This definition states that a functor from one category to another sends bicones associated with a diagram to bicones associated with the composition of that functor with another diagram, preserving the structure necessary for the transformation.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.whiskerIsBi.fullDefinition: def whiskerIsBilimitIff {f : J → C} (c : Bicone f) (g : K ≃ J) :     (c.whisker g).IsBilimit ≃ c.IsBilimit := by   refine equivOfSubsingletonOfSubsingleton (fun hc => ⟨?_, ?_⟩) fun hc => ⟨?_, ?_⟩   · let this := IsLimit.ofIsoLimit hc.isLimit (Bicone.whiskerToCone c g)     let this := (IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv (Discrete.functorComp f g).symm _) this     exact IsLimit.ofWhiskerEquivalence (Discrete.equivalence g) this   · let this := IsColimit.ofIsoColimit hc.isColimit (Bicone.whiskerToCocone c g)     let this := (IsColimit.precomposeHomEquiv (Discrete.functorComp f g) _) this     exact IsColimit.ofWhiskerEquivalence (Discrete.equivalence g) this   · apply IsLimit.ofIsoLimit _ (Bicone.whiskerToCone c g).symm     apply (IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv (Discrete.functorComp f g).symm _).symm _     exact IsLimit.whiskerEquivalence hc.isLimit (Discrete.equivalence g)   · apply IsColimit.ofIsoColimit _ (Bicone.whiskerToCocone c g).symm     apply (IsColimit.precomposeHomEquiv (Discrete.functorComp f g) _).symm _     exact IsColimit.whiskerEquivalence hc.isColimit (Discrete.equivalence g)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.whiskerIsBi.description: Whiskering a bicone with an equivalence between index types maintains the property of being a bilimit for the bicone.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.lift: This definition states that if a product exists for two objects, then any pair of morphisms from a third object to these two can be combined into a single morphism to the product object.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift_map.description: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of a lift from one biproduct and a map between two biproducts is equal to the lift of the composed morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapIso.{w, v, u} {J : Type w} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C]
  {f g : J → C} [HasBiproduct f] [HasBiproduct g] (p : (b : J) → f b ≅ g b) : ⨁ f ≅ ⨁ g
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapIso.comment:
Given a collection of isomorphisms between corresponding summands of a pair of biproducts
indexed by the same type, we obtain an isomorphism between the biproducts.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BiconeMorphism.hom: This definition describes a morphism connecting the cone points of two bicones within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.map: This definition provides a morphism from the cone point of a cone over one functor to the cone point of a limit cone over another functor, given a natural transformation between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.map: This definition establishes a morphism from the cocone point of a colimit associated with one functor to the cocone point of another cocone associated with a different functor, given a natural transformation between them.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapIso.fullDefinition: def biproduct.mapIso {f g : J → C} [HasBiproduct f] [HasBiproduct g] (p : ∀ b, f b ≅ g b) :     ⨁ f ≅ ⨁ g where   hom := biproduct.map fun b => (p b).hom   inv := biproduct.map fun b => (p b).inv
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapIso.description: This definition asserts that when there are isomorphisms between the corresponding summands of two biproducts, there exists an isomorphism between the biproducts themselves.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.whiskerE.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.whiskerEquiv.{w, v, u, u_1} {J : Type w} {K : Type u_1} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [HasZeroMorphisms C] {f : J → C} {g : K → C} (e : J ≃ K) (w : (j : J) → g (e j) ≅ f j) [HasBiproduct f]
  [HasBiproduct g] : ⨁ f ≅ ⨁ g
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.whiskerE.comment:
Two biproducts which differ by an equivalence in the indexing type,
and up to isomorphism in the factors, are isomorphic.

Unfortunately there are two natural ways to define each direction of this isomorphism
(because it is true for both products and coproducts separately).
We give the alternative definitions as lemmas below.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.ι: This definition describes a function that provides the morphism from a specific object in the diagram associated with a bicone to the cone point of that bicone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BiconeMorphism.hom: This definition describes a morphism connecting the cone points of two bicones within a category.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ι: This definition describes a natural transformation from a functor to a constant functor at a specified point in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.desc: This definition describes a morphism from the point of a colimit cocone to the point of another cocone, ensuring a connection between their respective structures.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι: This definition specifies an inclusion morphism from an individual summand to a biproduct object in the context of category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.desc: This definition specifies that given a collection of morphisms from the summands of a biproduct, there exists a corresponding morphism from the entire biproduct to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.desc: This definition states that a set of morphisms from each component of a coproduct to a common object induces a morphism from the coproduct itself to that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.ι: This definition specifies the morphism that corresponds to the inclusion of an element from a coproduct into the overall coproduct object within a category.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ι: This definition introduces a morphism that connects a given point of a fork on two parallel morphisms to the zero instance of a parallel pair formed by those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coprod.desc: This definition states that if a binary coproduct exists, then any pair of morphisms from two objects to a third object induces a unique morphism from the coproduct to that third object.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.whiskerE.fullDefinition: def biproduct.whiskerEquiv {f : J → C} {g : K → C} (e : J ≃ K) (w : ∀ j, g (e j) ≅ f j)     [HasBiproduct f] [HasBiproduct g] : ⨁ f ≅ ⨁ g where   hom := biproduct.desc fun j => (w j).inv ≫ biproduct.ι g (e j)   inv := biproduct.desc fun k => eqToHom (by simp) ≫ (w (e.symm k)).hom ≫ biproduct.ι f _
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.whiskerE.description: This definition states that two biproducts are isomorphic when there is an equivalence between their indexing types and the morphisms between corresponding factors are also isomorphic.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.isLimitF.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.isLimitFromSubtype.{w, v, u} {J : Type w} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [HasZeroMorphisms C] (f : J → C) (i : J) [HasBiproduct f] [HasBiproduct (Subtype.restrict (fun j => j ≠ i) f)] :
  IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (biproduct.fromSubtype f fun j => j ≠ i) ⋯)
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.isLimitF.comment:
The kernel of `biproduct.π f i` is the inclusion from the biproduct which omits `i`
from the index set `J` into the biproduct over `J`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.isLimitF.fullDefinition: def biproduct.isLimitFromSubtype :     IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (biproduct.fromSubtype f fun j => j ≠ i) (by simp) :     KernelFork (biproduct.π f i)) :=   Fork.IsLimit.mk' _ fun s =>     ⟨s.ι ≫ biproduct.toSubtype _ _, by       apply biproduct.hom_ext; intro j       rw [KernelFork.ι_ofι, Category.assoc, Category.assoc,         biproduct.toSubtype_fromSubtype_assoc, biproduct.map_π]       rcases Classical.em (i = j) with (rfl | h)       · rw [if_neg (Classical.not_not.2 rfl), comp_zero, comp_zero, KernelFork.condition]       · rw [if_pos (Ne.symm h), Category.comp_id], by       intro m hm       rw [← hm, KernelFork.ι_ofι, Category.assoc, biproduct.fromSubtype_toSubtype]       exact (Category.comp_id _).symm⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.isLimitF.description: This definition states that the kernel of the morphism associated with a biproduct projection omitting a specific index is itself a limit of a structure derived from the biproduct that excludes that index.

CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelForkBiproduc.fullDefinition: def kernelForkBiproductToSubtype (p : Set K) :     LimitCone (parallelPair (biproduct.toSubtype f p) 0) where   cone :=     KernelFork.ofι (biproduct.fromSubtype f pᶜ)       (by         ext j k         simp only [Category.assoc, biproduct.ι_fromSubtype_assoc, biproduct.ι_toSubtype_assoc,           comp_zero, zero_comp]         erw [dif_neg k.2]         simp only [zero_comp])   isLimit :=     KernelFork.IsLimit.ofι _ _ (fun {W} g _ => g ≫ biproduct.toSubtype f pᶜ)       (by         intro W' g' w         ext j         simp only [Category.assoc, biproduct.toSubtype_fromSubtype, Pi.compl_apply,           biproduct.map_π]         split_ifs with h         · simp         · replace w := w =≫ biproduct.π _ ⟨j, not_not.mp h⟩           simpa using w.symm)       (by aesop_cat)

  [HasZeroMorphisms C] (f : J → C) [HasBiproduct f] {b : Bicone f} (hb : b.IsBilimit) : b.pt ≅ ⨁ f
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.uniqueUp.comment:
Biproducts are unique up to isomorphism. This already follows because bilimits are limits,
but in the case of biproducts we can give an isomorphism with particularly nice definitional
properties, namely that `biproduct.lift b.π` and `biproduct.desc b.ι` are inverses of each
other.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.uniqueUp.fullDefinition: def biproduct.uniqueUpToIso (f : J → C) [HasBiproduct f] {b : Bicone f} (hb : b.IsBilimit) :     b.pt ≅ ⨁ f where   hom := biproduct.lift b.π   inv := biproduct.desc b.ι   hom_inv_id := by     rw [← biproduct.conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom f hb, ←       biproduct.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv f hb, Iso.hom_inv_id]   inv_hom_id := by     rw [← biproduct.conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom f hb, ←       biproduct.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv f hb, Iso.inv_hom_id]
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.uniqueUp.description: This definition asserts that biproducts in a category are uniquely determined up to isomorphism, providing an isomorphism that relates a bilimit to the biproduct in a way that allows for defining simple inverses between associated morphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroObject.mk: This theorem establishes that the existence of at least one zero object in a category is sufficient to define that category as having a zero object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero.mk: A categorical object is identified as a zero object if there exists a unique morphism to and from any other object in the category.
explanatories.Unique.mk: A unique type can be constructed from an inhabited type and the property that all its elements are equal to the default element.
explanatories.Inhabited.mk: Any type that has a default element is considered inhabited.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limitBiconeOfUniqu: This definition identifies the limit bicone associated with a functor indexed by a type that contains exactly one element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryFan.mk: This definition constructs a binary fan with a specified vertex and two morphisms projecting to its components in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.mk: This definition constructs a binary cofan with a specified vertex and two inclusions from the respective objects into that vertex.

CategoryTheory.Limits.hasBiproduct_uniqu.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) hasBiproduct_unique : HasBiproduct f :=   HasBiproduct.mk (limitBiconeOfUnique f)
CategoryTheory.Limits.hasBiproduct_uniqu.description: This definition establishes that for a uniquely indexed family of objects, the existence of a biproduct structure in a category can be guaranteed.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproductUniqueIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproductUniqueIso.{w, v, u} {J : Type w} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C]
  [Unique J] (f : J → C) : ⨁ f ≅ f default
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproductUniqueIso.comment: A biproduct over an index type with exactly one term is just the object over that term.

explanatories.Lean.Meta.TransparencyMode.default: This establishes a default setting for transparency mode that allows unfolding all constants except those marked as irreducible.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.uniqueUp: This definition asserts that biproducts in a category are uniquely determined up to isomorphism, providing an isomorphism that relates a bilimit to the biproduct in a way that allows for defining simple inverses between associated morphisms.
explanatories.Inhabited.default: This defines a function that generates a default element for any inhabited type, which is a type that has at least one value.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limitBiconeOfUniqu: This definition identifies the limit bicone associated with a functor indexed by a type that contains exactly one element.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproductUniqueIso.fullDefinition: def biproductUniqueIso : ⨁ f ≅ f default :=   (biproduct.uniqueUpToIso _ (limitBiconeOfUnique f).isBilimit).symm
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproductUniqueIso.description: This definition states that for a biproduct indexed by a type with only one element, there exists a unique isomorphism between the biproduct and the object corresponding to that single element.

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.pt.code:

  (self : BinaryBicone P Q) : C
CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.pt.comment:
A binary bicone for a pair of objects `P Q : C` consists of the cone point `X`,
maps from `X` to both `P` and `Q`, and maps from both `P` and `Q` to `X`,
so that `inl ≫ fst = 𝟙 P`, `inl ≫ snd = 0`, `inr ≫ fst = 0`, and `inr ≫ snd = 𝟙 Q`

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicones.ext.fullDefinition: def ext {P Q : C} {c c' : BinaryBicone P Q} (φ : c.pt ≅ c'.pt)     (winl : c.inl ≫ φ.hom = c'.inl := by aesop_cat)     (winr : c.inr ≫ φ.hom = c'.inr := by aesop_cat)     (wfst : φ.hom ≫ c'.fst = c.fst := by aesop_cat)     (wsnd : φ.hom ≫ c'.snd = c.snd := by aesop_cat) : c ≅ c' where   hom := { hom := φ.hom }   inv :=     { hom := φ.inv       wfst := φ.inv_comp_eq.mpr wfst.symm       wsnd := φ.inv_comp_eq.mpr wsnd.symm       winl := φ.comp_inv_eq.mpr winl.symm       winr := φ.comp_inv_eq.mpr winr.symm }

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.toBic.fullDefinition: def toBiconeFunctor {X Y : C} : BinaryBicone X Y ⥤ Bicone (pairFunction X Y) where   obj b :=     { pt := b.pt       π := fun j => WalkingPair.casesOn j b.fst b.snd       ι := fun j => WalkingPair.casesOn j b.inl b.inr       ι_π := fun j j' => by         rcases j with ⟨⟩ <;> rcases j' with ⟨⟩ <;> simp }   map f := {     hom := f.hom     wπ := fun i => WalkingPair.casesOn i f.wfst f.wsnd     wι := fun i => WalkingPair.casesOn i f.winl f.winr }

CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.uniqueUpToI.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.uniqueUpToIso.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] (X Y : C)
  [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y] {b : BinaryBicone X Y} (hb : b.IsBilimit) : b.pt ≅ X ⊞ Y
CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.uniqueUpToI.comment:
Binary biproducts are unique up to isomorphism. This already follows because bilimits are
limits, but in the case of biproducts we can give an isomorphism with particularly nice
definitional properties, namely that `biprod.lift b.fst b.snd` and `biprod.desc b.inl b.inr`
are inverses of each other.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.uniqueUpToI.fullDefinition: def biprod.uniqueUpToIso (X Y : C) [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y] {b : BinaryBicone X Y}     (hb : b.IsBilimit) : b.pt ≅ X ⊞ Y where   hom := biprod.lift b.fst b.snd   inv := biprod.desc b.inl b.inr   hom_inv_id := by     rw [← biprod.conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom X Y hb, ←       biprod.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv X Y hb, Iso.hom_inv_id]   inv_hom_id := by     rw [← biprod.conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom X Y hb, ←       biprod.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv X Y hb, Iso.inv_hom_id]
CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.uniqueUpToI.description: This definition asserts that binary biproducts in a category are unique up to isomorphism, accompanied by a specific isomorphism established through bilimit properties.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ι: This definition describes a natural transformation from a functor to a constant functor at a specified point in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms into a limit cone yield the same results when composed with the projection morphisms from the cone, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that two morphisms from a colimit are equal if they yield the same result when composed with the cocone's morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBiproduct.mk': This theorem states that if there is a nonempty limit bicone for a given functor, then that functor possesses a biproduct in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι: This definition specifies an inclusion morphism from an individual summand to a biproduct object in the context of category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms from an object to a biproduct agree on their compositions with the projection morphisms for all indices, then the morphisms themselves must be identical.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.hom_ext: This theorem asserts that if two morphisms to the limit of a functor yield the same results when composed with the canonical projections, then those two morphisms are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms from the colimit of a functor to an object are equal when composed with the canonical morphisms from the colimit, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.ι: This definition specifies the morphism that corresponds to the inclusion of an element from a coproduct into the overall coproduct object within a category.
explanatories.Sigma.snd: The second component of a dependent pair extracts the value associated with the first element from the pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.KernelFork: A kernel fork in a category is a special type of diagram consisting of a morphism and a zero morphism, where the latter serves as the second component of the fork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.mk': This definition provides a method to confirm that a given fork is a limit cone by requiring a proof of specific relationships involving morphisms from the fork to another structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ι: This definition introduces a morphism that connects a given point of a fork on two parallel morphisms to the zero instance of a parallel pair formed by those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.m: This definition provides a method for demonstrating that a specific cofork is a colimit by requiring the proof of certain relationships among morphisms and allowing reuse of the same structure in multiple parts of the proof.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsSplitMono.mk': This theorem establishes that a split monomorphism implies the existence of a corresponding split monomorphism property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsSplitEpi.mk': This theorem establishes that a morphism is classified as a split epimorphism if it satisfies the condition of being a split epimorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.snd: This definition describes a morphism from the cone point of a binary bicone to one of its objects, capturing the connection between the bicone and its components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicones.ext: This definition establishes that if two binary bicones have isomorphic cone points and their associated morphisms commute with the inclusion and projection maps, then the bicones themselves are isomorphic.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryFan.snd: This definition describes the second projection mapping from a binary fan to the right component of a pair in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproduct: This theorem asserts that the existence of a binary biproduct data structure for two objects in a category guarantees that these objects possess a binary biproduct.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.snd: This definition specifies the morphism that maps an element from a binary biproduct to its second component.
This theorem asserts that if two morphisms to the limit of a binary fan yield the same results when composed with both projections, then the morphisms themselves must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms into a binary biproduct agree on both projection maps, they are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.IsColi: This theorem proves that two morphisms from the point of a binary cofan to another object are equal if they agree on their compositions with the two respective projections of the cofan.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod.snd: This definition describes the projection morphism that extracts the second component from a product of two objects in a categorical setting.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.fstKe: This definition establishes a kernel fork that corresponds to the kernel of the first morphism in a binary bicone, specifically represented by the morphism associated with the second object in the bicone.

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isLim.fullDefinition: def BinaryBicone.isLimitFstKernelFork (i : IsLimit c.toCone) : IsLimit c.fstKernelFork :=   Fork.IsLimit.mk' _ fun s =>     ⟨s.ι ≫ c.snd, by apply BinaryFan.IsLimit.hom_ext i <;> simp, fun hm => by simp [← hm]⟩
CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isLim.description: This definition states that if a binary bicone is a limit, then the associated fork that emerges from the first component of the bicone also qualifies as a limit, confirming its status as a kernel.

CategoryTheory.equivalenceReflectsNormal.fullDefinition: def equivalenceReflectsNormalMono {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} D] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D)     [F.IsEquivalence] {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : NormalMono (F.map f)) : NormalMono f where   Z := F.objPreimage hf.Z   g := F.preimage (hf.g ≫ (F.objObjPreimageIso hf.Z).inv)   w := F.map_injective <| by     have reassoc' {W : D} (h : hf.Z ⟶ W) : F.map f ≫ hf.g ≫ h = 0 ≫ h := by       rw [← Category.assoc, eq_whisker hf.w]     simp [reassoc']   isLimit :=     @ReflectsLimit.reflects C _ D _ _ _ _ F _ _ <|       IsLimit.ofConeEquiv (Cones.postcomposeEquivalence (@compNatIso C _ _ _ _ _ D _ _ F _)) <|         IsLimit.ofIsoLimit           (IsLimit.ofIsoLimit             (IsKernel.ofCompIso _ _ (F.objObjPreimageIso hf.Z) (by               simp only [Functor.map_preimage, Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id])             hf.isLimit)             (ofιCongr (Category.comp_id _).symm))         <| by apply Iso.symm; apply isoOfι  -- Porting note: very fiddly unification here

CategoryTheory.NormalEpiCategory.pushout.fullDefinition: def pushout_of_epi {X Y Z : C} (a : X ⟶ Y) (b : X ⟶ Z) [Epi a] [Epi b] :     HasColimit (span a b) :=   let ⟨P, f, hfa, i⟩ := normalEpiOfEpi a   let ⟨Q, g, hgb, i'⟩ := normalEpiOfEpi b   let ⟨a', ha'⟩ :=     CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' i (cokernel.π (coprod.desc f g)) <|       calc         f ≫ cokernel.π (coprod.desc f g) =             coprod.inl ≫ coprod.desc f g ≫ cokernel.π (coprod.desc f g) := by           rw [coprod.inl_desc_assoc]         _ = coprod.inl ≫ (0 : P ⨿ Q ⟶ cokernel (coprod.desc f g)) := by rw [cokernel.condition]         _ = 0 := HasZeroMorphisms.comp_zero _ _
CategoryTheory.NormalEpiCategory.pushout.description: This definition asserts that in a category with normal epimorphisms, finite coproducts, and cokernels, the pushout of two epimorphisms exists.

CategoryTheory.NormalEpiCategory.hasColi.fullDefinition: def hasColimit_parallelPair {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : HasColimit (parallelPair f g) :=   have huv : (pushout.inl _ _ : Y ⟶ Q f g) = pushout.inr _ _ :=     calc       (pushout.inl _ _ : Y ⟶ Q f g) = 𝟙 _ ≫ pushout.inl _ _ := Eq.symm <| Category.id_comp _       _ = (coprod.inl ≫ coprod.desc (𝟙 Y) f) ≫ pushout.inl _ _ := by rw [coprod.inl_desc]       _ = (coprod.inl ≫ coprod.desc (𝟙 Y) g) ≫ pushout.inr _ _ := by         simp only [Category.assoc, pushout.condition]       _ = pushout.inr _ _ := by rw [coprod.inl_desc, Category.id_comp]

CategoryTheory.Limits.SingleObj.Types.Qu.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.SingleObj.Types.Quot.equivOrbitRelQuotient.{u, v} {G : Type v} [Group G]
  (J : SingleObj G ⥤ Type u) : Types.Quot J ≃ MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient G (J.obj (SingleObj.star G))
CategoryTheory.Limits.SingleObj.Types.Qu.comment:
The explicit quotient construction of the colimit of `J : SingleObj G ⥤ Type u` is
equivalent to the quotient of `J.obj (SingleObj.star G)` by the induced action.
