CategoryTheory.Limits.SingleObj.Types.Qu.fullDefinition: def Types.Quot.equivOrbitRelQuotient :     Types.Quot J ≃ MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient G (J.obj (SingleObj.star G)) where   toFun := Quot.lift (fun p => ⟦p.2⟧) <| fun a b h => Quotient.sound <|     (Types.Quot.Rel.iff_orbitRel J a.2 b.2).mp h   invFun := Quot.lift (fun x => Quot.mk _ ⟨SingleObj.star G, x⟩) <| fun a b h =>     Quot.sound <| (Types.Quot.Rel.iff_orbitRel J a b).mpr h   left_inv := fun x => Quot.inductionOn x (fun _ ↦ rfl)   right_inv := fun x => Quot.inductionOn x (fun _ ↦ rfl)
CategoryTheory.Limits.SingleObj.Types.Qu.description: The colimit of a functor from a single-object category to types can be represented as the quotient of the object's image under the equivalence relation defined by the induced group action.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.code: CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (a b : R ⟶ X) : Prop
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.comment:
`IsKernelPair f a b` expresses that `(a, b)` is a kernel pair for `f`, i.e. `a ≫ f = b ≫ f`
and the square
  R → X
  ↓   ↓
  X → Y
is a pullback square.
This is just an abbreviation for `IsPullback a b f f`.
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.fullDefinition: abbrev IsKernelPair :=   IsPullback a b f f
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.description: This definition states that a pair of morphisms forms a kernel pair for another morphism if they satisfy a specific equality and the corresponding square is a pullback square.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.id_of_mono.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.id_of_mono.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f] :
  IsKernelPair f (𝟙 X) (𝟙 X)
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.id_of_mono.comment: If `f` is a monomorphism, then `(𝟙 _, 𝟙 _)` is a kernel pair for `f`.
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.id_of_mono.description: This theorem asserts that if a morphism is a monomorphism, then the identity morphisms at the domain form a kernel pair for that morphism.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {a b : R ⟶ X} {S : C}
  (k : IsKernelPair f a b) (p q : S ⟶ X) (w : p ≫ f = q ≫ f) : S ⟶ R
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift.comment:
Given a pair of morphisms `p`, `q` to `X` which factor through `f`, they factor through any kernel
pair of `f`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: This definition describes a lifting morphism from an object related to a limit pullback cone that satisfies certain equalities with the morphisms in the cospan, establishing relationships with the projections of the cone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsPullback.isLimit: The cone associated with a pullback structure formed by two morphisms and a common codomain qualifies as a limit cone in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.w: This theorem states that for a commutative square within a category, the composition of specific morphisms results in equal morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.w: This theorem states that if a morphism is a regular epimorphism, then it coequalizes two specific maps, ensuring the equality of their compositions with the epimorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift: This definition states that for morphisms from a common object to a target object that satisfy a compatibility condition, there exists a morphism from an intermediary object to the pullback object formed by those morphisms.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift.fullDefinition: noncomputable def lift {S : C} (k : IsKernelPair f a b) (p q : S ⟶ X) (w : p ≫ f = q ≫ f) :     S ⟶ R :=   PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift k.isLimit _ _ w
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift.description: This definition specifies a construction that allows morphisms mapping to a target to factor through any kernel pair of a given morphism, provided they satisfy a specific equality with respect to that morphism.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift'.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {a b : R ⟶ X} {S : C}
  (k : IsKernelPair f a b) (p q : S ⟶ X) (w : p ≫ f = q ≫ f) : { t // t ≫ a = p ∧ t ≫ b = q }
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift'.comment:
Given a pair of morphisms `p`, `q` to `X` which factor through `f`, they factor through any kernel
pair of `f`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: This definition describes a lifting morphism from an object related to a limit pullback cone that satisfies certain equalities with the morphisms in the cospan, establishing relationships with the projections of the cone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.w: This theorem states that for a commutative square within a category, the composition of specific morphisms results in equal morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.w: This theorem states that if a morphism is a regular epimorphism, then it coequalizes two specific maps, ensuring the equality of their compositions with the epimorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift: This definition states that for morphisms from a common object to a target object that satisfy a compatibility condition, there exists a morphism from an intermediary object to the pullback object formed by those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: This definition describes a method to construct a morphism from an object to the point of a limit pullback cone satisfying specific compositional relationships based on given morphisms that equalize at the limit.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift'.fullDefinition: noncomputable def lift' {S : C} (k : IsKernelPair f a b) (p q : S ⟶ X) (w : p ≫ f = q ≫ f) :     { t : S ⟶ R // t ≫ a = p ∧ t ≫ b = q } :=   ⟨k.lift p q w, by simp⟩
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift'.description: This definition provides a construction for finding a morphism mapping to a specific kernel pair based on two morphisms that agree under the original morphism's action.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y Z : C} {a b : R ⟶ X}
  {f₁ : X ⟶ Y} {f₂ : Y ⟶ Z} (comm : a ≫ f₁ = b ≫ f₁) (big_k : IsKernelPair (f₁ ≫ f₂) a b) : IsKernelPair f₁ a b
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right.comment:
If `(a,b)` is a kernel pair for `f₁ ≫ f₂` and `a ≫ f₁ = b ≫ f₁`, then `(a,b)` is a kernel pair for
just `f₁`.
That is, to show that `(a,b)` is a kernel pair for `f₁` it suffices to only show the square
commutes, rather than to additionally show it's a pullback.
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right.description: This theorem asserts that if a pair of morphisms forms a kernel pair for the composition of two morphisms and they are equal when composed with the first, then they also form a kernel pair for just the first morphism.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right_of_mono.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y Z : C} {a b : R ⟶ X}
  {f₁ : X ⟶ Y} {f₂ : Y ⟶ Z} [Mono f₂] (big_k : IsKernelPair (f₁ ≫ f₂) a b) : IsKernelPair f₁ a b
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right.comment:
If `(a,b)` is a kernel pair for `f₁ ≫ f₂` and `f₂` is mono, then `(a,b)` is a kernel pair for
just `f₁`.
The converse of `comp_of_mono`.
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.cancel_right.description: This theorem establishes that if a pair of morphisms forms a kernel pair for the composition of two morphisms and the second morphism is a monomorphism, then that pair also serves as a kernel pair for just the first morphism.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.comp_of_mono.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.comp_of_mono.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y Z : C} {a b : R ⟶ X}
  {f₁ : X ⟶ Y} {f₂ : Y ⟶ Z} [Mono f₂] (small_k : IsKernelPair f₁ a b) : IsKernelPair (f₁ ≫ f₂) a b
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.comp_of_mono.comment:
If `(a,b)` is a kernel pair for `f₁` and `f₂` is mono, then `(a,b)` is a kernel pair for `f₁ ≫ f₂`.
The converse of `cancel_right_of_mono`.
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.comp_of_mono.description: This theorem establishes that if a pair of morphisms is a kernel pair for one morphism and the subsequent morphism is monomorphic, then that same pair remains a kernel pair for the composition of both morphisms.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.toCoequalize.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.toCoequalizer.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {a b : R ⟶ X}
  (k : IsKernelPair f a b) [r : RegularEpi f] : IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ f ⋯)
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.toCoequalize.comment:
If `(a,b)` is the kernel pair of `f`, and `f` is a coequalizer morphism for some parallel pair, then
`f` is a coequalizer morphism of `a` and `b`.

explanatories.Inhabited.mk: Any type that has a default element is considered inhabited.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: This definition describes a lifting morphism from an object related to a limit pullback cone that satisfies certain equalities with the morphisms in the cospan, establishing relationships with the projections of the cone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift: This definition specifies a construction that allows morphisms mapping to a target to factor through any kernel pair of a given morphism, provided they satisfy a specific equality with respect to that morphism.
explanatories.Subtype.mk: This theorem states that for any element and a property it satisfies, one can construct a subtype consisting of elements that possess that property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.mk: A pullback cone for two morphisms is created by two morphisms from a common object that satisfy a specific compatibility condition with respect to the given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.fac: This theorem shows that a specific lifting of a cone through a limit cone results in a commutative triangle involving the cone's projection morphisms and the natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingCospan.left: This definition represents the left point of the diagram used to describe a pullback in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingCospan.righ: This definition represents the right point of the diagram used to describe a pullback in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms into a limit cone yield the same results when composed with the projection morphisms from the cone, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommSq.w: This theorem states that for a commutative square within a category, the composition of specific morphisms results in equal morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.condi: The theorem asserts that in a pullback cone, the composition of the first projection with its associated morphism matches the composition of the second projection with the other morphism in the cospan.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.ofπ: The definition establishes how to construct a cofork for two morphisms by specifying a morphism that satisfies a certain equality involving their compositions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.w: This theorem states that if a morphism is a regular epimorphism, then it coequalizes two specific maps, ensuring the equality of their compositions with the epimorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.left: This definition specifies a morphism from a particular property of a regular epimorphism to its domain in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.right: This definition establishes a morphism from a specific structure associated with a regular epimorphism to the domain of that epimorphism within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.m: This definition provides a method to construct a colimit from a specified cofork by requiring proofs of a morphism's factorization, uniqueness, and a specific mapping from the cofork to the colimit's point.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.d: This definition specifies how to obtain a morphism from the point of a cofork to another object, given a compatible morphism that equates the images of two other morphisms through that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.isColimit: This definition states that a morphism identified as a regular epimorphism serves as the coequalizer in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.π: This definition describes a specific morphism associated with a cofork of two parallel morphisms, mapping from a particular object in a diagram to the point of the cofork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.condition: This theorem states that for a cofork, the composition of its projection with both morphisms yields the same result, ensuring a specific relationship between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.h: The theorem states that if two morphisms from a common point of a colimit diagram are equal when composed with the diagram's projection, then those two morphisms themselves must also be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift: This definition states that for morphisms from a common object to a target object that satisfy a compatibility condition, there exists a morphism from an intermediary object to the pullback object formed by those morphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.IsLim: The theorem establishes that if two morphisms from a common source to the point of a pullback cone give the same results when composed with the respective projections, then those two morphisms must be identical.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.toCoequalize.fullDefinition: def toCoequalizer (k : IsKernelPair f a b) [r : RegularEpi f] : IsColimit (Cofork.ofπ f k.w) := by   let t := k.isLimit.lift (PullbackCone.mk _ _ r.w)   have ht : t ≫ a = r.left := k.isLimit.fac _ WalkingCospan.left   have kt : t ≫ b = r.right := k.isLimit.fac _ WalkingCospan.right   refine Cofork.IsColimit.mk _     (fun s => Cofork.IsColimit.desc r.isColimit s.π       (by rw [← ht, assoc, s.condition, reassoc_of% kt]))     (fun s => ?_) (fun s m w => ?_)   · apply Cofork.IsColimit.π_desc' r.isColimit   · apply Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext r.isColimit     exact w.trans (Cofork.IsColimit.π_desc' r.isColimit _ _).symm
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.toCoequalize.description: This definition characterizes the coequalizer relationship of a morphism based on its kernel pair, asserting that if a specific pair forms a kernel pair of the morphism, then the morphism acts as a coequalizer for that pair when the morphism is regular epic.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift_fst_ass.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.lift_fst_assoc.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {a b : R ⟶ X}
  {S : C} (k : IsKernelPair f a b) (p q : S ⟶ X) (w : p ≫ f = q ≫ f) {Z : C} (h : X ⟶ Z) : k.lift p q w ≫ a ≫ h = p ≫ h

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.pullback.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.pullback.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X Y Z A : C} {g : Y ⟶ Z} {a₁ a₂ : A ⟶ Y}
  (h : IsKernelPair g a₁ a₂) (f : X ⟶ Z) [HasPullback f g] [HasPullback f (a₁ ≫ g)] :
  IsKernelPair (pullback.fst f g) (pullback.map f (a₁ ≫ g) f g (𝟙 X) a₁ (𝟙 Z) ⋯ ⋯)
    (pullback.map f (a₁ ≫ g) f g (𝟙 X) a₂ (𝟙 Z) ⋯ ⋯)
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.pullback.comment:
If `a₁ a₂ : A ⟶ Y` is a kernel pair for `g : Y ⟶ Z`, then `a₁ ×[Z] X` and `a₂ ×[Z] X`
(`A ×[Z] X ⟶ Y ×[Z] X`) is a kernel pair for `Y ×[Z] X ⟶ X`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.fst: The first projection of a pullback cone provides a morphism from the cone's point to the first object involved in the cospan formed by two given morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullback: This definition specifies the property of a category having a pullback for a given pair of morphisms from two objects to a common object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst: This definition describes the first projection map from the pullback object associated with a pair of morphisms to the first object of one of the morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.map: This definition establishes a morphism between the pullbacks of two pairs of morphisms that share a common object, under specified conditions relating to their compositions.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.pullback.description: If a specified pair of morphisms forms a kernel pair of another morphism, then their pullback along any morphism produces a new kernel pair for the composed morphism formed from the original and the pullback.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.mono_of_isIs.description: This theorem establishes that if a pair of morphisms forms a kernel pair for a given morphism and one of the morphisms in the pair is an isomorphism, then the original morphism must be a monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.isIso_of_mon.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.isIso_of_mono.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {a b : R ⟶ X}
  (h : IsKernelPair f a b) [Mono f] : IsIso a
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.isIso_of_mon.description: This theorem asserts that if a pair of morphisms forms a kernel pair for a given morphism and that morphism is a monomorphism, then one of the morphisms in the pair must be an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.of_isIso_of_.code:
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.of_isIso_of_mono.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {R X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} {a : R ⟶ X}
  [IsIso a] [Mono f] : IsKernelPair f a a
CategoryTheory.IsKernelPair.of_isIso_of_.description: This theorem states that if a morphism is both an isomorphism and a monomorphism, then it forms a kernel pair with itself for a given morphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMa.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMapIso.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {X Y : C}
  [HasPullbacks C] {U V₁ V₂ : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : U ⟶ Y) (i₁ : V₁ ⟶ pullback f i) (i₂ : V₂ ⟶ pullback f i)
  [HasPullback i₁ i₂] :
  pullback (diagonal f) (map (i₁ ≫ snd f i) (i₂ ≫ snd f i) f f (i₁ ≫ fst f i) (i₂ ≫ fst f i) i ⋯ ⋯) ≅ pullback i₁ i₂
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMa.comment:
This iso witnesses the fact that
given `f : X ⟶ Y`, `i : U ⟶ Y`, and `i₁ : V₁ ⟶ X ×[Y] U`, `i₂ : V₂ ⟶ X ×[Y] U`, the diagram

```
V₁ ×[X ×[Y] U] V₂ ⟶ V₁ ×[U] V₂
        |                 |
        |                 |
        ↓                 ↓
        X         ⟶   X ×[Y] X
```

is a pullback square.
Also see `pullback_fst_map_snd_isPullback`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMa.fullDefinition: def pullbackDiagonalMapIso :     pullback (diagonal f)         (map (i₁ ≫ snd _ _) (i₂ ≫ snd _ _) f f (i₁ ≫ fst _ _) (i₂ ≫ fst _ _) i           (by simp only [Category.assoc, condition])           (by simp only [Category.assoc, condition])) ≅       pullback i₁ i₂ where   hom :=     pullback.lift (pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _ ≫ pullback.snd _ _) (by       ext       · simp [Category.assoc, pullback_diagonal_map_snd_fst_fst, pullback_diagonal_map_snd_snd_fst]       · simp [Category.assoc, pullback.condition, pullback.condition_assoc])   inv :=     pullback.lift (pullback.fst _ _ ≫ i₁ ≫ pullback.fst _ _)       (pullback.map _ _ _ _ (𝟙 _) (𝟙 _) (pullback.snd _ _) (Category.id_comp _).symm         (Category.id_comp _).symm) (by         ext         · simp only [Category.assoc, diagonal_fst, Category.comp_id, limit.lift_π,             PullbackCone.mk_pt, PullbackCone.mk_π_app, limit.lift_π_assoc, cospan_left]         · simp only [condition_assoc, Category.assoc, diagonal_snd, Category.comp_id,             limit.lift_π, PullbackCone.mk_pt, PullbackCone.mk_π_app,             limit.lift_π_assoc, cospan_right])

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMa.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMapIso_hom_fst.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {X Y : C}
  [HasPullbacks C] {U V₁ V₂ : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (i : U ⟶ Y) (i₁ : V₁ ⟶ pullback f i) (i₂ : V₂ ⟶ pullback f i)
  [HasPullback i₁ i₂] :
  (pullbackDiagonalMapIso f i i₁ i₂).hom ≫ fst i₁ i₂ =
    snd (diagonal f) (map (i₁ ≫ snd f i) (i₂ ≫ snd f i) f f (i₁ ≫ fst f i) (i₂ ≫ fst f i) i ⋯ ⋯) ≫
      fst (i₁ ≫ snd f i) (i₂ ≫ snd f i)

CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMapIdIso.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {X Y : C}
  [HasPullbacks C] {S T : C} (f : X ⟶ T) (g : Y ⟶ T) (i : T ⟶ S) [HasPullback i i] [HasPullback f g]
  [HasPullback (f ≫ i) (g ≫ i)] [HasPullback (diagonal i) (map (f ≫ i) (g ≫ i) i i f g (𝟙 S) ⋯ ⋯)] :
  pullback (diagonal i) (map (f ≫ i) (g ≫ i) i i f g (𝟙 S) ⋯ ⋯) ≅ pullback f g
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackDiagonalMa.comment:
This iso witnesses the fact that
given `f : X ⟶ T`, `g : Y ⟶ T`, and `i : T ⟶ S`, the diagram

```
X ×ₜ Y ⟶ X ×ₛ Y
  |         |
  |         |
  ↓         ↓
  T    ⟶  T ×ₛ T
```

is a pullback square.
Also see `pullback_map_diagonal_isPullback`.

  {X Y S X' Y' S' : C} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g' : Y' ⟶ S') (i₁ : X ⟶ X') (i₂ : Y ⟶ Y') (i₃ : S ⟶ S')
  (e₁ : f ≫ i₃ = i₁ ≫ f') (e₂ : g ≫ i₃ = i₂ ≫ g') [Mono i₃] :
  pullback (fst (fst f' g') i₁) (fst (snd f' g') i₂) ≅ pullback f g
CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackFstFstIso.comment:
Given the following diagram with `S ⟶ S'` a monomorphism,

```
    X ⟶ X'
      ↘      ↘
        S ⟶ S'
      ↗      ↗
    Y ⟶ Y'
```

This iso witnesses the fact that

```
      X ×[S] Y ⟶ (X' ×[S'] Y') ×[Y'] Y
          |                  |
          |                  |
          ↓                  ↓
(X' ×[S'] Y') ×[X'] X ⟶ X' ×[S'] Y'
```

is a pullback square. The diagonal map of this square is `pullback.map`.
Also see `pullback_lift_map_is_pullback`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.extend.fullDefinition: def extend (s : Cone F) {X : C} (f : X ⟶ s.pt) : s.extend f ⟶ s where   hom := f
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.extend.description: This definition describes the construction of a morphism from an extended cone to the original cone based on a given morphism from a specific object in the category to the cone point.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.extendIso.comment: A cone extended by an isomorphism is isomorphic to the original cone.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.extendIso.fullDefinition: def extendIso (s : Cone F) {X : C} (f : X ≅ s.pt) : s.extend f.hom ≅ s where   hom := { hom := f.hom }   inv := { hom := f.inv }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.extendIso.description: This definition states that extending a cone by an isomorphism results in an isomorphic cone to the original one.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcompose.fullDefinition: def postcompose {G : J ⥤ C} (α : F ⟶ G) : Cone F ⥤ Cone G where   obj c :=     { pt := c.pt       π := c.π ≫ α }   map f := { hom := f.hom }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcompose.description: This definition specifies a functor that transforms a cone over one functor into a cone over another functor through the application of a natural transformation between the two functors.

  [Category.{v₃, u₃} C] {F G H : J ⥤ C} (α : F ⟶ G) (β : G ⟶ H) : postcompose (α ≫ β) ≅ postcompose α ⋙ postcompose β
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeC.comment:
Postcomposing a cone by the composite natural transformation `α ≫ β` is the same as
postcomposing by `α` and then by `β`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeC.fullDefinition: def postcomposeComp {G H : J ⥤ C} (α : F ⟶ G) (β : G ⟶ H) :     postcompose (α ≫ β) ≅ postcompose α ⋙ postcompose β :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun s => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeC.description: This definition shows that postcomposing a cone with a composite natural transformation is equivalent to postcomposing it sequentially with each individual transformation.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeI.fullDefinition: def postcomposeId : postcompose (𝟙 F) ≅ 𝟭 (Cone F) :=   NatIso.ofComponents fun s => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeI.description: This definition states that postcomposing with the identity morphism of a functor results in an isomorphism that preserves the structure of a cone associated with that functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeE.code:

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeE.fullDefinition: def postcomposeEquivalence {G : J ⥤ C} (α : F ≅ G) : Cone F ≌ Cone G where   functor := postcompose α.hom   inverse := postcompose α.inv   unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun s => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)   counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun s => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.postcomposeE.description: This definition indicates that if two functors are naturally isomorphic, then their associated categories of cones are equivalent.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.whiskeringEq.fullDefinition: def whiskeringEquivalence (e : K ≌ J) : Cone F ≌ Cone (e.functor ⋙ F) where   functor := whiskering e.functor   inverse := whiskering e.inverse ⋙ postcompose (e.invFunIdAssoc F).hom   unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun s => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)   counitIso :=     NatIso.ofComponents       fun s =>         Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)           (by             intro k             simpa [e.counit_app_functor] using s.w (e.unitInv.app k))
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.whiskeringEq.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the categories of cones over a functor and cones over the composition of that functor with an equivalence of categories.

The categories of cones over `F` and `G` are equivalent if `F` and `G` are naturally isomorphic

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.equivalenceO.fullDefinition: def equivalenceOfReindexing {G : K ⥤ C} (e : K ≌ J) (α : e.functor ⋙ F ≅ G) : Cone F ≌ Cone G :=   (whiskeringEquivalence e).trans (postcomposeEquivalence α)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.equivalenceO.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the categories of cones over two functors, provided there is an equivalence between their indexing categories and a natural isomorphism between the composed functors.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.functorialit.fullDefinition: def functoriality : Cone F ⥤ Cone (F ⋙ G) where   obj A :=     { pt := G.obj A.pt       π :=         { app := fun j => G.map (A.π.app j)           naturality := by intros; erw [← G.map_comp]; aesop_cat } }   map f :=     { hom := G.map f.hom       w := fun j => by simp [-ConeMorphism.w, ← f.w j] }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.functorialit.description: This definition describes a functor that transforms cones over a given functor into cones over the composition of that functor with another functor in a way that maintains the structure of the cones.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.functorialit.fullDefinition: def functorialityEquivalence (e : C ≌ D) : Cone F ≌ Cone (F ⋙ e.functor) :=   let f : (F ⋙ e.functor) ⋙ e.inverse ≅ F :=     Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫ isoWhiskerLeft _ e.unitIso.symm ≪≫ Functor.rightUnitor _   { functor := functoriality F e.functor     inverse := functoriality (F ⋙ e.functor) e.inverse ⋙ (postcomposeEquivalence f).functor     unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cones.ext (e.unitIso.app _)     counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cones.ext (e.counitIso.app _) }

CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.functorial.fullDefinition: def functorialityEquivalence (e : C ≌ D) : Cocone F ≌ Cocone (F ⋙ e.functor) :=   let f : (F ⋙ e.functor) ⋙ e.inverse ≅ F :=     Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫ isoWhiskerLeft _ e.unitIso.symm ≪≫ Functor.rightUnitor _   { functor := functoriality F e.functor     inverse := functoriality (F ⋙ e.functor) e.inverse ⋙ (precomposeEquivalence f.symm).functor     unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cocones.ext (e.unitIso.app _)     counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cocones.ext (e.counitIso.app _) }
CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.functorial.description: This definition asserts that an equivalence between two categories induces a corresponding equivalence between cocones over a functor and those over the composed functor with the equivalence's functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.coconeEquivalenceO.fullDefinition: def coconeEquivalenceOpConeOp : Cocone F ≌ (Cone F.op)ᵒᵖ where   functor :=     { obj := fun c => op (Cocone.op c)       map := fun {X} {Y} f =>         Quiver.Hom.op           { hom := f.hom.op             w := fun j => by               apply Quiver.Hom.unop_inj               dsimp               apply CoconeMorphism.w } }   inverse :=     { obj := fun c => Cone.unop (unop c)       map := fun {X} {Y} f =>         { hom := f.unop.hom.unop           w := fun j => by             apply Quiver.Hom.op_inj             dsimp             apply ConeMorphism.w } }   unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents (fun c => Cocones.ext (Iso.refl _))   counitIso :=     NatIso.ofComponents       (fun c => by         induction c         apply Iso.op         exact Cones.ext (Iso.refl _))       fun {X} {Y} f =>       Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (ConeMorphism.ext _ _ (by simp))   functor_unitIso_comp c := by     apply Quiver.Hom.unop_inj     apply ConeMorphism.ext     dsimp     apply comp_id

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.conePoints.comment:
We can prove two cone points `(s : Cone F).pt` and `(t : Cone G).pt` are isomorphic if
* both cones are limit cones
* their indexing categories are equivalent via some `e : J ≌ K`,
* the triangle of functors commutes up to a natural isomorphism: `e.functor ⋙ G ≅ F`.

This is the most general form of uniqueness of cone points,
allowing relabelling of both the indexing category (up to equivalence)
and the functor (up to natural isomorphism).

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.conePoints.fullDefinition: def conePointsIsoOfEquivalence {F : J ⥤ C} {s : Cone F} {G : K ⥤ C} {t : Cone G} (P : IsLimit s)     (Q : IsLimit t) (e : J ≌ K) (w : e.functor ⋙ G ≅ F) : s.pt ≅ t.pt :=   let w' : e.inverse ⋙ F ≅ G := (isoWhiskerLeft e.inverse w).symm ≪≫ invFunIdAssoc e G   { hom := Q.lift ((Cones.equivalenceOfReindexing e.symm w').functor.obj s)     inv := P.lift ((Cones.equivalenceOfReindexing e w).functor.obj t)     hom_inv_id := by       apply hom_ext P; intro j       dsimp [w']       simp only [Limits.Cone.whisker_π, Limits.Cones.postcompose_obj_π, fac, whiskerLeft_app,         assoc, id_comp, invFunIdAssoc_hom_app, fac_assoc, NatTrans.comp_app]       rw [counit_app_functor, ← Functor.comp_map]       have l :         NatTrans.app w.hom j = NatTrans.app w.hom (Prefunctor.obj (𝟭 J).toPrefunctor j) := by dsimp       rw [l,w.hom.naturality]       simp     inv_hom_id := by       apply hom_ext Q       aesop_cat }

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.coconePo.comment:
We can prove two cocone points `(s : Cocone F).pt` and `(t : Cocone G).pt` are isomorphic if
* both cocones are colimit cocones
* their indexing categories are equivalent via some `e : J ≌ K`,
* the triangle of functors commutes up to a natural isomorphism: `e.functor ⋙ G ≅ F`.

This is the most general form of uniqueness of cocone points,
allowing relabelling of both the indexing category (up to equivalence)
and the functor (up to natural isomorphism).

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.homIso'.fullDefinition: def homIso' (h : IsColimit t) (W : C) :     ULift.{u₁} (t.pt ⟶ W : Type v₃) ≅       { p : ∀ j, F.obj j ⟶ W // ∀ {j j' : J} (f : j ⟶ j'), F.map f ≫ p j' = p j } :=   h.homIso W ≪≫     { hom := fun ι =>         ⟨fun j => ι.app j, fun {j} {j'} f => by convert ← ι.naturality f; apply comp_id⟩       inv := fun p =>         { app := fun j => p.1 j           naturality := fun j j' f => by dsimp; rw [comp_id]; exact p.2 f } }
CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.homIso'.description: This definition provides an alternative formulation of the universal property of a colimit cocone, establishing an isomorphism between a morphism from the cocone point to another object and a certain structured set of morphisms indexed over the diagram.

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofFaithf.comment:

then it suffices to check that the induced maps for the image of t
can be lifted to maps of C.

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofFaithf.fullDefinition: def ofFaithful {t : Cocone F} {D : Type u₄} [Category.{v₄} D] (G : C ⥤ D) [G.Faithful]     (ht : IsColimit (mapCocone G t)) (desc : ∀ s : Cocone F, t.pt ⟶ s.pt)     (h : ∀ s, G.map (desc s) = ht.desc (mapCocone G s)) : IsColimit t :=   { desc     fac := fun s j => by apply G.map_injective; rw [G.map_comp, h]; apply ht.fac     uniq := fun s m w => by       apply G.map_injective; rw [h]       refine ht.uniq (mapCocone G s) _ fun j => ?_       convert ← congrArg (fun f => G.map f) (w j)       apply G.map_comp }
CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofFaithf.description: This definition states that if a faithful functor transforms a specific cocone into a colimit cocone, then it is sufficient to demonstrate that the corresponding induced mappings from the cocone can be extended to morphisms within the original category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofNatIso.fullDefinition: def ofNatIso {X : C} (h : coyoneda.obj (op X) ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u₁} ≅ F.cocones) :     IsColimit (colimitCocone h) where   desc s := homOfCocone h s   fac s j := by     have h := cocone_fac h s     cases s     injection h with h₁ h₂     simp only [heq_iff_eq] at h₂     conv_rhs => rw [← h₂]     rfl   uniq s m w := by     rw [← homOfCocone_cooneOfHom h m]     congr     rw [coconeOfHom_fac]     dsimp [Cocone.extend]; cases s; congr with j; exact w j

CategoryTheory.Limits.constLimAdj.fullDefinition: def constLimAdj : (const J : C ⥤ J ⥤ C) ⊣ lim where   homEquiv c g :=     { toFun := fun f => limit.lift _ ⟨c, f⟩       invFun := fun f =>         { app := fun j => f ≫ limit.π _ _ }       left_inv := by aesop_cat       right_inv := by aesop_cat }   unit := { app := fun c => limit.lift _ ⟨_, 𝟙 _⟩ }   counit := { app := fun g => { app := limit.π _ } }   -- This used to be automatic before leanprover/lean4#2644   homEquiv_unit := by     -- Sad that aesop can no longer do this!     intros     dsimp     ext     simp

CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.ι_desc.comment:
We have lots of lemmas describing how to simplify `colimit.ι F j ≫ _`,
and combined with `colimit.ext` we rely on these lemmas for many calculations.

However, since `Category.assoc` is a `@[simp]` lemma, often expressions are
right associated, and it's hard to apply these lemmas about `colimit.ι`.

We thus use `reassoc` to define additional `@[simp]` lemmas, with an arbitrary extra morphism.
(see `Tactic/reassoc_axiom.lean`)

CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.isoOfEq.fullDefinition: def HasColimit.isoOfEquivalence {F : J ⥤ C} [HasColimit F] {G : K ⥤ C} [HasColimit G] (e : J ≌ K)     (w : e.functor ⋙ G ≅ F) : colimit F ≅ colimit G :=   IsColimit.coconePointsIsoOfEquivalence (colimit.isColimit F) (colimit.isColimit G) e w
CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.isoOfEq.description: This definition establishes that if two functors have colimits and there is an equivalence between their indexing categories which respects the structure of these functors, then the colimits themselves are isomorphic.

CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.isoOfEq.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.isoOfEquivalence_hom_π.{v₁, u₁, v₂, u₂, v, u} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J]
  {K : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} K] {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {F : J ⥤ C} [HasColimit F] {G : K ⥤ C}
  [HasColimit G] (e : J ≌ K) (w : e.functor ⋙ G ≅ F) (j : J) :
  colimit.ι F j ≫ (HasColimit.isoOfEquivalence e w).hom =
    F.map (e.unit.app j) ≫
      w.inv.app ((e.functor ⋙ e.inverse).obj j) ≫ colimit.ι G (e.functor.obj ((e.functor ⋙ e.inverse).obj j))

CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.isoOfEq.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.isoOfEquivalence_inv_π.{v₁, u₁, v₂, u₂, v, u} {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J]
  {K : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} K] {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {F : J ⥤ C} [HasColimit F] {G : K ⥤ C}

CategoryTheory.Limits.colimConstAdj.fullDefinition: def colimConstAdj : (colim : (J ⥤ C) ⥤ C) ⊣ const J where   homEquiv f c :=     { toFun := fun g =>         { app := fun _ => colimit.ι _ _ ≫ g }       invFun := fun g => colimit.desc _ ⟨_, g⟩       left_inv := by aesop_cat       right_inv := by aesop_cat }   unit := { app := fun g => { app := colimit.ι _ } }   counit := { app := fun c => colimit.desc _ ⟨_, 𝟙 _⟩ }
CategoryTheory.Limits.colimConstAdj.description: This definition establishes an adjunction relationship between the colimit functor and the constant functor associated with a given category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.fac: This theorem establishes that the morphism from a cocone to its colimit, when composed with the corresponding arrow from the colimit, yields the arrow from the cocone at the same object, ensuring the commutativity of the involved diagram.

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.op: This defines the mapping of an arrow from one object to its opposite direction in the quiver structure.

CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.unop.fullDefinition: def IsColimit.unop {t : Cocone F.op} (P : IsColimit t) : IsLimit t.unop where   lift s := (P.desc s.op).unop   fac s j := congrArg Quiver.Hom.unop (P.fac s.op (Opposite.op j))   -- Porting note: thinks `op j` is `IsLimit.op j`   uniq s m w := by     dsimp     rw [← P.uniq s.op m.op]     · rfl     · dsimp       intro j       rw [← w]       rfl
CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.unop.description: This definition states that if a cocone of a functor is a colimit, then the corresponding inverted cocone is a limit for that functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.coneOfConeUncurry.fullDefinition: def coneOfConeUncurry {D : DiagramOfCones F} (Q : ∀ j, IsLimit (D.obj j))     (c : Cone (uncurry.obj F)) : Cone D.conePoints where   pt := c.pt   π :=     { app := fun j =>         (Q j).lift           { pt := c.pt             π :=               { app := fun k => c.π.app (j, k)                 naturality := fun k k' f => by                   dsimp; simp only [Category.id_comp]                   have := @NatTrans.naturality _ _ _ _ _ _ c.π (j, k) (j, k') (𝟙 j, f)                   dsimp at this                   simp? at this says                     simp only [Category.id_comp, Functor.map_id, NatTrans.id_app] at this                   exact this } }       naturality := fun j j' f =>         (Q j').hom_ext           (by             dsimp             intro k             simp only [Limits.ConeMorphism.w, Limits.Cones.postcompose_obj_π,               Limits.IsLimit.fac_assoc, Limits.IsLimit.fac, NatTrans.comp_app, Category.id_comp,               Category.assoc]             have := @NatTrans.naturality _ _ _ _ _ _ c.π (j, k) (j', k) (f, 𝟙 k)             dsimp at this             simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id,               NatTrans.id_app] at this             exact this) }

CategoryTheory.Limits.coneOfConeUncurryI.fullDefinition: def coneOfConeUncurryIsLimit {D : DiagramOfCones F} (Q : ∀ j, IsLimit (D.obj j))     {c : Cone (uncurry.obj F)} (P : IsLimit c) : IsLimit (coneOfConeUncurry Q c) where   lift s :=     P.lift       { pt := s.pt         π :=           { app := fun p => s.π.app p.1 ≫ (D.obj p.1).π.app p.2             naturality := fun p p' f => by               dsimp; simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc]               rcases p with ⟨j, k⟩               rcases p' with ⟨j', k'⟩               rcases f with ⟨fj, fk⟩               dsimp               slice_rhs 3 4 => rw [← NatTrans.naturality]               slice_rhs 2 3 => rw [← (D.obj j).π.naturality]               simp only [Functor.const_obj_map, Category.id_comp, Category.assoc]               have w := (D.map fj).w k'               dsimp at w               rw [← w]               have n := s.π.naturality fj               dsimp at n               simp only [Category.id_comp] at n               rw [n]               simp } }   fac s j := by     apply (Q j).hom_ext     intro k     simp   uniq s m w := by     refine P.uniq       { pt := s.pt         π := _ } m ?_     rintro ⟨j, k⟩     dsimp     rw [← w j]     simp

CategoryTheory.Limits.coconeOfCoconeUncu.fullDefinition: def coconeOfCoconeUncurry {D : DiagramOfCocones F} (Q : ∀ j, IsColimit (D.obj j))     (c : Cocone (uncurry.obj F)) : Cocone D.coconePoints where   pt := c.pt   ι :=     { app := fun j =>         (Q j).desc           { pt := c.pt             ι :=               { app := fun k => c.ι.app (j, k)                 naturality := fun k k' f => by                   dsimp; simp only [Category.comp_id]                   conv_lhs =>                     arg 1; equals (F.map (𝟙 _)).app _ ≫  (F.obj j).map f =>                       simp                   conv_lhs => arg 1; rw [← uncurry_obj_map F ((𝟙 j,f) : (j,k) ⟶ (j,k'))]                   rw [c.w] } }       naturality := fun j j' f =>         (Q j).hom_ext           (by             dsimp             intro k             simp only [Limits.CoconeMorphism.w_assoc, Limits.Cocones.precompose_obj_ι,               Limits.IsColimit.fac_assoc, Limits.IsColimit.fac, NatTrans.comp_app, Category.comp_id,               Category.assoc]             have := @NatTrans.naturality _ _ _ _ _ _ c.ι (j, k) (j', k) (f, 𝟙 k)             dsimp at this             simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id,               NatTrans.id_app] at this             exact this) }

CategoryTheory.Limits.coconeOfCoconeUncu.fullDefinition: def coconeOfCoconeUncurryIsColimit {D : DiagramOfCocones F} (Q : ∀ j, IsColimit (D.obj j))     {c : Cocone (uncurry.obj F)} (P : IsColimit c) : IsColimit (coconeOfCoconeUncurry Q c) where   desc s :=     P.desc       { pt := s.pt         ι :=           { app := fun p => (D.obj p.1).ι.app p.2 ≫ s.ι.app p.1             naturality := fun p p' f => by               dsimp; simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc]               rcases p with ⟨j, k⟩               rcases p' with ⟨j', k'⟩               rcases f with ⟨fj, fk⟩               dsimp               slice_lhs 2 3 => rw [(D.obj j').ι.naturality]               simp only [Functor.const_obj_map, Category.id_comp, Category.assoc]               have w := (D.map fj).w k               dsimp at w               slice_lhs 1 2 => rw [← w]               have n := s.ι.naturality fj               dsimp at n               simp only [Category.comp_id] at n               rw [← n]               simp } }   fac s j := by     apply (Q j).hom_ext     intro k     simp   uniq s m w := by     refine P.uniq       { pt := s.pt         ι := _ } m ?_     rintro ⟨j, k⟩     dsimp     rw [← w j]     simp

CategoryTheory.Limits.limitIsoLimitCurry.fullDefinition: noncomputable def limitIsoLimitCurryCompLim : limit G ≅ limit (curry.obj G ⋙ lim) := by   have i : G ≅ uncurry.obj ((@curry J _ K _ C _).obj G) := currying.symm.unitIso.app G   haveI : Limits.HasLimit (uncurry.obj ((@curry J _ K _ C _).obj G)) := hasLimitOfIso i   trans limit (uncurry.obj ((@curry J _ K _ C _).obj G))   · apply HasLimit.isoOfNatIso i   · exact limitUncurryIsoLimitCompLim ((@curry J _ K _ C _).obj G)
CategoryTheory.Limits.limitIsoLimitCurry.description: This definition expresses that the limit of a functor defined on a product category is naturally isomorphic to the limit of the functor obtained by first taking the limit in one direction and then curry-composing with the original functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.uniq: This theorem states that if a cocone forms a colimit and another cocone has a morphism from their points satisfying a specific condition, then that morphism must coincide with the unique map provided by the colimit's universal property.

CategoryTheory.pi.coneOfConeEvalIsLimit.fullDefinition: def coneOfConeEvalIsLimit {c : ∀ i, Cone (F ⋙ Pi.eval C i)} (P : ∀ i, IsLimit (c i)) :     IsLimit (coneOfConeCompEval c) where   lift s i := (P i).lift (coneCompEval s i)   fac s j := by     funext i     exact (P i).fac (coneCompEval s i) j   uniq s m w := by     funext i     exact (P i).uniq (coneCompEval s i) (m i) fun j => congr_fun (w j) i
CategoryTheory.pi.coneOfConeEvalIsLimit.description: This definition states that if there is a family of limit cones over the evaluation of a functor, then combining them results in a limit cone over the original functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.ReflectsLimits.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.ReflectsLimits.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) : Type (max (max (max (max u₁ u₂) v₁) v₂) (v₂ + 1))
CategoryTheory.Limits.ReflectsLimits.comment:
A functor `F : C ⥤ D` reflects (small) limits if
whenever the image of a cone over some `K : J ⥤ C` under `F` is a limit cone in `D`,
the cone was already a limit cone in `C`.
Note that we do not assume a priori that `D` actually has any limits.
CategoryTheory.Limits.ReflectsLimits.fullDefinition: abbrev ReflectsLimits (F : C ⥤ D) :=   ReflectsLimitsOfSize.{v₂, v₂} F
CategoryTheory.Limits.ReflectsLimits.description: This definition characterizes a functor as reflecting limits if the limit status of a cone in the target category implies that the cone was already a limit in the source category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.ReflectsColimits.description: This definition indicates that a functor reflects colimits if the cocones that appear as colimit cocones in the target category must also be colimit cocones in the source category.

CategoryTheory.preservesColimitNatIso.fullDefinition: def preservesColimitNatIso : colim ⋙ G ≅ (whiskeringRight J C D).obj G ⋙ colim :=   NatIso.ofComponents (fun F => preservesColimitIso G F)     (by       intro _ _ f       rw [← Iso.inv_comp_eq, ← Category.assoc, ← Iso.eq_comp_inv]       apply colimit.hom_ext; intro j       dsimp       erw [ι_colimMap_assoc]       simp only [ι_preservesColimitsIso_inv, whiskerRight_app, Category.assoc,         ι_preservesColimitsIso_inv_assoc, ← G.map_comp]       erw [ι_colimMap])

CategoryTheory.PreservesImage.iso.fullDefinition: def iso {X Y : A} (f : X ⟶ Y) : image (L.map f) ≅ L.obj (image f) :=   let aux1 : StrongEpiMonoFactorisation (L.map f) :=     { I := L.obj (Limits.image f)       m := L.map <| Limits.image.ι _       m_mono := preserves_mono_of_preservesLimit _ _       e := L.map <| factorThruImage _       e_strong_epi := @strongEpi_of_epi B _ _ _ _ _ (preserves_epi_of_preservesColimit L _)       fac := by rw [← L.map_comp, Limits.image.fac] }   IsImage.isoExt (Image.isImage (L.map f)) aux1.toMonoIsImage

CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesZeroMorp.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) preservesZeroMorphisms_of_isLeftAdjoint (F : C ⥤ D) [IsLeftAdjoint F] :     PreservesZeroMorphisms F where   map_zero X Y := by     let adj := Adjunction.ofIsLeftAdjoint F     calc       F.map (0 : X ⟶ Y) = F.map 0 ≫ F.map (adj.unit.app Y) ≫ adj.counit.app (F.obj Y) := ?_       _ = F.map 0 ≫ F.map ((rightAdjoint F).map (0 : F.obj X ⟶ _)) ≫ adj.counit.app (F.obj Y) := ?_       _ = 0 := ?_     · rw [Adjunction.left_triangle_components]       exact (Category.comp_id _).symm     · simp only [← Category.assoc, ← F.map_comp, zero_comp]     · simp only [Adjunction.counit_naturality, comp_zero]

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.isZero_iff: A functor is a zero object in a category if and only if it maps every object from its source category to a zero object in its target category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.ofIsZero: This definition states that if a functor is zero and a cone's point is also zero, then that cone is a limit in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.isZero: If every object in a category is mapped to a zero object in another category via a functor, then that functor itself is a zero object.

CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesLimitsOf.fullDefinition: def preservesLimitsOfShapeOfIsZero : PreservesLimitsOfShape J G where   preservesLimit {K} := ⟨fun hc => by     rw [Functor.isZero_iff] at hG     exact IsLimit.ofIsZero _ ((K ⋙ G).isZero (fun X ↦ hG _)) (hG _)⟩
CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesLimitsOf.description: This definition asserts that a zero functor preserves limits of any shape when mapping between categories.

CategoryTheory.Limits.KernelFork.isLimit.fullDefinition: def isLimitMapConeEquiv :     IsLimit (G.mapCone c) ≃ IsLimit (c.map G) := by   refine (IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv ?_ _).symm.trans (IsLimit.equivIsoLimit ?_)   refine parallelPair.ext (Iso.refl _) (Iso.refl _) ?_ ?_ <;> simp   exact Cones.ext (Iso.refl _) (by rintro (_|_) <;> aesop_cat)
CategoryTheory.Limits.KernelFork.isLimit.description: This definition establishes a bijective correspondence between the conditions for a mapped cone of a kernel fork to be a limit and the conditions for a kernel fork itself to be a limit, under functors that preserve zero morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitMapConeFork.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitMapConeForkEquiv'.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (G : C ⥤ D) [G.PreservesZeroMorphisms] {X Y Z : C}
  {f : X ⟶ Y} {h : Z ⟶ X} (w : h ≫ f = 0) :
  IsLimit (G.mapCone (KernelFork.ofι h w)) ≃ IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (G.map h) ⋯)
CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitMapConeFork.comment:
The map of a kernel fork is a limit iff
the kernel fork consisting of the mapped morphisms is a limit.
This essentially lets us commute `KernelFork.ofι` with `Functor.mapCone`.

This is a variant of `isLimitMapConeForkEquiv` for equalizers,
which we can't use directly between `G.map 0 = 0` does not hold definitionally.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitMapCocone.comment:
The map of a cokernel cofork is a colimit iff
the cokernel cofork consisting of the mapped morphisms is a colimit.
This essentially lets us commute `CokernelCofork.ofπ` with `Functor.mapCocone`.

This is a variant of `isColimitMapCoconeCoforkEquiv` for equalizers,
which we can't use directly between `G.map 0 = 0` does not hold definitionally.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBinaryBip.fullDefinition: def preservesBinaryBiproductOfPreservesBiproduct (F : C ⥤ D) [PreservesZeroMorphisms F] (X Y : C)     [PreservesBiproduct (pairFunction X Y) F] : PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F where   preserves {b} hb :=     { isLimit :=         IsLimit.ofIsoLimit             ((IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv (diagramIsoPair _) _).symm               (isBilimitOfPreserves F (b.toBiconeIsBilimit.symm hb)).isLimit) <|           Cones.ext (Iso.refl _) fun j => by             rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩ <;> simp       isColimit :=         IsColimit.ofIsoColimit             ((IsColimit.precomposeInvEquiv (diagramIsoPair _) _).symm               (isBilimitOfPreserves F (b.toBiconeIsBilimit.symm hb)).isColimit) <|           Cocones.ext (Iso.refl _) fun j => by             rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩ <;> simp }

`F.obj (⨁ f) ⟶ ⨁ (F.obj ∘ f)`.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct_hom.{w₁, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] {J : Type w₁} (F : C ⥤ D) (f : J → C) [HasBiproduct f]
  [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesBiproduct f F] :
  (F.mapBiproduct f).hom = biproduct.lift fun j => F.map (biproduct.π f j)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.π: This definition describes a function that provides the morphism from the cone point of a bicone to a specific object in the diagram associated with the bicone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift: This definition describes a method for constructing a morphism into a biproduct from a collection of morphisms into its individual summands.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.π: This definition specifies a projection morphism from a biproduct object to an individual summand in the context of category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a morphism from an object to the biproduct of two summands using given morphisms from that object to each summand.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct_hom.description: This theorem states that the induced morphism from the biproduct of a collection of objects under a functor is equal to the lift of the maps obtained by applying the functor to the projections of the original biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct_inv.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct_inv.{w₁, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] {J : Type w₁} (F : C ⥤ D) (f : J → C) [HasBiproduct f]
  [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesBiproduct f F] :
  (F.mapBiproduct f).inv = biproduct.desc fun j => F.map (biproduct.ι f j)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.ι: This definition describes a function that provides the morphism from a specific object in the diagram associated with a bicone to the cone point of that bicone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.desc: This definition specifies that given a collection of morphisms from the summands of a biproduct, there exists a corresponding morphism from the entire biproduct to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι: This definition specifies an inclusion morphism from an individual summand to a biproduct object in the context of category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.desc: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism from a binary biproduct to another object by using a pair of morphisms originating from each summand of that biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct_inv.description: This theorem states that the inverse of the morphism induced by a functor on a biproduct is equal to the morphism constructed from the projections of the biproduct, given that the functor preserves both zero morphisms and biproducts.

CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison.comment:
As for products, any functor between categories with binary biproducts gives rise to a
morphism `F.obj (X ⊞ Y) ⟶ F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift: This definition describes a method for constructing a morphism into a biproduct from a collection of morphisms into its individual summands.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a morphism from an object to the biproduct of two summands using given morphisms from that object to each summand.

CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison.fullDefinition: def biprodComparison : F.obj (X ⊞ Y) ⟶ F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y :=   biprod.lift (F.map biprod.fst) (F.map biprod.snd)
CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison.description: This definition establishes a morphism between the biproduct of two objects in one category and the biproduct of their images in another category under a functor that preserves binary biproducts.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.fst: This definition specifies the morphism that projects an element from a binary biproduct onto its first component.

CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison_.description: This theorem establishes that the composite morphism from a biproduct comparison map to the first component is equivalent to the image of the first component morphism under the functor, given that both the original and the image categories have binary biproducts.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.snd: This definition specifies the morphism that maps an element from a binary biproduct to its second component.

CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison_.description: The theorem asserts that the composition of the biproduct comparison morphism and the second projection morphism equals the image under the functor of the second projection morphism when both the original and image objects have binary biproducts.

CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison'.comment:
As for coproducts, any functor between categories with binary biproducts gives rise to a
morphism `F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y ⟶ F.obj (X ⊞ Y)`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.desc: This definition specifies that given a collection of morphisms from the summands of a biproduct, there exists a corresponding morphism from the entire biproduct to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.desc: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism from a binary biproduct to another object by using a pair of morphisms originating from each summand of that biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison'.fullDefinition: def biprodComparison' : F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y ⟶ F.obj (X ⊞ Y) :=   biprod.desc (F.map biprod.inl) (F.map biprod.inr)
CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison'.description: This definition states that for any functor between categories with binary biproducts, there is a morphism that relates the biproduct of the images of two objects to the image of the biproduct of those objects.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.inl: This definition describes the morphism that represents the inclusion of an object into the first summand of a binary biproduct.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison': This definition states that for any functor between categories with binary biproducts, there is a morphism that relates the biproduct of the images of two objects to the image of the biproduct of those objects.

CategoryTheory.Functor.inl_biprodCompari.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of a specific morphism with the functor's biproduct comparison for two objects equals the functor's image of the canonical inclusion morphism if both the objects and their images under the functor possess binary biproducts.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.inr: This definition specifies the morphism that includes an object into the second component of a binary biproduct structure in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison': This definition states that for any functor between categories with binary biproducts, there is a morphism that relates the biproduct of the images of two objects to the image of the biproduct of those objects.

CategoryTheory.Functor.inr_biprodCompari.description: This theorem asserts that the composition of the right-inclusion morphism of a binary biproduct and a specific functorial comparison morphism is equal to the image under the functor of the right-inclusion morphism when both the original and image objects have binary biproducts.

CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison'.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison'_comp_biprodComparison.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) (X Y : C)
  [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y] [HasBinaryBiproduct (F.obj X) (F.obj Y)] [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] :
  F.biprodComparison' X Y ≫ F.biprodComparison X Y = 𝟙 (F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y)
CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison'.comment:
The composition in the opposite direction is equal to the identity if and only if `F` preserves
the biproduct, see `preservesBinaryBiproduct_of_monoBiprodComparison`.
CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison'.description: This theorem states that when a functor preserves biproducts, the composition of the morphism relating the biproduct of the images of two objects with the morphism of the biproduct of those objects equals the identity morphism on the biproduct of the images.

CategoryTheory.Functor.splitEpiBiprodCom.comment: `biprodComparison F X Y` is a split epi.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison: This definition establishes a morphism between the biproduct of two objects in one category and the biproduct of their images in another category under a functor that preserves binary biproducts.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison': This definition states that for any functor between categories with binary biproducts, there is a morphism that relates the biproduct of the images of two objects to the image of the biproduct of those objects.

CategoryTheory.Functor.splitEpiBiprodCom.fullDefinition: def splitEpiBiprodComparison : SplitEpi (biprodComparison F X Y) where   section_ := biprodComparison' F X Y   id := by aesop
CategoryTheory.Functor.splitEpiBiprodCom.description: This definition states that the comparison morphism of the binary biproduct under a functor is a split epimorphism when both the source and target categories have binary biproducts and the functor preserves zero morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Functor.splitMonoBiprodCo.comment: `biprodComparison' F X Y` is a split mono.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison: This definition establishes a morphism between the biproduct of two objects in one category and the biproduct of their images in another category under a functor that preserves binary biproducts.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.biprodComparison': This definition states that for any functor between categories with binary biproducts, there is a morphism that relates the biproduct of the images of two objects to the image of the biproduct of those objects.

CategoryTheory.Functor.splitMonoBiprodCo.fullDefinition: def splitMonoBiprodComparison' : SplitMono (biprodComparison' F X Y) where   retraction := biprodComparison F X Y   id := by aesop
CategoryTheory.Functor.splitMonoBiprodCo.description: This definition asserts that the morphism induced by a functor on the comparison of binary biproducts is a split mono when the functor preserves zero morphisms and the biproduct structure.

CategoryTheory.Functor.hasBinaryBiproduc.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.hasBinaryBiproduct_of_preserves.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) (X Y : C)
  [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y] [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F] :
  HasBinaryBiproduct (F.obj X) (F.obj Y)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBinaryBicone: This definition creates a new binary bicone from an existing binary bicone by applying a functor that preserves zero morphisms to its objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesBiproduct: This definition asserts that if a functor preserves biproducts, then it will transform every bilimit bicone over a specified diagram into a bilimit bicone over the image of that diagram under the functor.
This definition asserts that if a functor preserves biproducts of a specific shape, then it also preserves the biproducts of any diagram indexed by that shape.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFiniteBip: This definition establishes that a functor preserves finite biproducts if it maintains biproducts for any finite indexing set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesBiproduct: This definition indicates that a functor preserves biproducts if it can maintain biproducts for any possible indexing shape.
This theorem establishes that if a functor preserves biproducts for every shape of diagram, then it preserves biproducts in general.
This theorem states that if a functor preserves biproducts for any indexed family of objects, then it specifically preserves biproducts for diagrams of a given shape.

This theorem asserts that if a functor can take any bilimit bicone over a diagram and produce a bilimit bicone over its image while preserving its structure, then it also preserves the biproducts associated with that diagram.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesBinaryBip: This definition states that if a functor preserves binary biproducts for two objects, then it maps any bilimit bicone over those objects to a bilimit bicone over their images under the functor.
This definition asserts that a functor preserves binary biproducts if it maintains the binary biproduct structure for every pair of objects within its categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBiproduct.mk: This theorem proves that the existence of a limit bicone for a collection of objects in a category implies that these objects have a biproduct in that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.bicone: This definition constructs a bicone for a functor that serves as both a limit cone and a colimit cocone, given that the functor possesses a biproduct.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.isBilimi: This definition asserts that if a functor has a biproduct, then the corresponding bicone structure is a bilimit bicone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproduct: This theorem establishes that the presence of binary biproduct data for two objects in a category guarantees the existence of a binary biproduct for those objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBiproduct.bi: This definition establishes a bicone structure that serves as both a limit cone and a colimit cocone for two objects within a category that has a binary biproduct.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBiproduct.is: This definition states that the bicone formed by two objects in a category, when they have a binary biproduct, satisfies the property of being a bilimit.

CategoryTheory.Functor.hasBinaryBiproduc.fullDefinition: instance hasBinaryBiproduct_of_preserves : HasBinaryBiproduct (F.obj X) (F.obj Y) :=   HasBinaryBiproduct.mk     { bicone := F.mapBinaryBicone (BinaryBiproduct.bicone X Y)       isBilimit := PreservesBinaryBiproduct.preserves (BinaryBiproduct.isBilimit _ _) }
CategoryTheory.Functor.hasBinaryBiproduc.description: This definition states that if a functor preserves binary biproducts and certain conditions are met in both categories, then the image of the functor applied to two objects also has a binary biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod.comment:
If `F` preserves a binary biproduct, we get a definitionally nice isomorphism
`F.obj (X ⊞ Y) ≅ F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesBiproduct: This definition asserts that if a functor preserves biproducts, then it will transform every bilimit bicone over a specified diagram into a bilimit bicone over the image of that diagram under the functor.
This definition asserts that if a functor preserves biproducts of a specific shape, then it also preserves the biproducts of any diagram indexed by that shape.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesFiniteBip: This definition establishes that a functor preserves finite biproducts if it maintains biproducts for any finite indexing set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesBiproduct: This definition indicates that a functor preserves biproducts if it can maintain biproducts for any possible indexing shape.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesBinaryBip: This definition states that if a functor preserves binary biproducts for two objects, then it maps any bilimit bicone over those objects to a bilimit bicone over their images under the functor.
This definition asserts that a functor preserves binary biproducts if it maintains the binary biproduct structure for every pair of objects within its categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.isBilimi: This definition asserts that if a functor has a biproduct, then the corresponding bicone structure is a bilimit bicone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.uniqueUp: This definition asserts that biproducts in a category are uniquely determined up to isomorphism, providing an isomorphism that relates a bilimit to the biproduct in a way that allows for defining simple inverses between associated morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBiproduct.is: This definition states that the bicone formed by two objects in a category, when they have a binary biproduct, satisfies the property of being a bilimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.uniqueUpToI: This definition asserts that binary biproducts in a category are unique up to isomorphism, accompanied by a specific isomorphism established through bilimit properties.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod.fullDefinition: def mapBiprod : F.obj (X ⊞ Y) ≅ F.obj X ⊞ F.obj Y :=   biprod.uniqueUpToIso _ _ (PreservesBinaryBiproduct.preserves (BinaryBiproduct.isBilimit _ _))
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod.description: This definition states that if a functor preserves binary biproducts, there exists a natural isomorphism between the image of the biproduct of two objects and the biproduct of their images under that functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod_hom.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod_hom.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) (X Y : C) [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y]
  [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F] :
  (F.mapBiprod X Y).hom = biprod.lift (F.map biprod.fst) (F.map biprod.snd)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift: This definition describes a method for constructing a morphism into a biproduct from a collection of morphisms into its individual summands.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a morphism from an object to the biproduct of two summands using given morphisms from that object to each summand.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod_hom.description: This theorem states that for a functor that preserves zero morphisms and binary biproducts, the hom-set of the functor's mapped biproduct is equal to the biproduct lift of the functor's images of the individual components.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod_inv.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod_inv.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) (X Y : C) [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y]
  [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F] :
  (F.mapBiprod X Y).inv = biprod.desc (F.map biprod.inl) (F.map biprod.inr)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.desc: This definition specifies that given a collection of morphisms from the summands of a biproduct, there exists a corresponding morphism from the entire biproduct to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.desc: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism from a binary biproduct to another object by using a pair of morphisms originating from each summand of that biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod_inv.description: This theorem establishes that the inverse of the morphism obtained from a functor mapping a binary biproduct is equal to the morphism constructed from the images of the summands of that biproduct under the functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.map_lift.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.map_lift_mapBiprod.{w₁, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms]
  {J : Type w₁} (f : J → C) [HasBiproduct f] [PreservesBiproduct f F] {W : C} (g : (j : J) → W ⟶ f j) :
  F.map (biproduct.lift g) ≫ (F.mapBiproduct f).hom = biproduct.lift fun j => F.map (g j)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift: This definition describes a method for constructing a morphism into a biproduct from a collection of morphisms into its individual summands.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the image of the biproduct under a functor and the biproduct of the images of the objects under that functor, provided the functor preserves zero morphisms and biproducts.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a morphism from an object to the biproduct of two summands using given morphisms from that object to each summand.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.map_lift.description: This theorem states that for a functor that preserves biproducts and zero morphisms, the image of the lift from a collection of morphisms to a biproduct coincides with the lift of the images of those morphisms under the functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapBipro.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapBiproduct_inv_map_desc.{w₁, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms]
  {J : Type w₁} (f : J → C) [HasBiproduct f] [PreservesBiproduct f F] {W : C} (g : (j : J) → f j ⟶ W) :
  (F.mapBiproduct f).inv ≫ F.map (biproduct.desc g) = biproduct.desc fun j => F.map (g j)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.desc: This definition specifies that given a collection of morphisms from the summands of a biproduct, there exists a corresponding morphism from the entire biproduct to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the image of the biproduct under a functor and the biproduct of the images of the objects under that functor, provided the functor preserves zero morphisms and biproducts.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.desc: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism from a binary biproduct to another object by using a pair of morphisms originating from each summand of that biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapBipro.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between the inverse of the functorial map of a biproduct and the composition with the functor's mapping of a morphism described by the biproduct's universal property.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapBipro.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapBiproduct_hom_desc.{w₁, v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms]
  {J : Type w₁} (f : J → C) [HasBiproduct f] [PreservesBiproduct f F] {W : C} (g : (j : J) → f j ⟶ W) :
  ((F.mapBiproduct f).hom ≫ biproduct.desc fun j => F.map (g j)) = F.map (biproduct.desc g)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.desc: This definition specifies that given a collection of morphisms from the summands of a biproduct, there exists a corresponding morphism from the entire biproduct to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiproduct: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the image of the biproduct under a functor and the biproduct of the images of the objects under that functor, provided the functor preserves zero morphisms and biproducts.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.desc: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism from a binary biproduct to another object by using a pair of morphisms originating from each summand of that biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.mapBipro.description: This theorem establishes that the morphism from the image of a biproduct under a functor, combined with the morphism derived from the images of the components, is equal to the image of the morphism obtained from the original biproduct's components, provided the functor preserves biproducts and zero morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.map_lift_ma.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.map_lift_mapBiprod.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] (X Y : C)
  [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y] [PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F] {W : C} (f : W ⟶ X) (g : W ⟶ Y) :
  F.map (biprod.lift f g) ≫ (F.mapBiprod X Y).hom = biprod.lift (F.map f) (F.map g)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift: This definition describes a method for constructing a morphism into a biproduct from a collection of morphisms into its individual summands.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod: This definition states that if a functor preserves binary biproducts, there exists a natural isomorphism between the image of the biproduct of two objects and the biproduct of their images under that functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.map_lift: This theorem states that for a functor that preserves biproducts and zero morphisms, the image of the lift from a collection of morphisms to a biproduct coincides with the lift of the images of those morphisms under the functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.map_lift_ma.description: This theorem establishes that the image under a functor of the lift of two morphisms into a binary biproduct is equal to the composition of the functor applied to the lift and the morphism associated with the biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift_mapBip.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift_mapBiprod.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] (X Y : C)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBiprod: This definition states that if a functor preserves binary biproducts, there exists a natural isomorphism between the image of the biproduct of two objects and the biproduct of their images under that functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift_mapBip.description: This theorem establishes a relation involving a functor that preserves binary biproducts, indicating that the composite of the lift of the functor's images corresponds to the image under the functor of the lift of the original morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.mapBiprod_i.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.mapBiprod_inv_map_desc.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasZeroMorphisms D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] (X Y : C)

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.sectionsEqui.fullDefinition: def sectionsEquiv {J : Type*} [Category J] (K : J ⥤ Type u) :     K.sections ≃ (K ⋙ uliftFunctor.{v, u}).sections where   toFun := fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨fun j => ⟨u j⟩, fun f => by simp [hu f]⟩   invFun := fun ⟨u, hu⟩ => ⟨fun j => (u j).down, @fun j j' f => by simp [← hu f]⟩   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := rfl
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.sectionsEqui.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the sections of a functor and the sections of its composition with a lifting functor, which is instrumental in demonstrating that the lifting functor preserves limits that may not exist in the source category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.op: This definition establishes a correspondence between colimit cocones and limit cones by showing that if a cocone is a colimit, its opposite is a limit.
