CategoryTheory.FunctorCategory.prodPrese.comment:
If `X × -` preserves colimits in `D` for any `X : D`, then the product functor `F ⨯ -` for
`F : C ⥤ D` also preserves colimits.

Note this is (mathematically) a special case of the statement that
"if limits commute with colimits in `D`, then they do as well in `C ⥤ D`"
but the story in Lean is a bit more complex, and this statement isn't directly a special case.
That is, even with a formalised proof of the general statement, there would still need to be some
work to convert to this version: namely, the natural isomorphism
`(evaluation C D).obj k ⋙ prod.functor.obj (F.obj k) ≅
  prod.functor.obj F ⋙ (evaluation C D).obj k`

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryProducts: This definition asserts that a category possesses binary products if it allows the formation of a product for every pair of its objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimits: This definition asserts that a category possesses all small colimits if it can form colimits for every diagram whose size is determined by its morphism sets.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesColimits: This definition characterizes a functor that maintains the structure of small colimit cones across diagrams in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluationJointlyR: This definition establishes that a cocone over a functor is considered a colimit if each evaluation of that cocone in the context of specific objects exhibits the colimit property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.evaluation: This definition describes a functor that evaluates a morphism in a category at a specific object, yielding a functor from the category of functors to another category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCocone: This definition states that applying a functor to a cocone results in a new cocone formed over the composition of the original functor with the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitOfPreserv: This definition states that if a functor preserves colimits and a cocone is a colimit in the source category, then the mapped cocone in the target category is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.mapCocon: This definition asserts that if two functors are naturally isomorphic, then a cocone being a colimit for one functor implies that it is also a colimit for the other functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.ofComponents: This definition outlines the process of creating a natural isomorphism between functors by providing isomorphisms at the object level and verifying naturality in one direction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prodComparison: This definition establishes a morphism that compares the product of two objects in one category to the product of their images under a functor in another category, provided that both categories have binary products.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prodComparison_nat: This theorem shows the naturality of the product comparison morphism by asserting a specific relationship between mappings in a category, ensuring that the product structures commute consistently with the functor applied to those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesLimit.pre: This definition specifies that if a functor preserves limits for a particular diagram, then any limit cone in the source category is transformed into a limit cone in the target category under the functor's mapping.

CategoryTheory.FunctorCategory.prodPrese.fullDefinition: def FunctorCategory.prodPreservesColimits [HasBinaryProducts D] [HasColimits D]     [∀ X : D, PreservesColimits (prod.functor.obj X)] (F : C ⥤ D) :     PreservesColimits (prod.functor.obj F) where   preservesColimitsOfShape {J : Type u} [Category.{u, u} J] :=     {       preservesColimit := fun {K : J ⥤ C ⥤ D} =>         ( {           preserves := fun {c : Cocone K} (t : IsColimit c) => by             apply evaluationJointlyReflectsColimits _ fun {k} => ?_             change IsColimit ((prod.functor.obj F ⋙ (evaluation _ _).obj k).mapCocone c)             let this :=               isColimitOfPreserves ((evaluation C D).obj k ⋙ prod.functor.obj (F.obj k)) t             apply IsColimit.mapCoconeEquiv _ this             apply (NatIso.ofComponents _ _).symm             · intro G               apply asIso (prodComparison ((evaluation C D).obj k) F G)             · intro G G'               apply prodComparison_natural ((evaluation C D).obj k) (𝟙 F) } ) }
CategoryTheory.FunctorCategory.prodPrese.description: This definition states that if a functor preserves colimits for every object in a category, then the product functor associated with that functor also preserves colimits.

  {J : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} J] {K : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} K] {F : J ⥤ K ⥤ C} (c : Cone F)
  (t : (k : K) → IsLimit (((evaluation K C).obj k).mapCone c)) : IsLimit c
CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluationJointlyR.comment:
The evaluation functors jointly reflect limits: that is, to show a cone is a limit of `F`
it suffices to show that each evaluation cone is a limit. In other words, to prove a cone is
limiting you can show it's pointwise limiting.

CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluationJointlyR.fullDefinition: def evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits {F : J ⥤ K ⥤ C} (c : Cone F)     (t : ∀ k : K, IsLimit (((evaluation K C).obj k).mapCone c)) : IsLimit c where   lift s :=     { app := fun k => (t k).lift ⟨s.pt.obj k, whiskerRight s.π ((evaluation K C).obj k)⟩       naturality := fun X Y f =>         (t Y).hom_ext fun j => by           rw [assoc, (t Y).fac _ j]           simpa using             ((t X).fac_assoc ⟨s.pt.obj X, whiskerRight s.π ((evaluation K C).obj X)⟩ j _).symm }   fac s j := by ext k; exact (t k).fac _ j   uniq s m w := by     ext x     exact (t x).hom_ext fun j =>       (congr_app (w j) x).trans         ((t x).fac ⟨s.pt.obj _, whiskerRight s.π ((evaluation K C).obj _)⟩ j).symm
CategoryTheory.Limits.evaluationJointlyR.description: This definition establishes that a cone over a functor is considered a limit if each evaluation of that cone in the context of particular objects exhibits the limit property.

CategoryTheory.Limits.combineCones.comment:
Given a functor `F` and a collection of limit cones for each diagram `X ↦ F X k`, we can stitch
them together to give a cone for the diagram `F`.
`combinedIsLimit` shows that the new cone is limiting, and `evalCombined` shows it is
(essentially) made up of the original cones.

CategoryTheory.Limits.combineCones.fullDefinition: def combineCones (F : J ⥤ K ⥤ C) (c : ∀ k : K, LimitCone (F.flip.obj k)) : Cone F where   pt :=     { obj := fun k => (c k).cone.pt       map := fun {k₁} {k₂} f => (c k₂).isLimit.lift ⟨_, (c k₁).cone.π ≫ F.flip.map f⟩       map_id := fun k =>         (c k).isLimit.hom_ext fun j => by           dsimp           simp       map_comp := fun {k₁} {k₂} {k₃} f₁ f₂ => (c k₃).isLimit.hom_ext fun j => by simp }   π :=     { app := fun j => { app := fun k => (c k).cone.π.app j }       naturality := fun j₁ j₂ g => by ext k; exact (c k).cone.π.naturality g }

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesCoequaliz.fullDefinition: def preservesCoequalizersOfPreservesPushoutsAndBinaryCoproducts [HasBinaryCoproducts C]     [HasPushouts C] [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) G]     [PreservesColimitsOfShape WalkingSpan G] : PreservesColimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair G :=   ⟨fun {K} =>     preservesColimitOfPreservesColimitCocone (coequalizerCoconeIsColimit K) <|       { desc := fun c => by           refine (PreservesPushout.iso _ _ _).inv ≫ pushout.desc ?_ ?_ ?_           · exact c.ι.app WalkingParallelPair.one           · exact c.ι.app WalkingParallelPair.one           apply (mapIsColimitOfPreservesOfIsColimit G _ _ (coprodIsCoprod _ _)).hom_ext           rintro (_ | _)           · simp only [BinaryCofan.ι_app_left, BinaryCofan.mk_inl, Category.assoc, ←               G.map_comp_assoc, coprod.inl_desc]           · simp only [BinaryCofan.ι_app_right, BinaryCofan.mk_inr, Category.assoc, ←               G.map_comp_assoc, coprod.inr_desc]             exact               (c.ι.naturality WalkingParallelPairHom.left).trans                 (c.ι.naturality WalkingParallelPairHom.right).symm         fac := fun c j => by           rcases j with (_ | _) <;>             simp only [Functor.mapCocone_ι_app, Cocone.ofCofork_ι, Category.id_comp,               eqToHom_refl, Category.assoc, Functor.map_comp, Cofork.ofπ_ι_app, pushout.inl_desc,               PreservesPushout.inl_iso_inv_assoc]           exact (c.ι.naturality WalkingParallelPairHom.left).trans (Category.comp_id _)         uniq := fun s m h => by           rw [Iso.eq_inv_comp]           have := h WalkingParallelPair.one           dsimp [coequalizerCocone] at this           ext <;>             simp only [PreservesPushout.inl_iso_hom_assoc, Category.id_comp, pushout.inl_desc,               pushout.inr_desc, PreservesPushout.inr_iso_hom_assoc, ← pushoutInl_eq_pushout_inr, ←               this] }⟩

isBinaryProductOfIsTerminalIsPullback.fullDefinition: def isBinaryProductOfIsTerminalIsPullback (F : Discrete WalkingPair ⥤ C) (c : Cone F) {X : C}     (hX : IsTerminal X) (f : F.obj ⟨WalkingPair.left⟩ ⟶ X) (g : F.obj ⟨WalkingPair.right⟩ ⟶ X)     (hc : IsLimit       (PullbackCone.mk (c.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.left⟩) (c.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.right⟩ : _) <|         hX.hom_ext (_ ≫ f) (_ ≫ g))) : IsLimit c where   lift s :=     hc.lift       (PullbackCone.mk (s.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.left⟩) (s.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.right⟩) (hX.hom_ext _ _))   fac s j :=     Discrete.casesOn j fun j =>       WalkingPair.casesOn j (hc.fac _ WalkingCospan.left) (hc.fac _ WalkingCospan.right)   uniq s m J := by     let c' :=       PullbackCone.mk (m ≫ c.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.left⟩) (m ≫ c.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.right⟩ : _)         (hX.hom_ext (_ ≫ f) (_ ≫ g))     dsimp; rw [← J, ← J]     apply hc.hom_ext     rintro (_ | (_ | _)) <;> simp only [PullbackCone.mk_π_app_one, PullbackCone.mk_π_app]     exacts [(Category.assoc _ _ _).symm.trans (hc.fac_assoc c' WalkingCospan.left f).symm,       (hc.fac c' WalkingCospan.left).symm, (hc.fac c' WalkingCospan.right).symm]

CategoryTheory.extendFan.comment:
Given `n+1` objects of `C`, a fan for the last `n` with point `c₁.pt` and
a binary fan on `c₁.pt` and `f 0`, we can build a fan for all `n+1`.

limit.

CategoryTheory.extendFanIsLimit.fullDefinition: def extendFanIsLimit {n : ℕ} (f : Fin (n + 1) → C) {c₁ : Fan fun i : Fin n => f i.succ}     {c₂ : BinaryFan (f 0) c₁.pt} (t₁ : IsLimit c₁) (t₂ : IsLimit c₂) :     IsLimit (extendFan c₁ c₂) where   lift s := by     apply (BinaryFan.IsLimit.lift' t₂ (s.π.app ⟨0⟩) _).1     apply t₁.lift ⟨_, Discrete.natTrans fun ⟨i⟩ => s.π.app ⟨i.succ⟩⟩   fac := fun s ⟨j⟩ => by     refine Fin.inductionOn j ?_ ?_     · apply (BinaryFan.IsLimit.lift' t₂ _ _).2.1     · rintro i -       dsimp only [extendFan_π_app]       rw [Fin.cases_succ, ← assoc, (BinaryFan.IsLimit.lift' t₂ _ _).2.2, t₁.fac]       rfl   uniq s m w := by     apply BinaryFan.IsLimit.hom_ext t₂     · rw [(BinaryFan.IsLimit.lift' t₂ _ _).2.1]       apply w ⟨0⟩     · rw [(BinaryFan.IsLimit.lift' t₂ _ _).2.2]       apply t₁.uniq ⟨_, _⟩       rintro ⟨j⟩       rw [assoc]       dsimp only [Discrete.natTrans_app]       rw [← w ⟨j.succ⟩]       dsimp only [extendFan_π_app]       rw [Fin.cases_succ]

CategoryTheory.extendCofan.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {n : ℕ} {f : Fin (n + 1) → C}
  (c₁ : Cofan fun i => f i.succ) (c₂ : BinaryCofan (f 0) c₁.pt) : Cofan f
CategoryTheory.extendCofan.comment:
Given `n+1` objects of `C`, a cofan for the last `n` with point `c₁.pt`
and a binary cofan on `c₁.X` and `f 0`, we can build a cofan for all `n+1`.

In `extendCofanIsColimit` we show that if the two given cofans are colimits,
then this cofan is also a colimit.

CategoryTheory.extendCofanIsColimit.fullDefinition: def extendCofanIsColimit {n : ℕ} (f : Fin (n + 1) → C) {c₁ : Cofan fun i : Fin n => f i.succ}     {c₂ : BinaryCofan (f 0) c₁.pt} (t₁ : IsColimit c₁) (t₂ : IsColimit c₂) :     IsColimit (extendCofan c₁ c₂) where   desc s := by     apply (BinaryCofan.IsColimit.desc' t₂ (s.ι.app ⟨0⟩) _).1     apply t₁.desc ⟨_, Discrete.natTrans fun i => s.ι.app ⟨i.as.succ⟩⟩   fac s := by     rintro ⟨j⟩     refine Fin.inductionOn j ?_ ?_     · apply (BinaryCofan.IsColimit.desc' t₂ _ _).2.1     · rintro i -       dsimp only [extendCofan_ι_app]       rw [Fin.cases_succ, assoc, (BinaryCofan.IsColimit.desc' t₂ _ _).2.2, t₁.fac]       rfl   uniq s m w := by     apply BinaryCofan.IsColimit.hom_ext t₂     · rw [(BinaryCofan.IsColimit.desc' t₂ _ _).2.1]       apply w ⟨0⟩     · rw [(BinaryCofan.IsColimit.desc' t₂ _ _).2.2]       apply t₁.uniq ⟨_, _⟩       rintro ⟨j⟩       dsimp only [Discrete.natTrans_app]       rw [← w ⟨j.succ⟩]       dsimp only [extendCofan_ι_app]       rw [Fin.cases_succ, assoc]

CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimitOfHasCop.fullDefinition: def buildIsColimit (t₁ : IsColimit c₁) (t₂ : IsColimit c₂) (hi : IsColimit i) :     IsColimit (buildColimit s t hs ht i) where   desc q := by     refine hi.desc (Cofork.ofπ ?_ ?_)     · refine t₂.desc (Cofan.mk _ fun j => ?_)       apply q.ι.app j     · apply t₁.hom_ext       intro j       cases' j with j       have reassoced_s (f : (p : J × J) × (p.fst ⟶ p.snd)) {W : C} (h : _ ⟶ W) :         c₁.ι.app ⟨f⟩ ≫ s ≫ h = F.map f.snd ≫ c₂.ι.app ⟨f.fst.snd⟩ ≫ h := by           simp only [← Category.assoc]           apply eq_whisker (hs f)       have reassoced_t (f : (p : J × J) × (p.fst ⟶ p.snd)) {W : C} (h : _ ⟶ W) :         c₁.ι.app ⟨f⟩ ≫ t ≫ h = c₂.ι.app ⟨f.fst.fst⟩ ≫ h := by           simp only [← Category.assoc]           apply eq_whisker (ht f)       simp [reassoced_s, reassoced_t]   uniq q m w :=     hi.hom_ext       (i.coequalizer_ext         (t₂.hom_ext fun j => by           cases' j with j           simpa using w j))   fac s j := by simp

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/002Q>.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoequalizers: This definition asserts that a category includes a coequalizer for every pair of morphisms, indicating the existence of a universal construction that identifies and "collapses" equivalent elements.

CategoryTheory.Limits.hasFiniteColimits_.description: A category that has both finite coproducts and coequalizers is guaranteed to have all finite colimits.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer.condit: The theorem asserts that the two morphisms from an object to a coequalizer, formed by the composition of two given morphisms, are equal when the coequalizer exists.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesColimitOf.fullDefinition: noncomputable def preservesColimitOfPreservesCoequalizersAndCoproduct :     PreservesColimitsOfShape J G where   preservesColimit {K} := by     let P := ∐ K.obj     let Q := ∐ fun f : Σp : J × J, p.fst ⟶ p.snd => K.obj f.1.1     let s : Q ⟶ P := Sigma.desc fun f => K.map f.2 ≫ colimit.ι (Discrete.functor K.obj) ⟨_⟩     let t : Q ⟶ P := Sigma.desc fun f => colimit.ι (Discrete.functor K.obj) ⟨f.1.1⟩     let I := coequalizer s t     let i : P ⟶ I := coequalizer.π s t     apply       preservesColimitOfPreservesColimitCocone         (buildIsColimit s t (by simp [s]) (by simp [t]) (colimit.isColimit _) (colimit.isColimit _)           (colimit.isColimit _))     apply IsColimit.ofIsoColimit (buildIsColimit _ _ _ _ _ _ _) _     · refine Cofan.mk (G.obj Q) fun j => G.map ?_       apply Sigma.ι _ j     -- fun j => G.map (Sigma.ι _ j)     · exact Cofan.mk _ fun f => G.map (Sigma.ι _ f)     · apply G.map s     · apply G.map t     · intro f       dsimp [s, Cofan.mk]       simp only [← G.map_comp, colimit.ι_desc]       congr     · intro f       dsimp [t, Cofan.mk]       simp only [← G.map_comp, colimit.ι_desc]       dsimp     · refine Cofork.ofπ (G.map i) ?_       rw [← G.map_comp, ← G.map_comp]       apply congrArg G.map       apply coequalizer.condition     · apply isColimitOfHasCoproductOfPreservesColimit     · apply isColimitOfHasCoproductOfPreservesColimit     · apply isColimitCoforkMapOfIsColimit       apply coequalizerIsCoequalizer     refine Cocones.ext (Iso.refl _) ?_     intro j     dsimp     simp -- See note [dsimp, simp].

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesFiniteCol.fullDefinition: noncomputable def preservesFiniteColimitsOfPreservesInitialAndPushouts [HasInitial C]     [HasPushouts C] (G : C ⥤ D) [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete.{0} PEmpty) G]     [PreservesColimitsOfShape WalkingSpan G] : PreservesFiniteColimits G := by   haveI : HasFiniteColimits C := hasFiniteColimits_of_hasInitial_and_pushouts   haveI : PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) G :=     preservesBinaryCoproductsOfPreservesInitialAndPushouts G   haveI : PreservesColimitsOfShape (WalkingParallelPair) G :=       (preservesCoequalizersOfPreservesPushoutsAndBinaryCoproducts G)   refine     @preservesFiniteColimitsOfPreservesCoequalizersAndFiniteCoproducts _ _ _ _ _ _ G _ ?_   apply PreservesFiniteCoproducts.mk   apply preservesFiniteCoproductsOfPreservesBinaryAndInitial G

CategoryTheory.Limits.CoproductsFromFini.fullDefinition: def liftToFinset [HasFiniteCoproducts C] (F : Discrete α ⥤ C) : Finset (Discrete α) ⥤ C where   obj s := ∐ fun x : s => F.obj x   map {_ Y} h := Sigma.desc fun y =>     Sigma.ι (fun (x : { x // x ∈ Y }) => F.obj x) ⟨y, h.down.down y.2⟩

CategoryTheory.Limits.CoproductsFromFini.fullDefinition: def liftToFinsetColimitCocone [HasFiniteCoproducts C] [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} C]     (F : Discrete α ⥤ C) : ColimitCocone F where   cocone :=     { pt := colimit (liftToFinset F)       ι :=         Discrete.natTrans fun j =>           @Sigma.ι _ _ _ (fun x : ({j} : Finset (Discrete α)) => F.obj x) _ ⟨j, by simp⟩ ≫             colimit.ι (liftToFinset F) {j} }   isColimit :=     { desc := fun s =>         colimit.desc (liftToFinset F)           { pt := s.pt             ι := { app := fun t => Sigma.desc fun x => s.ι.app x } }       uniq := fun s m h => by         apply colimit.hom_ext         rintro t         dsimp [liftToFinset]         apply colimit.hom_ext         rintro ⟨⟨j, hj⟩⟩         convert h j using 1         · simp [← colimit.w (liftToFinset F) ⟨⟨Finset.singleton_subset_iff.2 hj⟩⟩]           rfl         · aesop_cat }

explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow: This definition describes the category of structured arrows based on a functor that represents morphisms from a fixed object in one category to variable objects in another, along with the related morphisms that maintain a specific commutative condition.

CategoryTheory.prodPreservesConnectedLim.comment:
The functor `(X × -)` preserves any connected limit.
Note that this functor does not preserve the two most obvious disconnected limits - that is,
`(X × -)` does not preserve products or terminal object, eg `(X ⨯ A) ⨯ (X ⨯ B)` is not isomorphic to
`X ⨯ (A ⨯ B)` and `X ⨯ 1` is not isomorphic to `1`.

CategoryTheory.prodPreservesConnectedLim.fullDefinition: noncomputable def prodPreservesConnectedLimits [IsConnected J] (X : C) :     PreservesLimitsOfShape J (prod.functor.obj X) where   preservesLimit {K} :=     {       preserves := fun {c} l =>         { lift := fun s =>             prod.lift (s.π.app (Classical.arbitrary _) ≫ Limits.prod.fst) (l.lift (forgetCone s))           fac := fun s j => by             apply prod.hom_ext             · erw [assoc, limMap_π, comp_id, limit.lift_π]               exact (nat_trans_from_is_connected (s.π ≫ γ₁ X) j (Classical.arbitrary _)).symm             · simp [← l.fac (forgetCone s) j]           uniq := fun s m L => by             apply prod.hom_ext             · erw [limit.lift_π, ← L (Classical.arbitrary J), assoc, limMap_π, comp_id]               rfl             · rw [limit.lift_π]               apply l.uniq (forgetCone s)               intro j               simp [← L j] } }
CategoryTheory.prodPreservesConnectedLim.description: This definition states that a functor formed by taking the product with a given object preserves limits for any connected shape in a category with binary products.

CategoryTheory.biconeCategoryStruct.fullDefinition: instance biconeCategoryStruct : CategoryStruct (Bicone J) where   Hom := BiconeHom J   id j := Bicone.casesOn j BiconeHom.left_id BiconeHom.right_id fun k => BiconeHom.diagram (𝟙 k)   comp f g := by     rcases f with (_ | _ | _ | _ | f)     · exact g     · exact g     · cases g       apply BiconeHom.left     · cases g       apply BiconeHom.right     · rcases g with (_|_|_|_|g)       exact BiconeHom.diagram (f ≫ g)

CategoryTheory.biconeMk.fullDefinition: def biconeMk {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {F : J ⥤ C} (c₁ c₂ : Cone F) : Bicone J ⥤ C where   obj X := Bicone.casesOn X c₁.pt c₂.pt fun j => F.obj j   map f := by     rcases f with (_|_|_|_|f)     · exact 𝟙 _     · exact 𝟙 _     · exact c₁.π.app _     · exact c₂.π.app _     · exact F.map f   map_id X := by cases X <;> simp   map_comp f g := by     rcases f with (_|_|_|_|_)     · exact (Category.id_comp _).symm     · exact (Category.id_comp _).symm     · cases g       exact (Category.id_comp _).symm.trans (c₁.π.naturality _)     · cases g       exact (Category.id_comp _).symm.trans (c₂.π.naturality _)     · cases g       apply F.map_comp

CategoryTheory.finBiconeHom.fullDefinition: instance finBiconeHom [FinCategory J] (j k : Bicone J) : Fintype (j ⟶ k) := by   cases j <;> cases k   · exact       { elems := {BiconeHom.left_id}         complete := fun f => by cases f; simp }   · exact     { elems := ∅       complete := fun f => by cases f }   · exact     { elems := {BiconeHom.left _}       complete := fun f => by cases f; simp }   · exact     { elems := ∅       complete := fun f => by cases f }   · exact       { elems := {BiconeHom.right_id}         complete := fun f => by cases f; simp }   · exact     { elems := {BiconeHom.right _}       complete := fun f => by cases f; simp }   · exact     { elems := ∅       complete := fun f => by cases f }   · exact     { elems := ∅       complete := fun f => by cases f }   · exact     { elems := Finset.image BiconeHom.diagram Fintype.elems       complete := fun f => by         rcases f with (_|_|_|_|f)         simp only [Finset.mem_image]         use f         simpa using Fintype.complete _ }

explanatories.Small.mk: A type is considered small if there exists a non-empty set that is equivalent to it.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.mk: This theorem provides a way to construct a limit cone for a functor by using an existing cone that satisfies the properties of being a limit.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommaMorphism.w: This theorem establishes a relational equality between the morphisms of two objects in a comma category, demonstrating how the mappings corresponding to their respective left and right components interact.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.Rel.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.Rel.{v, u, w} {J : Type v} [Category.{w, v} J] (F : J ⥤ Type u) :
  (j : J) × F.obj j → (j : J) × F.obj j → Prop
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.Rel.comment:
The relation defining the quotient type which implements the colimit of a functor `F : J ⥤ Type u`.
See `CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot`.

explanatories.Nonempty.map: If there is at least one element in a nonempty type, then applying a function to that type results in another nonempty type.
This entity defines a morphism in a category that maps from the source of the original morphism to a specific component of its monomorphism factorization.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.Rel.fullDefinition: def Quot.Rel (F : J ⥤ Type u) : (Σ j, F.obj j) → (Σ j, F.obj j) → Prop := fun p p' =>   ∃ f : p.1 ⟶ p'.1, p'.2 = F.map f p.2
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.Rel.description: This definition specifies a relation that characterizes the elements of a quotient type for the colimit of a functor in a given category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.code: CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.{v, u, w} {J : Type v} [Category.{w, v} J] (F : J ⥤ Type u) : Type (max v u)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.comment:
A quotient type implementing the colimit of a functor `F : J ⥤ Type u`,
as pairs `⟨j, x⟩` where `x : F.obj j`, modulo the equivalence relation generated by
`⟨j, x⟩ ~ ⟨j', x'⟩` whenever there is a morphism `f : j ⟶ j'` so `F.map f x = x'`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.Rel: This definition specifies a relation that characterizes the elements of a quotient type for the colimit of a functor in a given category.
This entity defines a morphism in a category that maps from the source of the original morphism to a specific component of its monomorphism factorization.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.fullDefinition: def Quot (F : J ⥤ Type u) : Type (max v u) :=   _root_.Quot (Quot.Rel F)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.description: This definition describes a quotient type that represents the colimit of a functor as pairs of objects and their indices, subject to an equivalence relation determined by morphisms between those indices.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.Quot.ι.comment: Inclusion into the quotient type implementing the colimit.

CategoryTheory.Limits.compCoyonedaSectio.fullDefinition: def compCoyonedaSectionsEquiv (F : J ⥤ C) (X : C) :     (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op X)).sections ≃ ((const J).obj X ⟶ F) where   toFun s :=     { app := fun j => s.val j       naturality := fun j j' f => by         dsimp         rw [Category.id_comp]         exact (s.property f).symm }   invFun τ := ⟨τ.app, fun {j j'} f => by simpa using (τ.naturality f).symm⟩   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := rfl
CategoryTheory.Limits.compCoyonedaSectio.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the sections of a functor composed with the coyoneda construction at a point and the natural transformations from a constant functor to that functor.

CategoryTheory.Comma.coconeOfPreserves.fullDefinition: def coconeOfPreserves [PreservesColimit (F ⋙ fst L R) L] {c₁ : Cocone (F ⋙ fst L R)}     (t₁ : IsColimit c₁) (c₂ : Cocone (F ⋙ snd L R)) : Cocone F where   pt :=     { left := c₁.pt       right := c₂.pt       hom := (isColimitOfPreserves L t₁).desc (colimitAuxiliaryCocone _ c₂) }   ι :=     { app := fun j =>         { left := c₁.ι.app j           right := c₂.ι.app j           w := (isColimitOfPreserves L t₁).fac (colimitAuxiliaryCocone _ c₂) j }       naturality := fun j₁ j₂ t => by         ext         · simp [← c₁.w t]         · simp [← c₂.w t] }

CategoryTheory.Comma.coconeOfPreservesIs.fullDefinition: def coconeOfPreservesIsColimit [PreservesColimit (F ⋙ fst L R) L] {c₁ : Cocone (F ⋙ fst L R)}     (t₁ : IsColimit c₁) {c₂ : Cocone (F ⋙ snd L R)} (t₂ : IsColimit c₂) :     IsColimit (coconeOfPreserves F t₁ c₂) where   desc s :=     { left := t₁.desc ((fst L R).mapCocone s)       right := t₂.desc ((snd L R).mapCocone s)       w :=         (isColimitOfPreserves L t₁).hom_ext fun j => by           rw [coconeOfPreserves_pt_hom, (isColimitOfPreserves L t₁).fac_assoc,             colimitAuxiliaryCocone_ι_app, assoc, ← R.map_comp, t₂.fac, L.mapCocone_ι_app, ←             L.map_comp_assoc, t₁.fac]           exact (s.ι.app j).w }   uniq s m w := by     apply CommaMorphism.ext     · exact t₁.uniq ((fst L R).mapCocone s) _ (fun j => by simp [← w])     · exact t₂.uniq ((snd L R).mapCocone s) _ (fun j => by simp [← w])

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Over.pullback: This definition states that when a category has pullbacks, a morphism induces a functor that allows the pulling back of morphisms from one object in the over category along the given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv: This definition describes how to create an adjunction between two functors using a natural bijection that relates morphisms from one category to those in another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Over.w: The theorem states that the left morphism associated with one object in the over category, when composed with the right morphism of another object, equals the morphism of the first object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.lift_snd: This theorem asserts that a specific morphism lifted from two given morphisms in a pullback construction, when composed with the second projection, equals the original morphism from the second object in the pair.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Over.OverMorphism.ext: If two morphisms in the over category have the same left component, then they are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.hom_ext: Two morphisms into a pullback object are identical if their compositions with the projection morphisms from the pullback are identical.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.lift_π: This theorem asserts that for a functor with an established limit, the composition of the morphism lifting from a cone to the limit with the limit projection equals the morphism from the cone to the object corresponding to a specific index in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommaMorphism.right: This definition specifies a method to extract the morphism from the right component of a morphism between two comma objects formed by two functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Under.map: This definition describes a functor that maps the under category of one object to the under category of another object based on the morphism connecting them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.pt: This definition specifies the specific object in a category that serves as the cone point for a given cone associated with a functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Under.homMk: This definition states that a morphism in the under category can be specified by providing a morphism that fits into a commutative triangle.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.condition: This theorem states that the composition of the first morphism with the first inclusion of the pushout equals the composition of the second morphism with the second inclusion of the pushout, establishing a crucial condition for the pushout's universality.

CategoryTheory.Over.mapPullbackAdj.fullDefinition: def mapPullbackAdj {A B : C} (f : A ⟶ B) : Over.map f ⊣ pullback f :=   Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv     { homEquiv := fun g h =>         { toFun := fun X =>             Over.homMk (pullback.lift X.left g.hom (Over.w X)) (pullback.lift_snd _ _ _)           invFun := fun Y => by             refine Over.homMk ?_ ?_             · refine Y.left ≫ pullback.fst _ _             dsimp             rw [← Over.w Y, Category.assoc, pullback.condition, Category.assoc]; rfl           left_inv := fun X => by             ext             dsimp             simp           right_inv := fun Y => by             -- TODO: It would be nice to replace the next two lines with just `ext`.             apply OverMorphism.ext             apply pullback.hom_ext             · dsimp               simp only [limit.lift_π, PullbackCone.mk_pt, PullbackCone.mk_π_app]             · dsimp               simp only [limit.lift_π, PullbackCone.mk_pt, PullbackCone.mk_π_app, ← Over.w Y ]               rfl }       -- This used to be automatic before leanprover/lean4#2644       homEquiv_naturality_right := by intros; dsimp; congr 1; aesop_cat       }
CategoryTheory.Over.mapPullbackAdj.description: This definition asserts that the functor mapping from one object in the over category to another is a left adjoint to the functor that pulls back along a given morphism.

CategoryTheory.Over.pullbackId.fullDefinition: def pullbackId {A : C} : pullback (𝟙 A) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=   Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq (mapPullbackAdj _) (Adjunction.id.ofNatIsoLeft (Over.mapId A).symm)

  (hc₁ : IsColimit c₁) (hc₂ : IsColimit c₂) : BinaryCofan c₁.pt c₂.pt
CategoryTheory.Limits.MonoCoprod.binaryC.comment:

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.FilteredColi.comment:
An alternative relation on `Σ j, F.obj j`,
which generates the same equivalence relation as we use to define the colimit in `Type` above,
but that is more convenient when working with filtered colimits.

Elements in `F.obj j` and `F.obj j'` are equivalent if there is some `k : J` to the right
where their images are equal.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.FilteredColi.fullDefinition: noncomputable def isColimitOf (t : Cocone F) (hsurj : ∀ x : t.pt, ∃ i xi, x = t.ι.app i xi)     (hinj :       ∀ i j xi xj,         t.ι.app i xi = t.ι.app j xj → ∃ (k : _) (f : i ⟶ k) (g : j ⟶ k), F.map f xi = F.map g xj) :     IsColimit t := by   let α : t.pt → J := fun x => (hsurj x).choose   let f : ∀ (x : t.pt), F.obj (α x) := fun x => (hsurj x).choose_spec.choose   have hf : ∀ (x : t.pt), x = t.ι.app _ (f x) := fun x => (hsurj x).choose_spec.choose_spec   exact     { desc := fun s x => s.ι.app _ (f x)       fac := fun s j => by         ext y         obtain ⟨k, l, g, eq⟩ := hinj _ _ _ _ (hf (t.ι.app j y))         have h := congr_fun (s.ι.naturality g) (f (t.ι.app j y))         have h' := congr_fun (s.ι.naturality l) y         dsimp at h h' ⊢         rw [← h, ← eq, h']       uniq := fun s m hm => by         ext x         dsimp         nth_rw 1 [hf x]         rw [← hm, types_comp_apply] }

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift.fullDefinition: def lift (d : D) : C :=   (Classical.arbitrary (StructuredArrow d F)).right
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift.description: If a functor is final, then lifting an object from the codomain allows for the selection of an object in the domain with a corresponding morphism.

When `F : C ⥤ D` is cofinal, we denote by `homToLift` an arbitrary choice of morphism
`d ⟶ F.obj (lift F d)`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow: This definition describes the category of structured arrows based on a functor that represents morphisms from a fixed object in one category to variable objects in another, along with the related morphisms that maintain a specific commutative condition.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift.fullDefinition: def homToLift (d : D) : d ⟶ F.obj (lift F d) :=   (Classical.arbitrary (StructuredArrow d F)).hom
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift.description: For a cofinal functor, there exists a morphism from any object in the codomain to the image of its lift through the functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂, u_1} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Final] {d : D} (Z : (X : C) → (d ⟶ F.obj X) → Sort u_1)
  (h₁ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) → (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)
  (h₂ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) → (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)
  {X₀ : C} {k₀ : d ⟶ F.obj X₀} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.comment:
We provide an induction principle for reasoning about `lift` and `homToLift`.
We want to perform some construction (usually just a proof) about
the particular choices `lift F d` and `homToLift F d`,
it suffices to perform that construction for some other pair of choices
(denoted `X₀ : C` and `k₀ : d ⟶ F.obj X₀` below),
and to show how to transport such a construction
*both* directions along a morphism between such choices.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.fullDefinition: def induction {d : D} (Z : ∀ (X : C) (_ : d ⟶ F.obj X), Sort*)     (h₁ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)     (h₂ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)     {X₀ : C} {k₀ : d ⟶ F.obj X₀} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d) := by   apply Nonempty.some   apply     @isPreconnected_induction _ _ _ (fun Y : StructuredArrow d F => Z Y.right Y.hom) _ _       (StructuredArrow.mk k₀) z   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₁ _ _ _ _ f.right _ a     convert f.w.symm     dsimp     simp   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₂ _ _ _ _ f.right _ a     convert f.w.symm     dsimp     simp
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.description: An induction principle for final functors allows reasoning about the construction related to the lift and hom-to-lift operations by transferring properties through morphisms in the category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.extendCocon.fullDefinition: def extendCocone : Cocone (F ⋙ G) ⥤ Cocone G where   obj c :=     { pt := c.pt       ι :=         { app := fun X => G.map (homToLift F X) ≫ c.ι.app (lift F X)           naturality := fun X Y f => by             dsimp; simp             -- This would be true if we'd chosen `lift F X` to be `lift F Y`             -- and `homToLift F X` to be `f ≫ homToLift F Y`.             apply               induction F fun Z k =>                 G.map f ≫ G.map (homToLift F Y) ≫ c.ι.app (lift F Y) = G.map k ≫ c.ι.app Z             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc, ← Functor.comp_map, c.w, z]             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc, ← Functor.comp_map, c.w] at z               rw [z]             · rw [← Functor.map_comp_assoc] } }   map f := { hom := f.hom }

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.colimitComp.fullDefinition: def Final.colimitCompCoyonedaIso (d : D) [IsIso (colimit.pre (coyoneda.obj (op d)) F)] :     colimit (F ⋙ coyoneda.obj (op d)) ≅ PUnit :=   asIso (colimit.pre (coyoneda.obj (op d)) F) ≪≫ Coyoneda.colimitCoyonedaIso (op d)

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.lift.code:

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.lift.comment:

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.lift.fullDefinition: def lift (d : D) : C :=   (Classical.arbitrary (CostructuredArrow F d)).left
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.lift.description: Given an initial functor, an object in the target category can be associated with an arbitrary object in the source category that maps to it via a morphism induced by the functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.homToLift.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.homToLift.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow: This definition describes a structure where the objects are morphisms from the image of a functor to a target, along with morphisms that maintain a commutative triangle relationship.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift: For a cofinal functor, there exists a morphism from any object in the codomain to the image of its lift through the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.lift: Given an initial functor, an object in the target category can be associated with an arbitrary object in the source category that maps to it via a morphism induced by the functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.homToLift.fullDefinition: def homToLift (d : D) : F.obj (lift F d) ⟶ d :=   (Classical.arbitrary (CostructuredArrow F d)).hom

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂, u_1} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Initial] {d : D} (Z : (X : C) → (F.obj X ⟶ d) → Sort u_1)
  (h₁ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) → (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)
  (h₂ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) → (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)
  {X₀ : C} {k₀ : F.obj X₀ ⟶ d} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.comment:
We provide an induction principle for reasoning about `lift` and `homToLift`.
We want to perform some construction (usually just a proof) about
the particular choices `lift F d` and `homToLift F d`,
it suffices to perform that construction for some other pair of choices
(denoted `X₀ : C` and `k₀ : F.obj X₀ ⟶ d` below),
and to show how to transport such a construction
*both* directions along a morphism between such choices.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.fullDefinition: def induction {d : D} (Z : ∀ (X : C) (_ : F.obj X ⟶ d), Sort*)     (h₁ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)     (h₂ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)     {X₀ : C} {k₀ : F.obj X₀ ⟶ d} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d) := by   apply Nonempty.some   apply     @isPreconnected_induction _ _ _ (fun Y : CostructuredArrow F d => Z Y.left Y.hom) _ _       (CostructuredArrow.mk k₀) z   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₁ _ _ _ _ f.left _ a     convert f.w     dsimp     simp   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₂ _ _ _ _ f.left _ a     convert f.w     dsimp     simp
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.description: An induction principle for initial functors allows reasoning about the construction related to the lift and hom-to-lift operations by transferring properties through morphisms in the category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCon.fullDefinition: def extendCone : Cone (F ⋙ G) ⥤ Cone G where   obj c :=     { pt := c.pt       π :=         { app := fun d => c.π.app (lift F d) ≫ G.map (homToLift F d)           naturality := fun X Y f => by             dsimp; simp             -- This would be true if we'd chosen `lift F Y` to be `lift F X`             -- and `homToLift F Y` to be `homToLift F X ≫ f`.             apply               induction F fun Z k =>                 (c.π.app Z ≫ G.map k : c.pt ⟶ _) =                   c.π.app (lift F X) ≫ G.map (homToLift F X) ≫ G.map f             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, ← Functor.comp_map, ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc,                 c.w] at z               rw [z, Category.assoc]             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, ← Functor.comp_map, ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc,                 c.w, z, Category.assoc]             · rw [← Functor.map_comp] } }   map f := { hom := f.hom }
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCon.description: A cone over the composition of two functors can be transformed into a cone over the second functor while maintaining the same apex when the first functor is initial.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEquiv.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Initial] {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (G : D ⥤ E) : Cone (F ⋙ G) ≌ Cone G

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui.fullDefinition: def conesEquiv : Cone (F ⋙ G) ≌ Cone G where   functor := extendCone   inverse := Cones.whiskering F   unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)   counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui.description: The category of cones over the composition of an initial functor with another functor is equivalent to the category of cones over the second functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.final_comp.fullDefinition: instance final_comp [hF : Final F] [hG : Final G] : Final (F ⋙ G) := by   let s₁ : C ≌ AsSmall.{max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ u₃ v₃} C := AsSmall.equiv   let s₂ : D ≌ AsSmall.{max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ u₃ v₃} D := AsSmall.equiv   let s₃ : E ≌ AsSmall.{max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ u₃ v₃} E := AsSmall.equiv   let i : s₁.inverse ⋙ (F ⋙ G) ⋙ s₃.functor ≅       (s₁.inverse ⋙ F ⋙ s₂.functor) ⋙ (s₂.inverse ⋙ G ⋙ s₃.functor) :=     isoWhiskerLeft (s₁.inverse ⋙ F) (isoWhiskerRight s₂.unitIso (G ⋙ s₃.functor))   rw [final_iff_comp_equivalence (F ⋙ G) s₃.functor, final_iff_equivalence_comp s₁.inverse,     final_natIso_iff i, final_iff_isIso_colimit_pre]   rw [final_iff_comp_equivalence F s₂.functor, final_iff_equivalence_comp s₁.inverse,     final_iff_isIso_colimit_pre] at hF   rw [final_iff_comp_equivalence G s₃.functor, final_iff_equivalence_comp s₂.inverse,     final_iff_isIso_colimit_pre] at hG   intro H   rw [← colimit.pre_pre]   infer_instance

CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_op_of_fin.fullDefinition: instance initial_op_of_final (F : C ⥤ D) [Final F] : Initial F.op where   out d := isConnected_of_equivalent (structuredArrowOpEquivalence F (unop d))
CategoryTheory.Functor.initial_op_of_fin.description: A final functor induces an initial functor on its opposite category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Final] (d : D) : C
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift.comment:
When `F : C ⥤ D` is cofinal, we denote by `lift F d` an arbitrary choice of object in `C` such that
there exists a morphism `d ⟶ F.obj (lift F d)`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow: This definition describes the category of structured arrows based on a functor that represents morphisms from a fixed object in one category to variable objects in another, along with the related morphisms that maintain a specific commutative condition.
explanatories.Classical.arbitrary: A nonempty type can be represented by an arbitrary element chosen from it.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift.fullDefinition: def lift (d : D) : C :=   (Classical.arbitrary (StructuredArrow d F)).right
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift.description: If a functor is final, then lifting an object from the codomain allows for the selection of an object in the domain with a corresponding morphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Final] (d : D) : d ⟶ F.obj (lift F d)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift.comment:
When `F : C ⥤ D` is cofinal, we denote by `homToLift` an arbitrary choice of morphism
`d ⟶ F.obj (lift F d)`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow: This definition describes the category of structured arrows based on a functor that represents morphisms from a fixed object in one category to variable objects in another, along with the related morphisms that maintain a specific commutative condition.
explanatories.Classical.arbitrary: A nonempty type can be represented by an arbitrary element chosen from it.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift: If a functor is final, then lifting an object from the codomain allows for the selection of an object in the domain with a corresponding morphism.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift.fullDefinition: def homToLift (d : D) : d ⟶ F.obj (lift F d) :=   (Classical.arbitrary (StructuredArrow d F)).hom
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift.description: For a cofinal functor, there exists a morphism from any object in the codomain to the image of its lift through the functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂, u_1} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Final] {d : D} (Z : (X : C) → (d ⟶ F.obj X) → Sort u_1)
  (h₁ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) → (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)
  (h₂ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) → (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)
  {X₀ : C} {k₀ : d ⟶ F.obj X₀} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.comment:
We provide an induction principle for reasoning about `lift` and `homToLift`.
We want to perform some construction (usually just a proof) about
the particular choices `lift F d` and `homToLift F d`,
it suffices to perform that construction for some other pair of choices
(denoted `X₀ : C` and `k₀ : d ⟶ F.obj X₀` below),
and to show how to transport such a construction
*both* directions along a morphism between such choices.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.fullDefinition: def induction {d : D} (Z : ∀ (X : C) (_ : d ⟶ F.obj X), Sort*)     (h₁ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)     (h₂ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : d ⟶ F.obj X₁) (k₂ : d ⟶ F.obj X₂) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         k₁ ≫ F.map f = k₂ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)     {X₀ : C} {k₀ : d ⟶ F.obj X₀} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d) := by   apply Nonempty.some   apply     @isPreconnected_induction _ _ _ (fun Y : StructuredArrow d F => Z Y.right Y.hom) _ _       (StructuredArrow.mk k₀) z   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₁ _ _ _ _ f.right _ a     convert f.w.symm     dsimp     simp   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₂ _ _ _ _ f.right _ a     convert f.w.symm     dsimp     simp
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction.description: An induction principle for final functors allows reasoning about the construction related to the lift and hom-to-lift operations by transferring properties through morphisms in the category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.extendCocon.fullDefinition: def extendCocone : Cocone (F ⋙ G) ⥤ Cocone G where   obj c :=     { pt := c.pt       ι :=         { app := fun X => G.map (homToLift F X) ≫ c.ι.app (lift F X)           naturality := fun X Y f => by             dsimp; simp             -- This would be true if we'd chosen `lift F X` to be `lift F Y`             -- and `homToLift F X` to be `f ≫ homToLift F Y`.             apply               induction F fun Z k =>                 G.map f ≫ G.map (homToLift F Y) ≫ c.ι.app (lift F Y) = G.map k ≫ c.ι.app Z             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc, ← Functor.comp_map, c.w, z]             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc, ← Functor.comp_map, c.w] at z               rw [z]             · rw [← Functor.map_comp_assoc] } }   map f := { hom := f.hom }
CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.extendCocon.description: A cocone over the composition of two functors can be used to construct a cocone over the second functor based on the same cocone point.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.coconesEqui.fullDefinition: def coconesEquiv : Cocone (F ⋙ G) ≌ Cocone G where   functor := extendCocone   inverse := Cocones.whiskering F   unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cocones.ext (Iso.refl _)   counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cocones.ext (Iso.refl _)

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂, u_1} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Initial] {d : D} (Z : (X : C) → (F.obj X ⟶ d) → Sort u_1)
  (h₁ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) → (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)
  (h₂ : (X₁ X₂ : C) → (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) → (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) → (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) → F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)
  {X₀ : C} {k₀ : F.obj X₀ ⟶ d} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.comment:
We provide an induction principle for reasoning about `lift` and `homToLift`.
We want to perform some construction (usually just a proof) about
the particular choices `lift F d` and `homToLift F d`,
it suffices to perform that construction for some other pair of choices
(denoted `X₀ : C` and `k₀ : F.obj X₀ ⟶ d` below),
and to show how to transport such a construction
*both* directions along a morphism between such choices.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.fullDefinition: def induction {d : D} (Z : ∀ (X : C) (_ : F.obj X ⟶ d), Sort*)     (h₁ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₁ k₁ → Z X₂ k₂)     (h₂ :       ∀ (X₁ X₂) (k₁ : F.obj X₁ ⟶ d) (k₂ : F.obj X₂ ⟶ d) (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂),         F.map f ≫ k₂ = k₁ → Z X₂ k₂ → Z X₁ k₁)     {X₀ : C} {k₀ : F.obj X₀ ⟶ d} (z : Z X₀ k₀) : Z (lift F d) (homToLift F d) := by   apply Nonempty.some   apply     @isPreconnected_induction _ _ _ (fun Y : CostructuredArrow F d => Z Y.left Y.hom) _ _       (CostructuredArrow.mk k₀) z   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₁ _ _ _ _ f.left _ a     convert f.w     dsimp     simp   · intro j₁ j₂ f a     fapply h₂ _ _ _ _ f.left _ a     convert f.w     dsimp     simp
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction.description: An induction principle for initial functors allows reasoning about the construction related to the lift and hom-to-lift operations by transferring properties through morphisms in the category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCon.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCone.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {F : C ⥤ D} [F.Initial] {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] {G : D ⥤ E} : Cone (F ⋙ G) ⥤ Cone G
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCon.comment: Given a cone over `F ⋙ G`, we can construct a `Cone G` with the same cocone point.

explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Comma.hom: This definition specifies a method to extract the morphism connecting the left and right components of a comma object formed by two functors.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift: If a functor is final, then lifting an object from the codomain allows for the selection of an object in the domain with a corresponding morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift: For a cofinal functor, there exists a morphism from any object in the codomain to the image of its lift through the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CommaMorphism.w: This theorem establishes a relational equality between the morphisms of two objects in a comma category, demonstrating how the mappings corresponding to their respective left and right components interact.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.induction: An induction principle for final functors allows reasoning about the construction related to the lift and hom-to-lift operations by transferring properties through morphisms in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp: This statement defines the composition of two functors, where the first functor is applied to an object followed by the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.pt: This definition specifies the specific object in a category that serves as the cocone point for a given cocone associated with a functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp_map: The theorem demonstrates that the composition of two functors applied to a morphism is equivalent to first mapping the morphism through the first functor and then mapping the result through the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.w: This theorem states that for a cocone associated with a functor, the action on morphisms preserves the structure of the cocone, ensuring that the transformation commutes appropriately.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.CoconeMorphism.hom: This definition describes a morphism that connects the apex objects of two cocones associated with the same functor.
explanatories.Bool.true: The statement identifies the boolean value representing true, which is distinct from the logical proposition denoting truth.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.lift: Given an initial functor, an object in the target category can be associated with an arbitrary object in the source category that maps to it via a morphism induced by the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.homToLift: A morphism is chosen from an object obtained by lifting through an initial functor to a specified object in the target category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.induction: An induction principle for initial functors allows reasoning about the construction related to the lift and hom-to-lift operations by transferring properties through morphisms in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.pt: This definition specifies the specific object in a category that serves as the cone point for a given cone associated with a functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.π: This definition describes a natural transformation from a constant functor at a specific point to another functor, capturing the relationship between a cone and the functor it pertains to.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.w: This theorem establishes that for a given cone associated with a functor, the morphisms from the cone point to the images under the functor commute with the morphisms in the indexing category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.ConeMorphism.hom: This definition specifies the morphism that connects the vertex objects of two cones associated with the same functor.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Nonempty.map: If there is at least one element in a nonempty type, then applying a function to that type results in another nonempty type.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCon.fullDefinition: def extendCone : Cone (F ⋙ G) ⥤ Cone G where   obj c :=     { pt := c.pt       π :=         { app := fun d => c.π.app (lift F d) ≫ G.map (homToLift F d)           naturality := fun X Y f => by             dsimp; simp             -- This would be true if we'd chosen `lift F Y` to be `lift F X`             -- and `homToLift F Y` to be `homToLift F X ≫ f`.             apply               induction F fun Z k =>                 (c.π.app Z ≫ G.map k : c.pt ⟶ _) =                   c.π.app (lift F X) ≫ G.map (homToLift F X) ≫ G.map f             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, ← Functor.comp_map, ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc,                 c.w] at z               rw [z, Category.assoc]             · intro Z₁ Z₂ k₁ k₂ g a z               rw [← a, Functor.map_comp, ← Functor.comp_map, ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc,                 c.w, z, Category.assoc]             · rw [← Functor.map_comp] } }   map f := { hom := f.hom }
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCon.description: A cone over the composition of two functors can be transformed into a cone over the second functor while maintaining the same apex when the first functor is initial.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.lift: If a functor is final, then lifting an object from the codomain allows for the selection of an object in the domain with a corresponding morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.homToLift: For a cofinal functor, there exists a morphism from any object in the codomain to the image of its lift through the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.lift: Given an initial functor, an object in the target category can be associated with an arbitrary object in the source category that maps to it via a morphism induced by the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.homToLift: A morphism is chosen from an object obtained by lifting through an initial functor to a specified object in the target category.
explanatories.Nonempty.map: If there is at least one element in a nonempty type, then applying a function to that type results in another nonempty type.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limit_con.description: For a cone over the composition of two functors, the image of a morphism from the lifted object through the first functor, when mapped by the second functor, equals the morphism corresponding to the original object in the category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEquiv.{v₁, v₂, v₃, u₁, u₂, u₃} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Initial] {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (G : D ⥤ E) : Cone (F ⋙ G) ≌ Cone G
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui.comment:
If `F` is initial,
the category of cones on `F ⋙ G` is equivalent to the category of cones on `G`,
for any `G : D ⥤ E`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.whiskering: This definition describes a functor that maps cocones for a functor to cocones for the composition of two functors by whiskering on the left.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.ofComponents: This definition outlines the process of creating a natural isomorphism between functors by providing isomorphisms at the object level and verifying naturality in one direction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.extendCon: A cone over the composition of two functors can be transformed into a cone over the second functor while maintaining the same apex when the first functor is initial.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.whiskering: This definition describes a functor that transforms cones associated with one functor into cones associated with the composition of that functor with another functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso: This definition states that a specific functor composition related to an equivalence between categories is isomorphic to the identity functor of the first category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.inverse: This definition specifies a functor that serves as the inverse of an equivalence between two categories, allowing for mapping in the opposite direction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor: This definition introduces a functor that represents one direction of an equivalence between two categories.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui.fullDefinition: def conesEquiv : Cone (F ⋙ G) ≌ Cone G where   functor := extendCone   inverse := Cones.whiskering F   unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)   counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents fun c => Cones.ext (Iso.refl _)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui.description: The category of cones over the composition of an initial functor with another functor is equivalent to the category of cones over the second functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitWh.comment:
When `F : C ⥤ D` is initial, and `t : Cone G` for some `G : D ⥤ E`,
`t.whisker F` is a limit cone exactly when `t` is.

explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.whisker: This definition describes the process of transforming a cocone associated with a functor by precomposing it with another functor, effectively creating a new cocone for the composed functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui: The category of cones over the composition of an initial functor with another functor is equivalent to the category of cones over the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.whisker: This definition describes how to create a cone over the composition of two functors by precomposing a given cone with another functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.ofConeEqui: This definition states that if two functors have equivalent categories of cones, then the existence of a limit in one category corresponds to the existence of a limit in the other category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitWh.fullDefinition: def isLimitWhiskerEquiv (t : Cone G) : IsLimit (t.whisker F) ≃ IsLimit t :=   IsLimit.ofConeEquiv (conesEquiv F G).symm
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitWh.description: If a functor is initial, then a cone over the composition with another functor is a limit cone if and only if the original cone is a limit cone.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitEx.comment:
When `F` is initial, and `t : Cone (F ⋙ G)`,
`extendCone.obj t` is a limit cone exactly when `t` is.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.conesEqui: The category of cones over the composition of an initial functor with another functor is equivalent to the category of cones over the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.ofConeEqui: This definition states that if two functors have equivalent categories of cones, then the existence of a limit in one category corresponds to the existence of a limit in the other category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitEx.fullDefinition: def isLimitExtendConeEquiv (t : Cone (F ⋙ G)) : IsLimit (extendCone.obj t) ≃ IsLimit t :=   IsLimit.ofConeEquiv (conesEquiv F G)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitEx.description: If a functor is initial, then a cone over the composition of that functor with another functor is a limit cone if and only if the original cone is a limit cone.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone.comment: Given a limit cone over `G : D ⥤ E` we can construct a limit cone over `F ⋙ G`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm: This definition states that the equivalence between two categories is symmetric, meaning that if one category is equivalent to another, then the second category is also equivalent to the first.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitWh: If a functor is initial, then a cone over the composition with another functor is a limit cone if and only if the original cone is a limit cone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.isLimit: This definition establishes the condition that a limit cone in a category is considered a limit if its cone satisfies the appropriate limit properties.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.cone: This definition identifies the structure of a cone associated with a limit cone in a category, detailing how the cone is formed from a given functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone.fullDefinition: def limitConeComp (t : LimitCone G) : LimitCone (F ⋙ G) where   cone := _   isLimit := (isLimitWhiskerEquiv F _).symm t.isLimit
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone.description: From a limit cone in a category, one can construct a new limit cone for the composition of that functor with another functor.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.mk: This definition provides a construction method for creating a structured arrow from a given morphism between a fixed object and the image of a functor applied to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.mk: This definition creates a costructured arrow from a morphism between a specific object in the functor's image and a target object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.mk: This theorem states that given a cocone for a functor, one can construct a colimit for that functor, thus confirming the existence of colimits in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Final.mk: If every object in the codomain has a connected structured arrow to the functor, then the functor is final.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone: From a limit cone in a category, one can construct a new limit cone for the composition of that functor with another functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasLimit.mk: This theorem asserts that if a functor has a limit cone, then it is characterized as having a limit in the corresponding category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.getLimitCone: This definition provides a method to explicitly obtain a limit cone for a functor from the assertion that the functor has a limit, using the axiom of choice.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.comp_hasL.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) comp_hasLimit [HasLimit G] : HasLimit (F ⋙ G) :=   HasLimit.mk (limitConeComp F (getLimitCone G))
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.comp_hasL.description: If a functor is initial and another functor has a limit, then the composition of these two functors also has a limit.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.pre: This definition specifies a canonical morphism from the colimit of the composition of two functors to the colimit of the second functor alone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.pre_eq: This theorem provides an expression for the morphism connecting the colimit of a functor to that of its composition with another functor by incorporating the colimit cocones for both functors.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone: From a limit cone in a category, one can construct a new limit cone for the composition of that functor with another functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.getLimitCone: This definition provides a method to explicitly obtain a limit cone for a functor from the assertion that the functor has a limit, using the axiom of choice.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.pre: This definition specifies a canonical morphism that connects the limit of a functor to the limit of the composition of that functor with another functor that has a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.pre_eq: This theorem provides an equation relating the limit of a functor composed with another functor to the limit cone of the composition and the limit cone of the original functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift_self: This theorem states that the lifting of a cone through itself yields the identity morphism on its cone point.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.pre: This definition describes a functor that relates structured arrows with a fixed object in one category and two functors, transitioning from the composition of the functors to the latter functor alone while maintaining the same structured arrow object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.pre: This definition describes a functor that maps costructured arrows formed by the composition of two functors to a costructured arrow formed by the second functor while maintaining a fixed object in the target category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limit_pre.fullDefinition: instance limit_pre_isIso [HasLimit G] : IsIso (limit.pre G F) := by   rw [limit.pre_eq (limitConeComp F (getLimitCone G)) (getLimitCone G)]   erw [IsLimit.lift_self]   dsimp   infer_instance
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limit_pre.description: A limit of a functor is isomorphic to the limit of the composed functor when the original functor is initial.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso.comment:
When `F : C ⥤ D` is initial, and `G : D ⥤ E` has a limit, then `F ⋙ G` has a limit also and
`limit (F ⋙ G) ≅ limit G`

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.pre: This definition specifies a canonical morphism that connects the limit of a functor to the limit of the composition of that functor with another functor that has a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit: This definition denotes an arbitrary selection of a limit object for a functor that possesses a limit in a given category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.pre: This definition describes a functor that relates structured arrows with a fixed object in one category and two functors, transitioning from the composition of the functors to the latter functor alone while maintaining the same structured arrow object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.pre: This definition describes a functor that maps costructured arrows formed by the composition of two functors to a costructured arrow formed by the second functor while maintaining a fixed object in the target category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso.fullDefinition: def limitIso [HasLimit G] : limit (F ⋙ G) ≅ limit G :=   (asIso (limit.pre G F)).symm
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso.description: If a functor is initial and another functor has a limit, then the composition of the two functors also has a limit, and they are isomorphic.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone.comment: Given a limit cone over `F ⋙ G` we can construct a limit cone over `G`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm: This definition states that the equivalence between two categories is symmetric, meaning that if one category is equivalent to another, then the second category is also equivalent to the first.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.isLimitEx: If a functor is initial, then a cone over the composition of that functor with another functor is a limit cone if and only if the original cone is a limit cone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.isLimit: This definition establishes the condition that a limit cone in a category is considered a limit if its cone satisfies the appropriate limit properties.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.LimitCone.cone: This definition identifies the structure of a cone associated with a limit cone in a category, detailing how the cone is formed from a given functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone.fullDefinition: def limitConeOfComp (t : LimitCone (F ⋙ G)) : LimitCone G where   cone := extendCone.obj t.cone   isLimit := (isLimitExtendConeEquiv F _).symm t.isLimit
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitCone.description: A limit cone over the composition of an initial functor with another functor enables the construction of a limit cone over the second functor.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.hasLimit_.comment:
When `F` is initial, and `F ⋙ G` has a limit, then `G` has a limit also.

We can't make this an instance, because `F` is not determined by the goal.
(Even if this weren't a problem, it would cause a loop with `comp_hasLimit`.)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.hasLimit_.description: If an initial functor combined with another functor has a limit, then the second functor must also possess a limit.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial.limitIso'.comment:

  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {E : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} E] (F : C ⥤ D) (G : D ⥤ E) [G.Full] [G.Faithful]

CategoryTheory.Functor.final_comp.fullDefinition: instance final_comp [hF : Final F] [hG : Final G] : Final (F ⋙ G) := by   let s₁ : C ≌ AsSmall.{max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ u₃ v₃} C := AsSmall.equiv   let s₂ : D ≌ AsSmall.{max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ u₃ v₃} D := AsSmall.equiv   let s₃ : E ≌ AsSmall.{max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ u₃ v₃} E := AsSmall.equiv   let i : s₁.inverse ⋙ (F ⋙ G) ⋙ s₃.functor ≅       (s₁.inverse ⋙ F ⋙ s₂.functor) ⋙ (s₂.inverse ⋙ G ⋙ s₃.functor) :=     isoWhiskerLeft (s₁.inverse ⋙ F) (isoWhiskerRight s₂.unitIso (G ⋙ s₃.functor))   rw [final_iff_comp_equivalence (F ⋙ G) s₃.functor, final_iff_equivalence_comp s₁.inverse,     final_natIso_iff i, final_iff_isIso_colimit_pre]   rw [final_iff_comp_equivalence F s₂.functor, final_iff_equivalence_comp s₁.inverse,     final_iff_isIso_colimit_pre] at hF   rw [final_iff_comp_equivalence G s₃.functor, final_iff_equivalence_comp s₂.inverse,     final_iff_isIso_colimit_pre] at hG   intro H   rw [← colimit.pre_pre]   infer_instance
