explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.op: This definition establishes a correspondence between colimit cocones and limit cones by showing that if a cocone is a colimit, its opposite is a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.op: This definition states that if a structure forms a limit cone for a certain functor, then its dual structure forms a colimit cocone for the opposite functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.unop: This definition states that if a cocone of a functor is a colimit, then the corresponding inverted cocone is a limit for that functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.unop: This definition states that if a structure is a limit cone for a functor in a category, then its dual structure serves as a colimit cocone for the corresponding functor's opposite.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coneLeftOpOfCocone: This definition describes a method to transform a cocone associated with a contravariant functor into a cone associated with the corresponding left-op functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.desc: This definition describes a morphism from the point of a colimit cocone to the point of another cocone, ensuring a connection between their respective structures.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coconeOfConeLeftOp: This definition constructs a cocone for a functor by transforming a cone defined on the left-op of that functor, thereby altering its directionality.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.op_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in a quiver is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.op_comp: The theorem establishes that the operation for reversing the direction of the composition of two morphisms equals the composition of their individual reversals in the opposite order.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.op_unop: The theorem shows that applying the operation to revert the direction of a morphism and then applying the operation to reverse it returns the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.fac: This theorem establishes that the morphism from a cocone to its colimit, when composed with the corresponding arrow from the colimit, yields the arrow from the cocone at the same object, ensuring the commutativity of the involved diagram.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coconeOfConeLeftOp: This theorem determines the relationship between the morphism component of a cocone derived from a left adjoint functor and the morphism component of the cone associated with the original functor, demonstrating how they correspond under the operation of taking opposites.
explanatories.Opposite.op_unop: This theorem asserts that applying the opposite mapping and then the original mapping to an element of the opposite category returns the original element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that two morphisms from a colimit are equal if they yield the same result when composed with the cocone's morphisms.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.fac: This theorem shows that a specific lifting of a cone through a limit cone results in a commutative triangle involving the cone's projection morphisms and the natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms into a limit cone yield the same results when composed with the projection morphisms from the cone, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.Opposite.unop: This definition describes the canonical mapping from the opposite category of a type back to the original type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.unop: This definition outlines the process of converting a functor from the opposite category back to a functor in the original category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.unop: This definition transforms a cocone over a contravariant functor into an equivalent cone over the original functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.op: This definition transforms a cocone associated with a functor into a cone associated with the opposite functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.cone: This definition describes an arbitrary limit cone as a specific construction associated with a functor in a category that has a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.unop: This definition describes a process that transforms a cone associated with a contravariant functor into a cocone associated with the original functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.op: This definition describes the transformation that takes a cone of a functor and converts it into a cocone of the opposite functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp: This statement defines the composition of two functors, where the first functor is applied to an object followed by the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.inj: This definition retrieves the morphism from a specific object in a family to the designated point in the cofan associated with that family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.op: This definition introduces the concept of the opposite isomorphism, which associates an isomorphism between two objects in a category with an isomorphism between their opposites.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.desc: This definition states that a set of morphisms from each component of a coproduct to a common object induces a morphism from the coproduct itself to that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.ext: An isomorphism between two pullback cones can be established by providing an isomorphism between their cone points and verifying that it respects the first and second projections.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ext: An isomorphism between two pushout cocones can be established if there is an isomorphism between their points that preserves the structure of the morphisms corresponding to the pushout.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.h: The theorem states that if two morphisms from a common point of a colimit diagram are equal when composed with the diagram's projection, then those two morphisms themselves must also be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.hom_e: The theorem asserts that if two morphisms agree when composed with a specific morphism of a limit cone, then they must be equal.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitConeLeftOpO.fullDefinition: def isLimitConeLeftOpOfCocone (F : J ⥤ Cᵒᵖ) {c : Cocone F} (hc : IsColimit c) :     IsLimit (coneLeftOpOfCocone c) where   lift s := (hc.desc (coconeOfConeLeftOp s)).unop   fac s j :=     Quiver.Hom.op_inj <| by       simp only [coneLeftOpOfCocone_π_app, op_comp, Quiver.Hom.op_unop, IsColimit.fac,         coconeOfConeLeftOp_ι_app, op_unop]   uniq s m w := by     refine Quiver.Hom.op_inj (hc.hom_ext fun j => Quiver.Hom.unop_inj ?_)     simpa only [Quiver.Hom.op_unop, IsColimit.fac, coconeOfConeLeftOp_ι_app] using w (op j)
CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitConeLeftOpO.description: This definition states that a colimit for a functor can be transformed into a limit for its left-opposite functor in a corresponding category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.unop: This definition describes a process that transforms a cone associated with a contravariant functor into a cocone associated with the original functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.op: This definition describes the transformation that takes a cone of a functor and converts it into a cocone of the opposite functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.inj: This definition retrieves the morphism from a specific object in a family to the designated point in the cofan associated with that family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.op: This definition introduces the concept of the opposite isomorphism, which associates an isomorphism between two objects in a category with an isomorphism between their opposites.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.desc: This definition states that a set of morphisms from each component of a coproduct to a common object induces a morphism from the coproduct itself to that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.ext: An isomorphism between two pullback cones can be established by providing an isomorphism between their cone points and verifying that it respects the first and second projections.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ext: An isomorphism between two pushout cocones can be established if there is an isomorphism between their points that preserves the structure of the morphisms corresponding to the pushout.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.h: The theorem states that if two morphisms from a common point of a colimit diagram are equal when composed with the diagram's projection, then those two morphisms themselves must also be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.hom_e: The theorem asserts that if two morphisms agree when composed with a specific morphism of a limit cone, then they must be equal.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitConeRightOp.fullDefinition: def isLimitConeRightOpOfCocone (F : Jᵒᵖ ⥤ C) {c : Cocone F} (hc : IsColimit c) :     IsLimit (coneRightOpOfCocone c) where   lift s := (hc.desc (coconeOfConeRightOp s)).op   fac s j := Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (by simp)   uniq s m w := by     refine Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (hc.hom_ext fun j => Quiver.Hom.op_inj ?_)     simpa only [Quiver.Hom.unop_op, IsColimit.fac] using w (unop j)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.unop: This definition describes a process that transforms a cone associated with a contravariant functor into a cocone associated with the original functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.op: This definition describes the transformation that takes a cone of a functor and converts it into a cocone of the opposite functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp: This statement defines the composition of two functors, where the first functor is applied to an object followed by the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.inj: This definition retrieves the morphism from a specific object in a family to the designated point in the cofan associated with that family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.op: This definition introduces the concept of the opposite isomorphism, which associates an isomorphism between two objects in a category with an isomorphism between their opposites.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.desc: This definition states that a set of morphisms from each component of a coproduct to a common object induces a morphism from the coproduct itself to that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.ext: An isomorphism between two pullback cones can be established by providing an isomorphism between their cone points and verifying that it respects the first and second projections.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PushoutCocone.ext: An isomorphism between two pushout cocones can be established if there is an isomorphism between their points that preserves the structure of the morphisms corresponding to the pushout.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.h: The theorem states that if two morphisms from a common point of a colimit diagram are equal when composed with the diagram's projection, then those two morphisms themselves must also be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.IsLimit.hom_e: The theorem asserts that if two morphisms agree when composed with a specific morphism of a limit cone, then they must be equal.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitConeOfCocon.description: This definition states that a colimit for a functor from the left-opposite category can be transformed into a limit for the corresponding functor in the original category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim.fullDefinition: def isLimitEquivIsColimitUnop {X Y Z : Cᵒᵖ} {f : X ⟶ Z} {g : Y ⟶ Z} (c : PullbackCone f g) :     IsLimit c ≃ IsColimit c.unop :=   (IsLimit.equivIsoLimit c.unopOp).symm.trans c.unop.isColimitEquivIsLimitOp.symm
CategoryTheory.Limits.PullbackCone.isLim.description: A pullback cone serves as a limit in the opposite category if and only if its corresponding pushout cocone in the original category is a colimit.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.constant_of_preserves_mor: In a connected category, any function that produces the same output for objects connected by morphisms must yield the same value for all objects in that category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.isColimitPUn.fullDefinition: noncomputable def isColimitPUnitCocone [IsConnected C] : IsColimit (pUnitCocone.{w} C) where   desc s := s.ι.app Classical.ofNonempty   fac s j := by     ext ⟨⟩     apply constant_of_preserves_morphisms (s.ι.app · PUnit.unit)     intros X Y f     exact congrFun (s.ι.naturality f).symm PUnit.unit   uniq s m h := by     ext ⟨⟩     simp [← h Classical.ofNonempty]
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.isColimitPUn.description: This definition states that if a category is connected, then the cocone structure on the functor mapping every object to a single type with one element serves as a colimit cocone.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.colimitConst.fullDefinition: noncomputable def colimitConstPUnitIsoPUnit [IsConnected C] :     colimit (constPUnitFunctor.{w} C) ≅ PUnit.{w + 1} :=   IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (colimit.isColimit _) (isColimitPUnitCocone.{w} C)
CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.colimitConst.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the colimit of the constant functor that maps every object to a single unit type and the unit type itself, provided the category is connected.

Let `F` be a `Type`-valued functor. If two elements `a : F c` and `b : F d` represent the same

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Zigzag: Two objects in a category are connected by a zigzag relation if there exists a chain of morphisms between them that can include both forward and backward arrows.
explanatories.Sigma.fst: The first component of a dependent pair is extracted from the pair, returning the value of the first type.

CategoryTheory.Limits.Types.zigzag_of_eq.description: This theorem asserts that if two elements correspond to the same element in the colimit of a functor mapping to types, then their originating objects are related by a zigzag path.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.code:
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {ℰ : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₁, u₂} ℰ] (A : C ⥤ ℰ) : ℰ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.comment:
The functor taking `(E : ℰ) (c : Cᵒᵖ)` to the homset `(A.obj C ⟶ E)`. It is shown in `L_adjunction`
that this functor has a left adjoint (provided `E` has colimits) given by taking colimits over
categories of elements.
In the case where `ℰ = Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u` and `A = yoneda`, this functor is isomorphic to the identity.

Defined as in [MM92], Chapter I, Section 5, Theorem 2.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.fullDefinition: def restrictedYonedaHomEquiv' (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) (E : ℰ) :     (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda P ⋙ A ⟶       (Functor.const (CostructuredArrow yoneda P)).obj E) ≃       (P ⟶ (restrictedYoneda A).obj E) where   toFun f :=     { app := fun X x => f.app (CostructuredArrow.mk (yonedaEquiv.symm x))       naturality := fun {X₁ X₂} φ => by         ext x         let ψ : CostructuredArrow.mk (yonedaEquiv.symm (P.toPrefunctor.map φ x)) ⟶           CostructuredArrow.mk (yonedaEquiv.symm x) := CostructuredArrow.homMk φ.unop (by             dsimp [yonedaEquiv]             aesop_cat )         simpa using (f.naturality ψ).symm }   invFun g :=     { app := fun y => yonedaEquiv (y.hom ≫ g)       naturality := fun {X₁ X₂} φ => by         dsimp         rw [← CostructuredArrow.w φ]         dsimp [yonedaEquiv]         simp only [comp_id, id_comp]         refine (congr_fun (g.naturality φ.left.op) (X₂.hom.app (Opposite.op X₂.left)           (𝟙 _))).symm.trans ?_         dsimp         apply congr_arg         simpa using congr_fun (X₂.hom.naturality φ.left.op).symm (𝟙 _) }   left_inv f := by     ext ⟨X, ⟨⟨⟩⟩, φ⟩     suffices yonedaEquiv.symm (φ.app (Opposite.op X) (𝟙 X)) = φ by       dsimp       erw [yonedaEquiv_apply]       dsimp [CostructuredArrow.mk]       erw [this]     exact yonedaEquiv.injective (by aesop_cat)   right_inv g := by     ext X x     dsimp     erw [yonedaEquiv_apply]     dsimp     rw [yonedaEquiv_symm_app_apply]     simp
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.description: This defines an equivalence between morphisms in a certain structured context involving a category and a presheaf, capturing a relationship between arrow constructions and constant functors.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.code:
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYonedaHomEquiv.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {ℰ : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₁, u₂} ℰ] {A : C ⥤ ℰ} [yoneda.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension A] (L : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) ⥤ ℰ)
  (α : A ⟶ yoneda ⋙ L) [L.IsLeftKanExtension α] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) (E : ℰ) :
  (L.obj P ⟶ E) ≃ (P ⟶ (restrictedYoneda A).obj E)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.homEquiv: This definition states that there is a natural equivalence between morphisms from the cone point of a cocone to any object and cocones on the functor that have that object as their cone point when the cocone is a colimit.
explanatories.Equiv.trans: This definition establishes a method for composing two equivalence relations to create a new equivalence relation between the first and last types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda: This defines an equivalence between morphisms in a certain structured context involving a category and a presheaf, capturing a relationship between arrow constructions and constant functors.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.fullDefinition: noncomputable def restrictedYonedaHomEquiv (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) (E : ℰ) :     (L.obj P ⟶ E) ≃ (P ⟶ (restrictedYoneda A).obj E) :=   ((Functor.isPointwiseLeftKanExtensionOfIsLeftKanExtension _ α P).homEquiv E).trans     (restrictedYonedaHomEquiv' A P E)
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.restrictedYoneda.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between morphisms in a functor that can be seen as a left Kan extension and mappings from a presheaf to a specific object in a given category.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.yonedaAdjunction.comment:
If `L : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) ⥤ ℰ` is a pointwise left Kan extension
of a functor `A : C ⥤ ℰ` along the Yoneda embedding,
then `L` is a left adjoint of `restrictedYoneda A : ℰ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁`

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.yonedaAdjunction.fullDefinition: noncomputable def yonedaAdjunction : L ⊣ restrictedYoneda A :=   Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv     { homEquiv := restrictedYonedaHomEquiv L α       homEquiv_naturality_left_symm := fun {P Q X} f g => by         obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := (restrictedYonedaHomEquiv L α Q X).surjective g         apply (restrictedYonedaHomEquiv L α P X).injective         simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply, Equiv.symm_apply_apply]         ext Y y         dsimp [restrictedYonedaHomEquiv, restrictedYonedaHomEquiv', IsColimit.homEquiv]         rw [assoc, assoc, ← L.map_comp_assoc]         congr 3         apply yonedaEquiv.injective         simp [yonedaEquiv]       homEquiv_naturality_right := fun {P X Y} f g => by         apply (restrictedYonedaHomEquiv L α P Y).symm.injective         simp only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply]         dsimp [restrictedYonedaHomEquiv, restrictedYonedaHomEquiv', IsColimit.homEquiv]         apply (Functor.isPointwiseLeftKanExtensionOfIsLeftKanExtension L α P).hom_ext         intro p         rw [IsColimit.fac]         dsimp [restrictedYoneda, yonedaEquiv]         simp only [assoc]         congr 3         apply yonedaEquiv.injective         simp [yonedaEquiv] }
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.yonedaAdjunction.description: This definition establishes that if a functor serves as a pointwise left Kan extension of another functor along the Yoneda embedding, then it acts as a left adjoint to the functor defined by restricted Yoneda.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.yoneda: This definition describes the Yoneda embedding as a functor that maps a category into the category of presheaves on itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.HasPointwiseLeftK: This definition states that a functor has a pointwise left Kan extension along another functor if it possesses a pointwise left Kan extension at every object in the target category.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isIso_of_isLeftK.description: If a morphism arises as part of a left Kan extension of a functor along the Yoneda embedding, it is an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.functorToReprese.code:
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.functorToRepresentables.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) :
  P.Elementsᵒᵖ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.functorToReprese.comment:
A functor to the presheaf category in which everything in the image is representable (witnessed
by the fact that it factors through the yoneda embedding).
`coconeOfRepresentable` gives a cocone for this functor which is a colimit and has point `P`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryOfElements.π: This definition introduces a functor that extracts the underlying objects from the pairs in the category of elements for a functor, effectively forgetting the associated elements.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.leftOp: This definition specifies a method for transforming a functor from a category to the opposite of another category into a functor from the opposite of the first category to the second category.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.functorToReprese.fullDefinition: def functorToRepresentables (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) : P.Elementsᵒᵖ ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁ :=   (CategoryOfElements.π P).leftOp ⋙ yoneda
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.functorToReprese.description: This defines a functor that maps elements from a presheaf category to a new functorial structure where the images are representable, facilitated by its relation to the Yoneda embedding, and it provides a cocone that forms a colimit including the specified point.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.coconeOfRepresen.code:
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.coconeOfRepresentable.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) :
  Cocone (functorToRepresentables P)
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.coconeOfRepresen.comment:
This is a cocone with point `P` for the functor `functorToRepresentables P`. It is shown in
`colimitOfRepresentable P` that this cocone is a colimit: that is, we have exhibited an arbitrary
presheaf `P` as a colimit of representables.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.coconeOfRepresen.fullDefinition: noncomputable def coconeOfRepresentable (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) :     Cocone (functorToRepresentables P) where   pt := P   ι :=     { app := fun x => yonedaEquiv.symm x.unop.2       naturality := fun {x₁ x₂} f => by         dsimp         rw [comp_id]         erw [← yonedaEquiv_symm_map]         congr 1         rw [f.unop.2] }

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.colimitOfReprese.fullDefinition: noncomputable def colimitOfRepresentable (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) :     IsColimit (coconeOfRepresentable P) where   desc s :=     { app := fun X x => (s.ι.app (Opposite.op (Functor.elementsMk P X x))).app X (𝟙 _)       naturality := fun X Y f => by         ext x         have eq₁ := congr_fun (congr_app (s.w (CategoryOfElements.homMk (P.elementsMk X x)           (P.elementsMk Y (P.map f x)) f rfl).op) Y) (𝟙 _)         dsimp at eq₁ ⊢         simpa [← eq₁, id_comp] using           congr_fun ((s.ι.app (Opposite.op (P.elementsMk X x))).naturality f) (𝟙 _) }   fac s j := by     ext X x     let φ : j.unop ⟶ Functor.elementsMk P X ((yonedaEquiv.symm j.unop.2).app X x) := ⟨x.op, rfl⟩     simpa using congr_fun (congr_app (s.ι.naturality φ.op).symm X) (𝟙 _)   uniq s m hm := by     ext X x     dsimp     rw [← hm]     apply congr_arg     simp [coconeOfRepresentable_ι_app, yonedaEquiv]

  [Category.{v₁, u₂} ℰ] {A : C ⥤ ℰ} [yoneda.HasPointwiseLeftKanExtension A] (L : (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁) ⥤ ℰ)

  L ≅ yoneda.leftKanExtension A
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.uniqueExtensionA.comment:
Show that `yoneda.leftKanExtension A` is the unique colimit-preserving
functor which extends `A` to the presheaf category.

The second part of [MM92], Chapter I, Section 5, Corollary 4.
See Property 3 of https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Yoneda+extension#properties.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.Equifibered.comment:
A natural transformation is equifibered if every commutative square of the following form is
a pullback.
```
F(X) → F(Y)
 ↓      ↓
G(X) → G(Y)
```

CategoryTheory.HasForget₂.mk'.fullDefinition: def HasForget₂.mk' {C : Type u} {D : Type u'} [Category.{v} C] [ConcreteCategory.{w} C]     [Category.{v'} D] [ConcreteCategory.{w} D]     (obj : C → D) (h_obj : ∀ X, (forget D).obj (obj X) = (forget C).obj X)     (map : ∀ {X Y}, (X ⟶ Y) → (obj X ⟶ obj Y))     (h_map : ∀ {X Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}, HEq ((forget D).map (map f)) ((forget C).map f)) :     HasForget₂ C D where   forget₂ := Functor.Faithful.div _ _ _ @h_obj _ @h_map   forget_comp := by apply Functor.Faithful.div_comp

CategoryTheory.BundledHom.concreteCatego.fullDefinition: instance concreteCategory : ConcreteCategory.{u} (Bundled c) where   forget :=     { obj := fun X => X       map := @fun X Y f => 𝒞.toFun X.str Y.str f       map_id := fun X => 𝒞.id_toFun X.str       map_comp := fun f g => by dsimp; erw [𝒞.comp_toFun];rfl }   forget_faithful := { map_injective := by (intros; apply 𝒞.hom_ext) }

CategoryTheory.BundledHom.mkHasForget₂.fullDefinition: def mkHasForget₂ {d : Type u → Type u} {hom_d : ∀ ⦃α β : Type u⦄ (_ : d α) (_ : d β), Type u}     [BundledHom hom_d] (obj : ∀ ⦃α⦄, c α → d α)     (map : ∀ {X Y : Bundled c}, (X ⟶ Y) → (Bundled.map @obj X ⟶ (Bundled.map @obj Y)))     (h_map : ∀ {X Y : Bundled c} (f : X ⟶ Y), ⇑(map f) = ⇑f) :     HasForget₂ (Bundled c) (Bundled d) :=   HasForget₂.mk' (Bundled.map @obj) (fun _ => rfl) map (by     intros X Y f     rw [heq_eq_eq, forget_map_eq_coe, forget_map_eq_coe, h_map f])

CategoryTheory.UnbundledHom.bundledHom.fullDefinition: instance bundledHom : BundledHom fun α β (Iα : c α) (Iβ : c β) => Subtype (hom Iα Iβ) where   toFun _ _ := Subtype.val   id Iα := ⟨id, hom_id Iα⟩   id_toFun _ := rfl   comp _ _ _ g f := ⟨g.1 ∘ f.1, hom_comp g.2 f.2⟩   comp_toFun _ _ _ _ _ := rfl   hom_ext _ _ _ _ := Subtype.eq

CategoryTheory.Monad.algebraFunctorOfMon.comment:

lemmas about.

CategoryTheory.Monad.comparison.comment:
Given any adjunction `L ⊣ R`, there is a comparison functor `CategoryTheory.Monad.comparison R`
sending objects `Y : D` to Eilenberg-Moore algebras for `L ⋙ R` with underlying object `R.obj X`.

We later show that this is full when `R` is full, faithful when `R` is faithful,
and essentially surjective when `R` is reflective.

CategoryTheory.Monad.comparison.fullDefinition: def Monad.comparison (h : L ⊣ R) : D ⥤ h.toMonad.Algebra where   obj X :=     { A := R.obj X       a := R.map (h.counit.app X)       assoc := by         dsimp         rw [← R.map_comp, ← Adjunction.counit_naturality, R.map_comp] }   map f :=     { f := R.map f       h := by         dsimp         rw [← R.map_comp, Adjunction.counit_naturality, R.map_comp] }

CategoryTheory.Reflective.comparison_ess.fullDefinition: instance comparison_essSurj [Reflective R] :     (Monad.comparison (reflectorAdjunction R)).EssSurj := by   refine ⟨fun X => ⟨(reflector R).obj X.A, ⟨?_⟩⟩⟩   symm   refine Monad.Algebra.isoMk ?_ ?_   · exact asIso ((reflectorAdjunction R).unit.app X.A)   dsimp only [Functor.comp_map, Monad.comparison_obj_a, asIso_hom, Functor.comp_obj,     Monad.comparison_obj_A, Adjunction.toMonad_coe]   rw [← cancel_epi ((reflectorAdjunction R).unit.app X.A)]   dsimp only [Functor.id_obj, Functor.comp_obj]   rw [Adjunction.unit_naturality_assoc,     Adjunction.right_triangle_components, comp_id]   apply (X.unit_assoc _).symm

CategoryTheory.Monad.beckAlgebraCoequali.fullDefinition: def beckAlgebraCoequalizer : IsColimit (beckAlgebraCofork X) :=   Cofork.IsColimit.mk' _ fun s => by     have h₁ : (T : C ⥤ C).map X.a ≫ s.π.f = T.μ.app X.A ≫ s.π.f :=       congr_arg Monad.Algebra.Hom.f s.condition     have h₂ : (T : C ⥤ C).map s.π.f ≫ s.pt.a = T.μ.app X.A ≫ s.π.f := s.π.h     refine ⟨⟨T.η.app _ ≫ s.π.f, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩     · dsimp       rw [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc, h₂, Monad.right_unit_assoc,         show X.a ≫ _ ≫ _ = _ from T.η.naturality_assoc _ _, h₁, Monad.left_unit_assoc]     · ext       simpa [← T.η.naturality_assoc, T.left_unit_assoc] using T.η.app ((T : C ⥤ C).obj X.A) ≫= h₁     · intro m hm       ext       dsimp only       rw [← hm]       apply (X.unit_assoc _).symm
CategoryTheory.Monad.beckAlgebraCoequali.description: This definition establishes that the constructed cofork in the category of algebras serves as a colimit, demonstrating that any algebra can be viewed as a reflexive coequalizer of free algebras.

CategoryTheory.Monad.MonadicityInternal..fullDefinition: def comparisonLeftAdjointHomEquiv (A : adj.toMonad.Algebra) (B : D)     [HasCoequalizer (F.map A.a) (adj.counit.app (F.obj A.A))] :     (comparisonLeftAdjointObj adj A ⟶ B) ≃ (A ⟶ (comparison adj).obj B) :=   calc     (comparisonLeftAdjointObj adj A ⟶ B) ≃ { f : F.obj A.A ⟶ B // _ } :=       Cofork.IsColimit.homIso (colimit.isColimit _) B     _ ≃ { g : A.A ⟶ G.obj B // G.map (F.map g) ≫ G.map (adj.counit.app B) = A.a ≫ g } := by       refine (adj.homEquiv _ _).subtypeEquiv ?_       intro f       rw [← (adj.homEquiv _ _).injective.eq_iff, Adjunction.homEquiv_naturality_left,         adj.homEquiv_unit, adj.homEquiv_unit, G.map_comp]       dsimp       rw [adj.right_triangle_components_assoc, ← G.map_comp, F.map_comp, Category.assoc,         adj.counit_naturality, adj.left_triangle_components_assoc]       apply eq_comm     _ ≃ (A ⟶ (comparison adj).obj B) :=       { toFun := fun g =>           { f := _             h := g.prop }         invFun := fun f => ⟨f.f, f.h⟩         left_inv := fun g => by ext; rfl         right_inv := fun f => by ext; rfl }

CategoryTheory.Monad.monadicOfHasPreserv.comment:
Reflexive (crude) monadicity theorem. If `G` has a right adjoint, `D` has and `G` preserves
reflexive coequalizers and `G` reflects isomorphisms, then `G` is monadic.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Monad.Algebra.a: This definition describes the structure morphism that connects an object of a monad algebra to itself in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Monad.Algebra.unit: This theorem asserts that the application of the unit of a monad to an algebra object, when composed with its structure morphism, yields the identity morphism on that object.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Monad.Algebra.Hom.f: This definition describes a morphism between the underlying objects of two algebra structures associated with a morphism of monads in category theory.
This definition establishes an adjunction between the left adjoint of the comparison functor and the comparison functor itself, given the existence of appropriate coequalizers for algebra structures associated with an adjunction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Monad.beckCoequalizer: This definition states that the Beck cofork associated with a monad algebra functions as a colimit in the category theory framework.
This theorem establishes that the unit of the comparison adjunction applied to a monad algebra corresponds to the morphism obtained from the coequalizer of two specific morphisms in the algebra's structure.
This definition asserts that the unit cofork associated with a monad algebra is a colimit when a specific functor preserves the coequalizer of given morphisms.
This definition asserts that the counit cofork is a colimit provided that a certain functor reflects colimits associated with a specific adjunction.

This theorem establishes that the application of the counit of the comparison adjunction to an object in the target category can be expressed as the morphism obtained from the colimit of a specific pair of parallel morphisms involving the counit and its functorial mappings.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.isIso_of_reflects_iso: If a functor reflects isomorphisms and the image of a morphism under this functor is an isomorphism, then the original morphism must also be an isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Monad.forget: This definition describes a functor that maps each monad algebra to its underlying object in the category by discarding the algebraic structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.coconePo: This definition establishes that the points of cocones associated with a functor are unique up to isomorphism when those cocones are colimits.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.reflectsColimitOfR: This definition states that if a functor preserves colimits and reflects isomorphisms, then it also reflects the colimit of a given diagram when that colimit exists.

CategoryTheory.Monad.monadicOfHasPreserv.fullDefinition: def monadicOfHasPreservesReflexiveCoequalizersOfReflectsIsomorphisms : MonadicRightAdjoint G where   adj := adj   eqv := by     have : ∀ (X : Algebra adj.toMonad), IsIso ((comparisonAdjunction adj).unit.app X) := by       intro X       apply         @isIso_of_reflects_iso _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (Monad.forget adj.toMonad) ?_ _       · change IsIso ((comparisonAdjunction adj).unit.app X).f         rw [comparisonAdjunction_unit_f]         exact (IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (beckCoequalizer X)           (unitColimitOfPreservesCoequalizer X)).isIso_hom     have : ∀ (Y : D), IsIso ((comparisonAdjunction adj).counit.app Y) := by       intro Y       rw [comparisonAdjunction_counit_app]       -- Porting note: passing instances through       change IsIso (IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso _ ?_).hom       infer_instance       -- Porting note: passing instances through       apply @counitCoequalizerOfReflectsCoequalizer _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ ?_       apply reflectsColimitOfReflectsIsomorphisms     exact (comparisonAdjunction adj).toEquivalence.isEquivalence_inverse
CategoryTheory.Monad.monadicOfHasPreserv.description: This definition states that if a functor has a right adjoint, preserves reflexive coequalizers, and reflects isomorphisms, then it is monadic, confirming a specific form of monadicity in category theory.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.restrictionLT.{u, u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {J : Type u}
  [LinearOrder J] {j : J} (F : { i // i ≤ j } ⥤ C) {i : J} (hi : i ≤ j) : { k // k < i } ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.restric.comment:
The functor `{ k // k < i } ⥤ C` obtained by "restriction" of `F : { i // i ≤ j } ⥤ C`
when `i ≤ j`.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.restric.description: The functor defined by restricting the domain of a given functor to elements less than a specified index produces a new functor for that subset.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.mapSucc.comment:
The map `F.obj ⟨i, _⟩ ⟶ F.obj ⟨wellOrderSucc i, _⟩` when `F : { i // i ≤ j } ⥤ C`
and `i : J` is such that `i < j`.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.mapSucc.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev mapSucc' (i : J) (hi : i < j) :     F.obj ⟨i, hi.le⟩ ⟶ F.obj ⟨wellOrderSucc i, wellOrderSucc_le hi⟩ :=   F.map (homOfLE (by simpa only [Subtype.mk_le_mk] using self_le_wellOrderSucc i))
CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.mapSucc.description: The defined map provides a morphism between the images of a functor at an index and its successor under specific conditions in a well-ordered category.

CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.coconeO.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.coconeOfLE.{u, u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {J : Type u}
  [LinearOrder J] {j : J} (F : { i // i ≤ j } ⥤ C) {i : J} (hi : i ≤ j) : Cocone (Iteration.restrictionLT F hi)
CategoryTheory.Functor.Iteration.coconeO.comment:
Given `F : { i // i ≤ j } ⥤ C`, `i : J` such that `hi : i ≤ j`, this is the
cocone consisting of all maps `F.obj ⟨k, hk⟩ ⟶ F.obj ⟨i, hi⟩` for `k : J` such that `k < i`.

CategoryTheory.SmallObject.functor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def functor : Over S ⥤ Over S where   obj π := Over.mk (πFunctorObj f π.hom)   map {π₁ π₂} φ := Over.homMk (functorMap f π₁.hom π₂.hom φ.left (Over.w φ))   map_id _ := by ext; dsimp; simp   map_comp {π₁ π₂ π₃} φ φ' := by     ext1     dsimp     ext ⟨i, t, b, w⟩     · simp     · simp [functorMap, ι_functorMapTgt_assoc f π₁.hom π₂.hom φ.left (Over.w φ) i t b w _ rfl,         ι_functorMapTgt_assoc f π₁.hom π₃.hom (φ.left ≫ φ'.left) (Over.w (φ ≫ φ')) i t b w _ rfl,         ι_functorMapTgt_assoc f π₂.hom π₃.hom (φ'.left) (Over.w φ') i (t ≫ φ.left) b           (by simp [w]) (t ≫ φ.left ≫ φ'.left) (by simp)]

CategoryTheory.WithTerminal.liftUnique.fullDefinition: def liftUnique {D : Type*} [Category D] {Z : D} (F : C ⥤ D) (M : ∀ x : C, F.obj x ⟶ Z)     (hM : ∀ (x y : C) (f : x ⟶ y), F.map f ≫ M y = M x)     (G : WithTerminal C ⥤ D) (h : incl ⋙ G ≅ F)     (hG : G.obj star ≅ Z)     (hh : ∀ x : C, G.map (starTerminal.from (incl.obj x)) ≫ hG.hom = h.hom.app x ≫ M x) :     G ≅ lift F M hM :=   NatIso.ofComponents     (fun X =>       match X with       | of x => h.app x       | star => hG)     (by       rintro (X | X) (Y | Y) f       · apply h.hom.naturality       · cases f         exact hh _       · cases f       · cases f         change G.map (𝟙 _) ≫ hG.hom = hG.hom ≫ 𝟙 _         simp)

CategoryTheory.WithInitial.liftUnique.fullDefinition: def liftUnique {D : Type*} [Category D] {Z : D} (F : C ⥤ D) (M : ∀ x : C, Z ⟶ F.obj x)     (hM : ∀ (x y : C) (f : x ⟶ y), M x ≫ F.map f = M y)     (G : WithInitial C ⥤ D) (h : incl ⋙ G ≅ F)     (hG : G.obj star ≅ Z)     (hh : ∀ x : C, hG.symm.hom ≫ G.map (starInitial.to (incl.obj x)) = M x ≫ h.symm.hom.app x) :     G ≅ lift F M hM :=   NatIso.ofComponents     (fun X =>       match X with       | of x => h.app x       | star => hG)     (by       rintro (X | X) (Y | Y) f       · apply h.hom.naturality       · cases f       · cases f         change G.map _ ≫ h.hom.app _ = hG.hom ≫ _         symm         erw [← Iso.eq_inv_comp, ← Category.assoc, hh]         simp       · cases f         change G.map (𝟙 _) ≫ hG.hom = hG.hom ≫ 𝟙 _         simp)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.homEquiv: This definition describes an equivalence between morphisms in two categories that arises from an adjunction.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Adjunction.Co: This definition describes a functor that transforms a coalgebra associated with one functor into an algebra associated with another functor, leveraging the properties of their adjunction.

explanatories.Equiv.left_inv: This theorem asserts that the inverse function of an equivalence relation is a left inverse of the original function.
explanatories.Eq.symm: The symmetry of equality states that if one element is equal to another, then the second element is also equal to the first.

CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Adjunction.Al.fullDefinition: def AlgCoalgEquiv.unitIso (adj : F ⊣ G) :     𝟭 (Algebra F) ≅ Algebra.toCoalgebraOf adj ⋙ Coalgebra.toAlgebraOf adj where   hom :=     { app := fun A =>         { f := 𝟙 A.1           h := by             erw [F.map_id, Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]             apply (adj.homEquiv _ _).left_inv A.str } }   inv :=     { app := fun A =>         { f := 𝟙 A.1           h := by             erw [F.map_id, Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]             apply ((adj.homEquiv _ _).left_inv A.str).symm }       naturality := fun A₁ A₂ f => by         ext         dsimp         erw [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]         rfl }
CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Adjunction.Al.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the identity functor on algebras over a left adjoint and the composition of converting an algebra to a coalgebra and then back to an algebra via the corresponding right adjoint.

CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Adjunction.Al.fullDefinition: def AlgCoalgEquiv.counitIso (adj : F ⊣ G) :     Coalgebra.toAlgebraOf adj ⋙ Algebra.toCoalgebraOf adj ≅ 𝟭 (Coalgebra G) where   hom :=     { app := fun V =>         { f := 𝟙 V.1           h := by             dsimp             erw [G.map_id, Category.id_comp, Category.comp_id]             apply (adj.homEquiv _ _).right_inv V.str }       naturality := fun V₁ V₂ f => by         ext         dsimp         erw [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]         rfl }   inv :=     { app := fun V =>         { f := 𝟙 V.1           h := by             dsimp             rw [G.map_id, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]             apply ((adj.homEquiv _ _).right_inv V.str).symm } }

CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpiStruct.desc.comment:
For every `W` with a morphism `e : Y ⟶ W` that coequalizes every pair of morphisms
`g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Y` which `f` coequalizes, `desc e h` is a morphism `X ⟶ W`...

CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpiStruct.desc.fullDefinition: desc : ∀ {W : C} (e : Y ⟶ W),     (∀ {Z : C} (g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Y), g₁ ≫ f = g₂ ≫ f → g₁ ≫ e = g₂ ≫ e) → (X ⟶ W)   /-- ...factorizing `e` through `f`... -/   fac : ∀ {W : C} (e : Y ⟶ W)     (h : ∀ {Z : C} (g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Y), g₁ ≫ f = g₂ ≫ f → g₁ ≫ e = g₂ ≫ e),     f ≫ desc e h = e   /-- ...and as such, unique. -/   uniq : ∀ {W : C} (e : Y ⟶ W)     (h : ∀ {Z : C} (g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Y), g₁ ≫ f = g₂ ≫ f → g₁ ≫ e = g₂ ≫ e)     (m : X ⟶ W), f ≫ m = e → m = desc e h
CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpiStruct.desc.description: For any morphism that coequalizes pairs of morphisms which another morphism also coequalizes, there exists a corresponding morphism from the initial object to the new object.

CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiFamilyStructO.fullDefinition: def effectiveEpiFamilyStructOfIsIsoDesc {B : C} {α : Type*} (X : α → C)     (π : (a : α) → (X a ⟶ B)) [HasCoproduct X] [IsIso (Sigma.desc π)] :     EffectiveEpiFamilyStruct X π where   desc e _ := (asIso (Sigma.desc π)).inv ≫ (Sigma.desc e)   fac e h := by     intro a     have : π a = Sigma.ι X a ≫ (asIso (Sigma.desc π)).hom := by simp only [asIso_hom,       colimit.ι_desc, Cofan.mk_pt, Cofan.mk_ι_app]     rw [this, Category.assoc]     simp only [asIso_hom, asIso_inv, IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc, colimit.ι_desc, Cofan.mk_pt,       Cofan.mk_ι_app]   uniq e h m hm := by     simp only [asIso_inv, IsIso.eq_inv_comp]     ext a     simp only [colimit.ι_desc_assoc, Discrete.functor_obj, Cofan.mk_pt, Cofan.mk_ι_app,       colimit.ι_desc]     exact hm a

CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiFamilyStructC.fullDefinition: def effectiveEpiFamilyStructCompOfEffectiveEpiSplitEpi' {α : Type*} {B : C} {X Y : α → C}     (f : (a : α) → X a ⟶ B) (g : (a : α) → Y a ⟶ X a) (i : (a : α) → X a ⟶ Y a)     (hi : ∀ a, i a ≫ g a = 𝟙 _) [EffectiveEpiFamily _ f] :     EffectiveEpiFamilyStruct _ (fun a ↦ g a ≫ f a) where   desc e w := EffectiveEpiFamily.desc _ f (fun a ↦ i a ≫ e a) fun a₁ a₂ g₁ g₂ _ ↦ (by     simp only [← Category.assoc]     apply w _ _ (g₁ ≫ i a₁) (g₂ ≫ i a₂)     simpa [← Category.assoc, Category.assoc, hi])   fac e w a := by     simp only [Category.assoc, EffectiveEpiFamily.fac]     rw [← Category.id_comp (e a), ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc]     apply w     simp only [Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp, ← Category.assoc]     aesop   uniq _ _ _ hm := by     apply EffectiveEpiFamily.uniq _ f     intro a     rw [← hm a, ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc, hi, Category.id_comp]

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.d: This definition specifies how to obtain a morphism from the point of a cofork to another object, given a compatible morphism that equates the images of two other morphisms through that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.isColimit: This definition states that a morphism identified as a regular epimorphism serves as the coequalizer in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.RegularEpi.w: This theorem states that if a morphism is a regular epimorphism, then it coequalizes two specific maps, ensuring the equality of their compositions with the epimorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.IsColimit.h: The theorem states that if two morphisms from a common point of a colimit diagram are equal when composed with the diagram's projection, then those two morphisms themselves must also be equal.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.desc: The descent along an effective epimorphism provides a morphism from the initial object to another object that factors through the effective epimorphism while preserving the necessary equality conditions between morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.fac: The factorization of a morphism through an effective epimorphism yields a morphism that, when composed with the effective epimorphism, results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpi.uniq: The uniqueness of morphisms factoring through an effective epimorphism is proven by demonstrating that any such morphism, satisfying the necessary equality condition, must coincide with the morphism produced by descending along the effective epimorphism.

CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiStructOfRegul.fullDefinition: def effectiveEpiStructOfRegularEpi {B X : C} (f : X ⟶ B) [RegularEpi f] :     EffectiveEpiStruct f where   desc _ h := Cofork.IsColimit.desc isColimit _ (h _ _ w)   fac _ _ := Cofork.IsColimit.π_desc' isColimit _ _   uniq _ _ _ hg := Cofork.IsColimit.hom_ext isColimit (hg.trans     (Cofork.IsColimit.π_desc' _ _ _).symm)
CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiStructOfRegul.description: An effective epimorphism structure can be derived from a regular epimorphism, establishing that the regular epimorphism possesses the properties characteristic of effective epimorphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unit: This definition describes the unit morphism of an equivalence between two categories, relating the identity functor of the first category to the composition of the equivalence's functor and its inverse.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.congrArg: If two values are equal, then applying the same function to both yields equal results.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp_obj: This theorem states that the application of a composed functor to an object yields the same result as applying the first functor to the object and then the second functor to the result.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.homEquiv_couni: This theorem depicts the naturality condition of the counit in an adjunction, relating a morphism in one category to the composition of a mapped morphism and the counit's application in another category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.id_obj: The theorem states that the identity functor applied to an object in a category returns that same object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.toAdjunction_: This theorem asserts that the counit of an adjunction derived from an equivalence between two categories is identical to the counit of the equivalence itself.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counit: This definition describes the counit morphism of an equivalence between two categories, relating the composition of the equivalence's inverse and functor to the identity functor of the second category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpiFamily.fac: The factorization of a morphism through an effective epimorphic family yields a morphism that, when composed with the relevant projection, equals the original morphism for each component.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.fun_inv_map: This theorem establishes a relationship between the mapping of a morphism through the functor of an equivalence and the composition of the counit and its inverse, illustrating how these transformations interact within the structure of the categories involved.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.inv_hom_id_app: This theorem establishes that every element is identical to itself, underscoring the foundational principle of equality in mathematics.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.EffectiveEpiFamily.uniq: The uniqueness of the morphism from the object to the target object is demonstrated by showing that any morphism satisfying a specified condition must equal the morphism obtained through an effective epimorphic family.

CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiFamilyStructO.fullDefinition: def effectiveEpiFamilyStructOfEquivalence : EffectiveEpiFamilyStruct (fun a ↦ e.functor.obj (X a))     (fun a ↦ e.functor.map (π a)) where   desc ε h := (e.toAdjunction.homEquiv _ _).symm       (EffectiveEpiFamily.desc X π (fun a ↦ e.unit.app _ ≫ e.inverse.map (ε a))       (effectiveEpiFamilyStructOfEquivalence_aux e X π ε h))   fac ε h a := by     simp only [Functor.comp_obj, Adjunction.homEquiv_counit, Functor.id_obj,       Equivalence.toAdjunction_counit]     have := congrArg ((fun f ↦ f ≫ e.counit.app _) ∘ e.functor.map)       (EffectiveEpiFamily.fac X π (fun a ↦ e.unit.app _ ≫ e.inverse.map (ε a))       (effectiveEpiFamilyStructOfEquivalence_aux e X π ε h) a)     simp only [Functor.id_obj, Functor.comp_obj, Function.comp_apply, Functor.map_comp,         Category.assoc, Equivalence.fun_inv_map, Iso.inv_hom_id_app, Category.comp_id] at this     simp [this]   uniq ε h m hm := by     simp only [Functor.comp_obj, Adjunction.homEquiv_counit, Functor.id_obj,       Equivalence.toAdjunction_counit]     have := EffectiveEpiFamily.uniq X π (fun a ↦ e.unit.app _ ≫ e.inverse.map (ε a))       (effectiveEpiFamilyStructOfEquivalence_aux e X π ε h)     specialize this (e.unit.app _ ≫ e.inverse.map m) fun a ↦ ?_     · rw [← congrArg e.inverse.map (hm a)]       simp     · simp [← this]
CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiFamilyStructO.description: This definition describes a structure that relates effective epimorphic families between two categories connected by an equivalence, showing that such families in the first category are preserved through the equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.localization.comment:
If `adj : G ⊣ F` is an adjunction between two categories `C₁` and `C₂` that
are equipped with localization functors `L₁ : C₁ ⥤ D₁` and `L₂ : C₂ ⥤ D₂` with
respect to `W₁ : MorphismProperty C₁` and `W₂ : MorphismProperty C₂`, and that
the functors `F : C₂ ⥤ C₁` and `G : C₁ ⥤ C₂` induce functors `F' : D₂ ⥤ D₁`
and `G' : D₁ ⥤ D₂` on the localized categories, then the adjunction `adj`
induces an adjunction `G' ⊣ F'`.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.localization.fullDefinition: noncomputable def localization : G' ⊣ F' :=   Adjunction.mkOfUnitCounit     { unit := Localization.ε adj L₁ W₁ L₂ G' F'       counit := Localization.η adj L₁ L₂ W₂ G' F'       left_triangle := by         apply natTrans_ext L₁ W₁         intro X₁         have eq := congr_app adj.left_triangle X₁         dsimp at eq         rw [NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.comp_app, whiskerRight_app, Localization.ε_app,           Functor.associator_hom_app, id_comp, whiskerLeft_app, G'.map_comp, G'.map_comp,           assoc, assoc]         erw [(Localization.η adj L₁ L₂ W₂ G' F').naturality, Localization.η_app,           assoc, assoc, ← G'.map_comp_assoc, ← G'.map_comp_assoc, assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id_app,           comp_id, (CatCommSq.iso G L₁ L₂ G').inv.naturality_assoc, ← L₂.map_comp_assoc, eq,           L₂.map_id, id_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id_app]         rfl       right_triangle := by         apply natTrans_ext L₂ W₂         intro X₂         have eq := congr_app adj.right_triangle X₂         dsimp at eq         rw [NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.comp_app, whiskerLeft_app, whiskerRight_app,           Localization.η_app, Functor.associator_inv_app, id_comp, F'.map_comp, F'.map_comp]         erw [← (Localization.ε _ _ _ _ _ _).naturality_assoc, Localization.ε_app,           assoc, assoc, ← F'.map_comp_assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id_app, F'.map_id, id_comp,           ← NatTrans.naturality, ← L₁.map_comp_assoc, eq, L₁.map_id, id_comp,           Iso.inv_hom_id_app]         rfl }

CategoryTheory.LocalizerMorphism.IsRightDerivabilityStructure.Constructor.fromRightResolution.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5,
    u_6}
  {C₁ : Type u_1} {C₂ : Type u_2} [Category.{u_4, u_1} C₁] [Category.{u_5, u_2} C₂] {W₁ : MorphismProperty C₁}
  {W₂ : MorphismProperty C₂} (Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂) [W₁.IsMultiplicative] {D : Type u_3} [Category.{u_6, u_3} D]
  (L : C₂ ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization W₂] {X₂ : C₂} {X₃ : D} (y : L.obj X₂ ⟶ X₃) :
  Φ.RightResolution X₂ ⥤
    (TwoSquare.mk Φ.functor (Φ.functor ⋙ L) L (𝟭 D) (Φ.functor ⋙ L).rightUnitor.inv).CostructuredArrowDownwards y
CategoryTheory.LocalizerMorphism.IsRight.comment:
Given `Φ : LocalizerMorphism W₁ W₂`, `L : C₂ ⥤ D` a localization functor for `W₂` and
a morphism `y : L.obj X₂ ⟶ X₃`, this is the functor which sends `R : Φ.RightResolution d` to
`(isoOfHom L W₂ R.w R.hw).inv ≫ y` in the category `w.CostructuredArrowDownwards y`
where `w` is `TwoSquare.mk Φ.functor (Φ.functor ⋙ L) L (𝟭 _) (Functor.rightUnitor _).inv`.

  [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (L : C ⥤ D) {W : MorphismProperty C} [L.IsLocalization W]
  [W.ContainsIdentities] {J : Type} [Finite J] [HasProductsOfShape J C] (hW : W.IsStableUnderProductsOfShape J)

CategoryTheory.Localization.HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom.{w, w', v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  (W : MorphismProperty C) (M : Type w') [AddMonoid M] [HasShift C M] (X Y : C) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Localization.HasSmallLoca.comment:
Given objects `X` and `Y` in a category `C`, this is the property that
all the types of morphisms from `X⟦a⟧` to `Y⟦b⟧` are `w`-small
in the localized category with respect to a class of morphisms `W`.

CategoryTheory.Localization.HasSmallLoca.fullDefinition: abbrev HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom : Prop :=   ∀ (a b : M), HasSmallLocalizedHom.{w} W (X⟦a⟧) (Y⟦b⟧)
CategoryTheory.Localization.HasSmallLoca.description: This definition describes a property indicating that the morphisms from a shifted version of one object to a shifted version of another in a localized category are small in a specific sense related to a given class of morphisms.

  {M : Type w'} [AddMonoid M] [HasShift C M] [W.IsCompatibleWithShift M] {X Y : C} [HasSmallLocalizedHom W X Y]
  (f : SmallHom W X Y) (a : M) [HasSmallLocalizedHom W ((shiftFunctor C a).obj X) ((shiftFunctor C a).obj Y)] :
  SmallHom W ((shiftFunctor C a).obj X) ((shiftFunctor C a).obj Y)
CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallHom.shi.comment:
Given `f : SmallHom W X Y` and `a : M`, this is the element
in `SmallHom W (X⟦a⟧) (Y⟦a⟧)` obtained by shifting by `a`.

CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallHom.shi.fullDefinition: noncomputable def shift : SmallHom.{w} W (X⟦a⟧) (Y⟦a⟧) :=   (W.shiftLocalizerMorphism a).smallHomMap f
CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallHom.shi.description: This definition constructs a new morphism in a localized category from an existing morphism by applying a shift operation defined by an additive monoid.

CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallShifted.fullDefinition: noncomputable def shift {a : M} [HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom.{w} W M X Y]     [HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom.{w} W M Y Y]   (f : SmallShiftedHom.{w} W X Y a) (n a' : M) (h : a + n = a') :     SmallHom.{w} W (X⟦n⟧) (Y⟦a'⟧) :=   (SmallHom.shift f n).comp (SmallHom.mk W ((shiftFunctorAdd' C a n a' h).inv.app Y))

CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallHom.equiv_shift.{w, w', v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {W : MorphismProperty C} {M : Type w'} [AddMonoid M] [HasShift C M] [HasShift D M]
  [W.IsCompatibleWithShift M] (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization W] [L.CommShift M] {X Y : C} [HasSmallLocalizedHom W X Y]
  (f : SmallHom W X Y) (a : M) [HasSmallLocalizedHom W ((shiftFunctor C a).obj X) ((shiftFunctor C a).obj Y)] :
  (SmallHom.equiv W L) (f.shift a) =
    (L.commShiftIso a).hom.app X ≫ (shiftFunctor D a).map ((SmallHom.equiv W L) f) ≫ (L.commShiftIso a).inv.app Y

  [L.IsLocalization W] [HasShift D M] [L.CommShift M] {X Y : C} [HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom W M X Y] {m : M} :

and `L` commutes with the shifts.

CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallShifted.fullDefinition: noncomputable def equiv [HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom.{w} W M X Y] {m : M} :     SmallShiftedHom.{w} W X Y m ≃ ShiftedHom (L.obj X) (L.obj Y) m :=   (SmallHom.equiv W L).trans ((L.commShiftIso m).app Y).homToEquiv

CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallShifted.code:
CategoryTheory.Localization.SmallShiftedHom.equiv_shift'.{w, w', v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] (W : MorphismProperty C) {M : Type w'} [AddMonoid M] [HasShift C M]
  [W.IsCompatibleWithShift M] (L : C ⥤ D) [L.IsLocalization W] [HasShift D M] [L.CommShift M] {X Y : C} {a : M}
  [HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom W M X Y] [HasSmallLocalizedShiftedHom W M Y Y] (f : SmallShiftedHom W X Y a) (n a' : M)
  (h : a + n = a') :
  (SmallHom.equiv W L) (f.shift n a' h) =
    (L.commShiftIso n).hom.app X ≫
      (shiftFunctor D n).map ((SmallHom.equiv W L) f) ≫
        (shiftFunctor D n).map ((L.commShiftIso a).hom.app Y) ≫
          (shiftFunctorAdd' D a n a' h).inv.app (L.obj Y) ≫ (L.commShiftIso a').inv.app Y

  [Category.{u_3, u_1} C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [∀ (n : ℤ), (shiftFunctor C n).Additive]
  [Pretriangulated C] {W : MorphismProperty C} [self : W.IsCompatibleWithTriangulation] (T₁ T₂ : Triangle C) :
  T₁ ∈ distinguishedTriangles →
    T₂ ∈ distinguishedTriangles →
      ∀ (a : T₁.obj₁ ⟶ T₂.obj₁) (b : T₁.obj₂ ⟶ T₂.obj₂),
        W a →
          W b →
            T₁.mor₁ ≫ b = a ≫ T₂.mor₁ →
              ∃ c, ∃ (_ : W c), T₁.mor₂ ≫ c = b ≫ T₂.mor₂ ∧ T₁.mor₃ ≫ (shiftFunctor C 1).map a = c ≫ T₂.mor₃

CategoryTheory.CategoryOfElements.fromCo.fullDefinition: def fromCostructuredArrow (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) : (CostructuredArrow yoneda F)ᵒᵖ ⥤ F.Elements where   obj X := ⟨op (unop X).1, yonedaEquiv.1 (unop X).3⟩   map {X Y} f :=     ⟨f.unop.1.op, by       convert (congr_fun ((unop X).hom.naturality f.unop.left.op) (𝟙 _)).symm       simp only [Equiv.toFun_as_coe, Quiver.Hom.unop_op, yonedaEquiv_apply, types_comp_apply,         Category.comp_id, yoneda_obj_map]       have : yoneda.map f.unop.left ≫ (unop X).hom = (unop Y).hom := by         convert f.unop.3       erw [← this]       simp only [yoneda_map_app, FunctorToTypes.comp]       erw [Category.id_comp]⟩

CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ofEquiv : MonoidalClosed C where   closed X :=     { rightAdj := F.toFunctor ⋙ ihom (F.obj X) ⋙ G       adj := (adj.comp ((ihom.adjunction (F.obj X)).comp           adj.toEquivalence.symm.toAdjunction)).ofNatIsoLeft             (Iso.compInverseIso (H := adj.toEquivalence) (MonoidalFunctor.commTensorLeft F X)) }
CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv.description: This definition allows the property of being monoidal closed to be transferred from one monoidal category to another through a monoidal equivalence of categories.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_cu.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_curry_def.{v, u, u₂, v₂} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] (F : MonoidalFunctor C D) {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F.toFunctor ⊣ G)
  [F.IsEquivalence] [MonoidalClosed D] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z) :
  curry f =
    (adj.homEquiv Y ((ihom (F.obj X)).obj (F.obj Z)))
      (curry
        ((adj.toEquivalence.symm.toAdjunction.homEquiv (F.obj X ⊗ F.obj Y) Z)
          ((F.commTensorLeft X).compInverseIso.hom.app Y ≫ f)))
CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_cu.comment:
Suppose we have a monoidal equivalence `F : C ≌ D`, with `D` monoidal closed. We can pull the
monoidal closed instance back along the equivalence. For `X, Y, Z : C`, this lemma describes the
resulting currying map `Hom(X ⊗ Y, Z) → Hom(Y, (X ⟶[C] Z))`. (`X ⟶[C] Z` is defined to be
`F⁻¹(F(X) ⟶[D] F(Z))`, so currying in `C` is given by essentially conjugating currying in
`D` by `F.`)

CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_cu.description: This theorem shows that, under a monoidal equivalence between two categories where the target category is monoidal closed, the process of currying a morphism from the tensor product of two objects in the source category corresponds to a specific transformation involving currying in the target category.

CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_un.code:
CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_uncurry_def.{v, u, u₂, v₂} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [MonoidalCategory C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] [MonoidalCategory D] (F : MonoidalFunctor C D) {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F.toFunctor ⊣ G)
  [F.IsEquivalence] [MonoidalClosed D] {X Y Z : C} (f : Y ⟶ (ihom X).obj Z) :
  uncurry f =
    (F.commTensorLeft X).compInverseIso.inv.app Y ≫
      (adj.toEquivalence.symm.toAdjunction.homEquiv ((F.toFunctor ⋙ tensorLeft (F.obj X)).obj Y) Z).symm
        (uncurry ((adj.homEquiv Y ((ihom (F.obj X)).obj (adj.toEquivalence.symm.inverse.obj Z))).symm f))
CategoryTheory.MonoidalClosed.ofEquiv_un.comment:
Suppose we have a monoidal equivalence `F : C ≌ D`, with `D` monoidal closed. We can pull the
monoidal closed instance back along the equivalence. For `X, Y, Z : C`, this lemma describes the
resulting uncurrying map `Hom(Y, (X ⟶[C] Z)) → Hom(X ⊗ Y ⟶ Z)`. (`X ⟶[C] Z` is
defined to be `F⁻¹(F(X) ⟶[D] F(Z))`, so uncurrying in `C` is given by essentially conjugating
uncurrying in `D` by `F.`)

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedIhom.fullDefinition: def closedIhom (F : D ⥤ C) : (D ⥤ C) ⥤ D ⥤ C :=   ((whiskeringRight₂ D Cᵒᵖ C C).obj internalHom).obj (Groupoid.invFunctor D ⋙ F.op)

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedIhom_obj_ma.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.closedIhom_obj_map.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {D : Type u_1} {C : Type u_2} [Groupoid D]

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedUnit.fullDefinition: def closedUnit (F : D ⥤ C) : 𝟭 (D ⥤ C) ⟶ tensorLeft F ⋙ closedIhom F where   app G :=   { app := fun X => (ihom.coev (F.obj X)).app (G.obj X)     naturality := by       intro X Y f       dsimp       simp only [ihom.coev_naturality, closedIhom_obj_map, Monoidal.tensorObj_map]       dsimp       rw [coev_app_comp_pre_app_assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, tensorHom_def]       simp }

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedCounit.fullDefinition: def closedCounit (F : D ⥤ C) : closedIhom F ⋙ tensorLeft F ⟶ 𝟭 (D ⥤ C) where   app G :=   { app := fun X => (ihom.ev (F.obj X)).app (G.obj X)     naturality := by       intro X Y f       dsimp       simp only [closedIhom_obj_map, pre_comm_ihom_map]       rw [tensorHom_def]       simp }

CategoryTheory.Exponentiable.comment:
An object `X` is *exponentiable* if `(X × -)` is a left adjoint.
We define this as being `Closed` in the cartesian monoidal structure.

CategoryTheory.Exponentiable.fullDefinition: abbrev Exponentiable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteProducts C] (X : C) :=   Closed X

CategoryTheory.binaryProductExponentiabl.code:
CategoryTheory.binaryProductExponentiable.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasFiniteProducts C] {X Y : C}
  (hX : Exponentiable X) (hY : Exponentiable Y) : Exponentiable (X ⨯ Y)
CategoryTheory.binaryProductExponentiabl.comment:
If `X` and `Y` are exponentiable then `X ⨯ Y` is.

CategoryTheory.frobeniusMorphism.{v, u, u'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v, u'} D]
  [HasFiniteProducts C] [HasFiniteProducts D] (F : C ⥤ D) {L : D ⥤ C} (h : L ⊣ F) (A : C) :
  prod.functor.obj (F.obj A) ⋙ L ⟶ L ⋙ prod.functor.obj A
CategoryTheory.frobeniusMorphism.comment:
The Frobenius morphism for an adjunction `L ⊣ F` at `A` is given by the morphism

    L(FA ⨯ B) ⟶ LFA ⨯ LB ⟶ A ⨯ LB

natural in `B`, where the first morphism is the product comparison and the latter uses the counit
of the adjunction.

We will show that if `C` and `D` are cartesian closed, then this morphism is an isomorphism for all
`A` iff `F` is a cartesian closed functor, i.e. it preserves exponentials.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prodComparisonNatT: This definition describes a natural transformation between functors that relates the product of an object with another object in the source category to the product of the image of that object under the functor with the image of the other object in the target category.

CategoryTheory.uniqueHomsetOfInitialIsoT.fullDefinition: def uniqueHomsetOfInitialIsoTerminal [HasInitial C] (i : ⊥_ C ≅ ⊤_ C) (X Y : C) : Unique (X ⟶ Y) :=   Equiv.unique <|     calc       (X ⟶ Y) ≃ (X ⨯ ⊤_ C ⟶ Y) := Iso.homCongr (prod.rightUnitor _).symm (Iso.refl _)       _ ≃ (X ⨯ ⊥_ C ⟶ Y) := (Iso.homCongr (prod.mapIso (Iso.refl _) i.symm) (Iso.refl _))       _ ≃ (⊥_ C ⟶ Y ^^ X) := (exp.adjunction _).homEquiv _ _
CategoryTheory.uniqueHomsetOfInitialIsoT.description: In a cartesian closed category where the initial object is isomorphic to the terminal object, it follows that there is only one morphism between any two objects.

CategoryTheory.exponentialIdealReflectiv.comment:
If `D` is a reflective subcategory, the property of being an exponential ideal is equivalent to
the presence of a natural isomorphism `i ⋙ exp A ⋙ leftAdjoint i ⋙ i ≅ i ⋙ exp A`, that is:
`(A ⟹ iB) ≅ i L (A ⟹ iB)`, naturally in `B`.
The converse is given in `ExponentialIdeal.mk_of_iso`.

CategoryTheory.exponentialIdeal_of_prese.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 10) exponentialIdeal_of_preservesBinaryProducts     [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) (reflector i)] : ExponentialIdeal i := by   let ir := reflectorAdjunction i   let L : C ⥤ D := reflector i   let η : 𝟭 C ⟶ L ⋙ i := ir.unit   let ε : i ⋙ L ⟶ 𝟭 D := ir.counit   apply ExponentialIdeal.mk'   intro B A   let q : i.obj (L.obj (A ⟹ i.obj B)) ⟶ A ⟹ i.obj B := by     apply CartesianClosed.curry (ir.homEquiv _ _ _)     apply _ ≫ (ir.homEquiv _ _).symm ((exp.ev A).app (i.obj B))     exact prodComparison L A _ ≫ Limits.prod.map (𝟙 _) (ε.app _) ≫ inv (prodComparison _ _ _)   have : η.app (A ⟹ i.obj B) ≫ q = 𝟙 (A ⟹ i.obj B) := by     dsimp     rw [← curry_natural_left, curry_eq_iff, uncurry_id_eq_ev, ← ir.homEquiv_naturality_left,       ir.homEquiv_apply_eq, assoc, assoc, prodComparison_natural_assoc, L.map_id,       ← prod.map_id_comp_assoc, ir.left_triangle_components, prod.map_id_id, id_comp]     apply IsIso.hom_inv_id_assoc   haveI : IsSplitMono (η.app (A ⟹ i.obj B)) := IsSplitMono.mk' ⟨_, this⟩   apply mem_essImage_of_unit_isSplitMono
CategoryTheory.exponentialIdeal_of_prese.description: An ideal is identified as an exponential ideal if it preserves binary products in a category that is cartesian closed and has finite products.

CategoryTheory.cartesianClosedOfReflecti.fullDefinition: def cartesianClosedOfReflective : CartesianClosed D :=   { __ := monoidalOfHasFiniteProducts D -- Porting note (#10754): added this instance     closed := fun B =>       { rightAdj := i ⋙ exp (i.obj B) ⋙ reflector i         adj := by           apply (exp.adjunction (i.obj B)).restrictFullyFaithful i.fullyFaithfulOfReflective             i.fullyFaithfulOfReflective           · symm             refine NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => ?_) (fun f => ?_)             · haveI :=                 Adjunction.rightAdjointPreservesLimits.{0, 0} (reflectorAdjunction i)               apply asIso (prodComparison i B X)             · dsimp [asIso]               rw [prodComparison_natural, Functor.map_id]           · apply (exponentialIdealReflective i _).symm } }

CategoryTheory.bijection.{v₁, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] [Category.{v₁, u₂} D]
  (i : D ⥤ C) [HasFiniteProducts C] [Reflective i] [CartesianClosed C] [HasFiniteProducts D] [ExponentialIdeal i]
  (A B : C) (X : D) : ((reflector i).obj (A ⨯ B) ⟶ X) ≃ ((reflector i).obj A ⨯ (reflector i).obj B ⟶ X)
CategoryTheory.bijection.comment:
We construct a bijection between morphisms `L(A ⨯ B) ⟶ X` and morphisms `LA ⨯ LB ⟶ X`.
This bijection has two key properties:
* It is natural in `X`: See `bijection_natural`.
* When `X = LA ⨯ LB`, then the backwards direction sends the identity morphism to the product
  comparison morphism: See `bijection_symm_apply_id`.

Together these help show that `L` preserves binary products. This should be considered
*internal implementation* towards `preservesBinaryProductsOfExponentialIdeal`.

CategoryTheory.bijection.fullDefinition: noncomputable def bijection (A B : C) (X : D) :     ((reflector i).obj (A ⨯ B) ⟶ X) ≃ ((reflector i).obj A ⨯ (reflector i).obj B ⟶ X) :=   calc     _ ≃ (A ⨯ B ⟶ i.obj X) := (reflectorAdjunction i).homEquiv _ _     _ ≃ (B ⨯ A ⟶ i.obj X) := (Limits.prod.braiding _ _).homCongr (Iso.refl _)     _ ≃ (A ⟶ B ⟹ i.obj X) := (exp.adjunction _).homEquiv _ _     _ ≃ (i.obj ((reflector i).obj A) ⟶ B ⟹ i.obj X) :=       (unitCompPartialBijective _ (ExponentialIdeal.exp_closed (i.obj_mem_essImage _) _))     _ ≃ (B ⨯ i.obj ((reflector i).obj A) ⟶ i.obj X) := ((exp.adjunction _).homEquiv _ _).symm     _ ≃ (i.obj ((reflector i).obj A) ⨯ B ⟶ i.obj X) :=       ((Limits.prod.braiding _ _).homCongr (Iso.refl _))     _ ≃ (B ⟶ i.obj ((reflector i).obj A) ⟹ i.obj X) := (exp.adjunction _).homEquiv _ _     _ ≃ (i.obj ((reflector i).obj B) ⟶ i.obj ((reflector i).obj A) ⟹ i.obj X) :=       (unitCompPartialBijective _ (ExponentialIdeal.exp_closed (i.obj_mem_essImage _) _))     _ ≃ (i.obj ((reflector i).obj A) ⨯ i.obj ((reflector i).obj B) ⟶ i.obj X) :=       ((exp.adjunction _).homEquiv _ _).symm     _ ≃ (i.obj ((reflector i).obj A ⨯ (reflector i).obj B) ⟶ i.obj X) :=       haveI : PreservesLimits i := (reflectorAdjunction i).rightAdjointPreservesLimits       haveI := preservesSmallestLimitsOfPreservesLimits i       Iso.homCongr (PreservesLimitPair.iso _ _ _).symm (Iso.refl (i.obj X))     _ ≃ ((reflector i).obj A ⨯ (reflector i).obj B ⟶ X) :=       i.fullyFaithfulOfReflective.homEquiv.symm
CategoryTheory.bijection.description: A bijection is established between morphisms from the product of two objects to another object in a reflective context and morphisms from the reflections of those two objects, demonstrating the preservation of binary products.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback.comment:

CategoryTheory.Sieve.pushforward.description: The pushforward operation maps a sieve from one object to another along a morphism, including all morphisms that factor through the original sieve.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.galoisCoinsertionOf.fullDefinition: def galoisCoinsertionOfMono (f : Y ⟶ X) [Mono f] :     GaloisCoinsertion (Sieve.pushforward f) (Sieve.pullback f) := by   apply (galoisConnection f).toGaloisCoinsertion   rintro S Z g ⟨g₁, hf, hg₁⟩   rw [cancel_mono f] at hf   rwa [← hf]

CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion_is.fullDefinition: instance functorInclusion_is_mono : Mono S.functorInclusion :=   ⟨fun f g h => by     ext Y y     simpa [Subtype.ext_iff_val] using congr_fun (NatTrans.congr_app h Y) y⟩
CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion_is.description: This definition confirms that the functor inclusion associated with a sieve corresponds to a monomorphism in the category framework.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor.code:
CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} {R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁}
  (f : R ⟶ yoneda.obj X) : Sieve X
CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor.comment:
A natural transformation to a representable functor induces a sieve. This is the left inverse of
`functorInclusion`, shown in `sieveOfSubfunctor_functorInclusion`.

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.arrows: This definition establishes a construction that converts a sieve on an object in a category into a corresponding presieve on the same object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.downward_closed: This theorem states that if a sieve is satisfied for a morphism, then it also holds under the composition with any other morphism leading into the first one.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.functor: A sieve defines a presheaf, which is a functor that maps an opposite category to types.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.FunctorToTypes.naturality: This theorem demonstrates that the natural transformation between two functors commutes with morphisms, preserving the structure when mapping through each functor.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor.fullDefinition: def sieveOfSubfunctor {R} (f : R ⟶ yoneda.obj X) : Sieve X where   arrows Y g := ∃ t, f.app (Opposite.op Y) t = g   downward_closed := by     rintro Y Z _ ⟨t, rfl⟩ g     refine ⟨R.map g.op t, ?_⟩     rw [FunctorToTypes.naturality _ _ f]     simp
CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor.description: This definition states that a natural transformation from a subfunctor to the Yoneda functor produces a sieve on a specified object within a category.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion_ap.code:
CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion_app.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} (S : Sieve X) (Y : Cᵒᵖ)
  (f : S.functor.obj Y) : S.functorInclusion.app Y f = ↑f
CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion_ap.description: This theorem states that the application of the inclusion functor to an object in a sieve yields the same element as the original object lifted to the type associated with the sieve.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor_a.code:
CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor_apply.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} {R : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁}
  (f : R ⟶ yoneda.obj X) (Y : C) (g : Y ⟶ X) : (sieveOfSubfunctor f).arrows g = ∃ t, f.app (Opposite.op Y) t = g

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.arrows: This definition establishes a construction that converts a sieve on an object in a category into a corresponding presieve on the same object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.functor: A sieve defines a presheaf, which is a functor that maps an opposite category to types.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor_a.description: This theorem states that a morphism belongs to the arrows of the sieve derived from a subfunctor if and only if there exists an element such that the application of the subfunctor to the corresponding object retrieves that morphism.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor_f.code:
CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor_functorInclusion.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C}

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion: This definition indicates a natural inclusion of the functor associated with a sieve into the functor represented by the Yoneda embedding at a given object.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.sieveOfSubfunctor_f.description: This theorem asserts that the sieve generated by the inclusion functor of a given sieve is precisely that sieve itself.

explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
