CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion_to.fullDefinition: instance functorInclusion_top_isIso : IsIso (⊤ : Sieve X).functorInclusion :=   ⟨⟨{ app := fun Y a => ⟨a, ⟨⟩⟩ }, rfl, rfl⟩⟩
CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorInclusion_to.description: This definition asserts that the functor inclusion from the terminal presieve is an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.siev.code:
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.sieves.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (self : GrothendieckTopology C)
  (X : C) : Set (Sieve X)
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.siev.comment:
A Grothendieck topology on `C` consists of a set of sieves for each object `X`,
which satisfy some axioms.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Top.top: A function that retrieves the top element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback: This definition describes a construction that transforms a sieve on one object into a sieve on another object via the inverse image along a given morphism.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.siev.fullDefinition: sieves : ∀ X : C, Set (Sieve X)   /-- The sieves associated to each object must contain the top sieve.     Use `GrothendieckTopology.top_mem`. -/   top_mem' : ∀ X, ⊤ ∈ sieves X   /-- Stability under pullback. Use `GrothendieckTopology.pullback_stable`. -/   pullback_stable' : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ ⦃S : Sieve X⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), S ∈ sieves X → S.pullback f ∈ sieves Y   /-- Transitivity of sieves in a Grothendieck topology.     Use `GrothendieckTopology.transitive`. -/   transitive' :     ∀ ⦃X⦄ ⦃S : Sieve X⦄ (_ : S ∈ sieves X) (R : Sieve X),       (∀ ⦃Y⦄ ⦃f : Y ⟶ X⦄, S f → R.pullback f ∈ sieves Y) → R ∈ sieves X
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.siev.description: This definition specifies that a Grothendieck topology on a category consists of a collection of sieves associated with each object in that category, which must adhere to specific axioms.

  (h : J₁.sieves = J₂.sieves) : J₁ = J₂
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.ext.comment:
An extensionality lemma in terms of the coercion to a pi-type.
We prove this explicitly rather than deriving it so that it is in terms of the coercion rather than
the projection `.sieves`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.siev: This definition specifies that a Grothendieck topology on a category consists of a collection of sieves associated with each object in that category, which must adhere to specific axioms.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.ext: This theorem states that two sieves on the same object are equal if they contain the same arrows from any other object.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.ext.description: If two Grothendieck topologies on a category have the same associated sieves, then they are considered equal.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.top_.code:

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.top_.description: Every Grothendieck topology on a category enforces that the top sieve is included in the collection of sieves associated with each object.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pull.description: If a sieve is part of a Grothendieck topology for one object, then its pullback via any morphism to another object will also be included in the topology for that second object.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.tran.code:
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.transitive'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (self : GrothendieckTopology C)

Transitivity of sieves in a Grothendieck topology.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.supe.code:
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.superset_covering.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : C} {S R : Sieve X}

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.supe.comment:
If `S` is a subset of `R`, and `S` is covering, then `R` is covering as well.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00Z5> (2), or discussion after [MM92] Chapter III,
Section 2, Definition 1.

The intersection of two covering sieves is covering.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.bind: This definition describes a process that constructs a sieve on an object by combining a presieve defined on that object with a sieve associated with each morphism in the presieve's domain.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.bind.description: If a sieve is covering in a Grothendieck topology and a family of sieves associated with it is also covering for each object, then the combined sieve formed by binding these families remains covering.

also known as the indiscrete, coarse, or chaotic topology.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.triv.fullDefinition: def trivial : GrothendieckTopology C where   sieves X := {⊤}   top_mem' X := rfl   pullback_stable' X Y S f hf := by     rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hf ⊢     simp [hf]   transitive' X S hS R hR := by     rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff, ← Sieve.id_mem_iff_eq_top] at hS     simpa using hR hS

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.dens.fullDefinition: def dense : GrothendieckTopology C where   sieves X S := ∀ {Y : C} (f : Y ⟶ X), ∃ (Z : _) (g : Z ⟶ Y), S (g ≫ f)   top_mem' X Y f := ⟨Y, 𝟙 Y, ⟨⟩⟩   pullback_stable' := by     intro X Y S h H Z f     rcases H (f ≫ h) with ⟨W, g, H'⟩     exact ⟨W, g, by simpa⟩   transitive' := by     intro X S H₁ R H₂ Y f     rcases H₁ f with ⟨Z, g, H₃⟩     rcases H₂ H₃ (𝟙 Z) with ⟨W, h, H₄⟩     exact ⟨W, h ≫ g, by simpa using H₄⟩

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Righ.code: CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.RightOreCondition.{v, u} (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] : Prop
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Righ.comment:
A category satisfies the right Ore condition if any span can be completed to a commutative square.
NB. Any category with pullbacks obviously satisfies the right Ore condition, see
`right_ore_of_pullbacks`.
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Righ.fullDefinition: def RightOreCondition (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] : Prop :=   ∀ {X Y Z : C} (yx : Y ⟶ X) (zx : Z ⟶ X), ∃ (W : _) (wy : W ⟶ Y) (wz : W ⟶ Z), wy ≫ yx = wz ≫ zx
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Righ.description: A category satisfies the right Ore condition if every span of objects can be transformed into a commutative square.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.righ.description: If a category has pullbacks, then the right Ore condition holds for that category.

  GrothendieckTopology C

The atomic Grothendieck topology: a sieve is covering iff it is nonempty.
For the pullback stability condition, we need the right Ore condition to hold.

See https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/atomic+site, or [MM92] Chapter III, Section 2, example (f).

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.atom.fullDefinition: def atomic (hro : RightOreCondition C) : GrothendieckTopology C where   sieves X S := ∃ (Y : _) (f : Y ⟶ X), S f   top_mem' X := ⟨_, 𝟙 _, ⟨⟩⟩   pullback_stable' := by     rintro X Y S h ⟨Z, f, hf⟩     rcases hro h f with ⟨W, g, k, comm⟩     refine ⟨_, g, ?_⟩     simp [comm, hf]   transitive' := by     rintro X S ⟨Y, f, hf⟩ R h     rcases h hf with ⟨Z, g, hg⟩     exact ⟨_, _, hg⟩
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.atom.description: The atomic Grothendieck topology on a category is defined such that a sieve is considered covering if and only if it is nonempty, under the condition that the right Ore condition holds.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove.comment:

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove.fullDefinition: def Cover (X : C) : Type max u v :=   { S : Sieve X // S ∈ J X } -- deriving Preorder

using this.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.generateSingleton.comment:

CategoryTheory.Sieve.generateSingleton.fullDefinition: def Sieve.generateSingleton {X Y : C} (f : Y ⟶ X) : Sieve X where   arrows Z := { g | ∃ (e : Z ⟶ Y), e ≫ f = g }   downward_closed := by     rintro W Z g ⟨e,rfl⟩ q     exact ⟨q ≫ e, by simp⟩
CategoryTheory.Sieve.generateSingleton.description: The sieve generated by a morphism consists of all morphisms that factor through that morphism, providing convenient definitional properties.

explanatories.Exists.choose_spec: An element chosen from an existence assertion satisfies the property asserted by that existence statement.

CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiStructOfIsCol.fullDefinition: def effectiveEpiStructOfIsColimit {X Y : C} (f : Y ⟶ X)     (Hf : IsColimit (Sieve.generateSingleton f : Presieve X).cocone) :     EffectiveEpiStruct f :=   let aux {W : C} (e : Y ⟶ W)     (h : ∀ {Z : C} (g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Y), g₁ ≫ f = g₂ ≫ f → g₁ ≫ e = g₂ ≫ e) :     Cocone (Sieve.generateSingleton f).arrows.diagram :=     { pt := W       ι := {         app := fun ⟨T,hT⟩ => hT.choose ≫ e         naturality := by           rintro ⟨A,hA⟩ ⟨B,hB⟩ (q : A ⟶ B)           dsimp; simp only [← Category.assoc, Category.comp_id]           apply h           rw [Category.assoc, hB.choose_spec, hA.choose_spec, Over.w] } }   { desc := fun {W} e h => Hf.desc (aux e h)     fac := by       intro W e h       dsimp       have := Hf.fac (aux e h) ⟨Over.mk f, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩       dsimp at this; rw [this]; clear this       nth_rewrite 2 [← Category.id_comp e]       apply h       generalize_proofs hh       rw [hh.choose_spec, Category.id_comp]     uniq := by       intro W e h m hm       dsimp       apply Hf.uniq (aux e h)       rintro ⟨A,g,hA⟩       dsimp       nth_rewrite 1 [← hA, Category.assoc, hm]       apply h       generalize_proofs hh       rwa [hh.choose_spec] }
CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiStructOfIsCol.description: This construction provides a structure for a morphism to be considered an effective epimorphism if the associated sieve generated by a single morphism is shown to meet the criteria of being a colimit cocone.

CategoryTheory.isColimitOfEffectiveEpiSt.fullDefinition: def isColimitOfEffectiveEpiStruct {X Y : C} (f : Y ⟶ X) (Hf : EffectiveEpiStruct f) :     IsColimit (Sieve.generateSingleton f : Presieve X).cocone :=   letI D := FullSubcategory fun T : Over X => Sieve.generateSingleton f T.hom   letI F : D ⥤ _ := (Sieve.generateSingleton f).arrows.diagram   { desc := fun S => Hf.desc (S.ι.app ⟨Over.mk f, ⟨𝟙 _, by simp⟩⟩) <| by       intro Z g₁ g₂ h       let Y' : D := ⟨Over.mk f, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩       let Z' : D := ⟨Over.mk (g₁ ≫ f), g₁, rfl⟩       let g₁' : Z' ⟶ Y' := Over.homMk g₁       let g₂' : Z' ⟶ Y' := Over.homMk g₂ (by simp [h])       change F.map g₁' ≫ _ = F.map g₂' ≫ _       simp only [S.w]     fac := by       rintro S ⟨T,g,hT⟩       dsimp       nth_rewrite 1 [← hT, Category.assoc, Hf.fac]       let y : D := ⟨Over.mk f, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩       let x : D := ⟨Over.mk T.hom, g, hT⟩       let g' : x ⟶ y := Over.homMk g       change F.map g' ≫ _ = _       rw [S.w]       rfl     uniq := by       intro S m hm       dsimp       generalize_proofs h1 h2       apply Hf.uniq _ h2       exact hm ⟨Over.mk f, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩ }
CategoryTheory.isColimitOfEffectiveEpiSt.description: An arrow is shown to create a colimit if it is part of an effective epimorphic structure.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.generateFamily.fullDefinition: def Sieve.generateFamily {B : C} {α : Type*} (X : α → C) (π : (a : α) → (X a ⟶ B)) :     Sieve B where   arrows Y := { f | ∃ (a : α) (g : Y ⟶ X a), g ≫ π a = f }   downward_closed := by     rintro Y₁ Y₂ g₁ ⟨a,q,rfl⟩ e     exact ⟨a, e ≫ q, by simp⟩
CategoryTheory.Sieve.generateFamily.description: This definition creates a sieve of morphisms that factor through a specified morphism in a family of morphisms directed toward a common object.

CategoryTheory.effectiveEpiFamilyStructO.fullDefinition: def effectiveEpiFamilyStructOfIsColimit {B : C} {α : Type*}     (X : α → C) (π : (a : α) → (X a ⟶ B))     (H : IsColimit (Sieve.generateFamily X π : Presieve B).cocone) :     EffectiveEpiFamilyStruct X π :=   let aux {W : C} (e : (a : α) → (X a ⟶ W))     (h : ∀ {Z : C} (a₁ a₂ : α) (g₁ : Z ⟶ X a₁) (g₂ : Z ⟶ X a₂),       g₁ ≫ π _ = g₂ ≫ π _ → g₁ ≫ e _ = g₂ ≫ e _) :     Cocone (Sieve.generateFamily X π).arrows.diagram := {       pt := W       ι := {         app := fun ⟨T,hT⟩ => hT.choose_spec.choose ≫ e hT.choose         naturality := by           intro ⟨A,a,(g₁ : A.left ⟶ _),ha⟩ ⟨B,b,(g₂ : B.left ⟶ _),hb⟩ (q : A ⟶ B)           dsimp; rw [Category.comp_id, ← Category.assoc]           apply h; rw [Category.assoc]           generalize_proofs h1 h2 h3 h4           rw [h2.choose_spec, h4.choose_spec, Over.w] } }   { desc := fun {W} e h => H.desc (aux e h)     fac := by       intro W e h a       dsimp       have := H.fac (aux e h) ⟨Over.mk (π a), a, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩       dsimp at this; rw [this]; clear this       conv_rhs => rw [← Category.id_comp (e a)]       apply h       generalize_proofs h1 h2       rw [h2.choose_spec, Category.id_comp]     uniq := by       intro W e h m hm       apply H.uniq (aux e h)       rintro ⟨T, a, (g : T.left ⟶ _), ha⟩       dsimp       nth_rewrite 1 [← ha, Category.assoc, hm]       apply h       generalize_proofs h1 h2       rwa [h2.choose_spec] }

CategoryTheory.isColimitOfEffectiveEpiFa.fullDefinition: def isColimitOfEffectiveEpiFamilyStruct {B : C} {α : Type*}     (X : α → C) (π : (a : α) → (X a ⟶ B)) (H : EffectiveEpiFamilyStruct X π) :     IsColimit (Sieve.generateFamily X π : Presieve B).cocone :=   letI D := FullSubcategory fun T : Over B => Sieve.generateFamily X π T.hom   letI F : D ⥤ _ := (Sieve.generateFamily X π).arrows.diagram   { desc := fun S => H.desc (fun a => S.ι.app ⟨Over.mk (π a), ⟨a,𝟙 _, by simp⟩⟩) <| by       intro Z a₁ a₂ g₁ g₂ h       dsimp       let A₁ : D := ⟨Over.mk (π a₁), a₁, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩       let A₂ : D := ⟨Over.mk (π a₂), a₂, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩       let Z' : D := ⟨Over.mk (g₁ ≫ π a₁), a₁, g₁, rfl⟩       let i₁ : Z' ⟶ A₁ := Over.homMk g₁       let i₂ : Z' ⟶ A₂ := Over.homMk g₂       change F.map i₁ ≫ _ = F.map i₂ ≫ _       simp only [S.w]     fac := by       intro S ⟨T, a, (g : T.left ⟶ X a), hT⟩       dsimp       nth_rewrite 1 [← hT, Category.assoc, H.fac]       let A : D := ⟨Over.mk (π a), a, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩       let B : D := ⟨Over.mk T.hom, a, g, hT⟩       let i : B ⟶ A := Over.homMk g       change F.map i ≫ _ = _       rw [S.w]       rfl     uniq := by       intro S m hm; dsimp       apply H.uniq       intro a       exact hm ⟨Over.mk (π a), a, 𝟙 _, by simp⟩ }
CategoryTheory.isColimitOfEffectiveEpiFa.description: This construction demonstrates that a family of morphisms forms a colimit cocone if it is structured as an effective epimorphism.

CategoryTheory.Pretopology.coverings.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasPullbacks C] (self : Pretopology C)
  (X : C) : Set (Presieve X)

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve: This definition describes a presieve as a collection of morphisms that all have a common codomain in a given category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.singleton: This definition describes a singleton presieve, which consists of a single morphism from one object to another within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.bind: This definition describes a construction that, given a set of morphisms with a common codomain, generates a new set of morphisms also with that codomain by composing them with arrows in a specified function for each morphism in the original set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.tran: If a sieve is included in the collection for an object in a Grothendieck topology, then any sieve that can be pulled back along morphisms related to that sieve is also included in the collection for the same object.

CategoryTheory.Pretopology.coverings.fullDefinition: coverings : ∀ X : C, Set (Presieve X)   has_isos : ∀ ⦃X Y⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsIso f], Presieve.singleton f ∈ coverings X   pullbacks : ∀ ⦃X Y⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) (S), S ∈ coverings X → pullbackArrows f S ∈ coverings Y   transitive :     ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (S : Presieve X) (Ti : ∀ ⦃Y⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), S f → Presieve Y),       S ∈ coverings X → (∀ ⦃Y⦄ (f) (H : S f), Ti f H ∈ coverings Y) → S.bind Ti ∈ coverings X

CategoryTheory.Pretopology.toGrothendiec.fullDefinition: def toGrothendieck (K : Pretopology C) : GrothendieckTopology C where   sieves X S := ∃ R ∈ K X, R ≤ (S : Presieve _)   top_mem' X := ⟨Presieve.singleton (𝟙 _), K.has_isos _, fun _ _ _ => ⟨⟩⟩   pullback_stable' X Y S g := by     rintro ⟨R, hR, RS⟩     refine ⟨_, K.pullbacks g _ hR, ?_⟩     rw [← Sieve.sets_iff_generate, Sieve.pullbackArrows_comm]     apply Sieve.pullback_monotone     rwa [Sieve.giGenerate.gc]   transitive' := by     rintro X S ⟨R', hR', RS⟩ R t     choose t₁ t₂ t₃ using t     refine ⟨_, K.transitive _ _ hR' fun _ f hf => t₂ (RS _ hf), ?_⟩     rintro Y _ ⟨Z, g, f, hg, hf, rfl⟩     apply t₃ (RS _ hg) _ hf
CategoryTheory.Pretopology.toGrothendiec.description: This definition establishes a method to form a Grothendieck topology from a pretopology by identifying coverings based on the inclusion of families from the original pretopology.

CategoryTheory.Pretopology.ofGrothendiec.fullDefinition: def ofGrothendieck (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Pretopology C where   coverings X R := Sieve.generate R ∈ J X   has_isos X Y f i := J.covering_of_eq_top (by simp)   pullbacks X Y f R hR := by     simp only [Set.mem_def, Sieve.pullbackArrows_comm]     apply J.pullback_stable f hR   transitive X S Ti hS hTi := by     apply J.transitive hS     intro Y f     rintro ⟨Z, g, f, hf, rfl⟩     rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]     apply J.pullback_stable g     apply J.superset_covering _ (hTi _ hf)     rintro Y g ⟨W, h, g, hg, rfl⟩     exact ⟨_, h, _, ⟨_, _, _, hf, hg, rfl⟩, by simp⟩

CategoryTheory.Pretopology.gi.fullDefinition: def gi : GaloisInsertion (toGrothendieck C) (ofGrothendieck C) where   gc K J := by     constructor     · intro h X R hR       exact h _ ⟨_, hR, Sieve.le_generate R⟩     · rintro h X S ⟨R, hR, RS⟩       apply J.superset_covering _ (h _ hR)       rwa [Sieve.giGenerate.gc]   le_l_u J X S hS := ⟨S, J.superset_covering (Sieve.le_generate S.arrows) hS, le_rfl⟩   choice x _ := toGrothendieck C x   choice_eq _ _ := rfl

CategoryTheory.Pretopology.trivial.fullDefinition: def trivial : Pretopology C where   coverings X S := ∃ (Y : _) (f : Y ⟶ X) (_ : IsIso f), S = Presieve.singleton f   has_isos X Y f i := ⟨_, _, i, rfl⟩   pullbacks X Y f S := by     rintro ⟨Z, g, i, rfl⟩     refine ⟨pullback g f, pullback.snd _ _, ?_, ?_⟩     · refine ⟨⟨pullback.lift (f ≫ inv g) (𝟙 _) (by simp), ⟨?_, by aesop_cat⟩⟩⟩       ext       · rw [assoc, pullback.lift_fst, ← pullback.condition_assoc]         simp       · simp     · apply pullback_singleton   transitive := by     rintro X S Ti ⟨Z, g, i, rfl⟩ hS     rcases hS g (singleton_self g) with ⟨Y, f, i, hTi⟩     refine ⟨_, f ≫ g, ?_, ?_⟩     · infer_instance     -- Porting note: the next four lines were just "ext (W k)"     apply funext     rintro W     apply Set.ext     rintro k     constructor     · rintro ⟨V, h, k, ⟨_⟩, hh, rfl⟩       rw [hTi] at hh       cases hh       apply singleton.mk     · rintro ⟨_⟩       refine bind_comp g singleton.mk ?_       rw [hTi]       apply singleton.mk

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.code:
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.{w, v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
  (R : Presieve X) : Type (max (max u₁ w) v₁)
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.comment:
A family of elements for a presheaf `P` given a collection of arrows `R` with fixed codomain `X`
consists of an element of `P Y` for every `f : Y ⟶ X` in `R`.
A presheaf is a sheaf (resp, separated) if every *compatible* family of elements has exactly one
(resp, at most one) amalgamation.

This data is referred to as a `family` in [MM92], Chapter III, Section 4. It is also a concrete
version of the elements of the middle object in https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00VM which is
more useful for direct calculations. It is also used implicitly in Definition C2.1.2 in [Elephant].

  {X : C} {R : Presieve X} (x : FamilyOfElements P R) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.comment:
A family of elements for the arrow set `R` is *compatible* if for any `f₁ : Y₁ ⟶ X` and
`f₂ : Y₂ ⟶ X` in `R`, and any `g₁ : Z ⟶ Y₁` and `g₂ : Z ⟶ Y₂`, if the square `g₁ ≫ f₁ = g₂ ≫ f₂`
commutes then the elements of `P Z` obtained by restricting the element of `P Y₁` along `g₁` and
restricting the element of `P Y₂` along `g₂` are the same.

In special cases, this condition can be simplified, see `pullbackCompatible_iff` and
`compatible_iff_sieveCompatible`.

This is referred to as a "compatible family" in Definition C2.1.2 of [Elephant], and on nlab:
https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/sheaf#GeneralDefinitionInComponents

For a more explicit version in the case where `R` is of the form `Presieve.ofArrows`, see
`CategoryTheory.Presieve.Arrows.Compatible`.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.fullDefinition: def FamilyOfElements.Compatible (x : FamilyOfElements P R) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃Y₁ Y₂ Z⦄ (g₁ : Z ⟶ Y₁) (g₂ : Z ⟶ Y₂) ⦃f₁ : Y₁ ⟶ X⦄ ⦃f₂ : Y₂ ⟶ X⦄ (h₁ : R f₁) (h₂ : R f₂),     g₁ ≫ f₁ = g₂ ≫ f₂ → P.map g₁.op (x f₁ h₁) = P.map g₂.op (x f₂ h₂)
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.description: This definition specifies a condition for a family of elements pertaining to a presheaf to be compatible, meaning that certain morphism relationships preserve the equality of elements obtained from the presheaf when restricted.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.code:
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.PullbackCompatible.{w, v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} {X : C} {R : Presieve X} (x : FamilyOfElements P R) [R.hasPullbacks] : Prop
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.comment:
If the category `C` has pullbacks, this is an alternative condition for a family of elements to be
compatible: For any `f : Y ⟶ X` and `g : Z ⟶ X` in the presieve `R`, the restriction of the
given elements for `f` and `g` to the pullback agree.
This is equivalent to being compatible (provided `C` has pullbacks), shown in
`pullbackCompatible_iff`.

This is the definition for a "matching" family given in [MM92], Chapter III, Section 4,
Equation (5). Viewing the type `FamilyOfElements` as the middle object of the fork in
https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00VM, this condition expresses that `pr₀* (x) = pr₁* (x)`,
using the notation defined there.

For a more explicit version in the case where `R` is of the form `Presieve.ofArrows`, see
`CategoryTheory.Presieve.Arrows.PullbackCompatible`.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.code:
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.IsAmalgamation.{w, v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} {X : C} {R : Presieve X} (x : FamilyOfElements P R) (t : P.obj (op X)) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.comment:
The given element `t` of `P.obj (op X)` is an *amalgamation* for the family of elements `x` if every
restriction `P.map f.op t = x_f` for every arrow `f` in the presieve `R`.

This is the definition given in https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/sheaf#GeneralDefinitionInComponents,
and https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/matching+family, as well as [MM92], Chapter III, Section 4,
equation (2).

  (R : Presieve X) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor.comment:
We define `P` to be a sheaf for the presieve `R` if every compatible family has a unique
amalgamation.

This is the definition of a sheaf for the given presieve given in C2.1.2 of [Elephant], and
https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/sheaf#GeneralDefinitionInComponents.
Using `compatible_iff_sieveCompatible`,
this is equivalent to the definition of a sheaf in [MM92], Chapter III, Section 4.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor.description: This definition characterizes a presheaf as a sheaf for a given presieve by stating that any compatible family of elements has a unique amalgamation.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.YonedaSheafCondi.code:
CategoryTheory.Presieve.YonedaSheafCondition.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v₁)
  (S : Sieve X) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Presieve.YonedaSheafCondi.comment:
This is an equivalent condition to be a sheaf, which is useful for the abstraction to local
operators on elementary toposes. However this definition is defined only for sieves, not presieves.
The equivalence between this and `IsSheafFor` is given in `isSheafFor_iff_yonedaSheafCondition`.
This version is also useful to establish that being a sheaf is preserved under isomorphism of
presheaves.

See the discussion before Equation (3) of [MM92], Chapter III, Section 4. See also C2.1.4 of
[Elephant]. This is also a direct reformulation of <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00Z8>.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.isSheafFor_subsi.comment:
If a presieve `R` on `X` has a subsieve `S` such that:

* `P` is a sheaf for `S`.
* For every `f` in `R`, `P` is separated for the pullback of `S` along `f`,

then `P` is a sheaf for `R`.

This is closely related to [Elephant] C2.1.6(i).

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsCl.code:

  {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : Prop
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsCl.comment:
A sieve is closed for the Grothendieck topology if it contains every arrow it covers.
In the case of the usual topology on a topological space, this means that the open cover contains
every open set which it covers.

Note this has no relation to a closed subset of a topological space.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: A sieve on one object in a Grothendieck topology is said to cover a morphism to another object if the pullback of that sieve along the morphism is also included in the topology for the second object.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsCl.fullDefinition: def IsClosed {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃Y : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), J₁.Covers S f → S f
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsCl.description: A sieve is considered closed in a Grothendieck topology if it includes all morphisms that it can cover.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.cove.comment: If `S` is `J₁`-closed, then `S` covers exactly the arrows it contains.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.clos.fullDefinition: def closureOperator (X : C) : ClosureOperator (Sieve X) :=   .ofPred J₁.close J₁.IsClosed J₁.le_close J₁.close_isClosed fun _ _ ↦ J₁.le_close_of_isClosed

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pull.code:

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback: This definition describes a construction that transforms a sieve on one object into a sieve on another object via the inverse image along a given morphism.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pull.description: The closure of a sieve under a Grothendieck topology remains unchanged when the sieve is pulled back along a morphism.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.mono.code:
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.monotone_close.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C)
  {X : C} : Monotone J₁.close

explanatories.Monotone: A function is considered monotone if it preserves the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output will not exceed the corresponding output of the larger input.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.mono.description: The closure of a sieve in a Grothendieck topology is a monotone operation, meaning that if one sieve is contained within another, their closures maintain that containment.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.clos.code:
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.close_close.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C)
  {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : J₁.close (J₁.close S) = J₁.close S
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.clos.description: The closure of a sieve in a Grothendieck topology is idempotent, meaning that taking the closure twice yields the same result as taking it once.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.clos.code:
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.close_eq_top_iff_mem.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C) {X : C} (S : Sieve X) : J₁.close S = ⊤ ↔ S ∈ J₁.sieves X
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.clos.comment:
The sieve `S` is in the topology iff its closure is the maximal sieve. This shows that the closure
operator determines the topology.
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.clos.description: The closure of a sieve is maximal if and only if the sieve itself belongs to the topology defined by that closure operation.

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C) :
  Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max v u)
CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves.comment:
The presheaf sending each object to the set of `J`-closed sieves on it. This presheaf is a `J`-sheaf
(and will turn out to be a subobject classifier for the category of `J`-sheaves).

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsCl: A sieve is considered closed in a Grothendieck topology if it includes all morphisms that it can cover.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback: This definition describes a construction that transforms a sieve on one object into a sieve on another object via the inverse image along a given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.isCl: If a sieve is closed in a Grothendieck topology, then its pullback along any morphism retains this closed property.
explanatories.Opposite.unop: This definition describes the canonical mapping from the opposite category of a type back to the original type.

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves.fullDefinition: def Functor.closedSieves : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type max v u where   obj X := { S : Sieve X.unop // J₁.IsClosed S }   map f S := ⟨S.1.pullback f.unop, J₁.isClosed_pullback f.unop _ S.2⟩
CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves.description: This definition describes a functor that assigns to each object in a category the set of closed sieves associated with a given Grothendieck topology, highlighting its role as a sheaf.

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves_obj.code:
CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves_obj.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C)
  (X : Cᵒᵖ) : (Functor.closedSieves J₁).obj X = { S // J₁.IsClosed S }

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsCl: A sieve is considered closed in a Grothendieck topology if it includes all morphisms that it can cover.

CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves_obj.description: The functor maps an object to the collection of closed sieves in the corresponding Grothendieck topology.

CategoryTheory.classifier_isSheaf.code:
CategoryTheory.classifier_isSheaf.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C) :
  Presieve.IsSheaf J₁ (Functor.closedSieves J₁)
CategoryTheory.classifier_isSheaf.comment:
The presheaf of `J`-closed sieves is a `J`-sheaf.
The proof of this is adapted from [MM92], Chapter III, Section 7, Lemma 1.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves: This definition describes a functor that assigns to each object in a category the set of closed sieves associated with a given Grothendieck topology, highlighting its role as a sheaf.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheaf: A presheaf is defined as a sheaf for a topology if it satisfies the sheaf condition for every sieve associated with that topology.

CategoryTheory.classifier_isSheaf.description: The presheaf formed from J-closed sieves in a Grothendieck topology satisfies the sheaf condition.

CategoryTheory.le_topology_of_closedSiev.code:
CategoryTheory.le_topology_of_closedSieves_isSheaf.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  {J₁ J₂ : GrothendieckTopology C} (h : Presieve.IsSheaf J₁ (Functor.closedSieves J₂)) : J₁ ≤ J₂
CategoryTheory.le_topology_of_closedSiev.comment:
If presheaf of `J₁`-closed sieves is a `J₂`-sheaf then `J₁ ≤ J₂`. Note the converse is true by
`classifier_isSheaf` and `isSheaf_of_le`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.closedSieves: This definition describes a functor that assigns to each object in a category the set of closed sieves associated with a given Grothendieck topology, highlighting its role as a sheaf.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheaf: A presheaf is defined as a sheaf for a topology if it satisfies the sheaf condition for every sieve associated with that topology.

CategoryTheory.le_topology_of_closedSiev.description: If a presheaf of closed sieves for one Grothendieck topology is a sheaf for another, then the first topology is a refinement of the second.

CategoryTheory.topology_eq_iff_same_shea.code:
CategoryTheory.topology_eq_iff_same_sheaves.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {J₁ J₂ : GrothendieckTopology C} :
  J₁ = J₂ ↔ ∀ (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max v u)), Presieve.IsSheaf J₁ P ↔ Presieve.IsSheaf J₂ P
CategoryTheory.topology_eq_iff_same_shea.comment: If being a sheaf for `J₁` is equivalent to being a sheaf for `J₂`, then `J₁ = J₂`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheaf: A presheaf is defined as a sheaf for a topology if it satisfies the sheaf condition for every sieve associated with that topology.

CategoryTheory.topology_eq_iff_same_shea.description: Two Grothendieck topologies are equal if and only if they yield the same sheaves for all presieves.

CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.code:
CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (c : (X : C) → ClosureOperator (Sieve X))
  (hc : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X), (c Y) (Sieve.pullback f S) = Sieve.pullback f ((c X) S)) :
  GrothendieckTopology C
CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.comment:
A closure (increasing, inflationary and idempotent) operation on sieves that commutes with pullback
induces a Grothendieck topology.
In fact, such operations are in bijection with Grothendieck topologies.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback: This definition describes a construction that transforms a sieve on one object into a sieve on another object via the inverse image along a given morphism.
explanatories.Membership.mem: The membership relation defines a property indicating that an element belongs to a set.
explanatories.ClosureOperator.monotone: This theorem asserts that a closure operator is monotone, meaning it preserves the order when applied to elements in a partially ordered set.
explanatories.ClosureOperator.idempotent: This theorem asserts that applying a closure operator twice to an element yields the same result as applying it once, demonstrating its idempotent nature.
explanatories.Top.top: A function that retrieves the top element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.eq_top_iff: An element in a partially ordered set is equal to the maximum element if and only if the maximum element is less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback_eq_top_iff: This theorem establishes a biconditional relationship between the membership of a morphism in a sieve and the equivalence of the pullback of that morphism with the top object in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback_top: This theorem asserts that the pullback of a morphism with the terminal sieve results in the terminal sieve.
explanatories.top_unique: In an ordered type with a unique maximum element, any element that is at least as large as this maximum element must be equal to it.
explanatories.ClosureOperator.le_closure: This theorem states that every element in a partially ordered set is less than or equal to its closure according to a closure operator, illustrating a property known as extensivity.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.

CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.fullDefinition: def topologyOfClosureOperator (c : ∀ X : C, ClosureOperator (Sieve X))     (hc : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X), c _ (S.pullback f) = (c _ S).pullback f) :     GrothendieckTopology C where   sieves X := { S | c X S = ⊤ }   top_mem' X := top_unique ((c X).le_closure _)   pullback_stable' X Y S f hS := by     rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hS     rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, hc, hS, Sieve.pullback_top]   transitive' X S hS R hR := by     rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hS     rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ← (c X).idempotent, eq_top_iff, ← hS]     apply (c X).monotone fun Y f hf => _     intros Y f hf     rw [Sieve.pullback_eq_top_iff_mem, ← hc]     apply hR hf
CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.description: A closure operation on sieves that is increasing, inflationary, idempotent, and commutes with pullback defines a Grothendieck topology.

CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.code:
CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator_self.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology C) :
  topologyOfClosureOperator J₁.closureOperator ⋯ = J₁
CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.comment: The topology given by the closure operator `J.close` on a Grothendieck topology is the same as `J`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.clos: A Grothendieck topology generates a set of closure operators applicable to sieves associated with its objects.

CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.description: The topology induced by the closure operator of a Grothendieck topology is identical to the original topology.

CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator.code:
CategoryTheory.topologyOfClosureOperator_close.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (c : (X : C) → ClosureOperator (Sieve X))
  (pb : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Sieve X), (c Y) (Sieve.pullback f S) = Sieve.pullback f ((c X) S)) (X : C)
  (S : Sieve X) : (topologyOfClosureOperator c pb).close S = (c X) S

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.FirstObj.code:
CategoryTheory.Equalizer.FirstObj.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max v u)) {X : C}
  (R : Presieve X) : Type (max v u)
CategoryTheory.Equalizer.FirstObj.comment:
The middle object of the fork diagram given in Equation (3) of [MM92], as well as the fork diagram
of <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00VM>.

explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.FirstObj.fullDefinition: def FirstObj : Type max v u :=   ∏ᶜ fun f : ΣY, { f : Y ⟶ X // R f } => P.obj (op f.1)
CategoryTheory.Equalizer.FirstObj.description: This definition identifies a type representing the first object in a specific diagram that appears in certain mathematical contexts involving presieves and categories.

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.firstObjEqFamil.code:
CategoryTheory.Equalizer.firstObjEqFamily.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max v u)) {X : C}
  (R : Presieve X) : FirstObj P R ≅ Presieve.FamilyOfElements P R

explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equalizer.FirstObj: This definition identifies a type representing the first object in a specific diagram that appears in certain mathematical contexts involving presieves and categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.π: This definition describes the morphism from a product object to a component object in a category, specifically extracting the projection for an indexed family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements: This definition describes a family of elements for a presheaf associated with a collection of morphisms that share a common codomain.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.firstObjEqFamil.fullDefinition: def firstObjEqFamily : FirstObj P R ≅ R.FamilyOfElements P where   hom t Y f hf := Pi.π (fun f : ΣY, { f : Y ⟶ X // R f } => P.obj (op f.1)) ⟨_, _, hf⟩ t   inv := Pi.lift fun f x => x _ f.2.2
CategoryTheory.Equalizer.firstObjEqFamil.description: This definition demonstrates that the first object in a particular diagram is isomorphic to a family of elements derived from the same diagram in category theory.

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.forkMap.code:

  (R : Presieve X) : P.obj (op X) ⟶ FirstObj P R

The left morphism of the fork diagram given in Equation (3) of [MM92], as well as the fork diagram
of <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00VM>.

explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.forkMap.fullDefinition: def forkMap : P.obj (op X) ⟶ FirstObj P R :=   Pi.lift fun f => P.map f.2.1.op

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Sieve.SecondObj.code:

  (S : Sieve X) : Type (max v u)

CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Sieve.SecondObj.fullDefinition: def SecondObj : Type max v u :=   ∏ᶜ fun f : Σ(Y Z : _) (_ : Z ⟶ Y), { f' : Y ⟶ X // S f' } => P.obj (op f.2.1)

Given a sieve `S` on `X : C`, a presheaf `P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A`, and an object `E` of `A`,

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.conesEquivSieveCompatibleFamily_apply_coe.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {A : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} A] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) {X : C} (S : Sieve X) (E : Aᵒᵖ)
  (π : (S.arrows.diagram.op ⋙ P).cones.obj E) (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (h : S.arrows f) :

category_theory.presheaf.is_sheaf_iff_is.code:
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isLimit_pretopology.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {A : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} A] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) [HasPullbacks C] (K : Pretopology C) :
  IsSheaf (Pretopology.toGrothendieck C K) P ↔
    ∀ ⦃X : C⦄, ∀ R ∈ K.coverings X, Nonempty (IsLimit (P.mapCone (generate R).arrows.cocone.op))
category_theory.presheaf.is_sheaf_iff_is.comment:
A presheaf `P` is a sheaf for the Grothendieck topology generated by a pretopology `K`
iff for every covering presieve `R` of `K`, the natural cone associated to `P` and
`Sieve.generate R` is a limit cone.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgama.code:
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgamate.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {A : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} A] {E : A} {X : C} {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (hP : IsSheaf J P)
  (S : J.Cover X) (x : (I : S.Arrow) → E ⟶ P.obj (op I.Y))
  (hx : ∀ ⦃I₁ I₂ : S.Arrow⦄ (r : I₁.Relation I₂), x I₁ ≫ P.map r.g₁.op = x I₂ ≫ P.map r.g₂.op) : E ⟶ P.obj (op X)
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgama.comment:
This is a wrapper around `Presieve.IsSheafFor.amalgamate` to be used below.
If `P`s a sheaf, `S` is a cover of `X`, and `x` is a collection of morphisms from `E`
to `P` evaluated at terms in the cover which are compatible, then we can amalgamate
the `x`s to obtain a single morphism `E ⟶ P.obj (op X)`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheaf: A presheaf is defined as a sheaf for a topology if it satisfies the sheaf condition for every sieve associated with that topology.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Over.w: The theorem states that the left morphism associated with one object in the over category, when composed with the right morphism of another object, equals the morphism of the first object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.op: This definition transforms a cocone associated with a functor into a cone associated with the opposite functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.ConeMorphism.w: This theorem states that the composition of two natural transformations and a morphism between cones yields a commutative triangle involving the relevant cone projections at each object in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: The collection of covers for an object in a category, according to a specific Grothendieck topology, is defined as a poset.
The defined concept specifies the source object associated with an arrow in a covering sieve within a Grothendieck topology.
A covering sieve in a Grothendieck topology associated with an object is guaranteed to be a member of the collection of sieves for that object in the topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheafFor.amalg: This definition provides a method to derive the amalgamation of a compatible family of elements associated with a sheaf and a presieve.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: The definition specifies that an arrow associated with a covering sieve in a Grothendieck topology is a morphism from an object to another object, establishing the relationship within the topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multifork.conditio: In a multifork within a category, the morphisms corresponding to two different inputs from a multicospan index are equal when composed with the same arrow from the multifork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.w: This theorem establishes that for a given cone associated with a functor, the morphisms from the cone point to the images under the functor commute with the morphisms in the indexing category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: This theorem states that if an arrow is part of a covering sieve in a Grothendieck topology, then that arrow belongs to the collection of arrows associated with the corresponding sieve.
This definition describes the relationship between two arrows in a covering sieve of a Grothendieck topology by relating the source of one arrow to the target of another.

The theorem establishes that if two arrows in a covering sieve relate to each other, then their corresponding morphisms to a common object can be expressed as equal when composed with the respective morphisms of the arrows.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.w: This theorem demonstrates that, in the presence of pullbacks, the composition of specific morphisms derived from a presieve results in an equality between two different mappings through a related fork diagram.
explanatories.Nonempty.map: If there is at least one element in a nonempty type, then applying a function to that type results in another nonempty type.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgama.fullDefinition: def IsSheaf.amalgamate {A : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} A] {E : A} {X : C} {P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A}     (hP : Presheaf.IsSheaf J P) (S : J.Cover X) (x : ∀ I : S.Arrow, E ⟶ P.obj (op I.Y))     (hx : ∀ ⦃I₁ I₂ : S.Arrow⦄ (r : I₁.Relation I₂),        x I₁ ≫ P.map r.g₁.op = x I₂ ≫ P.map r.g₂.op) : E ⟶ P.obj (op X) :=   (hP _ _ S.condition).amalgamate (fun Y f hf => x ⟨Y, f, hf⟩) fun _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h₁ h₂ w =>     @hx { hf := h₁ } { hf := h₂ } { w := w }
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgama.description: If a presheaf is a sheaf with respect to a specific Grothendieck topology, then compatible morphisms from a fixed object to the presheaf, associated with a covering of a specified object, can be combined into a single morphism to that presheaf evaluated at the target of the original object.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgama: If a presheaf is a sheaf with respect to a specific Grothendieck topology, then compatible morphisms from a fixed object to the presheaf, associated with a covering of a specified object, can be combined into a single morphism to that presheaf evaluated at the target of the original object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: The definition specifies that an arrow associated with a covering sieve in a Grothendieck topology is a morphism from an object to another object, establishing the relationship within the topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgama: The mapping obtained through the amalgamation process for a family of morphisms associated with a sheaf is equal to the original morphism from the arrow of the covering sieve when composed with the presheaf.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.hom_ext: This theorem establishes that two morphisms from an object to a sheaf of types are equal if they agree on all morphisms from a covering sieve associated with a specified topology.

explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: A multifork associated with a covering sieve and a presheaf indicates that the limit condition holds, which is equivalent to satisfying the sheaf condition at that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multifork: A multifork is a structured collection that represents a cone over a defined diagram called a multicospan.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multifork.ι: This definition describes a morphism from the cone point of a multifork to an object on the left side of a multicospan index, relating elements within that structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multifork.conditio: In a multifork within a category, the morphisms corresponding to two different inputs from a multicospan index are equal when composed with the same arrow from the multifork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.w: This theorem establishes that for a given cone associated with a functor, the morphisms from the cone point to the images under the functor commute with the morphisms in the indexing category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.WalkingMulticospan: The function defined for a walking multicospan yields a morphism between the left endpoint of a specified object and the corresponding right endpoint derived from an element of a different type.

explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: This definition describes the relationship between two arrows in a covering sieve of a Grothendieck topology by relating the source of one arrow to the target of another.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.fac: This theorem shows that a specific lifting of a cone through a limit cone results in a commutative triangle involving the cone's projection morphisms and the natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.uniq: This theorem asserts that a morphism from one cone to another is uniquely determined by the condition that it satisfies a commutativity property with respect to the projections of the cones involved.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.Sigma.fst: The first component of a dependent pair is extracted from the pair, returning the value of the first type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.lift: This definition indicates how a morphism from a fixed object to each element of a product can be combined into a morphism from that object to the overall product object in a category.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst: This definition describes the first projection map from the pullback object associated with a pair of morphisms to the first object of one of the morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.hom_ext: This theorem asserts that if two morphisms to the limit of a functor yield the same results when composed with the canonical projections, then those two morphisms are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.w: This theorem demonstrates that, in the presence of pullbacks, the composition of specific morphisms derived from a presieve results in an equality between two different mappings through a related fork diagram.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ι: This definition introduces a morphism that connects a given point of a fork on two parallel morphisms to the zero instance of a parallel pair formed by those morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isLimitOfIsSheaf.fullDefinition: def isLimitOfIsSheaf {X : C} (S : J.Cover X) (hP : IsSheaf J P) : IsLimit (S.multifork P) where   lift := fun E : Multifork _ => hP.amalgamate S (fun I => E.ι _)     (fun _ _ r => E.condition ⟨_, _, r⟩)   fac := by     rintro (E : Multifork _) (a | b)     · apply hP.amalgamate_map     · rw [← E.w (WalkingMulticospan.Hom.fst b),         ← (S.multifork P).w (WalkingMulticospan.Hom.fst b), ← assoc]       congr 1       apply hP.amalgamate_map   uniq := by     rintro (E : Multifork _) m hm     apply hP.hom_ext S     intro I     erw [hm (WalkingMulticospan.left I)]     symm     apply hP.amalgamate_map

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheafForIsShea.fullDefinition: def isSheafForIsSheafFor' (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (s : A ⥤ Type max v₁ u₁)     [∀ J, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete.{max v₁ u₁} J) s] (U : C) (R : Presieve U) :     IsLimit (s.mapCone (Fork.ofι _ (w R P))) ≃       IsLimit (Fork.ofι _ (Equalizer.Presieve.w (P ⋙ s) R)) := by   apply Equiv.trans (isLimitMapConeForkEquiv _ _) _   apply (IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv _ _).symm.trans (IsLimit.equivIsoLimit _)   · apply NatIso.ofComponents _ _     · rintro (_ | _)       · apply PreservesProduct.iso s       · apply PreservesProduct.iso s     · rintro _ _ (_ | _)       · refine limit.hom_ext (fun j => ?_)         dsimp [Equalizer.Presieve.firstMap, firstMap]         simp only [limit.lift_π, map_lift_piComparison, assoc, Fan.mk_π_app, Functor.map_comp]         rw [piComparison_comp_π_assoc]       · refine limit.hom_ext (fun j => ?_)         dsimp [Equalizer.Presieve.secondMap, secondMap]         simp only [limit.lift_π, map_lift_piComparison, assoc, Fan.mk_π_app, Functor.map_comp]         rw [piComparison_comp_π_assoc]       · dsimp         simp   · refine Fork.ext (Iso.refl _) ?_     dsimp [Equalizer.forkMap, forkMap]     simp [Fork.ι]
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheafForIsShea.description: This definition provides an equivalence between the conditions for the existence of a limit for mapped cones from a presheaf and the existence of a limit for a particular fork constructed from an equalizer and the presheaf in a category equipped with products and pullbacks.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multifork.ofι: This definition introduces a multifork structure using a collection of morphisms that satisfy a specified compatibility condition between the associated mappings and given structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: The theorem establishes that if two arrows in a covering sieve relate to each other, then their corresponding morphisms to a common object can be expressed as equal when composed with the respective morphisms of the arrows.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.forkMap: This definition describes a morphism from the value of a presheaf at a specified object to the first object of a given presieve in the context of a categorical product structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Pi.π: This definition describes the morphism from a product object to a component object in a category, specifically extracting the projection for an indexed family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.firstMap: There exists a morphism from the first object to the second object associated with a given presieve and a functor into another category, assuming both the presence of products in the latter category and pullbacks in the source category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.secondMap: This definition specifies the morphism between the first and second objects associated with a presieve in a category with products and pullbacks.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.hom_ext: This theorem asserts that if two morphisms to the limit of a functor yield the same results when composed with the canonical projections, then those two morphisms are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.lift_π: This theorem asserts that for a functor with an established limit, the composition of the morphism lifting from a cone to the limit with the limit projection equals the morphism from the cone to the object corresponding to a specific index in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fan.mk_π_app: The theorem demonstrates that the application of the projection morphism from a constructed fan to a specific point in a discrete indexing category is equal to the corresponding morphism defined for that specific index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.w: The composition of morphisms derived from a presieve with respect to a presheaf satisfies a specific equality relation when pulling back through the first and second components of the related fork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ofι: This definition describes how to create a fork, a specific diagram of morphisms, on two given morphisms by providing a morphism that maps into one of the source objects, under the condition that the compositions with both morphisms are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.w: This theorem demonstrates that, in the presence of pullbacks, the composition of specific morphisms derived from a presieve results in an equality between two different mappings through a related fork diagram.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitMapConeFork: This definition establishes a correspondence between the limit of a mapped fork in one category and the limit of the original morphisms in another category, allowing for the interchange of operations involving forks and functorial mappings.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.postcompos: This definition states that a cone retains its limit property if it is transformed through post-composition with a natural isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.equivIsoLi: This definition states that an isomorphism between two cones implies a corresponding equivalence between the properties of being limit cones for each of those cones.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesProduct.i: This definition asserts that if a functor preserves limits and both the source and target diagrams possess products, then there exists an isomorphism between the product of the original objects and the image of that product under the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.firstM: This definition specifies a morphism that maps the first object in a specific diagram associated with a presieve to the second object within that same framework in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.map_lift_piCompari: This theorem establishes an equality between a composed morphism involving a functor and a natural transformation from a lift of morphisms into a product and its corresponding product morphism after applying the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equalizer.Presieve.second: This definition describes a morphism that connects the first object to the second object in a specific categorical framework related to equalizers and presieves.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equalizer.forkMap: This definition describes the morphism from the object associated with a given presheaf to the first object in a specific diagram related to presieves in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ι: This definition introduces a morphism that connects a given point of a fork on two parallel morphisms to the zero instance of a parallel pair formed by those morphisms.

category_theory.presheaf.is_sheaf_for_is.fullDefinition: def isSheafForIsSheafFor' (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (s : A ⥤ Type max v₁ u₁)     [∀ J, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete.{max v₁ u₁} J) s] (U : C) (R : Presieve U) :     IsLimit (s.mapCone (Fork.ofι _ (w R P))) ≃       IsLimit (Fork.ofι _ (Equalizer.Presieve.w (P ⋙ s) R)) := by   apply Equiv.trans (isLimitMapConeForkEquiv _ _) _   apply (IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv _ _).symm.trans (IsLimit.equivIsoLimit _)   · apply NatIso.ofComponents _ _     · rintro (_ | _)       · apply PreservesProduct.iso s       · apply PreservesProduct.iso s     · rintro _ _ (_ | _)       · refine limit.hom_ext (fun j => ?_)         dsimp [Equalizer.Presieve.firstMap, firstMap]         simp only [limit.lift_π, map_lift_piComparison, assoc, Fan.mk_π_app, Functor.map_comp]         rw [piComparison_comp_π_assoc]       · refine limit.hom_ext (fun j => ?_)         dsimp [Equalizer.Presieve.secondMap, secondMap]         simp only [limit.lift_π, map_lift_piComparison, assoc, Fan.mk_π_app, Functor.map_comp]         rw [piComparison_comp_π_assoc]       · dsimp         simp   · refine Fork.ext (Iso.refl _) ?_     dsimp [Equalizer.forkMap, forkMap]     simp [Fork.ι]

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSh.description: This theorem establishes that a presheaf is a sheaf with respect to a given Grothendieck topology if and only if the composition of the presheaf with a certain functor also results in a sheaf under the same topology, provided that the functor preserves and reflects limits appropriately.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSh.comment:
For a concrete category `(A, s)` where the forgetful functor `s : A ⥤ Type v` preserves limits and
reflects isomorphisms, and `A` has limits, an `A`-valued presheaf `P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A` is a sheaf iff its
underlying `Type`-valued presheaf `P ⋙ s : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type` is a sheaf.

Note this lemma applies for "algebraic" categories, eg groups, abelian groups and rings, but not
for the category of topological spaces, topological rings, etc since reflecting isomorphisms doesn't
hold.

  {i₁ i₂ : E.I₀} {W : C} (p₁ : W ⟶ E.X i₁) (p₂ : W ⟶ E.X i₂) : Sieve W
CategoryTheory.PreOneHypercover.sieve₁.comment:
Given an object `W` equipped with morphisms `p₁ : W ⟶ E.X i₁`, `p₂ : W ⟶ E.X i₂`,
this is the sieve of `W` which consists of morphisms `g : Z ⟶ W` such that there exists `j`
and `h : Z ⟶ E.Y j` such that `g ≫ p₁ = h ≫ E.p₁ j` and `g ≫ p₂ = h ≫ E.p₂ j`.
See lemmas `sieve₁_eq_pullback_sieve₁'` and `sieve₁'_eq_sieve₁` for equational lemmas
regarding this sieve.

  {A : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂, u₂} A] {B : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃, u₃} B] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} (F : A ⥤ B)
  (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) {X : C} (S : J.Cover X) :

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove.comment:
Mapping the multifork associated to a cover `S : J.Cover X` and a presheaf `P` with
respect to a functor `F` is isomorphic (upto a natural isomorphism of the underlying functors)
to the multifork associated to `S` and `P ⋙ F`.

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheafFor_bind.code:
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheafFor_bind.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : C} (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (U : Sieve X)
  (B : ⦃Y : C⦄ → ⦃f : Y ⟶ X⦄ → U.arrows f → Sieve Y) (hU : Presieve.IsSheafFor P U.arrows)
  (hB : ∀ ⦃Y : C⦄ ⦃f : Y ⟶ X⦄ (hf : U.arrows f), Presieve.IsSheafFor P (B hf).arrows)
  (hB' :
    ∀ ⦃Y : C⦄ ⦃f : Y ⟶ X⦄ (h : U.arrows f) ⦃Z : C⦄ (g : Z ⟶ Y),
      Presieve.IsSeparatedFor P (Sieve.pullback g (B h)).arrows) :
  Presieve.IsSheafFor P (Sieve.bind U.arrows B).arrows
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheafFor_bind.comment:
To show `P` is a sheaf for the binding of `U` with `B`, it suffices to show that `P` is a sheaf for
`U`, that `P` is a sheaf for each sieve in `B`, and that it is separated for any pullback of any
sieve in `B`.

This is mostly an auxiliary lemma to show `isSheafFor_trans`.
Adapted from [Elephant], Lemma C2.1.7(i) with suggestions as mentioned in
https://math.stackexchange.com/a/358709/

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheafFor_trans.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {X : C} (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) (R S : Sieve X)
  (hR : Presieve.IsSheafFor P R.arrows)
  (hR' : ∀ ⦃Y : C⦄ ⦃f : Y ⟶ X⦄, S.arrows f → Presieve.IsSeparatedFor P (Sieve.pullback f R).arrows)
  (hS : ∀ ⦃Y : C⦄ ⦃f : Y ⟶ X⦄, R.arrows f → Presieve.IsSheafFor P (Sieve.pullback f S).arrows) :
  Presieve.IsSheafFor P S.arrows
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheafFor_trans.comment:
Given two sieves `R` and `S`, to show that `P` is a sheaf for `S`, we can show:
* `P` is a sheaf for `R`
* `P` is a sheaf for the pullback of `S` along any arrow in `R`
* `P` is separated for the pullback of `R` along any arrow in `S`.

This is mostly an auxiliary lemma to construct `finestTopology`.
Adapted from [Elephant], Lemma C2.1.7(ii) with suggestions as mentioned in
https://math.stackexchange.com/a/358709

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.finestTopologySingl.fullDefinition: def finestTopologySingle (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v) : GrothendieckTopology C where   sieves X S := ∀ (Y) (f : Y ⟶ X), Presieve.IsSheafFor P (S.pullback f : Presieve Y)   top_mem' X Y f := by     rw [Sieve.pullback_top]     exact Presieve.isSheafFor_top_sieve P   pullback_stable' X Y S f hS Z g := by     rw [← pullback_comp]     apply hS   transitive' X S hS R hR Z g := by     -- This is the hard part of the construction, showing that the given set of sieves satisfies     -- the transitivity axiom.     refine isSheafFor_trans P (pullback g S) _ (hS Z g) ?_ ?_     · intro Y f _       rw [← pullback_comp]       apply (hS _ _).isSeparatedFor     · intro Y f hf       have := hR hf _ (𝟙 _)       rw [pullback_id, pullback_comp] at this       apply this
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.finestTopologySingl.description: This definition outlines the construction of the largest Grothendieck topology for which a specified presheaf qualifies as a sheaf.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThruAlong.code:
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThruAlong.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {X Y : C} (S : Presieve Y)
  (T : Presieve X) (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThruAlong.comment:
Given a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X`, a presieve `S` on `Y` and presieve `T` on `X`,
we say that *`S` factors through `T` along `f`*, written `S.FactorsThruAlong T f`,
provided that for any morphism `g : Z ⟶ Y` in `S`, there exists some
morphism `e : W ⟶ X` in `T` and some morphism `i : Z ⟶ W` such that the obvious
square commutes: `i ≫ e = g ≫ f`.

This is used in the definition of a coverage.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.op: This definition transforms a cocone associated with a functor into a cone associated with the opposite functor.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThruAlong.fullDefinition: def FactorsThruAlong {X Y : C} (S : Presieve Y) (T : Presieve X) (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃Z : C⦄ ⦃g : Z ⟶ Y⦄, S g →   ∃ (W : C) (i : Z ⟶ W) (e : W ⟶ X), T e ∧ i ≫ e = g ≫ f
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThruAlong.description: A presieve on one object is said to factor through another presieve along a morphism if every morphism in the first presieve can be connected to a morphism in the second presieve through a commutative square.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThru.code: CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThru.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] {X : C} (S T : Presieve X) : Prop
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThru.comment:
Given `S T : Presieve X`, we say that `S` factors through `T` if any morphism in `S`
factors through some morphism in `T`.

The lemma `Presieve.isSheafFor_of_factorsThru` gives a *sufficient* condition for a
presheaf to be a sheaf for a presieve `T`, in terms of `S.FactorsThru T`, provided
that the presheaf is a sheaf for `S`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.op: This definition transforms a cocone associated with a functor into a cone associated with the opposite functor.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThru.fullDefinition: def FactorsThru {X : C} (S T : Presieve X) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃Z : C⦄ ⦃g : Z ⟶ X⦄, S g →   ∃ (W : C) (i : Z ⟶ W) (e : W ⟶ X), T e ∧ i ≫ e = g
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FactorsThru.description: A presieve is said to factor through another presieve if every morphism in the first presieve can be related to a morphism in the second presieve.

CategoryTheory.Coverage.covering.fullDefinition: covering : ∀ (X : C), Set (Presieve X)   /-- Given any covering sieve `S` on `X` and a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X`, there exists     some covering sieve `T` on `Y` such that `T` factors through `S` along `f`. -/   pullback : ∀ ⦃X Y : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) (S : Presieve X) (_ : S ∈ covering X),     ∃ (T : Presieve Y), T ∈ covering Y ∧ T.FactorsThruAlong S f

CategoryTheory.Coverage.ofGrothendieck.code:
CategoryTheory.Coverage.ofGrothendieck.{u_1, u_2} (C : Type u_1) [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) :
  Coverage C
CategoryTheory.Coverage.ofGrothendieck.comment:
Associate a coverage to any Grothendieck topology.
If `J` is a Grothendieck topology, and `K` is the associated coverage, then a presieve
`S` is a covering presieve for `K` if and only if the sieve that it generates is a
covering sieve for `J`.

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Coverage.covering: The collection of covering presieves for a given object in a category describes the various ways that this object can be covered by presieves.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.generate: This definition creates the least sieve that encompasses a specified collection of morphisms on an object in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback: This definition describes a construction that transforms a sieve on one object into a sieve on another object via the inverse image along a given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.generate_sieve: This theorem asserts that the sieve generated by the arrows of a given sieve is equal to the original sieve itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pull: This theorem asserts that if a sieve is included in the collection associated with one object in a Grothendieck topology, then its pullback along any morphism to another object is also included in the collection associated with that second object.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

CategoryTheory.Coverage.ofGrothendieck.fullDefinition: def ofGrothendieck (J : GrothendieckTopology C) : Coverage C where   covering X := { S | Sieve.generate S ∈ J X }   pullback := by     intro X Y f S (hS : Sieve.generate S ∈ J X)     refine ⟨(Sieve.generate S).pullback f, ?_, fun Z g h => h⟩     dsimp     rw [Sieve.generate_sieve]     exact J.pullback_stable _ hS
CategoryTheory.Coverage.ofGrothendieck.description: This definition establishes a correspondence between coverings and Grothendieck topologies by associating a coverage to a given Grothendieck topology.

CategoryTheory.Coverage.toGrothendieck.code:
CategoryTheory.Coverage.toGrothendieck.{u_1, u_2} (C : Type u_1) [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] (K : Coverage C) :
  GrothendieckTopology C
CategoryTheory.Coverage.toGrothendieck.comment:
The Grothendieck topology associated to a coverage `K`.
It is defined *inductively* as follows:
1. If `S` is a covering presieve for `K`, then the sieve generated by `S` is a covering
  sieve for the associated Grothendieck topology.
2. The top sieves are in the associated Grothendieck topology.
3. Add all sieves required by the *local character* axiom of a Grothendieck topology.

The pullback compatibility condition for a coverage ensures that the
associated Grothendieck topology is pullback stable, and so an additional constructor
in the inductive construction is not needed.

CategoryTheory.Coverage.toGrothendieck.fullDefinition: def toGrothendieck (K : Coverage C) : GrothendieckTopology C where   sieves := Saturate K   top_mem' := .top   pullback_stable' := by     intro X Y S f hS     induction hS generalizing Y with     | of X S hS =>       obtain ⟨R,hR1,hR2⟩ := K.pullback f S hS       suffices Sieve.generate R ≤ (Sieve.generate S).pullback f from         saturate_of_superset _ this (Saturate.of _ _ hR1)       rintro Z g ⟨W, i, e, h1, h2⟩       obtain ⟨WW, ii, ee, hh1, hh2⟩ := hR2 h1       refine ⟨WW, i ≫ ii, ee, hh1, ?_⟩       simp only [hh2, reassoc_of% h2, Category.assoc]     | top X => apply Saturate.top     | transitive X R S _ hS H1 _ =>       apply Saturate.transitive       · apply H1 f       intro Z g hg       rw [← Sieve.pullback_comp]       exact hS hg   transitive' X S hS R hR := .transitive _ _ _ hS hR

CategoryTheory.Coverage.gi.fullDefinition: def gi : GaloisInsertion (toGrothendieck C) (ofGrothendieck C) where   choice K _ := toGrothendieck _ K   choice_eq := fun _ _ => rfl   le_l_u J X S hS := by     rw [← Sieve.generate_sieve S]     apply Saturate.of     dsimp [ofGrothendieck]     rwa [Sieve.generate_sieve S]   gc K J := by     constructor     · intro H X S hS       exact H _ <| Saturate.of _ _ hS     · intro H X S hS       induction hS with       | of X S hS => exact H _ hS       | top => apply J.top_mem       | transitive X R S _ _ H1 H2 => exact J.transitive H1 _ H2

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.ι_pre: This theorem states a condition relating the canonical morphisms of colimits under composition and precomposition of functors within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: There exists an isomorphism between a covering sieve and its pullback with respect to the identity morphism in a Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.w: This theorem establishes that for a functor with an existing colimit, the morphism from one object to another in the indexing category, when composed with the corresponding colimit morphism, gives a consistent relation between the colimit points of both objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.ι: This definition describes the morphism that connects an object produced by a functor to the colimit object associated with that functor in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.diag: The theorem states that the application of the pullback diagram functor for a presheaf and a morphism between objects relates to the multiequalizer structure defined by the covering associated with the target object in a Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: The pullback of a covering sieve with respect to a composed morphism is isomorphic to the pullback of the sieve with respect to the second morphism followed by the pullback with respect to the first morphism.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.id: The identity functor on a category maps each object and morphism to itself, preserving their structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: The definition specifies that an arrow associated with a covering sieve in a Grothendieck topology is a morphism from an object to another object, establishing the relationship within the topology.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plus.fullDefinition: def plusObj : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D where   obj X := colimit (J.diagram P X.unop)   map f := colimMap (J.diagramPullback P f.unop) ≫ colimit.pre _ _   map_id := by     intro X     refine colimit.hom_ext (fun S => ?_)     dsimp     simp only [diagramPullback_app, colimit.ι_pre, ι_colimMap_assoc, Category.comp_id]     let e := S.unop.pullbackId     dsimp only [Functor.op, pullback_obj]     erw [← colimit.w _ e.inv.op, ← Category.assoc]     convert Category.id_comp (colimit.ι (diagram J P (unop X)) S)     refine Multiequalizer.hom_ext _ _ _ (fun I => ?_)     dsimp     simp only [Multiequalizer.lift_ι, Category.id_comp, Category.assoc]     dsimp [Cover.Arrow.map, Cover.Arrow.base]     cases I     congr     simp   map_comp := by     intro X Y Z f g     refine colimit.hom_ext (fun S => ?_)     dsimp     simp only [diagramPullback_app, colimit.ι_pre_assoc, colimit.ι_pre, ι_colimMap_assoc,       Category.assoc]     let e := S.unop.pullbackComp g.unop f.unop     dsimp only [Functor.op, pullback_obj]     erw [← colimit.w _ e.inv.op, ← Category.assoc, ← Category.assoc]     congr 1     refine Multiequalizer.hom_ext _ _ _ (fun I => ?_)     dsimp     simp only [Multiequalizer.lift_ι, Category.assoc]     cases I     dsimp only [Cover.Arrow.base, Cover.Arrow.map]     congr 2     simp
CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plus.description: This definition introduces a construction that associates a new presheaf to an existing presheaf within the context of a Grothendieck topology, facilitating the accumulation of functions over covering sieves.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.ι_pre: This theorem states a condition relating the canonical morphisms of colimits under composition and precomposition of functors within a category.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.diagram_map.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
  {D : Type w} [Category.{max v u, w} D] [∀ (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) (X : C) (S : J.Cover X), HasMultiequalizer (S.index P)]
  (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) (X : C) {S T : (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ} (f : S ⟶ T) :
  (J.diagram P X).map f =
    Multiequalizer.lift ((unop T).index P) ((fun S => multiequalizer ((unop S).index P)) S)
      (fun I => Multiequalizer.ι ((unop S).index P) (Cover.Arrow.map I f.unop)) ⋯

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.FamilyOfElements.comment:

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.FamilyOfElements.description: A family of elements from a presheaf is compatible if the pullback of each element is consistent regardless of the morphism or index used to derive it.
