CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plus.fullDefinition: def plusCompIso : J.plusObj P ⋙ F ≅ J.plusObj (P ⋙ F) :=   NatIso.ofComponents     (fun X => by       refine ?_ ≪≫ HasColimit.isoOfNatIso (J.diagramCompIso F P X.unop)       refine         (isColimitOfPreserves F               (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P (unop X)))).coconePointUniqueUpToIso           (colimit.isColimit _))     (by       intro X Y f       apply (isColimitOfPreserves F (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P X.unop))).hom_ext       intro W       dsimp [plusObj, plusMap]       simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]       slice_rhs 1 2 =>         erw [(isColimitOfPreserves F (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P X.unop))).fac]       slice_lhs 1 3 =>         simp only [← F.map_comp]         dsimp [colimMap, IsColimit.map, colimit.pre]         simp only [colimit.ι_desc_assoc, colimit.ι_desc]         dsimp [Cocones.precompose]         simp only [Category.assoc, colimit.ι_desc]         dsimp [Cocone.whisker]         rw [F.map_comp]       simp only [Category.assoc]       slice_lhs 2 3 =>         erw [(isColimitOfPreserves F (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P Y.unop))).fac]       dsimp       simp only [HasColimit.isoOfNatIso_ι_hom_assoc, GrothendieckTopology.diagramPullback_app,         colimit.ι_pre, HasColimit.isoOfNatIso_ι_hom, ι_colimMap_assoc]       simp only [← Category.assoc]       dsimp       congr 1       ext       dsimp       simp only [Category.assoc]       erw [Multiequalizer.lift_ι, diagramCompIso_hom_ι, diagramCompIso_hom_ι, ← F.map_comp,         Multiequalizer.lift_ι])

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plus: This definition introduces a construction that associates a new presheaf to an existing presheaf within the context of a Grothendieck topology, facilitating the accumulation of functions over covering sieves.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasColimit.isoOfNa: This definition states that if two functors are naturally isomorphic, then their respective colimit objects are also isomorphic in the given category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitOfPreserv: This definition states that if a functor preserves colimits and a cocone is a colimit in the source category, then the mapped cocone in the target category is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.isColimit: This definition asserts that an arbitrary cocone over a functor with a colimit possesses the structure of a colimit cocone, confirming its properties as such.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.coconePo: This definition establishes that the points of cocones associated with a functor are unique up to isomorphism when those cocones are colimits.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that two morphisms from a colimit are equal if they yield the same result when composed with the cocone's morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plus: This definition constructs a morphism between enhanced objects associated with two presheaves based on a specified natural transformation within the framework of a Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.fac: This theorem establishes that the morphism from a cocone to its colimit, when composed with the corresponding arrow from the colimit, yields the arrow from the cocone at the same object, ensuring the commutativity of the involved diagram.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimMap: This definition describes a morphism from the colimit of one functor to the colimit of another, which is induced by a natural transformation between those functors, highlighting the functorial nature of colimits.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.map: This definition establishes a morphism from the cocone point of a colimit associated with one functor to the cocone point of another cocone associated with a different functor, given a natural transformation between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.pre: This definition specifies a canonical morphism from the colimit of the composition of two functors to the colimit of the second functor alone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.ι_desc: This theorem establishes a formula that relates the morphism from the colimit of a functor to a cocone with the evaluation at a particular index of that cocone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.precompose: This definition establishes a functor that allows for the transformation of a cocone over one functor into a corresponding cocone over another functor via a natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.whisker: This definition describes the process of transforming a cocone associated with a functor by precomposing it with another functor, effectively creating a new cocone for the composed functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.diag: The theorem states that the application of the pullback diagram functor for a presheaf and a morphism between objects relates to the multiequalizer structure defined by the covering associated with the target object in a Grothendieck topology.

category_theory.grothendieck_topology.pl.fullDefinition: def plusCompIso : J.plusObj P ⋙ F ≅ J.plusObj (P ⋙ F) :=   NatIso.ofComponents     (fun X => by       refine ?_ ≪≫ HasColimit.isoOfNatIso (J.diagramCompIso F P X.unop)       refine         (isColimitOfPreserves F               (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P (unop X)))).coconePointUniqueUpToIso           (colimit.isColimit _))     (by       intro X Y f       apply (isColimitOfPreserves F (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P X.unop))).hom_ext       intro W       dsimp [plusObj, plusMap]       simp only [Functor.map_comp, Category.assoc]       slice_rhs 1 2 =>         erw [(isColimitOfPreserves F (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P X.unop))).fac]       slice_lhs 1 3 =>         simp only [← F.map_comp]         dsimp [colimMap, IsColimit.map, colimit.pre]         simp only [colimit.ι_desc_assoc, colimit.ι_desc]         dsimp [Cocones.precompose]         simp only [Category.assoc, colimit.ι_desc]         dsimp [Cocone.whisker]         rw [F.map_comp]       simp only [Category.assoc]       slice_lhs 2 3 =>         erw [(isColimitOfPreserves F (colimit.isColimit (J.diagram P Y.unop))).fac]       dsimp       simp only [HasColimit.isoOfNatIso_ι_hom_assoc, GrothendieckTopology.diagramPullback_app,         colimit.ι_pre, HasColimit.isoOfNatIso_ι_hom, ι_colimMap_assoc]       simp only [← Category.assoc]       dsimp       congr 1       ext       dsimp       simp only [Category.assoc]       erw [Multiequalizer.lift_ι, diagramCompIso_hom_ι, diagramCompIso_hom_ι, ← F.map_comp,         Multiequalizer.lift_ι])

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.ι_plusCompIso_hom.{w₁, w₂, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {D : Type w₁} [Category.{max v u, w₁} D] {E : Type w₂} [Category.{max v u, w₂} E]
  (F : D ⥤ E) [∀ (α β : Type (max v u)) (fst snd : β → α), HasLimitsOfShape (WalkingMulticospan fst snd) D]
  [∀ (α β : Type (max v u)) (fst snd : β → α), HasLimitsOfShape (WalkingMulticospan fst snd) E]
  [(X : C) → (W : J.Cover X) → (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) → PreservesLimit (W.index P).multicospan F] (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D)
  [∀ (X : C), HasColimitsOfShape (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ D] [∀ (X : C), HasColimitsOfShape (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ E]
  [(X : C) → PreservesColimitsOfShape (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ F] (X : Cᵒᵖ) (W : (J.Cover (unop X))ᵒᵖ) :
  F.map (colimit.ι (J.diagram P (unop X)) W) ≫ (J.plusCompIso F P).hom.app X =
    (J.diagramCompIso F P (unop X)).hom.app W ≫ colimit.ι (J.diagram (P ⋙ F) (unop X)) W

CategoryTheory.constantPresheafAdj.fullDefinition: noncomputable def constantPresheafAdj {T : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) :     Functor.const Cᵒᵖ ⊣ (evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op T) :=   Adjunction.mkOfUnitCounit {     unit := (Functor.constCompEvaluationObj D (op T)).hom     counit := {       app := fun F => {         app := fun ⟨X⟩ => F.map (IsTerminal.from hT X).op         naturality := fun _ _ _ => by           simp only [Functor.comp_obj, Functor.const_obj_obj, Functor.id_obj, Functor.const_obj_map,             Category.id_comp, ← Functor.map_comp]           congr           simp }       naturality := by intros; ext; simp /- Note: `aesop` works but is kind of slow -/ } }

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.multiforkEvaluation.code:
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.multiforkEvaluationCone.{w, w', v, u, z, z'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {D : Type w} [Category.{w', w} D] {K : Type z} [Category.{z', z} K] (F : K ⥤ Sheaf J D)
  (E : Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D)) (X : C) (W : J.Cover X) (S : Multifork (W.index E.pt)) :
  Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D ⋙ (evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X))
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.multiforkEvaluation.comment:
An auxiliary definition to be used below.

Whenever `E` is a cone of shape `K` of sheaves, and `S` is the multifork associated to a
covering `W` of an object `X`, with respect to the cone point `E.X`, this provides a cone of
shape `K` of objects in `D`, with cone point `S.X`.

See `isLimitMultiforkOfIsLimit` for more on how this definition is used.

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.multiforkEvaluation.fullDefinition: def multiforkEvaluationCone (F : K ⥤ Sheaf J D) (E : Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D)) (X : C)     (W : J.Cover X) (S : Multifork (W.index E.pt)) :     Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D ⋙ (evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X)) where   pt := S.pt   π :=     { app := fun k => (Presheaf.isLimitOfIsSheaf J (F.obj k).1 W (F.obj k).2).lift <|         Multifork.ofι _ S.pt (fun i => S.ι i ≫ (E.π.app k).app (op i.Y))           (by             intro i             simp only [Category.assoc]             erw [← (E.π.app k).naturality, ← (E.π.app k).naturality]             dsimp             simp only [← Category.assoc]             congr 1             apply S.condition)       naturality := by         intro i j f         dsimp [Presheaf.isLimitOfIsSheaf]         rw [Category.id_comp]         apply Presheaf.IsSheaf.hom_ext (F.obj j).2 W         intro ii         rw [Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgamate_map, Category.assoc, ← (F.map f).val.naturality, ←           Category.assoc, Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgamate_map]         dsimp [Multifork.ofι]         erw [Category.assoc, ← E.w f]         aesop_cat } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.multiforkEvaluation.description: This definition provides a construction of a cone for a sheaf given a cone of its presheaf and a multifork associated with a covering of an object, ensuring that the new cone has a specific shape and point aligned with the structure of the original cone.

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLimitMultiforkOfI.code:
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLimitMultiforkOfIsLimit.{w, w', v, u, z, z'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {D : Type w} [Category.{w', w} D] {K : Type z} [Category.{z', z} K]
  [HasLimitsOfShape K D] (F : K ⥤ Sheaf J D) (E : Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D)) (hE : IsLimit E) (X : C)
  (W : J.Cover X) : IsLimit (W.multifork E.pt)
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLimitMultiforkOfI.comment:
If `E` is a cone of shape `K` of sheaves, which is a limit on the level of presheaves,
this definition shows that the limit presheaf satisfies the multifork variant of the sheaf
condition, at a given covering `W`.

This is used below in `isSheaf_of_isLimit` to show that the limit presheaf is indeed a sheaf.

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLimitMultiforkOfI.fullDefinition: def isLimitMultiforkOfIsLimit (F : K ⥤ Sheaf J D) (E : Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D))     (hE : IsLimit E) (X : C) (W : J.Cover X) : IsLimit (W.multifork E.pt) :=   Multifork.IsLimit.mk _     (fun S => (isLimitOfPreserves ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X)) hE).lift <|       multiforkEvaluationCone F E X W S)     (by       intro S i       apply (isLimitOfPreserves ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op i.Y)) hE).hom_ext       intro k       dsimp [Multifork.ofι]       erw [Category.assoc, (E.π.app k).naturality]       dsimp       rw [← Category.assoc]       erw [(isLimitOfPreserves ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X)) hE).fac         (multiforkEvaluationCone F E X W S)]       dsimp [multiforkEvaluationCone, Presheaf.isLimitOfIsSheaf]       erw [Presheaf.IsSheaf.amalgamate_map]       rfl)     (by       intro S m hm       apply (isLimitOfPreserves ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X)) hE).hom_ext       intro k       dsimp       erw [(isLimitOfPreserves ((evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X)) hE).fac]       apply Presheaf.IsSheaf.hom_ext (F.obj k).2 W       intro i       dsimp only [multiforkEvaluationCone, Presheaf.isLimitOfIsSheaf]       rw [(F.obj k).cond.amalgamate_map]       dsimp [Multifork.ofι]       change _ = S.ι i ≫ _       erw [← hm, Category.assoc, ← (E.π.app k).naturality, Category.assoc]       rfl) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isLimitMultiforkOfI.description: This definition establishes that if a cone of sheaves is a limit for presheaves, then it also satisfies the multifork version of the sheaf condition for a specified covering, confirming that the limit presheaf is indeed a sheaf.

  {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {D : Type w} [Category.{w', w} D] {K : Type z} [Category.{z', z} K]
  [HasLimitsOfShape K D] (F : K ⥤ Sheaf J D) (E : Cone (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf J D)) (hE : IsLimit E) (X : C)

category_theory.Sheaf.is_limit_multifork.comment:
If `E` is a cone of shape `K` of sheaves, which is a limit on the level of presheaves,
this definition shows that the limit presheaf satisfies the multifork variant of the sheaf
condition, at a given covering `W`.

This is used below in `isSheaf_of_isLimit` to show that the limit presheaf is indeed a sheaf.

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isSheaf_of_isLimit.comment:
If `E` is a cone which is a limit on the level of presheaves,
then the limit presheaf is again a sheaf.

This is used to show that the forgetful functor from sheaves to presheaves creates limits.

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.sheafifyCocone.comment:
Construct a cocone by sheafifying a cocone point of a cocone `E` of presheaves
over a functor which factors through sheaves.
In `isColimitSheafifyCocone`, we show that this is a colimit cocone when `E` is a colimit.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Cove: The collection of covers for an object in a category, according to a specific Grothendieck topology, is defined as a poset.
This definition describes the relationship between two arrows in a covering sieve of a Grothendieck topology by relating the source of one arrow to the target of another.
This definition establishes a connection between a covering associated with a Grothendieck topology and a presheaf by creating a corresponding multicospan index.

The theorem establishes that if two arrows in a covering sieve relate to each other, then their corresponding morphisms to a common object can be expressed as equal when composed with the respective morphisms of the arrows.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasMultiequalizer: The definition specifies that a multicospan has a multiequalizer if there exists a limit for the associated multicospan structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.w: This theorem establishes that for a functor with an existing colimit, the morphism from one object to another in the indexing category, when composed with the corresponding colimit morphism, gives a consistent relation between the colimit points of both objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.toSh: The definition establishes a canonical morphism from a given functor to its sheafification according to a specified Grothendieck topology.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.toSh.description: The theorem asserts that the application of a functor via sheafification in a specific Grothendieck topology is equivalent to the process of sheafifying the functor directly.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.IsGe: This definition specifies the condition under which a Grothendieck topology is considered to be generated by one-hypercovers of a certain size.

CategoryTheory.Functor.isContinuous_of_p.description: This theorem establishes that a functor is continuous if it preserves one-hypercovers and the source Grothendieck topology is generated by one-hypercovers.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presieve.IsSheaf: A presheaf is defined as a sheaf for a topology if it satisfies the sheaf condition for every sieve associated with that topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf: This definition characterizes a sheaf of a category as a presheaf that satisfies the condition of being a sheaf of types for every object in the target category, relative to a specified Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.op: This definition describes a natural isomorphism between the opposite functors of two functors that are naturally isomorphic to each other.

CategoryTheory.Functor.op_comp_isSheaf.description: This theorem establishes that the composition of an opposite functor with a sheaf results in a presheaf that qualifies as a sheaf under a specified Grothendieck topology when the original functor is continuous.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op: This definition describes the concept of the opposite of a functor, which allows a functor from one category to be viewed as a functor between the opposite categories of both the source and target.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.SheafOfTypes.val: The underlying presheaf of a sheaf of types for a given topology is represented as a functor from the opposite category to types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.val: This definition specifies the functor representing the underlying presheaf of a given sheaf with respect to a specified Grothendieck topology.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.NatIso.op: This definition describes a natural isomorphism between the opposite functors of two functors that are naturally isomorphic to each other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.OneH: This definition describes the image of a one-hypercover in a category under a functor that preserves its structure, resulting in a new one-hypercover in the target category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.op_comp_isSheaf: This theorem establishes that the composition of an opposite functor with a sheaf results in a presheaf that qualifies as a sheaf under a specified Grothendieck topology when the original functor is continuous.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sheaf.Hom.val: A morphism between two sheaves corresponds to a morphism between their underlying presheaves.

CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardC.description: This definition describes a functor that provides a sheaf-theoretic pushforward from one Grothendieck topology to another, applicable when the functor preserves continuity between the two topologies.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction: This definition establishes an adjunction between the functors representing sheafification and inclusion, indicating that they are related in a way that one reverses the effect of the other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.abelianOfAdjunction: This definition states that a preadditive category is abelian if it is connected to an abelian category through a pair of functors that preserve zero morphisms and finite limits, along with an adjunction between them.

CategoryTheory.sheafIsAbelian.fullDefinition: instance sheafIsAbelian : Abelian (Sheaf J D) :=   let adj := sheafificationAdjunction J D   abelianOfAdjunction _ _ (asIso adj.counit) adj set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
CategoryTheory.sheafIsAbelian.description: This definition states that if a category of sheaves over a specified Grothendieck topology on an abelian category also has the property of being abelian, then the sheaf category itself is abelian as well.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.shea.comment:

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.plus: This definition asserts that there exists an isomorphism between the composition of the plus object of a presheaf with a functor and the plus object of the functor applied to the presheaf itself, given certain conditions on limits and colimits in the respective categories.
This definition describes a functor that maps presheaves to their corresponding plus objects in the context of a Grothendieck topology.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.shea.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the sheafification of a functor applied to a presheaf and the sheafification of the composition of that functor with the original presheaf.

CategoryTheory.Sieve.coverByImage.comment:
For a functor `G : C ⥤ D`, and an object `U : D`, `Sieve.coverByImage G U` is the sieve of `U`
consisting of those arrows that factor through images of `G`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.fullyFaithfulFuncto: This definition states that when a functor is fully faithful, there exists a Galois coinsertion between the pushforward and pullback operations induced by that functor.
explanatories.GaloisCoinsertion.u_l_eq: The theorem states that in a Galois coinsertion, applying the function from the second set to the image of an element in the first set returns the original element from the first set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.functorPushforward_: This theorem asserts that the pushforward of the trivial sieve under a functor is also trivial.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.top_: Every Grothendieck topology on a category enforces that the top sieve is included in the collection of sieves associated with each object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback: This definition describes a construction that transforms a sieve on one object into a sieve on another object via the inverse image along a given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pull: This theorem asserts that if a sieve is included in the collection associated with one object in a Grothendieck topology, then its pullback along any morphism to another object is also included in the collection associated with that second object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.tran: If a sieve is included in the collection for an object in a Grothendieck topology, then any sieve that can be pulled back along morphisms related to that sieve is also included in the collection for the same object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.pullback_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the pullback of the composition of two morphisms with respect to a sieve is equivalent to first taking the pullback of the first morphism with the sieve and then taking the pullback of the second morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.supe: If one covering sieve is a subset of another, then the larger sieve is also a covering sieve in the Grothendieck topology for that object.

CategoryTheory.presheafHom.comment:
Given two presheaves `F` and `G` on a category `C` with values in a category `A`,
this `presheafHom F G` is the presheaf of types which sends an object `X : C`
to the type of morphisms between the "restrictions" of `F` and `G` to the category `Over X`.

CategoryTheory.presheafHom.fullDefinition: def presheafHom : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type _ where   obj X := (Over.forget X.unop).op ⋙ F ⟶ (Over.forget X.unop).op ⋙ G   map f := whiskerLeft (Over.map f.unop).op   map_id := by     rintro ⟨X⟩     ext φ ⟨Y⟩     simpa [Over.mapId] using φ.naturality ((Over.mapId X).hom.app Y).op   map_comp := by     rintro ⟨X⟩ ⟨Y⟩ ⟨Z⟩ ⟨f : Y ⟶ X⟩ ⟨g : Z ⟶ Y⟩     ext φ ⟨W⟩     simpa [Over.mapComp] using φ.naturality ((Over.mapComp g f).hom.app W).op
CategoryTheory.presheafHom.description: This definition constructs a presheaf that assigns to each object in a category the type of morphisms between the restrictions of two given presheaves to the over category of that object.

CategoryTheory.presheafHom_map_app.code:

  {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} {X Y Z : C} (f : Z ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ X) (h : Z ⟶ X) (w : f ≫ g = h) (α : (presheafHom F G).obj (op X)) :
  ((presheafHom F G).map g.op α).app (op (Over.mk f)) = α.app (op (Over.mk h))
CategoryTheory.presheafHom_map_app.comment:
Equational lemma for the presheaf structure on `presheafHom`.
It is advisable to use this lemma rather than `dsimp [presheafHom]` which may result
in the need to prove equalities of objects in an `Over` category.

CategoryTheory.presheafHomSectionsEquiv.fullDefinition: def presheafHomSectionsEquiv : (presheafHom F G).sections ≃ (F ⟶ G) where   toFun s :=     { app := fun X => (s.1 X).app ⟨Over.mk (𝟙 _)⟩       naturality := by         rintro ⟨X₁⟩ ⟨X₂⟩ ⟨f : X₂ ⟶ X₁⟩         dsimp         refine Eq.trans ?_ ((s.1 ⟨X₁⟩).naturality           (Over.homMk f : Over.mk f ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 X₁)).op)         erw [← s.2 f.op, presheafHom_map_app_op_mk_id]         rfl }   invFun f := ⟨fun X => whiskerLeft _ f, fun _ => rfl⟩   left_inv s := by     dsimp     ext ⟨X⟩ ⟨Y : Over X⟩     have H := s.2 Y.hom.op     dsimp at H ⊢     rw [← H]     apply presheafHom_map_app_op_mk_id   right_inv f := rfl

Opens.grothendieckTopology.fullDefinition: def grothendieckTopology : GrothendieckTopology (Opens T) where   sieves X S := ∀ x ∈ X, ∃ (U : _) (f : U ⟶ X), S f ∧ x ∈ U   top_mem' X x hx := ⟨_, 𝟙 _, trivial, hx⟩   pullback_stable' X Y S f hf y hy := by     rcases hf y (f.le hy) with ⟨U, g, hg, hU⟩     refine ⟨U ⊓ Y, homOfLE inf_le_right, ?_, hU, hy⟩     apply S.downward_closed hg (homOfLE inf_le_left)   transitive' X S hS R hR x hx := by     rcases hS x hx with ⟨U, f, hf, hU⟩     rcases hR hf _ hU with ⟨V, g, hg, hV⟩     exact ⟨_, g ≫ f, hg, hV⟩

CategoryTheory.coherentCoverage.fullDefinition: def coherentCoverage [Precoherent C] : Coverage C where   covering B := { S | ∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (X : α → C) (π : (a : α) → (X a ⟶ B)),     S = Presieve.ofArrows X π ∧ EffectiveEpiFamily X π }   pullback := by     rintro B₁ B₂ f S ⟨α, _, X₁, π₁, rfl, hS⟩     obtain ⟨β,_,X₂,π₂,h,i,ι,hh⟩ := Precoherent.pullback f α X₁ π₁ hS     refine ⟨Presieve.ofArrows X₂ π₂, ⟨β, inferInstance, X₂, π₂, rfl, h⟩, ?_⟩     rintro _ _ ⟨b⟩     exact ⟨(X₁ (i b)), ι _, π₁ _, ⟨_⟩, hh _⟩

CategoryTheory.Preregular.exists_fac.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [self : Preregular C] {X Y Z : C}
  (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y) [EffectiveEpi g] : ∃ W h, ∃ (_ : EffectiveEpi h), ∃ i, i ≫ g = h ≫ f
CategoryTheory.Preregular.exists_fac.comment:
For `X`, `Y`, `Z`, `f`, `g` like in the diagram, where `g` is an effective epi, there exists
an object `W`, an effective epi `h : W ⟶ X` and a morphism `i : W ⟶ Z` making the diagram
commute.
```
W --i-→ Z
|       |
h       g
↓       ↓
X --f-→ Y
```
CategoryTheory.Preregular.exists_fac.description: This theorem asserts that given a commutative diagram involving an effective epimorphism, there exists an object and effective epimorphism such that the original morphisms can be factored through this new object, preserving the structure of the diagram.

CategoryTheory.regularCoverage.fullDefinition: def regularCoverage [Preregular C] : Coverage C where   covering B := { S | ∃ (X : C) (f : X ⟶ B), S = Presieve.ofArrows (fun (_ : Unit) ↦ X)     (fun (_ : Unit) ↦ f) ∧ EffectiveEpi f }   pullback := by     intro X Y f S ⟨Z, π, hπ, h_epi⟩     have := Preregular.exists_fac f π     obtain ⟨W, h, _, i, this⟩ := this     refine ⟨Presieve.singleton h, ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩     · exact ⟨W, h, by {rw [Presieve.ofArrows_pUnit h]}, inferInstance⟩     · intro W g hg       cases hg       refine ⟨Z, i, π, ⟨?_, this⟩⟩       cases hπ       rw [Presieve.ofArrows_pUnit]       exact Presieve.singleton.mk

explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.

CategoryTheory.extensiveCoverage.fullDefinition: def extensiveCoverage [FinitaryPreExtensive C] : Coverage C where   covering B := { S | ∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (X : α → C) (π : (a : α) → (X a ⟶ B)),     S = Presieve.ofArrows X π ∧ IsIso (Sigma.desc π) }   pullback := by     intro X Y f S ⟨α, hα, Z, π, hS, h_iso⟩     let Z' : α → C := fun a ↦ pullback f (π a)     let π' : (a : α) → Z' a ⟶ Y := fun a ↦ pullback.fst _ _     refine ⟨@Presieve.ofArrows C _ _ α Z' π', ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩     · constructor       exact ⟨hα, Z', π', ⟨by simp only, FinitaryPreExtensive.sigma_desc_iso (fun x => π x) f h_iso⟩⟩     · intro W g hg       rcases hg with ⟨a⟩       refine ⟨Z a, pullback.snd _ _, π a, ?_, by rw [CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition]⟩       rw [hS]       exact Presieve.ofArrows.mk a

CategoryTheory.regularTopology.SingleEqu.fullDefinition: def SingleEqualizerCondition (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ⦃X B : C⦄ (π : X ⟶ B) : Prop :=   ∀ (c : PullbackCone π π) (_ : IsLimit c),     Nonempty (IsLimit (Fork.ofι (P.map π.op) (equalizerCondition_w P c)))
CategoryTheory.regularTopology.SingleEqu.description: A contravariant functor is said to satisfy the Single Equalizer Condition with respect to a morphism if it maps its kernel pair to an equalizer diagram.

CategoryTheory.regularTopology.isLimit_f.fullDefinition: noncomputable def isLimit_forkOfι_equiv (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) {X B : C} (π : X ⟶ B)     (c : PullbackCone π π) (hc : IsLimit c) :     IsLimit (Fork.ofι (P.map π.op) (equalizerCondition_w P c)) ≃     IsLimit (P.mapCone (Sieve.ofArrows (fun (_ : Unit) ↦ X) fun _ ↦ π).arrows.cocone.op) := by   let S := (Sieve.ofArrows (fun (_ : Unit) => X) (fun _ => π)).arrows   let X' := S.categoryMk π ⟨_, 𝟙 _, π, ofArrows.mk (), Category.id_comp _⟩   let P' := S.categoryMk (c.fst ≫ π) ⟨_, c.fst, π, ofArrows.mk (), rfl⟩   let fst : P' ⟶ X' := Over.homMk c.fst   let snd : P' ⟶ X' := Over.homMk c.snd c.condition.symm   let F : S.categoryᵒᵖ ⥤ D := S.diagram.op ⋙ P   let G := parallelPair (P.map c.fst.op) (P.map c.snd.op)   let H := parallelPair fst.op snd.op   have : H.Initial := parallelPair_pullback_initial π c hc   let i : H ⋙ F ≅ G := parallelPair.ext (Iso.refl _) (Iso.refl _) (by aesop) (by aesop)   refine (IsLimit.equivOfNatIsoOfIso i.symm _ _ ?_).trans (Functor.Initial.isLimitWhiskerEquiv H _)   refine Cones.ext (Iso.refl _) ?_   rintro ⟨_ | _⟩   all_goals aesop

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.π: This definition describes a natural transformation from a constant functor at a specific point to another functor, capturing the relationship between a cone and the functor it pertains to.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multiequalizer.ι: The definition specifies a canonical morphism from the multiequalizer of a multicospan index to the corresponding objects on the left within the categorical framework.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multiequalizer.lif: The theorem demonstrates that the composition of a specific lift of morphisms from a multiequalizer corresponds to the morphism associated with an element of the multicospan index, ensuring a consistent mapping through the structure of that index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.ι: This definition describes the morphism that connects an object produced by a functor to the colimit object associated with that functor in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.π: This definition specifies a projection morphism from the limit object of a functor to the object corresponding to a specific element of the indexing category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.app: This definition establishes the use of a natural isomorphism on an object, allowing for a specific application notation within a designated namespace.

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.cone.fullDefinition: def coneCompEvaluationOfConeCompDiagramFunctorCompEvaluation {X : C} {K : Type max v u}     [SmallCategory K] {F : K ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D} {W : J.Cover X} (i : W.Arrow)     (E : Cone (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X ⋙ (evaluation (J.Cover X)ᵒᵖ D).obj (op W))) :     Cone (F ⋙ (evaluation _ _).obj (op i.Y)) where   pt := E.pt   π :=     { app := fun k => E.π.app k ≫ Multiequalizer.ι (W.index (F.obj k)) i       naturality := by         intro a b f         dsimp         rw [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, ← E.w f]         dsimp [diagramNatTrans]         simp only [Multiequalizer.lift_ι, Category.assoc] }

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multiequalizer.con: The theorem asserts that in the presence of a multiequalizer structure, the morphisms corresponding to two different elements from the same basic structure are equal when appropriately composed.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Multiequalizer.hom: If two morphisms from a common object to a multiequalizer are equal when restricted to every component of the multiequalizer, then those two morphisms must be identical.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms from the colimit of a functor to an object are equal when composed with the canonical morphisms from the colimit, then the two morphisms must be equal.

category_theory.grothendieck_topology.li.fullDefinition: def liftToPlusObjLimitObj {K : Type max v u} [SmallCategory K] [FinCategory K]     [HasLimitsOfShape K D] [PreservesLimitsOfShape K (forget D)]     [ReflectsLimitsOfShape K (forget D)] (F : K ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D) (X : C)     (S : Cone (F ⋙ J.plusFunctor D ⋙ (evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X))) :     S.pt ⟶ (J.plusObj (limit F)).obj (op X) :=   let e := colimitLimitIso (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X)   let t : J.diagram (limit F) X ≅ limit (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X) :=     (isLimitOfPreserves (J.diagramFunctor D X) (limit.isLimit F)).conePointUniqueUpToIso       (limit.isLimit _)   let p : (J.plusObj (limit F)).obj (op X) ≅ colimit (limit (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X)) :=     HasColimit.isoOfNatIso t   let s :     colimit (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X).flip ≅ F ⋙ J.plusFunctor D ⋙ (evaluation Cᵒᵖ D).obj (op X) :=     NatIso.ofComponents (fun k => colimitObjIsoColimitCompEvaluation _ k)       (by         intro i j f         rw [← Iso.eq_comp_inv, Category.assoc, ← Iso.inv_comp_eq]         refine colimit.hom_ext (fun w => ?_)         dsimp [plusMap]         erw [colimit.ι_map_assoc,           colimitObjIsoColimitCompEvaluation_ι_inv (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X).flip w j,           colimitObjIsoColimitCompEvaluation_ι_inv_assoc (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X).flip w i]         rw [← (colimit.ι (F ⋙ J.diagramFunctor D X).flip w).naturality]         rfl)   limit.lift _ S ≫ (HasLimit.isoOfNatIso s.symm).hom ≫ e.inv ≫ p.inv

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.pres.fullDefinition: instance preservesLimitsOfShape_plusFunctor     (K : Type max v u) [SmallCategory K] [FinCategory K] [HasLimitsOfShape K D]     [PreservesLimitsOfShape K (forget D)] [ReflectsLimitsOfShape K (forget D)] :     PreservesLimitsOfShape K (J.plusFunctor D) := by   constructor; intro F; apply preservesLimitOfEvaluation; intro X   apply preservesLimitOfPreservesLimitCone (limit.isLimit F)   refine ⟨fun S => liftToPlusObjLimitObj.{w, v, u} F X.unop S, ?_, ?_⟩   · intro S k     apply liftToPlusObjLimitObj_fac   · intro S m hm     dsimp [liftToPlusObjLimitObj]     simp_rw [← Category.assoc, Iso.eq_comp_inv, ← Iso.comp_inv_eq]     refine limit.hom_ext (fun k => ?_)     simp only [limit.lift_π, Category.assoc, ← hm]     congr 1     refine colimit.hom_ext (fun k => ?_)     dsimp [plusMap, plusObj]     erw [colimit.ι_map, colimit.ι_desc_assoc, limit.lift_π]     conv_lhs => dsimp     simp only [Category.assoc]     rw [ι_colimitLimitIso_limit_π_assoc]     simp only [NatIso.ofComponents_inv_app, colimitObjIsoColimitCompEvaluation_ι_app_hom,       Iso.symm_inv]     conv_lhs =>       dsimp [IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso]     rw [← Category.assoc, ← NatTrans.comp_app, limit.lift_π]     rfl

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Subp.fullDefinition: noncomputable def Subpresheaf.sheafifyLift (f : G.toPresheaf ⟶ F') (h : Presieve.IsSheaf J F') :     (G.sheafify J).toPresheaf ⟶ F' where   app U s := (h (G.sieveOfSection s.1) s.prop).amalgamate     (_) ((G.family_of_elements_compatible s.1).compPresheafMap f)   naturality := by     intro U V i     ext s     apply (h _ ((Subpresheaf.sheafify J G).toPresheaf.map i s).prop).isSeparatedFor.ext     intro W j hj     refine (Presieve.IsSheafFor.valid_glue (h _ ((G.sheafify J).toPresheaf.map i s).2)       ((G.family_of_elements_compatible _).compPresheafMap _) _ hj).trans ?_     dsimp     conv_rhs => rw [← FunctorToTypes.map_comp_apply]     change _ = F'.map (j ≫ i.unop).op _     refine Eq.trans ?_ (Presieve.IsSheafFor.valid_glue (h _ s.2)       ((G.family_of_elements_compatible s.1).compPresheafMap f) (j ≫ i.unop) ?_).symm     swap -- Porting note: need to swap two goals otherwise the first goal needs to be proven     -- inside the second goal any way     · dsimp [Presieve.FamilyOfElements.compPresheafMap] at hj ⊢       rwa [FunctorToTypes.map_comp_apply]     · dsimp [Presieve.FamilyOfElements.compPresheafMap]       exact congr_arg _ (Subtype.ext (FunctorToTypes.map_comp_apply _ _ _ _).symm)

CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.imag.fullDefinition: noncomputable def imageFactorization {F F' : Sheaf J TypeMax.{v, u}} (f : F ⟶ F') :     Limits.ImageFactorisation f where   F := imageMonoFactorization f   isImage :=     { lift := fun I => by         -- Porting note: need to specify the target category (TypeMax.{v, u}) for this to work.         haveI M := (Sheaf.Hom.mono_iff_presheaf_mono J TypeMax.{v, u} _).mp I.m_mono         haveI := isIso_toImagePresheaf I.m.1         refine ⟨Subpresheaf.homOfLe ?_ ≫ inv (toImagePresheaf I.m.1)⟩         apply Subpresheaf.sheafify_le         · conv_lhs => rw [← I.fac]           apply imagePresheaf_comp_le         · rw [← isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type]           exact F'.2         · apply Presieve.isSheaf_iso J (asIso <| toImagePresheaf I.m.1)           rw [← isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type]           exact I.I.2       lift_fac := fun I => by         ext1         dsimp [imageMonoFactorization]         generalize_proofs h         rw [← Subpresheaf.homOfLe_ι h, Category.assoc]         congr 1         rw [IsIso.inv_comp_eq, toImagePresheaf_ι] }

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.equalizerSieve.{w, v', v, u', u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u'}
  [Category.{v', u'} D] [ConcreteCategory D] {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D} {X : Cᵒᵖ} (x y : (forget D).obj (F.obj X)) : Sieve (unop X)
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.equalizerSieve.comment:
If `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D` is a presheaf with values in a concrete category, if `x` and `y` are
elements in `F.obj X`, this is the sieve of `X.unop` consisting of morphisms `f`
such that `F.map f.op x = F.map f.op y`.

explanatories.Opposite.unop: This definition describes the canonical mapping from the opposite category of a type back to the original type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.arrows: This definition establishes a construction that converts a sieve on an object in a category into a corresponding presieve on the same object.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.equalizerSieve.fullDefinition: def equalizerSieve {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D} {X : Cᵒᵖ} (x y : F.obj X) : Sieve X.unop where   arrows _ f := F.map f.op x = F.map f.op y   downward_closed {X Y} f hf g := by     dsimp at hf ⊢     simp [hf]
CategoryTheory.Presheaf.equalizerSieve.description: This definition constructs a sieve for a given object in a presheaf category based on the equality of elements in the presheaf, defined on a concrete category.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.equalizerSieve_s.description: This theorem states that the sieve corresponding to two identical elements in a presheaf category is the maximal sieve.

CategoryTheory.Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_iff_equalizerSieve_mem_imp.{w, v', v, u', u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  {D : Type u'} [Category.{v', u'} D] [ConcreteCategory D] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {F₁ F₂ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ D}
  (φ : F₁ ⟶ F₂) :

    ∀ ⦃X : Cᵒᵖ⦄ (x y : (forget D).obj (F₁.obj X)),

This theorem establishes a biconditional relationship stating that a morphism between presheaves is locally injective if and only if the initial morphism is locally injective when the second morphism is also locally injective, under a specified Grothendieck topology.

This theorem establishes a biconditional relationship indicating that a morphism between presheaves is locally injective with respect to a specified Grothendieck topology if and only if its composition with the forgetful functor from a concrete category is also locally injective.

CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsLocallyInjective.comment:
If `φ : F₁ ⟶ F₂` is a morphism of sheaves, this is an abbreviation for
`Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective J φ.val`. Under suitable assumptions, it
is equivalent to the injectivity of all maps `φ.val.app X`,
see `isLocallyInjective_iff_injective`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.sheafToPresheaf: This definition establishes a functor that maps sheaves, defined in terms of a specific Grothendieck topology, to their corresponding presheaves.

this is the family of elements of `R` defined over the sieve `Presheaf.imageSieve φ r'`
which sends a map in this sieve to an arbitrary choice of a preimage of the
restriction of `r'`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.imageSieve: This definition describes the sieve associated with a morphism between two presheaves, consisting of maps into a given object that relate to sections from the image of the morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Presheaf.localPreimage: This definition provides a construction for obtaining a preimage in one presheaf based on the presence of a morphism in the associated sieve of a mapping from another presheaf.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Sieve.arrows: This definition establishes a construction that converts a sieve on an object in a category into a corresponding presieve on the same object.

CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.fullDefinition: noncomputable def localPreimage :     FamilyOfElements R (Presheaf.imageSieve φ r').arrows :=   fun _ f hf => Presheaf.localPreimage φ r' f hf
CategoryTheory.Presieve.FamilyOfElements.description: This definition characterizes a family of elements from one presheaf in terms of the preimages of sections that lie within the associated sieve of another presheaf induced by a morphism.

CategoryTheory.SingleObj.mapHom.code:
CategoryTheory.SingleObj.mapHom.{u, v} (M : Type u) [Monoid M] (N : Type v) [Monoid N] :
  (M →* N) ≃ SingleObj M ⥤ SingleObj N
CategoryTheory.SingleObj.mapHom.comment:
There is a 1-1 correspondence between monoid homomorphisms `M → N` and functors between the
    corresponding single-object categories. It means that `SingleObj` is a fully faithful
    functor.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/001F> --
although we do not characterize when the functor is full or faithful.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.of_right_adjoi.description: If a category is filtered and has a functor with a left adjoint, then the corresponding codomain category is also filtered.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃.code:
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [IsFilteredOrEmpty C] {j₁ j₂ : C}
  (f g h : j₁ ⟶ j₂) : C
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃.comment:
`coeq₃ f g h`, for morphisms `f g h : j₁ ⟶ j₂`, is an arbitrary choice of object
which admits a morphism `coeq₃Hom f g h : j₂ ⟶ coeq₃ f g h` such that
`coeq₃_condition₁`, `coeq₃_condition₂` and `coeq₃_condition₃` are satisfied.
Its existence is ensured by `IsFiltered`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.leftToMax: This definition asserts the existence of a morphism from one object to the maximum of itself and another object in a filtered or empty category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.rightToMax: This definition indicates the existence of a morphism from one object to a selected maximum object among two in a filtered category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeqHom: This definition indicates that for morphisms between two objects in a filtered or empty category, there exists a morphism to their coequalizer that satisfies a specific compatibility condition.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃.fullDefinition: noncomputable def coeq₃ {j₁ j₂ : C} (f g h : j₁ ⟶ j₂) : C :=   coeq (coeqHom f g ≫ leftToMax (coeq f g) (coeq g h))     (coeqHom g h ≫ rightToMax (coeq f g) (coeq g h))
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃.description: This definition asserts the existence of an object in a filtered or empty category for given morphisms between two objects, which satisfies specific compatibility conditions with respect to those morphisms.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃Hom.code:
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃Hom.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [IsFilteredOrEmpty C] {j₁ j₂ : C}
  (f g h : j₁ ⟶ j₂) : j₂ ⟶ coeq₃ f g h
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃Hom.comment:
`coeq₃Hom f g h`, for morphisms `f g h : j₁ ⟶ j₂`, is an arbitrary choice of morphism
`j₂ ⟶ coeq₃ f g h` such that `coeq₃_condition₁`, `coeq₃_condition₂` and `coeq₃_condition₃`

explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.leftToMax: This definition asserts the existence of a morphism from one object to the maximum of itself and another object in a filtered or empty category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.rightToMax: This definition indicates the existence of a morphism from one object to a selected maximum object among two in a filtered category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeqHom: This definition indicates that for morphisms between two objects in a filtered or empty category, there exists a morphism to their coequalizer that satisfies a specific compatibility condition.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃Hom.fullDefinition: noncomputable def coeq₃Hom {j₁ j₂ : C} (f g h : j₁ ⟶ j₂) : j₂ ⟶ coeq₃ f g h :=   coeqHom f g ≫     leftToMax (coeq f g) (coeq g h) ≫       coeqHom (coeqHom f g ≫ leftToMax (coeq f g) (coeq g h))         (coeqHom g h ≫ rightToMax (coeq f g) (coeq g h))
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃Hom.description: This definition states that for three parallel morphisms between two objects in a filtered or empty category, there exists a morphism to their coequalizer that meets specific compatibility conditions.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃_conditio.description: This theorem states that in a filtered or empty category, the composition of a morphism with the coequalizer of two morphisms from one object to another yields the same result when either morphism is used.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃_conditio.code:

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.coeq₃_conditio.code:

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.span.code:
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.span.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [IsFilteredOrEmpty C] {i j j' : C} (f : i ⟶ j)
  (f' : i ⟶ j') : ∃ k g g', f ≫ g = f' ≫ g'
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.span.comment:
For every span `j ⟵ i ⟶ j'`, there
exists a cocone `j ⟶ k ⟵ j'` such that the square commutes.
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.span.description: This theorem asserts that for any pair of morphisms from one object to two others in a filtered or empty category, there exists a third object and two morphisms that complete the square formed by those relationships.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.bowtie.code:
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.bowtie.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [IsFilteredOrEmpty C] {j₁ j₂ k₁ k₂ : C}
  (f₁ : j₁ ⟶ k₁) (g₁ : j₁ ⟶ k₂) (f₂ : j₂ ⟶ k₁) (g₂ : j₂ ⟶ k₂) : ∃ s α β, f₁ ≫ α = g₁ ≫ β ∧ f₂ ≫ α = g₂ ≫ β
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.bowtie.comment:
Given a "bowtie" of morphisms
```
 j₁   j₂
 |\  /|
 | \/ |
 | /\ |
 |/  \∣
 vv  vv
 k₁  k₂
```
in a filtered category, we can construct an object `s` and two morphisms from `k₁` and `k₂` to `s`,
making the resulting squares commute.
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.bowtie.description: This theorem states that in a filtered category with a specific arrangement of morphisms, it is possible to find an object and two morphisms such that the corresponding squares formed by these morphisms commute.

CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.tulip.comment:
Given a "tulip" of morphisms
```
 j₁    j₂    j₃
 |\   / \   / |
 | \ /   \ /  |
 |  vv    vv  |
 \  k₁    k₂ /
  \         /
   \       /
    \     /
     \   /
      v v
       l
```
in a filtered category, we can construct an object `s` and three morphisms from `k₁`, `k₂` and `l`
to `s`, making the resulting squares commute.
CategoryTheory.IsFiltered.tulip.description: This theorem demonstrates that in a filtered category, a specific configuration of morphisms, often visualized as a "tulip" diagram, allows the construction of an object and morphisms that create commuting squares.

CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.eq.code:

CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.eqHom.description: This definition asserts the existence of a morphism that connects an equivalence object for two parallel morphisms in a cofiltered or empty category, respecting a specific condition of equality involving those morphisms.

there exists a cone `j ⟵ k ⟶ j'` such that the square commutes.
CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.cospan.description: This theorem states that given a specific arrangement of morphisms in a cofiltered category, it is always possible to find an object and two morphisms forming a cone that satisfies the necessary commutativity condition.

CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.inf_exists.code:
CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.inf_exists.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [IsCofiltered C] (O : Finset C)
  (H : Finset ((X : C) ×' (Y : C) ×' (_ : X ∈ O) ×' (_ : Y ∈ O) ×' (X ⟶ Y))) :
  ∃ S T, ∀ {X Y : C} (mX : X ∈ O) (mY : Y ∈ O) {f : X ⟶ Y}, ⟨X, ⟨Y, ⟨mX, ⟨mY, f⟩⟩⟩⟩ ∈ H → T mX ≫ f = T mY
CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.inf_exists.comment:
Given any `Finset` of objects `{X, ...}` and
indexed collection of `Finset`s of morphisms `{f, ...}` in `C`,
there exists an object `S`, with a morphism `T X : S ⟶ X` from each `X`,
such that the triangles commute: `T X ≫ f = T Y`, for `f : X ⟶ Y` in the `Finset`.
CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.inf_exists.description: This theorem states that in a cofiltered category, given a finite collection of objects and specific morphisms between them, there exists another object with morphisms to each object that ensures the commutativity of certain triangles associated with those morphisms.

CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.inf.code:

CategoryTheory.IsCofiltered.inf.comment:
An arbitrary choice of object "to the left"
of a finite collection of objects `O` and morphisms `H`,
making all the triangles commute.

explanatories.Inf.inf: A function that computes the greatest lower bound of two elements in a set or lattice structure.

CategoryTheory.GlueData.mapGlueData.fullDefinition: def mapGlueData : GlueData C' where   J := D.J   U i := F.obj (D.U i)   V i := F.obj (D.V i)   f i j := F.map (D.f i j)   f_mono i j := preserves_mono_of_preservesLimit _ _   f_id i := inferInstance   t i j := F.map (D.t i j)   t_id i := by     simp [D.t_id i]   t' i j k :=     (PreservesPullback.iso F (D.f i j) (D.f i k)).inv ≫       F.map (D.t' i j k) ≫ (PreservesPullback.iso F (D.f j k) (D.f j i)).hom   t_fac i j k := by simpa [Iso.inv_comp_eq] using congr_arg (fun f => F.map f) (D.t_fac i j k)   cocycle i j k := by     simp only [Category.assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc, ← Functor.map_comp_assoc, D.cocycle,       Iso.inv_hom_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, Category.id_comp]

CategoryTheory.GlueData'.t''.fullDefinition: def GlueData'.t'' (D : GlueData' C) (i j k : D.J) :     pullback (D.f' i j) (D.f' i k) ⟶ pullback (D.f' j k) (D.f' j i) :=   if hij : i = j then     (pullbackSymmetry _ _).hom ≫       pullback.map _ _ _ _ (eqToHom (by aesop)) (eqToHom (by aesop)) (eqToHom (by aesop))         (by aesop) (by aesop)   else if hik : i = k then     have : IsIso (pullback.snd (D.f' j k) (D.f' j i)) := by       subst hik; infer_instance     pullback.fst _ _ ≫ eqToHom (dif_neg hij) ≫ D.t _ _ _ ≫       eqToHom (dif_neg (Ne.symm hij)).symm ≫ inv (pullback.snd _ _)   else if hjk : j = k then     have : IsIso (pullback.snd (D.f' j k) (D.f' j i)) := by       apply (config := { allowSynthFailures := true}) pullback_snd_iso_of_left_iso       simp only [hjk, GlueData'.f', ↓reduceDIte]       infer_instance     pullback.fst _ _ ≫ eqToHom (dif_neg hij) ≫ D.t _ _ _ ≫       eqToHom (dif_neg (Ne.symm hij)).symm ≫ inv (pullback.snd _ _)   else     haveI := Ne.symm hij     pullback.map _ _ _ _ (eqToHom (by aesop)) (eqToHom (by rw [dif_neg hik]))         (eqToHom (by aesop)) (by aesop) (by delta f'; aesop) ≫       D.t' i j k hij hik hjk ≫       pullback.map _ _ _ _ (eqToHom (by aesop)) (eqToHom (by aesop)) (eqToHom (by aesop))         (by delta f'; aesop) (by delta f'; aesop)

CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofMkLEMk_comp_o.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between morphisms derived from monomorphisms, demonstrating how compositions of certain morphisms through specified subobjects are equal under given conditions.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofLE_refl.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofLE_refl.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {B : C} (X : Subobject B) :
  X.ofLE X ⋯ = 𝟙 (underlying.obj X)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofLE_refl.description: This theorem asserts that the comparison morphism of a subobject with itself is equal to the identity morphism on the underlying object of that subobject.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofMkLEMk_refl.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofMkLEMk_refl.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {B A₁ : C} (f : A₁ ⟶ B) [Mono f] :

CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEq.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEq.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {B : C} (X Y : Subobject B) (h : X = Y) :
  underlying.obj X ≅ underlying.obj Y
CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEq.comment:
An equality of subobjects gives an isomorphism of the corresponding objects.
(One could use `underlying.mapIso (eqToIso h))` here, but this is more readable.)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Comma.hom: This definition specifies a method to extract the morphism connecting the left and right components of a comma object formed by two functors.
explanatories.LE.le.hom: This definition represents an inequality between two elements in a preorder as a morphism in the associated category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofLE: This definition establishes a morphism from the underlying object of one subobject to the underlying object of another when there is an inequality between those subobjects.
explanatories.Eq.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.
explanatories.Eq.ge: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEq.fullDefinition: def isoOfEq {B : C} (X Y : Subobject B) (h : X = Y) : (X : C) ≅ (Y : C) where   hom := ofLE _ _ h.le   inv := ofLE _ _ h.ge
CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEq.description: An equality of two subobjects leads to an isomorphism between their corresponding underlying objects.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEqMk.code:

  [Mono f] (h : X = mk f) : underlying.obj X ≅ A
CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEqMk.comment: An equality of subobjects gives an isomorphism of the corresponding objects.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofMkLE: This definition describes a morphism from an object to the underlying object of a subobject, based on an established inequality of subobjects verified by a morphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfEqMk.description: This definition asserts that if two subobjects of a category are equal, then there exists an isomorphism between the underlying objects corresponding to those subobjects and another object linked by a monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfMkEq.description: This definition states that when a subobject is represented by a monomorphism that is equal to another morphism, then an isomorphism is established between the corresponding objects.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.isoOfMkEqMk.description: This definition asserts that if two subobjects corresponding to monomorphisms are equal, then the associated objects are isomorphic.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {Y : D} (F : MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y) : Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower.comment:
Any functor `MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y` descends to a functor
`Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y`, because `MonoOver Y` is thin.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver: This definition describes a category consisting of all monomorphisms targeting a specific object, serving as a full subcategory within a broader over category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map: This definition specifies a functor that allows for a mapping from a category to another while preserving the structure of their thin skeletons.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.map: This definition establishes a functor that maps monomorphisms over one object to monomorphisms over another object through post-composition with a specified monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower.fullDefinition: def lower {Y : D} (F : MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y) : Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y :=   ThinSkeleton.map F
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower.description: This definition establishes a functor that connects the category of subobjects under one monomorphism to the category of subobjects under another monomorphism, leveraging the thin structure of the latter category.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower_iso.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower_iso.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C}
  (F₁ F₂ : MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y) (h : F₁ ≅ F₂) : lower F₁ = lower F₂
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower_iso.comment:
Isomorphic functors become equal when lowered to `Subobject`.
(It's not as evil as usual to talk about equality between functors
because the categories are thin and skeletal.)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver: This definition describes a category consisting of all monomorphisms targeting a specific object, serving as a full subcategory within a broader over category.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower_iso.description: If two functors from monomorphisms over one object to monomorphisms over another object are isomorphic, their lower-level representations as subobjects are equal.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower₂.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower₂.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C}
  (F : MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y ⥤ MonoOver Z) : Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject Z

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver: This definition describes a category consisting of all monomorphisms targeting a specific object, serving as a full subcategory within a broader over category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map₂: This definition describes how a functor between categories can be adapted to map from the thin skeleton of one category to the thin skeleton of another category, preserving the structure in the process.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower₂.fullDefinition: def lower₂ (F : MonoOver X ⥤ MonoOver Y ⥤ MonoOver Z) : Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject Z :=   ThinSkeleton.map₂ F
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower₂.description: This definition provides a functorial construction for relating subobjects across three categorical objects, based on relationships between monomorphisms.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower_comm.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower_comm.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C}
  (F : MonoOver Y ⥤ MonoOver X) : toThinSkeleton (MonoOver Y) ⋙ lower F = F ⋙ toThinSkeleton (MonoOver X)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton: This definition constructs the thin skeleton category by taking the quotient of objects from a thin category, resulting in a preorder with specific definitional properties.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver: This definition describes a category consisting of all monomorphisms targeting a specific object, serving as a full subcategory within a broader over category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.toThinSkeleton: This definition establishes a functor that maps a category to its thin skeleton.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower_comm.description: This theorem establishes a relationship between two functors involving monomorphisms that demonstrates a specific equality when transitioning to the lower representations of the involved categories.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerAdjunction.comment:
An adjunction between `MonoOver A` and `MonoOver B` gives an adjunction
between `Subobject A` and `Subobject B`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver: This definition describes a category consisting of all monomorphisms targeting a specific object, serving as a full subcategory within a broader over category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.lowerAdjunct: This definition shows that an adjunction between two categories leads to an adjunction between their respective thin skeletons.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerAdjunction.fullDefinition: def lowerAdjunction {A : C} {B : D} {L : MonoOver A ⥤ MonoOver B} {R : MonoOver B ⥤ MonoOver A}     (h : L ⊣ R) : lower L ⊣ lower R :=   ThinSkeleton.lowerAdjunction _ _ h
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerAdjunction.description: This definition states that an adjunction between the categories of monomorphisms targeted at two objects induces an adjunction between the corresponding categories of subobjects.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerEquivalenc.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerEquivalence.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u₂}
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {A : C} {B : D} (e : MonoOver A ≌ MonoOver B) : Subobject A ≌ Subobject B
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerEquivalenc.comment:
An equivalence between `MonoOver A` and `MonoOver B` gives an equivalence
between `Subobject A` and `Subobject B`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver: This definition describes a category consisting of all monomorphisms targeting a specific object, serving as a full subcategory within a broader over category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor: This definition introduces a functor that represents one direction of an equivalence between two categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.counitIso: This definition describes that the composition of a functor and its inverse related to an equivalence between categories is isomorphic to the identity functor of the second category.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map_iso_eq: This theorem asserts that if two functors from one category to a thin category are isomorphic, then their respective mappings to the thin skeleton of the category are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.inverse: This definition specifies a functor that serves as the inverse of an equivalence between two categories, allowing for mapping in the opposite direction.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToIso: An equality between two objects in a category corresponds to an isomorphism between those objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.unitIso: This definition states that a specific functor composition related to an equivalence between categories is isomorphic to the identity functor of the first category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map_id_eq: This theorem states that the mapping induced by the identity morphism of a category is equal to the identity morphism of its thin skeleton.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map_comp_eq: The theorem states that the map functor of the composition of two functors from one category to another is equal to the composition of their respective map functors when the first category is thin.
explanatories.OrderIso.symm: This definition describes the inverse of an order isomorphism, which establishes a correspondence between two ordered sets in the reverse direction.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerEquivalenc.fullDefinition: def lowerEquivalence {A : C} {B : D} (e : MonoOver A ≌ MonoOver B) : Subobject A ≌ Subobject B where   functor := lower e.functor   inverse := lower e.inverse   unitIso := by     apply eqToIso     convert ThinSkeleton.map_iso_eq e.unitIso     · exact ThinSkeleton.map_id_eq.symm     · exact (ThinSkeleton.map_comp_eq _ _).symm   counitIso := by     apply eqToIso     convert ThinSkeleton.map_iso_eq e.counitIso     · exact (ThinSkeleton.map_comp_eq _ _).symm     · exact ThinSkeleton.map_id_eq.symm
CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerEquivalenc.description: This definition establishes that an equivalence of categories of monomorphisms over two objects implies an equivalence of the corresponding categories of subobjects.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasPullbacks C] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject X
CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback.comment:
When `C` has pullbacks, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` induces a functor `Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject X`,
by pulling back a monomorphism along `f`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower: This definition establishes a functor that connects the category of subobjects under one monomorphism to the category of subobjects under another monomorphism, leveraging the thin structure of the latter category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.pullback: This definition establishes a functor that relates the category of monomorphisms over one object to the category of monomorphisms over another object by pulling back along a morphism when the category allows for pullbacks.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback.fullDefinition: def pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) : Subobject Y ⥤ Subobject X :=   lower (MonoOver.pullback f)
CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback.description: A morphism in a category with pullbacks induces a functor that pulls back subobjects along that morphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback_id.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback_id.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} [HasPullbacks C]
  (x : Subobject X) : (pullback (𝟙 X)).obj x = x

explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullbacks: This definition indicates that a category possesses pullbacks for every possible pair of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.pullback: This definition establishes a functor that relates the category of monomorphisms over one object to the category of monomorphisms over another object by pulling back along a morphism when the category allows for pullbacks.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback_id.description: The theorem states that pulling back a subobject using the identity morphism results in the original subobject itself.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback_comp.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C} [HasPullbacks C]
  (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (x : Subobject Z) : (pullback (f ≫ g)).obj x = (pullback f).obj ((pullback g).obj x)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullbacks: This definition indicates that a category possesses pullbacks for every possible pair of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.pullback: This definition establishes a functor that relates the category of monomorphisms over one object to the category of monomorphisms over another object by pulling back along a morphism when the category allows for pullbacks.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.pullback_comp.description: This theorem states that the pullback of a composition of two morphisms is equivalent to the pullback of the first morphism applied to the result of the pullback of the second morphism applied to a given subobject.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.map.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.map.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f] :
  Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y
CategoryTheory.Subobject.map.comment:
We can map subobjects of `X` to subobjects of `Y`
by post-composition with a monomorphism `f : X ⟶ Y`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map: This definition specifies a functor that allows for a mapping from a category to another while preserving the structure of their thin skeletons.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lower: This definition establishes a functor that connects the category of subobjects under one monomorphism to the category of subobjects under another monomorphism, leveraging the thin structure of the latter category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.map: This definition establishes a functor that maps monomorphisms over one object to monomorphisms over another object through post-composition with a specified monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.map.fullDefinition: def map (f : X ⟶ Y) [Mono f] : Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y :=   lower (MonoOver.map f)
CategoryTheory.Subobject.map.description: This definition describes a functor that allows the mapping of subobjects from one object to subobjects of another object through post-composition with a specified monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_id.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_id.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X : C} (x : Subobject X) :
  (map (𝟙 X)).obj x = x

explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map: This definition specifies a functor that allows for a mapping from a category to another while preserving the structure of their thin skeletons.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.map: This definition establishes a functor that maps monomorphisms over one object to monomorphisms over another object through post-composition with a specified monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_id.description: This theorem shows that the mapping of an identity morphism on an object to a subobject is equal to the original subobject itself.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_comp.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
  [Mono f] [Mono g] (x : Subobject X) : (map (f ≫ g)).obj x = (map g).obj ((map f).obj x)

explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map: This definition specifies a functor that allows for a mapping from a category to another while preserving the structure of their thin skeletons.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.map: This definition establishes a functor that maps monomorphisms over one object to monomorphisms over another object through post-composition with a specified monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_comp.description: This theorem indicates that for subobjects arising from monomorphisms, composing the mappings associated with two morphisms maintains compatibility in their respective images under the mapping of the combined morphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIso.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIso.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {A B : C} (e : A ≅ B) :
  Subobject A ≌ Subobject B
CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIso.comment: Isomorphic objects have equivalent subobject lattices.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lowerEquivalenc: This definition establishes that an equivalence of categories of monomorphisms over two objects implies an equivalence of the corresponding categories of subobjects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.mapIso: This definition establishes that if two objects are isomorphic, then their corresponding categories of monomorphisms are equivalent.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIso.fullDefinition: def mapIso {A B : C} (e : A ≅ B) : Subobject A ≌ Subobject B :=   lowerEquivalence (MonoOver.mapIso e)
CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIso.description: This definition states that there is an equivalence of subobject categories between two isomorphic objects in a category.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIsoToOrderIs.code:
CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIsoToOrderIso.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} (e : X ≅ Y) :
  Subobject X ≃o Subobject Y
CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIsoToOrderIs.comment:
In fact, there's a type level bijection between the subobjects of isomorphic objects,
which preserves the order.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.comp: This statement defines the composition of two functors, where the first functor is applied to an object followed by the second functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory.obj: This definition specifies the object type within a category that is identified as a full subcategory, which includes all objects that satisfy a certain property.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ThinSkeleton.map: This definition specifies a functor that allows for a mapping from a category to another while preserving the structure of their thin skeletons.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.MonoOver.map: This definition establishes a functor that maps monomorphisms over one object to monomorphisms over another object through post-composition with a specified monomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_id: This theorem shows that the mapping of an identity morphism on an object to a subobject is equal to the original subobject itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.map_comp: This theorem indicates that for subobjects arising from monomorphisms, composing the mappings associated with two morphisms maintains compatibility in their respective images under the mapping of the combined morphism.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.mapIsoToOrderIs.fullDefinition: def mapIsoToOrderIso (e : X ≅ Y) : Subobject X ≃o Subobject Y where   toFun := (map e.hom).obj   invFun := (map e.inv).obj   left_inv g := by simp_rw [← map_comp, e.hom_inv_id, map_id]   right_inv g := by simp_rw [← map_comp, e.inv_hom_id, map_id]   map_rel_iff' {A B} := by     dsimp     constructor     · intro h       apply_fun (map e.inv).obj at h       · simpa only [← map_comp, e.hom_inv_id, map_id] using h       · apply Functor.monotone     · intro h       apply_fun (map e.hom).obj at h       · exact h       · apply Functor.monotone

CategoryTheory.Subobject.exists.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {X Y : C} [HasImages C] (f : X ⟶ Y) :
  Subobject X ⥤ Subobject Y
CategoryTheory.Subobject.exists.comment:
The functor from subobjects of `X` to subobjects of `Y` given by
sending the subobject `S` to its "image" under `f`, usually denoted $\exists_f$.
For instance, when `C` is the category of types,
viewing `Subobject X` as `Set X` this is just `Set.image f`.

This functor is left adjoint to the `pullback f` functor (shown in `existsPullbackAdj`)
provided both are defined, and generalises the `map f` functor, again provided it is defined.

describe the subobjects of `A` as the subobjects `P` of `B` in `C` for which `A.hom` factors
through the image of `P` under `T`.

CategoryTheory.StructuredArrow.subobject.fullDefinition: def subobjectEquiv [HasLimits C] [PreservesLimits T] (A : StructuredArrow S T) :     Subobject A ≃o { P : Subobject A.right // ∃ q, q ≫ T.map P.arrow = A.hom } where   toFun P := ⟨projectSubobject P, projectSubobject_factors P⟩   invFun P := liftSubobject P.val P.prop.choose_spec   left_inv P := lift_projectSubobject _ _   right_inv P := Subtype.ext (by simp only [liftSubobject, homMk_right, projectSubobject_mk,       Subobject.mk_arrow, Subtype.coe_eta])   map_rel_iff' := by     apply Subobject.ind₂     intro P Q f g hf hg     refine ⟨fun h => Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_comm ?_ ?_, fun h => ?_⟩     · exact homMk (Subobject.ofMkLEMk _ _ h)         ((cancel_mono (T.map g.right)).1 (by simp [← T.map_comp]))     · aesop_cat     · refine Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_comm (Subobject.ofMkLEMk _ _ h).right ?_       exact congr_arg CommaMorphism.right (Subobject.ofMkLEMk_comp h)

CategoryTheory.CostructuredArrow.quotien.fullDefinition: def quotientEquiv [HasColimits C] [PreservesColimits S] (A : CostructuredArrow S T) :     Subobject (op A) ≃o { P : Subobject (op A.left) // ∃ q, S.map P.arrow.unop ≫ q = A.hom } where   toFun P := ⟨projectQuotient P, projectQuotient_factors P⟩   invFun P := liftQuotient P.val P.prop.choose_spec   left_inv P := lift_projectQuotient _ _   right_inv P := Subtype.ext (by simp only [liftQuotient, Quiver.Hom.unop_op, homMk_left,       Quiver.Hom.op_unop, projectQuotient_mk, Subobject.mk_arrow])   map_rel_iff' := by     apply Subobject.ind₂     intro P Q f g hf hg     refine ⟨fun h => Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_comm ?_ ?_, fun h => ?_⟩     · refine (homMk (Subobject.ofMkLEMk _ _ h).unop ((cancel_epi (S.map g.unop.left)).1 ?_)).op       dsimp       simp only [← S.map_comp_assoc, unop_left_comp_ofMkLEMk_unop, unop_op, CommaMorphism.w,         Functor.const_obj_obj, right_eq_id, Functor.const_obj_map, Category.comp_id]     · apply Quiver.Hom.unop_inj       ext       exact unop_left_comp_ofMkLEMk_unop _     · refine Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_comm (Subobject.ofMkLEMk _ _ h).unop.left.op ?_       refine Quiver.Hom.unop_inj ?_       have := congr_arg Quiver.Hom.unop (Subobject.ofMkLEMk_comp h)       simpa only [unop_op, Functor.id_obj, Functor.const_obj_obj, MonoOver.mk'_obj, Over.mk_left,         MonoOver.mk'_arrow, unop_comp, Quiver.Hom.unop_op, comp_left]           using congr_arg CommaMorphism.left this

CategoryTheory.MonoOver.inf.comment:
When `[HasPullbacks C]`, `MonoOver A` has "intersections", functorial in both arguments.

As `MonoOver A` is only a preorder, this doesn't satisfy the axioms of `SemilatticeInf`,
but we reuse all the names from `SemilatticeInf` because they will be used to construct
`SemilatticeInf (subobject A)` shortly.

CategoryTheory.MonoOver.inf.fullDefinition: def inf {A : C} : MonoOver A ⥤ MonoOver A ⥤ MonoOver A where   obj f := pullback f.arrow ⋙ map f.arrow   map k :=     { app := fun g => by         apply homMk _ _         · apply pullback.lift (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _ ≫ k.left) _           rw [pullback.condition, assoc, w k]         dsimp         rw [pullback.lift_snd_assoc, assoc, w k] }
CategoryTheory.MonoOver.inf.description: This definition indicates that in a category with pullbacks, the collection of monomorphisms over a specific object has a functorial structure that allows for the definition of intersections in a two-variable manner, even though it does not strictly adhere to the formal structure of a semilattice.
