category_theory.mono_over.inf.comment:
When `[HasPullbacks C]`, `MonoOver A` has "intersections", functorial in both arguments.

As `MonoOver A` is only a preorder, this doesn't satisfy the axioms of `SemilatticeInf`,
but we reuse all the names from `SemilatticeInf` because they will be used to construct
`SemilatticeInf (subobject A)` shortly.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Over.coprod: In a category with binary coproducts, there is a functorial operation that allows the combination of over categories based on a given object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.prod: This definition indicates that the product of two objects in a category can be accessed through a specified notation, provided that a binary product exists for those objects.

CategoryTheory.Subobject.semilatticeSup.fullDefinition: instance semilatticeSup {B : C} : SemilatticeSup (Subobject B) where   sup := fun m n => (sup.obj m).obj n   le_sup_left := fun m n => Quotient.inductionOn₂' m n fun _ _ => ⟨MonoOver.leSupLeft _ _⟩   le_sup_right := fun m n => Quotient.inductionOn₂' m n fun _ _ => ⟨MonoOver.leSupRight _ _⟩   sup_le := fun m n k =>     Quotient.inductionOn₃' m n k fun _ _ _ ⟨i⟩ ⟨j⟩ => ⟨MonoOver.supLe _ _ _ i j⟩

CategoryTheory.Subobject.subobjectOrderI.fullDefinition: def subobjectOrderIso {X : C} (Y : Subobject X) : Subobject (Y : C) ≃o Set.Iic Y where   toFun Z :=     ⟨Subobject.mk (Z.arrow ≫ Y.arrow),       Set.mem_Iic.mpr (le_of_comm ((underlyingIso _).hom ≫ Z.arrow) (by simp))⟩   invFun Z := Subobject.mk (ofLE _ _ Z.2)   left_inv Z := mk_eq_of_comm _ (underlyingIso _) (by aesop_cat)   right_inv Z := Subtype.ext (mk_eq_of_comm _ (underlyingIso _) (by           dsimp           simp [← Iso.eq_inv_comp]))   map_rel_iff' {W Z} := by     dsimp     constructor     · intro h       exact le_of_comm (((underlyingIso _).inv ≫ ofLE _ _ (Subtype.mk_le_mk.mp h) ≫         (underlyingIso _).hom)) (by aesop_cat)     · intro h       exact Subtype.mk_le_mk.mpr (le_of_comm         ((underlyingIso _).hom ≫ ofLE _ _ h ≫ (underlyingIso _).inv) (by simp))
CategoryTheory.Subobject.subobjectOrderI.description: This definition establishes an order isomorphism between the subobject lattice of a given subobject and the interval of ideals that are less than or equal to that subobject in the category.

category_theory.limits.le_kernel_subobje.description: The theorem demonstrates that if an arrow from a subobject to the codomain of a morphism becomes zero when composed with that morphism, then this subobject can be considered a subobject of the kernel of the morphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelSubobjectIso.code:

  {X' : C} (f : X' ⟶ X) [IsIso f] (g : X ⟶ Y) [HasKernel g] :

CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelSubobjectIso.comment:
The isomorphism between the kernel of `f ≫ g` and the kernel of `g`,
when `f` is an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernelOrderHom.comment:
Taking cokernels is an order-reversing map from the subobjects of `X` to the quotient objects
of `X`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject: This definition describes a category consisting of isomorphism classes of monomorphisms that map into a specific object within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk: This construction provides a way to generate a subobject from a monomorphism mapping to a specific object within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.equalizer.conditio: The theorem establishes the condition that the equalizer morphism corresponding to two parallel arrows in a category satisfies the equality when composed with both of those arrows.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.equalizer.lift: A morphism from one object to another that behaves like a factorization through a certain equalizer can be constructed if it satisfies a specific equality condition involving two parallel morphisms.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.condition: The inclusion morphism from the kernel of a morphism into its source maps to zero when composed with the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.comp_zero: This theorem states that the composition of any morphism with a zero morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift: A morphism that satisfies the condition of mapping to zero when composed with another morphism can be lifted to factor through the kernel of the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lift: This definition establishes a function on subobjects of a specific object in a category, derived from a function defined on monomorphisms mapping to that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.π: The morphism from the target of a given morphism in a category to its cokernel is defined, provided the cokernel exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk_eq_mk_of_com: This theorem states that two subobjects are considered equal if there exists a commuting isomorphism between them that connects their respective arrows.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.op: This definition introduces the concept of the opposite isomorphism, which associates an isomorphism between two objects in a category with an isomorphism between their opposites.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.coconePo: This definition establishes that the points of cocones associated with a functor are unique up to isomorphism when those cocones are colimits.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.isColimit: This definition asserts that an arbitrary cocone over a functor with a colimit possesses the structure of a colimit cocone, confirming its properties as such.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isCokernelEpiComp: If a morphism has a cokernel and another morphism is epimorphic, then the cokernel of the first morphism naturally induces a cokernel for the composition of these morphisms.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.unop_comp: The theorem asserts that the operation for reversing the direction of the composition of two morphisms in an opposite category results in the composition of their individual reversals in the original order.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_op: The theorem establishes that applying the operation to reverse the direction of a morphism and then applying the operation to revert it returns the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.comp_cocon: The theorem establishes a relationship where the composite of the canonical morphism from a colimit to a cocone point, unique up to isomorphism, equals the morphism from the cocone at a specific index.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer.cofork: The theorem states that the projection morphism from the coequalizer of two morphisms is equal to the specified projection associated with those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.ind₂: This theorem asserts that if a property holds for pairs of subobjects defined by monomorphisms into a specific object, then it also holds for any two subobjects of that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lift_mk: This theorem states that the function defined for subobjects constructed from monomorphisms maps directly to the value assigned to the morphism that represents the subobject.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_com: This theorem establishes that if two monomorphisms to the same object are related by a morphism that commutes with them, then the corresponding subobjects can be compared, with one being less than or equal to the other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.desc: Any morphism that annihilates another morphism can be factored through the cokernel of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofMkLEMk_comp: This theorem asserts that when there is an inequality of subobjects represented by two monomorphisms, the morphism derived from that inequality followed by the second morphism equals the first monomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.condition: The composition of a morphism with its cokernel projection always results in zero when the morphism has a cokernel.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.π_desc: The projection from the cokernel to any morphism that annihilates the original morphism is equivalent to that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.conePointU: This definition asserts that the cone points of limits for a given functor are unique up to isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.image.lift: This definition describes a morphism from the image of a given morphism to a specific component of another monomorphism factorization of that morphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernelOrderHom.fullDefinition: def cokernelOrderHom [HasCokernels C] (X : C) : Subobject X →o (Subobject (op X))ᵒᵈ where   toFun :=     Subobject.lift (fun A f _ => Subobject.mk (cokernel.π f).op)       (by         rintro A B f g hf hg i rfl         refine Subobject.mk_eq_mk_of_comm _ _ (Iso.op ?_) (Quiver.Hom.unop_inj ?_)         · exact (IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso (colimit.isColimit _)             (isCokernelEpiComp (colimit.isColimit _) i.hom rfl)).symm         · simp only [Iso.comp_inv_eq, Iso.op_hom, Iso.symm_hom, unop_comp, Quiver.Hom.unop_op,             colimit.comp_coconePointUniqueUpToIso_hom, Cofork.ofπ_ι_app,             coequalizer.cofork_π])   monotone' :=     Subobject.ind₂ _ <| by       intro A B f g hf hg h       dsimp only [Subobject.lift_mk]       refine Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_comm (cokernel.desc f (cokernel.π g) ?_).op ?_       · rw [← Subobject.ofMkLEMk_comp h, Category.assoc, cokernel.condition, comp_zero]       · exact Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (cokernel.π_desc _ _ _)
CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernelOrderHom.description: This definition establishes an order-reversing correspondence between the subobjects of a given object in a category and the quotient objects of its dual, specifically applicable when cokernels exist.

category_theory.limits.cokernel_order_ho.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernelOrderHom.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasCokernels C]
  (X : C) : Subobject X →o (Subobject (op X))ᵒᵈ
category_theory.limits.cokernel_order_ho.comment:
Taking cokernels is an order-reversing map from the subobjects of `X` to the quotient objects
of `X`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk: This construction provides a way to generate a subobject from a monomorphism mapping to a specific object within a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.equalizer.ι: This definition provides a way to access the inclusion morphism from the equalizer of two parallel arrows to one of their common source objects, assuming such an equalizer exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.equalizer.lift: A morphism from one object to another that behaves like a factorization through a certain equalizer can be constructed if it satisfies a specific equality condition involving two parallel morphisms.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.ι: The morphism from the kernel of a morphism into the source of that morphism is defined in the context of categories with zero morphisms, under the assumption that a kernel exists for the given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift: A morphism that satisfies the condition of mapping to zero when composed with another morphism can be lifted to factor through the kernel of the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Arrow.mk: This definition specifies a construction of an object in the arrow category corresponding to a morphism in the original category.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lift: This definition establishes a function on subobjects of a specific object in a category, derived from a function defined on monomorphisms mapping to that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk_eq_mk_of_com: This theorem states that two subobjects are considered equal if there exists a commuting isomorphism between them that connects their respective arrows.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.op: This definition introduces the concept of the opposite isomorphism, which associates an isomorphism between two objects in a category with an isomorphism between their opposites.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.unop_comp: The theorem asserts that the operation for reversing the direction of the composition of two morphisms in an opposite category results in the composition of their individual reversals in the original order.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.ind₂: This theorem asserts that if a property holds for pairs of subobjects defined by monomorphisms into a specific object, then it also holds for any two subobjects of that object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lift_mk: This theorem states that the function defined for subobjects constructed from monomorphisms maps directly to the value assigned to the morphism that represents the subobject.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk_le_mk_of_com: This theorem establishes that if two monomorphisms to the same object are related by a morphism that commutes with them, then the corresponding subobjects can be compared, with one being less than or equal to the other.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.ofMkLEMk_comp: This theorem asserts that when there is an inequality of subobjects represented by two monomorphisms, the morphism derived from that inequality followed by the second morphism equals the first monomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.conePointU: This definition asserts that the cone points of limits for a given functor are unique up to isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.isLimit: This definition provides evidence that the cone derived from a functor has the properties of a limit cone in the context of a category that possesses a limit for that functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isKernelCompMono: Every kernel of a morphism induces a kernel for the composition with another morphism when that second morphism is a monomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.parallelPair: The definition represents a diagram in a category formed by two morphisms that share the same source and target objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.unop: This definition describes a method for retrieving an isomorphism in the original category from an isomorphism that exists in the opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.limit.conePointUni: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the unique isomorphism connecting two limit cones results in a relationship between the projection morphism from the limit and the morphism from the cone to the specific object in the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.zero_comp: This theorem states that composing a zero morphism with any morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.op_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in a quiver is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.image.ι: This definition describes the morphism that includes the image of a morphism as it maps into the target of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.image.lift: This definition describes a morphism from the image of a given morphism to a specific component of another monomorphism factorization of that morphism.

CategoryTheory.Limits.imageSubobject_com.comment:
The morphism `imageSubobject (h ≫ f) ⟶ imageSubobject f`
is an epimorphism when `h` is an epimorphism.
In general this does not imply that `imageSubobject (h ≫ f) = imageSubobject f`,
although it will when the ambient category is abelian.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.image.preComp: This definition describes a morphism from the image of the composition of two morphisms to the image of the second morphism, under the condition that both the second morphism and their composition have images.

CategoryTheory.ShiftMkCore.F.fullDefinition: F : A → C ⥤ C   /-- the shift by 0 identifies to the identity functor -/   zero : F 0 ≅ 𝟭 C   /-- the composition of shift functors identifies to the shift by the sum -/   add : ∀ n m : A, F (n + m) ≅ F n ⋙ F m   /-- compatibility with the associativity -/   assoc_hom_app : ∀ (m₁ m₂ m₃ : A) (X : C),     (add (m₁ + m₂) m₃).hom.app X ≫ (F m₃).map ((add m₁ m₂).hom.app X) =       eqToHom (by rw [add_assoc]) ≫ (add m₁ (m₂ + m₃)).hom.app X ≫         (add m₂ m₃).hom.app ((F m₁).obj X) := by aesop_cat   /-- compatibility with the left addition with 0 -/   zero_add_hom_app : ∀ (n : A) (X : C), (add 0 n).hom.app X =     eqToHom (by dsimp; rw [zero_add]) ≫ (F n).map (zero.inv.app X) := by aesop_cat   /-- compatibility with the right addition with 0 -/   add_zero_hom_app : ∀ (n : A) (X : C), (add n 0).hom.app X =     eqToHom (by dsimp; rw [add_zero]) ≫ zero.inv.app ((F n).obj X) := by aesop_cat

CategoryTheory.hasShiftMk.fullDefinition: def hasShiftMk (h : ShiftMkCore C A) : HasShift C A :=   ⟨{ Discrete.functor h.F with       ε := h.zero.inv       μ := fun m n => (h.add m.as n.as).inv       μ_natural_left := by         rintro ⟨X⟩ ⟨Y⟩ ⟨⟨⟨rfl⟩⟩⟩ ⟨X'⟩         ext         dsimp         simp       μ_natural_right := by         rintro ⟨X⟩ ⟨Y⟩ ⟨X'⟩ ⟨⟨⟨rfl⟩⟩⟩         ext         dsimp         simp       associativity := by         rintro ⟨m₁⟩ ⟨m₂⟩ ⟨m₃⟩         ext X         simp [endofunctorMonoidalCategory, h.assoc_inv_app_assoc]       left_unitality := by         rintro ⟨n⟩         ext X         simp [endofunctorMonoidalCategory, h.zero_add_inv_app, ← Functor.map_comp]       right_unitality := by         rintro ⟨n⟩         ext X         simp [endofunctorMonoidalCategory, h.add_zero_inv_app]}⟩

CategoryTheory.Functor.FullyFaithful.has.fullDefinition: def hasShift :     HasShift C A :=   hasShiftMk C A     { F := s       zero := zero hF s i       add := add hF s i       assoc_hom_app := fun m₁ m₂ m₃ X => hF.map_injective (by         have h := shiftFunctorAdd'_assoc_hom_app m₁ m₂ m₃ _ _ (m₁+m₂+m₃) rfl rfl rfl (F.obj X)         simp only [shiftFunctorAdd'_eq_shiftFunctorAdd] at h         rw [← cancel_mono ((i m₃).hom.app ((s m₂).obj ((s m₁).obj X)))]         simp only [Functor.comp_obj, Functor.map_comp, map_add_hom_app,           Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc, NatTrans.naturality_assoc, Functor.comp_map,           Iso.inv_hom_id_app, Category.comp_id]         erw [(i m₃).hom.naturality]         rw [Functor.comp_map, map_add_hom_app,           Functor.map_comp, Functor.map_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id_app_assoc,           ← Functor.map_comp_assoc _ ((i (m₁ + m₂)).inv.app X), Iso.inv_hom_id_app,           Functor.map_id, Category.id_comp, reassoc_of% h,           dcongr_arg (fun a => (i a).hom.app X) (add_assoc m₁ m₂ m₃)]         simp [shiftFunctorAdd', eqToHom_map])       zero_add_hom_app := fun n X => hF.map_injective (by         have this := dcongr_arg (fun a => (i a).hom.app X) (zero_add n)         rw [← cancel_mono ((i n).hom.app ((s 0).obj X)) ]         simp [this, map_add_hom_app,           shiftFunctorAdd_zero_add_hom_app, eqToHom_map]         congr 1         erw [(i n).hom.naturality]         dsimp         simp)       add_zero_hom_app := fun n X => hF.map_injective (by         have := dcongr_arg (fun a => (i a).hom.app X) (add_zero n)         simp [this, ← NatTrans.naturality_assoc, eqToHom_map,           shiftFunctorAdd_add_zero_hom_app]) }

CategoryTheory.PredicateShift.comment:
Given a predicate `P : C → Prop` on objects of a category equipped with a shift by `A`,

  [Category.{u_6, u_1} C] [Category.{u_7, u_2} D] {F : C ⥤ D} {A : Type u_4} [AddMonoid A] [HasShift C A] [HasShift D A]

  (a₁ a₂ a₃ : A) (h : a₁ + a₂ = a₃) (b₁ b₂ b₃ : B) (h₁ : b₁ = φ a₁) (h₂ : b₂ = φ a₂) (h₃ : b₃ = φ a₃) :

CategoryTheory.Functor.ShiftSequence.induced_shiftIso_hom_app_obj.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7} {C : Type u_1}
  {D : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} [Category.{u_7, u_1} C] [Category.{u_6, u_2} D] [Category.{u_5, u_3} A] {L : C ⥤ D}

  [G.ShiftSequence M] (F' : M → D ⥤ A) (e' : (m : M) → L ⋙ F' m ≅ G.shift m) [((whiskeringLeft C D A).obj L).Full]
  [((whiskeringLeft C D A).obj L).Faithful] (n a a' : M) (ha' : n + a = a') (X : C) :

CategoryTheory.Abelian.coimageImageCompa.comment:
The canonical map from the abelian coimage to the abelian image.
In any abelian category this is an isomorphism.

Conversely, any additive category with kernels and cokernels and
in which this is always an isomorphism, is abelian.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0107>

CategoryTheory.NonPreadditiveAbelian.σ.comment:
The composite `A ⨯ A ⟶ cokernel (diag A) ⟶ A` given by the natural projection into the cokernel
followed by the inverse of `r`. In the category of modules, using the normal kernels and
cokernels, this map is equal to the map `(a, b) ↦ a - b`, hence the name `σ` for
"subtraction".

CategoryTheory.Abelian.epiIsCokernelOfKe.comment:
In an abelian category, an epi is the cokernel of its kernel. More precisely:
If `f` is an epimorphism and `s` is some limit kernel cone on `f`, then `f` is a cokernel
of `fork.ι s`.

CategoryTheory.Abelian.monoIsKernelOfCokernel.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Abelian C] {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y}
  [Mono f] (s : Cofork f 0) (h : IsColimit s) : IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι f ⋯)
CategoryTheory.Abelian.monoIsKernelOfCok.comment:
In an abelian category, a mono is the kernel of its cokernel. More precisely:
If `f` is a monomorphism and `s` is some colimit cokernel cocone on `f`, then `f` is a kernel
of `cofork.π s`.

CategoryTheory.Abelian.PullbackToBiprodu.comment:
The canonical map `pullback f g ⟶ X ⊞ Y` induces a kernel cone on the map

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.ι: The morphism from the kernel of a morphism into the source of that morphism is defined in the context of categories with zero morphisms, under the assumption that a kernel exists for the given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.condition: The composition of a morphism with its cokernel projection always results in zero when the morphism has a cokernel.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.desc: Any morphism that annihilates another morphism can be factored through the cokernel of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.KernelFork: A kernel fork in a category is a special type of diagram consisting of a morphism and a zero morphism, where the latter serves as the second component of the fork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ι: This definition introduces a morphism that connects a given point of a fork on two parallel morphisms to the zero instance of a parallel pair formed by those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.KernelFork.ofι: A morphism that satisfies the property of mapping to zero when composed with another morphism uniquely defines a kernel fork over that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.condition: The inclusion morphism from the kernel of a morphism into its source maps to zero when composed with the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.colimit.desc: This definition describes a morphism that relates the colimit object of a functor to the point of any chosen cocone over that functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.image.ι: This definition represents the inclusion map from the image of a morphism to its codomain in an abelian category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.image.ι: This definition describes the morphism that includes the image of a morphism as it maps into the target of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork: The definition specifies that a fork on two morphisms between the same objects in a category is a cone over the parallel pair formed by those morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.KernelFork.conditi: In a category, if a kernel fork exists for a morphism, then the composition of the first morphism in the fork with the original morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.CokernelCofork.con: The projection morphism from a cokernel cofork, when composed with the original morphism, results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.desc: This definition describes a morphism from the point of a colimit cocone to the point of another cocone, ensuring a connection between their respective structures.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.desc: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism from a binary biproduct to another object by using a pair of morphisms originating from each summand of that biproduct.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift_desc: This theorem expresses that the composition of the lift of a morphism pair into a binary biproduct with a corresponding descent morphism equals the sum of the original morphisms composed with their respective target morphisms in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_neg: This theorem demonstrates that composing a morphism with the negation of another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to negating the composition of the first morphism with the second morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.condition: The theorem asserts that the composition of the first projection from a pullback with one morphism is equal to the composition of the second projection with the other morphism, establishing a condition that must hold for pullbacks in a categorical context.
explanatories.add_right_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, each element added to its additive inverse equals the identity element, which is zero.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.condition: This theorem states that the composition of the first morphism with the first inclusion of the pushout equals the composition of the second morphism with the second inclusion of the pushout, establishing a crucial condition for the pushout's universality.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pushout.desc: This definition describes how a pair of morphisms from the objects in a pushout to a common object can induce a morphism from the pushout object to that common object, given a specific condition relating the two morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.condition: This theorem states that for a cofork, the composition of its projection with both morphisms yields the same result, ensuring a specific relationship between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ι: This definition describes a natural transformation from a functor to a constant functor at a specified point in a category.

CategoryTheory.Abelian.PullbackToBiprodu.fullDefinition: def isLimitPullbackToBiproduct : IsLimit (pullbackToBiproductFork f g) :=   Fork.IsLimit.mk _     (fun s =>       pullback.lift (Fork.ι s ≫ biprod.fst) (Fork.ι s ≫ biprod.snd) <|         sub_eq_zero.1 <| by           rw [Category.assoc, Category.assoc, ← comp_sub, sub_eq_add_neg, ← comp_neg, ←             biprod.desc_eq, KernelFork.condition s])     (fun s => by       apply biprod.hom_ext <;> rw [Fork.ι_ofι, Category.assoc]       · rw [biprod.lift_fst, pullback.lift_fst]       · rw [biprod.lift_snd, pullback.lift_snd])     fun s m h => by apply pullback.hom_ext <;> simp [← h]
CategoryTheory.Abelian.PullbackToBiprodu.description: This definition states that the canonical morphism from the pullback of two maps to their biproduct is a limit representing the kernel of the induced map.

CategoryTheory.Abelian.epi_pullback_of_e.fullDefinition: instance epi_pullback_of_epi_f [Epi f] : Epi (pullback.snd f g) :=   -- It will suffice to consider some morphism e : Y ⟶ R such that     -- pullback.snd f g ≫ e = 0 and show that e = 0.     epi_of_cancel_zero _ fun {R} e h => by     -- Consider the morphism u := (0, e) : X ⊞ Y⟶ R.     let u := biprod.desc (0 : X ⟶ R) e     -- The composite pullback f g ⟶ X ⊞ Y ⟶ R is zero by assumption.     have hu : PullbackToBiproductIsKernel.pullbackToBiproduct f g ≫ u = 0 := by simpa [u]     -- pullback_to_biproduct f g is a kernel of (f, -g), so (f, -g) is a     -- cokernel of pullback_to_biproduct f g     have :=       epiIsCokernelOfKernel _         (PullbackToBiproductIsKernel.isLimitPullbackToBiproduct f g)     -- We use this fact to obtain a factorization of u through (f, -g) via some d : Z ⟶ R.     obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' this u hu     dsimp at d; dsimp [u] at hd     -- But then f ≫ d = 0:     have : f ≫ d = 0 := calc       f ≫ d = (biprod.inl ≫ biprod.desc f (-g)) ≫ d := by rw [biprod.inl_desc]       _ = biprod.inl ≫ u := by rw [Category.assoc, hd]       _ = 0 := biprod.inl_desc _ _     -- But f is an epimorphism, so d = 0...     have : d = 0 := (cancel_epi f).1 (by simpa)     -- ...or, in other words, e = 0.     calc       e = biprod.inr ≫ biprod.desc (0 : X ⟶ R) e := by rw [biprod.inr_desc]       _ = biprod.inr ≫ biprod.desc f (-g) ≫ d := by rw [← hd]       _ = biprod.inr ≫ biprod.desc f (-g) ≫ 0 := by rw [this]       _ = (biprod.inr ≫ biprod.desc f (-g)) ≫ 0 := by rw [← Category.assoc]       _ = 0 := HasZeroMorphisms.comp_zero _ _
CategoryTheory.Abelian.epi_pullback_of_e.description: This definition states that in an abelian category, the pullback of an epimorphism is also an epimorphism.

category_theory.abelian.epi_pullback_of_.fullDefinition: instance epi_pullback_of_epi_g [Epi g] : Epi (pullback.fst f g) :=   -- It will suffice to consider some morphism e : X ⟶ R such that   -- pullback.fst f g ≫ e = 0 and show that e = 0.   epi_of_cancel_zero _ fun {R} e h => by     -- Consider the morphism u := (e, 0) : X ⊞ Y ⟶ R.     let u := biprod.desc e (0 : Y ⟶ R)     -- The composite pullback f g ⟶ X ⊞ Y ⟶ R is zero by assumption.     have hu : PullbackToBiproductIsKernel.pullbackToBiproduct f g ≫ u = 0 := by simpa [u]     -- pullback_to_biproduct f g is a kernel of (f, -g), so (f, -g) is a     -- cokernel of pullback_to_biproduct f g     have :=       epiIsCokernelOfKernel _         (PullbackToBiproductIsKernel.isLimitPullbackToBiproduct f g)     -- We use this fact to obtain a factorization of u through (f, -g) via some d : Z ⟶ R.     obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' this u hu     dsimp at d; dsimp [u] at hd     -- But then (-g) ≫ d = 0:     have : (-g) ≫ d = 0 := calc       (-g) ≫ d = (biprod.inr ≫ biprod.desc f (-g)) ≫ d := by rw [biprod.inr_desc]       _ = biprod.inr ≫ u := by rw [Category.assoc, hd]       _ = 0 := biprod.inr_desc _ _     -- But g is an epimorphism, thus so is -g, so d = 0...     have : d = 0 := (cancel_epi (-g)).1 (by simpa)     -- ...or, in other words, e = 0.     calc       e = biprod.inl ≫ biprod.desc e (0 : Y ⟶ R) := by rw [biprod.inl_desc]       _ = biprod.inl ≫ biprod.desc f (-g) ≫ d := by rw [← hd]       _ = biprod.inl ≫ biprod.desc f (-g) ≫ 0 := by rw [this]       _ = (biprod.inl ≫ biprod.desc f (-g)) ≫ 0 := by rw [← Category.assoc]       _ = 0 := HasZeroMorphisms.comp_zero _ _

CategoryTheory.Abelian.epi_fst_of_factor.comment:
Suppose `f` and `g` are two morphisms with a common codomain and suppose we have written `g` as
an epimorphism followed by a monomorphism. If `f` factors through the mono part of this
factorization, then any pullback of `g` along `f` is an epimorphism.

CategoryTheory.Abelian.mono_pushout_of_m.fullDefinition: instance mono_pushout_of_mono_f [Mono f] : Mono (pushout.inr _ _ : Z ⟶ pushout f g) :=   mono_of_cancel_zero _ fun {R} e h => by     let u := biprod.lift (0 : R ⟶ Y) e     have hu : u ≫ BiproductToPushoutIsCokernel.biproductToPushout f g = 0 := by simpa [u]     have :=       monoIsKernelOfCokernel _         (BiproductToPushoutIsCokernel.isColimitBiproductToPushout f g)     obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := KernelFork.IsLimit.lift' this u hu     dsimp at d     dsimp [u] at hd     have : d ≫ f = 0 := calc       d ≫ f = d ≫ biprod.lift f (-g) ≫ biprod.fst := by rw [biprod.lift_fst]       _ = u ≫ biprod.fst := by rw [← Category.assoc, hd]       _ = 0 := biprod.lift_fst _ _     have : d = 0 := (cancel_mono f).1 (by simpa)     calc       e = biprod.lift (0 : R ⟶ Y) e ≫ biprod.snd := by rw [biprod.lift_snd]       _ = (d ≫ biprod.lift f (-g)) ≫ biprod.snd := by rw [← hd]       _ = (0 ≫ biprod.lift f (-g)) ≫ biprod.snd := by rw [this]       _ = 0 ≫ biprod.lift f (-g) ≫ biprod.snd := by rw [Category.assoc]       _ = 0 := zero_comp

CategoryTheory.Abelian.mono_pushout_of_m.fullDefinition: instance mono_pushout_of_mono_g [Mono g] : Mono (pushout.inl f g) :=   mono_of_cancel_zero _ fun {R} e h => by     let u := biprod.lift e (0 : R ⟶ Z)     have hu : u ≫ BiproductToPushoutIsCokernel.biproductToPushout f g = 0 := by simpa [u]     have :=       monoIsKernelOfCokernel _         (BiproductToPushoutIsCokernel.isColimitBiproductToPushout f g)     obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := KernelFork.IsLimit.lift' this u hu     dsimp at d     dsimp [u] at hd     have : d ≫ (-g) = 0 := calc       d ≫ (-g) = d ≫ biprod.lift f (-g) ≫ biprod.snd := by rw [biprod.lift_snd]       _ = biprod.lift e (0 : R ⟶ Z) ≫ biprod.snd := by rw [← Category.assoc, hd]       _ = 0 := biprod.lift_snd _ _     have : d = 0 := (cancel_mono (-g)).1 (by simpa)     calc       e = biprod.lift e (0 : R ⟶ Z) ≫ biprod.fst := by rw [biprod.lift_fst]       _ = (d ≫ biprod.lift f (-g)) ≫ biprod.fst := by rw [← hd]       _ = (0 ≫ biprod.lift f (-g)) ≫ biprod.fst := by rw [this]       _ = 0 ≫ biprod.lift f (-g) ≫ biprod.fst := by rw [Category.assoc]       _ = 0 := zero_comp

CategoryTheory.NonPreadditiveAbelian.abe.fullDefinition: def abelian : Abelian C :=   {/- We need the `convert`s here because the instances we have are slightly different from the        instances we need: `HasKernels` depends on an instance of `HasZeroMorphisms`. In the        case of `NonPreadditiveAbelian`, this instance is an explicit argument. However, in the case        of `abelian`, the `HasZeroMorphisms` instance is derived from `Preadditive`. So we need to        transform an instance of "has kernels with NonPreadditiveAbelian.HasZeroMorphisms" to an        instance of "has kernels with NonPreadditiveAbelian.Preadditive.HasZeroMorphisms".        Luckily, we have a `subsingleton` instance for `HasZeroMorphisms`, so `convert` can        immediately close the goal it creates for the two instances of `HasZeroMorphisms`,        and the proof is complete. -/     NonPreadditiveAbelian.preadditive with     has_finite_products := by infer_instance     has_kernels := by convert (by infer_instance : Limits.HasKernels C)     has_cokernels := by convert (by infer_instance : Limits.HasCokernels C)     normalMonoOfMono := by       intro _ _ f _       convert normalMonoOfMono f     normalEpiOfEpi := by       intro _ _ f _       convert normalEpiOfEpi f }

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelIsoOfEq: If two morphisms are equal, their respective kernels are isomorphic in the context of the given category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.AbelianOfAdjunction.coima: This definition introduces an auxiliary isomorphism between the kernels of two morphisms involving cokernels in a preadditive category with a specific adjoint functor pair, under certain categorical conditions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.coimage: This definition identifies the coimage of a morphism in an abelian category as the cokernel of its kernel.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.image: This definition describes the abelian image of a morphism as the kernel of its cokernel within an abelian category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesLimits: This definition introduces the concept of a functor that preserves small limits by transforming limit cones from a diagram into limit cones in another category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.rightAdjointPr: This definition states that a right adjoint functor is guaranteed to preserve limits in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.ι: The morphism from the kernel of a morphism into the source of that morphism is defined in the context of categories with zero morphisms, under the assumption that a kernel exists for the given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelComparison: A morphism from the kernel of one object to the kernel of the image of that object under a functor is established, given that both the original and the functor preserve kernels.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.coimageIsoImage: This definition indicates that there exists a canonical isomorphism between the abelian coimage and the abelian image of a morphism in an abelian category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.PreservesKernel.is: This definition states that if a functor preserves the kernel of a morphism, then the object corresponding to the kernel of that morphism under the functor is isomorphic to the kernel of the image of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.image.ι: This definition represents the inclusion map from the image of a morphism to its codomain in an abelian category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.coimage.π: This definition describes the projection morphism from an object to its coimage in an abelian category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.symm: This definition states that the equivalence between two categories is symmetric, meaning that if one category is equivalent to another, then the second category is also equivalent to the first.

category_theory.abelian_of_adjunction.co.fullDefinition: def coimageIsoImage {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Abelian.coimage f ≅ Abelian.image f := by   have : PreservesLimits F := adj.rightAdjointPreservesLimits   calc     Abelian.coimage f ≅ cokernel (kernel.ι f) := Iso.refl _     _ ≅ G.obj (cokernel (F.map (kernel.ι f))) := (cokernelIso _ _ i adj _).symm     _ ≅ G.obj (cokernel (kernelComparison f F ≫ kernel.ι (F.map f))) :=       (G.mapIso (cokernelIsoOfEq (by simp)))     _ ≅ G.obj (cokernel (kernel.ι (F.map f))) := G.mapIso (cokernelEpiComp _ _)     _ ≅ G.obj (Abelian.coimage (F.map f)) := Iso.refl _     _ ≅ G.obj (Abelian.image (F.map f)) := G.mapIso (Abelian.coimageIsoImage _)     _ ≅ G.obj (kernel (cokernel.π (F.map f))) := Iso.refl _     _ ≅ kernel (G.map (cokernel.π (F.map f))) := PreservesKernel.iso _ _     _ ≅ kernel (cokernel.π f) := coimageIsoImageAux F G i adj f     _ ≅ Abelian.image f := Iso.refl _

CategoryTheory.abelianOfAdjunction.code:
CategoryTheory.abelianOfAdjunction.{v, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v, u₁} C] [Preadditive C] [HasFiniteProducts C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v, u₂} D] [Abelian D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] (G : D ⥤ C)
  [G.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] (i : F ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 C) (adj : G ⊣ F) : Abelian C
CategoryTheory.abelianOfAdjunction.comment:
If `C` is an additive category, `D` is an abelian category,
we have `F : C ⥤ D` `G : D ⥤ C` (both preserving zero morphisms),
`G` is left exact (that is, preserves finite limits),
and further we have `adj : G ⊣ F` and `i : F ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 C`,
then `C` is also abelian.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03A3>

explanatories.CategoryTheory.AbelianOfAdjunction.hasKe: This theorem establishes that if a preadditive category has an adjoint functor pair where the right adjoint preserves zero morphisms and finite limits, then the category has kernels.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.AbelianOfAdjunction.hasCo: This theorem establishes that if a preadditive category has an adjoint functor pair where the right adjoint preserves zero morphisms and there exists an isomorphism between their composition and the identity functor, then the category has cokernels.

CategoryTheory.abelianOfAdjunction.fullDefinition: def abelianOfAdjunction {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasFiniteProducts C]     {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v} D] [Abelian D] (F : C ⥤ D) [Functor.PreservesZeroMorphisms F]     (G : D ⥤ C) [Functor.PreservesZeroMorphisms G] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] (i : F ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 C)     (adj : G ⊣ F) : Abelian C := by   haveI := hasKernels F G i   haveI := hasCokernels F G i adj   have : ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y), IsIso (Abelian.coimageImageComparison f) := by     intro X Y f     rw [← coimageIsoImage_hom F G i adj f]     infer_instance   apply Abelian.ofCoimageImageComparisonIsIso
CategoryTheory.abelianOfAdjunction.description: This definition states that a preadditive category is abelian if it is connected to an abelian category through a pair of functors that preserve zero morphisms and finite limits, along with an adjunction between them.

CategoryTheory.Abelian.subobjectIsoSubob.comment:
In an abelian category, the subobjects and quotient objects of an object `X` are
order-isomorphic via taking kernels and cokernels.
Implemented here using subobjects in the opposite category,
since mathlib does not have a notion of quotient objects at the time of writing.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject: This definition describes a category consisting of isomorphism classes of monomorphisms that map into a specific object within a category.
explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.OrderIso.ofHomInv: This definition specifies that two order homomorphisms are inverses of each other if their compositions yield the identity order homomorphism, thus establishing an order isomorphism between the two preordered types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernelOrderHom: This definition establishes an order-reversing correspondence between the subobjects of a given object in a category and the quotient objects of its dual, specifically applicable when cokernels exist.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernelOrderHom: This definition establishes a mapping that reverses the order from the quotient objects of a given object to its subobjects within a category.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp: This defines a construction for the composition of two order-preserving functions that results in another order-preserving function.
explanatories.OrderHom.ext: This theorem demonstrates that if two order homomorphisms agree on their underlying functions, then they are equal as order homomorphisms.
explanatories.funext: If two functions yield the same output for every input, then those functions are considered equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.ind: This theorem states that if a property holds for all subobjects defined by monomorphisms into a specific object, then it also holds for any subobject of that object.
explanatories.OrderHom.comp_coe: This theorem establishes that the composition of two order homomorphisms is equivalent to the composition of their underlying functions.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.lift_mk: This theorem states that the function defined for subobjects constructed from monomorphisms maps directly to the value assigned to the morphism that represents the subobject.
explanatories.OrderHom.id_coe: This theorem states that the coercion of the identity order homomorphism is equal to the standard identity function, confirming their equivalence.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Subobject.mk_eq_mk_of_com: This theorem states that two subobjects are considered equal if there exists a commuting isomorphism between them that connects their respective arrows.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_inj: The theorem states that the operation for reversing the direction of morphisms in an opposite quiver is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.epiDesc: This definition states that in an abelian category, if a morphism becomes zero when precomposed with the kernel of an epimorphism, then it can be factored through that epimorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.condition: The composition of a morphism with its cokernel projection always results in zero when the morphism has a cokernel.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.ι: The morphism from the kernel of a morphism into the source of that morphism is defined in the context of categories with zero morphisms, under the assumption that a kernel exists for the given morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.desc: Any morphism that annihilates another morphism can be factored through the cokernel of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.condition: The inclusion morphism from the kernel of a morphism into its source maps to zero when composed with the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.cancel_epi: There is no theorem or definition provided in this input, so there is nothing to summarize.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.π: The morphism from the target of a given morphism in a category to its cokernel is defined, provided the cokernel exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.unop_comp: The theorem asserts that the operation for reversing the direction of the composition of two morphisms in an opposite category results in the composition of their individual reversals in the original order.
explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_op: The theorem establishes that applying the operation to reverse the direction of a morphism and then applying the operation to revert it returns the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.unop_id_op: The theorem demonstrates that the operation for reverting the direction of the identity morphism of the opposite object equals the identity morphism of the original object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.π_desc_as: For any morphism leading to a cokernel of another morphism, the composition of the corresponding morphisms commutes when a specific relation is satisfied involving the cokernel's projection and the morphism's descent.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.comp_epiDesc: This theorem establishes that for an epimorphism in an abelian category, the composition of the epimorphism with a specific canonical morphism equals the original morphism if a certain condition involving the kernel holds.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.unop_id: The theorem indicates that the operation for reversing the direction of the identity morphism in an opposite category yields the identity morphism of the original object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.π_desc: The projection from the cokernel to any morphism that annihilates the original morphism is equivalent to that morphism itself.
explanatories.Opposite.unop_op: This theorem establishes that applying the original mapping to the opposite of an element retrieves the original element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.monoLift: This definition states that in an abelian category, any morphism that vanishes when composed with the cokernel of a monomorphism can be factored through that monomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel.lift: A morphism that satisfies the condition of mapping to zero when composed with another morphism can be lifted to factor through the kernel of the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.cancel_mono: This theorem indicates a lack of any specified context, results, or definitions, rendering it effectively empty or undefined in its current form.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.assoc: This theorem establishes that the operation of composing morphisms within a category adheres to the property of associativity.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.image.fac: This theorem asserts that a morphism can be expressed as the composition of its canonical factor through the image and the inclusion map into the codomain within an abelian category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Abelian.monoLift_comp: This theorem asserts that if a morphism is monomorphic and another morphism factors through its cokernel, then a specific lift of the first morphism followed by the original morphism equals the second morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.Opposite.unop: This definition describes the canonical mapping from the opposite category of a type back to the original type.

CategoryTheory.Abelian.subobjectIsoSubob.fullDefinition: def subobjectIsoSubobjectOp [Abelian C] (X : C) : Subobject X ≃o (Subobject (op X))ᵒᵈ := by   refine OrderIso.ofHomInv (cokernelOrderHom X) (kernelOrderHom X) ?_ ?_   · change (cokernelOrderHom X).comp (kernelOrderHom X) = _     refine OrderHom.ext _ _ (funext (Subobject.ind _ ?_))     intro A f hf     dsimp only [OrderHom.comp_coe, Function.comp_apply, kernelOrderHom_coe, Subobject.lift_mk,       cokernelOrderHom_coe, OrderHom.id_coe, id]     refine Subobject.mk_eq_mk_of_comm _ _         ⟨?_, ?_, Quiver.Hom.unop_inj ?_, Quiver.Hom.unop_inj ?_⟩ ?_     · exact (Abelian.epiDesc f.unop _ (cokernel.condition (kernel.ι f.unop))).op     · exact (cokernel.desc _ _ (kernel.condition f.unop)).op     · rw [← cancel_epi (cokernel.π (kernel.ι f.unop))]       simp only [unop_comp, Quiver.Hom.unop_op, unop_id_op, cokernel.π_desc_assoc,         comp_epiDesc, Category.comp_id]     · simp only [← cancel_epi f.unop, unop_comp, Quiver.Hom.unop_op, unop_id, comp_epiDesc_assoc,         cokernel.π_desc, Category.comp_id]     · exact Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (by simp only [unop_comp, Quiver.Hom.unop_op, comp_epiDesc])   · change (kernelOrderHom X).comp (cokernelOrderHom X) = _     refine OrderHom.ext _ _ (funext (Subobject.ind _ ?_))     intro A f hf     dsimp only [OrderHom.comp_coe, Function.comp_apply, cokernelOrderHom_coe, Subobject.lift_mk,       kernelOrderHom_coe, OrderHom.id_coe, id, unop_op, Quiver.Hom.unop_op]     refine Subobject.mk_eq_mk_of_comm _ _ ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ ?_     · exact Abelian.monoLift f _ (kernel.condition (cokernel.π f))     · exact kernel.lift _ _ (cokernel.condition f)     · simp only [← cancel_mono (kernel.ι (cokernel.π f)), Category.assoc, image.fac, monoLift_comp,         Category.id_comp]     · simp only [← cancel_mono f, Category.assoc, monoLift_comp, image.fac, Category.id_comp]     · simp only [monoLift_comp]

explanatories.Quiver.Hom.unop_op: The theorem establishes that applying the operation to reverse the direction of a morphism and then applying the operation to revert it returns the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.unop_comp: The theorem asserts that the operation for reversing the direction of the composition of two morphisms in an opposite category results in the composition of their individual reversals in the original order.

explanatories.Opposite.op: This theorem establishes the canonical mapping from an original type to its opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.op: This definition introduces the concept of the opposite isomorphism, which associates an isomorphism between two objects in a category with an isomorphism between their opposites.
explanatories.Opposite.unop_op: This theorem establishes that applying the original mapping to the opposite of an element retrieves the original element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Iso.unop: This definition describes a method for retrieving an isomorphism in the original category from an isomorphism that exists in the opposite category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.image.ι: This definition describes the morphism that includes the image of a morphism as it maps into the target of that morphism.

  pseudoApply f p = pseudoApply g q → ∃ s, pseudoApply (pullback.fst f g) s = p ∧ pseudoApply (pullback.snd f g) s = q
CategoryTheory.Abelian.Pseudoelement.pse.comment:
If `f : P ⟶ R` and `g : Q ⟶ R` are morphisms and `p : P` and `q : Q` are pseudoelements such
that `f p = g q`, then there is some `s : pullback f g` such that `fst s = p` and `snd s = q`.

Remark: Borceux claims that `s` is unique, but this is false. See
`Counterexamples/Pseudoelement.lean` for details.

The class of morphisms in an abelian category that are epimorphisms

CategoryTheory.Abelian.epiWithInjectiveK.fullDefinition: def epiWithInjectiveKernel : MorphismProperty C :=   fun _ _ f => Epi f ∧ Injective (kernel f)

CategoryTheory.Abelian.epiWithInjectiveK.code:
CategoryTheory.Abelian.epiWithInjectiveKernel_iff.{u_1, u_2} {C : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} C] [Abelian C]
  {X Y : C} (g : X ⟶ Y) :
  epiWithInjectiveKernel g ↔
    ∃ I, ∃ (_ : Injective I), ∃ f, ∃ (w : f ≫ g = 0), Nonempty (ShortComplex.mk f g w).Splitting
CategoryTheory.Abelian.epiWithInjectiveK.comment:
A morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` is epi with an injective kernel iff there exists a morphism
`f : I ⟶ X` with `I` injective such that `f ≫ g = 0` and
the short complex `I ⟶ X ⟶ Y` has a splitting.

explanatories.HomotopyCategory: The homotopy category consists of chain complexes shaped by a specific structure, where chain maps are considered equivalent if they are homotopic to each other.
explanatories.ComplexShape.down: This definition specifies a complex shape suitable for homology, where the morphism exists only between consecutive components.
explanatories.HomotopyCategory.quotient: The quotient functor maps chain complexes to their equivalence classes in the homotopy category, identifying complexes that are related by homotopies.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id: A functor preserves identity morphisms by ensuring that the image of an identity morphism in one category is the identity morphism of the corresponding object in the mapped category.
explanatories.HomotopyCategory.eq_of_homotopy: This theorem establishes that if two chain maps between homological complexes are homotopic, their corresponding images in the quotient category are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_comp: A functor maintains the composition of morphisms when mapping them from one category to another.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.g: This definition specifies the second morphism in a short complex within a category that accommodates zero morphisms.

CategoryTheory.projectiveResolutions.fullDefinition: def projectiveResolutions : C ⥤ HomotopyCategory C (ComplexShape.down ℕ) where   obj X := (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj (projectiveResolution X).complex   map f := (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).map (ProjectiveResolution.lift f _ _)   map_id X := by     rw [← (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).map_id]     apply HomotopyCategory.eq_of_homotopy     apply ProjectiveResolution.liftIdHomotopy   map_comp f g := by     rw [← (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).map_comp]     apply HomotopyCategory.eq_of_homotopy     apply ProjectiveResolution.liftCompHomotopy
CategoryTheory.projectiveResolutions.description: This definition establishes a functor that assigns to each object in an abelian category its projective resolution, mapping into the homotopy category of down-graded chain complexes.

When `F : C ⥤ D` is an additive functor, this is
the functor `C ⥤ HomotopyCategory D (ComplexShape.up ℕ)` which
sends `X : C` to `F` applied to an injective resolution of `X`.

CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isoRi.fullDefinition: noncomputable def InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedToHomotopyCategoryObj {X : C}     (I : InjectiveResolution X) (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] :     F.rightDerivedToHomotopyCategory.obj X ≅       (F.mapHomologicalComplex _ ⋙ HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj I.cocomplex :=   (F.mapHomotopyCategory _).mapIso I.iso ≪≫     (F.mapHomotopyCategoryFactors _).app I.cocomplex

CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isoRi.code:
CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedToHomotopyCategoryObj_hom_naturality_assoc.{v, u, u_1, u_2}
  {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] {D : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} D] [Abelian C] [HasInjectiveResolutions C]
  [Abelian D] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (I : InjectiveResolution X) (J : InjectiveResolution Y)
  (φ : I.cocomplex ⟶ J.cocomplex) (comm : I.ι.f 0 ≫ φ.f 0 = f ≫ J.ι.f 0) (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive]
  {Z : HomotopyCategory D (ComplexShape.up ℕ)}
  (h :
    (HomotopyCategory.quotient D (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj J.cocomplex) ⟶
      Z) :
  F.rightDerivedToHomotopyCategory.map f ≫ (J.isoRightDerivedToHomotopyCategoryObj F).hom ≫ h =
    (I.isoRightDerivedToHomotopyCategoryObj F).hom ≫
      (HomotopyCategory.quotient D (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map φ) ≫ h

CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDifferentialOb.fullDefinition: def mapDifferentialObject (F : C ⥤ D)     (η : (shiftFunctor C (1 : S)).comp F ⟶ F.comp (shiftFunctor D (1 : S)))     (hF : ∀ c c', F.map (0 : c ⟶ c') = 0) : DifferentialObject S C ⥤ DifferentialObject S D where   obj X :=     { obj := F.obj X.obj       d := F.map X.d ≫ η.app X.obj       d_squared := by         rw [Functor.map_comp, ← Functor.comp_map F (shiftFunctor D (1 : S))]         slice_lhs 2 3 => rw [← η.naturality X.d]         rw [Functor.comp_map]         slice_lhs 1 2 => rw [← F.map_comp, X.d_squared, hF]         rw [zero_comp, zero_comp] }   map f :=     { f := F.map f.f       comm := by         dsimp         slice_lhs 2 3 => rw [← Functor.comp_map F (shiftFunctor D (1 : S)), ← η.naturality f.f]         slice_lhs 1 2 => rw [Functor.comp_map, ← F.map_comp, f.comm, F.map_comp]         rw [Category.assoc] }   map_id := by intros; ext; simp [autoParam]   map_comp := by intros; ext; simp [autoParam]

explanatories.CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor: This definition describes a shift functor that acts as an autoequivalence on a category, moving objects and morphisms upward by an element from an additive monoid.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.shiftFunctor.description: This theorem states that applying the shift functor to a graded object results in the evaluation of the original object at a translated position determined by the shift value and the integer input.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObjectWithShift: This definition introduces a type that represents β-graded objects in a category while incorporating a shift functor defined by translation through a specified element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor: This definition describes a shift functor that acts as an autoequivalence on a category, moving objects and morphisms upward by an element from an additive monoid.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map: This definition constructs a morphism between the coproducts of two families of objects in a category based on a specified collection of morphisms between corresponding objects in each family.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.shiftFunctor.description: This theorem establishes that the application of a shift functor to a morphism between shifted graded objects translates the input by adding an integer multiple of a specified shift element to the argument of the morphism.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.zero_apply.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.zero_apply.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] (β : Type w)
  (X Y : GradedObject β C) (b : β) : 0 b = 0
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.zero_apply.description: This theorem states that the zero morphism applied to any element of a graded object defined over a specified type results in the zero morphism itself.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroMorph.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroMorphisms.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroMorphisms C]
  (β : Type w) : HasZeroMorphisms (GradedObject β C)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroMorph.fullDefinition: instance hasZeroMorphisms [HasZeroMorphisms C] (β : Type w) :     HasZeroMorphisms.{max w v} (GradedObject β C) where
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroMorph.description: This definition asserts that if a category has zero morphisms, then the corresponding graded object in that category also possesses zero morphisms.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroObjec.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroObject.{w, v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [HasZeroObject C]
  [HasZeroMorphisms C] (β : Type w) : HasZeroObject (GradedObject β C)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroObjec.fullDefinition: instance hasZeroObject [HasZeroObject C] [HasZeroMorphisms C] (β : Type w) :     HasZeroObject.{max w v} (GradedObject β C) := by   refine ⟨⟨fun _ => 0, fun X => ⟨⟨⟨fun b => 0⟩, fun f => ?_⟩⟩, fun X =>     ⟨⟨⟨fun b => 0⟩, fun f => ?_⟩⟩⟩⟩ <;> aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasZeroObjec.description: This definition asserts that if a category has a zero object and zero morphisms, then the associated graded objects also possess a zero object structure.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.total.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.total.{v, u} (β : Type) (C : Type u) [Category.{v, u} C] [HasCoproducts C] :
  GradedObject β C ⥤ C
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.total.comment: The total object of a graded object is the coproduct of the graded components.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Sigma.map: This definition constructs a morphism between the coproducts of two families of objects in a category based on a specified collection of morphisms between corresponding objects in each family.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.total.fullDefinition: noncomputable def total : GradedObject β C ⥤ C where   obj X := ∐ fun i : β => X i   map f := Limits.Sigma.map fun i => f i
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.total.description: This definition introduces a functor that associates a graded object with its total object, represented as the coproduct of its graded components in a category.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} {C : Type u_4}
  (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) (j : J) (i : ↑(p ⁻¹' {j})) : C
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun.comment:
If `X : GradedObject I C` and `p : I → J`, `X.mapObjFun p j` is the family of objects `X i`
for `i : I` such that `p i = j`.
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun.fullDefinition: abbrev mapObjFun (j : J) (i : p ⁻¹' {j}) : C := X i
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun.description: This definition describes a construction that retrieves the specific objects from a graded object based on a mapping function and a particular index in the target set.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} {C : Type u_4}
  [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) : Prop
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap.comment:
Given `X : GradedObject I C` and `p : I → J`, `X.HasMap p` is the condition that
for all `j : J`, the coproduct of all `X i` such `p i = j` exists.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoproduct: This definition characterizes the existence of a coproduct in a category as the presence of a colimit for a functor derived from a discrete type mapping to that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun: This definition describes a construction that retrieves the specific objects from a graded object based on a mapping function and a particular index in the target set.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap.fullDefinition: abbrev HasMap : Prop := ∀ (j : J), HasCoproduct (X.mapObjFun p j)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap.description: This definition specifies a condition for a graded object in a category to have a mapping function that ensures the existence of coproducts for the elements indexed by the image of that mapping.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObj.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObj.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} {C : Type u_4}
  [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) [X.HasMap p] : GradedObject J C
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObj.comment:
Given `X : GradedObject I C` and `p : I → J`, `X.mapObj p` is the graded object by `J`
which in degree `j` consists of the coproduct of the `X i` such that `p i = j`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun: This definition describes a construction that retrieves the specific objects from a graded object based on a mapping function and a particular index in the target set.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObj.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mapObj : GradedObject J C := fun j => ∐ (X.mapObjFun p j)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObj.description: This definition describes a construction that produces a new graded object indexed by one type from an existing graded object indexed by another type, mapping elements according to a specified function.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjFun.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} {C : Type u_4}
  [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) (j : J) : Type (max (max u_4 u_5) u_1)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.comment:
Given `X : GradedObject I C`, `p : I → J` and `j : J`,
`CofanMapObjFun X p j` is the type `Cofan (X.mapObjFun p j)`. The point object of
such colimits cofans are isomorphic to `X.mapObj p j`, see `CofanMapObjFun.iso`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObjFun: This definition describes a construction that retrieves the specific objects from a graded object based on a mapping function and a particular index in the target set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan: This definition describes a cofan as a collection of morphisms from a family of objects indexed by a type to a single object.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.fullDefinition: abbrev CofanMapObjFun (j : J) : Type _ := Cofan (X.mapObjFun p j)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.description: This definition introduces a type representing the colimit cofan objects associated with a graded object, mapping through a specified function to another index type.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.pt: This definition specifies the specific object in a category that serves as the cocone point for a given cocone associated with a functor.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.fullDefinition: def CofanMapObjFun.mk (j : J) (pt : C) (ι' : ∀ (i : I) (_ : p i = j), X i ⟶ pt) :     CofanMapObjFun X p j :=   Cofan.mk pt (fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => ι' i hi)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.description: This definition introduces a constructor for a specific type of functor that relates components of a graded object to a target object based on a given mapping and index.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObj.comment:
The canonical inclusion `X i ⟶ X.mapObj p j` when `i : I` and `j : J` are such

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObj.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ιMapObj (i : I) (j : J) (hij : p i = j) : X i ⟶ X.mapObj p j :=   Sigma.ι (X.mapObjFun p j) ⟨i, hij⟩
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObj.description: This definition specifies a morphism that represents the inclusion of an element from a graded object into the image of that object under a mapping defined by a function, given that the function's output at that element matches a specified target.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObj.code:

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCofanMapObj.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} {C : Type u_4}
  [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) [X.HasMap p] (j : J) : IsColimit (X.cofanMapObj p j)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.comment:
Given `X : GradedObject I C`, `p : I → J` and `j : J`, `X.mapObj p j` satisfies
the universal property of the coproduct of those `X i` such that `p i = j`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObj: This definition establishes a function that creates a cofan from a graded object based on a mapping and an index, corresponding to the coproduct decomposition associated with that mapping.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.fullDefinition: noncomputable def isColimitCofanMapObj (j : J) : IsColimit (X.cofanMapObj p j) :=   colimit.isColimit _
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.description: This definition asserts that a specific cofan object associated with a graded object and a mapping satisfies the universal property of a coproduct, ensuring it is a colimit within the category.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.descMapObj.comment:
This is the morphism `X.mapObj p j ⟶ A` constructed from a family of
morphisms `X i ⟶ A` for all `i : I` such that `p i = j`.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.descMapObj.fullDefinition: noncomputable def descMapObj {A : C} {j : J} (φ : ∀ (i : I) (_ : p i = j), X i ⟶ A) :     X.mapObj p j ⟶ A :=   Cofan.IsColimit.desc (X.isColimitCofanMapObj p j) (fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => φ i hi)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.descMapObj.description: This definition constructs a morphism from a specific object associated with a graded object to another object based on a family of morphisms that apply when the mapping from the index type satisfies a particular condition.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.comment:
If `c : CofanMapObjFun X p j` is a colimit cofan, this is the induced
isomorphism `c.pt ≅ X.mapObj p j`.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.fullDefinition: noncomputable def iso : c.pt ≅ X.mapObj p j :=   IsColimit.coconePointUniqueUpToIso hc (X.isColimitCofanMapObj p j)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the point of a colimit cofan associated with a graded object and a newly constructed object derived from the same graded object using a specified mapping.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapMap.comment:
The canonical morphism of `J`-graded objects `X.mapObj p ⟶ Y.mapObj p` induced by
a morphism `X ⟶ Y` of `I`-graded objects and a map `p : I → J`.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapMap.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mapMap : X.mapObj p ⟶ Y.mapObj p := fun j =>   X.descMapObj p (fun i hi => φ i ≫ Y.ιMapObj p i j hi)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapMap.description: This definition describes the canonical morphism between two newly constructed graded objects, induced by a morphism between their original graded structures and a specified mapping from one indexing type to another.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjC.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjComp.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3}
  {C : Type u_4} [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) (q : J → K) (r : I → K)
  (hpqr : ∀ (i : I), q (p i) = r i) (k : K) (c : (j : J) → q j = k → X.CofanMapObjFun p j)
  (c' : Cofan fun j => (c ↑j ⋯).pt) : X.CofanMapObjFun r k
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjC.comment:
Given maps `p : I → J`, `q : J → K` and `r : I → K` such that `q.comp p = r`,
`X : GradedObject I C`, `k : K`, the datum of cofans `X.CofanMapObjFun p j` for all
`j : J` and of a cofan for all the points of these cofans, this is a cofan of
type `X.CofanMapObjFun r k`, which is a colimit (see `isColimitCofanMapObjComp`) if the
given cofans are.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjC.fullDefinition: def cofanMapObjComp : X.CofanMapObjFun r k :=   CofanMapObjFun.mk _ _ _ c'.pt (fun i hi =>     (c (p i) (by rw [hpqr, hi])).inj ⟨i, rfl⟩ ≫ c'.inj (⟨p i, by       rw [Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_singleton_iff, hpqr, hi]⟩))
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjC.description: This definition describes a construction that yields a cofan for a graded object, connecting three different mappings under a specific condition, resulting in a cofan of a specified type that is a colimit if the constituent cofans are colimits.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCofanMapObjComp.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2}
  {K : Type u_3} {C : Type u_4} [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) (q : J → K) (r : I → K)
  (hpqr : ∀ (i : I), q (p i) = r i) (k : K) (c : (j : J) → q j = k → X.CofanMapObjFun p j)
  (hc : (j : J) → (hj : q j = k) → IsColimit (c j hj)) (c' : Cofan fun j => (c ↑j ⋯).pt) (hc' : IsColimit c') :
  IsColimit (X.cofanMapObjComp p q r hpqr k c c')
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.comment:
Given maps `p : I → J`, `q : J → K` and `r : I → K` such that `q.comp p = r`,
`X : GradedObject I C`, `k : K`, the cofan constructed by `cofanMapObjComp` is a colimit.
In other words, if we have, for all `j : J` such that `hj : q j = k`,
a colimit cofan `c j hj` which computes the coproduct of the `X i` such that `p i = j`,
and also a colimit cofan which computes the coproduct of the points of these `c j hj`, then
the point of this latter cofan computes the coproduct of the `X i` such that `r i = k`.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.fullDefinition: def isColimitCofanMapObjComp :     IsColimit (cofanMapObjComp X p q r hpqr k c c') :=   mkCofanColimit _     (fun s => Cofan.IsColimit.desc hc'       (fun ⟨j, (hj : q j = k)⟩ => Cofan.IsColimit.desc (hc j hj)         (fun ⟨i, (hi : p i = j)⟩ => s.inj ⟨i, by           simp only [Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_singleton_iff, ← hpqr, hi, hj]⟩)))     (fun s ⟨i, (hi : r i = k)⟩ => by simp)     (fun s m hm => by       apply Cofan.IsColimit.hom_ext hc'       rintro ⟨j, rfl : q j = k⟩       apply Cofan.IsColimit.hom_ext (hc j rfl)       rintro ⟨i, rfl : p i = j⟩       dsimp       rw [Cofan.IsColimit.fac, Cofan.IsColimit.fac, ← hm]       dsimp       rw [assoc])
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.description: This definition states that under specific mappings between types and given a graded object, a constructed cofan is a colimit if certain conditions regarding equivalences and colimits of associated structures are satisfied.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObjOrZer.comment: The canonical inclusion `X i ⟶ X.mapObj p j` when `p i = j`, the zero morphism otherwise.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObj: This definition describes a construction that produces a new graded object indexed by one type from an existing graded object indexed by another type, mapping elements according to a specified function.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObjOrZer.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ιMapObjOrZero : X i ⟶ X.mapObj p j :=   if h : p i = j     then X.ιMapObj p i j h     else 0
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObjOrZer.description: This definition specifies a morphism from an object in a graded object to the mapped object corresponding to a specified function if the mapping holds, and assigns the zero morphism otherwise.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap: This definition specifies a condition for a graded object in a category to have a mapping function that ensures the existence of coproducts for the elements indexed by the image of that mapping.
explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObjOrZer.description: This theorem proves that a certain construction of maps relating graded objects with zero morphisms is equal to the standard construction of maps when a specific condition on the indices is satisfied.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap: This definition specifies a condition for a graded object in a category to have a mapping function that ensures the existence of coproducts for the elements indexed by the image of that mapping.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObj: This definition specifies a morphism that represents the inclusion of an element from a graded object into the image of that object under a mapping defined by a function, given that the function's output at that element matches a specified target.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapMap: This definition describes the canonical morphism between two newly constructed graded objects, induced by a morphism between their original graded structures and a specified mapping from one indexing type to another.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ι_mapMap.description: This theorem asserts that under specific conditions involving a morphism between graded objects and a mapping from one index set to another, a certain diagram involving the indexed objects and their mappings commutes correctly.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapObjOrZer.description: This theorem establishes that if a mapping from one index type to another produces different values for given indices, then the corresponding component of the graded object's mapping is the zero morphism.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.comment:
Given a bifunctor `F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃` and types `I` and `J`, this is the obvious
functor `GradedObject I C₁ ⥤ GradedObject J C₂ ⥤ GradedObject (I × J) C₃`.
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.fullDefinition: def mapBifunctor (I J : Type*) :     GradedObject I C₁ ⥤ GradedObject J C₂ ⥤ GradedObject (I × J) C₃ where   obj X :=     { obj := fun Y ij => (F.obj (X ij.1)).obj (Y ij.2)       map := fun φ ij => (F.obj (X ij.1)).map (φ ij.2) }   map φ :=     { app := fun Y ij => (F.map (φ ij.1)).app (Y ij.2) }
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.description: This definition describes a functor that maps graded objects indexed by two types to a new graded object indexed by the Cartesian product of those types, utilizing a given bifunctor between categories.
