  {C₂ : Type u_2} {C₃ : Type u_3} [Category.{u_7, u_1} C₁] [Category.{u_8, u_2} C₂] [Category.{u_9, u_3} C₃]
  (F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃) {I : Type u_4} {J : Type u_5} {K : Type u_6} (p : I × J → K) (X : GradedObject I C₁)
  (Y : GradedObject J C₂) [(((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y).HasMap p] : GradedObject K C₃
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.comment:
Given a bifunctor `F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃`, graded objects `X : GradedObject I C₁` and
 `Y : GradedObject J C₂` and a map `p : I × J → K`, this is the `K`-graded object sending
`k` to the coproduct of `(F.obj (X i)).obj (Y j)` for `p ⟨i, j⟩ = k`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasMap: This definition specifies a condition for a graded object in a category to have a mapping function that ensures the existence of coproducts for the elements indexed by the image of that mapping.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapObj: This definition describes a construction that produces a new graded object indexed by one type from an existing graded object indexed by another type, mapping elements according to a specified function.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mapBifunctorMapObj (X : GradedObject I C₁) (Y : GradedObject J C₂)   [HasMap (((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y) p] : GradedObject K C₃ :=     (((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y).mapObj p
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.description: This definition specifies a graded object that combines two existing graded objects using a bifunctor and a provided mapping from their indexing types to a new index type.

  (F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃) {I : Type u_4} {J : Type u_5} {K : Type u_6} (p : I × J → K) (X : GradedObject I C₁)
  (Y : GradedObject J C₂) [(((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y).HasMap p] (i : I) (j : J) (k : K) (h : p (i, j) = k) :
  (F.obj (X i)).obj (Y j) ⟶ mapBifunctorMapObj F p X Y k

The inclusion of `(F.obj (X i)).obj (Y j)` in `mapBifunctorMapObj F p X Y k`

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapBifuncto.fullDefinition: noncomputable def ιMapBifunctorMapObj     (X : GradedObject I C₁) (Y : GradedObject J C₂)     [HasMap (((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y) p]     (i : I) (j : J) (k : K) (h : p ⟨i, j⟩ = k) :     (F.obj (X i)).obj (Y j) ⟶ mapBifunctorMapObj F p X Y k :=   (((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y).ιMapObj p ⟨i, j⟩ k h

The maps `mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₁ Y₁ ⟶ mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₂ Y₂` which express
the functoriality of `mapBifunctorMapObj`, see `mapBifunctorMap`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapMap: This definition describes the canonical morphism between two newly constructed graded objects, induced by a morphism between their original graded structures and a specified mapping from one indexing type to another.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mapBifunctorMapMap {X₁ X₂ : GradedObject I C₁} (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂)     {Y₁ Y₂ : GradedObject J C₂} (g : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂)     [HasMap (((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X₁).obj Y₁) p]     [HasMap (((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X₂).obj Y₂) p] :     mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₁ Y₁ ⟶ mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₂ Y₂ :=   GradedObject.mapMap (((mapBifunctor F I J).map f).app Y₁ ≫     ((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X₂).map g) p
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.description: This definition establishes a morphism that demonstrates the functoriality of a construction combining two graded objects via a bifunctor, connecting the images of their respective mappings.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.descMapObj: This definition constructs a morphism from a specific object associated with a graded object to another object based on a family of morphisms that apply when the mapping from the index type satisfies a particular condition.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mapBifunctorMapObjDesc     {X : GradedObject I C₁} {Y : GradedObject J C₂} {A : C₃} {k : K}     [HasMap (((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y) p]     (f : ∀ (i : I) (j : J) (_ : p ⟨i, j⟩ = k), (F.obj (X i)).obj (Y j) ⟶ A) :     mapBifunctorMapObj F p X Y k ⟶ A :=   descMapObj _ _ (fun ⟨i, j⟩ hij => f i j hij)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.description: This definition introduces a morphism from a constructed graded object to another object, generated by a function that relates pairs of indices from the original graded objects through a specified mapping.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.comment:
The isomorphism `mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₁ Y₁ ≅ mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₂ Y₂`
induced by isomorphisms `X₁ ≅ X₂` and `Y₁ ≅ Y₂`.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.fullDefinition: noncomputable def mapBifunctorMapMapIso (e : X₁ ≅ X₂) (e' : Y₁ ≅ Y₂) :     mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₁ Y₁ ≅ mapBifunctorMapObj F p X₂ Y₂ where   hom := mapBifunctorMapMap F p e.hom e'.hom   inv := mapBifunctorMapMap F p e.inv e'.inv   hom_inv_id := by ext; simp   inv_hom_id := by ext; simp
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.description: This definition describes an isomorphism between two constructions that combine graded objects using a bifunctor, established based on isomorphisms of the original graded objects involved.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.single.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {J : Type u_1} {C : Type u_2} [Category.{u_3, u_2} C] [HasInitial C]
  [DecidableEq J] (j : J) : C ⥤ GradedObject J C
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.single.comment:
The functor which sends `X : C` to the graded object which is `X` in degree `j`
and the initial object in other degrees.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToHom: An equality between two objects in a category induces a morphism from one object to the other.
explanatories.if_pos: If a condition is true, then the result of a conditional expression evaluating that condition will equal the first option.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.if_neg: If a condition is proven to be false, then the result of a conditional expression will yield the alternative value.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.single.fullDefinition: noncomputable def single (j : J) : C ⥤ GradedObject J C where   obj X i := if i = j then X else ⊥_ C   map {X₁ X₂} f i :=     if h : i = j then eqToHom (if_pos h) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (if_pos h).symm     else eqToHom (by dsimp; rw [if_neg h, if_neg h])
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.single.description: This definition describes a functor that maps objects from a category to a graded object where a specific object is placed at one degree and the remaining degrees are filled with the initial object of the category.

explanatories.if_pos: If a condition is true, then the result of a conditional expression evaluating that condition will equal the first option.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.singleObjApp.fullDefinition: noncomputable def singleObjApplyIsoOfEq (j : J) (X : C) (i : J) (h : i = j) :     (single j).obj X i ≅ X := eqToIso (if_pos h)
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.singleObjApp.description: This definition establishes a canonical isomorphism between an object in a graded structure and the original object when the degree of the graded structure matches a specified value.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.singleObjApp.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev singleObjApplyIso (j : J) (X : C) :     (single j).obj X j ≅ X := singleObjApplyIsoOfEq j X j rfl

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapTrifuncto.fullDefinition: def mapTrifunctorObj {I₁ : Type*} (X₁ : GradedObject I₁ C₁) (I₂ I₃ : Type*) :     GradedObject I₂ C₂ ⥤ GradedObject I₃ C₃ ⥤ GradedObject (I₁ × I₂ × I₃) C₄ where   obj X₂ :=     { obj := fun X₃ x => ((F.obj (X₁ x.1)).obj (X₂ x.2.1)).obj (X₃ x.2.2)       map := fun {X₃ Y₃} φ x => ((F.obj (X₁ x.1)).obj (X₂ x.2.1)).map (φ x.2.2) }   map {X₂ Y₂} φ :=     { app := fun X₃ x => ((F.obj (X₁ x.1)).map (φ x.2.1)).app (X₃ x.2.2) }

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapTrifuncto.fullDefinition: def mapTrifunctor (I₁ I₂ I₃ : Type*) :     GradedObject I₁ C₁ ⥤ GradedObject I₂ C₂ ⥤ GradedObject I₃ C₃ ⥤       GradedObject (I₁ × I₂ × I₃) C₄ where   obj X₁ := mapTrifunctorObj F X₁ I₂ I₃   map {X₁ Y₁} φ :=     { app := fun X₂ =>         { app := fun X₃ x => ((F.map (φ x.1)).app (X₂ x.2.1)).app (X₃ x.2.2) }       naturality := fun {X₂ Y₂} ψ => by         ext X₃ x         dsimp         simp only [← NatTrans.comp_app]         congr 1         rw [NatTrans.naturality] }

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapTrifuncto.fullDefinition: def mapTrifunctorMapNatTrans (α : F ⟶ F') (I₁ I₂ I₃ : Type*) :     mapTrifunctor F I₁ I₂ I₃ ⟶ mapTrifunctor F' I₁ I₂ I₃ where   app X₁ :=     { app := fun X₂ =>         { app := fun X₃ i => ((α.app _).app _).app _ }       naturality := fun {X₂ Y₂} φ => by         ext X₃ ⟨i₁, i₂, i₃⟩         dsimp         simp only [← NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.naturality] }   naturality := fun {X₁ Y₁} φ => by     ext X₂ X₃ ⟨i₁, i₂, i₃⟩     dsimp     simp only [← NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.naturality]

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapTrifuncto.comment:
Given a trifunctor `F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₃`, graded objects `X₁ : GradedObject I₁ C₁`,

explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapTrifuncto: This definition establishes a functor that maps graded objects across three categories and combines them into a new graded object that reflects the interactions between the original objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.functor: This definition asserts that any function mapping from a discrete type to a category yields a functor between the discrete category and that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor: This definition describes a functor that maps graded objects indexed by two types to a new graded object indexed by the Cartesian product of those types, utilizing a given bifunctor between categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition describes a mapping from a product of two index types to a specific indexed type defined within the structure of a bifunctor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor: This definition specifies a graded object that combines two existing graded objects using a bifunctor and a provided mapping from their indexing types to a new index type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition specifies a mapping from a combination of two index types and a third type to a specific output type within the context of a bifunctor.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This theorem confirms that a specific bilinear mapping is consistent by showing that the value obtained from applying certain maps to a tuple is equal to the result of the original mapping defined on that tuple.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF: This definition introduces a type representing the colimit cofan objects associated with a graded object, mapping through a specified function to another index type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObj: This definition establishes a function that creates a cofan from a graded object based on a mapping and an index, corresponding to the coproduct decomposition associated with that mapping.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof: This definition asserts that a specific cofan object associated with a graded object and a mapping satisfies the universal property of a coproduct, ensuring it is a colimit within the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCocone: This definition states that applying a functor to a cocone results in a new cocone formed over the composition of the original functor with the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitOfPreserv: This definition states that if a functor preserves colimits and a cocone is a colimit in the source category, then the mapped cocone in the target category is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.precompose: This definition establishes a functor that allows for the transformation of a cocone over one functor into a corresponding cocone over another functor via a natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.whiskering: This definition establishes that whiskering by an equivalence between two categories results in an equivalence between the categories of cocones associated with a functor and the composed functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivalence: This definition establishes an equivalence between two discrete categories by promoting a type-level equivalence between their underlying types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor: This definition introduces a functor that represents one direction of an equivalence between two categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso: This definition shows that for functors from a discrete category, a natural isomorphism is characterized by a set of isomorphisms since the naturality conditions are trivially satisfied.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToIso: An equality between two objects in a category corresponds to an isomorphism between those objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.precompo: This definition establishes an equivalence between the condition of a cocone transformed by a natural isomorphism being a colimit and the original cocone being a colimit.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.whiskerE: This definition establishes a correspondence between colimit cocones in different categories, indicating that one is a colimit if and only if the whiskered cocone in the target category is also a colimit under the equivalence of categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofIsoCol: This definition states that if a cocone is a colimit and there is an isomorphism between two cocones, then the second cocone is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof: This definition states that under specific mappings between types and given a graded object, a constructed cofan is a colimit if certain conditions regarding equivalences and colimits of associated structures are satisfied.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.inj: This definition retrieves the morphism from a specific object in a family to the designated point in the cofan associated with that family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition introduces an auxiliary type used within the context of a specific bifunctor's index data structure.

bifunctors can be computed as a composition of the actions of these two bifunctors.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.categoryOfGr.description: This theorem states that in the category of graded objects, the composition of morphisms can be evaluated at each index from the grading, ensuring that the resulting morphism at that index equals the composition of the morphisms at that index.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.comapEq.description: This definition asserts that if two functions are propositionally equal, then their corresponding pullbacks in the category result in isomorphic objects.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.comapEquiv.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between graded objects indexed by two types, given a corresponding equivalence between those types.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.hasShift.fullDefinition: instance hasShift {β : Type*} [AddCommGroup β] (s : β) : HasShift (GradedObjectWithShift s C) ℤ :=   hasShiftMk _ _     { F := fun n => comap C fun b : β => b + n • s       zero := comapEq C (by aesop_cat) ≪≫ Pi.comapId β fun _ => C       add := fun m n => comapEq C (by ext; dsimp; rw [add_comm m n, add_zsmul, add_assoc]) ≪≫           (Pi.comapComp _ _ _).symm }

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.shiftFunctor.description: This theorem establishes that the application of a shift functor to a morphism between shifted graded objects translates the input by adding an integer multiple of a specified shift element to the argument of the morphism.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjComp.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2} {K : Type u_3}
  {C : Type u_4} [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) (q : J → K) (r : I → K)
  (hpqr : ∀ (i : I), q (p i) = r i) (k : K) (c : (j : J) → q j = k → X.CofanMapObjFun p j)
  (c' : Cofan fun j => (c ↑j ⋯).pt) : X.CofanMapObjFun r k
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjC.comment:
Given maps `p : I → J`, `q : J → K` and `r : I → K` such that `q.comp p = r`,
`X : GradedObject I C`, `k : K`, the datum of cofans `X.CofanMapObjFun p j` for all
`j : J` and of a cofan for all the points of these cofans, this is a cofan of
type `X.CofanMapObjFun r k`, which is a colimit (see `isColimitCofanMapObjComp`) if the
given cofans are.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjC.fullDefinition: def cofanMapObjComp : X.CofanMapObjFun r k :=   CofanMapObjFun.mk _ _ _ c'.pt (fun i hi =>     (c (p i) (by rw [hpqr, hi])).inj ⟨i, rfl⟩ ≫ c'.inj (⟨p i, by       rw [Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_singleton_iff, hpqr, hi]⟩))
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObjC.description: This definition describes a construction that yields a cofan for a graded object, connecting three different mappings under a specific condition, resulting in a cofan of a specified type that is a colimit if the constituent cofans are colimits.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCofanMapObjComp.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {I : Type u_1} {J : Type u_2}
  {K : Type u_3} {C : Type u_4} [Category.{u_5, u_4} C] (X : GradedObject I C) (p : I → J) (q : J → K) (r : I → K)
  (hpqr : ∀ (i : I), q (p i) = r i) (k : K) (c : (j : J) → q j = k → X.CofanMapObjFun p j)
  (hc : (j : J) → (hj : q j = k) → IsColimit (c j hj)) (c' : Cofan fun j => (c ↑j ⋯).pt) (hc' : IsColimit c') :
  IsColimit (X.cofanMapObjComp p q r hpqr k c c')
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.comment:
Given maps `p : I → J`, `q : J → K` and `r : I → K` such that `q.comp p = r`,
`X : GradedObject I C`, `k : K`, the cofan constructed by `cofanMapObjComp` is a colimit.
In other words, if we have, for all `j : J` such that `hj : q j = k`,
a colimit cofan `c j hj` which computes the coproduct of the `X i` such that `p i = j`,
and also a colimit cofan which computes the coproduct of the points of these `c j hj`, then
the point of this latter cofan computes the coproduct of the `X i` such that `r i = k`.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.fullDefinition: def isColimitCofanMapObjComp :     IsColimit (cofanMapObjComp X p q r hpqr k c c') :=   mkCofanColimit _     (fun s => Cofan.IsColimit.desc hc'       (fun ⟨j, (hj : q j = k)⟩ => Cofan.IsColimit.desc (hc j hj)         (fun ⟨i, (hi : p i = j)⟩ => s.inj ⟨i, by           simp only [Set.mem_preimage, Set.mem_singleton_iff, ← hpqr, hi, hj]⟩)))     (fun s ⟨i, (hi : r i = k)⟩ => by simp)     (fun s m hm => by       apply Cofan.IsColimit.hom_ext hc'       rintro ⟨j, rfl : q j = k⟩       apply Cofan.IsColimit.hom_ext (hc j rfl)       rintro ⟨i, rfl : p i = j⟩       dsimp       rw [Cofan.IsColimit.fac, Cofan.IsColimit.fac, ← hm]       dsimp       rw [assoc])
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof.description: This definition states that under specific mappings between types and given a graded object, a constructed cofan is a colimit if certain conditions regarding equivalences and colimits of associated structures are satisfied.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.comment:
Given a bifunctor `F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃` and types `I` and `J`, this is the obvious
functor `GradedObject I C₁ ⥤ GradedObject J C₂ ⥤ GradedObject (I × J) C₃`.
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.fullDefinition: def mapBifunctor (I J : Type*) :     GradedObject I C₁ ⥤ GradedObject J C₂ ⥤ GradedObject (I × J) C₃ where   obj X :=     { obj := fun Y ij => (F.obj (X ij.1)).obj (Y ij.2)       map := fun φ ij => (F.obj (X ij.1)).map (φ ij.2) }   map φ :=     { app := fun Y ij => (F.map (φ ij.1)).app (Y ij.2) }
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.description: This definition describes a functor that maps graded objects indexed by two types to a new graded object indexed by the Cartesian product of those types, utilizing a given bifunctor between categories.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.code:
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctorMapObj.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5, u_6, u_7, u_8, u_9} {C₁ : Type u_1}
  {C₂ : Type u_2} {C₃ : Type u_3} [Category.{u_7, u_1} C₁] [Category.{u_8, u_2} C₂] [Category.{u_9, u_3} C₃]
  (F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃) {I : Type u_4} {J : Type u_5} {K : Type u_6} (p : I × J → K) (X : GradedObject I C₁)
  (Y : GradedObject J C₂) [(((mapBifunctor F I J).obj X).obj Y).HasMap p] : GradedObject K C₃
CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.comment:
Given a bifunctor `F : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₃`, graded objects `X : GradedObject I C₁` and
 `Y : GradedObject J C₂` and a map `p : I × J → K`, this is the `K`-graded object sending
`k` to the coproduct of `(F.obj (X i)).obj (Y j)` for `p ⟨i, j⟩ = k`.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.ιMapBifuncto.description: This definition establishes an inclusion from a combined object derived from a functor applied to specific graded objects to a newly constructed graded object indexed by a mapping when the inputs satisfy a certain condition.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasGoodTrifu.comment:
Given bifunctors `F₁₂ : C₁ ⥤ C₂ ⥤ C₁₂`, `G : C₁₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₄`, graded objects
`X₁ : GradedObject I₁ C₁`, `X₂ : GradedObject I₂ C₂`, `X₃ : GradedObject I₃ C₃` and
`ρ₁₂ : BifunctorComp₁₂IndexData r`, this asserts that for all `i₁₂ : ρ₁₂.I₁₂` and `i₃ : I₃`,
the functor `G(-, X₃ i₃)` commutes wich the coproducts of the `F₁₂(X₁ i₁, X₂ i₂)`
such that `ρ₁₂.p ⟨i₁, i₂⟩ = i₁₂`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor: This definition describes a functor that maps graded objects indexed by two types to a new graded object indexed by the Cartesian product of those types, utilizing a given bifunctor between categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition describes a mapping from a product of two index types to a specific indexed type defined within the structure of a bifunctor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.flip: This concept refers to the process of reversing the order of the arguments in a bifunctor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor: This definition introduces a functor that represents one direction of an equivalence between two categories.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.HasGoodTrifu.description: This definition establishes a condition under which a functor relating two categories commutes with the coproduct of graded objects combined through a bifunctor, for each specified index linking the combined inputs.

explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapTrifuncto: This definition establishes a functor that maps graded objects across three categories and combines them into a new graded object that reflects the interactions between the original objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.id: This definition specifies the identity morphism for a given object within a categorical structure, which serves as a fundamental building block for morphisms in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id: A functor preserves identity morphisms by ensuring that the image of an identity morphism in one category is the identity morphism of the corresponding object in the mapped category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.id_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the identity morphism functions as a left identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing the identity with any morphism results in that morphism itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Category.comp_id: This theorem establishes that the identity morphism acts as a right identity in the composition of morphisms within a category, ensuring that composing any morphism with the identity results in the original morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition introduces a type that serves as an auxiliary structure related to a specific bilinear mapping between indexed sets.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.functor: This definition asserts that any function mapping from a discrete type to a category yields a functor between the discrete category and that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor: This definition describes a functor that maps graded objects indexed by two types to a new graded object indexed by the Cartesian product of those types, utilizing a given bifunctor between categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition describes a mapping from a product of two index types to a specific indexed type defined within the structure of a bifunctor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor: This definition specifies a graded object that combines two existing graded objects using a bifunctor and a provided mapping from their indexing types to a new index type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition specifies a mapping from a combination of two index types and a third type to a specific output type within the context of a bifunctor.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This theorem confirms that a specific bilinear mapping is consistent by showing that the value obtained from applying certain maps to a tuple is equal to the result of the original mapping defined on that tuple.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.CofanMapObjF: This definition introduces a type representing the colimit cofan objects associated with a graded object, mapping through a specified function to another index type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofan₃MapBif: This definition constructs a mapping object for a cofan in a graded setting, specifically addressing the interactions between graded objects under the application of two bifunctors and ensuring the existence of specific mapping conditions.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofanMapObj: This definition establishes a function that creates a cofan from a graded object based on a mapping and an index, corresponding to the coproduct decomposition associated with that mapping.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof: This definition asserts that a specific cofan object associated with a graded object and a mapping satisfies the universal property of a coproduct, ensuring it is a colimit within the category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCocone: This definition states that applying a functor to a cocone results in a new cocone formed over the composition of the original functor with the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitOfPreserv: This definition states that if a functor preserves colimits and a cocone is a colimit in the source category, then the mapped cocone in the target category is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.precompose: This definition establishes a functor that allows for the transformation of a cocone over one functor into a corresponding cocone over another functor via a natural transformation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.whiskering: This definition establishes that whiskering by an equivalence between two categories results in an equivalence between the categories of cocones associated with a functor and the composed functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.equivalence: This definition establishes an equivalence between two discrete categories by promoting a type-level equivalence between their underlying types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor: This definition introduces a functor that represents one direction of an equivalence between two categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.natIso: This definition shows that for functors from a discrete category, a natural isomorphism is characterized by a set of isomorphisms since the naturality conditions are trivially satisfied.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.eqToIso: An equality between two objects in a category corresponds to an isomorphism between those objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.precompo: This definition establishes an equivalence between the condition of a cocone transformed by a natural isomorphism being a colimit and the original cocone being a colimit.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.whiskerE: This definition establishes a correspondence between colimit cocones in different categories, indicating that one is a colimit if and only if the whiskered cocone in the target category is also a colimit under the equivalence of categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofIsoCol: This definition states that if a cocone is a colimit and there is an isomorphism between two cocones, then the second cocone is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof: This definition states that under specific mappings between types and given a graded object, a constructed cofan is a colimit if certain conditions regarding equivalences and colimits of associated structures are satisfied.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.inj: This definition retrieves the morphism from a specific object in a family to the designated point in the cofan associated with that family of objects.

CategoryTheory.GradedObject.mapBifunctor.comment:
The action on graded objects of a trifunctor obtained by composition of two
bifunctors can be computed as a composition of the actions of these two bifunctors.

Given bifunctors `F : C₁ ⥤ C₂₃ ⥤ C₄`, `G₂₃ : C₂ ⥤ C₃ ⥤ C₂₃`, graded objects
`X₁ : GradedObject I₁ C₁`, `X₂ : GradedObject I₂ C₂`, `X₃ : GradedObject I₃ C₃` and

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.precompo: This definition establishes an equivalence between the condition of a cocone transformed by a natural isomorphism being a colimit and the original cocone being a colimit.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.whiskerE: This definition establishes a correspondence between colimit cocones in different categories, indicating that one is a colimit if and only if the whiskered cocone in the target category is also a colimit under the equivalence of categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofIsoCol: This definition states that if a cocone is a colimit and there is an isomorphism between two cocones, then the second cocone is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.isColimitCof: This definition states that under specific mappings between types and given a graded object, a constructed cofan is a colimit if certain conditions regarding equivalences and colimits of associated structures are satisfied.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofan.inj: This definition retrieves the morphism from a specific object in a family to the designated point in the cofan associated with that family of objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.BifunctorCom: This definition introduces an auxiliary type used within the context of a specific bifunctor's index data structure.
This definition describes a mapping that takes a pair of indices from two types and produces an index in a third type, associated with a bifunctorial construction.
This definition specifies a mapping from a product of one index type and a derived type relating to a bifunctor to a result type in the context of a specific bilinear mapping.
This theorem establishes the consistency of a bilinear mapping by demonstrating that a derived value from specific index transformations matches the original mapping output.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.GradedObject.cofan₃MapBif: This definition introduces a mapping function that constructs a cofan from graded objects and bifunctors, facilitating the inclusion of structured data in a categorical context.

bifunctors can be computed as a composition of the actions of these two bifunctors.

CategoryTheory.TwoSquare.comment:
A `2`-square consists of a natural transformation `T ⋙ R ⟶ L ⋙ B`
involving fours functors `T`, `L`, `R`, `B` that are on the
top/left/right/bottom sides of a square of categories.

CategoryTheory.Dial.tensorHom.fullDefinition: @[simps] def tensorHom {X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂ : Dial C} (f : X₁ ⟶ X₂) (g : Y₁ ⟶ Y₂) :     tensorObj X₁ Y₁ ⟶ tensorObj X₂ Y₂ where   f := prod.map f.f g.f   F := π(prod.map π₁ π₁ ≫ f.F, prod.map π₂ π₂ ≫ g.F)   le := by     simp only [tensorObj, Subobject.inf_pullback]     apply inf_le_inf <;> rw [← Subobject.pullback_comp, ← Subobject.pullback_comp]     · have := (Subobject.pullback (prod.map π₁ π₁ :         (X₁.src ⨯ Y₁.src) ⨯ X₂.tgt ⨯ Y₂.tgt ⟶ _)).monotone (Hom.le f)       rw [← Subobject.pullback_comp, ← Subobject.pullback_comp] at this       convert this using 3 <;> simp     · have := (Subobject.pullback (prod.map π₂ π₂ :         (X₁.src ⨯ Y₁.src) ⨯ X₂.tgt ⨯ Y₂.tgt ⟶ _)).monotone (Hom.le g)       rw [← Subobject.pullback_comp, ← Subobject.pullback_comp] at this       convert this using 3 <;> simp

  (T : Triangle C) : Triangle C
CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle..comment:
If you rotate a triangle, you get another triangle.
Given a triangle of the form:
```
      f       g       h
  X  ───> Y  ───> Z  ───> X⟦1⟧
```
applying `rotate` gives a triangle of the form:
```
      g       h        -f⟦1⟧'
  Y  ───> Z  ───>  X⟦1⟧ ───> Y⟦1⟧
```

Given a triangle of the form:
```
      f       g       h
  X  ───> Y  ───> Z  ───> X⟦1⟧
```
applying `rotate` gives a triangle of the form:
```
      g       h        -f⟦1⟧'
  Y  ───> Z  ───>  X⟦1⟧ ───> Y⟦1⟧
```

This definition establishes a triangle in a category formed by specified morphisms between three objects, along with a morphism that connects the last object back to the first object shifted by one.
This definition identifies the second morphism between the second and third objects within a triangle in a category.
This definition specifies the third morphism from the third object of a triangle back to the first object shifted by one position within a category.

category_theory.pretriangulated.triangle.fullDefinition: def Triangle.rotate (T : Triangle C) : Triangle C :=   Triangle.mk T.mor₂ T.mor₃ (-T.mor₁⟦1⟧')
category_theory.pretriangulated.triangle.description: This definition describes the construction of a new triangle by rotating the morphisms of an existing triangle within a category.

CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle..comment:
Given a triangle of the form:
```
      f       g       h
  X  ───> Y  ───> Z  ───> X⟦1⟧
```
applying `invRotate` gives a triangle that can be thought of as:
```
        -h⟦-1⟧'     f       g
  Z⟦-1⟧  ───>  X  ───> Y  ───> Z
```
(note that this diagram doesn't technically fit the definition of triangle, as `Z⟦-1⟧⟦1⟧` is
not necessarily equal to `Z`, but it is isomorphic, by the `counitIso` of `shiftEquiv C 1`)

CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle..fullDefinition: noncomputable def Triangle.shiftFunctor (n : ℤ) : Triangle C ⥤ Triangle C where   obj T := Triangle.mk (n.negOnePow • T.mor₁⟦n⟧') (n.negOnePow • T.mor₂⟦n⟧')     (n.negOnePow • T.mor₃⟦n⟧' ≫ (shiftFunctorComm C 1 n).hom.app T.obj₁)   map f :=     { hom₁ := f.hom₁⟦n⟧'       hom₂ := f.hom₂⟦n⟧'       hom₃ := f.hom₃⟦n⟧'       comm₁ := by         dsimp         simp only [Linear.units_smul_comp, Linear.comp_units_smul, ← Functor.map_comp, f.comm₁]       comm₂ := by         dsimp         simp only [Linear.units_smul_comp, Linear.comp_units_smul, ← Functor.map_comp, f.comm₂]       comm₃ := by         dsimp         rw [Linear.units_smul_comp, Linear.comp_units_smul, ← Functor.map_comp_assoc, ← f.comm₃,           Functor.map_comp, assoc, assoc]         erw [(shiftFunctorComm C 1 n).hom.naturality]         rfl }

CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.Triangle..fullDefinition: noncomputable def Triangle.shiftFunctorAdd' (a b n : ℤ) (h : a + b = n) :     Triangle.shiftFunctor C n ≅ Triangle.shiftFunctor C a ⋙ Triangle.shiftFunctor C b :=   NatIso.ofComponents     (fun T => Triangle.isoMk _ _       ((CategoryTheory.shiftFunctorAdd' C a b n h).app _)       ((CategoryTheory.shiftFunctorAdd' C a b n h).app _)       ((CategoryTheory.shiftFunctorAdd' C a b n h).app _)       (by         subst h         dsimp         rw [Linear.units_smul_comp, NatTrans.naturality, Linear.comp_units_smul, Functor.comp_map,           Functor.map_units_smul, Linear.comp_units_smul, smul_smul, Int.negOnePow_add, mul_comm])       (by         subst h         dsimp         rw [Linear.units_smul_comp, NatTrans.naturality, Linear.comp_units_smul, Functor.comp_map,           Functor.map_units_smul, Linear.comp_units_smul, smul_smul, Int.negOnePow_add, mul_comm])       (by         subst h         dsimp         rw [Linear.units_smul_comp, Linear.comp_units_smul, Functor.map_units_smul,           Linear.units_smul_comp, Linear.comp_units_smul, smul_smul, assoc,           Functor.map_comp, assoc]         erw [← NatTrans.naturality_assoc]         simp only [shiftFunctorAdd'_eq_shiftFunctorAdd, Int.negOnePow_add,           shiftFunctorComm_hom_app_comp_shift_shiftFunctorAdd_hom_app, add_comm a]))     (by aesop_cat)

CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.distingui.fullDefinition: distinguishedTriangles : Set (Triangle C)   /-- a triangle that is isomorphic to a distinguished triangle is distinguished -/   isomorphic_distinguished :     ∀ T₁ ∈ distinguishedTriangles, ∀ (T₂) (_ : T₂ ≅ T₁), T₂ ∈ distinguishedTriangles   /-- obvious triangles `X ⟶ X ⟶ 0 ⟶ X⟦1⟧` are distinguished -/   contractible_distinguished : ∀ X : C, contractibleTriangle X ∈ distinguishedTriangles   /-- any morphism `X ⟶ Y` is part of a distinguished triangle `X ⟶ Y ⟶ Z ⟶ X⟦1⟧` -/   distinguished_cocone_triangle :     ∀ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y),       ∃ (Z : C) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (h : Z ⟶ X⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distinguishedTriangles   /-- a triangle is distinguished iff it is so after rotating it -/   rotate_distinguished_triangle :     ∀ T : Triangle C, T ∈ distinguishedTriangles ↔ T.rotate ∈ distinguishedTriangles   /-- given two distinguished triangle, a commutative square         can be extended as morphism of triangles -/   complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism :     ∀ (T₁ T₂ : Triangle C) (_ : T₁ ∈ distinguishedTriangles) (_ : T₂ ∈ distinguishedTriangles)       (a : T₁.obj₁ ⟶ T₂.obj₁) (b : T₁.obj₂ ⟶ T₂.obj₂) (_ : T₁.mor₁ ≫ b = a ≫ T₂.mor₁),       ∃ c : T₁.obj₃ ⟶ T₂.obj₃, T₁.mor₂ ≫ c = b ≫ T₂.mor₂ ∧ T₁.mor₃ ≫ a⟦1⟧' = c ≫ T₂.mor₃

`inr : T.obj₃ ⟶ T.obj₂` and `fst : T.obj₂ ⟶ T.obj₁` satisfying suitable relations, this

CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.binaryBip.fullDefinition: def binaryBiproductData (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) (hT₀ : T.mor₃ = 0)     (inr : T.obj₃ ⟶ T.obj₂) (inr_snd : inr ≫ T.mor₂ = 𝟙 _) (fst : T.obj₂ ⟶ T.obj₁)     (total : fst ≫ T.mor₁ + T.mor₂ ≫ inr = 𝟙 T.obj₂) :     BinaryBiproductData T.obj₁ T.obj₃ := by   have : Mono T.mor₁ := T.mono₁ hT hT₀   have eq : fst ≫ T.mor₁ = 𝟙 T.obj₂ - T.mor₂ ≫ inr := by rw [← total, add_sub_cancel_right]   exact     { bicone :=       { pt := T.obj₂         fst := fst         snd := T.mor₂         inl := T.mor₁         inr := inr         inl_fst := by           simp only [← cancel_mono T.mor₁, assoc, id_comp, eq, comp_sub, comp_id,             comp_distTriang_mor_zero₁₂_assoc _ hT, zero_comp, sub_zero]         inl_snd := comp_distTriang_mor_zero₁₂ _ hT         inr_fst := by           simp only [← cancel_mono T.mor₁, assoc, eq, comp_sub, reassoc_of% inr_snd,             comp_id, sub_self, zero_comp]         inr_snd := inr_snd }       isBilimit := isBinaryBilimitOfTotal _ total }

CategoryTheory.SemiadditiveOfBinaryBipro.fullDefinition: def addCommMonoidHomOfHasBinaryBiproducts : AddCommMonoid (X ⟶ Y) where   add := (· +ᵣ ·)   add_assoc :=     (EckmannHilton.mul_assoc (isUnital_leftAdd X Y) (isUnital_rightAdd X Y) (distrib X Y)).assoc   zero := 0   zero_add := (isUnital_rightAdd X Y).left_id   add_zero := (isUnital_rightAdd X Y).right_id   add_comm :=     (EckmannHilton.mul_comm (isUnital_leftAdd X Y) (isUnital_rightAdd X Y) (distrib X Y)).comm   nsmul := letI : Add (X ⟶ Y) := ⟨(· +ᵣ ·)⟩; nsmulRec

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel: The cokernel of a morphism is defined as the object obtained by taking the coequalizer of the morphism with the zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Injective.syzygies: This definition introduces an injective object that can be associated with a morphism under the condition that the category has enough injectives and has a cokernel.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.cokernel.π: The morphism from the target of a given morphism in a category to its cokernel is defined, provided the cokernel exists.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Projective.π: This definition describes an epimorphism from a chosen projective object over another object to that object itself in a category with enough projectives.

CategoryTheory.Injective.d.fullDefinition: abbrev d : Y ⟶ syzygies f :=   cokernel.π f ≫ ι (cokernel f)
CategoryTheory.Injective.d.description: This definition specifies a morphism from an object to the syzygies of another morphism in a category that has enough injectives and zero morphisms, demonstrating how the cokernel's projection interacts with injectives.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Injective.mk: This theorem establishes that an object is injective if every morphism into it from another object can be extended via a monomorphism.

CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.mk.description: This theorem constructs an injective presentation of an object by relating it to a morphism from the object to an injective one, under the condition that the morphism is monomorphic.

CategoryTheory.Injective.enoughInjective.code:
CategoryTheory.Injective.enoughInjectives_of_enoughProjectives_op.{v₁, u₁} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [EnoughProjectives Cᵒᵖ] : EnoughInjectives C
CategoryTheory.Injective.enoughInjective.description: This theorem establishes that if a category has enough projectives, then it also has enough injectives.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.map_injective.description: This theorem asserts that if a functor preserves monomorphisms and is part of an adjunction, then the image of an injective object under the right adjoint functor is also injective.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injective_of_m.code:
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injective_of_map_injective.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} D] {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) [G.Full] [G.Faithful] (I : D)
  (hI : Injective (G.obj I)) : Injective I
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injective_of_m.description: This theorem shows that if an object is injective with respect to a functor that is full and faithful, then the corresponding object in a related category is also injective when the functors form an adjunction.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapInjectivePr.comment:
Given an adjunction `F ⊣ G` such that `F` preserves monos, `G` maps an injective presentation
of `X` to an injective presentation of `G(X)`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.J: This definition describes an injective presentation of an object as a morphism to some injective object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.inj: This theorem asserts that if an object has an injective presentation, then the target of that presentation is itself injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.f: This definition describes a morphism from an object to an associated injective object that represents its injective presentation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.mon: This theorem states that an object with an injective presentation is represented by a monomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero.injective: This theorem states that if an object is zero in a category, then it is injective.
explanatories.Equiv.injective: This theorem states that an equivalence relation is injective if the corresponding function from the first type to the second type is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.map_injective: This theorem asserts that if a functor preserves monomorphisms and is part of an adjunction, then the image of an injective object under the right adjoint functor is also injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_injective: This statement does not provide any specific theorem or definition; therefore, it does not present any mathematical or logical assertion.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapInjectivePr.fullDefinition: def mapInjectivePresentation (adj : F ⊣ G) [F.PreservesMonomorphisms] (X : D)     (I : InjectivePresentation X) : InjectivePresentation (G.obj X) where   J := G.obj I.J   injective := adj.map_injective _ I.injective   f := G.map I.f   mono := by     haveI : PreservesLimitsOfSize.{0, 0} G := adj.rightAdjointPreservesLimits; infer_instance
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapInjectivePr.description: This definition states that under an adjunction where the left functor preserves monomorphisms, the image of an injective presentation in the right category is also an injective presentation.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injectivePrese.code:
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injectivePresentationOfMap.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  {D : Type u_1} [Category.{u_2, u_1} D] {F : C ⥤ D} {G : D ⥤ C} (adj : F ⊣ G) [F.PreservesMonomorphisms]
  [F.ReflectsMonomorphisms] (X : C) (I : InjectivePresentation (F.obj X)) : InjectivePresentation X
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injectivePrese.comment:
Given an adjunction `F ⊣ G` such that `F` preserves monomorphisms and is faithful,
then any injective presentation of `F(X)` can be pulled back to an injective presentation of `X`.
This is similar to `mapInjectivePresentation`.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.J: This definition describes an injective presentation of an object as a morphism to some injective object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.inj: This theorem asserts that if an object has an injective presentation, then the target of that presentation is itself injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.f: This definition describes a morphism from an object to an associated injective object that represents its injective presentation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero.injective: This theorem states that if an object is zero in a category, then it is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.homEquiv: This definition describes an equivalence between morphisms in two categories that arises from an adjunction.
explanatories.Equiv.injective: This theorem states that an equivalence relation is injective if the corresponding function from the first type to the second type is injective.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Injective.injective_of_ad: This theorem states that if there is an adjoint pair of functors between two categories and one object is injective in the second category, then its image under the right adjoint functor is injective in the first category.

CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injectivePrese.fullDefinition: def injectivePresentationOfMap (adj : F ⊣ G)     [F.PreservesMonomorphisms] [F.ReflectsMonomorphisms] (X : C)     (I : InjectivePresentation <| F.obj X) :     InjectivePresentation X where   J := G.obj I.J   injective := Injective.injective_of_adjoint adj _   f := adj.homEquiv _ _ I.f
CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injectivePrese.description: This definition states that under an adjunction where the left functor preserves and reflects monomorphisms, an injective presentation of an image object can be pulled back to an injective presentation of the original object.

CategoryTheory.EnoughInjectives.of_adjun.code:
CategoryTheory.EnoughInjectives.of_adjunction.{v₁, v₂, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C]
  [Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} (adj : L ⊣ R) [L.PreservesMonomorphisms] [L.ReflectsMonomorphisms]
  [EnoughInjectives D] : EnoughInjectives C
CategoryTheory.EnoughInjectives.of_adjun.description: This theorem asserts that the existence of an adjunction between two categories, where one functor preserves and reflects monomorphisms, implies that the first category has enough injectives if the second category does.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.injectivePres.comment:
Given an equivalence of categories `F`, an injective presentation of `F(X)` induces an
injective presentation of `X.`

explanatories.CategoryTheory.InjectivePresentation.f: This definition describes a morphism from an object to an associated injective object that represents its injective presentation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.injectivePrese: This definition states that under an adjunction where the left functor preserves and reflects monomorphisms, an injective presentation of an image object can be pulled back to an injective presentation of the original object.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.injectivePres.fullDefinition: def injectivePresentationOfMapInjectivePresentation (X : C)     (I : InjectivePresentation (F.functor.obj X)) : InjectivePresentation X :=   F.toAdjunction.injectivePresentationOfMap _ I
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.injectivePres.description: This definition establishes that an injective presentation of an object in one category induces an injective presentation of the corresponding object in another category related by a categorical equivalence.

CategoryTheory.Equivalence.enoughInjecti.code:
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.enoughInjectives_iff.{v₁, u₁, u_1, u_2} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D : Type u_1}
  [Category.{u_2, u_1} D] (F : C ≌ D) : EnoughInjectives C ↔ EnoughInjectives D
CategoryTheory.Equivalence.enoughInjecti.description: This theorem establishes that a category has enough injectives if and only if its equivalent category does as well.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [self : Preadditive C] (P Q R : C)
  (f f' : P ⟶ Q) (g : Q ⟶ R) : (f + f') ≫ g = f ≫ g + f' ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp.description: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition with a morphism preserves the addition of morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [self : Preadditive C] (P Q R : C)
  (f : P ⟶ Q) (g g' : Q ⟶ R) : f ≫ (g + g') = f ≫ g + f ≫ g'
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add.description: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.homGroup.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.homGroup.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [self : Preadditive C] (P Q : C) :
  AddCommGroup (P ⟶ Q)
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.homGroup.comment:
A category is called preadditive if `P ⟶ Q` is an abelian group such that composition is
linear in both variables.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp: This definition describes the composition of morphisms in a category, which is expressed using a specific notation to connect objects through their relationships.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition with a morphism preserves the addition of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.homGroup.fullDefinition: homGroup : ∀ P Q : C, AddCommGroup (P ⟶ Q) := by infer_instance   add_comp : ∀ (P Q R : C) (f f' : P ⟶ Q) (g : Q ⟶ R), (f + f') ≫ g = f ≫ g + f' ≫ g := by     aesop_cat   comp_add : ∀ (P Q R : C) (f : P ⟶ Q) (g g' : Q ⟶ R), f ≫ (g + g') = f ≫ g + f ≫ g' := by     aesop_cat
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.homGroup.description: This definition establishes that the set of morphisms between two objects in a preadditive category forms an abelian group.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.inducedCatego.fullDefinition: instance inducedCategory : Preadditive.{v} (InducedCategory C F) where   homGroup P Q := @Preadditive.homGroup C _ _ (F P) (F Q)   add_comp _ _ _ _ _ _ := add_comp _ _ _ _ _ _   comp_add _ _ _ _ _ _ := comp_add _ _ _ _ _ _
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.inducedCatego.description: This definition describes how a functor from one category to another induces a preadditive structure on the resulting category.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.fullSubcatego.description: This definition describes a preadditive structure for the full subcategory of a given category that satisfies a specified property.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.leftComp.fullDefinition: def leftComp {P Q : C} (R : C) (f : P ⟶ Q) : (Q ⟶ R) →+ (P ⟶ R) :=   mk' (fun g => f ≫ g) fun g g' => by simp

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.rightComp.fullDefinition: def rightComp (P : C) {Q R : C} (g : Q ⟶ R) : (P ⟶ Q) →+ (P ⟶ R) :=   mk' (fun f => f ≫ g) fun f f' => by simp
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.rightComp.description: This definition describes a group homomorphism that represents the operation of composing morphisms from a fixed object on the right with morphisms from another object to a third object in a preadditive category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.rightComp: This definition describes a group homomorphism that represents the operation of composing morphisms from a fixed object on the right with morphisms from another object to a third object in a preadditive category.

explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_add: This theorem asserts that an additive monoid homomorphism preserves the addition operation, meaning the image of the sum of two elements is equal to the sum of their images.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.compHom.fullDefinition: def compHom : (P ⟶ Q) →+ (Q ⟶ R) →+ (P ⟶ R) :=   AddMonoidHom.mk' (fun f => leftComp _ f) fun f₁ f₂ =>     AddMonoidHom.ext fun g => (rightComp _ g).map_add f₁ f₂
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.compHom.description: This definition characterizes the composition of two morphisms in a preadditive category as a bilinear group homomorphism that maps pairs of morphisms to a resulting morphism connecting the first and last objects.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sub_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sub_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f f' : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) : (f - f') ≫ g = f ≫ g - f' ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sub_comp.description: This theorem states that the composition of the difference of two morphisms with a subsequent morphism is equal to the difference of their individual compositions with that morphism in a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sub.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sub.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g g' : Q ⟶ R) : f ≫ (g - g') = f ≫ g - f ≫ g'
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sub.description: This theorem establishes that composing a morphism with the difference of two other morphisms yields the same result as composing it with each morphism separately and then taking their difference.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) : (-f) ≫ g = -f ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp.description: This theorem establishes that negating a morphism before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category yields the same result as negating the composition of the morphism with the second morphism.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_neg.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_neg.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) : f ≫ (-g) = -f ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_neg.description: This theorem demonstrates that composing a morphism with the negation of another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to negating the composition of the first morphism with the second morphism.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp_neg.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp_neg.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) : (-f) ≫ (-g) = f ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp_neg.description: This theorem shows that the composition of negated morphisms equals the composition of the original morphisms in a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.nsmul_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.nsmul_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) (n : ℕ) : (n • f) ≫ g = n • f ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.nsmul_comp.description: This theorem asserts that in a preadditive category, scalar multiplication of a morphism commutes with the composition of that morphism with other morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_nsmul.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_nsmul.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) (n : ℕ) : f ≫ (n • g) = n • f ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_nsmul.description: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition of a morphism with a scalar multiple of another morphism is equal to the scalar multiplication of the first morphism followed by the second morphism.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) (n : ℤ) : (n • f) ≫ g = n • f ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp.description: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying a morphism by an integer before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to multiplying the composition by the same integer.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q)
  (g : Q ⟶ R) (n : ℤ) : f ≫ (n • g) = n • f ≫ g
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul.description: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, composing a morphism with an integer-scaled morphism is equivalent to scaling the composition of the original morphism with the other morphism by the same integer.

CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sum.code:
CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sum.{v, u, u_1} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {P Q R : C}

explanatories.add_assoc: This theorem states that the addition operation is associative, meaning that the grouping of three elements being added does not affect the result.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.nsmulRec: This definition describes a recursive function for scalar multiplication in an additive monoid, which adds an element to itself a specified number of times.
explanatories.sub_eq_add_neg: Subtracting an element from another is equivalent to adding the negative of that element.
explanatories.zsmulRec: This definition describes a function that extends scalar multiplication to integers in an additive group, operating by repeatedly adding an element for positive integers and accounting for negatives by using inverses.
explanatories.add_left_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, the sum of an element and its additive inverse equals the zero element.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition with a morphism preserves the addition of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.functorCategoryPreadditiv.fullDefinition: instance functorCategoryPreadditive : Preadditive (C ⥤ D) where   homGroup F G :=     { nsmul := nsmulRec       zsmul := zsmulRec       sub := fun α β => { app := fun X => α.app X - β.app X }       add_assoc := by         intros         ext         apply add_assoc       zero_add := by         intros         dsimp         ext         apply zero_add       add_zero := by         intros         dsimp         ext         apply add_zero       add_comm := by         intros         dsimp         ext         apply add_comm       sub_eq_add_neg := by         intros         dsimp         ext         apply sub_eq_add_neg       add_left_neg := by         intros         dsimp         ext         apply add_left_neg }   add_comp := by     intros     dsimp     ext     apply add_comp   comp_add := by     intros     dsimp     ext     apply comp_add
CategoryTheory.functorCategoryPreadditiv.description: This definition asserts that the functor category formed from two preadditive categories is itself a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.appHom.fullDefinition: def appHom (X : C) : (F ⟶ G) →+ (F.obj X ⟶ G.obj X) where   toFun α := α.app X   map_zero' := rfl   map_add' _ _ := rfl

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_zero.code:

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_add.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_add.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_4, u_1} C]

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_add.description: This theorem states that the application of the sum of two natural transformations at a fixed object equals the sum of their individual applications at that object.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_sub.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_sub.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_4, u_1} C]

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_sub.description: This theorem states that the application of the difference of two natural transformations at a fixed object equals the difference of their individual applications at that object.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_neg.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_neg.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_4, u_1} C]

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_nsmul.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_nsmul.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_4, u_1} C]

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_nsmul.description: This theorem asserts that the application of a natural transformation scaled by a natural number at a fixed object equals the scaling of the application of that transformation at that object.

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_zsmul.code:

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.appHom_apply.code:

CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_sum.code:
CategoryTheory.NatTrans.app_sum.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4, u_5} {C : Type u_1} {D : Type u_2} [Category.{u_5, u_1} C]

CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitOfTotal.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitOfTotal.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {J : Type} [Fintype J]
  {f : J → C} (b : Bicone f) (total : ∑ j : J, b.π j ≫ b.ι j = 𝟙 b.pt) : b.IsBilimit
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitOfTotal.comment:
In a preadditive category, we can construct a biproduct for `f : J → C` from
any bicone `b` for `f` satisfying `total : ∑ j : J, b.π j ≫ b.ι j = 𝟙 b.X`.

(That is, such a bicone is a limit cone and a colimit cocone.)

CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitOfTotal.fullDefinition: def isBilimitOfTotal {f : J → C} (b : Bicone f) (total : ∑ j : J, b.π j ≫ b.ι j = 𝟙 b.pt) :     b.IsBilimit where   isLimit :=     { lift := fun s => ∑ j : J, s.π.app ⟨j⟩ ≫ b.ι j       uniq := fun s m h => by         erw [← Category.comp_id m, ← total, comp_sum]         apply Finset.sum_congr rfl         intro j _         have reassoced : m ≫ Bicone.π b j ≫ Bicone.ι b j = s.π.app ⟨j⟩ ≫ Bicone.ι b j := by           erw [← Category.assoc, eq_whisker (h ⟨j⟩)]         rw [reassoced]       fac := fun s j => by         cases j         simp only [sum_comp, Category.assoc, Bicone.toCone_π_app, b.ι_π, comp_dite]         -- See note [dsimp, simp].         dsimp         simp }   isColimit :=     { desc := fun s => ∑ j : J, b.π j ≫ s.ι.app ⟨j⟩       uniq := fun s m h => by         erw [← Category.id_comp m, ← total, sum_comp]         apply Finset.sum_congr rfl         intro j _         erw [Category.assoc, h ⟨j⟩]       fac := fun s j => by         cases j         simp only [comp_sum, ← Category.assoc, Bicone.toCocone_ι_app, b.ι_π, dite_comp]         dsimp; simp }
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitOfTotal.description: This definition states that in a preadditive category, a bicone satisfying a specific totality condition can be considered a biproduct, indicating it acts as both a limit cone and a colimit cocone.

explanatories.nonempty_fintype: This theorem states that if a type is finite, then it must also have at least one finite enumeration.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.π: This definition specifies a projection morphism from a biproduct object to an individual summand in the context of category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι: This definition specifies an inclusion morphism from an individual summand to a biproduct object in the context of category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift: This definition describes a method for constructing a morphism into a biproduct from a collection of morphisms into its individual summands.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι_π: This theorem establishes a relationship between the morphisms in a biproduct, asserting that the composition of the inclusion and projection morphisms behaves like the identity or zero depending on whether the indices are equal.
explanatories.Finset.sum_dite_eq': The sum of a function's values over a finite set, conditioned on equality to a specific element, equals the value of the function at that element multiplied by a characteristic that indicates its presence in the set.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.desc: This definition specifies that given a collection of morphisms from the summands of a biproduct, there exists a corresponding morphism from the entire biproduct to another object.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι_π_asso: This theorem establishes a relationship involving the indexed projections and inclusions of a biproduct, illustrating how they interact with other morphisms based on whether their indices are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.lift_des: In a preadditive category, the composition of the lifting morphism of a biproduct with its corresponding descending morphism equals the sum of the products of the individual morphisms from a specific object to each component of the biproduct.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.dite: This defines a dependent if-then-else mechanism that allows for conditional branching based on a proposition, where the outcome can depend on proofs of both the truth and falsehood of that proposition.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι_π_ne: This theorem states that the composition of the inclusion morphism of one summand and the projection morphism of a different summand in a biproduct is equal to zero.
explanatories.Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply: This theorem asserts a relationship between the equality of an image under an equivalence and the equality of the original element with its image under the inverse of that equivalence.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.lift: This definition specifies a morphism from the point of any cone to the point of a limit cone associated with a given functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.desc: This definition describes a morphism from the point of a colimit cocone to the point of another cocone, ensuring a connection between their respective structures.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.lift: This definition describes a method to construct a morphism from an object to the biproduct of two summands using given morphisms from that object to each summand.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.desc: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism from a binary biproduct to another object by using a pair of morphisms originating from each summand of that biproduct.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ι: This definition introduces a morphism that connects a given point of a fork on two parallel morphisms to the zero instance of a parallel pair formed by those morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.reindex.fullDefinition: def biproduct.reindex {β γ : Type} [Finite β] (ε : β ≃ γ)     (f : γ → C) [HasBiproduct f] [HasBiproduct (f ∘ ε)] : ⨁ f ∘ ε ≅ ⨁ f where   hom := biproduct.desc fun b => biproduct.ι f (ε b)   inv := biproduct.lift fun b => biproduct.π f (ε b)   hom_inv_id := by     ext b b'     by_cases h : b' = b     · subst h; simp     · have : ε b' ≠ ε b := by simp [h]       simp [biproduct.ι_π_ne _ h, biproduct.ι_π_ne _ this]   inv_hom_id := by     cases nonempty_fintype β     ext g g'     by_cases h : g' = g <;>       simp [Preadditive.sum_comp, Preadditive.comp_sum, biproduct.lift_desc,         biproduct.ι_π, biproduct.ι_π_assoc, comp_dite, Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply,         Finset.sum_dite_eq' Finset.univ (ε.symm g') _, h]
CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.reindex.description: This definition provides an isomorphism between the biproducts of two functors indexed by equivalent types, allowing reindexing of the biproduct under an equivalence of the index sets in a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isBinaryBilimitOfT.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBinaryBilimitOfTotal.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {X Y : C}
  (b : BinaryBicone X Y) (total : b.fst ≫ b.inl + b.snd ≫ b.inr = 𝟙 b.pt) : b.IsBilimit
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBinaryBilimitOfT.comment:
In a preadditive category, we can construct a binary biproduct for `X Y : C` from
any binary bicone `b` satisfying `total : b.fst ≫ b.inl + b.snd ≫ b.inr = 𝟙 b.X`.

(That is, such a bicone is a limit cone and a colimit cocone.)

CategoryTheory.Limits.isBinaryBilimitOfT.fullDefinition: def isBinaryBilimitOfTotal {X Y : C} (b : BinaryBicone X Y)     (total : b.fst ≫ b.inl + b.snd ≫ b.inr = 𝟙 b.pt) : b.IsBilimit where   isLimit :=     { lift := fun s =>       (BinaryFan.fst s ≫ b.inl : s.pt ⟶ b.pt) + (BinaryFan.snd s ≫ b.inr : s.pt ⟶ b.pt)       uniq := fun s m h => by         have reassoced (j : WalkingPair) {W : C} (h' : _ ⟶ W) :           m ≫ b.toCone.π.app ⟨j⟩ ≫ h' = s.π.app ⟨j⟩ ≫ h' := by             rw [← Category.assoc, eq_whisker (h ⟨j⟩)]         erw [← Category.comp_id m, ← total, comp_add, reassoced WalkingPair.left,           reassoced WalkingPair.right]       fac := fun s j => by rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩ <;> simp }   isColimit :=     { desc := fun s =>         (b.fst ≫ BinaryCofan.inl s : b.pt ⟶ s.pt) + (b.snd ≫ BinaryCofan.inr s : b.pt ⟶ s.pt)       uniq := fun s m h => by         erw [← Category.id_comp m, ← total, add_comp, Category.assoc, Category.assoc,           h ⟨WalkingPair.left⟩, h ⟨WalkingPair.right⟩]       fac := fun s j => by rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩ <;> simp }
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBinaryBilimitOfT.description: This definition states that in a preadditive category, any binary bicone that satisfies a specific totality condition can be identified as a bilimit bicone, effectively forming a binary biproduct for the given objects.

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.ofLim.fullDefinition: def BinaryBicone.ofLimitCone {X Y : C} {t : Cone (pair X Y)} (ht : IsLimit t) :     BinaryBicone X Y where   pt := t.pt   fst := t.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.left⟩   snd := t.π.app ⟨WalkingPair.right⟩   inl := ht.lift (BinaryFan.mk (𝟙 X) 0)   inr := ht.lift (BinaryFan.mk 0 (𝟙 Y))

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that if two morphisms into a limit cone yield the same results when composed with the projection morphisms from the cone, then the two morphisms must be equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.hom_ext: This theorem states that two morphisms from a colimit are equal if they yield the same result when composed with the cocone's morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isBinaryBilimitOfT: This definition states that in a preadditive category, any binary bicone that satisfies a specific totality condition can be identified as a bilimit bicone, effectively forming a binary biproduct for the given objects.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.IsColi: This theorem proves that two morphisms from the point of a binary cofan to another object are equal if they agree on their compositions with the two respective projections of the cofan.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Limits.binaryBiconeOfIsSp.fullDefinition: def binaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} [IsSplitMono f] {c : CokernelCofork f}     (i : IsColimit c) : BinaryBicone X c.pt where   pt := Y   fst := retraction f   snd := c.π   inl := f   inr :=     let c' : CokernelCofork (𝟙 Y - (𝟙 Y - retraction f ≫ f)) :=       CokernelCofork.ofπ (Cofork.π c) (by simp)     let i' : IsColimit c' := isCokernelEpiComp i (retraction f) (by simp)     let i'' := isColimitCoforkOfCokernelCofork i'     (splitEpiOfIdempotentOfIsColimitCofork C (by simp) i'').section_   inl_fst := by simp   inl_snd := by simp   inr_fst := by     dsimp only     rw [splitEpiOfIdempotentOfIsColimitCofork_section_,       isColimitCoforkOfCokernelCofork_desc, isCokernelEpiComp_desc]     dsimp only [cokernelCoforkOfCofork_ofπ]     letI := epi_of_isColimit_cofork i     apply zero_of_epi_comp c.π     simp only [sub_comp, comp_sub, Category.comp_id, Category.assoc, IsSplitMono.id, sub_self,       Cofork.IsColimit.π_desc_assoc, CokernelCofork.π_ofπ, IsSplitMono.id_assoc]     apply sub_eq_zero_of_eq     apply Category.id_comp   inr_snd := by apply SplitEpi.id

CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitBinaryBic.fullDefinition: def isBilimitBinaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} [IsSplitMono f]     {c : CokernelCofork f} (i : IsColimit c) : (binaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel i).IsBilimit :=   isBinaryBilimitOfTotal _     (by       simp only [binaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel_fst,         binaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel_inr,         binaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel_snd,         splitEpiOfIdempotentOfIsColimitCofork_section_]       dsimp only [binaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel_pt]       rw [isColimitCoforkOfCokernelCofork_desc, isCokernelEpiComp_desc]       simp only [binaryBiconeOfIsSplitMonoOfCokernel_inl, Cofork.IsColimit.π_desc,         cokernelCoforkOfCofork_π, Cofork.π_ofπ, add_sub_cancel])
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitBinaryBic.description: In a preadditive category, a bicone derived from a split monomorphism and its cokernel is confirmed to be a bilimit, extending a version of the splitting lemma.

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil.fullDefinition: def BinaryBicone.isBilimitOfKernelInl {X Y : C} (b : BinaryBicone X Y)     (hb : IsLimit b.sndKernelFork) : b.IsBilimit :=   isBinaryBilimitOfIsLimit _ <|     BinaryFan.IsLimit.mk _ (fun f g => f ≫ b.inl + g ≫ b.inr) (fun f g => by simp)       (fun f g => by simp) fun {T} f g m h₁ h₂ => by       dsimp at m       have h₁' : ((m : T ⟶ b.pt) - (f ≫ b.inl + g ≫ b.inr)) ≫ b.fst = 0 := by         simpa using sub_eq_zero.2 h₁       have h₂' : (m - (f ≫ b.inl + g ≫ b.inr)) ≫ b.snd = 0 := by simpa using sub_eq_zero.2 h₂       obtain ⟨q : T ⟶ X, hq : q ≫ b.inl = m - (f ≫ b.inl + g ≫ b.inr)⟩ :=         KernelFork.IsLimit.lift' hb _ h₂'       rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← hq, ← Category.comp_id q, ← b.inl_fst, ← Category.assoc, hq, h₁',         zero_comp]
CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil.description: In a preadditive category, if a binary bicone is such that one of its components acts as the kernel for a morphism, then that bicone can be classified as a bilimit.
