CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil.fullDefinition: def BinaryBicone.isBilimitOfCokernelFst {X Y : C} (b : BinaryBicone X Y)     (hb : IsColimit b.inrCokernelCofork) : b.IsBilimit :=   isBinaryBilimitOfIsColimit _ <|     BinaryCofan.IsColimit.mk _ (fun f g => b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g) (fun f g => by simp)       (fun f g => by simp) fun {T} f g m h₁ h₂ => by       dsimp at m       have h₁' : b.inl ≫ (m - (b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g)) = 0 := by simpa using sub_eq_zero.2 h₁       have h₂' : b.inr ≫ (m - (b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g)) = 0 := by simpa using sub_eq_zero.2 h₂       obtain ⟨q : X ⟶ T, hq : b.fst ≫ q = m - (b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g)⟩ :=         CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' hb _ h₂'       rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← hq, ← Category.id_comp q, ← b.inl_fst, Category.assoc, hq, h₁',         comp_zero]
CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil.description: If a binary bicone has its first morphism as the cokernel of its second morphism, then that bicone is confirmed to be a bilimit.

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBilimitOfCokernelSnd.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C]

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil.comment:
If `b` is a binary bicone such that `b.snd` is a cokernel of `b.inl`, then `b` is a bilimit
bicone.

CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil.fullDefinition: def BinaryBicone.isBilimitOfCokernelSnd {X Y : C} (b : BinaryBicone X Y)     (hb : IsColimit b.inlCokernelCofork) : b.IsBilimit :=   isBinaryBilimitOfIsColimit _ <|     BinaryCofan.IsColimit.mk _ (fun f g => b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g) (fun f g => by simp)       (fun f g => by simp) fun {T} f g m h₁ h₂ => by       dsimp at m       have h₁' : b.inl ≫ (m - (b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g)) = 0 := by simpa using sub_eq_zero.2 h₁       have h₂' : b.inr ≫ (m - (b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g)) = 0 := by simpa using sub_eq_zero.2 h₂       obtain ⟨q : Y ⟶ T, hq : b.snd ≫ q = m - (b.fst ≫ f + b.snd ≫ g)⟩ :=         CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' hb _ h₁'       rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← hq, ← Category.id_comp q, ← b.inr_snd, Category.assoc, hq, h₂',         comp_zero]

CategoryTheory.Limits.binaryBiconeOfIsSp.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.binaryBiconeOfIsSplitEpiOfKernel.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] {X Y : C}
  {f : X ⟶ Y} [IsSplitEpi f] {c : KernelFork f} (i : IsLimit c) : BinaryBicone c.pt Y
CategoryTheory.Limits.binaryBiconeOfIsSp.comment:
Every split epi `f` with a kernel induces a binary bicone with `f` as its `snd` and
the kernel map as its `inl`.
We will show in `binary_bicone_of_is_split_mono_of_cokernel` that this binary bicone is in fact
already a biproduct.

CategoryTheory.Limits.binaryBiconeOfIsSp.fullDefinition: def binaryBiconeOfIsSplitEpiOfKernel {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} [IsSplitEpi f] {c : KernelFork f}     (i : IsLimit c) : BinaryBicone c.pt Y :=   { pt := X     fst :=       let c' : KernelFork (𝟙 X - (𝟙 X - f ≫ section_ f)) := KernelFork.ofι (Fork.ι c) (by simp)       let i' : IsLimit c' := isKernelCompMono i (section_ f) (by simp)       let i'' := isLimitForkOfKernelFork i'       (splitMonoOfIdempotentOfIsLimitFork C (by simp) i'').retraction     snd := f     inl := c.ι     inr := section_ f     inl_fst := by apply SplitMono.id     inl_snd := by simp     inr_fst := by       dsimp only       rw [splitMonoOfIdempotentOfIsLimitFork_retraction, isLimitForkOfKernelFork_lift,         isKernelCompMono_lift]       dsimp only [kernelForkOfFork_ι]       letI := mono_of_isLimit_fork i       apply zero_of_comp_mono c.ι       simp only [comp_sub, Category.comp_id, Category.assoc, sub_self, Fork.IsLimit.lift_ι,         Fork.ι_ofι, IsSplitEpi.id_assoc]     inr_snd := by simp }
CategoryTheory.Limits.binaryBiconeOfIsSp.description: Every split epimorphism with a kernel produces a binary bicone where the kernel morphism serves as one of the mappings and the split epimorphism acts as the other.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitBinaryBic.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitBinaryBiconeOfIsSplitEpiOfKernel.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C]
  {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} [IsSplitEpi f] {c : KernelFork f} (i : IsLimit c) :
  (binaryBiconeOfIsSplitEpiOfKernel i).IsBilimit
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitBinaryBic.comment:
The bicone constructed in `binaryBiconeOfIsSplitEpiOfKernel` is a bilimit.
This is a version of the splitting lemma that holds in all preadditive categories.

CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitBinaryBic.fullDefinition: def isBilimitBinaryBiconeOfIsSplitEpiOfKernel {X Y : C} {f : X ⟶ Y} [IsSplitEpi f]     {c : KernelFork f} (i : IsLimit c) : (binaryBiconeOfIsSplitEpiOfKernel i).IsBilimit :=   BinaryBicone.isBilimitOfKernelInl _ <| i.ofIsoLimit <| Fork.ext (Iso.refl _) (by simp)
CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitBinaryBic.description: This definition confirms that the bicone derived from a split epimorphism's kernel is a bilimit in any preadditive category, extending a version of the splitting lemma.

CategoryTheory.subsingleton_preadditive_.fullDefinition: instance subsingleton_preadditive_of_hasBinaryBiproducts {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]     [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasBinaryBiproducts C] : Subsingleton (Preadditive C) where   allEq := fun a b => by     apply Preadditive.ext; funext X Y; apply AddCommGroup.ext; funext f g     have h₁ := @biprod.add_eq_lift_id_desc _ _ a _ _ f g       (by convert (inferInstance : HasBinaryBiproduct X X); subsingleton)     have h₂ := @biprod.add_eq_lift_id_desc _ _ b _ _ f g       (by convert (inferInstance : HasBinaryBiproduct X X); subsingleton)     refine h₁.trans (Eq.trans ?_ h₂.symm)     congr! 2 <;> subsingleton

CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] [HasBinaryBiproducts C]
  {X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂ : C} (f₁₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (f₁₂ : X₁ ⟶ Y₂) (f₂₁ : X₂ ⟶ Y₁) (f₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) [IsIso f₁₁] :
  (L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂) ×'
    (R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) ×'
      (g₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) ×' L.hom ≫ Biprod.ofComponents f₁₁ f₁₂ f₂₁ f₂₂ ≫ R.hom = biprod.map f₁₁ g₂₂
CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian'.comment:
If `f` is a morphism `X₁ ⊞ X₂ ⟶ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂` whose `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` entry is an isomorphism,
then we can construct isomorphisms `L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂` and `R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂`
so that `L.hom ≫ g ≫ R.hom` is diagonal (with `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` component still `f`),
via Gaussian elimination.

(This is the version of `Biprod.gaussian` written in terms of components.)

CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian'.fullDefinition: def Biprod.gaussian' [IsIso f₁₁] :     Σ' (L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂) (R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) (g₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂),       L.hom ≫ Biprod.ofComponents f₁₁ f₁₂ f₂₁ f₂₂ ≫ R.hom = biprod.map f₁₁ g₂₂ :=   ⟨Biprod.unipotentLower (-f₂₁ ≫ inv f₁₁), Biprod.unipotentUpper (-inv f₁₁ ≫ f₁₂),     f₂₂ - f₂₁ ≫ inv f₁₁ ≫ f₁₂, by ext <;> simp; abel⟩
CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian'.description: This definition describes a process of diagonalizing a morphism between biproducts, using isomorphisms and Gaussian elimination when one of the component morphisms is an isomorphism.

    (R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) ×' (g₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) ×' L.hom ≫ f ≫ R.hom = biprod.map (biprod.inl ≫ f ≫ biprod.fst) g₂₂

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.inl: This definition describes the morphism corresponding to the first inclusion in a binary cofan within a categorical framework.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.inr: This definition describes a morphism that represents the second inclusion from a binary cofan into the right component of an associated structured pair in category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.inl: This definition describes the morphism that represents the inclusion of an object into the first summand of a binary biproduct.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.inr: This definition specifies the morphism that includes an object into the second component of a binary biproduct structure in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.map: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism between two binary biproducts by using morphisms defined on their respective summands.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Biprod.ofComponents_eq: This theorem states that in a preadditive category with binary biproducts, a morphism from the biproduct of two pairs of components is equal to the morphism formed by their respective projections through certain inclusion mappings.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian': This definition describes a process of diagonalizing a morphism between biproducts, using isomorphisms and Gaussian elimination when one of the component morphisms is an isomorphism.

CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian.fullDefinition: def Biprod.gaussian (f : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ⟶ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) [IsIso (biprod.inl ≫ f ≫ biprod.fst)] :     Σ' (L : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ X₁ ⊞ X₂) (R : Y₁ ⊞ Y₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) (g₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂),       L.hom ≫ f ≫ R.hom = biprod.map (biprod.inl ≫ f ≫ biprod.fst) g₂₂ := by   let this :=     Biprod.gaussian' (biprod.inl ≫ f ≫ biprod.fst) (biprod.inl ≫ f ≫ biprod.snd)       (biprod.inr ≫ f ≫ biprod.fst) (biprod.inr ≫ f ≫ biprod.snd)   rwa [Biprod.ofComponents_eq] at this
CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian.description: If a morphism from the biproduct of two objects to another has an isomorphism in its first entry, it allows for the construction of specific isomorphisms such that the composition results in a diagonal block structure while preserving that first component morphism.

CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim'.code:
CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim'.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] [HasBinaryBiproducts C]
  {X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂ : C} (f₁₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁) (f₁₂ : X₁ ⟶ Y₂) (f₂₁ : X₂ ⟶ Y₁) (f₂₂ : X₂ ⟶ Y₂) [IsIso f₁₁]
  [IsIso (Biprod.ofComponents f₁₁ f₁₂ f₂₁ f₂₂)] : X₂ ≅ Y₂
CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim'.comment:
If `X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂` via a two-by-two matrix whose `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` entry is an isomorphism,
then we can construct an isomorphism `X₂ ≅ Y₂`, via Gaussian elimination.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.map: This definition describes how to construct a morphism between two biproducts using a collection of maps between their corresponding summands indexed by the same type.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biprod.map: This definition provides a way to construct a morphism between two binary biproducts by using morphisms defined on their respective summands.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Biprod.ofComponents: This definition constructs a morphism between the biproducts of two objects by combining their individual morphisms into a "matrix" structure, respecting the relationships established by the specified components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Biprod.gaussian': This definition describes a process of diagonalizing a morphism between biproducts, using isomorphisms and Gaussian elimination when one of the component morphisms is an isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.isIso_right_of_isIso_bipr: If the biproduct map of two morphisms is invertible, then the second morphism is also invertible.

CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim'.fullDefinition: def Biprod.isoElim' [IsIso f₁₁] [IsIso (Biprod.ofComponents f₁₁ f₁₂ f₂₁ f₂₂)] : X₂ ≅ Y₂ := by   obtain ⟨L, R, g, w⟩ := Biprod.gaussian' f₁₁ f₁₂ f₂₁ f₂₂   letI : IsIso (biprod.map f₁₁ g) := by     rw [← w]     infer_instance   letI : IsIso g := isIso_right_of_isIso_biprod_map f₁₁ g   exact asIso g
CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim'.description: This definition states that if a biproduct of two objects is isomorphic to another biproduct where one component morphism is an isomorphism, then an isomorphism between the second objects can be constructed using Gaussian elimination.

CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim.code:
CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim.{v, u} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C] [Preadditive C] [HasBinaryBiproducts C]
  {X₁ X₂ Y₁ Y₂ : C} (f : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) [IsIso (biprod.inl ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.fst)] : X₂ ≅ Y₂
CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim.comment:
If `f` is an isomorphism `X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂` whose `X₁ ⟶ Y₁` entry is an isomorphism,
then we can construct an isomorphism `X₂ ≅ Y₂`, via Gaussian elimination.

CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim.fullDefinition: def Biprod.isoElim (f : X₁ ⊞ X₂ ≅ Y₁ ⊞ Y₂) [IsIso (biprod.inl ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.fst)] : X₂ ≅ Y₂ :=   letI :     IsIso       (Biprod.ofComponents (biprod.inl ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.fst) (biprod.inl ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.snd)         (biprod.inr ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.fst) (biprod.inr ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.snd)) := by     simp only [Biprod.ofComponents_eq]     infer_instance   Biprod.isoElim' (biprod.inl ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.fst) (biprod.inl ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.snd)     (biprod.inr ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.fst) (biprod.inr ≫ f.hom ≫ biprod.snd)
CategoryTheory.Biprod.isoElim.description: If an isomorphism exists between the biproducts of two pairs of objects and the first entry of this isomorphism is an isomorphism, then an isomorphism can be derived between the second objects of these pairs through a process akin to Gaussian elimination.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.π: This definition describes a function that provides the morphism from the cone point of a bicone to a specific object in the diagram associated with the bicone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Bicone.ι: This definition describes a function that provides the morphism from a specific object in the diagram associated with a bicone to the cone point of that bicone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.π: This definition describes a natural transformation from a constant functor at a specific point to another functor, capturing the relationship between a cone and the functor it pertains to.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocone.ι: This definition describes a natural transformation from a functor to a constant functor at a specified point in a category.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biproduct.ι: This definition specifies an inclusion morphism from an individual summand to a biproduct object in the context of category theory.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.π: This definition describes a specific morphism associated with a cofork of two parallel morphisms, mapping from a particular object in a diagram to the point of the cofork.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ι: This definition introduces a morphism that connects a given point of a fork on two parallel morphisms to the zero instance of a parallel pair formed by those morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Biproduct.column_nonzero_.description: In a preadditive category, if an isomorphism exists from the biproduct of two families of objects, then the identity morphism on one summand is zero if the compositions with the biproduct projections yield zero for all components.

CategoryTheory.Biproduct.columnNonzeroOf.comment:
If `f : ⨁ S ⟶ ⨁ T` is an isomorphism, and `s` is a non-trivial summand of the source,
then there is some `t` in the target so that the `s, t` matrix entry of `f` is nonzero.

explanatories.Trunc: This definition introduces a type that represents the quotient of another type under the trivial equivalence relation, facilitating computability while encapsulating the idea of propositional truncation.
explanatories.truncSigmaOfExists: This definition states that if there exists an element satisfying a property within a finite type, then this existence can be represented in a truncated dependent sum format.
explanatories.Classical.not_exists_not: The absence of an element that does not satisfy a property is equivalent to the assertion that every element satisfies that property.

CategoryTheory.Biproduct.columnNonzeroOf.fullDefinition: def Biproduct.columnNonzeroOfIso {σ τ : Type} [Fintype τ] {S : σ → C} [HasBiproduct S] {T : τ → C}     [HasBiproduct T] (s : σ) (nz : 𝟙 (S s) ≠ 0) (f : ⨁ S ⟶ ⨁ T) [IsIso f] :     Trunc (Σ't : τ, biproduct.ι S s ≫ f ≫ biproduct.π T t ≠ 0) := by   classical     apply truncSigmaOfExists     have t := Biproduct.column_nonzero_of_iso'.{v} s f     by_contra h     simp only [not_exists_not] at h     exact nz (t h)
CategoryTheory.Biproduct.columnNonzeroOf.description: If an isomorphism exists between two biproducts and one of the summands in the source is non-trivial, then there is a corresponding non-zero entry in the target matrix.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesProductOf.comment:
A functor between preadditive categories that preserves (zero morphisms and) finite biproducts
preserves finite products.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.functor: This definition asserts that any function mapping from a discrete type to a category yields a functor between the discrete category and that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.ofIsoLimit: This definition establishes that if one cone is a limit cone, then any cone isomorphic to it is also a limit cone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biconeIsBilimitOfL: This definition asserts that any limit cone over a finite family of objects can be transformed into a bilimit bicone within a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.ext: In a preadditive category, if two objects have isomorphic hom groups, they are considered equal.
explanatories.AddCommGroup.ext: This theorem asserts that two additive commutative groups are equal if their addition operations are identical.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.postcompos: This definition establishes an equivalence between the property of being a limit for a cone after postcomposition with the inverse of a natural isomorphism and the property of being a limit for the original cone.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.compNatIsoDiscre: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the composition of two functors, showing that applying a functor to a discrete functor results in an equivalent form of composition with the objects from the first functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitOfPreserv: This definition states that if a functor preserves biproducts and a bicone is a bilimit, then the image of that bicone under the functor is also a bilimit.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesProductOf.fullDefinition: def preservesProductOfPreservesBiproduct {f : J → C} [PreservesBiproduct f F] :     PreservesLimit (Discrete.functor f) F where   preserves hc :=     IsLimit.ofIsoLimit         ((IsLimit.postcomposeInvEquiv (Discrete.compNatIsoDiscrete _ _) _).symm           (isBilimitOfPreserves F (biconeIsBilimitOfLimitConeOfIsLimit hc)).isLimit) <|       Cones.ext (Iso.refl _) (by rintro ⟨⟩; simp)
CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesProductOf.description: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves zero morphisms and finite biproducts also preserves finite products.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesProductsO.fullDefinition: def preservesProductsOfShapeOfPreservesBiproductsOfShape [PreservesBiproductsOfShape J F] :     PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete J) F where   preservesLimit {_} := preservesLimitOfIsoDiagram _ Discrete.natIsoFunctor.symm

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBiproduct.fullDefinition: def preservesBiproductOfPreservesProduct {f : J → C} [PreservesLimit (Discrete.functor f) F] :     PreservesBiproduct f F where   preserves {b} hb :=     isBilimitOfIsLimit _ <|       IsLimit.ofIsoLimit           ((IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv (Discrete.compNatIsoDiscrete _ _) (F.mapCone b.toCone)).symm             (isLimitOfPreserves F hb.isLimit)) <|         Cones.ext (Iso.refl _) (by rintro ⟨⟩; simp)
CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBiproduct.description: A functor between preadditive categories that preserves finite products and zero morphisms also preserves finite biproducts.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBiproduct.code:
CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBiproductOfMonoBiproductComparison.{v, v', u, u'} {C : Type u} [Category.{v, u} C]
  [Preadditive C] {D : Type u'} [Category.{v', u'} D] [Preadditive D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] {J : Type}
  [Fintype J] {f : J → C} [HasBiproduct f] [HasBiproduct (F.obj ∘ f)] [Mono (F.biproductComparison f)] :
  PreservesBiproduct f F
CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBiproduct.comment:
If the (product-like) biproduct comparison for `F` and `f` is a monomorphism, then `F`
preserves the biproduct of `f`. For the converse, see `mapBiproduct`.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBiproduct.fullDefinition: def preservesBiproductOfMonoBiproductComparison {f : J → C} [HasBiproduct f]     [HasBiproduct (F.obj ∘ f)] [Mono (biproductComparison F f)] : PreservesBiproduct f F := by   haveI : HasProduct fun b => F.obj (f b) := by     change HasProduct (F.obj ∘ f)     infer_instance   have that : piComparison F f =       (F.mapIso (biproduct.isoProduct f)).inv ≫         biproductComparison F f ≫ (biproduct.isoProduct _).hom := by     ext j     convert piComparison_comp_π F f j; simp [← Function.comp_def, ← Functor.map_comp]   haveI : IsIso (biproductComparison F f) := isIso_of_mono_of_isSplitEpi _   haveI : IsIso (piComparison F f) := by     rw [that]     infer_instance   haveI := PreservesProduct.ofIsoComparison F f   apply preservesBiproductOfPreservesProduct
CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBiproduct.description: This definition asserts that if the comparison morphism between a functor and a biproduct is a monomorphism, then the functor preserves the biproduct structure of the given collection of objects.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.functor: This definition asserts that any function mapping from a discrete type to a category yields a functor between the discrete category and that category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofIsoCol: This definition states that if a cocone is a colimit and there is an isomorphism between two cocones, then the second cocone is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.biconeIsBilimitOfC: This definition asserts that any cocone that serves as a colimit can be transformed into a bilimit bicone within a preadditive category.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.ext: In a preadditive category, if two objects have isomorphic hom groups, they are considered equal.
explanatories.AddCommGroup.ext: This theorem asserts that two additive commutative groups are equal if their addition operations are identical.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Discrete.compNatIsoDiscre: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the composition of two functors, showing that applying a functor to a discrete functor results in an equivalent form of composition with the objects from the first functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isBilimitOfPreserv: This definition states that if a functor preserves biproducts and a bicone is a bilimit, then the image of that bicone under the functor is also a bilimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.precompo: This definition establishes an equivalence between the condition of a cocone transformed by a natural isomorphism being a colimit and the original cocone being a colimit.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBinaryPro.fullDefinition: def preservesBinaryProductOfPreservesBinaryBiproduct {X Y : C} [PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F] :     PreservesLimit (pair X Y) F where   preserves {c} hc := IsLimit.ofIsoLimit         ((IsLimit.postcomposeInvEquiv (diagramIsoPair _) _).symm           (isBinaryBilimitOfPreserves F (binaryBiconeIsBilimitOfLimitConeOfIsLimit hc)).isLimit) <|       Cones.ext (by dsimp; rfl) fun j => by         rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩ <;> simp

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBinaryBip.fullDefinition: def preservesBinaryBiproductOfMonoBiprodComparison {X Y : C} [HasBinaryBiproduct X Y]     [HasBinaryBiproduct (F.obj X) (F.obj Y)] [Mono (biprodComparison F X Y)] :     PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F := by   have that :     prodComparison F X Y =       (F.mapIso (biprod.isoProd X Y)).inv ≫ biprodComparison F X Y ≫ (biprod.isoProd _ _).hom := by     ext <;> simp [← Functor.map_comp]   haveI : IsIso (biprodComparison F X Y) := isIso_of_mono_of_isSplitEpi _   haveI : IsIso (prodComparison F X Y) := by     rw [that]     infer_instance   haveI := PreservesLimitPair.ofIsoProdComparison F X Y   apply preservesBinaryBiproductOfPreservesBinaryProduct

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cones.ext: This definition states that two cones associated with a functor are isomorphic if their apexes are isomorphic and the corresponding structure maps are compatible with this isomorphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.ofIsoCol: This definition states that if a cocone is a colimit and there is an isomorphism between two cocones, then the second cocone is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.ext: This definition states that two cocones are isomorphic if there is an isomorphism between their apexes that commutes with the corresponding cocone structure maps.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.pair: This definition describes a functor that maps a structured pair of points to two objects in a category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.binaryBiconeIsBili: This definition establishes that any colimit cocone over a finite pair of objects can be converted into a bilimit bicone within a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.ext: In a preadditive category, if two objects have isomorphic hom groups, they are considered equal.
explanatories.AddCommGroup.ext: This theorem asserts that two additive commutative groups are equal if their addition operations are identical.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.precompo: This definition establishes an equivalence between the condition of a cocone transformed by a natural isomorphism being a colimit and the original cocone being a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.diagramIsoPair: This definition asserts that any functor originating from a structured pair can be naturally identified with the pair of its respective components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isBinaryBilimitOfP: This definition states that a functor preserves binary biproducts if it maps any bilimit bicone over two objects to a bilimit bicone over their images under the functor.

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBinaryCop.fullDefinition: def preservesBinaryCoproductOfPreservesBinaryBiproduct {X Y : C} [PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F] :     PreservesColimit (pair X Y) F where   preserves {c} hc :=     IsColimit.ofIsoColimit         ((IsColimit.precomposeHomEquiv (diagramIsoPair _) _).symm           (isBinaryBilimitOfPreserves F               (binaryBiconeIsBilimitOfColimitCoconeOfIsColimit hc)).isColimit) <|       Cocones.ext (by dsimp; rfl) fun j => by         rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩ <;> simp

CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesBinaryBip.fullDefinition: def preservesBinaryBiproductOfPreservesBinaryCoproduct {X Y : C} [PreservesColimit (pair X Y) F] :     PreservesBinaryBiproduct X Y F where   preserves {b} hb :=     isBinaryBilimitOfIsColimit _ <|       IsColimit.ofIsoColimit           ((IsColimit.precomposeInvEquiv (diagramIsoPair _) (F.mapCocone b.toCocone)).symm             (isColimitOfPreserves F hb.isColimit)) <|         Cocones.ext (Iso.refl _) fun j => by           rcases j with ⟨⟨⟩⟩ <;> simp

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.parallelPair: The definition represents a diagram in a category formed by two morphisms that share the same source and target objects.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapCone: This definition describes how to obtain a new cone in one category from an existing cone in another category by applying a functor that maps between the two categories.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.ofLim: Any limit cone over a pair of objects in a preadditive category can be transformed into a binary bicone structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.snd: This definition describes a morphism from the cone point of a binary bicone to one of its objects, capturing the connection between the bicone and its components.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.sndKe: This definition constructs a kernel fork associated with the second component of a binary bicone, using the inclusion morphism from the first summand.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isLim: This definition asserts that the kernel fork associated with the second projection of a binary bicone is indeed a limit if the original cone is a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitMapConeBina: This definition establishes a natural equivalence between the property of a functor mapping a binary fan being a limit and the corresponding binary fan formed from the mapped morphisms also being a limit.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.isBil: In a preadditive category, if a binary bicone is such that one of its components acts as the kernel for a morphism, then that bicone can be classified as a bilimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.mapBinaryBicone: This definition creates a new binary bicone from an existing binary bicone by applying a functor that preserves zero morphisms to its objects.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitMapConeFork: This definition establishes a bijection between the limit property of a mapped cone of a kernel fork and the limit property of the kernel fork formed by the images of the morphisms, under a functor that preserves zero morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.inl_s: This theorem asserts that in a binary bicone setup, the composition of the inclusion morphism of one object with the projection morphism to another yields a zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitOfPreserves: This definition establishes that if a functor preserves limits and a certain cone is a limit in the source category, then applying the functor will yield a limit cone in the target category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryCofan.mk: This definition constructs a binary cofan with a specified vertex and two inclusions from the respective objects into that vertex.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.kernelForkOfF: This theorem demonstrates the equivalence of the kernel fork of a fork formed by a morphism and a condition relating two morphisms to the kernel fork associated with the given morphism in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitForkMapOfIs: This definition states that if a functor preserves limit structures, then the limit property of a kernel fork in one category is preserved when mapped to another category under the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isLimitMapConeFork: This definition establishes a correspondence between the limit of a mapped fork in one category and the limit of the original morphisms in another category, allowing for the interchange of operations involving forks and functorial mappings.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.condition: The theorem states that for a given fork formed by two morphisms, the morphism from the fork satisfies the condition that it composed with both morphisms results in the same outcome.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.parallelPair.eqOfH: This definition provides a method to create a natural isomorphism between two parallel pairs of morphisms when the morphisms in each pair are equal.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_sub: The theorem states that applying an additive functor to the difference of two morphisms results in the difference of their individual images under the functor.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.isLimitForkOf: This definition establishes that if a kernel of the difference between two morphisms is a limit, then the corresponding fork associated with that kernel is also a limit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.postcompos: This definition states that a cone retains its limit property if it is transformed through post-composition with a natural isomorphism.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.functorial: This definition describes a functor that transforms cocones over a given functor into cocones over the composition of that functor with another functor while preserving the cocone structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.condition: This theorem states that for a cofork, the composition of its projection with both morphisms yields the same result, ensuring a specific relationship between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.parallelPair.ext: The definition constructs a natural isomorphism between two functors derived from a walking parallel pair based on specific isomorphisms at the vertices and the corresponding morphisms between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.ext: An isomorphism between two coforks can be established by providing an isomorphism between their respective cocone points and ensuring that the associated morphisms commute.

CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesEqualize.fullDefinition: def preservesEqualizerOfPreservesKernels [∀ {X Y} (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesLimit (parallelPair f 0) F]     {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : PreservesLimit (parallelPair f g) F := by   letI := preservesBinaryBiproductsOfPreservesBinaryProducts F   haveI := additive_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts F   constructor; intro c i   let c' := isLimitKernelForkOfFork (i.ofIsoLimit (Fork.isoForkOfι c))   dsimp only [kernelForkOfFork_ofι] at c'   let iFc := isLimitForkMapOfIsLimit' F _ c'   apply IsLimit.ofIsoLimit _ ((Cones.functoriality _ F).mapIso (Fork.isoForkOfι c).symm)   apply (isLimitMapConeForkEquiv F (Fork.condition c)).invFun   let p : parallelPair (F.map (f - g)) 0 ≅ parallelPair (F.map f - F.map g) 0 :=     parallelPair.eqOfHomEq F.map_sub rfl   exact     IsLimit.ofIsoLimit       (isLimitForkOfKernelFork ((IsLimit.postcomposeHomEquiv p _).symm iFc))       (Fork.ext (Iso.refl _) (by simp [p]))

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.BinaryBicone.ofCol: Any colimit cocone over a pair of objects in a preadditive category can be transformed into a binary bicone structure.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitOfPreserv: This definition states that if a functor preserves colimits and a cocone is a colimit in the source category, then the mapped cocone in the target category is also a colimit.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.additive_of_prese: The theorem states that a functor which preserves binary biproducts and zero morphisms is classified as an additive functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.condition: The theorem states that for a given fork formed by two morphisms, the morphism from the fork satisfies the condition that it composed with both morphisms results in the same outcome.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Fork.ext: This definition states that to establish an isomorphism between two forks, it is sufficient to provide an isomorphism of their cone points that satisfies a specific commutativity condition with respect to their morphisms.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cocones.functorial: This definition describes a functor that transforms cocones over a given functor into cocones over the composition of that functor with another functor while preserving the cocone structure.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.isColimitCoke: This definition states that if a cofork of two morphisms is a colimit, then the associated cokernel cofork formed from that cofork is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.isoCoforkOf: Every cofork can be seen as isomorphic to a cofork defined by a specific universal property associated with a given collection of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.cokernelCofor: This theorem demonstrates that the cokernel cofork of a cofork constructed from a morphism and a relation involving another morphism is equal to the cokernel cofork defined from the same morphism and structure.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitCoforkMap: This definition indicates that if a functor preserves certain cokernels and a specific cofork derived from a morphism is a colimit, then the corresponding cofork of the mapped morphism is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitMapCocone: This definition establishes an equivalence between the property of a cocone being a colimit after mapping through a functor and the property of a corresponding cocone formed by the images of that functor also being a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.condition: This theorem states that for a cofork, the composition of its projection with both morphisms yields the same result, ensuring a specific relationship between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.parallelPair.ext: The definition constructs a natural isomorphism between two functors derived from a walking parallel pair based on specific isomorphisms at the vertices and the corresponding morphisms between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.isColimitCofo: This definition asserts that if a cofork corresponds to the cokernel of the difference between two morphisms in a preadditive category, then it itself is a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.precompo: This definition establishes an equivalence between the condition of a cocone transformed by a natural isomorphism being a colimit and the original cocone being a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.ext: An isomorphism between two coforks can be established by providing an isomorphism between their respective cocone points and ensuring that the associated morphisms commute.

CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesCoequali.fullDefinition: def preservesCoequalizerOfPreservesCokernels     [∀ {X Y} (f : X ⟶ Y), PreservesColimit (parallelPair f 0) F] {X Y : C} (f g : X ⟶ Y) :     PreservesColimit (parallelPair f g) F := by   letI := preservesBinaryBiproductsOfPreservesBinaryCoproducts F   haveI := additive_of_preservesBinaryBiproducts F   constructor   intro c i   let c' := isColimitCokernelCoforkOfCofork (i.ofIsoColimit (Cofork.isoCoforkOfπ c))   dsimp only [cokernelCoforkOfCofork_ofπ] at c'   let iFc := isColimitCoforkMapOfIsColimit' F _ c'   apply     IsColimit.ofIsoColimit _ ((Cocones.functoriality _ F).mapIso (Cofork.isoCoforkOfπ c).symm)   apply (isColimitMapCoconeCoforkEquiv F (Cofork.condition c)).invFun   let p : parallelPair (F.map (f - g)) 0 ≅ parallelPair (F.map f - F.map g) 0 :=     parallelPair.ext (Iso.refl _) (Iso.refl _) (by simp) (by simp)   exact     IsColimit.ofIsoColimit       (isColimitCoforkOfCokernelCofork ((IsColimit.precomposeHomEquiv p.symm _).symm iFc))       (Cofork.ext (Iso.refl _) (by simp [p]))

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitCoforkMap: This definition indicates that if a functor preserves certain cokernels and a specific cofork derived from a morphism is a colimit, then the corresponding cofork of the mapped morphism is also a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.isColimitMapCocone: This definition establishes an equivalence between the property of a cocone being a colimit after mapping through a functor and the property of a corresponding cocone formed by the images of that functor also being a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.condition: This theorem states that for a cofork, the composition of its projection with both morphisms yields the same result, ensuring a specific relationship between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.parallelPair.ext: The definition constructs a natural isomorphism between two functors derived from a walking parallel pair based on specific isomorphisms at the vertices and the corresponding morphisms between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.isColimitCofo: This definition asserts that if a cofork corresponds to the cokernel of the difference between two morphisms in a preadditive category, then it itself is a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.IsColimit.precompo: This definition establishes an equivalence between the condition of a cocone transformed by a natural isomorphism being a colimit and the original cocone being a colimit.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.Cofork.ext: An isomorphism between two coforks can be established by providing an isomorphism between their respective cocone points and ensuring that the associated morphisms commute.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Algebra.Hom.f: This definition describes the underlying morphism between the carriers of two algebras associated with the same endofunctor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_add: The theorem asserts that for an additive functor, the image of the sum of two morphisms is equal to the sum of the images of each morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition with a morphism preserves the addition of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Algebra.Hom.h: This theorem establishes a compatibility condition between the structure morphisms of two algebras associated with the same endofunctor and a morphism between them.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Algebra.Hom.e: This theorem states that if two morphisms between algebras of an endofunctor are equal when their underlying functions are equal, then the morphisms themselves are identical.
explanatories.add_assoc: This theorem states that the addition operation is associative, meaning that the grouping of three elements being added does not affect the result.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_zero: This theorem establishes that a functor, which preserves zero morphisms, will map the zero morphism from one category to the zero morphism in another category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.zero_comp: This theorem states that composing a zero morphism with any morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Limits.comp_zero: This theorem states that the composition of any morphism with a zero morphism results in a zero morphism.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_nsmul: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition of a morphism with a scalar multiple of another morphism is equal to the scalar multiplication of the first morphism followed by the second morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_nsmul: The theorem states that applying an additive functor to the scalar multiplication of a morphism results in the same scalar multiplication applied to the functor's image of that morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.nsmul_comp: This theorem asserts that in a preadditive category, scalar multiplication of a morphism commutes with the composition of that morphism with other morphisms.
explanatories.zero_smul: This theorem confirms that scalar multiplication of any element by zero yields zero within a structure that supports scalar multiplication with zero.
explanatories.succ_nsmul: This theorem establishes that multiplying an element in an additive monoid by a successor of a natural number is equivalent to adding the result of multiplying that element by the original natural number to the element itself.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_neg: The theorem states that applying an additive functor to the negation of a morphism results in the negation of the image of that morphism under the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.neg_comp: This theorem establishes that negating a morphism before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category yields the same result as negating the composition of the morphism with the second morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_neg: This theorem demonstrates that composing a morphism with the negation of another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to negating the composition of the first morphism with the second morphism.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_sub: The theorem states that applying an additive functor to the difference of two morphisms results in the difference of their individual images under the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.sub_comp: This theorem states that the composition of the difference of two morphisms with a subsequent morphism is equal to the difference of their individual compositions with that morphism in a preadditive category.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_sub: This theorem establishes that composing a morphism with the difference of two other morphisms yields the same result as composing it with each morphism separately and then taking their difference.
explanatories.sub_eq_add_neg: Subtracting an element from another is equivalent to adding the negative of that element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, composing a morphism with an integer-scaled morphism is equivalent to scaling the composition of the original morphism with the other morphism by the same integer.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Functor.map_zsmul: The theorem states that applying an additive functor to a scalar multiplication of a morphism results in the scalar multiplication of the image of that morphism under the functor.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.zsmul_comp: This theorem demonstrates that multiplying a morphism by an integer before composing it with another morphism in a preadditive category is equivalent to multiplying the composition by the same integer.
explanatories.natCast_zsmul: This theorem asserts that in a subtractive negative monoid, scaling an element by a natural number either through a natural number cast or directly leads to the same result.
explanatories.negSucc_zsmul: This theorem states that in a subtractive negative monoid, scaling an element by the negative successor of a natural number is equivalent to negating the scaling of that element by one more than the original natural number.
explanatories.neg_inj: The negation of two elements in an involutive negation structure is equal if and only if the original elements are equal.
explanatories.nsmul_eq_smul_cast: The theorem establishes that multiplying an element of a module by a natural number is equivalent to multiplying that element by the corresponding integer represented by the same natural number.
explanatories.add_left_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, the sum of an element and its additive inverse equals the zero element.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.Coalgebra.Hom: This definition describes the morphism that relates the underlying objects of two coalgebras through a given morphism between them.
This theorem provides a compatibility condition for morphisms between coalgebras, linking their structure maps through the action of the endofunctor.
This theorem demonstrates that two morphisms between coalgebras are equal if their corresponding structure morphisms are identical.

β.f           h := by simp only [Functor.map_sub, sub_comp, Endofunctor.Algebra.Hom.h, comp_sub] }       zsmul := fun r α =>         { f := r • α.f           h := by rw [comp_zsmul, Functor.map_zsmul, zsmul_comp, Endofunctor.Algebra.Hom.h] }       add_assoc := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply add_assoc       zero_add := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply zero_add       add_zero := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply add_zero       nsmul_zero := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply zero_smul       nsmul_succ := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply succ_nsmul       sub_eq_add_neg := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply sub_eq_add_neg       zsmul_zero' := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply zero_smul       zsmul_succ' := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         dsimp         simp only [natCast_zsmul, succ_nsmul]         rfl       zsmul_neg' := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         simp only [negSucc_zsmul, neg_inj, nsmul_eq_smul_cast ℤ]       add_left_neg := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply add_left_neg       add_comm := by         intros         apply Algebra.Hom.ext         apply add_comm }   add_comp := by     intros     apply Algebra.Hom.ext     apply add_comp   comp_add := by     intros     apply Algebra.Hom.ext     apply comp_add

explanatories.sub_eq_add_neg: Subtracting an element from another is equivalent to adding the negative of that element.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_zsmul: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, composing a morphism with an integer-scaled morphism is equivalent to scaling the composition of the original morphism with the other morphism by the same integer.

explanatories.natCast_zsmul: This theorem asserts that in a subtractive negative monoid, scaling an element by a natural number either through a natural number cast or directly leads to the same result.
explanatories.negSucc_zsmul: This theorem states that in a subtractive negative monoid, scaling an element by the negative successor of a natural number is equivalent to negating the scaling of that element by one more than the original natural number.
explanatories.neg_inj: The negation of two elements in an involutive negation structure is equal if and only if the original elements are equal.
explanatories.nsmul_eq_smul_cast: The theorem establishes that multiplying an element of a module by a natural number is equivalent to multiplying that element by the corresponding integer represented by the same natural number.
explanatories.add_left_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, the sum of an element and its additive inverse equals the zero element.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Comonad.Coalgebra.Hom.f: This definition describes the morphism that relates the underlying objects of two coalgebras in the context of a comonad.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Comonad.Coalgebra.Hom.h: This theorem establishes that a morphism between coalgebras associated with a comonad commutes with their respective structure morphisms, ensuring compatibility within the coalgebra framework.

CategoryTheory.Monad.algebraPreadditive.fullDefinition: instance Monad.algebraPreadditive : Preadditive (Monad.Algebra T) where   homGroup F G :=     { add := fun α β =>         { f := α.f + β.f           h := by simp only [Functor.map_add, add_comp, Monad.Algebra.Hom.h, comp_add] }       zero :=         { f := 0           h := by simp only [Functor.map_zero, zero_comp, comp_zero] }       nsmul := fun n α =>         { f := n • α.f           h := by rw [Functor.map_nsmul, nsmul_comp, Monad.Algebra.Hom.h, comp_nsmul] }       neg := fun α =>         { f := -α.f           h := by simp only [Functor.map_neg, neg_comp, Monad.Algebra.Hom.h, comp_neg] }       sub := fun α β =>         { f := α.f - β.f           h := by simp only [Functor.map_sub, sub_comp, Monad.Algebra.Hom.h, comp_sub] }       zsmul := fun r α =>         { f := r • α.f           h := by rw [Functor.map_zsmul, zsmul_comp, Monad.Algebra.Hom.h, comp_zsmul] }       add_assoc := by         intros         ext         apply add_assoc       zero_add := by         intros         ext         apply zero_add       add_zero := by         intros         ext         apply add_zero       nsmul_zero := by         intros         ext         apply zero_smul       nsmul_succ := by         intros         ext         apply succ_nsmul       sub_eq_add_neg := by         intros         ext         apply sub_eq_add_neg       zsmul_zero' := by         intros         ext         apply zero_smul       zsmul_succ' := by         intros         ext         dsimp         simp only [natCast_zsmul, succ_nsmul]         rfl       zsmul_neg' := by         intros         ext         simp only [negSucc_zsmul, neg_inj, nsmul_eq_smul_cast ℤ]       add_left_neg := by         intros         ext         apply add_left_neg       add_comm := by         intros         ext         apply add_comm }   add_comp := by     intros     ext     apply add_comp   comp_add := by     intros     ext     apply comp_add

CategoryTheory.Mat_.hasFiniteBiproducts.comment:
We now prove that `Mat_ C` has finite biproducts.

Be warned, however, that `Mat_ C` is not necessarily Krull-Schmidt,
and so the internal indexing of a biproduct may have nothing to do with the external indexing,
even though the construction we give uses a sigma type.
See however `isoBiproductEmbedding`.

CategoryTheory.Mat_.hasFiniteBiproducts.fullDefinition: instance hasFiniteBiproducts : HasFiniteBiproducts (Mat_ C) where   out n :=     { has_biproduct := fun f =>         hasBiproduct_of_total           { pt := ⟨Σ j, (f j).ι, fun p => (f p.1).X p.2⟩             π := fun j x y => by               refine if h : x.1 = j then ?_ else 0               refine if h' : @Eq.ndrec (Fin n) x.1 (fun j => (f j).ι) x.2 _ h = y then ?_ else 0               apply eqToHom               substs h h'               rfl             -- Notice we were careful not to use `subst` until we had a goal in `Prop`.             ι := fun j x y => by               refine if h : y.1 = j then ?_ else 0               refine if h' : @Eq.ndrec _ y.1 (fun j => (f j).ι) y.2 _ h = x then ?_ else 0               apply eqToHom               substs h h'               rfl             ι_π := fun j j' => by               ext x y               dsimp               simp_rw [dite_comp, comp_dite]               simp only [ite_self, dite_eq_ite, dif_ctx_congr, Limits.comp_zero, Limits.zero_comp,                 eqToHom_trans, Finset.sum_congr]               erw [Finset.sum_sigma]               dsimp               simp only [if_congr, if_true, dif_ctx_congr, Finset.sum_dite_irrel, Finset.mem_univ,                 Finset.sum_const_zero, Finset.sum_congr, Finset.sum_dite_eq']               split_ifs with h h'               · substs h h'                 simp only [CategoryTheory.eqToHom_refl, CategoryTheory.Mat_.id_apply_self]               · subst h                 rw [eqToHom_refl, id_apply_of_ne _ _ _ h']               · rfl }           (by             dsimp             ext1 ⟨i, j⟩             rintro ⟨i', j'⟩             rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_apply]             dsimp             rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]; rotate_left             · intro b _ hb               apply Finset.sum_eq_zero               intro x _               rw [dif_neg hb.symm, zero_comp]             · intro hi               simp at hi             rw [Finset.sum_eq_single j]; rotate_left             · intro b _ hb               rw [dif_pos rfl, dif_neg, zero_comp]               simp only               tauto             · intro hj               simp at hj             simp only [eqToHom_refl, dite_eq_ite, ite_true, Category.id_comp, ne_eq,               Sigma.mk.inj_iff, not_and, id_def]             by_cases h : i' = i             · subst h               rw [dif_pos rfl]               simp only [heq_eq_eq, true_and]               by_cases h : j' = j               · subst h                 simp               · rw [dif_neg h, dif_neg (Ne.symm h)]             · rw [dif_neg h, dif_neg]               tauto) } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

category_theory.Mat_.has_finite_biproduc.fullDefinition: instance hasFiniteBiproducts : HasFiniteBiproducts (Mat_ C) where   out n :=     { has_biproduct := fun f =>         hasBiproduct_of_total           { pt := ⟨Σ j, (f j).ι, fun p => (f p.1).X p.2⟩             π := fun j x y => by               refine if h : x.1 = j then ?_ else 0               refine if h' : @Eq.ndrec (Fin n) x.1 (fun j => (f j).ι) x.2 _ h = y then ?_ else 0               apply eqToHom               substs h h'               rfl             -- Notice we were careful not to use `subst` until we had a goal in `Prop`.             ι := fun j x y => by               refine if h : y.1 = j then ?_ else 0               refine if h' : @Eq.ndrec _ y.1 (fun j => (f j).ι) y.2 _ h = x then ?_ else 0               apply eqToHom               substs h h'               rfl             ι_π := fun j j' => by               ext x y               dsimp               simp_rw [dite_comp, comp_dite]               simp only [ite_self, dite_eq_ite, dif_ctx_congr, Limits.comp_zero, Limits.zero_comp,                 eqToHom_trans, Finset.sum_congr]               erw [Finset.sum_sigma]               dsimp               simp only [if_congr, if_true, dif_ctx_congr, Finset.sum_dite_irrel, Finset.mem_univ,                 Finset.sum_const_zero, Finset.sum_congr, Finset.sum_dite_eq']               split_ifs with h h'               · substs h h'                 simp only [CategoryTheory.eqToHom_refl, CategoryTheory.Mat_.id_apply_self]               · subst h                 rw [eqToHom_refl, id_apply_of_ne _ _ _ h']               · rfl }           (by             dsimp             ext1 ⟨i, j⟩             rintro ⟨i', j'⟩             rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_apply]             dsimp             rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]; rotate_left             · intro b _ hb               apply Finset.sum_eq_zero               intro x _               rw [dif_neg hb.symm, zero_comp]             · intro hi               simp at hi             rw [Finset.sum_eq_single j]; rotate_left             · intro b _ hb               rw [dif_pos rfl, dif_neg, zero_comp]               simp only               tauto             · intro hj               simp at hj             simp only [eqToHom_refl, dite_eq_ite, ite_true, Category.id_comp, ne_eq,               Sigma.mk.inj_iff, not_and, id_def]             by_cases h : i' = i             · subst h               rw [dif_pos rfl]               simp only [heq_eq_eq, true_and]               by_cases h : j' = j               · subst h                 simp               · rw [dif_neg h, dif_neg (Ne.symm h)]             · rw [dif_neg h, dif_neg]               tauto) } set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

category_theory.Mat_.iso_biproduct_embed.fullDefinition: def isoBiproductEmbedding (M : Mat_ C) : M ≅ ⨁ fun i => (embedding C).obj (M.X i) where   hom := biproduct.lift fun i j k => if h : j = i then eqToHom (congr_arg M.X h) else 0   inv := biproduct.desc fun i j k => if h : i = k then eqToHom (congr_arg M.X h) else 0   hom_inv_id := by     simp only [biproduct.lift_desc]     funext i j     dsimp [id_def]     rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single i]; rotate_left     · intro b _ hb       dsimp       simp only [Finset.sum_singleton]       rw [dif_neg hb.symm, zero_comp]     · intro h       simp at h     simp   inv_hom_id := by     apply biproduct.hom_ext     intro i     apply biproduct.hom_ext'     intro j     simp only [Category.id_comp, Category.assoc, biproduct.lift_π, biproduct.ι_desc_assoc,       biproduct.ι_π]     ext ⟨⟩ ⟨⟩     simp only [embedding, comp_apply, comp_dite, dite_comp, comp_zero, zero_comp,       Finset.sum_dite_eq', Finset.mem_univ, ite_true, eqToHom_refl, Category.comp_id]     split_ifs with h     · subst h       simp     · rfl set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

CategoryTheory.Mat.equivalenceSingleObjI.fullDefinition: def equivalenceSingleObjInverse : Mat_ (SingleObj Rᵐᵒᵖ) ⥤ Mat R where   obj X := FintypeCat.of X.ι   map f i j := MulOpposite.unop (f i j)   map_id X := by     ext     simp only [Mat_.id_def, id_def]     split_ifs <;> rfl   map_comp f g := by     -- Porting note: this proof was automatic in mathlib3     ext     simp only [Mat_.comp_apply, comp_apply]     apply Finset.unop_sum set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

CategoryTheory.HomOrthogonal.matrixDecom.fullDefinition: noncomputable def matrixDecomposition (o : HomOrthogonal s) {α β : Type} [Finite α] [Finite β]     {f : α → ι} {g : β → ι} :     ((⨁ fun a => s (f a)) ⟶ ⨁ fun b => s (g b)) ≃       ∀ i : ι, Matrix (g ⁻¹' {i}) (f ⁻¹' {i}) (End (s i)) where   toFun z i j k :=     eqToHom         (by           rcases k with ⟨k, ⟨⟩⟩           simp) ≫       biproduct.components z k j ≫         eqToHom           (by             rcases j with ⟨j, ⟨⟩⟩             simp)   invFun z :=     biproduct.matrix fun j k =>       if h : f j = g k then z (f j) ⟨k, by simp [h]⟩ ⟨j, by simp⟩ ≫ eqToHom (by simp [h]) else 0   left_inv z := by     ext j k     simp only [biproduct.matrix_π, biproduct.ι_desc]     split_ifs with h     · simp       rfl     · symm       apply o.eq_zero h   right_inv z := by     ext i ⟨j, w⟩ ⟨k, ⟨⟩⟩     simp only [eqToHom_refl, biproduct.matrix_components, Category.id_comp]     split_ifs with h     · simp     · exfalso       exact h w.symm
CategoryTheory.HomOrthogonal.matrixDecom.description: Morphisms between two direct sums of objects from a hom orthogonal family are equivalent to block diagonal matrices where each block corresponds to a specific object and entries are endomorphisms of that object.

Endomorphisms of a simple object form a field if they are finite dimensional.

explanatories.MulAction.mul_smul: This theorem states that the action of multiplying two elements behaves associatively with respect to both multiplication and the action on another element.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.

CategoryTheory.fieldEndOfFiniteDimension.fullDefinition: noncomputable def fieldEndOfFiniteDimensional (X : C) [Simple X] [I : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (X ⟶ X)] :     Field (End X) := by   classical exact     { (inferInstance : DivisionRing (End X)) with       mul_comm := fun f g => by         obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := endomorphism_simple_eq_smul_id 𝕜 f         obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := endomorphism_simple_eq_smul_id 𝕜 g         simp [← mul_smul, mul_comm c d] }
CategoryTheory.fieldEndOfFiniteDimension.description: The endomorphisms of a simple object in a finite-dimensional linear category form a field.

CategoryTheory.finrank_hom_simple_simple.comment:
**Schur's lemma** for `𝕜`-linear categories:
if hom spaces are finite dimensional, then the hom space between simples is at most 1-dimensional.

See `finrank_hom_simple_simple_eq_one_iff` and `finrank_hom_simple_simple_eq_zero_iff` below
for the refinements when we know whether or not the simples are isomorphic.

CategoryTheory.ForgetEnrichment.code:
CategoryTheory.ForgetEnrichment.{v, u₁} (W : Type (v + 1)) [Category.{v, v + 1} W] [MonoidalCategory W] (C : Type u₁)
  [EnrichedCategory W C] : Type u₁
CategoryTheory.ForgetEnrichment.comment:
A type synonym for `C`, which should come equipped with a `V`-enriched category structure.
In a moment we will equip this with the (honest) category structure
so that `X ⟶ Y` is `(𝟙_ W) ⟶ (X ⟶[W] Y)`.

We obtain this category by
transporting the enrichment in `V` along the lax monoidal functor `coyonedaTensorUnit`,
then using the equivalence of `Type`-enriched categories with honest categories.

This is sometimes called the "underlying" category of an enriched category,
although some care is needed as the functor `coyonedaTensorUnit`,
which always exists, does not necessarily coincide with
"the forgetful functor" from `V` to `Type`, if such exists.
When `V` is any of `Type`, `Top`, `AddCommGroup`, or `Module R`,
`coyonedaTensorUnit` is just the usual forgetful functor, however.
For `V = Algebra R`, the usual forgetful functor is coyoneda of `R[X]`, not of `R`.
(Perhaps we should have a typeclass for this situation: `ConcreteMonoidal`?)

CategoryTheory.enrichedNatTransYoneda.fullDefinition: def enrichedNatTransYoneda (F G : EnrichedFunctor V C D) : Vᵒᵖ ⥤ Type max u₁ w where   obj A := GradedNatTrans ((Center.ofBraided V).obj (unop A)) F G   map f σ :=     { app := fun X => f.unop ≫ σ.app X       naturality := fun X Y => by         have p := σ.naturality X Y         dsimp at p ⊢         rw [← id_tensor_comp_tensor_id (f.unop ≫ σ.app Y) _, id_tensor_comp, Category.assoc,           Category.assoc, ← braiding_naturality_assoc, id_tensor_comp_tensor_id_assoc, p, ←           tensor_comp_assoc, Category.id_comp] }

CategoryTheory.enrichedFunctorTypeEquivF.fullDefinition: def enrichedFunctorTypeEquivFunctor {C : Type u₁} [𝒞 : EnrichedCategory (Type v) C] {D : Type u₂}     [𝒟 : EnrichedCategory (Type v) D] : EnrichedFunctor (Type v) C D ≃ C ⥤ D where   toFun F :=     { obj := fun X => F.obj X       map := fun f => F.map _ _ f       map_id := fun X => congr_fun (F.map_id X) PUnit.unit       map_comp := fun f g => congr_fun (F.map_comp _ _ _) ⟨f, g⟩ }   invFun F :=     { obj := fun X => F.obj X       map := fun X Y f => F.map f       map_id := fun X => by ext ⟨⟩; exact F.map_id X       map_comp := fun X Y Z => by ext ⟨f, g⟩; exact F.map_comp f g }   left_inv _ := rfl   right_inv _ := rfl

CategoryTheory.enrichedNatTransYonedaTyp.fullDefinition: def enrichedNatTransYonedaTypeIsoYonedaNatTrans {C : Type v} [EnrichedCategory (Type v) C]     {D : Type v} [EnrichedCategory (Type v) D] (F G : EnrichedFunctor (Type v) C D) :     enrichedNatTransYoneda F G ≅       yoneda.obj (enrichedFunctorTypeEquivFunctor F ⟶ enrichedFunctorTypeEquivFunctor G) :=   NatIso.ofComponents     (fun α =>       { hom := fun σ x =>           { app := fun X => σ.app X x             naturality := fun X Y f => congr_fun (σ.naturality X Y) ⟨x, f⟩ }         inv := fun σ =>           { app := fun X x => (σ x).app X             naturality := fun X Y => by ext ⟨x, f⟩; exact (σ x).naturality f } })     (by aesop_cat)

CategoryTheory.linearYoneda.comment:
The Yoneda embedding for `R`-linear categories `C`,
sending an object `X : C` to the `Module R`-valued presheaf on `C`,
with value on `Y : Cᵒᵖ` given by `Module.of R (unop Y ⟶ X)`.

explanatories.ModuleCat.of: This definition constructs the category of modules over a ring using an existing additive commutative group that also satisfies the module property.
explanatories.Opposite.unop: This definition describes the canonical mapping from the opposite category of a type back to the original type.
explanatories.ModuleCat.ofHom: This definition identifies a linear map between two modules over a ring as a morphism in the category of modules associated with those modules.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Linear.leftComp: This defines an R-linear mapping that represents composition of morphisms in a category by fixing a left argument.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Linear.rightComp: This defines an R-linear mapping that represents composition of morphisms in a category by fixing a right argument.

CategoryTheory.linearYoneda.fullDefinition: def linearYoneda : C ⥤ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat R where   obj X :=     { obj := fun Y => ModuleCat.of R (unop Y ⟶ X)       map := fun f => ModuleCat.ofHom (Linear.leftComp R _ f.unop) }   map {X₁ X₂} f :=     { app := fun Y => @ModuleCat.ofHom R _ (Y.unop ⟶ X₁) (Y.unop ⟶ X₂) _ _ _ _         (Linear.rightComp R _ f) }
CategoryTheory.linearYoneda.description: This defines the Yoneda embedding for R-linear categories, which assigns to each object a presheaf represented by the module of morphisms from objects in the opposite category.

CategoryTheory.IsSeparating.comment:
We say that `𝒢` is a separating set if the functors `C(G, -)` for `G ∈ 𝒢` are collectively
faithful, i.e., if `h ≫ f = h ≫ g` for all `h` with domain in `𝒢` implies `f = g`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Set.op: The opposite of a set is the set formed by taking the opposite of each of its members.

CategoryTheory.IsSeparating.description: This definition states that a set is separating if the corresponding functors defined on it collectively demonstrate faithfulness by ensuring that equalities of morphisms imply equality of their respective mappings.

CategoryTheory.hasInitial_of_isCoseparat.comment:
An ingredient of the proof of the Special Adjoint Functor Theorem: a complete well-powered
category with a small coseparating set has an initial object.

In fact, it follows from the Special Adjoint Functor Theorem that `C` is already cocomplete,
see `hasColimits_of_hasLimits_of_isCoseparating`.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.add.comment:
The addition on the morphisms in the category `Quotient r` when `r` is compatible
with the addition.

explanatories.Quot.liftOn₂: This defines a method to apply a function to equivalence classes derived from two sets, effectively extending the function to the corresponding quotient structures.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.compClosure_iff_: This theorem indicates that two morphisms are related by a specific relation if and only if they can be obtained from each other through a series of compositions using that relation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor_map_eq_i: This theorem establishes that the images of two morphisms under a functor are equal if and only if the morphisms themselves are related by a specific relation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Congruence.equivalence: This theorem establishes that a specific relationship on morphisms, which is a congruence, forms an equivalence relation across all hom-sets in the category.
explanatories.Equivalence.refl: An equivalence relation satisfies reflexivity, meaning every element is related to itself.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.add.fullDefinition: def add {X Y : Quotient r} (f g : X ⟶ Y) : X ⟶ Y :=   Quot.liftOn₂ f g (fun a b => Quot.mk _ (a + b))     (fun f g₁ g₂ h₁₂ => by       simp only [compClosure_iff_self] at h₁₂       erw [functor_map_eq_iff]       exact hr _ _ _ _ (Congruence.equivalence.refl f) h₁₂)     (fun f₁ f₂ g h₁₂ => by       simp only [compClosure_iff_self] at h₁₂       erw [functor_map_eq_iff]       exact hr _ _ _ _ h₁₂ (Congruence.equivalence.refl g))
CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.add.description: This definition specifies how to add morphisms in the quotient category when the underlying relation is compatible with the addition operation on morphisms.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.neg.comment:
The negation on the morphisms in the category `Quotient r` when `r` is compatible
with the addition.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.compClosure_iff_: This theorem indicates that two morphisms are related by a specific relation if and only if they can be obtained from each other through a series of compositions using that relation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor_map_eq_i: This theorem establishes that the images of two morphisms under a functor are equal if and only if the morphisms themselves are related by a specific relation.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Congruence.equivalence: This theorem establishes that a specific relationship on morphisms, which is a congruence, forms an equivalence relation across all hom-sets in the category.
explanatories.Equivalence.refl: An equivalence relation satisfies reflexivity, meaning every element is related to itself.
explanatories.Quot.liftOn: The process of lifting a function onto the quotient of a set, while ensuring that equivalent elements map to the same value, can be rearranged so that the quotient appears as the first argument.
explanatories.Equivalence.symm: An equivalence relation demonstrates symmetry, meaning if one element is related to another, then the second element is also related to the first.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.neg.fullDefinition: def neg {X Y : Quotient r} (f : X ⟶ Y) : X ⟶ Y :=   Quot.liftOn f (fun a => Quot.mk _ (-a))     (fun f g => by       intro hfg       simp only [compClosure_iff_self] at hfg       erw [functor_map_eq_iff]       apply Congruence.equivalence.symm       convert hr f g _ _ hfg (Congruence.equivalence.refl (-f-g)) using 1 <;> abel)
CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.neg.description: This definition describes how to negate morphisms in the quotient category when the underlying relation is compatible with the addition operation on morphisms.

  Preadditive (Quotient r)
CategoryTheory.Quotient.preadditive.comment:
The preadditive structure on the category `Quotient r` when `r` is compatible
with the addition.

explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.add: This definition specifies how to add morphisms in the quotient category when the underlying relation is compatible with the addition operation on morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.Preadditive.neg: This definition describes how to negate morphisms in the quotient category when the underlying relation is compatible with the addition operation on morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor: This definition describes a functor that maps a category to its quotient category formed by an equivalence relation on the morphisms.
explanatories.add_assoc: This theorem states that the addition operation is associative, meaning that the grouping of three elements being added does not affect the result.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.nsmulRec: This definition describes a recursive function for scalar multiplication in an additive monoid, which adds an element to itself a specified number of times.
explanatories.zsmulRec: This definition describes a function that extends scalar multiplication to integers in an additive group, operating by repeatedly adding an element for positive integers and accounting for negatives by using inverses.
explanatories.add_left_neg: This theorem asserts that in an additive group, the sum of an element and its additive inverse equals the zero element.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.add_comp: This theorem states that in a preadditive category, the composition with a morphism preserves the addition of morphisms.
explanatories.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.comp_add: This theorem establishes how the composition of maps interacts with the addition of morphisms in a preadditive category.

CategoryTheory.Quotient.preadditive.fullDefinition: def preadditive : Preadditive (Quotient r) where   homGroup P Q :=     let iZ : Zero (P ⟶ Q) :=       { zero := Quot.mk _ 0 }     let iA : Add (P ⟶ Q) :=       { add := Preadditive.add r hr }     let iN : Neg (P ⟶ Q) :=       { neg := Preadditive.neg r hr }     { add_assoc := by rintro ⟨_⟩ ⟨_⟩ ⟨_⟩; exact congr_arg (functor r).map (add_assoc _ _ _)       zero_add := by rintro ⟨_⟩; exact congr_arg (functor r).map (zero_add _)       add_zero := by rintro ⟨_⟩; exact congr_arg (functor r).map (add_zero _)       add_comm := by rintro ⟨_⟩ ⟨_⟩; exact congr_arg (functor r).map (add_comm _ _)       add_left_neg := by rintro ⟨_⟩; exact congr_arg (functor r).map (add_left_neg _)       -- todo: use a better defeq       nsmul := nsmulRec       zsmul := zsmulRec }   add_comp := by     rintro _ _ _ ⟨_⟩ ⟨_⟩ ⟨_⟩     exact congr_arg (functor r).map (by apply Preadditive.add_comp)   comp_add := by     rintro _ _ _ ⟨_⟩ ⟨_⟩ ⟨_⟩     exact congr_arg (functor r).map (by apply Preadditive.comp_add)

CategoryTheory.Quotient.Linear.module'.fullDefinition: def module' (X Y : C) : Module R ((functor r).obj X ⟶ (functor r).obj Y) :=   letI := smul r hr ((functor r).obj X) ((functor r).obj Y)   { smul_zero := fun a => by       dsimp       rw [← (functor r).map_zero X Y, smul_eq, smul_zero]     zero_smul := fun f => by       obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := (functor r).map_surjective f       dsimp       rw [zero_smul, Functor.map_zero]     one_smul := fun f => by       obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := (functor r).map_surjective f       dsimp       rw [one_smul]     mul_smul := fun a b f => by       obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := (functor r).map_surjective f       dsimp       rw [mul_smul]     smul_add := fun a f g => by       obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := (functor r).map_surjective f       obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := (functor r).map_surjective g       dsimp       rw [← (functor r).map_add, smul_eq, ← (functor r).map_add, smul_add]     add_smul := fun a b f => by       obtain ⟨f, rfl⟩ := (functor r).map_surjective f       dsimp       rw [add_smul, Functor.map_add] }
